chapters.title: Pre-historic and Proto-historic Sites of Rajasthan
factsheet: Kalibangan (Hanumangarh) lies on the left bank of the dry Ghaggar; the name means 'black bangles'; excavated by B.B. Lal and B.K. Thapar, 1961-69.
Kalibangan gave the world's earliest attested ploughed field (pre-Harappan, criss-cross furrows) and a row of seven fire altars on the citadel.
Kalibangan is the only Harappan site where BOTH the citadel and the lower town were fortified; it has no elaborate covered drainage system.
Luigi Pio Tessitori first drew attention to Kalibangan (1917-18); A. Ghosh identified it as Harappan in 1951-52; the site museum opened in 1983.
Kalibangan Period I = pre-Harappan (bricks 30x20x10 cm, 3:2:1); Period II = Mature Harappan (bricks 30x15x7.5 cm, 4:2:1).
Kalibangan yielded evidence of an earthquake around 2600 BCE and a cylinder seal showing a woman between two spear-bearing men; three burial types.
Bagor (Bhilwara), on the Kothari river, is India's largest and best-documented Mesolithic site; excavated by V.N. Misra, 1967-70.
Bagor gave some of India's earliest evidence of animal domestication (c. 5000 BCE); microliths dominate the tool kit; five human burials were found.
Tilwara (Barmer) is a Mesolithic site on the Luni, excavated by V.N. Misra (1967-68); Didwana-Singi Talav (Nagaur) and Budha Pushkar (Ajmer) are Palaeolithic.
Ahar (Udaipur), on the Ayad-Berach, was called Tambavati ('place of copper') and Aghatpur/Aghatdurg; first dug by Akshay Kirti Vyas (1953), then R.C. Agrawal and H.D. Sankalia (1961-62).
The Ahar culture (= Banas culture, c. 2800-1500 BCE) is marked by Black-and-Red Ware with white linear designs and heavy copper use with almost no microliths.
Gilund (Rajsamand) on the Banas was first excavated by B.B. Lal; the later Indo-American work was by V.S. Shinde and G.L. Possehl.
Balathal (Udaipur) was excavated by V.N. Misra from 1993; it has a massive fortified enclosure and the oldest skeletal evidence of leprosy in India (c. 2000 BCE).
Ojiyana (Bhilwara) was excavated by B.R. Meena of the ASI Jaipur Circle, 1999-2000; an Ahar-culture site on a hill slope with painted bull and cow figurines.
Ganeshwar (Sikar, Neem ka Thana) on the Kantli was excavated by R.C. Agrawal and Vijay Kumar; over 2,000 copper objects and Ochre Coloured Pottery (OCP).
The Ganeshwar-Jodhpura culture is believed to have supplied copper to the Harappans; Jodhpura (Jaipur region) lies on the Sabi river.
Bairath/Viratnagar (Jaipur) has two Ashokan minor rock edicts; the Bhabru (Calcutta-Bairat) edict names the Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha and is in the Asiatic Society, Kolkata.
Bijak-ki-Pahadi at Bairath has India's oldest free-standing circular Buddhist temple (chaitya-griha); Bairath was excavated by Daya Ram Sahni in 1936-37.
Bairath yielded punch-marked silver coins and Indo-Greek coins in a jar; Bhim ji ki Dungri and Ganesh Dungri are its other mounds.
Rairh (Tonk), on the Dheel, was excavated by K.N. Puri (1938-39): 3,075 punch-marked coins and huge iron slag heaps; called the 'Tata Nagar of ancient India'.
Sunari (Jhunjhunu) on the Kantli has the earliest iron-smelting furnaces so far reported from Rajasthan.
Noh (Bharatpur) shows a four-fold sequence - OCP, Black-and-Red Ware, Painted Grey Ware and Northern Black Polished Ware; the colossal Yaksha statue 'Jakh Baba' came from here.
Nagari (Chittorgarh) is ancient Madhyamika, capital of the Shivi janapada; the Ghosundi-Hathibada inscription was found close by.
Rang Mahal (Hanumangarh) on the Ghaggar was excavated by a Swedish expedition led by Hanna Rydh (1952-54); Kushana-Gupta period material.
Baror (Sri Ganganagar) and Sothi (Bikaner) are Ghaggar-valley pre-Harappan/Harappan sites; A. Ghosh named the 'Sothi culture' after Sothi.
Kurada (Nagaur) is a copper-hoard site; Jhadol (Udaipur), Pindpadaliya (Chittorgarh) and Malah (Bharatpur) are other proto-historic finds.
OCP, Black-and-Red Ware (BRW), Painted Grey Ware (PGW) and Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW) are the four diagnostic proto-historic wares of Rajasthan.
Bhinmal (Jalore) was excavated by R.C. Agrawal (1953-54) and yielded Roman/Greek wine vessels and Shaka-period material.
Sequence to remember: Didwana (Palaeolithic) - Bagor/Tilwara (Mesolithic) - Ahar/Ganeshwar/Balathal (Chalcolithic) - Kalibangan (Bronze/Harappan) - Sunari/Rairh/Noh (Iron Age).
Excavation years to remember: Bairath 1936-37, Rairh 1938-39, Rang Mahal 1952-54, Kalibangan 1961-69, Bagor 1967-70, Balathal from 1993, Ojiyana 1999-2000.

questions.q: Kalibangan, the Harappan site of Rajasthan, is situated on the left bank of which river?
questions.exp: Kalibangan lies in Hanumangarh district on the left bank of the now-dry Ghaggar, identified by many scholars with the Vedic Saraswati.

questions.q: Which of the following sites has yielded the world's earliest known evidence of a ploughed agricultural field?
questions.exp: A pre-Harappan field with criss-cross plough furrows was exposed south-east of the Kalibangan settlement. The same site gave a row of seven fire altars on the citadel.

questions.q: The excavation of Kalibangan between 1961 and 1969 was carried out under the direction of
opts: A. Ghosh and Luigi Pio Tessitori
Daya Ram Sahni and K.N. Puri
questions.exp: B.B. Lal directed the nine seasons of work at Kalibangan with B.K. Thapar; A. Ghosh had identified the mound as Harappan in 1951-52.

questions.q: The name 'Kalibangan' is derived from
opts: the black soil of the Ghaggar bed
a local ruler named Kali Singh
black bangles found on the site
questions.exp: 'Kali bangan' literally means black bangles, after the terracotta bangle fragments scattered over the mounds.

questions.q: Bagor, the largest Mesolithic site of India, is situated on the bank of the river
questions.exp: Bagor lies on the Kothari, a tributary of the Banas, in Bhilwara district. It is famous for its microlithic industry and early animal domestication.

questions.q: The Mesolithic site of Bagor was excavated under the direction of
questions.exp: V.N. Misra of Deccan College excavated Bagor between 1967 and 1970. He also worked at Tilwara and later at Balathal.

questions.q: Bagor is located in which district of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Bagor is in Bhilwara district, about 25 km west of Bhilwara town, on the Kothari river.

questions.q: The ancient name 'Tambavati', meaning 'the place of copper', refers to which archaeological site?
questions.exp: Ahar in Udaipur was known as Tambavati because of its extensive copper working; it was also called Aghatpur or Aghatdurg.

questions.q: The Ahar culture is also known as the
questions.exp: Because its sites cluster in the Banas basin, the Ahar culture is also called the Banas culture; it is dated roughly 2800-1500 BCE.

questions.q: The oldest skeletal evidence of leprosy in India was reported from which site of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: A skeleton of about 2000 BCE from Balathal (Udaipur) carries the oldest known bone evidence of leprosy in India. Balathal also has a massive fortified enclosure.

questions.q: The excavation of Ojiyana was conducted under the direction of
questions.exp: B.R. Meena of the ASI Jaipur Circle excavated Ojiyana in 1999-2000. It is an Ahar-culture settlement noted for painted bull and cow figurines.

questions.q: Ganeshwar, famous for its large hoard of copper objects, is located in which district?
questions.exp: Ganeshwar lies in the Neem ka Thana area of Sikar district, near the copper belt of Khetri.

questions.q: Ganeshwar is situated on the bank of which river?
questions.exp: Ganeshwar stands near the source of the Kantli river in Sikar district. Sunari in Jhunjhunu also lies on the Kantli.

questions.q: The characteristic pottery of the Ganeshwar-Jodhpura culture is
questions.exp: Ochre Coloured Pottery (OCP) is the hallmark of the Ganeshwar-Jodhpura complex, whose people are thought to have supplied copper to the Harappans.

questions.q: The proto-historic site of Jodhpura is situated on the bank of the river
questions.exp: Jodhpura lies on the Sabi river in the Kotputli area. Together with Ganeshwar it defines the Ganeshwar-Jodhpura copper culture.

questions.q: The Bhabru (Calcutta-Bairat) rock edict of Ashoka, which mentions the Buddha, the Dhamma and the Sangha, was found at
questions.exp: The Bhabru edict was found at Bairath (Viratnagar) in the Jaipur region and is preserved in the Asiatic Society, Kolkata. A second minor rock edict survives at the site.

questions.q: India's oldest known free-standing circular Buddhist temple (chaitya-griha) has been reported from
questions.exp: The circular brick and timber chaitya on Bijak-ki-Pahadi at Bairath is dated to the 3rd century BCE and is the oldest free-standing Buddhist structure in India.

questions.q: Bairath was excavated in 1936-37 under the direction of
questions.exp: Daya Ram Sahni excavated Bairath in 1936-37; Captain Burt had noticed the Ashokan edict there back in 1837.

questions.q: Which archaeological site of Rajasthan yielded a hoard of 3,075 punch-marked silver coins along with extensive iron slag?
questions.exp: Rairh in Tonk district, excavated by K.N. Puri in 1938-39, gave 3,075 punch-marked coins and huge quantities of iron slag, earning it the tag 'Tata Nagar of ancient India'.

questions.q: Rairh, often described as the 'Tata Nagar of ancient India', lies in which district?
questions.exp: Rairh is in Tonk district on the Dheel river. Its iron slag heaps indicate large-scale early iron smelting.

questions.q: The earliest iron-smelting furnaces so far reported from Rajasthan were found at
questions.exp: Sunari in Jhunjhunu district, on the Kantli, has yielded the earliest iron-smelting furnaces of Rajasthan.

questions.q: The colossal Yaksha statue locally worshipped as 'Jakh Baba' was recovered from which site?
questions.exp: The large Yaksha image called Jakh Baba was found at Noh in Bharatpur district, a site with a four-fold cultural sequence from OCP to NBPW.

questions.q: The ancient town of Madhyamika, capital of the Shivi janapada, is identified with the site of
questions.exp: Nagari near Chittorgarh is ancient Madhyamika. The Ghosundi-Hathibada inscription was found in its neighbourhood.

questions.q: Rang Mahal in Hanumangarh district was excavated by a Swedish expedition led by
questions.exp: Hanna Rydh led the Swedish excavation at Rang Mahal in 1952-54, exposing Kushana-Gupta period remains on the Ghaggar.

questions.q: Singi Talav near Didwana is associated with which prehistoric period?
questions.exp: Singi Talav near Didwana in Nagaur district has yielded Lower and Middle Palaeolithic Acheulian tools.

questions.q: The Mesolithic site of Tilwara is situated on the bank of the river
questions.exp: Tilwara lies on the Luni in the Barmer-Balotra region and was excavated by V.N. Misra in 1967-68.

questions.q: Kurada, known for a hoard of copper implements, is located in which district?
questions.exp: Kurada in Nagaur district produced a notable hoard of copper tools and weapons of the Chalcolithic period.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Kalibangan:
I. It is the only Harappan site where both the citadel and the lower town were fortified.
II. A row of seven fire altars was found on the citadel mound.
III. It possessed an elaborate covered drainage system like Mohenjo-daro.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Kalibangan's lower town was also walled, which is unusual among Harappan sites. Unlike Mohenjo-daro it had no developed covered drainage.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Ahar culture:
I. Its characteristic pottery is Black-and-Red Ware bearing white linear designs.
II. The type-site lies on the Ayad river, a tributary of the Berach.
III. Microliths form the dominant tool type of the culture.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Ahar people relied on copper rather than stone, so microliths are almost absent - a point of contrast with the Malwa and Jorwe cultures.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Bagor:
I. It is the largest and best-documented Mesolithic site of India.
II. It has provided some of the earliest evidence of animal domestication in India.
III. It was excavated between 1967 and 1970.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Bagor's microlithic industry is one of the richest in South Asia and its animal bones point to domestication around 5000 BCE.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Ganeshwar:
I. It has yielded more than two thousand copper objects.
II. Its people are believed to have supplied copper to the Harappans.
III. It lies in the Neem ka Thana area.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Arrowheads, spearheads, fish-hooks, bangles and chisels of copper dominate the Ganeshwar assemblage, alongside OCP.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Balathal:
I. It lies in Udaipur district.
II. Excavations there were led by V.N. Misra from 1993.
III. A massive fortified enclosure of stone and mud-brick was exposed at the site.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Balathal has both a Chalcolithic (Ahar culture) phase and a later early historic phase with iron.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Bairath:
I. Two minor rock edicts of Ashoka have been reported from the site.
II. The Bhabru edict is now preserved in the Asiatic Society, Kolkata.
III. Punch-marked and Indo-Greek coins were recovered from the site.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Bairath is the only place in Rajasthan to yield Ashokan edicts, and its coin hoard included Indo-Greek issues.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Gilund:
I. It is situated on the Banas river in Rajsamand district.
II. It was first excavated by B.B. Lal.
III. It belongs to the Ahar-Banas cultural complex.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Later Indo-American excavations at Gilund were directed by V.S. Shinde and G.L. Possehl.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Ojiyana:
I. It is located in Bhilwara district.
II. It is an Ahar-culture settlement built on a hill slope.
III. Painted terracotta figurines of bulls and cows were recovered there.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Ojiyana is unusual among Ahar-culture sites for being laid out on a slope rather than a plain.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the site of Noh:
I. It lies in Bharatpur district.
II. It has revealed a four-fold cultural sequence of OCP, Black-and-Red Ware, Painted Grey Ware and Northern Black Polished Ware.
III. It was excavated under the direction of R.C. Agrawal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Noh's stratified sequence makes it a key type-site for the proto-historic to early historic transition in eastern Rajasthan.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Kalibangan:
I. Period I at the site represents the pre-Harappan culture.
II. The mud bricks of Period I measured 30 x 15 x 7.5 cm.
III. Period II represents the Mature Harappan occupation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Period I used mud bricks of 30 x 20 x 10 cm (ratio 3:2:1); the 30 x 15 x 7.5 cm (4:2:1) bricks belong to Mature Harappan Period II.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of a prehistoric site and its district is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Sunari lies in Jhunjhunu district on the Kantli. Sikar is the district of Ganeshwar.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about Kalibangan is NOT correct?
opts: Evidence of an early earthquake was found there.
A cylinder seal was recovered from the site.
questions.exp: Kalibangan is the only Harappan city where the lower town too was fortified. Signs of an earthquake around 2600 BCE were also detected.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a Chalcolithic site of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Sunari in Jhunjhunu is an Iron Age site famous for early iron-smelting furnaces; the other three belong to the Ahar-Banas Chalcolithic complex.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of a site and its excavator is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Ganeshwar was excavated by R.C. Agrawal and Vijay Kumar. B.B. Lal is associated with Kalibangan and Gilund.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Mesolithic site of Bagor is NOT correct?
opts: It lies on the Kothari river in Bhilwara district.
Microliths form the dominant tool assemblage.
It yielded a row of seven fire altars.
It has provided early evidence of animal domestication.
questions.exp: The row of seven fire altars belongs to Kalibangan, not Bagor.

questions.q:
Arrange the following sites of Rajasthan in the correct chronological order of the cultural stage they principally represent, from the earliest to the latest:
I. Kalibangan
II. Bagor
III. Didwana
IV. Sunari
questions.exp: Didwana (Palaeolithic) - Bagor (Mesolithic) - Kalibangan (Bronze Age/Harappan) - Sunari (Iron Age).

questions.q:
Arrange the following excavations in the correct chronological order, from the earliest to the latest:
I. Rairh
II. Bairath
III. Ojiyana
IV. Rang Mahal
questions.exp: Bairath 1936-37, Rairh 1938-39, Rang Mahal 1952-54, Ojiyana 1999-2000.

chapters.title: Sources of Rajasthan History
factsheet: Barli inscription (Ajmer district) - Rajasthan's oldest Brahmi inscription; Prakrit; refers to Lord Vira (Mahavira); brought to light by G.H. Ojha in 1912; kept in the museum at Ajmer.

Ghosundi / Hathibada inscription (near Nagari, Chittorgarh) - 1st century BCE, Brahmi; earliest epigraphic evidence of Bhagavata worship of Sankarshana and Vasudeva; king Sarvatata performed an Ashvamedha.
Yupa (sacrificial pillar) inscriptions: Nandsa (Bhilwara) 225 CE, Barnala 227 CE, Badva (Baran) 238 CE of three Maukhari brothers, Bichpuria/Uniara (Tonk) 274 CE.
Bijaygarh pillar at Bayana, 'Bhim ki Lat' - VS 428 = 371 CE; Varika ruler Vishnuvardhana's Pundarika yajna.
Man Mori inscription (Chittorgarh, 713 CE) was found by Col. James Tod at Mansarovar; it records the Maurya rulers of Chittor and was lost at sea on its way to England.
Samoli inscription (Udaipur, 646 CE) of Shiladitya - earliest evidence of mining activity in Mewar; Nagda/Aparajita inscription 661 CE.
Mandore inscription (837 CE) and Ghatiyala inscription (861 CE, Kakkuka) relate to the Pratiharas of Mandore.
Harsha (Harshnath) inscription, Sikar, 973 CE - earliest surviving Chauhan record; gives the Chauhan genealogy and the Shiva temple on Harshagiri.
Atpur (Ahar) inscription of 977 CE, of Shaktikumar - genealogy of the Guhilas of Mewar from Guhadatta.
Bijolia inscription (Bhilwara, 1170 CE) - of Someshvara's reign; calls the Chauhans of Sambhar and Ajmer Vatsa-gotra Brahmins and says Ajayaraja founded Ajmer.
Delhi-Shivalik (Delhi-Topra) pillar inscription of 1164 CE - Chauhan Vigraharaja IV (Visaladeva), claiming conquest from the Himalaya to the Vindhyas.
Chirwa inscription (Udaipur, 1273 CE) - Guhila rulers Jaitrasimha, Tejasimha and Samarasimha; composed by Ratnaprabha Suri.
Ranakpur inscription (1439 CE) - traces Rana Kumbha's line from Bappa Rawal; Dharanashah (Depa) built the Chaumukha Adinatha temple.
Kumbhalgarh inscription (1460 CE, five slabs) composed by Kavi Mahesh; the Kirti Stambha Prashasti of Chittorgarh was written by Atri and his son Mahesh.
Raisingh Prashasti (Junagarh fort, Bikaner, 1594 CE) - composed by the Jain sage Jaita; history of the Bikaner Rathores.
Raj Prashasti (Rajsamand, 1676 CE) - 25 black-stone slabs by Ranchhod Bhatt Tailang on Maharana Raj Singh; the largest stone inscription in India.
Rajor inscription (Rajorgarh, Alwar, 960 CE) of Mathanadeva - the only record that actually uses the term 'Gurjara-Pratihara'.
Coins: Gadhiya (Indo-Sasanian, western Rajasthan), Rupak and Dramma (Chauhan period), punch-marked Karshapanas (3,075 found at Rairh).

State coins - Jaipur: Jhadshahi; Jodhpur: Vijayshahi and Bhimshahi; Bikaner: Gajshahi; Jaisalmer: Akhaishahi and Muhammadshahi; Mewar: Swaroopshahi and Chandori; Kota: Gumanshahi; Bundi: Ramshahi and Katarshahi; Pratapgarh: Salimshahi.
Archival bahis (Bikaner State Archives) - Hakikat Bahi (daily routine of the ruler), Hukumat ri Bahi (royal orders), Kamthana Bahi (construction works), Kharita Bahi (correspondence).
Other archival records: Pattas (grants), Parwanas (orders), Sanads, Khatoot and Jama-bandi papers of the former states.
Muhnot Nainsi (1610-70), Diwan of Maharaja Jaswant Singh I of Jodhpur, wrote Nainsi ri Khyat and Marwar ra Pargana ri Vigat; G.H. Ojha called him the 'Abul Fazl of Rajputana'.

'Marwar ra Pargana ri Vigat' is regarded as the first gazetteer of Rajasthan; other khyats are Bankidas ri Khyat (Marwar), Dayaldas ri Khyat (Bikaner), Mundiyar ri Khyat and Bhation ri Khyat (Jaisalmer).
Raso literature: Prithviraj Raso - Chand Bardai (Pingal); Bisaldev Raso - Narpati Nalha; Khuman Raso - Dalpat Vijay; Hammir Raso - Sarangdhar.
Sanskrit sources: Hammir Mahakavya - Nayanchandra Suri; Prithviraja Vijaya - Jayanaka; Kuvalayamala - Uddyotana Suri (778 CE, at Jalore).
Vachanika and prabandha: Achaldas Khichi ri Vachanika - Shivdas Gadan; Kanhadde Prabandh - Padmanabh (1455); Veli Krishan Rukmani Ri - Prithviraj Rathore.
Modern histories: Vansh Bhaskar - Suryamal Mishran (Bundi, Dingal); Veer Vinod - Kaviraj Shyamaldas (Mewar); Rajputane ka Itihas - Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha.
Persian sources: Tabaqat-i-Nasiri (Minhaj-us-Siraj), Tarikh-i-Firozshahi (Ziauddin Barani), Akbarnama and Ain-i-Akbari (Abul Fazl), Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri (Jahangir), Padshahnama (Abdul Hamid Lahori).

Col. James Tod - Political Agent to the Western Rajput States from 1818; 'Annals and Antiquities of Rajasthan' (London, 1829-32) and 'Travels in Western India' (posthumous); called the father of Rajasthan's history and locally 'Ghode wale Baba'; his guru was the Jain yati Gyanchandra.
The Rajasthan State Archives at Bikaner is the principal repository of princely-state records; the museum at Ajmer (1908) holds the Barli inscription.

questions.q: The oldest known inscription of Rajasthan, written in Brahmi script and referring to Lord Vira (Mahavira), was found at
questions.exp: The Barli inscription, found near Bhilot Mata temple in Ajmer district and brought to notice by G.H. Ojha in 1912, is Rajasthan's earliest Brahmi record and is preserved in the museum at Ajmer.

questions.q: The Ghosundi inscription provides the earliest epigraphic evidence in Rajasthan of the worship of
questions.exp: The 1st century BCE Ghosundi-Hathibada inscription records a stone enclosure for the worship of Sankarshana and Vasudeva, the earliest Bhagavata evidence in the state.

questions.q: The Ghosundi and Hathibada inscriptions are located in which district?
questions.exp: Both lie near Nagari (ancient Madhyamika) in Chittorgarh district. The record mentions an Ashvamedha performed by king Sarvatata.

questions.q: The Bijolia rock inscription of 1170 CE describes the Chauhans of Sambhar and Ajmer as
questions.exp: The Bijolia inscription of Someshvara's reign calls the Chauhans Vatsa-gotra Brahmins and states that Ajayaraja founded Ajmer.

questions.q: The Raj Prashasti, the largest stone inscription in India, was composed by
questions.exp: Ranchhod Bhatt Tailang composed the Raj Prashasti in 1676 CE; it is engraved on 25 black stone slabs on the embankment of the Rajsamand lake and celebrates Maharana Raj Singh.

questions.q: The Raisingh Prashasti of 1594 CE is inscribed in which fort?
questions.exp: The Raisingh Prashasti, composed by the Jain sage Jaita, is in the Junagarh fort at Bikaner and records the history of the Bikaner Rathores.

questions.q: The Chirwa inscription of 1273 CE is an important source for the history of the
questions.exp: The Chirwa inscription (Udaipur district) records the Guhila rulers Jaitrasimha, Tejasimha and Samarasimha and was composed by Ratnaprabha Suri.

questions.q: The Nandsa Yupa inscription is located in which district?
questions.exp: The Nandsa yupa (sacrificial pillar) inscription of 225 CE is in Bhilwara district; the Badva yupa pillars of 238 CE are in Baran district.

questions.q: The Badva yupa pillar inscriptions of 238 CE record a sacrifice performed by three brothers belonging to which family?
questions.exp: The Badva pillars record a Triratra sacrifice by Balavardhana, Somadeva and Balasimha, sons of Maharaja Bala of the Maukhari family.

questions.q: Who among the following is described as the 'father of the history of Rajasthan'?
questions.exp: Colonel James Tod, Political Agent to the Western Rajput States from 1818, wrote 'Annals and Antiquities of Rajasthan' and is popularly remembered in Rajasthan as 'Ghode wale Baba'.

questions.q: Colonel James Tod's 'Annals and Antiquities of Rajasthan' was first published in London in
questions.exp: The first volume appeared in 1829 and the second in 1832. His 'Travels in Western India' was published posthumously.

questions.q: Who among the following is described as the 'Abul Fazl of Rajputana'?
questions.exp: G.H. Ojha gave Muhnot Nainsi, Diwan of Maharaja Jaswant Singh I of Jodhpur, the title 'Abul Fazl of Rajputana' for the detail of his chronicles.

questions.q: 'Marwar ra Pargana ri Vigat' by Muhnot Nainsi is generally regarded as
opts: a Dingal poem on Rao Jodha
questions.exp: The Vigat gives pargana-wise details of Marwar's villages, revenue and society and is treated as Rajasthan's first gazetteer.

questions.q: 'Vansh Bhaskar', a Dingal work dealing largely with the history of Bundi, was written by
questions.exp: Suryamal Mishran of Bundi wrote Vansh Bhaskar; it was completed after his death by Muraridan.

questions.q: 'Hammir Mahakavya' was composed by
questions.exp: Nayanchandra Suri wrote the Sanskrit Hammir Mahakavya on Hammir Dev, the Chauhan ruler of Ranthambore.

questions.q: 'Kuvalayamala', composed in 778 CE at Jalore, is the work of
questions.exp: Uddyotana Suri composed the Prakrit Kuvalayamala at Jabalipura (Jalore); it is a valuable source on the languages and society of 8th century Rajasthan.

questions.q: 'Veer Vinod', the official history of Mewar, was written by
questions.exp: Kaviraj Shyamaldas compiled Veer Vinod at the court of Maharana Sajjan Singh of Mewar.

questions.q: The 'Jhadshahi' coins were issued by which of the following princely states?
questions.exp: Jhadshahi was the currency of Jaipur state. Jodhpur issued Vijayshahi, Bikaner Gajshahi and Jaisalmer Akhaishahi coins.

questions.q: Among the archival records of the former Rajasthan states, the 'Kamthana Bahi' contains information about
opts: the daily routine of the ruler
questions.exp: Kamthana Bahis record construction and repair works. Hakikat Bahi records the ruler's daily routine and Kharita Bahi official correspondence.

questions.q: The Rajasthan State Archives, the principal repository of the records of the former princely states, is located at
questions.exp: The Rajasthan State Archives at Bikaner holds the bahis, pattas, parwanas and khyats of the former states.

questions.q: 'Achaldas Khichi ri Vachanika' was written by
questions.exp: Shivdas Gadan wrote this vachanika describing the struggle of Achaldas Khichi of Gagron against Hoshang Shah of Malwa.

questions.q: 'Bisaldev Raso' was composed by
questions.exp: Narpati Nalha wrote Bisaldev Raso on the Chauhan ruler Vigraharaja IV (Visaladeva). Chand Bardai wrote Prithviraj Raso and Dalpat Vijay Khuman Raso.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Raj Prashasti inscription:
I. It is engraved on twenty-five black stone slabs.
II. It was composed by Ranchhod Bhatt Tailang in 1676 CE.
III. It is the largest stone inscription in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The slabs are set into the Nauchowki embankment of the Rajsamand lake built by Maharana Raj Singh.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Muhnot Nainsi:
I. He was Diwan of Maharaja Jaswant Singh I of Jodhpur.
II. He wrote 'Nainsi ri Khyat' and 'Marwar ra Pargana ri Vigat'.
III. His works were written in Persian.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Nainsi wrote in Rajasthani (Marwari-Dingal), not Persian.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Colonel James Tod:
I. He served as Political Agent to the Western Rajput States from 1818.
II. His 'Travels in Western India' was published after his death.
III. He recovered the Man Mori inscription from the bank of the Mansarovar at Chittorgarh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Man Mori slab was lost at sea while being shipped to England.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Barli inscription:
I. It is written in Brahmi script.
II. It refers to Lord Vira, that is Mahavira.
III. It is preserved in the museum at Ajmer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Its date is disputed - G.H. Ojha read it as 443 BCE, while most epigraphists place it in the 2nd-1st century BCE.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the archival records of the former Rajasthan states:
I. 'Hakikat Bahi' records the daily routine of the ruler.
II. 'Hukumat ri Bahi' preserves copies of the orders issued by the ruler.
III. 'Kamthana Bahi' records official correspondence with other states.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Kamthana Bahis deal with construction works; correspondence was recorded in the Kharita Bahi.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. 'Tabaqat-i-Nasiri' was written by Minhaj-us-Siraj.
II. 'Tarikh-i-Firozshahi' was written by Ziauddin Barani.
III. 'Padshahnama' was written by Abul Fazl.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Padshahnama was written by Abdul Hamid Lahori. Abul Fazl wrote the Akbarnama and Ain-i-Akbari.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the coins of the princely states of Rajasthan:
I. The silver coins of Bikaner were called Gajshahi.
II. The coins of Jodhpur were called Vijayshahi.
III. The coins of Jaisalmer were called Ramshahi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Jaisalmer issued Akhaishahi and Muhammadshahi coins; Ramshahi coins belong to Bundi.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Work)     List-II (Author)
A. Prithviraj Raso   1. Dalpat Vijay
B. Bisaldev Raso     2. Chand Bardai
C. Khuman Raso       3. Sarangdhar
D. Hammir Raso       4. Narpati Nalha
questions.exp: Prithviraj Raso - Chand Bardai; Bisaldev Raso - Narpati Nalha; Khuman Raso - Dalpat Vijay; Hammir Raso - Sarangdhar.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Inscription)     List-II (District)
A. Bijolia              1. Udaipur
B. Harsha               2. Bikaner
C. Chirwa               3. Bhilwara
D. Raisingh Prashasti   4. Sikar
questions.exp: Bijolia - Bhilwara; Harsha - Sikar; Chirwa - Udaipur; Raisingh Prashasti - Bikaner (Junagarh fort).

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Coin)   List-II (Princely state)
A. Gajshahi     1. Jaipur
B. Jhadshahi    2. Bikaner
C. Akhaishahi   3. Jaisalmer
D. Gumanshahi   4. Kota
questions.exp: Gajshahi - Bikaner; Jhadshahi - Jaipur; Akhaishahi - Jaisalmer; Gumanshahi - Kota.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Work)          List-II (Author)
A. Akbarnama           1. Abdul Hamid Lahori
B. Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri   2. Minhaj-us-Siraj
C. Padshahnama         3. Abul Fazl
D. Tabaqat-i-Nasiri    4. Jahangir
questions.exp: Akbarnama - Abul Fazl; Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri - Jahangir; Padshahnama - Abdul Hamid Lahori; Tabaqat-i-Nasiri - Minhaj-us-Siraj.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Work)            List-II (Author)
A. Nainsi ri Khyat       1. Bankidas
B. Dayaldas ri Khyat     2. Muhnot Nainsi
C. Bankidas ri Khyat     3. Dayaldas Sidhaich
D. Veer Vinod            4. Kaviraj Shyamaldas
questions.exp: Nainsi ri Khyat - Muhnot Nainsi; Dayaldas ri Khyat - Dayaldas Sidhaich (Bikaner); Bankidas ri Khyat - Bankidas; Veer Vinod - Kaviraj Shyamaldas.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Inscription)     List-II (Year)
A. Bijolia inscription   1. 1439 CE
B. Atpur inscription     2. 977 CE
C. Ranakpur inscription  3. 1170 CE
D. Raj Prashasti         4. 1676 CE
questions.exp: Bijolia 1170 CE; Atpur (Ahar) 977 CE; Ranakpur 1439 CE; Raj Prashasti 1676 CE.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of a work and its author is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Veli Krishan Rukmani Ri - Prithviraj Rathore
questions.exp: Vansh Bhaskar was written by Suryamal Mishran of Bundi; Bankidas wrote Bankidas ri Khyat.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of an archival record and its content is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Hakikat Bahi - daily routine of the ruler
Hukumat ri Bahi - land revenue settlement
questions.exp: Hukumat ri Bahi preserves copies of the orders issued by the ruler, not revenue settlements.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of a coin and the state that issued it is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Chandori and Swaroopshahi coins belong to Mewar (Udaipur); Bikaner issued Gajshahi coins.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Bijolia inscription is NOT correct?
opts: It is engraved in Bhilwara district.
It describes the Chauhans of Sambhar as Vatsa-gotra Brahmins.
It records the construction of the Rajsamand lake.
questions.exp: The Rajsamand lake and its Raj Prashasti belong to Maharana Raj Singh of Mewar in the 17th century.

questions.q:
Arrange the following inscriptions of Rajasthan in the correct chronological order, from the earliest to the latest:
I. Bijolia inscription
II. Atpur (Ahar) inscription
III. Raj Prashasti
IV. Ranakpur inscription
questions.exp: Atpur 977 CE, Bijolia 1170 CE, Ranakpur 1439 CE, Raj Prashasti 1676 CE.

chapters.title: Early Dynasties of Rajasthan
factsheet: Gurjara-Pratihara founder Nagabhata I (c. 730-760 CE) ruled from Bhinmal/Jalore and checked the Arab advance from Sindh; title Nagavaloka.
Vatsaraja (title Ranahastin) began the tripartite struggle for Kannauj against the Palas and the Rashtrakutas; Nagabhata II finally captured Kannauj and made it the capital.
Mihir Bhoj (c. 836-885 CE) was the greatest Pratihara; his title Adivaraha appears on his coins; the Gwalior prashasti is his key record.
The Arab merchant Sulaiman (851 CE, Silsilat-ut-Tawarikh) called the Pratihara kingdom 'Juzr', praised its cavalry and called its ruler the greatest foe of Islam.
Mahendrapala I (title Raghukula-chudamani) patronised Rajashekhara, author of Karpuramanjari, Kavyamimamsa, Bala-Ramayana and Bala-Bharata.

Pratihara branches: Mandore (founder Harishchandra; Ghatiyala inscription of Kakkuka, 861 CE), Bhinmal-Jalore, and the imperial line at Kannauj; Mahmud of Ghazni sacked Kannauj under Rajyapala (1018).
Osian (Jodhpur) has an 8th-11th century Pratihara temple group including the Sachiya Mata and Mahavira temples; it is the traditional origin place of the Oswal Jains.
Rajor inscription (960 CE, Rajorgarh in Alwar): Mathanadeva, a Gurjara-Pratihara feudatory, built the Shiva temple of Lachchhukesvara.
Varika dynasty of Bayana: Vishnuvardhana's Bijaygarh pillar ('Bhim ki Lat'), VS 428 = 371-72 CE, records a Pundarika yajna; he was probably a Gupta feudatory.
Chauhans (Chahamanas) of Shakambhari: first historical ruler Vasudeva (c. 551 CE), linked with the Sambhar salt lake; Simharaja was the first to take the title Maharajadhiraja.
The Harsha (Harshnath) inscription of 973 CE, Sikar, is the earliest surviving record of the Chauhans of Shakambhari.
Ajayaraja II (c. 1110-1135) founded Ajayameru (Ajmer) and shifted the capital there; his queen Somaladevi issued coins in her own name.
Arnoraja (1135-50) built the Ana Sagar lake at Ajmer and defeated Turkish raiders; he was killed by his son Jagaddeva.

Vigraharaja IV 'Visaladeva' (1150-64) took Delhi from the Tomaras and wrote the Sanskrit play Harakeli Nataka; his court poet Somadeva wrote Lalita-Vigraharaja Nataka; both survive on slabs in the Adhai Din ka Jhonpra at Ajmer.
Prithviraja III (1177-92) defeated the Chandela Paramardi (1182), won Tarain I (1191) and lost Tarain II (1192) to Muhammad Ghori; Jayanaka wrote Prithviraja Vijaya, Chand Bardai the Prithviraj Raso.
Chauhans of Ranthambore: Hammir Dev was defeated by Alauddin Khalji in 1301 - the first jauhar/saka of Rajasthan; Hammir Mahakavya by Nayanchandra Suri.
Chauhans of Jalore (Sonagara branch, founded by Kirtipala): Kanhadadeva was defeated by Alauddin Khalji in 1311; Padmanabh's Kanhadde Prabandh narrates it.
Chauhans of Nadol were founded by Lakshmana, brother of Vakpatiraja I of Shakambhari; the Deora branch ruled Sirohi (Sirohi town founded 1425 by Rao Sahasmal).
Hada Chauhans: Rao Deva took Bundi from Jaita Meena in 1241; Kota became a separate state under Madho Singh, recognised by Shah Jahan in 1631.
Guhilas of Mewar: founder Guhadatta (Guhil, c. 566 CE); early capital Nagda; Bappa Rawal (Kalbhoj) is credited with taking Chittor from the Maurya chief Man Mori.
The Guhilas split into the Rawal line (Chittor) and the Rana/Sisodia line; the Atpur inscription of 977 CE gives the early genealogy; the Samoli inscription of 646 CE names Shiladitya.
Paramaras of Abu: founder Dhumraj, capital Chandravati; Dharavarsha was a contemporary of Prithviraja III; Paramaras of Vagad (Dungarpur-Banswara) had their capital at Arthuna.
Dilwara: Vimal Vasahi (1031 CE) built by Vimal Shah, minister of Bhima I of Gujarat; Luna Vasahi (1230 CE) built by the brothers Vastupala and Tejpala.
Shivi (Shibi) janapada had its capital at Madhyamika (Nagari, Chittorgarh); its coins read 'Majhamikaya Shibijanapadasa'.
Malava coins with the legend 'Malavanam Jaya' were found in thousands at Nagar/Karkotanagar (Tonk); Yaudheya coins carry Brahmanyadeva (Kartikeya).
Other ancient tribes: Arjunayanas (Bharatpur-Alwar), Rajanyas (Noh, Bharatpur) and the Nagas of eastern Rajasthan.
Mauryas of Chittor: Man Mori built the Man Sarovar (Man Mori inscription, 713 CE); the Kanaswa inscription (738 CE, Kota) of Dhavala also records Maurya rule.
Hunas under Toramana and Mihirakula raided north-western India in the early 6th century; the Rashtrakutas of Hastikundi (Hathundi, Pali) were a local branch.
Solanki (Chalukya) rulers of Gujarat such as Kumarapala and Bhima II controlled Abu and Kiradu; the Kiradu temples lie in Barmer district.
Bhinmal (Srimal), an early Pratihara capital, is traditionally the birthplace of the astronomer Brahmagupta and the poet Magha (Shishupala Vadha).

questions.q: The founder of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty, who checked the Arab advance from Sindh, was
questions.exp: Nagabhata I (c. 730-760 CE) ruled from Bhinmal and Jalore and repulsed the Arab armies; the Gwalior prashasti praises him as a destroyer of the mlechchhas.

questions.q: Which Pratihara ruler finally captured Kannauj and made it the capital of the empire?
questions.exp: Nagabhata II defeated his rivals in the tripartite struggle and shifted the Pratihara capital to Kannauj.

questions.q: The Pratihara ruler Mihir Bhoj assumed which of the following titles, found on his coins?
questions.exp: Mihir Bhoj's silver coins carry the title Adivaraha. Nagavaloka was Nagabhata I's title and Raghukulachudamani that of Mahendrapala I.

questions.q: The Arab merchant who in 851 CE described the Pratihara kingdom as 'Juzr' and its ruler as the greatest foe of Islam was
questions.exp: Sulaiman's Silsilat-ut-Tawarikh praised the cavalry of Mihir Bhoj's kingdom, which he called Juzr.

questions.q: Rajashekhara, the author of 'Karpuramanjari' and 'Kavyamimamsa', adorned the court of
questions.exp: Rajashekhara was the teacher and court poet of Mahendrapala I and later stayed on under Mahipala; he also wrote Bala-Ramayana and Bala-Bharata.

questions.q: The group of early temples at Osian, built largely in the Pratihara period, is located in which district?
questions.exp: Osian in Jodhpur district has some of Rajasthan's oldest surviving temples, including the Sachiya Mata and Mahavira temples.

questions.q: The Rajor inscription of 960 CE records the building of a Shiva temple by which ruler?
questions.exp: Mathanadeva, a Gurjara-Pratihara feudatory at Rajorgarh in Alwar, built the temple of Lachchhukesvara Mahadeva. This is the only inscription that actually uses the term 'Gurjara-Pratihara'.

questions.q: The Bijaygarh (Bayana) pillar inscription of VS 428 records a Pundarika sacrifice performed by which Varika ruler?
questions.exp: Vishnuvardhana of the Varika family raised the pillar, locally called 'Bhim ki Lat', in 371-72 CE; he was probably a feudatory of the Guptas.

questions.q: The first historically attested ruler of the Chauhans of Shakambhari was
questions.exp: Vasudeva (c. 551 CE) is the earliest Chauhan king named in the records; tradition connects him with the acquisition of the Sambhar salt lake.

questions.q: The city of Ajayameru (Ajmer) was founded by the Chauhan ruler
questions.exp: Ajayaraja II founded Ajayameru around 1113 CE and moved the Chauhan capital there from Shakambhari.

questions.q: The Ana Sagar lake at Ajmer was built by
questions.exp: Arnoraja (also called Anaji), who ruled 1135-50, had the Ana Sagar excavated; he also defeated the Ghaznavid forces near Ajmer.

questions.q: The Sanskrit play 'Harakeli Nataka' was written by
questions.exp: Vigraharaja IV himself wrote Harakeli Nataka, modelled on Bharavi's Kiratarjuniya; fragments survive on slabs reused in the Adhai Din ka Jhonpra.

questions.q: 'Lalita-Vigraharaja Nataka' was composed by
questions.exp: Somadeva, court poet of Vigraharaja IV, wrote Lalita-Vigraharaja Nataka in honour of his patron.

questions.q: Vigraharaja IV wrested control of Delhi from which dynasty?
questions.exp: Vigraharaja IV (Visaladeva) took Dhillika (Delhi) from the Tomaras; his 1164 CE Delhi-Shivalik pillar inscription claims conquest from the Himalaya to the Vindhyas.

questions.q: The Second Battle of Tarain was fought in
questions.exp: Prithviraja III won the First Battle of Tarain in 1191 but was defeated by Muhammad Ghori in the Second Battle of Tarain in 1192.

questions.q: Hammir Dev, the Chauhan ruler defeated by Alauddin Khalji in 1301, ruled from
questions.exp: Ranthambore fell to Alauddin Khalji in 1301; the episode is celebrated as the first saka and jauhar of Rajasthan and is described in the Hammir Mahakavya.

questions.q: Kanhadadeva, defeated by Alauddin Khalji in 1311, was the Chauhan ruler of
questions.exp: Kanhadadeva of Jalore fell in 1311. Padmanabh's Kanhadde Prabandh (1455) narrates the struggle.

questions.q: The Sonagara branch of the Chauhans, which ruled at Jalore, was founded by
questions.exp: Kirtipala (Kitu), a son of the Nadol line, founded the Sonagara Chauhans of Jalore.

questions.q: The Chauhans of Nadol were founded by
questions.exp: Lakshmana, a brother of Vakpatiraja I of Shakambhari, established the Nadol branch of the Chauhans in Marwar.

questions.q: Rao Deva, the founder of Hada rule at Bundi in 1241, took the town from
questions.exp: Rao Deva defeated the Meena chief Jaita and took Bundi in 1241, founding the Hada Chauhan line of Hadoti.

questions.q: The founder of the Guhila dynasty of Mewar was
questions.exp: Guhadatta (Guhil), around 566 CE, is regarded as the founder of the Guhila line; Bappa Rawal, identified with Kalbhoj, came later.

questions.q: The early capital of the Guhilas of Mewar, before the acquisition of Chittor, was
questions.exp: Nagda near Udaipur was the early Guhila capital; the centre later moved to Ahar and then to Chittor.

questions.q: The capital of the Paramaras of Abu was
questions.exp: Chandravati at the foot of Mount Abu was the Paramara capital; Arthuna was the capital of the Paramaras of Vagad.

questions.q: The capital of the Paramaras of Vagad was
questions.exp: Arthuna in present Banswara district was the capital of the Vagad Paramaras; its ruined temples survive.

questions.q: Coins bearing the legend 'Majhamikaya Shibijanapadasa' belong to which ancient janapada?
questions.exp: These coins belong to the Shivi (Shibi) janapada whose capital Madhyamika is identified with Nagari near Chittorgarh.

questions.q: Thousands of coins of the Malava tribe have been discovered at which place in Tonk district?
questions.exp: Nagar (Karkotanagar) in Tonk district yielded a very large number of Malava coins bearing the legend 'Malavanam Jaya'.

questions.q: Bhinmal, an early Pratihara capital, is traditionally regarded as the birthplace of the astronomer
questions.exp: Brahmagupta, author of the Brahmasphutasiddhanta, is traditionally associated with Bhinmal (Srimal) in Jalore district, as is the poet Magha.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Gurjara-Pratiharas:
I. Vatsaraja began the tripartite struggle for Kannauj.
II. The Pratiharas fought the Palas and the Rashtrakutas for control of Kannauj.
III. Mahmud of Ghazni attacked Kannauj during the reign of Rajyapala.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Kannauj was the prize in the long tripartite contest, and Rajyapala abandoned it before Mahmud in 1018.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Vigraharaja IV:
I. He was also known as Visaladeva.
II. He captured Delhi from the Tomaras.
III. The Delhi-Shivalik pillar inscription of 1164 CE belongs to his reign.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Bisaldev Raso by Narpati Nalha also celebrates him.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Prithviraja III:
I. He defeated the Chandela ruler Paramardi in 1182.
II. He defeated Muhammad Ghori in the First Battle of Tarain in 1191.
III. His court poet Chand Bardai composed 'Prithviraja Vijaya' in Sanskrit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Prithviraja Vijaya was composed in Sanskrit by the Kashmiri poet Jayanaka; Chand Bardai is credited with the Prithviraj Raso.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Guhilas of Mewar:
I. The Atpur inscription of 977 CE gives their early genealogy.
II. Bappa Rawal is credited with wresting Chittor from the Maurya chief Man Mori.
III. The dynasty later divided into the Rawal and the Rana (Sisodia) branches.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Samoli inscription of 646 CE is another early Guhila record.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Varika dynasty:
I. Its known centre was Bayana in the present Bharatpur region.
II. The Bijaygarh pillar inscription of Vishnuvardhana is dated VS 428.
III. Vishnuvardhana is generally regarded as a feudatory of the Guptas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. VS 428 corresponds to 371-72 CE, the age of Samudragupta.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Vimal Vasahi temple at Dilwara was built in 1031 CE by Vimal Shah.
II. The Luna Vasahi temple was built by the brothers Vastupala and Tejpala.
III. The Paramaras of Abu had their capital at Arthuna.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Paramaras of Abu had their capital at Chandravati; Arthuna was the capital of the Vagad Paramaras.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Deora branch of the Chauhans ruled at Sirohi.
II. The Hada branch of the Chauhans ruled at Bundi and Kota.
III. The Sonagara branch of the Chauhans ruled at Nadol.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Sonagara Chauhans ruled at Jalore, not Nadol; Nadol had its own Chauhan line founded by Lakshmana.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the ancient republics of Rajasthan:
I. The Malava coins bear the legend 'Malavanam Jaya'.
II. The Yaudheya coins carry the figure of Brahmanyadeva (Kartikeya).
III. The Arjunayanas were settled in the Bharatpur-Alwar region.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Rajanyas, another such tribe, are associated with Noh in Bharatpur.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Harishchandra is regarded as the founder of the Pratihara line of Mandore.
II. The Ghatiyala inscription of 861 CE belongs to the Pratihara ruler Kakkuka.
III. Nagabhata I ruled from Bhinmal and Jalore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Mandore was the oldest of the Pratihara branches in Rajasthan.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Simharaja was the first Chauhan ruler to assume the title Maharajadhiraja.
II. The Harsha inscription of 973 CE is the earliest surviving record of the Chauhans of Shakambhari.
III. Someshvara was the father of Prithviraja III.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Harsha inscription from Harshagiri in Sikar district also records the Shiva temple there.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Dynasty)          List-II (Capital)
A. Paramaras of Abu     1. Nagda
B. Paramaras of Vagad   2. Shakambhari
C. Guhilas (early)      3. Chandravati
D. Chauhans (early)     4. Arthuna
questions.exp: Paramaras of Abu - Chandravati; Paramaras of Vagad - Arthuna; early Guhilas - Nagda; early Chauhans - Shakambhari (Sambhar).

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Chauhan ruler)   List-II (Associated with)
A. Ajayaraja II     1. First Battle of Tarain
B. Arnoraja         2. Ana Sagar lake
C. Vigraharaja IV   3. Conquest of Delhi from the Tomaras
D. Prithviraja III  4. Foundation of Ajmer
questions.exp: Ajayaraja II founded Ajmer; Arnoraja built the Ana Sagar; Vigraharaja IV took Delhi; Prithviraja III won Tarain I.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

B. Vatsaraja        2. Nagavaloka

D. Mahendrapala I   4. Ranahastin
questions.exp: Nagabhata I - Nagavaloka; Vatsaraja - Ranahastin; Mihir Bhoj - Adivaraha; Mahendrapala I - Raghukulachudamani.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

A. Sonagara   1. Bundi
B. Deora      2. Ranthambore

questions.exp: Sonagara - Jalore; Deora - Sirohi; Hada - Bundi; Chahamanas of Ranastambhapura - Ranthambore.
