questions.exp: Shivi - Madhyamika (Nagari); Malava - Nagar in Tonk; Rajanya - Noh; Varika - Bayana.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Silsilat-ut-Tawarikh is Sulaiman's account of 851 CE, which describes the kingdom of Mihir Bhoj, not Vatsaraja.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about Prithviraja III is NOT correct?
opts: He belonged to the Chauhans of Shakambhari.
He defeated Muhammad Ghori at Tarain in 1191.
He shifted his capital permanently from Ajmer to Delhi.
Chand Bardai is traditionally regarded as his court poet.
questions.exp: Ajmer remained the Chauhan capital; Delhi had been annexed earlier by Vigraharaja IV and was held through a Tomara feudatory.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of a dynasty and its area of rule is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The Hada Chauhans ruled Hadoti, that is Bundi and Kota; Jalore was the seat of the Sonagara Chauhans.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of an inscription and the dynasty it relates to is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The Ghatiyala inscription of 861 CE belongs to the Pratihara ruler Kakkuka of Mandore.

questions.q: Which one of the following rulers was NOT a Chauhan?
questions.exp: Bappa Rawal belonged to the Guhila dynasty of Mewar; the other three are Chauhans of different branches.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Gurjara-Pratiharas is NOT correct?
opts: Nagabhata I resisted the Arab invaders from Sindh.
Nagabhata II made Kannauj his capital.
Mihir Bhoj was a contemporary of the Arab writer Sulaiman.
Rajyapala defeated Mahmud of Ghazni at Kannauj in 1018.
questions.exp: Rajyapala abandoned Kannauj before Mahmud of Ghazni in 1018 and was later killed by the Chandela ruler for having fled.

questions.q:
Arrange the following rulers in the correct chronological order, from the earliest to the latest:
I. Prithviraja III
II. Mihir Bhoj
III. Vigraharaja IV
IV. Ajayaraja II
questions.exp: Mihir Bhoj (836-885), Ajayaraja II (c. 1110-1135), Vigraharaja IV (1150-1164), Prithviraja III (1177-1192).

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Nagabhata I of the Pratihara dynasty is praised in the Gwalior inscription as a destroyer of the mlechchhas.
Reason (R): He successfully resisted the Arab armies advancing from Sindh.
Select the correct answer from the codes given below:
opts: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.exp: The Gwalior prashasti of Mihir Bhoj praises Nagabhata I precisely because he checked the Arab advance from Sindh in the 8th century.

chapters.title: Mewar: Guhil-Sisodia Dynasty
factsheet: Guhil (Guhaditya) founded the Guhil dynasty of Mewar c. 566 CE; earliest capital Nagda (Nagahrada), near Udaipur.
Bappa Rawal (identified with Kalbhoj, c. 734 CE) wrested Chittor from the Mori (Maurya) ruler Man Mori; titles 'Hindu Suraj' and 'Rajguru'.
Eklingji (Kailashpuri) is the tutelary deity of Mewar; the Maharanas ruled as 'Diwan' of Eklingji.
Allat shifted the capital from Nagda to Ahar — hence the 'Aharya' branch of the Guhils.
Jaitrasimha (Jaitra Singh, 1213-1253) repulsed Iltutmish's attack on Nagda and made Chittor the capital — the golden age of the Rawal line.
FIRST saka of Chittor, 1303 — Alauddin Khilji vs Rawal Ratan Singh; jauhar associated with Rani Padmini; Chittor renamed Khizrabad after Khizr Khan.

Rana Hammir (1326-1364) recovered Chittor from Maldeo of Jalore, defeated Muhammad bin Tughlaq at SINGOLI (1336), founded the SISODIA branch; title 'Vishamghati Panchanan'; first Mewar ruler styled 'Rana'.
Rana Lakha (1382-1421) — Jawar zinc-silver mines discovered; Pichola lake built in his reign by a Banjara. Rana Mokal was his son by Hansabai of Marwar.
Rana Kumbha (1433-1468) defeated Mahmud Khilji of Malwa at SARANGPUR (1437) and built the VIJAY STAMBH at Chittorgarh — 9 storeys, c. 37 m.
The Kirti Stambh at Chittorgarh is a 12th-century JAIN tower dedicated to Adinatha — built by the merchant Jijaji Rathore, NOT by Kumbha.
Kumbha built 32 of Mewar's 84 forts, incl. KUMBHALGARH (architect Mandan) — wall c. 36 km, second-longest continuous wall in the world; Badal Mahal; birthplace of Maharana Pratap.
Kumbha's titles: Abhinav Bharatacharya, Hindu Suratrana, Haalguru (lord of hill forts), Rajguru, Danguru, Chhapguru.
Kumbha's works: Sangeet Raj, Sangeet Mimansa, Sudprabandh, Kamraj Ratisar and RASIK PRIYA (commentary on Jayadeva's Gita Govinda).

Kumbha's court: Mandan (Prasad Mandan, Roop Mandan, Rajvallabh, Devata Murti Prakaran), Natha (Vastu Manjari), Govind (Kalanidhi, Dwar Deepika), Kanha Vyas (Ekling Mahatmya), Atri & Mahesh (Kumbhalgarh Prashasti).
Kumbha was murdered at Kumbhalgarh in 1468 by his son Uda (Udai Singh I).
Rana Sanga (Sangram Singh I, 1509-1528): Khatoli 1517 (vs Ibrahim Lodi), Bari/Dholpur 1518, Gagron 1519 (vs Mahmud Khilji II), Bayana Feb 1527; defeated by BABUR at KHANWA, 17 March 1527; died 1528.
SECOND saka of Chittor, 1535 — Bahadur Shah of Gujarat; jauhar led by Rani Karnavati; Vikramaditya was then Rana; Banbir usurped the throne in 1536.
Panna Dhai saved the infant Udai Singh II from Banbir by sacrificing her own son Chandan.
Udai Singh II founded UDAIPUR in 1559 and made it the new capital of Mewar.
THIRD saka of Chittor — Akbar's siege, 23 Oct 1567 to 23 Feb 1568; defended by Jaimal Rathore of Merta and Patta (Fatta) Sisodia of Kelwa; Akbar placed their statues at the gate of Agra Fort.
Maharana Pratap: b. 9 May 1540 at Kumbhalgarh; coronation at GOGUNDA in 1572; d. 19 January 1597 at Chavand.

Battle of HALDIGHATI, 18 June 1576 — Mughal force led by Man Singh I of Amber with Asaf Khan; Pratap's horse Chetak; Hakim Khan Sur led the Afghan contingent; Jhala Man (Bida) wore Pratap's insignia. Col. Tod: 'Thermopylae of Mewar'.
Battle of DEWAIR (1582) — Pratap's decisive victory, called the 'Marathon of Mewar' by Col. Tod; Chavand made capital in 1585; Bhamashah financed the struggle; Punja Bhil led the Bhils.

Amar Singh I concluded the Mewar-Mughal TREATY OF 1615 with Jahangir (negotiated by Prince Khurram): no matrimonial alliance, the Rana need not attend court in person (Prince Karan Singh went instead), Chittor returned but never to be repaired.
Karan Singh built Jagmandir on Lake Pichola and sheltered the rebel Prince Khurram; Jagat Singh I built the Jagdish temple, Udaipur (1651) — golden age of Mewar painting (Sahibdin).

Raj Singh I (1652-1680) built RAJSAMAND lake as famine relief; the RAJPRASHASTI of Ranchhod Bhatt on 25 slabs at Nauchowki is the largest stone inscription in India; married Charumati of Kishangarh; installed Shrinathji at Sihad (Nathdwara) in 1672; opposed Aurangzeb's jaziya.
Maharana Jai Singh built JAISAMAND (Dhebar) lake; Amar Singh II concluded the DEBARI agreement (1708) with Ajit Singh of Marwar and Sawai Jai Singh II of Amber.
Sangram Singh II built Saheliyon ki Bari, Udaipur; Jagat Singh II presided over the HURDA Conference (17 July 1734).
Bhim Singh signed Mewar's treaty with the British on 13 January 1818; Col. James Tod became the first Political Agent in Mewar; the Krishna Kumari episode belongs to his reign.
Maharana Fateh Singh refused to attend Lord Curzon's Delhi Durbar of 1903; Bhupal Singh, the last Maharana, became the first Rajpramukh of the United State of Rajasthan (18 April 1948).

questions.q: Bappa Rawal, the celebrated early ruler of the Guhil dynasty of Mewar, is identified in the sources with which other name?
questions.exp: Bappa Rawal (c. 734 CE) is identified with Kalbhoj. He is credited with taking Chittor from the Mori (Maurya) ruler Man Mori and bore the titles Hindu Suraj and Rajguru.

questions.q: The Maharanas of Mewar traditionally governed the state as the 'Diwan' (deputy) of which deity?
questions.exp: Eklingji at Kailashpuri near Udaipur is the tutelary deity of the House of Mewar; the ruler styled himself Diwan of Eklingji. Shrinathji at Nathdwara arrived only in 1672.

questions.q: Which Guhil ruler shifted the capital of Mewar from Nagda to Ahar?
questions.exp: Allat moved the seat of power to Ahar, after which the branch came to be called Aharya. Jaitrasimha later made Chittor the capital.

questions.q: The first saka of Chittorgarh in 1303 took place during the invasion of:
questions.exp: Alauddin Khilji besieged Chittor in 1303 during the reign of Rawal Ratan Singh; the jauhar is traditionally associated with Rani Padmini.

questions.q: After capturing Chittor in 1303, Alauddin Khilji renamed it:
questions.exp: Chittor was renamed Khizrabad after Alauddin's son Khizr Khan, who was placed in charge of the fort.

questions.q: The Battle of Singoli (1336) was fought between Rana Hammir of Mewar and:
questions.exp: Rana Hammir defeated the Delhi Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq at Singoli in 1336, completing the recovery of Mewar's independence.

questions.q: Rana Hammir is regarded as the founder of which branch of the Guhils of Mewar?
questions.exp: Hammir belonged to the Sisoda line and founded the Sisodia branch; he was also the first Mewar ruler to bear the title 'Rana' in place of 'Rawal'.

questions.q: In the Battle of Sarangpur (1437), Rana Kumbha defeated:
questions.exp: Kumbha's victory over Sultan Mahmud Khilji of Malwa at Sarangpur in 1437 is commemorated by the Vijay Stambh at Chittorgarh.

questions.q: The Vijay Stambh at Chittorgarh was raised by Rana Kumbha to commemorate his victory over:
questions.exp: The nine-storeyed Vijay Stambh (c. 37 m) marks Kumbha's victory over Mahmud Khilji. It is distinct from the Jain Kirti Stambh, which is much older.

questions.q: Which architect is credited with the construction of Kumbhalgarh fort under Rana Kumbha?
questions.exp: Mandan, Kumbha's chief architect, designed Kumbhalgarh and wrote treatises such as Prasad Mandan, Roop Mandan and Rajvallabh.

questions.q: Rana Kumbha's commentary on Jayadeva's Gita Govinda is titled:
questions.exp: Rasik Priya is Kumbha's commentary on the Gita Govinda. Sangeet Mimansa and Sudprabandh are his own separate compositions.

questions.q: Which of the following treatises on music was composed by Maharana Kumbha?
questions.exp: Sangeet Raj is Kumbha's best-known musical treatise. Sangeet Ratnakar was written much earlier by Sharangdeva, on which Kumbha only wrote a commentary.

questions.q: The title 'Abhinav Bharatacharya' was borne by which ruler of Mewar?
questions.exp: Kumbha's mastery of music and dramaturgy earned him 'Abhinav Bharatacharya'. His other titles include Hindu Suratrana and Haalguru.

questions.q: Rana Kumbha was assassinated in 1468 by:
questions.exp: Kumbha was murdered at Kumbhalgarh by his son Uda, who usurped the throne; Uda was later displaced by Kumbha's other son Raimal.

questions.q: The Battle of Khanwa (1527) was fought between Babur and:
questions.exp: Babur defeated the Rajput confederacy led by Rana Sanga at Khanwa on 17 March 1527; Medini Rai of Chanderi was one of Sanga's allies.

questions.q: Rana Sanga defeated Ibrahim Lodi in which battle of 1517?
questions.exp: Sanga defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Khatoli (1517) and again at Bari/Dholpur (1518); at Gagron (1519) he defeated Mahmud Khilji II of Malwa.

questions.q: The second saka of Chittorgarh took place during the invasion of:
questions.exp: Bahadur Shah of Gujarat stormed Chittor in 1535; the jauhar is associated with Rani Karnavati, and Vikramaditya was then the Rana.

questions.q: Panna Dhai sacrificed her own son Chandan to save the life of:
questions.exp: Panna Dhai substituted her son for the infant Udai Singh II when the usurper Banbir sought to kill him.

questions.q: The city of Udaipur was founded in 1559 by:
questions.exp: Udai Singh II founded Udaipur in 1559 and shifted the capital there after Chittor fell to Akbar in 1568.

questions.q: During Akbar's siege of Chittorgarh (1567-68), the fort was defended by:
opts: Jaimal of Merta and Patta of Kelwa
questions.exp: Rana Udai Singh II withdrew to the hills, leaving Jaimal Rathore of Merta and Patta (Fatta) Sisodia of Kelwa to defend Chittor; the third saka followed on 23 February 1568.

questions.q: Maharana Pratap's coronation in 1572 took place at:
questions.exp: Pratap was crowned at Gogunda in 1572; he was born at Kumbhalgarh in 1540 and later made Chavand his capital in 1585.

questions.q: The Mughal army at the Battle of Haldighati (1576) was commanded by:
questions.exp: Man Singh I of Amber, assisted by Asaf Khan, led the Mughal force at Haldighati on 18 June 1576. Shahbaz Khan led Akbar's later campaigns against Pratap.

questions.q: Colonel James Tod described the Battle of Haldighati as the:
questions.exp: Tod called Haldighati the 'Thermopylae of Mewar'; he reserved the phrase 'Marathon of Mewar' for the Battle of Dewair (1582).

questions.q: Which Afghan commander led a contingent on Maharana Pratap's side at the Battle of Haldighati?
questions.exp: Hakim Khan Sur, a descendant of the Sur line, commanded the Afghan contingent in Pratap's army at Haldighati.

questions.q: Maharana Pratap made which place his capital in 1585?
questions.exp: After the victory at Dewair (1582), Pratap recovered much of Mewar and established his capital at Chavand in 1585, where he died in 1597.

questions.q: The Rajprashasti inscription at Rajsamand was composed by:
questions.exp: The Rajprashasti, engraved on 25 slabs at the Nauchowki of Rajsamand lake, was composed in Sanskrit by Ranchhod Bhatt and is the largest stone inscription in India.

questions.q: Jaisamand (Dhebar) lake in Mewar was constructed by:
questions.exp: Maharana Jai Singh built the Jaisamand or Dhebar lake on the Gomti river; Rajsamand was the work of his predecessor Raj Singh I.

questions.q: Saheliyon ki Bari at Udaipur was built during the reign of:
questions.exp: Sangram Singh II laid out the Saheliyon ki Bari garden at Udaipur. Jagat Singh II, his successor, presided over the Hurda Conference of 1734.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Bappa Rawal:
I. He is identified with Kalbhoj.
II. He shifted the capital of Mewar to Ahar.
III. He is credited with taking Chittor from the Mori ruler Man Mori.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Bappa Rawal is identified with Kalbhoj and took Chittor from Man Mori. The capital was shifted to Ahar much later, by Allat.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Rana Hammir:
I. He defeated Muhammad bin Tughlaq at the Battle of Singoli.
II. He was the first ruler of Mewar to use the title 'Rana'.
III. He founded the Sisodia branch of the Guhils.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Hammir replaced the older 'Rawal' style with 'Rana' and founded the Sisodia line after recovering Chittor.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Rana Kumbha:
I. He defeated Mahmud Khilji at Sarangpur in 1437.
II. He built the Kirti Stambh at Chittorgarh, dedicated to the Jain Tirthankara Adinatha.
III. He composed the Sangeet Raj.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Kirti Stambh is a 12th-century Jain tower built by the merchant Jijaji Rathore; Kumbha built the Vijay Stambh. Statements I and III are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Rana Sanga:
I. He defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Khatoli in 1517.
II. Medini Rai of Chanderi and Mahmud Lodi were among his allies at Khanwa.
III. He was killed on the battlefield of Khanwa.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Sanga survived Khanwa (17 March 1527) and died in 1528. Statements I and II are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the third saka of Chittorgarh:
I. It occurred during Akbar's siege of 1567-68.
II. The fort was defended by Jaimal of Merta and Patta of Kelwa.
III. Maharana Udai Singh II personally led the defence of the fort.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Udai Singh II withdrew to the hills before the siege closed, entrusting the fort to Jaimal and Patta. Statements I and II are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Maharana Pratap:
I. He was born at Kumbhalgarh.
II. He was crowned at Gogunda in 1572.
III. He made Chavand his capital in 1585.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Pratap was born at Kumbhalgarh in 1540, crowned at Gogunda in 1572, and shifted his seat to Chavand in 1585.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Mewar-Mughal treaty of 1615:
I. Mewar was not required to enter into matrimonial relations with the Mughals.
II. The Rana was required to attend the Mughal court in person every year.
III. Chittor was returned to Mewar on condition that it would not be repaired.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Rana was exempted from personal attendance; a prince (Karan Singh) represented Mewar at the Mughal court. Statements I and III are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Maharana Raj Singh I:
I. He built the Rajsamand lake as a famine-relief work.
II. He married Charumati, a princess of Kishangarh.
III. He gave shelter to the idol of Shrinathji at Sihad.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Raj Singh I openly defied Aurangzeb over Charumati's marriage, over jaziya, and by sheltering Shrinathji at Sihad (Nathdwara) in 1672.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Debari agreement of 1708:
I. It was concluded between Mewar, Marwar and Amber.
II. Its object was joint Rajput resistance to the Mughal emperor.
III. It provided that each signatory would accept a Mughal mansab of 5,000.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Debari agreement bound Amar Singh II of Mewar, Ajit Singh of Marwar and Sawai Jai Singh II of Amber against the Mughals; it contained no mansab clause.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Ruler)   List-II (Battle)
A. Rana Hammir   1. Khanwa
B. Rana Kumbha   2. Haldighati
C. Rana Sanga    3. Singoli
D. Maharana Pratap  4. Sarangpur
questions.exp: Hammir-Singoli (1336), Kumbha-Sarangpur (1437), Sanga-Khanwa (1527), Pratap-Haldighati (1576).

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Monument / Lake)   List-II (Builder)
A. Vijay Stambh   1. Maharana Jai Singh
B. Jagdish Temple, Udaipur  2. Rana Kumbha
C. Rajsamand Lake  3. Jagat Singh I
D. Jaisamand Lake  4. Raj Singh I
questions.exp: Vijay Stambh-Kumbha; Jagdish temple (1651)-Jagat Singh I; Rajsamand-Raj Singh I; Jaisamand-Jai Singh.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Work)   List-II (Author)
A. Sangeet Raj  1. Ranchhod Bhatt
B. Rajvallabh   2. Kanha Vyas
C. Rajprashasti 3. Rana Kumbha
D. Ekling Mahatmya  4. Mandan
questions.exp: Sangeet Raj-Kumbha; Rajvallabh-Mandan; Rajprashasti-Ranchhod Bhatt; Ekling Mahatmya-Kanha Vyas.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Event)   List-II (Mewar ruler)
A. First saka of Chittor   1. Vikramaditya
B. Second saka of Chittor  2. Rawal Ratan Singh
C. Third saka of Chittor   3. Amar Singh I
D. Treaty with Jahangir    4. Udai Singh II
questions.exp: 1303-Rawal Ratan Singh; 1535-Vikramaditya; 1567-68-Udai Singh II; 1615 treaty-Amar Singh I.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Ruler)   List-II (Capital / city)
A. Bappa Rawal  1. Udaipur
B. Allat        2. Chittor
C. Jaitrasimha  3. Nagda
D. Udai Singh II  4. Ahar
questions.exp: Bappa Rawal-Nagda; Allat-Ahar; Jaitrasimha made Chittor the capital; Udai Singh II founded Udaipur.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Mewar ruler)   List-II (Associated act)
A. Amar Singh I  1. Sheltered Prince Khurram at Jagmandir
B. Karan Singh   2. Debari agreement of 1708
C. Raj Singh I   3. Treaty with Jahangir, 1615
D. Amar Singh II 4. Open protest against Aurangzeb's jaziya
questions.exp: Amar Singh I signed the 1615 treaty; Karan Singh built Jagmandir and sheltered Khurram; Raj Singh I protested jaziya; Amar Singh II led the Debari alliance.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Khanwa (1527) was fought by Rana Sanga against Babur, long after Kumbha's death in 1468.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a work of Maharana Kumbha?
questions.exp: Prasad Mandan is an architectural treatise by Mandan, Kumbha's chief architect, not by Kumbha himself.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about Maharana Pratap is NOT correct?
opts: He recaptured Chittorgarh after the Battle of Dewair.
He was born at Kumbhalgarh in 1540.
He was crowned at Gogunda in 1572.
questions.exp: Pratap recovered most of Mewar after Dewair (1582), but Chittorgarh, Ajmer and Mandalgarh remained with the Mughals.

questions.q: Which one of the following lake-builder pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Udai Sagar - Maharana Udai Singh II
questions.exp: Pichola was built in the reign of Rana Lakha by a Banjara; Raj Singh I built the Rajsamand lake.

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT a provision of the Mewar-Mughal treaty of 1615?
opts: Chittor was to be restored but not repaired.
Mewar was to send a princess in marriage to the Mughal emperor.
The Rana was exempted from personal attendance at the Mughal court.
Mewar was to keep a contingent of 1,500 horse in Mughal service.
questions.exp: The exemption from matrimonial alliance was the treaty's most distinctive clause and the reason Mewar never gave a daughter to the Mughals.

questions.q:
Arrange the following rulers of Mewar in correct chronological order:
I. Rana Sanga
II. Rana Hammir
III. Udai Singh II
IV. Rana Kumbha
questions.exp: Hammir (1326-64), Kumbha (1433-68), Sanga (1509-28), Udai Singh II (1537-72).

questions.q:
Arrange the following battles in correct chronological order:
I. Haldighati
II. Sarangpur
III. Khanwa
IV. Singoli
questions.exp: Singoli 1336, Sarangpur 1437, Khanwa 1527, Haldighati 1576.

chapters.title: Marwar, Dhundhar, Bikaner, Jaisalmer, Hadoti & Other States
factsheet: MARWAR (Rathores): founder Rao Siha (d. 1273, Pali region); Rao Chunda obtained MANDORE and made it his capital; Rao Ranmal was killed at Chittor in 1438.
Rao Jodha founded JODHPUR and laid the foundation of MEHRANGARH fort on Chidiyatunk hill on 12 May 1459; the fort is also called Garh Chintamani and Mayurdhwaj.
Rao Bika, son of Rao Jodha, founded BIKANER in 1488 (Akshaya Tritiya) and built the Karni Mata temple at Deshnok.

Rao Maldeo (1532-62), 'Hashmat Wala Raja' of the Persian chroniclers, was defeated by Sher Shah Suri at GIRI SUMEL/SAMMEL (January 1544); his commanders Jaita and Kumpa fell; Sher Shah: 'for a handful of bajra I nearly lost the empire of Hindustan'.
Rao Chandrasen (1562-81), the 'Pratap of Marwar' / 'forgotten hero', withdrew from Akbar's NAGAUR darbar (1570) and fought on from Bhadrajun and Siwana.
Mota Raja Udai Singh (1583-95) was the first Rathore of Marwar to accept Mughal suzerainty; his daughter Jagat Gosain (Jodhabai) married Prince Salim and was the mother of Shah Jahan.
Amar Singh Rathore of Nagaur — 'Katar ka Dhani'; Battle of Matira ri Rad (Battle of the Watermelon, 1644) against Bikaner.

Maharaja Jaswant Singh I (1638-78) fought Aurangzeb at DHARMAT (1658) for Dara Shikoh and died at Jamrud (1678); his court had MUHNOT NAINSI, author of 'Nainsi ri Khyat' and 'Marwar ra Pargana ri Vigat'.
DURGADAS RATHORE — 'Redeemer of Marwar'; protected Ajit Singh for 30 years against Aurangzeb; his chhatri is at Ujjain on the Shipra.
Khejarli sacrifice, 1730 (reign of Abhay Singh): Amrita Devi Bishnoi and 363 people died protecting khejri trees; the Amrita Devi Bishnoi Wildlife Protection Award is named after her.

Maharaja Man Singh of Jodhpur (1803-43) patronised the NATH sect and built the Mahamandir; Battle of Gingoli (1807) arose from the Krishna Kumari dispute. Maharaja Umaid Singh built UMAID BHAWAN palace (begun 1929).
AMBER-JAIPUR (Kachhwahas): founder Dulha Rai (c. 1137, Dausa); Kokil Dev shifted the capital to AMBER.
Raja Bharmal of Amber was the first Rajput ruler to ally with Akbar; his daughter Harkha Bai married Akbar in 1562 at Sambhar.

Raja MAN SINGH I held the highest mansab of 7,000 under Akbar, was governor of Kabul, Bihar and Bengal, commanded at Haldighati (1576), built the Amber palace, brought the SHILA DEVI idol from Bengal and built the Govind Dev temple at Vrindavan.

MIRZA RAJA JAI SINGH I signed the TREATY OF PURANDAR with Shivaji on 11 June 1665 (Shivaji surrendered 23 of 35 forts); his court poet was Bihari, author of 'Bihari Satsai'; he died at Burhanpur in 1667.

SAWAI JAI SINGH II (1700-43) received the title 'Sawai' from Aurangzeb; founded JAIPUR on 18 November 1727 to the plan of VIDYADHAR BHATTACHARYA; built five Jantar Mantars (Jaipur, Delhi, Ujjain, Mathura, Varanasi); wrote 'Zij-i-Muhammad Shahi'; built Nahargarh; Jaipur is a UNESCO World Heritage City (2019).
Sawai Ishwari Singh won the Battle of Rajmahal (1747) and built the ISAR LAT (Sargasuli); he lost Bagru (1748) and died in 1750. Madho Singh I founded Sawai Madhopur (1763).
Sawai Pratap Singh built HAWA MAHAL (1799), architect Lal Chand Ustad, 953 jharokhas; he wrote poetry under the pen-name 'Brajnidhi'; Battle of Tunga (1787) against the Marathas.

Sawai Ram Singh II (1835-80) had Jaipur painted pink for the Prince of Wales (1876), built Albert Hall and Ram Prakash Theatre, founded Maharaja College and Rajasthan's first girls' school. Man Singh II was the last ruler and the first Rajpramukh of Rajasthan.

BIKANER: Rai Singh (1574-1612) built JUNAGARH fort (1589-94); Karan Singh received the title 'Jangaldhar Badshah'; Anup Singh founded the ANUP SANSKRIT LIBRARY; Surat Singh captured Bhatner in 1805 and renamed it Hanumangarh.

Maharaja GANGA SINGH (1887-1943), 'Bhagirath of Rajasthan' — Gang Canal (opened 1927), Ganga Risala camel corps, member of the Imperial War Cabinet, signatory at Versailles (1919), first Chancellor of the Chamber of Princes.

JAISALMER (Bhatis): Rawal Jaisal shifted the capital from LODRAVA and founded Jaisalmer; three sakas — first under Mulraj/Ratan Singh vs Alauddin Khilji, second vs Firoz Shah Tughlaq, third ('ardh saka', c. 1550) under Rawal Lunkaran, in which jauhar could not be completed.

HADOTI: Rao Deva founded BUNDI in 1241 after defeating the Meena chief Jaita; Rao Surjan Singh surrendered RANTHAMBORE to Akbar in 1569; Rao Ratan Singh received the title 'Sarbuland Rai' from Jahangir; Rao Chhatrasal built the Chhatra Mahal and fell at Samugarh (1658); Rao Umed Singh built the Chitrashala.

KOTA was separated from Bundi in 1631 by Shah Jahan for Rao Madho Singh; Zalim Singh Jhala, the great administrator of Kota, won the Battle of BHATWARA (1761) against Jaipur; Jhalawar was carved out of Kota in 1838 for Jhala Madan Singh — the last princely state created in Rajputana.
GAGRON fort (Jhalawar), at the confluence of the Ahu and Kali Sindh, is the classic JAL-DURG of Rajasthan; Achaldas Khichi died defending it against Hoshang Shah of Malwa.
BHARATPUR (Jats, Sinsinwar): Churaman and Badan Singh laid the foundations; Maharaja SURAJ MAL (d. 25 Dec 1763), the 'Plato of the Jat community', built LOHAGARH fort and the Deeg palaces.

ALWAR was founded on 25 December 1775 by Rao Raja Pratap Singh Naruka, a Kachhwaha offshoot; Bala Qila is its fort; Bakhtawar Singh signed the treaty with Wellesley in 1803 after the Battle of Laswari.

TONK, founded in 1817 by the Pindari leader Amir Khan, was the ONLY Muslim princely state of Rajputana. Karauli was Yaduvanshi (Jadaun), Sirohi Deora Chauhan, Dungarpur/Banswara/Pratapgarh Guhil (Vagad branch).
Sirohi city was founded by Rao Sahastramal in 1425 (his father Rao Sobha founded Shivpuri in 1405); SIROHI was the LAST Rajputana state to sign a treaty with the British (1823).

SHEKHAWATI takes its name from Rao Shekha (1433-88), a Kachhwaha of Amarsar; KISHANGARH was founded by Kishan Singh, son of Mota Raja Udai Singh of Jodhpur, and produced Savant Singh (Nagari Das) and the Bani Thani.

questions.q: The founder of the Rathore dynasty of Marwar was:
questions.exp: Rao Siha, who settled in the Pali region and died in 1273, is regarded as the progenitor of the Rathores of Marwar.

questions.q: Which Rathore ruler obtained Mandore and made it the capital of Marwar?
questions.exp: Rao Chunda acquired Mandore and shifted his seat there; Mandore remained the Rathore capital until Rao Jodha founded Jodhpur in 1459.

questions.q: Jodhpur city and the Mehrangarh fort were founded in 1459 by:
questions.exp: Rao Jodha laid the foundation of Jodhpur and Mehrangarh on 12 May 1459, shifting the capital from Mandore.

questions.q: The Battle of Giri Sumel (1544) was fought between Sher Shah Suri and:
questions.exp: Sher Shah defeated Rao Maldeo of Marwar at Giri Sumel; Maldeo's commanders Jaita and Kumpa fell in the battle.

questions.q: Rao Chandrasen of Marwar carried on his resistance to Akbar chiefly from which strongholds?
questions.exp: Driven out of Jodhpur, Chandrasen made Bhadrajun and later Siwana his bases and fought on until his death in 1581; Akbar then declared Marwar khalsa.

questions.q: The first Rathore ruler of Marwar to accept Mughal suzerainty was:
questions.exp: Mota Raja Udai Singh accepted Mughal service in 1583; his daughter Jagat Gosain married Prince Salim and became the mother of Shah Jahan.

questions.q: Maharaja Jaswant Singh I of Marwar fought against Aurangzeb on behalf of Dara Shikoh in the Battle of:
questions.exp: Jaswant Singh I was defeated at Dharmat in 1658. He later died at Jamrud in 1678, triggering the Marwar succession crisis.

questions.q: After a struggle of nearly thirty years, who was finally recognised as the ruler of Marwar in 1708?
questions.exp: Ajit Singh, the posthumous son of Jaswant Singh I, recovered Jodhpur in 1708; he was murdered by his son Bakht Singh in 1724.

questions.q: Muhnot Nainsi, author of 'Marwar ra Pargana ri Vigat', was a minister in the court of:
questions.exp: Muhnot Nainsi served Jaswant Singh I; his 'Nainsi ri Khyat' and 'Vigat' are the earliest systematic Rajasthani historical chronicles.

questions.q: Maharaja Man Singh of Jodhpur (1803-43), who built the Mahamandir, was a patron of which sect?
questions.exp: Man Singh became a devotee of the Nath yogis and built the Mahamandir at Jodhpur as the sect's centre; he also founded the Man Pustakalaya.

questions.q: The Umaid Bhawan Palace at Jodhpur was built during the reign of:
questions.exp: Construction of Umaid Bhawan began in 1929 as a famine-relief project under Maharaja Umaid Singh.

questions.q: The founder of the Kachhwaha state of Dhundhar was:
questions.exp: Dulha Rai established Kachhwaha power near Dausa in the 12th century; his successor Kokil Dev shifted the capital to Amber.

questions.q: The first Rajput ruler to enter into a matrimonial alliance with Emperor Akbar in 1562 was:
opts: Mota Raja Udai Singh of Marwar
questions.exp: Bharmal gave his daughter Harkha Bai in marriage to Akbar at Sambhar in 1562, beginning the Mughal-Kachhwaha alliance.

questions.q: Raja Man Singh I of Amber brought the idol of Shila Devi, installed at Amber, from:
questions.exp: Man Singh I brought the Shila Devi idol from Jessore in Bengal during his campaigns as governor; he also built the Govind Dev temple at Vrindavan.

questions.q: The Treaty of Purandar (1665) with Shivaji was negotiated on the Mughal side by:
questions.exp: Mirza Raja Jai Singh I of Amber concluded the Treaty of Purandar on 11 June 1665, under which Shivaji surrendered 23 of his 35 forts.

questions.q: The poet Bihari, author of the 'Bihari Satsai', adorned the court of:
questions.exp: Bihari composed the Satsai in the court of Mirza Raja Jai Singh I of Amber.

questions.q: The plan of the city of Jaipur, founded in 1727, was prepared by:
questions.exp: Sawai Jai Singh II founded Jaipur on 18 November 1727 on a grid plan drawn by Vidyadhar Bhattacharya; Jaipur became a UNESCO World Heritage City in 2019.

questions.q: The astronomical table 'Zij-i-Muhammad Shahi' was prepared under the patronage of:
questions.exp: Sawai Jai Singh II compiled the Zij-i-Muhammad Shahi, dedicated to Emperor Muhammad Shah, and built five Jantar Mantar observatories.

questions.q: The Hawa Mahal at Jaipur was built in 1799 by:
questions.exp: Sawai Pratap Singh built the Hawa Mahal to a design by Lal Chand Ustad; it has 953 jharokhas and is shaped like Krishna's crown.

questions.q: Jaipur was painted pink in 1876 by Sawai Ram Singh II to welcome:
questions.exp: Ram Singh II had the city washed in terracotta pink for the visit of the Prince of Wales (later Edward VII), giving Jaipur the name 'Pink City'.

questions.q: Bikaner was founded in 1488 by:
questions.exp: Rao Bika, a son of Rao Jodha of Jodhpur, founded Bikaner in 1488 and built the Karni Mata temple at Deshnok.

questions.q: The Junagarh fort at Bikaner was built by:
questions.exp: Raja Rai Singh, a general of Akbar, built Junagarh between 1589 and 1594; unlike most Rajasthan forts it stands on level ground.

questions.q: The Anup Sanskrit Library at Bikaner was founded by:
questions.exp: Anup Singh (1669-98), a scholar-ruler and general in the Deccan, assembled the Anup Sanskrit Library; his reign is the golden age of Bikaner painting.

questions.q: The Gang Canal, opened in 1927, was the achievement of which ruler?
opts: Maharaja Man Singh II of Jaipur
questions.exp: Ganga Singh, the 'Bhagirath of Rajasthan', brought Sutlej water to Bikaner through the Gang Canal, Rajasthan's oldest canal system.

questions.q: Rawal Jaisal founded Jaisalmer after shifting his capital from:
questions.exp: Rawal Jaisal abandoned Lodrava, which lay exposed to invasion, and built a new fort on the Trikuta hill at Jaisalmer.

questions.q: Bundi was founded in 1241 by which Hada Chauhan ruler?
questions.exp: Rao Deva took Bundi from the Meena chief Jaita in 1241 and named the surrounding tract Haravati (Hadoti).

questions.q: Kota became a separate princely state in 1631 when Shah Jahan recognised as its ruler:
questions.exp: Kota was detached from Bundi in 1631 in favour of Rao Madho Singh, a son of Rao Ratan Singh of Bundi.

questions.q: In the Battle of Bhatwara (1761), the forces of Kota under Zalim Singh Jhala defeated the ruler of:
questions.exp: Zalim Singh Jhala's victory at Bhatwara over Sawai Madho Singh I of Jaipur, in a dispute over Ranthambore, established his ascendancy in Kota.

questions.q: The Lohagarh fort of Bharatpur was built by:
questions.exp: Suraj Mal built Lohagarh, the 'iron fort', which withstood Lord Lake's siege in 1805. He is called the 'Plato of the Jat community'.

questions.q: Which was the only Muslim princely state of Rajputana, founded in 1817?
questions.exp: Tonk was created for the Pindari leader Amir Khan when he submitted to the British in 1817; it was the only Muslim-ruled state of Rajputana.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Rao Maldeo of Marwar:
I. Persian chroniclers described him as 'Hashmat Wala Raja'.
II. He was defeated by Sher Shah Suri at Giri Sumel in 1544.
III. His commanders Jaita and Kumpa died fighting in that battle.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. After the battle Sher Shah's general Khawas Khan occupied Jodhpur; Maldeo recovered his territories by 1545-46.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Rao Chandrasen:
I. He withdrew from Akbar's Nagaur darbar of 1570 rather than accept Mughal suzerainty.
II. He is known as the 'Pratap of Marwar'.
III. He founded the city of Jodhpur.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Jodhpur was founded by Rao Jodha in 1459, long before Chandrasen. Statements I and II are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Durgadas Rathore:
I. He protected Ajit Singh, the posthumous son of Jaswant Singh I.
II. He obtained shelter for Ajit Singh from Raj Singh I of Mewar.
III. His cenotaph stands at Ujjain on the bank of the Shipra.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Durgadas's thirty-year struggle ended with the Debari agreement and Ajit Singh's restoration in 1708.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Raja Man Singh I of Amber:
I. He held the highest mansab of 7,000 under Akbar.
II. He served as governor of Bengal and Bihar.
III. He commanded the Mughal army at the Battle of Khanwa.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Khanwa was fought in 1527, before Man Singh's birth; he commanded at Haldighati in 1576. Statements I and II are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Sawai Jai Singh II:
I. He founded Jaipur on 18 November 1727.
II. He built observatories at Jaipur, Delhi, Ujjain, Mathura and Varanasi.
III. He received the title 'Sawai' from Emperor Shah Jahan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The title 'Sawai' was conferred by Aurangzeb. Statements I and II are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the rulers of Bikaner:
I. Raja Rai Singh served as a general of Akbar.
II. Karan Singh received the title 'Jangaldhar Badshah'.
III. Surat Singh captured Bhatner in 1805 and renamed it Hanumangarh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Bikaner's rulers served the Mughals from Rai Singh's time; Bhatner was taken from the Bhattis on a Tuesday and renamed Hanumangarh.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Jaisalmer:
I. Rawal Jaisal shifted his capital from Lodrava to Jaisalmer.
II. The third saka of Jaisalmer, under Rawal Lunkaran, is called an 'ardh saka' because the jauhar could not be completed.
III. The Jaisalmer fort is classified as a jal-durg.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Jaisalmer fort stands on the Trikuta hill and is a giri-durg (also described as a dhanva-durg because of the surrounding desert); Gagron is the classic jal-durg.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Hadoti:
I. Bundi was founded by Rao Deva in 1241 after defeating the Meena chief Jaita.
II. Rao Surjan Singh surrendered Ranthambore to Akbar in 1569.
III. Kota was separated from Bundi by Emperor Jahangir.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Kota was made a separate state by Shah Jahan in 1631 for Rao Madho Singh. Statements I and II are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Bharatpur:
I. Its rulers belonged to the Sinsinwar Jat clan.
II. Maharaja Suraj Mal was killed near Delhi in 1763.
III. The palaces of Deeg were begun by Badan Singh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Suraj Mal died on 25 December 1763 and Bharatpur was the strongest Jat power of 18th-century north India.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Alwar state was founded by Rao Raja Pratap Singh Naruka in 1775.
II. The Narukas were an offshoot of the Kachhwahas of Amber.
III. Sirohi was the first Rajputana state to sign a subsidiary treaty with the British.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Sirohi was the LAST Rajputana state to enter into treaty relations with the British, in 1823. Statements I and II are correct.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

A. Rao Jodha   1. Bundi
B. Rao Bika    2. Shekhawati
C. Rao Shekha  3. Jodhpur
D. Rao Deva    4. Bikaner
questions.exp: Rao Jodha-Jodhpur (1459); Rao Bika-Bikaner (1488); Rao Shekha-Shekhawati (Amarsar); Rao Deva-Bundi (1241).

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

B. Junagarh    2. Rao Jodha
C. Lohagarh    3. Sawai Jai Singh II
D. Nahargarh   4. Raja Rai Singh
questions.exp: Mehrangarh-Rao Jodha; Junagarh-Rai Singh; Lohagarh-Suraj Mal; Nahargarh-Sawai Jai Singh II.

questions.q:

questions.exp: Giri Sumel 1544; Bhatwara 1761; Tunga 1787; Gingoli 1807.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Personality)   List-II (Epithet)
A. Rao Maldeo   1. Plato of the Jat community
B. Rao Chandrasen  2. Redeemer of Marwar
C. Durgadas Rathore  3. Hashmat Wala Raja
D. Maharaja Suraj Mal  4. Pratap of Marwar
questions.exp: Maldeo-Hashmat Wala Raja; Chandrasen-Pratap of Marwar; Durgadas-Redeemer of Marwar; Suraj Mal-Plato of the Jat community.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Kachhwaha ruler)   List-II (Monument)
A. Man Singh I   1. Jantar Mantar, Jaipur
B. Sawai Jai Singh II  2. Amber Palace
C. Sawai Ishwari Singh  3. Hawa Mahal
D. Sawai Pratap Singh   4. Isar Lat (Sargasuli)
questions.exp: Man Singh I-Amber Palace; Sawai Jai Singh II-Jantar Mantar; Ishwari Singh-Isar Lat (after Rajmahal, 1747); Pratap Singh-Hawa Mahal (1799).

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Princely state)   List-II (Ruling clan)
A. Jaisalmer  1. Deora Chauhan
B. Karauli    2. Jat (Sinsinwar)
C. Sirohi     3. Bhati
D. Bharatpur  4. Yaduvanshi (Jadaun)
questions.exp: Jaisalmer-Bhati; Karauli-Yaduvanshi Jadaun; Sirohi-Deora Chauhan; Bharatpur-Sinsinwar Jat.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Scholar / poet)   List-II (Patron)
A. Muhnot Nainsi  1. Mirza Raja Jai Singh I
B. Bihari         2. Maharaja Abhay Singh
C. Dayaldas       3. Maharaja Jaswant Singh I
D. Karnidan       4. Maharaja Ratan Singh of Bikaner
questions.exp: Nainsi served Jaswant Singh I; Bihari, Mirza Raja Jai Singh I; Dayaldas wrote 'Bikaner ra Rathoran ri Khyat' under Ratan Singh; Karnidan wrote 'Suraj Prakash' under Abhay Singh.

questions.q: Which one of the following state-founder pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Alwar was founded in 1775 by Rao Raja Pratap Singh Naruka; Bakhtawar Singh was his successor, who signed the treaty with the British in 1803.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about Rao Jodha is NOT correct?
opts: He laid the foundation of the Mehrangarh fort.
He shifted the Rathore capital from Mandore.
He founded the city of Bikaner in 1488.
questions.exp: Bikaner was founded by his son Rao Bika in 1488, not by Rao Jodha himself.

questions.q: Which one of the following ruler-battle pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Rao Maldeo - Battle of Giri Sumel
Jaswant Singh I - Battle of Dharmat
Zalim Singh Jhala - Battle of Bhatwara
questions.exp: Marwar's contingent at Khanwa (1527) was sent by Rao Ganga; Maldeo ruled from 1532.

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT a ruler of Amber or Jaipur?
questions.exp: Rao Surjan Singh was the Hada Chauhan ruler of Bundi who surrendered Ranthambore to Akbar in 1569.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about Maharaja Ganga Singh of Bikaner is NOT correct?
opts: He built the Gang Canal, opened in 1927.
He was the first Rajpramukh of Rajasthan.
He was a member of the Imperial War Cabinet during the First World War.
He raised the Ganga Risala camel corps.
questions.exp: The first Rajpramukh of Rajasthan was Sawai Man Singh II of Jaipur. Ganga Singh died in 1943, before integration.

questions.q: Which one of the following princely state-ruling clan pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Kota, carved out of Bundi in 1631, was ruled by the Hada Chauhans like its parent state.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in the chronological order of their foundation:
I. Bikaner
II. Jodhpur
III. Jaipur
IV. Bundi
questions.exp: Bundi 1241, Jodhpur 1459, Bikaner 1488, Jaipur 1727.

questions.q:
Arrange the following battles in correct chronological order:
I. Bhatwara
II. Giri Sumel
III. Tunga
IV. Dharmat
questions.exp: Giri Sumel 1544, Dharmat 1658, Bhatwara 1761, Tunga 1787.

chapters.title: Rajasthan & the Mughals; Medieval Administration and Revenue System
factsheet: Babur defeated Rana Sanga's Rajput confederacy at KHANWA (17 March 1527); Sanga's allies included Medini Rai of Chanderi, Rao Ganga of Marwar's contingent and the Afghan claimant Mahmud Lodi.
Akbar's Rajput policy began in 1562 with Raja BHARMAL of Amber, the first Rajput chief to accept Mughal service and to give a daughter (Harkha Bai) in marriage — the wedding took place at Sambhar.
Akbar besieged CHITTOR 23 Oct 1567 - 23 Feb 1568; Jaimal of Merta and Patta of Kelwa fell; Akbar later set up their statues at the gate of Agra Fort.
RANTHAMBORE was surrendered to Akbar in 1569 by Rao Surjan Singh Hada of Bundi, who received the title 'Rao Raja'; Kalinjar followed in the same year.
Akbar's NAGAUR darbar (1570) drew the submission of Bikaner and Jaisalmer; Rao Chandrasen of Marwar withdrew rather than submit.
MEWAR alone among the major Rajput states never gave a daughter in marriage to the Mughals.

Jahangir concluded the MEWAR TREATY OF 1615 with Maharana Amar Singh I, negotiated by Prince Khurram: Chittor restored but not to be repaired; no matrimonial alliance; Prince Karan Singh to attend the imperial court in place of the Rana; 1,500 horse to be supplied.

Mota Raja Udai Singh of Marwar (1583) and his daughter Jagat Gosain (mother of Shah Jahan) mark the Rathore entry into the Mughal system; the last Rajput-Mughal marriage was Ajit Singh's daughter to Farrukhsiyar (1715).
AURANGZEB reimposed the JAZIYA in 1679; the Marwar succession dispute after Jaswant Singh I's death (1678) triggered the RAJPUT WAR of 1679-81 involving Marwar and Mewar.
Prince Akbar, Aurangzeb's son, rebelled with Rajput support in 1681 and fled to the Marathas; Durgadas Rathore escorted his children.
Aurangzeb's Rajasthan war ended with a treaty with Mewar's Jai Singh in 1681; Marwar's struggle continued until Ajit Singh's restoration (1708) and the DEBARI agreement.

Akbar created the SUBAH OF AJMER in 1580 as one of the twelve original subahs; it had SEVEN sarkars (Ajmer, Jodhpur, Chittor, Ranthambore, Nagaur, Sirohi, Bikaner) and roughly covered modern Rajasthan; parts of eastern Rajasthan lay in Agra and Delhi subahs.
MANSABDARI: ZAT fixed personal rank, status and salary; SAWAR fixed the cavalry contingent to be maintained. Mansabs were neither hereditary nor transferable.
DAGH = branding of horses; CHEHRA (huliya) = descriptive roll of soldiers — enforced by Akbar to stop fraud in musters. Du-aspa/sih-aspa allowed extra troopers without raising zat.
Man Singh I of Amber held the highest Rajput mansab under Akbar (7,000); watan jagirs left Rajput chiefs in possession of their homelands.

LAND CATEGORIES in medieval Rajasthan: KHALSA (direct state control), JAGIR (assigned to nobles for service), BHOM (hereditary, tax-free, held by Bhomias for local defence/police duty), SASAN/DHARMARTH (tax-free religious grant), DOLI (small tax-free charitable grant), INAM (reward grant).
ADMINISTRATIVE UNITS: state - sarkar/pargana - tapa/hawala - village (gaon/mauza). The pargana was the key revenue unit.

CENTRAL OFFICIALS: Pradhan (prime minister), Diwan (revenue and finance), Bakshi (military department, pay and muster), Khan-i-Saman (stores), Kotwal (law and order, prices and weights in towns), Khajanchi (treasury), Dyodhidar (palace security), Waqia-navis (news writer).

PARGANA OFFICIALS: Hakim (head of the pargana, administrative and judicial), Amil/Amalguzar (revenue collection), Faujdar (police and military), Potdar (accounts), Khufia-navis (secret reports); assisted by Kanungo and Chaudhary.
VILLAGE OFFICIALS: Patwari (land records and revenue), Chaudhary/Muqaddam (headman), Talwati (weighing and measuring produce), Kanwari (crop protection).
BATAI (bhag-batai) = crop-sharing, the state's share usually one-third. Its two forms: LATTA/LATA — the harvested crop is cut and divided; KUNTA — the STANDING crop is appraised before harvest.

OTHER ASSESSMENTS: Bighori/Beghodi (cash rate per bigha by soil fertility), Muqata/Mukata (fixed lump-sum), Dori (assessment by measurement with a rope), Ghughri (share based on seed sown), HAL/HALIBAKSHI (assessment per plough, roughly 15-30 bighas), Kankut (estimate of grain), ZABTI (Akbar's measurement-based cash system under Todar Mal).
BHAICHARA = joint/village-brotherhood assessment in which the community shared the revenue burden.

LAG-BAG = the cesses and customary levies beyond land revenue (e.g. Nyauta lag, Chanwari lag on daughters' weddings, Ghar-ginti house tax). BETHBEGAR = unpaid forced labour exacted from peasants and artisans.

OTHER REVENUE TERMS: Udrang (fixed share from hereditary holders), Bhag (state's share of produce), Hiranya (state's share taken in cash), Dastoor (illegal exaction by revenue staff), Barani (unirrigated land).
FEUDAL RANKS: Mewar - Solah (16) Umrao, Battis (32) Sardar, and Gol; Marwar - Rajvi, Sardar, Ganayat, Mutsaddi; Jaipur - the Barah (12) Kotri, headed by the Rajawat.

MILITARY: Pyade (infantry); cavalry graded Yak-aspa, Du-aspa, Sih-aspa and Nim-aspa; Bargir (state-equipped) vs Siledar (self-equipped); Ahadi = the ruler's own standing troops, Jamiyat = a noble's contingent.
RECORD SERIES of the Rajput states: Bahi-khata records such as Hakikat Bahi, Kamthana Bahi and Pattas/Parwanas; Muhnot Nainsi's 'Marwar ra Pargana ri Vigat' is the classic revenue gazetteer.

questions.q: Which Afghan claimant to the throne of Delhi fought on Rana Sanga's side at the Battle of Khanwa?
questions.exp: Mahmud Lodi, a brother of Ibrahim Lodi, joined the Rajput confederacy at Khanwa (1527) along with Hasan Khan Mewati and Medini Rai of Chanderi.

questions.q: Akbar's marriage with Harkha Bai, the daughter of Raja Bharmal, took place in 1562 at:
questions.exp: The marriage that opened Mughal-Rajput matrimonial relations was solemnised at Sambhar in 1562, while Akbar was returning from his pilgrimage to Ajmer.

questions.q: Ranthambore was surrendered to Akbar in 1569 by:
questions.exp: Rao Surjan Singh of Bundi handed over Ranthambore to Akbar in 1569 and received the title 'Rao Raja' with a jagir in the Banaras region.

questions.q: After the fall of Chittor in 1568, Akbar had statues of Jaimal and Patta erected at the gate of:
questions.exp: Abul Fazl records that stone elephants bearing the statues of the two defenders were placed outside the gate of Agra Fort in recognition of their valour.

questions.q: Which major Rajput state never entered into a matrimonial alliance with the Mughals?
questions.exp: The Sisodias of Mewar refused matrimonial ties throughout; the exemption was formally written into the treaty of 1615.

questions.q: The Mewar-Mughal treaty of 1615 was concluded during the reign of the Mughal emperor:
questions.exp: Jahangir authorised the settlement with Maharana Amar Singh I; his son Prince Khurram (later Shah Jahan) conducted the negotiations.

questions.q: Under the terms of the 1615 treaty, who was sent to attend the Mughal court on behalf of Mewar?
questions.exp: The Rana was excused personal attendance; the heir apparent Karan Singh represented Mewar at the imperial court.

questions.q: Aurangzeb reimposed the jaziya on non-Muslims in the year:
questions.exp: The reimposition of jaziya in 1679, coinciding with the Marwar succession crisis, precipitated the Rajput war of 1679-81.

questions.q: Which son of Aurangzeb rebelled in 1681 with Rajput support and later fled to the Marathas?
questions.exp: Prince Akbar, aided by Durgadas Rathore and the Mewar-Marwar alliance, proclaimed himself emperor in 1681 but was outmanoeuvred and fled to the Deccan.

questions.q: The subah of Ajmer, which covered most of present-day Rajasthan, was created by Akbar in:
questions.exp: Ajmer was one of the twelve original subahs of Akbar's administrative reorganisation of 1580 and comprised seven sarkars.

questions.q: In the Mughal mansabdari system, the rank denoting a noble's personal status and pay was called:
questions.exp: Zat fixed personal rank, precedence and salary, while sawar fixed the size of the cavalry contingent to be maintained.

questions.q: In the Mughal military system, 'dagh' referred to:
opts: the cash salary of a mansabdar
questions.exp: Dagh was the branding of cavalry horses with the imperial mark; chehra was the descriptive roll of the soldier. Both were enforced by Akbar to prevent fraudulent musters.

questions.q: 'Chehra' in the Mughal and Rajput military systems meant:
opts: the branding mark on a horse
the descriptive roll of a soldier
a cavalry grade with two horses
the pay certificate of a mansabdar
questions.exp: Chehra (huliya) recorded a soldier's physical description so that substitutes could not be presented at inspections.

questions.q: In medieval Rajasthan, 'Khalsa' land meant land which was:
opts: assigned to nobles for military service
held by Bhomias in return for local defence
under the direct control of the state
questions.exp: Khalsa was crown land whose revenue went straight to the state treasury, as opposed to jagir land assigned to nobles.

questions.q: In the administrative structure of the Rajput states of Rajasthan, the principal revenue unit comprising a group of villages was the:
questions.exp: The pargana was the key unit of revenue administration, headed by the Hakim and served by the Amil, Faujdar and Potdar; several parganas made a sarkar.

questions.q: In the feudal order of Mewar, the highest class of nobles was known as the:
questions.exp: Mewar's nobility was graded as the Solah Umrao, the Battis Sardar and the Gol; Jaipur had the Barah (twelve) Kotri and Marwar the Rajvi, Sardar and Ganayat classes.

questions.q: In the Batai system of medieval Rajasthan, the state's share of the produce was usually:
questions.exp: Under batai (crop-sharing) the state normally took about one-third of the harvest, the cultivator retaining the rest.

questions.q: The 'Halibakshi' (Hal) system of revenue assessment in medieval Rajasthan levied the demand on the basis of:
opts: the number of wells in the holding
the number of ploughs used by the cultivator
questions.exp: Under the Hal or Halibakshi system the unit of assessment was the plough, reckoned at roughly 15-30 bighas of land.

questions.q: The practice of 'Bethbegar' in medieval Rajasthan referred to:
opts: unpaid forced labour exacted from peasants and artisans
a cess levied on marriages in the peasant's family
the branding of cattle for revenue records
the transfer of a jagir on the holder's death
questions.exp: Bethbegar (begar) obliged villagers to render labour without wages to the state or the jagirdar; it was among the most resented feudal burdens.

questions.q: The highest-ranking official of a pargana in the Rajput states was the:
questions.exp: The Hakim headed the pargana in both administrative and judicial matters; the Amil looked after revenue collection under him.

questions.q: The village-level official responsible for maintaining land records in medieval Rajasthan was the:
questions.exp: The Patwari kept the village land records and assisted in collection; the Kotwal's charge was law and order in towns.

questions.q: 'Lag-Bag' in the revenue system of the Rajput states referred to:
opts: additional cesses and customary levies beyond the land revenue
the share of the crop taken by the state
grants of tax-free land to temples
the cavalry contingent maintained by a jagirdar
questions.exp: Lag-bag covered a wide range of extra exactions such as nyauta lag and chanwari lag levied on the peasantry for the ruler's or noble's family occasions.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Raja Bharmal of Amber accepted Mughal suzerainty in 1562.
II. Rao Chandrasen of Marwar was the first Rathore ruler to accept Mughal suzerainty.
III. Akbar captured Chittor in 1568 and Ranthambore in 1569.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Rao Chandrasen resisted the Mughals to the end; the first Rathore of Marwar to submit was Mota Raja Udai Singh in 1583.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Akbar's Nagaur darbar of 1570:
I. It was held to receive the submission of the Rajput chiefs of western Rajasthan.
II. Rai Singh of Bikaner accepted Mughal suzerainty there.
III. Rao Chandrasen of Marwar accepted a mansab of 5,000 at this darbar.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Chandrasen attended but withdrew without submitting, and Marwar was later declared khalsa. Statements I and II are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Aurangzeb's relations with the Rajputs:
I. He reimposed the jaziya in 1679.
II. The dispute over the Marwar succession after Jaswant Singh I's death led to the Rajput war.
III. Maharana Raj Singh I of Mewar gave shelter to the infant Ajit Singh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Rathore-Sisodia alliance of 1679-81 was the sharpest Rajput challenge to Mughal authority in Rajasthan.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the mansabdari system:
I. Zat determined the personal rank and salary of a mansabdar.
II. Sawar determined the number of cavalrymen he had to maintain.
III. Mansabs were hereditary and passed automatically to the holder's son.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Mansabs were neither hereditary nor transferable; on a mansabdar's death the rank lapsed to the emperor. Statements I and II are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about revenue assessment in medieval Rajasthan:
I. Under the Latta method the harvested crop was divided after it was cut.
II. Under the Kunta method the standing crop was appraised before harvest.
III. Both were varieties of the Batai system.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Latta-Kunta together formed the crop-sharing (batai) family of assessments.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about land categories in medieval Rajasthan:
I. Jagir land was assigned to nobles for military or administrative service.
II. Bhom land was hereditary and tax-free, held in return for local service.
III. Doli was land granted to nobles in lieu of a cavalry contingent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Doli was a small tax-free charitable grant, often made to Brahmins, Charans or for religious merit. Statements I and II are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about officials in the Rajput states:
I. The Bakshi headed the military department and supervised pay and musters.
II. The Kotwal maintained law and order and regulated prices and weights in towns.
III. The Patwari was the head of the pargana administration.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The pargana was headed by the Hakim; the Patwari worked at the village level. Statements I and II are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Mewar-Mughal settlement of 1615:
I. Amar Singh I was the first Mewar ruler to accept Mughal suzerainty.
II. Mewar was exempted from matrimonial alliance with the Mughals.
III. Chittor was restored to Mewar with permission to refortify it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Chittor was returned on the express condition that its defences would never be repaired. Statements I and II are correct.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Land category)   List-II (Meaning)
A. Khalsa  1. Hereditary tax-free land held for local service
B. Jagir   2. Land under the direct control of the state
C. Sasan   3. Assignment to a noble for service
D. Bhom    4. Tax-free grant for religious purposes
questions.exp: Khalsa-state land; Jagir-service assignment; Sasan-religious grant; Bhom-hereditary tax-free land of the Bhomias.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Official)   List-II (Function)
A. Hakim   1. Head of the pargana
B. Amil    2. Law and order in towns
C. Kotwal  3. Village land records
D. Patwari 4. Collection of land revenue
questions.exp: Hakim headed the pargana, Amil collected revenue, Kotwal kept order in towns, Patwari maintained village records.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Revenue method)   List-II (Basis of assessment)
A. Latta   1. Fixed lump-sum cash payment
B. Kunta   2. Division of the harvested crop
C. Bighori 3. Appraisal of the standing crop
D. Muqata  4. Cash rate levied per bigha
questions.exp: Latta-division of the cut crop; Kunta-appraisal of standing crop; Bighori-rate per bigha; Muqata-fixed lump sum.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Event)   List-II (Year)
A. Fall of Chittor to Akbar   1. 1679
B. Surrender of Ranthambore   2. 1615
C. Mewar-Mughal treaty        3. 1568
D. Reimposition of jaziya     4. 1569
questions.exp: Chittor 1568; Ranthambore 1569; Mewar treaty 1615; jaziya reimposed 1679.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of medieval Rajasthani terms and their meanings is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Bethbegar - a cess levied on peasant marriages
Khalsa - land under direct state control
Bhom - hereditary tax-free land for local service
Lag-Bag - additional cesses beyond land revenue
questions.exp: Bethbegar was unpaid forced labour; the marriage cess was the chanwari lag, one of the lag-bag exactions.

questions.q: Which one of the following officials was NOT connected with pargana administration?
questions.exp: The Dyodhidar was a palace official responsible for the security of and access to the royal apartments.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of a Mughal emperor and an event in Rajasthan is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Shah Jahan - Treaty with Maharana Amar Singh I of Mewar
Jahangir - Restoration of Chittor to Mewar
questions.exp: The 1615 treaty was concluded by Jahangir, though it was negotiated by Prince Khurram, who only later became Shah Jahan.

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT a category of landholding in medieval Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Iqta was a revenue assignment of the Delhi Sultanate, not a category used in the Rajput states of Rajasthan.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about medieval Rajasthan's revenue system is NOT correct?
opts: Under Batai the state took roughly one-third of the produce.
Halibakshi assessed revenue on the basis of the plough.
Bhaichara assessment made the village community jointly responsible.
Under the Zabti system the revenue was fixed as a share of the standing crop.
questions.exp: Zabti (Akbar's system, developed by Todar Mal) fixed cash rates on measured land using average yields and prices, not a share of the standing crop; that was kunta.

questions.q:
Consider the following statement of Assertion (A) and Reason (R):
Assertion (A): Maharana Amar Singh I concluded a treaty with Jahangir in 1615.
Reason (R): Two decades of continuous Mughal campaigning had exhausted the resources of Mewar.
Select the correct answer:
opts: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.exp: Repeated campaigns under Akbar and Jahangir drained Mewar's men and treasury, and the nobles pressed Amar Singh I to accept terms in 1615.

chapters.title: Rajputana under the British; 19th-Century Conditions & Reform
factsheet: Treaty of Surji-Anjangaon (30 Dec 1803) with Daulat Rao Scindia opened Rajputana to British influence; Ajmer passed to the British in 1818.
Karauli was the FIRST Rajputana state to sign a subsidiary treaty with the British (November 1817); Sirohi was the LAST (1823).
Sir Charles Metcalfe negotiated most of the 1817-18 subsidiary treaties on the British side; Lord Hastings was the Governor-General.
Treaty order (1817-18): Karauli (Nov 1817), Tonk (Nov 1817), Kota (Dec 1817), Jodhpur (Jan 1818), Udaipur (Jan 1818), Bundi (Feb 1818), Bikaner (Mar 1818), Jaipur (Apr 1818), Jaisalmer (Dec 1818).
Tonk was created in 1817 for the Pindari leader Amir Khan - the only Muslim-ruled state of Rajputana.
Jhalawar (1838), carved out of Kota, was the last princely state created in Rajputana by the British.
Rajputana Agency was constituted in 1832; head = Agent to the Governor-General (AGG). HQ Ajmer 1832-1845, Mount Abu 1845-1947.
Mount Abu was leased by the British from Sirohi state; it became the AGG's hill headquarters.
Ajmer-Merwara was under DIRECT British rule (a Chief Commissioner's province), not a princely state; a Part 'C' state in 1950; merged into Rajasthan on 1 Nov 1956.
Colonel James Tod, Political Agent to the Western Rajput States (from 1818, HQ Udaipur), wrote 'Annals and Antiquities of Rajast'han'.
Sati was first declared illegal in Rajputana by Rao Vishnu Singh of BUNDI in 1822 - seven years before Bentinck's 1829 Regulation.
Female infanticide (kanya vadh) was first banned by Maharao Ram Singh of KOTA in 1833; Jodhpur framed rules in 1839.
Slavery (dasa pratha) was declared illegal in Kota and Bundi in 1832.
Tyag pratha (extortion by Charans/Bhats at weddings) was first outlawed by Maharaja Man Singh of JODHPUR in 1841.
Samadhi pratha was banned in Jaipur in 1844.
Dakan pratha (branding women as witches) was declared illegal by Maharana Swaroop Singh of MEWAR in October 1853.
Anmel vivah (ill-matched marriage) and child marriage were prohibited by the Alwar state Act of 1903.
Har Bilas Sharda of Ajmer piloted the Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929 - the 'Sharda Act'.
Walterkrit Rajputana Hitkarini Sabha - founded 1888 at AJMER by Colonel C.K.M. Walter, AGG of Rajputana; originally 'Rajputana Hitkarini Sabha'.

Walter Sabha aims: curb marriage and death-feast (nukta/mrityu bhoj) expenditure, end dowry and polygamy, fix marriage age at 14 for girls and 18 for boys. It was NOT a political body and did NOT campaign for widow remarriage.
Desh Hitaishini Sabha - Udaipur, 1877, under Maharana Sajjan Singh; targeted marriage expenditure and polygamy.
Sarva Hitkarini Sabha - Churu, 1907, founded by Swami Gopal Das with Pandit Kanhaiyalal and Pandit Shriram.
Mayo College, Ajmer (1875), named after Viceroy Lord Mayo - the 'Eton of the East', a school for princes and nobles.
Swami Dayanand Saraswati toured Rajputana (Karauli 1865, Ajmer, Bharatpur and Udaipur 1881); he revised the Satyarth Prakash at Naulakha Mahal, Udaipur, as Maharana Sajjan Singh's guest.
Dayanand Saraswati died at AJMER on 30 October 1883; his Paropkarini Sabha continues there.
The Chhappaniya Akal - famine of Vikram Samvat 1956 (1899-1900) - was the worst famine in Rajputana's recorded history.
The Mer/Merwara tract of the Aravallis was pacified by Colonel Hall; the Merwara Battalion was raised in 1822 to police it.
Under the 1817-18 treaties the states surrendered external relations and accepted British paramountcy, kept internal autonomy, and several paid tribute (khiraj).

questions.q: Which princely state of Rajputana was the first to sign a subsidiary alliance treaty with the British in November 1817?
questions.exp: Karauli signed first, in November 1817. Most other Rajputana states followed in 1818, and Sirohi was the last, in 1823.

questions.q: Sirohi holds the distinction of being the last Rajputana state to conclude a subsidiary treaty with the British. In which year did it do so?
questions.exp: Sirohi signed in 1823, six years after Karauli. Mount Abu was later leased by the British from Sirohi as the AGG's headquarters.

questions.q: Most of the subsidiary treaties of 1817-18 with the Rajputana states were negotiated on the British side by:
questions.exp: Sir Charles Metcalfe, then Resident at Delhi, conducted the negotiations under Governor-General Lord Hastings. James Tod became Political Agent to the Western Rajput States only after the treaties.

questions.q: The Rajputana Agency, the apex British political establishment for the Rajput states, was constituted in:
questions.exp: The Rajputana Agency was created in 1832 with its head styled Agent to the Governor-General (AGG), stationed first at Ajmer.

questions.q: In which year was the headquarters of the Agent to the Governor-General for Rajputana shifted from Ajmer to Mount Abu?
questions.exp: The AGG's headquarters moved to Mount Abu in 1845 and remained there until 1947. Ajmer had housed it from 1832.

questions.q: Ajmer came under direct British administration in 1818 after being ceded by:
questions.exp: Daulat Rao Scindia ceded Ajmer to the British in 1818. Ajmer-Merwara was thereafter British territory, not a princely state.

questions.q: Sati was declared illegal for the first time in Rajputana in 1822 by the ruler of which state?
questions.exp: Rao Vishnu Singh of Bundi banned sati in 1822, seven years before Lord William Bentinck's Regulation of 1829.

questions.q: Dakan pratha, the practice of branding women as witches, was declared illegal in 1853 by:
questions.exp: Maharana Swaroop Singh of Mewar outlawed dakan pratha in October 1853 under British persuasion.

questions.q: The Walterkrit Rajputana Hitkarini Sabha, founded in 1888, had its headquarters at:
questions.exp: The Sabha was established at Ajmer in 1888, the seat of British administration in Rajputana. It worked purely on social reform among the Rajput aristocracy.

questions.q: The Walterkrit Rajputana Hitkarini Sabha was founded by:
questions.exp: Colonel C.K.M. Walter, Agent to the Governor-General for Rajputana, founded it in 1888; the body is named after him.

questions.q: The minimum marriageable ages recommended by the Walterkrit Rajputana Hitkarini Sabha were:
opts: 14 years for girls and 18 years for boys
12 years for girls and 16 years for boys
16 years for girls and 21 years for boys
15 years for girls and 20 years for boys
questions.exp: The Sabha fixed 14 for girls and 18 for boys, along with curbs on dowry, polygamy and death-feast expenditure.

questions.q: Mayo College, the school founded for the princes and nobles of Rajputana, was established at Ajmer in:
questions.exp: Mayo College opened at Ajmer in 1875 and is nicknamed the 'Eton of the East'.

questions.q: Mayo College, Ajmer is named after:
questions.exp: It commemorates Viceroy Lord Mayo, who proposed a college for the education of the sons of Rajputana's ruling houses.

questions.q: The Desh Hitaishini Sabha (1877), which attacked lavish marriage expenditure and polygamy, was set up at Udaipur under the patronage of:
questions.exp: Maharana Sajjan Singh of Mewar patronised the Desh Hitaishini Sabha in 1877; he also hosted Swami Dayanand at Udaipur in 1881.

questions.q: The Sarva Hitkarini Sabha, founded in 1907 by Swami Gopal Das, functioned from which town?
questions.exp: Swami Gopal Das founded it at Churu in 1907 with Pandit Kanhaiyalal and Pandit Shriram; it opened schools for girls and Harijans.

questions.q: Swami Dayanand Saraswati, the founder of the Arya Samaj, died on 30 October 1883 at:
questions.exp: Dayanand died at Ajmer, where the Paropkarini Sabha he founded is still located. He had earlier stayed at Udaipur as Maharana Sajjan Singh's guest.

questions.q: The Child Marriage Restraint Act of 1929 is popularly named after which reformer from Ajmer?
questions.exp: Har Bilas Sharda of Ajmer piloted the Bill, hence the 'Sharda Act'. It fixed 14 for girls and 18 for boys across British India.

questions.q: Female infanticide was declared illegal for the first time in Rajputana in 1833 by:
opts: Maharaja Ram Singh II of Jaipur
questions.exp: Maharao Ram Singh of Kota banned kanya vadh in 1833. Jodhpur framed rules against it in 1839.

questions.q: The 'Chhappaniya Akal', the most severe famine in Rajputana's recorded history, occurred in which years of the Christian era?
questions.exp: It is named after Vikram Samvat 1956, corresponding to 1899-1900. Livestock losses and migration were catastrophic.

questions.q: Mount Abu, which became the headquarters of the Rajputana Agency, was leased by the British from which princely state?
questions.exp: Mount Abu was leased from Sirohi in the 1840s. At integration, Abu and Delwara initially went to Bombay and returned to Rajasthan only in 1956.

questions.q: The princely state of Tonk was created by the British in 1817 in favour of which Pindari leader?
questions.exp: Amir Khan surrendered to the British and was granted Tonk, which became the only Muslim-ruled state of Rajputana.

questions.q: After the Constitution came into force in 1950, Ajmer-Merwara was classified as which category of state?
questions.exp: Ajmer was a Part 'C' state with its own legislature (Dhara Sabha) until it merged into Rajasthan on 1 November 1956.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajputana Agency:
I. It was constituted in 1832.
II. Its head was designated Agent to the Governor-General.
III. Its headquarters remained at Ajmer throughout its existence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Agency was created in 1832 and headed by an AGG, but the headquarters shifted from Ajmer to Mount Abu in 1845.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Walterkrit Rajputana Hitkarini Sabha:
I. It was set up in 1888 at Ajmer.
II. Its membership was drawn largely from rulers, jagirdars and state officials.
III. It aimed at reducing expenditure on marriages and death feasts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Sabha was an aristocratic reform body created by the British political establishment, not a popular movement.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the subsidiary treaties concluded by the Rajputana states in 1817-18:
I. The states surrendered control over their external relations to the British.
II. Several states agreed to pay an annual tribute to the British.
III. The British undertook to protect the states from external aggression and internal rebellion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three were standard clauses. The states retained internal autonomy but became subordinate allies under British paramountcy.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Ajmer-Merwara under the British:
I. It was administered directly by the British and not through a princely ruler.
II. It came to the British from the Marathas.
III. It was merged into Rajasthan in 1949.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Ajmer came from Daulat Rao Scindia in 1818 and was directly ruled. It merged into Rajasthan only on 1 November 1956, in the seventh stage of integration.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Colonel James Tod:
I. He served as Political Agent to the Western Rajput States.
II. He wrote 'Annals and Antiquities of Rajast'han'.
III. He was the first Agent to the Governor-General for Rajputana.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Tod was a Political Agent from 1818 with headquarters at Udaipur and wrote the Annals; the AGG's office was created only in 1832, after his departure.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about social reform legislation in the princely states of Rajputana:
I. Slavery was declared illegal in Kota and Bundi in 1832.
II. Tyag pratha was first outlawed by Maharaja Man Singh of Jodhpur.
III. Samadhi pratha was banned in Jaipur in 1844.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Reform in the states was piecemeal and driven largely by pressure from the Political Agents.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the state of Tonk:
I. It was created for the Pindari chief Amir Khan.
II. It was the only Muslim-ruled princely state of Rajputana.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Both are correct. Tonk was carved out in 1817 for Amir Khan, and remained Rajputana's only state with a Muslim ruling house.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Swami Dayanand Saraswati's association with Rajasthan:
I. He revised the Satyarth Prakash while staying at Udaipur.
II. Maharana Sajjan Singh of Mewar was his host.
III. He died at Jodhpur in 1883.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Dayanand revised the Satyarth Prakash at Naulakha Mahal, Udaipur, as Maharana Sajjan Singh's guest, but he died at Ajmer on 30 October 1883.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Social practice)   List-II (State and year of first prohibition)
A. Sati                    1. Kota, 1833
B. Female infanticide      2. Bundi, 1822
C. Tyag pratha             3. Mewar, 1853
D. Dakan pratha            4. Jodhpur, 1841
questions.exp: Sati - Bundi 1822 (Rao Vishnu Singh); female infanticide - Kota 1833 (Maharao Ram Singh); tyag pratha - Jodhpur 1841 (Maharaja Man Singh); dakan pratha - Mewar 1853 (Maharana Swaroop Singh).

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Institution)                       List-II (Place)
A. Walterkrit Rajputana Hitkarini Sabha    1. Churu
B. Desh Hitaishini Sabha                   2. Ajmer
C. Sarva Hitkarini Sabha                   3. Mount Abu
D. Headquarters of the AGG (from 1845)     4. Udaipur
questions.exp: Walter Sabha - Ajmer (1888); Desh Hitaishini Sabha - Udaipur (1877); Sarva Hitkarini Sabha - Churu (1907); the AGG's headquarters moved to Mount Abu in 1845.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Body/Institution)          List-II (Associated person)
A. Walterkrit Hitkarini Sabha      1. Swami Gopal Das
B. Sarva Hitkarini Sabha           2. Lord Mayo
C. Desh Hitaishini Sabha           3. Colonel C.K.M. Walter
D. Mayo College, Ajmer             4. Maharana Sajjan Singh
questions.exp: Colonel Walter founded the Hitkarini Sabha; Swami Gopal Das the Sarva Hitkarini Sabha at Churu; Maharana Sajjan Singh patronised the Desh Hitaishini Sabha; Mayo College is named after Viceroy Lord Mayo.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (State)   List-II (Year of subsidiary treaty with the British)
A. Karauli       1. 1823
B. Jaipur        2. 1817
C. Sirohi        3. 1838
D. Jhalawar      4. 1818
questions.exp: Karauli signed first in 1817, Jaipur in 1818 and Sirohi last in 1823. Jhalawar was not an original signatory - it was created out of Kota in 1838.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Practice abolished)   List-II (Ruler who abolished it)
A. Sati                       1. Maharao Ram Singh
B. Female infanticide         2. Maharana Swaroop Singh
C. Dakan pratha               3. Rao Vishnu Singh
D. Tyag pratha                4. Maharaja Man Singh
questions.exp: Rao Vishnu Singh of Bundi (sati), Maharao Ram Singh of Kota (female infanticide), Maharana Swaroop Singh of Mewar (dakan pratha) and Maharaja Man Singh of Jodhpur (tyag pratha).

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT an objective of the Walterkrit Rajputana Hitkarini Sabha?
opts: Fixing a minimum age of marriage
Securing political representation for the people of the states
