questions.exp: The Sabha was strictly a social reform body of rulers and jagirdars sponsored by the British Agency; it never took up political rights or representative government.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs relating to the subsidiary treaties of Rajputana is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Sirohi signed in 1823, making it the last Rajputana state to enter into a treaty with the British.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the office of the Agent to the Governor-General (AGG) for Rajputana is NOT correct?
opts: The office was created along with the Rajputana Agency in 1832
Its headquarters was shifted to Mount Abu in 1845
Ajmer-Merwara was administered by a princely ruler under its supervision
Political Agents in individual states reported to the AGG
questions.exp: Ajmer-Merwara was directly ruled British territory under a Commissioner, never a princely state.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Sarva Hitkarini Sabha - Swami Gopal Das
Desh Hitaishini Sabha - Maharana Sajjan Singh
Walterkrit Rajputana Hitkarini Sabha - Colonel C.K.M. Walter
Mayo College, Ajmer - Colonel James Tod
questions.exp: Mayo College is named after Viceroy Lord Mayo; James Tod had left India decades earlier and was a Political Agent, not an educationist.

questions.q:
Arrange the following social reform measures of the Rajputana states in correct chronological order:
I. Prohibition of tyag pratha in Jodhpur
II. Prohibition of sati in Bundi
III. Prohibition of female infanticide in Kota
IV. Prohibition of slavery in Kota and Bundi
questions.exp: Sati in Bundi (1822), slavery in Kota-Bundi (1832), female infanticide in Kota (1833) and tyag pratha in Jodhpur (1841).

chapters.title: 1857 in Rajasthan; Peasant and Tribal Movements
factsheet: In 1857 Rajputana had six British cantonments: Nasirabad (Ajmer), Neemuch, Erinpura (Pali), Deoli (Tonk), Kherwara (Udaipur) and Beawar. Kherwara and Beawar did not revolt.
The revolt in Rajasthan began at NASIRABAD on 28 May 1857 - 15th and 30th Native Infantry mutinied and marched to Delhi.
Neemuch cantonment revolted on 3 June 1857; the sepoys moved on Delhi via Chittor. Mohammad Ali Beg/Ali Beg is remembered here.
Erinpura: the Jodhpur Legion revolted on 21 August 1857 with the cry 'Chalo Delhi, Maro Firangi'.
Thakur Khushal Singh Champawat of AUWA led the Marwar rebels; Battle of Bithoda (8 Sep 1857) and Battle of Chelawas (18 Sep 1857).
Monck Mason, Political Agent of Jodhpur, was killed at Auwa/Chelawas and his head hung at the Auwa fort gate.

Kota revolted on 15 October 1857 under Lala Jaidayal (Kayastha) and Mehrab Khan; Major Burton, the Political Agent, was killed. Kota stayed in rebel hands about six months until General H.G. Roberts recovered it in March 1858.
The Agent to the Governor-General for Rajputana during 1857 was George Patrick Lawrence, with headquarters at Mount Abu (Ajmer treasury shifted for safety).
Rulers who sided with the British: Ram Singh II (Jaipur), Takht Singh (Jodhpur), Swaroop Singh (Udaipur), Sardar Singh (Bikaner), Ram Singh (Kota), Narendra Singh (Karauli).
Tantya Tope entered Rajasthan through Banswara and Pratapgarh, was defeated near Bhilwara and near Sikar, and was finally hanged at Sipri on 18 April 1859.

BIJOLIA (Bhilwara district, a first-class thikana of Mewar) - India's longest peasant movement, 1897-1941; 84 villages, 84 types of lag (cesses); the Chanwari lag of 1903 (marriage tax) and Talwar Bandhai were notorious.

Bijolia leaders in sequence: Nanji Patel and Thakri Patel (1897) -> Sadhu Sitaram Das (from 1913) -> Vijay Singh Pathik (from 1916) -> Manikya Lal Verma -> Haribhau Upadhyaya and Jamnalal Bajaj (from 1927).
Vijay Singh Pathik's real name was Bhoop Singh Gurjar (b. Guthawali, Bulandshahr); he founded the Rajasthan Seva Sangh (Wardha, 1919) and edited Rajasthan Kesari.
The Bijolia movement was publicised nationally by 'Pratap' (Kanpur, Ganesh Shankar Vidyarthi) and by 'Abhyudaya' and 'Bharat Mitra'; Gandhi sent Mahadev Desai to study it.

BEGUN (Bengu) movement 1921-23 - leader Ram Narayan Chaudhary; Rupaji and Kripaji Dhakad were killed in the Govindpura firing (July 1923); the settlement was mocked as the 'Bolshevik Agreement' by the British officer Trench.
Barad/Bundi movement - Pandit Nayanuram Sharma; the Dabi kand of 2 April 1923, where Nanakji Bhil was killed, is called 'Rajasthan ka Jallianwala Bagh'.
NEEMUCHANA (Alwar), 14 May 1925 - troops of Maharaja Jai Singh fired on assembled peasants; Gandhi denounced it in Young India as 'double-dyed dyerism'.
Sikar/Shekhawati Jat movement - Sikarwati Jat Kisan Panchayat; the Kudan kand of 25 April 1935 in Sikar; Thakur Deshraj and the Jat Mahasabha were prominent.
Bikaner: Dudhwa Khara peasant movement (from 1946) - Kumbharam Arya, Raghuvar Dayal Goyal; Birbal Singh died in the Raisinghnagar firing.
Marwar Kisan Sabha and the Dabra kand of 13 March 1947 in Jodhpur state.
BHIL/BHAGAT movement - Govind Giri (Govind Guru), born 1858 at Bansiya/Bedsa in Dungarpur; founded the SAMP SABHA in 1883; preached 33 rules and lit a dhuni on Mangarh hill.
MANGARH massacre - 17 November 1913, on the Banswara-Gujarat border; firing by British forces under Major S. Bailey killed about 1,500 Bhils; called the 'Adivasi Jallianwala Bagh'.
EKI (Bhomat) movement - Motilal Tejawat, an Oswal of Kolyari village in Jhadol, Udaipur state; began 1921; slogan 'Na Hakim, Na Hukum'; called 'Bavji' and 'Adivasiyon ka Masiha'.

Tejawat's charter of 21 demands was called 'Mewar ki Pukar'; the Neemda (Nimda) firing of 7 March 1922 and the Palchitariya firing of 1923 crushed the movement; he surrendered in 1929 on Gandhi's advice.

MEENA movement - the Meenas were listed under the Criminal Tribes Act (1924) and the Jaipur Jarayam Pesha Act (1930); Meena Kshatriya Mahasabha formed 1933; at the Bagawas conference (28 Oct 1946) about 26,000 Meena chowkidars resigned; the Act was repealed in 1952.
MER revolt of Merwara (1820-21) was suppressed by Colonel Hall, who raised the Merwara Battalion.
Manikya Lal Verma wrote the song 'Panchhida' and later led the Mewar Prajamandal; he began his public life in the Bijolia movement.

questions.q: The revolt of 1857 in Rajasthan began on 28 May 1857 at which cantonment?
questions.exp: Nasirabad in Ajmer district was the first to rise, when the 15th and 30th Native Infantry mutinied and marched towards Delhi.

questions.q: The Neemuch cantonment joined the revolt of 1857 in which month?
questions.exp: Neemuch revolted on 3 June 1857; the sepoys burnt the cantonment and moved towards Delhi via Chittor.

questions.q: Which of the following cantonments of Rajputana did NOT witness a mutiny in 1857 but is counted among the six British cantonments of the region?
questions.exp: Kherwara (Udaipur) and Beawar remained quiet. Nasirabad, Neemuch, Erinpura and Deoli all saw disturbance.

questions.q: The Jodhpur Legion revolted at Erinpura on 21 August 1857 raising which slogan?
questions.exp: The Erinpura rebels marched under the cry 'Chalo Delhi, Maro Firangi' and later joined Thakur Khushal Singh at Auwa.

questions.q: Who led the rebels of Auwa in Marwar during the revolt of 1857?
questions.exp: Thakur Kushal Singh Champawat of Auwa defeated the Jodhpur state forces at Bithoda on 8 September 1857 and became the outstanding rebel leader of Rajputana.

questions.q: The British Political Agent killed by the rebels at Auwa in 1857 was:
questions.exp: Monck Mason, Political Agent of Jodhpur, was killed in the fighting around Auwa and Chelawas; his head was hung at the fort gate.

questions.q: At Kota, the revolt of 15 October 1857 was led by Mehrab Khan and:
questions.exp: Lala Jaidayal, a Kayastha official, and Mehrab Khan led the Kota rising in which Major Burton, the Political Agent, was killed.

questions.q: Which British officer was killed by the rebels at Kota in October 1857?
questions.exp: Major Burton, the Political Agent at Kota, was killed along with his sons. Kota remained in rebel hands for about six months.

questions.q: Who was the Agent to the Governor-General for Rajputana at the time of the revolt of 1857?
questions.exp: George Patrick Lawrence was the AGG in 1857, operating from Mount Abu; he moved the Ajmer treasury for safety.

questions.q: Tantya Tope, who entered Rajasthan during the revolt, was finally captured and hanged in 1859 at:
questions.exp: Tantya Tope was hanged at Sipri (Shivpuri) on 18 April 1859. He had earlier been defeated near Bhilwara and near Sikar in Rajasthan.

questions.q: The Bijolia peasant movement, the longest peasant movement of modern India, began in which year?
questions.exp: It began in 1897 with a peasant deputation led by Nanji Patel and Thakri Patel, and continued in phases until 1941.

questions.q: The Bijolia thikana, the centre of the famous peasant movement, belonged to which princely state and lies in which present-day district?
questions.exp: Bijolia was a first-class thikana of Mewar and lies in present-day Bhilwara district.

questions.q: The real name of Vijay Singh Pathik, the leader of the Bijolia peasant movement, was:
questions.exp: Vijay Singh Pathik was born Bhoop Singh Gurjar at Guthawali in Bulandshahr; he adopted the new name after the Lahore conspiracy case of 1915.

questions.q: The 'Chanwari lag' imposed in 1903, which inflamed the Bijolia peasants, was a tax on:
questions.exp: Chanwari lag was a marriage cess. Bijolia's peasants were subjected to some 84 different lags and forced labour (begar).

questions.q: Which sadhu took over the leadership of the Bijolia peasant movement from 1913?
questions.exp: Sadhu Sitaram Das organised the peasants from 1913 and later brought in Vijay Singh Pathik.

questions.q: Two Hindi newspapers that carried the Bijolia peasants' cause to a national audience were:
opts: Amrit Bazar Patrika and Bombay Chronicle
questions.exp: 'Abhyudaya' and 'Bharat Mitra' publicised Bijolia, as did 'Pratap' of Kanpur, edited by Ganesh Shankar Vidyarthi.

questions.q: Rupaji and Kripaji, whose deaths in the Govindpura firing of 1923 are commemorated as martyrdoms, belonged to which peasant movement?
questions.exp: The Begun (Bengu) movement of 1921-23, led by Ram Narayan Chaudhary, saw the Govindpura firing in which Rupaji and Kripaji Dhakad were killed.

questions.q: The agreement that ended the Begun peasant movement was derisively described by the British officer Trench as the:
questions.exp: Because the settlement conceded so much to the cultivators, Trench called it a 'Bolshevik Agreement'.

questions.q: The Neemuchana firing, which Mahatma Gandhi condemned in Young India as 'double-dyed dyerism', took place in which princely state?
questions.exp: The firing of 14 May 1925 occurred at Neemuchana in Alwar state under Maharaja Jai Singh, after peasants resisted a steep land revenue increase.

questions.q: The Dabi incident of 1923, in which Nanakji Bhil was killed, is associated with the peasant movement of which state?
questions.exp: The Dabi kand of 2 April 1923 belongs to the Barad peasant movement of Bundi state, led by Pandit Nayanuram Sharma; it is often called Rajasthan's Jallianwala Bagh.

questions.q: The Samp Sabha, an organisation for the moral and social uplift of the Bhils, was founded in 1883 by:
questions.exp: Govind Giri (Govind Guru), born in Dungarpur, founded the Samp Sabha in 1883 and preached 33 rules of conduct to the Bhils.

questions.q: The Mangarh massacre, in which about 1,500 Bhils were killed by British forces, occurred on:
questions.exp: The firing at Mangarh hill on 17 November 1913 predates Jallianwala Bagh and is called the 'Adivasi Jallianwala Bagh'.

questions.q: Motilal Tejawat, leader of the Eki movement, belonged to which community and village?
questions.exp: Tejawat was an Oswal (Bania) of Kolyari village in the Jhadol thikana of Udaipur state; the Bhils called him 'Bavji'.

questions.q: 'Mewar ki Pukar', the charter presented by Motilal Tejawat to the Maharana, contained how many demands?
questions.exp: It listed 21 demands; the Maharana accepted 18 but rejected those on forest rights, begar and crop protection against wild boar.

questions.q: The Meena Kshatriya Mahasabha was formed to resist which colonial-era legislation?
opts: The Criminal Tribes Act and the Jaipur Jarayam Pesha Act
questions.exp: The Meenas were listed as a criminal tribe in 1924 and under the Jaipur Jarayam Pesha Act of 1930; the Mahasabha, formed in 1933, campaigned until repeal in 1952.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the revolt of 1857 in Rajasthan:
I. The revolt began at Nasirabad on 28 May 1857.
II. Kherwara and Beawar cantonments did not revolt.
III. Most of the ruling princes of Rajputana supported the British.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Jaipur, Jodhpur, Udaipur, Bikaner, Kota and Karauli all stood with the British; the rebellion was carried by sepoys and jagirdars.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Auwa episode of 1857:
I. Thakur Kushal Singh defeated the Jodhpur state forces at Bithoda.
II. Monck Mason, the Political Agent, was killed there.
III. Kushal Singh belonged to the Champawat clan of Rathores.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Kushal Singh surrendered only in 1860 and died at Udaipur in 1864.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Kota revolt of 1857:
I. It broke out on 15 October 1857.
II. Major Burton, the Political Agent, was killed.
III. The Maharao of Kota led the rebels against the British.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Maharao Ram Singh of Kota was himself besieged by his own troops; he did not lead the rebels. The city was recovered by General Roberts in March 1858.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Bijolia peasant movement:
I. It lasted from 1897 to 1941.
II. Vijay Singh Pathik assumed its leadership in 1916.
III. Manikya Lal Verma was associated with it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Bijolia is regarded as the longest-running peasant movement in modern Indian history.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Govind Guru:
I. He founded the Samp Sabha in 1883.
II. He worked among the Bhils and Garasias.
III. He led the Eki movement in Bhomat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Eki (Bhomat) movement was led by Motilal Tejawat, not Govind Guru. Govind Guru's Bhagat movement culminated in the Mangarh firing of 1913.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Eki movement:
I. Its slogan was 'Na Hakim, Na Hukum'.
II. The Neemda firing of March 1922 was part of it.
III. Motilal Tejawat surrendered in 1929 on Gandhi's advice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The movement spread over the Bhomat tract of Mewar and adjoining Idar and Sirohi.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Meena movement of Rajasthan:
I. Some 26,000 Meena chowkidars resigned at the Bagawas conference of 1946.
II. The Jarayam Pesha Act applicable to them was repealed in 1952.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Both are correct. The mass resignation of chowkidars was the decisive act of protest against the 'criminal tribe' stigma.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Shekhawati and Sikar peasant movements:
I. The Sikarwati Jat Kisan Panchayat organised the cultivators.
II. The Kudan incident took place in Sikar.
III. The movement was directed against the enhancement of lagaan by the thikanedars.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Kudan firing of 25 April 1935 is the best remembered episode of the Shekhawati Jat movement.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Centre of 1857 revolt)   List-II (Date)
A. Nasirabad                     1. 15 October 1857
B. Neemuch                       2. 28 May 1857
C. Erinpura                      3. 3 June 1857
D. Kota                          4. 21 August 1857
questions.exp: Nasirabad 28 May, Neemuch 3 June, Erinpura 21 August and Kota 15 October 1857.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Movement)   List-II (Leader)
A. Bijolia          1. Ram Narayan Chaudhary
B. Begun            2. Vijay Singh Pathik
C. Barad (Bundi)    3. Motilal Tejawat
D. Eki              4. Nayanuram Sharma
questions.exp: Bijolia - Vijay Singh Pathik; Begun - Ram Narayan Chaudhary; Barad of Bundi - Pandit Nayanuram Sharma; Eki - Motilal Tejawat.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Incident)   List-II (Place/State)
A. Neemuchana       1. Sikar
B. Kudan            2. Bundi
C. Dabi             3. Alwar
D. Govindpura       4. Begun
questions.exp: Neemuchana was in Alwar, Kudan in Sikar, Dabi in Bundi and Govindpura in the Begun thikana of Mewar.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Personality)      List-II (Association)
A. Govind Guru            1. Meena Kshatriya Mahasabha
B. Motilal Tejawat        2. Samp Sabha
C. Kumbharam Arya         3. Eki movement
D. Jai Ram (Meena)        4. Dudhwa Khara movement
questions.exp: Govind Guru founded the Samp Sabha; Tejawat led the Eki movement; Kumbharam Arya led the Dudhwa Khara movement in Bikaner; the Meena Kshatriya Mahasabha led the Meena agitation.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (British officer)     List-II (Event of 1857 or after)
A. Monck Mason               1. Killed at Kota
B. Major Burton              2. AGG for Rajputana in 1857
C. George Patrick Lawrence   3. Killed at Auwa
D. Major S. Bailey           4. Mangarh firing of 1913
questions.exp: Monck Mason died at Auwa, Major Burton at Kota, Lawrence was the AGG, and Major S. Bailey commanded at Mangarh in 1913.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs relating to the revolt of 1857 in Rajasthan is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Nasirabad - First centre of revolt in Rajasthan
Erinpura - Revolt of the Jodhpur Legion
questions.exp: Major Burton was killed at Kota, not Deoli. Deoli was a cantonment in Tonk state.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs (peasant movement - princely state) is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The Dudhwa Khara movement of 1946, led by Kumbharam Arya, belonged to Bikaner state.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT correctly associated with the Bijolia peasant movement?
questions.exp: Kumbharam Arya belongs to the Dudhwa Khara movement in Bikaner state, not Bijolia.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The Kudan incident in Sikar took place in 1935, during the Shekhawati Jat peasant movement.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Eki movement is NOT correct?
opts: It was led by Motilal Tejawat
It drew its strength mainly from the Bhils of the Bhomat tract
Its charter of demands was called 'Mewar ki Pukar'
It was launched by the Mewar Prajamandal in 1938
questions.exp: The Eki movement began in 1921, long before the Mewar Prajamandal was founded in 1938 by Manikya Lal Verma.

questions.q:
Arrange the following events of the revolt of 1857 in Rajasthan in correct chronological order:
I. Revolt at Kota
II. Revolt at Nasirabad
III. Revolt at Erinpura
IV. Revolt at Neemuch
questions.exp: Nasirabad (28 May), Neemuch (3 June), Erinpura (21 August) and Kota (15 October) 1857.

questions.q:
Arrange the following events of Rajasthan's agrarian and tribal history in correct chronological order:
I. Start of the Bijolia peasant movement
II. Foundation of the Samp Sabha by Govind Guru
III. Mangarh massacre
IV. Dabi incident in Bundi state
questions.exp: Samp Sabha 1883, Bijolia 1897, Mangarh 1913 and the Dabi kand of Bundi in 1923.

chapters.title: Prajamandals, Press, Freedom Fighters & Integration of Rajasthan
factsheet: JAIPUR Prajamandal (1931) - Kapoor Chand Patni; the FIRST Prajamandal of Rajasthan; reorganised in 1936-38 under Heera Lal Shastri with Jamnalal Bajaj's backing.
MARWAR (Jodhpur) Prajamandal (1934) - Jai Narayan Vyas and Bhanwar Lal Sarraf; Marwar Hitkarini Sabha (1938) and Marwar Lok Parishad; Balmukund Bissa died in jail, 1942.
MEWAR (Udaipur) Prajamandal (1938) - Manikya Lal Verma; banned soon after and revived in 1941.
BIKANER Prajamandal (1936) - Magharam Vaidya, founded outside the state at Calcutta because of the ban on political activity.

Other Prajamandals: Bundi 1931 (Kantilal, Rishidutt Mehta), Dholpur 1936, Alwar 1938 (Hari Narayan Sharma), Bharatpur 1938 (Gopilal Yadav), Karauli 1938, Shahpura 1938 (Ramesh Chandra Ojha, Laduram Vyas), Kishangarh 1939, Sirohi 1939 (Gokul Bhai Bhatt), Kota 1939 (Pandit Nayanuram Sharma), Banswara 1943, Dungarpur 1944 (Bhogilal Pandya), Jaisalmer 1945 (Mithalal Vyas), Pratapgarh 1945, Jhalawar 1946.
All India States' Peoples Conference - founded 1927 at Bombay; Vijay Singh Pathik was among its office-bearers; Jawaharlal Nehru presided at the Ludhiana session of 1939.
Rajputana Madhya Bharat Sabha - 1918, formed at the Delhi Congress session under Jamnalal Bajaj's lead; headquarters Ajmer.
Rajasthan Seva Sangh - founded 1919 at Wardha by Vijay Singh Pathik; shifted to Ajmer in 1920; a nursery for Rajasthan's peasant and political movements.
Rajputana Deshi Rajya Lok Parishad - first session at Ajmer, 1931, presided over by Ram Narayan Chaudhary.
NEWSPAPERS: Mazahrul-Saroor (Bharatpur, 1849) is regarded as Rajasthan's earliest newspaper; Rajputana Gazette (Ajmer, 1885, Maulvi Murad Ali).
Rajasthan Kesari - founded 1920 at Wardha by Vijay Singh Pathik, financed by Jamnalal Bajaj.
Naveen Rajasthan (Ajmer, 1922) - Vijay Singh Pathik, organ of the Rajasthan Seva Sangh; Tarun Rajasthan (Ajmer, 1923) - Ram Narayan Chaudhary and Jai Narayan Vyas.
TYAG BHUMI - founded 1927 by HARIBHAU UPADHYAYA, the most influential nationalist weekly of Rajasthan; Upadhyaya later became Chief Minister of Ajmer state (1952-56).
Agnibaan - Jai Narayan Vyas, from Beawar; Akhand Bharat - Jai Narayan Vyas, from Bombay (1938).
'Pratap' of Kanpur (Ganesh Shankar Vidyarthi) and the Allahabad papers 'Abhyudaya' and 'Bharat Mitra' carried the Bijolia peasants' cause to all India.
REVOLUTIONARIES: Arjun Lal Sethi founded the Vardhaman Vidyalaya (Jaipur, 1907) and the Jain Shiksha Prachark Samiti.

Kesari Singh Barhath of Shahpura wrote 'Chetavani ra Chungatya' (1903), 13 sorthas urging Maharana Fateh Singh to boycott the Delhi Durbar; he founded the Veer Bharat Sabha and was jailed at Hazaribagh.
Jorawar Singh Barhath took part in the Hardinge bomb attack in Delhi (23 December 1912); Pratap Singh Barhath died of torture in Bareilly Central Jail.

Rao Gopal Singh Kharwa, Sagarmal Gopa (Jaisalmer - wrote 'Jaisalmer ka Gundaraj' and 'Azadi ke Diwane', died in jail 4 April 1946) and Gokul Bhai Bhatt ('the Gandhi of Rajasthan') were leading figures.
WOMEN: Ratan Devi and Anjana Devi Chaudhary (Bijolia/Begun), Kishori Devi, Narayani Devi Verma, Rama Devi, Nagendra Bala.

INTEGRATION STAGE 1 - MATSYA UNION, 18 March 1948: Alwar, Bharatpur, Dholpur, Karauli plus the Neemrana chiefship. Capital Alwar; Rajpramukh Udaybhan Singh of Dholpur; PRIME MINISTER SHOBHA RAM; inaugurated by N.V. Gadgil.

STAGE 2 - RAJASTHAN UNION (Eastern Rajasthan), 25 March 1948: Kota, Bundi, Tonk, Jhalawar, Dungarpur, Banswara, Pratapgarh, Kishangarh, Shahpura and the Kushalgarh chiefship. Capital Kota; Rajpramukh Bhim Singh of Kota; PM Gokul Lal Asawa.
STAGE 3 - SANYUKT (United) RAJASTHAN, 18 April 1948: Udaipur joined. Capital Udaipur; Rajpramukh Maharana Bhupal Singh; PM Manikya Lal Verma; inaugurated by Jawaharlal Nehru.

STAGE 4 - VRIHAD (Greater) RAJASTHAN, 30 March 1949: Jaipur, Jodhpur, Bikaner and Jaisalmer joined. Capital Jaipur; Rajpramukh SAWAI MAN SINGH II; Maharajpramukh Bhupal Singh; PM Heera Lal Shastri; inaugurated by SARDAR VALLABHBHAI PATEL. 30 March is celebrated as RAJASTHAN DAY.
STAGE 5 - SANYUKT VRIHAD RAJASTHAN, 15 May 1949: the Matsya Union merged in, on the recommendation of the Shankar Rao Deo committee.
STAGE 6 - RAJASTHAN, 26 January 1950: Sirohi merged (Abu and Delwara went to Bombay); Rajasthan became a Part 'B' state; Heera Lal Shastri became its first Chief Minister.

STAGE 7 - PUNARGATHIT (Reorganised) RAJASTHAN, 1 November 1956: Ajmer-Merwara, Abu Road and Delwara added, Sunel Tappa gained, Sironj lost to Madhya Pradesh; Rajpramukh abolished by the 7th Constitutional Amendment; GURUMUKH NIHAL SINGH became the first Governor; Mohan Lal Sukhadia was Chief Minister.
Rajasthan was formed out of 19 princely states, 3 chiefships (Neemrana, Kushalgarh, Lava) and the Chief Commissioner's province of Ajmer-Merwara.
Sawai Man Singh II of Jaipur was the first and the only Rajpramukh of Rajasthan; V.P. Menon, Secretary of the States Ministry, executed the mergers under Sardar Patel.
The capital question was settled in favour of Jaipur on the recommendation of a committee headed by B.R. Patel.

questions.q: Which was the first Prajamandal to be established in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The Jaipur Prajamandal, founded in 1931 by Kapoor Chand Patni, was the earliest. It was reorganised in the late 1930s under Heera Lal Shastri.

questions.q: The Jaipur Prajamandal was founded in 1931 by:
questions.exp: Kapoor Chand Patni founded it in 1931; Jamnalal Bajaj and Heera Lal Shastri gave it national direction after its reorganisation.

questions.q: The Mewar Prajamandal, established in 1938, was founded by:
questions.exp: Manikya Lal Verma, who began his public life in the Bijolia movement, founded the Mewar Prajamandal in 1938; it was banned and revived in 1941.

questions.q: The Marwar Prajamandal is chiefly associated with which leader?
questions.exp: Jai Narayan Vyas led the Marwar Prajamandal and the later Marwar Lok Parishad; Bhanwar Lal Sarraf was associated with the Marwar Hitkarini Sabha.

questions.q: The Bikaner Prajamandal, founded in 1936, is associated with:
questions.exp: Magharam Vaidya founded the Bikaner Prajamandal in 1936; because political activity was banned inside the state, it was organised from Calcutta.

questions.q: Gokul Bhai Bhatt, popularly called 'the Gandhi of Rajasthan', led the Prajamandal of which state?
questions.exp: Gokul Bhai Bhatt organised the Sirohi Prajamandal in 1939 and later opposed the transfer of Abu to Bombay.

questions.q: Bhogilal Pandya, who is remembered as a builder of tribal education in the Vagad region, led the Prajamandal of:
questions.exp: Bhogilal Pandya founded the Dungarpur Prajamandal in 1944; Haridev Joshi, later Chief Minister, was among his associates.

questions.q: The All India States' Peoples Conference, the umbrella body for movements in the princely states, was founded in:
questions.exp: It was founded in 1927 at Bombay. Jawaharlal Nehru presided over its Ludhiana session in 1939.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Seva Sangh was founded in 1919 at:
questions.exp: Vijay Singh Pathik founded it at Wardha in 1919 and moved it to Ajmer in 1920; it guided the Bijolia and Begun movements.

questions.q: The Rajputana Madhya Bharat Sabha was formed in 1918 during a Congress session held at:
questions.exp: It was formed at the Delhi Congress session of 1918 under Jamnalal Bajaj's lead, with its headquarters at Ajmer.

questions.q: Who was the editor of the nationalist weekly 'Tyag Bhumi'?
questions.exp: Haribhau Upadhyaya founded and edited Tyag Bhumi from 1927; he later became Chief Minister of Ajmer state.

questions.q: 'Rajasthan Kesari', started in 1920, was published from Wardha under the editorship of:
questions.exp: Vijay Singh Pathik edited Rajasthan Kesari from Wardha with Jamnalal Bajaj's financial support; it publicised the Bijolia movement.

questions.q: The newspaper 'Agnibaan' was published by:
questions.exp: Jai Narayan Vyas brought out Agnibaan from Beawar; he also published Tarun Rajasthan and, from Bombay, Akhand Bharat.

questions.q: 'Mazahrul-Saroor', generally regarded as the earliest newspaper of Rajasthan, was published from:
questions.exp: Mazahrul-Saroor appeared from Bharatpur in 1849, well before the Ajmer press of the 1880s.

questions.q: The 'Rajputana Gazette', published from Ajmer in 1885, was edited by:
questions.exp: Maulvi Murad Ali edited the Rajputana Gazette. Ajmer, being British territory, was the freest place for the press in Rajputana.

questions.q: 'Naveen Rajasthan', published from Ajmer in 1922, was the organ of which organisation?
questions.exp: Naveen Rajasthan was the mouthpiece of Vijay Singh Pathik's Rajasthan Seva Sangh after it moved to Ajmer.

questions.q: Pandit Arjun Lal Sethi founded which educational institution at Jaipur in 1907?
questions.exp: The Vardhaman Vidyalaya became a centre of revolutionary activity; Sethi also ran the Jain Shiksha Prachark Samiti.

questions.q: 'Chetavani ra Chungatya', a set of sorthas urging Maharana Fateh Singh to boycott the Delhi Durbar, was composed by:
questions.exp: Kesari Singh Barhath of Shahpura wrote the 13 sorthas in 1903; the Maharana went to Delhi but did not attend the Durbar.

questions.q: Which member of the Barhath family took part in the bomb attack on Viceroy Lord Hardinge in Delhi in 1912?
questions.exp: Jorawar Singh Barhath was involved in the Hardinge bomb case of 23 December 1912 and evaded capture for the rest of his life.

questions.q: Sagarmal Gopa, who died in jail in 1946, was a freedom fighter of which princely state?
questions.exp: Sagarmal Gopa of Jaisalmer wrote 'Jaisalmer ka Gundaraj' and 'Azadi ke Diwane'; a branch canal of the Indira Gandhi Canal is named after him.

questions.q: The Matsya Union, the first stage in the integration of Rajasthan, was formed on:
questions.exp: The Matsya Union of Alwar, Bharatpur, Dholpur and Karauli was inaugurated on 18 March 1948 with its capital at Alwar.

questions.q: Who was the Prime Minister of the Matsya Union?
questions.exp: Shobha Ram (Kumawat) was the Prime Minister of the Matsya Union, whose Rajpramukh was Udaybhan Singh of Dholpur.

questions.q: The Rajpramukh of the Matsya Union was the ruler of which state?
questions.exp: Maharaj Rana Udaybhan Singh of Dholpur was made Rajpramukh, though the capital was fixed at Alwar.

questions.q: Vrihad (Greater) Rajasthan, formed on 30 March 1949, was inaugurated by:
questions.exp: Sardar Patel inaugurated Vrihad Rajasthan at Jaipur on 30 March 1949, which is observed as Rajasthan Day.

questions.q: Who was the first and only Rajpramukh of Rajasthan?
opts: Sawai Man Singh II of Jaipur
questions.exp: Sawai Man Singh II became Rajpramukh on 30 March 1949; the office was abolished by the 7th Constitutional Amendment in 1956.

questions.q: Which territory was transferred out of Rajasthan to Madhya Pradesh when the state was reorganised on 1 November 1956?
questions.exp: The Sironj sub-division of Kota went to Madhya Pradesh, while Ajmer-Merwara, Abu Road, Delwara and Sunel Tappa came to Rajasthan.

questions.q: Rajasthan's present shape was completed on 1 November 1956, when the first Governor of the state took charge. He was:
questions.exp: Gurumukh Nihal Singh became the first Governor of Rajasthan on 1 November 1956, replacing the abolished office of Rajpramukh.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Prajamandal movement in Rajasthan:
I. The Jaipur Prajamandal was the first to be founded.
II. The Bikaner Prajamandal had to be organised outside the state.
III. Manikya Lal Verma founded the Mewar Prajamandal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Bikaner's ban on political activity forced its Prajamandal to be organised from Calcutta in 1936.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Vijay Singh Pathik:
I. His original name was Bhoop Singh.
II. He founded the Rajasthan Seva Sangh.
III. He edited 'Rajasthan Kesari'.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Pathik linked the Bijolia peasants to the national movement through the Seva Sangh and its press.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about 'Tyag Bhumi':
I. It was edited by Haribhau Upadhyaya.
II. It began publication in 1927.
III. Its editor later became Chief Minister of Ajmer state.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Haribhau Upadhyaya headed the Ajmer state ministry from 1952 to 1956 and later held portfolios in Rajasthan.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Barhath family of revolutionaries:
I. Kesari Singh Barhath founded the Veer Bharat Sabha.
II. Pratap Singh Barhath died in Bareilly Central Jail.
III. Jorawar Singh Barhath was linked with the Hardinge bomb case.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Barhaths of Shahpura are the outstanding revolutionary family of Rajasthan.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Matsya Union:
I. It comprised Alwar, Bharatpur, Dholpur and Karauli.
II. Its capital was Bharatpur.
III. Shobha Ram was its Prime Minister.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The capital of the Matsya Union was Alwar, not Bharatpur. The name 'Matsya' was suggested by K.M. Munshi after the ancient janapada.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the formation of Vrihad Rajasthan on 30 March 1949:
I. Jaipur, Jodhpur, Bikaner and Jaisalmer joined at this stage.
II. Sawai Man Singh II was made Rajpramukh and Bhupal Singh Maharajpramukh.
III. Heera Lal Shastri became its Prime Minister.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Jaipur was chosen as the capital on the recommendation of a committee headed by B.R. Patel.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the merger of the Matsya Union with Rajasthan:
I. It took place on 15 May 1949.
II. It followed the recommendation of a committee headed by Shankar Rao Deo.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Both are correct. The merged unit was called Sanyukt Vrihad Rajasthan, the fifth stage of integration.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sirohi question in the integration of Rajasthan:
I. Sirohi joined Rajasthan on 26 January 1950.
II. Abu and Delwara were transferred to Bombay state.
III. Abu Road and Delwara returned to Rajasthan in 1956.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Gokul Bhai Bhatt led the agitation against the transfer of Abu to Bombay.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the units that formed Rajasthan:
I. Nineteen princely states were merged.
II. Neemrana, Kushalgarh and Lava were the three chiefships.
III. Ajmer-Merwara was merged in the last stage.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Rajasthan finally comprised 19 princely states, 3 chiefships and the Chief Commissioner's province of Ajmer-Merwara.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the press in the Rajasthan freedom movement:
I. 'Naveen Rajasthan' was published from Ajmer.
II. 'Agnibaan' was edited by Jai Narayan Vyas.
III. 'Rajasthan Kesari' was published from Bharatpur.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Rajasthan Kesari was published from Wardha in Maharashtra, not Bharatpur. Bharatpur was the home of the earlier Mazahrul-Saroor.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Prajamandal)   List-II (Founder)
A. Jaipur              1. Manikya Lal Verma
B. Marwar              2. Kapoor Chand Patni
C. Mewar               3. Gokul Bhai Bhatt
D. Sirohi              4. Jai Narayan Vyas
questions.exp: Jaipur - Kapoor Chand Patni (1931); Marwar - Jai Narayan Vyas (1934); Mewar - Manikya Lal Verma (1938); Sirohi - Gokul Bhai Bhatt (1939).

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Newspaper)      List-II (Editor/Founder)
A. Tyag Bhumi           1. Vijay Singh Pathik
B. Agnibaan             2. Maulvi Murad Ali
C. Rajasthan Kesari     3. Haribhau Upadhyaya
D. Rajputana Gazette    4. Jai Narayan Vyas
questions.exp: Tyag Bhumi - Haribhau Upadhyaya; Agnibaan - Jai Narayan Vyas; Rajasthan Kesari - Vijay Singh Pathik; Rajputana Gazette - Maulvi Murad Ali.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Newspaper)        List-II (Place of publication)
A. Mazahrul-Saroor        1. Wardha
B. Rajasthan Kesari       2. Bharatpur
C. Naveen Rajasthan       3. Bombay
D. Akhand Bharat          4. Ajmer
questions.exp: Mazahrul-Saroor - Bharatpur (1849); Rajasthan Kesari - Wardha (1920); Naveen Rajasthan - Ajmer (1922); Akhand Bharat - Bombay (1938).

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Stage of integration)     List-II (Date)
A. Matsya Union                   1. 30 March 1949
B. Rajasthan Union                2. 18 April 1948
C. Sanyukt Rajasthan              3. 18 March 1948
D. Vrihad Rajasthan               4. 25 March 1948
questions.exp: Matsya Union 18 March 1948, Rajasthan Union 25 March 1948, Sanyukt Rajasthan 18 April 1948 and Vrihad Rajasthan 30 March 1949.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Union)          List-II (Prime Minister)
A. Matsya Union         1. Manikya Lal Verma
B. Rajasthan Union      2. Heera Lal Shastri
C. Sanyukt Rajasthan    3. Shobha Ram
D. Vrihad Rajasthan     4. Gokul Lal Asawa
questions.exp: Shobha Ram headed the Matsya Union, Gokul Lal Asawa the Rajasthan Union, Manikya Lal Verma the Sanyukt Rajasthan and Heera Lal Shastri the Vrihad Rajasthan.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Personality)        List-II (Association)
A. Arjun Lal Sethi          1. Jaisalmer ka Gundaraj
B. Sagarmal Gopa            2. Vardhaman Vidyalaya
C. Kesari Singh Barhath     3. Mewar Prajamandal
D. Manikya Lal Verma        4. Chetavani ra Chungatya
questions.exp: Arjun Lal Sethi founded the Vardhaman Vidyalaya; Sagarmal Gopa wrote 'Jaisalmer ka Gundaraj'; Kesari Singh Barhath composed 'Chetavani ra Chungatya'; Manikya Lal Verma founded the Mewar Prajamandal.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs (Prajamandal - leader) is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The Kota Prajamandal was led by Pandit Nayanuram Sharma; Manikya Lal Verma belonged to Mewar.

questions.q: Which one of the following newspapers was NOT published by Jai Narayan Vyas?
questions.exp: Tyag Bhumi was Haribhau Upadhyaya's paper. Jai Narayan Vyas published Agnibaan, Akhand Bharat and, with Ram Narayan Chaudhary, Tarun Rajasthan.

questions.q: Which one of the following states was NOT a constituent of the Matsya Union?
questions.exp: Kishangarh joined the Rajasthan Union of 25 March 1948. The Matsya Union consisted of Alwar, Bharatpur, Dholpur, Karauli and the Neemrana chiefship.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched with regard to the integration of Rajasthan?
opts: Sanyukt Rajasthan - inaugurated by Jawaharlal Nehru
Vrihad Rajasthan - inaugurated by Sardar Patel
Matsya Union - inaugurated by N.V. Gadgil
Rajasthan Union - inaugurated by Rajendra Prasad
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Union of 25 March 1948 was also inaugurated by N.V. Gadgil, not by Rajendra Prasad.

questions.q: Which one of the following did NOT become part of Rajasthan on 1 November 1956?
questions.exp: Sironj was transferred out of Rajasthan to Madhya Pradesh in 1956; the other three were added.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the office of Rajpramukh is NOT correct?
opts: Sawai Man Singh II was Rajasthan's Rajpramukh
The Rajpramukh of the Rajasthan Union was Bhim Singh of Kota
The office was abolished by the 7th Constitutional Amendment
Bhupal Singh of Mewar was Rajasthan's second Rajpramukh
questions.exp: Bhupal Singh was Rajpramukh of Sanyukt Rajasthan and later Maharajpramukh, but Sawai Man Singh II remained Rajasthan's only Rajpramukh until the office was abolished in 1956.

questions.q:
Arrange the following stages in the integration of Rajasthan in correct chronological order:
I. Vrihad Rajasthan
II. Matsya Union
III. Sanyukt Rajasthan
IV. Rajasthan Union
questions.exp: Matsya Union (18 March 1948), Rajasthan Union (25 March 1948), Sanyukt Rajasthan (18 April 1948) and Vrihad Rajasthan (30 March 1949).

chapters.title: Architecture: Forts, Palaces, Temples, Havelis, Stepwells
factsheet: UNESCO 'Hill Forts of Rajasthan' inscribed 2013 (37th session) - six forts: Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Amber, Jaisalmer, Gagron. Other UNESCO sites: Keoladeo National Park (1985), Jantar Mantar Jaipur (2010), Walled City of Jaipur (2019).
Fort typology (Shukraniti/Manu): giri (hill), jal/audak (water), dhanva/marusthaliya (desert), van/aranya (forest), eran (ravine), parikh (moat), sahay (allies), sainya (army).
Gagron (Jhalawar) - the jal-durg; at the confluence of the Kali Sindh and Ahu; built by Bijaldev Dod; said to rest on rock with no laid foundation; two sakas (1423, 1444).
Jaisalmer Fort - dhanva durg; founded 1156 by Rawal Jaisal on Trikuta hill; 'Sonar Quila'; a 'living fort'; 99 bastions; yellow sandstone, no lime mortar.
Chittorgarh - largest fort of India by area; on the Mesa plateau; founded by the Mori ruler Chitrangada; three sakas (1303 Alauddin Khilji, 1535 Bahadur Shah, 1568 Akbar).
Vijay Stambh, Chittorgarh - Rana Kumbha, completed 1448, nine storeys, 37.19 m; architect Sutradhar Jaita with sons; marks victory over Mahmud Khilji of Malwa at Sarangpur (1437).
Kirti Stambh, Chittorgarh - 12th century Jain tower dedicated to Adinath, raised by the Bagherwal merchant Jija; seven storeys, about 22 m.
Kumbhalgarh (Rajsamand) - Rana Kumbha, 1443-58, architect Mandan; 36-km wall, 'Great Wall of India'; Katargarh citadel; birthplace of Maharana Pratap.
Mehrangarh (Jodhpur) - Rao Jodha, 1459, on Chidiyatunk hill; Lohapol, Phool Mahal, Moti Mahal; Jaswant Thada (1899) stands beside it.
Junagarh (Bikaner) - Raja Rai Singh, 1589-94, supervised by Karan Chand; a plains/parikh fort, not a hill fort; Anup Mahal, Karan Mahal, Phool Mahal.
Amber Fort (Jaipur) - present form begun by Raja Man Singh I in 1592; Sheesh Mahal, Ganesh Pol, Diwan-i-Aam, Jagat Shiromani temple; capital moved to Jaipur 1727.
Jaigarh (Jaipur) - Sawai Jai Singh II, 1726, on Cheel ka Teela; houses Jaivana, the world's largest cannon on wheels; Asia's largest cannon foundry.
Nahargarh (Jaipur) - Sawai Jai Singh II, 1734, originally named Sudarshangarh; Madhavendra Bhawan added by Sawai Madho Singh II.
Taragarh, Ajmer - 'Garh Beetli', built by Ajayaraja Chauhan; called the 'Gibraltar of Rajasthan'. Bundi also has a Taragarh (Rao Bar Singh Hada).
Bhatner (Hanumangarh) - oldest fort of Rajasthan, on the Ghaggar; built by Bhupat, son of Bhati Jaisal; renamed Hanumangarh in 1805.
Lohagarh (Bharatpur) - Maharaja Suraj Mal, 1733; moat/parikh fort never taken by the British; Jawahar Burj and Fateh Burj.

Jalore Fort - Sonagir/Swarnagiri/Kanchangiri; fell to Alauddin Khilji in 1311 (Kanhadde Prabandh). Siwana Fort - Veer Narayan Panwar; saka of Sataldev. Achalgarh (Mount Abu, Sirohi) - Paramara fort rebuilt by Rana Kumbha in 1452; Achaleshwar Mahadev temple.
Dilwara (Mount Abu) - Vimal Vasahi (1031, Vimal Shah, Adinath), Luna Vasahi (1230, Vastupal-Tejpal, Neminath), Pittalhar (Bhima Shah), Khartar Vasahi (Parshvanath); Maru-Gurjara marble style.
Ranakpur (Pali) - Chaumukha temple of Adinath; patron Dharna Shah (Porwal), architect Depak, in Rana Kumbha's reign; 1,444 carved pillars.
Osian (Jodhpur) - Gurjara-Pratihara temple cluster, 'Khajuraho of Rajasthan'; Sachiya Mata temple. Kiradu (Barmer) - Someshwar temple, Solanki style.
Ambika Mata temple, Jagat (Udaipur), 961 CE - the 'Khajuraho of Mewar'. Sas-Bahu temple, Nagda (Udaipur), 975 CE.
Neelkanth Mahadev temple at Rajorgarh (Alwar) - built by the Bargujar ruler Mathandeva; Rajor inscription of 960 CE.
Sun temples: Jhalrapatan (Padmanabh temple, 10th c., Jhalawar), Osian, Varman (Sirohi), Ranakpur Surya Narayan. Harshnath temple - Sikar.
Adhai Din ka Jhonpra, Ajmer - Qutbuddin Aibak, 1199, on the site of a Sanskrit college of Vigraharaja IV; screen added by Iltutmish. Dargah of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti, Ajmer.
Hawa Mahal (Jaipur) - Sawai Pratap Singh, 1799; architect Lal Chand Ustad; five storeys, 953 jharokhas, shaped like Krishna's crown.
Umaid Bhawan (Jodhpur) - Maharaja Umaid Singh, 1929-43; architect Henry Vaughan Lanchester; Chittar sandstone, hence 'Chittar Palace'; a famine-relief work.
Lalgarh Palace (Bikaner) - Maharaja Ganga Singh; architect Sir Samuel Swinton Jacob; red Dulmera sandstone; named after his father Lall Singh.

Stepwells: Chand Baori, Abhaneri (Dausa) - Nikumbha ruler Chanda, c. 8th-9th c., 3,500 steps, 13 storeys; Raniji ki Baori, Bundi (Rani Nathavati, 1699); Toorji ka Jhalra, Jodhpur; Panna Meena ka Kund, Amber.

Havelis: Patwon ki Haveli, Jaisalmer (Guman Chand Patwa, 1805; five havelis, the largest in Rajasthan); Nathmal ki Haveli and Salim Singh ki Haveli, Jaisalmer; painted havelis of Shekhawati (Nawalgarh, Mandawa, Fatehpur).
Chhatris: Gaitor (Kachhwaha rulers, Jaipur), Chaurasi Khambon ki Chhatri (Bundi), Jaswant Thada (Jodhpur), Devkund (Bikaner), Kshar Bagh (Kota).

questions.q: The serial property 'Hill Forts of Rajasthan' was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in which year?
questions.exp: The six hill forts were inscribed in 2013 at the 37th session of the World Heritage Committee. The group comprises Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Amber, Jaisalmer and Gagron.

questions.q: Gagron Fort of Jhalawar is classified as which type of fort?
questions.exp: Gagron stands at the confluence of the Kali Sindh and the Ahu and is the textbook jal (audak) durg of Rajasthan. It is also said to be the only fort raised on rock without a laid foundation.

questions.q: Gagron Fort is situated at the confluence of which two rivers?
questions.exp: The Kali Sindh and the Ahu meet at Gagron in Jhalawar district, giving the fort water on three sides. The dargah of Sufi saint Mitthe Shah lies below the fort.

questions.q: The Jaisalmer Fort, popularly called Sonar Quila, was founded on the Trikuta hill by
questions.exp: Rawal Jaisal of the Bhati dynasty founded the fort in 1156 CE. Built of yellow sandstone without lime mortar, it is one of the few 'living forts' of the world, with residents still inside.

questions.q: The Vijay Stambh at Chittorgarh was raised by Rana Kumbha to commemorate his victory over
questions.exp: The nine-storeyed tower, completed in 1448, marks Kumbha's victory over Mahmud Khilji of Malwa at Sarangpur in 1437. It stands 37.19 m high and is the emblem of the Rajasthan Police.

questions.q: The architect credited with the construction of the Vijay Stambh at Chittorgarh was
questions.exp: Sutradhar Jaita, assisted by his sons Napa, Puja and Poma, built the Vijay Stambh. Mandan was Rana Kumbha's other great architect, associated with Kumbhalgarh.

questions.q: Kumbhalgarh Fort was designed by which architect of Rana Kumbha's court?
questions.exp: Mandan, Kumbha's chief architect, wrote treatises such as Prasad Mandan, Rajvallabh Mandan and Devata Murti Prakaran. The fort was built between 1443 and 1458.

questions.q: Junagarh Fort at Bikaner was built between 1589 and 1594 by
questions.exp: Construction was supervised by Rai Singh's minister Karan Chand. Junagarh is a plains fort, not a hill fort, and contains the Anup Mahal, Karan Mahal and Phool Mahal.

questions.q: Bhatner Fort, regarded as one of the oldest forts of Rajasthan, stands on the bank of which river?
questions.exp: Bhatner is situated on the Ghaggar at Hanumangarh and was built by Bhupat, son of the Bhati ruler Jaisal. The town was renamed Hanumangarh in 1805.

questions.q: The fort of Ajmer known as Garh Beetli and described as the 'Gibraltar of Rajasthan' was built by
questions.exp: Taragarh at Ajmer was raised by Ajayaraja (Ajaypal) Chauhan on the Beetli hill. Bundi has a separate Taragarh, built by Rao Bar Singh Hada.

questions.q: The Jaivana, described as the largest cannon on wheels in the world, is preserved in which fort?
questions.exp: Jaigarh Fort on Cheel ka Teela hill, built by Sawai Jai Singh II in 1726, housed Asia's largest cannon foundry where the Jaivana was cast in 1720.

questions.q: Nahargarh Fort, originally named Sudarshangarh, was built in 1734 by
questions.exp: Sawai Jai Singh II built it as a defensive outpost for his new capital Jaipur. The Madhavendra Bhawan, with nine identical suites for the queens, was added by Sawai Madho Singh II.

questions.q: Achalgarh Fort, rebuilt in 1452 by Rana Kumbha over an earlier Paramara structure, is located in which district?
questions.exp: Achalgarh stands on Mount Abu in Sirohi district and guards the Achaleshwar Mahadev temple, where a toe-impression of Shiva is worshipped instead of a linga.

questions.q: The fort of Jalore, also called Sonagir or Swarnagiri, was captured in 1311 by
questions.exp: Kanhaddev Songara's defence of Jalore against Alauddin Khilji is described in Padmanabh's Kanhadde Prabandh. The fort stands on the Sonagir hill in Jalore district.

questions.q: The Dilwara Jain temples, built in white marble in the Maru-Gurjara style, are located at
questions.exp: The five Dilwara temples stand on Mount Abu in Sirohi district. The oldest is the Vimal Vasahi of 1031, dedicated to Adinath.

questions.q: The Chaumukha temple at Ranakpur, built during the reign of Rana Kumbha, is dedicated to
questions.exp: The four-faced Chaumukha temple honours Adinath, the first Tirthankara, and was commissioned by the Porwal merchant Dharna Shah. It has 1,444 individually carved pillars.

questions.q: The Ambika Mata temple, popularly called the 'Khajuraho of Mewar', is situated at which village?
questions.exp: The temple at Jagat in Udaipur district is dated 961 CE and is famous for the density of its sculpted figures. Baroli in Chittorgarh is known for the Ghateshwar Mahadev temple.

questions.q: The Neelkanth Mahadev temple at Rajorgarh, referred to in the Rajor inscription of 960 CE, was built by
questions.exp: Mathandeva of the Bargujar (Badgujar) line built the Shiva temple at Rajorgarh in present-day Alwar district. The Rajor inscription is a key source for early medieval Rajasthan.

questions.q: Adhai Din ka Jhonpra at Ajmer was raised in 1199 on the site of a Sanskrit college by
questions.exp: Qutbuddin Aibak converted a Sanskrit college founded by the Chauhan ruler Vigraharaja IV into a mosque; the arched screen in front was added later by Iltutmish.

questions.q: Hawa Mahal at Jaipur was built in 1799 by
questions.exp: Its architect was Lal Chand Ustad. The five-storeyed pink-and-red sandstone screen has 953 jharokhas and is shaped like the crown of Krishna.

questions.q: Umaid Bhawan Palace at Jodhpur, built between 1929 and 1943, was designed by the British architect
questions.exp: The palace, built of Chittar hill sandstone and hence also called Chittar Palace, was undertaken by Maharaja Umaid Singh as a famine-relief project.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Chittorgarh Fort:
I. It stands on the Mesa plateau and is the largest fort of India in terms of area.
II. It was originally founded by the Mori (Maurya) ruler Chitrangada.
III. The Kirti Stambh within it was built by Rana Kumbha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Kirti Stambh is a 12th-century Jain tower dedicated to Adinath, raised by the Bagherwal merchant Jija; it is the Vijay Stambh that belongs to Rana Kumbha.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Amber Fort:
I. Its present structure was begun by Raja Man Singh I in 1592.
II. The Sheesh Mahal and the Ganesh Pol are located within it.
III. The Kachhwaha capital was shifted from Amber to Jaipur in 1727.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Jagat Shiromani temple, built by Man Singh's queen Kanakwati, also stands in Amber town.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Jal Mahal:
I. It stands in the Man Sagar lake at Jaipur.
II. It was built during the reign of Sawai Madho Singh I.
III. It is an island palace situated in Lake Pichola.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Jal Mahal lies in the Man Sagar lake at Jaipur. Jag Mandir and Jag Niwas are the island palaces of Lake Pichola at Udaipur.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the stepwells of Rajasthan:
I. Toorji ka Jhalra is a stepwell at Jodhpur.
II. Panna Meena ka Kund lies close to the Amber fort at Jaipur.
III. Bundi is popularly known as the city of stepwells.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Bundi's best-known stepwell is the Raniji ki Baori, built in 1699 by Rani Nathavati.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Kumbhalgarh Fort:
I. It was built by Rana Kumbha in the fifteenth century.
II. Maharana Pratap was born in this fort.
III. It lies in Rajsamand district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Its innermost citadel is called Katargarh, and the fort was captured only once, in 1578, by the Mughal general Shahbaz Khan.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Mehrangarh Fort:
I. It was founded by Rao Jodha in 1459.
II. It stands on the Chidiyatunk hill.
III. Jaswant Thada, a marble cenotaph, stands near it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Jaswant Thada was built in 1899 in memory of Maharaja Jaswant Singh II of Jodhpur.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the UNESCO World Heritage Sites of Rajasthan:
I. Keoladeo National Park was inscribed in 1985.
II. The Jantar Mantar at Jaipur was inscribed in 2010.
III. The walled city of Jaipur was inscribed in 2019.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Together with the Hill Forts of Rajasthan (2013), Rajasthan has four World Heritage properties.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Hawa Mahal:
I. It was designed by the architect Lal Chand Ustad.
II. It has five storeys and 953 jharokhas.
III. It was built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Hawa Mahal was built in 1799 by Sawai Pratap Singh, not Sawai Jai Singh II. Its honeycomb facade allowed royal women to watch processions unseen.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Lohagarh Fort:
I. It was built by Maharaja Suraj Mal of Bharatpur.
II. It is protected by a broad moat and is classed as a parikh durg.
III. It was captured by the British in the siege of 1805.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The British besieged Lohagarh in 1805 but failed to take it, which is why it is called the iron fort. Its mud ramparts absorbed cannon fire.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Fort)   List-II (District)
A. Gagron        1. Jhalawar
B. Bhatner       2. Hanumangarh
C. Kumbhalgarh   3. Rajsamand
D. Taragarh (Garh Beetli)   4. Ajmer
questions.exp: Gagron is in Jhalawar, Bhatner in Hanumangarh, Kumbhalgarh in Rajsamand and Taragarh (Garh Beetli) in Ajmer.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Dilwara temple)   List-II (Patron)
A. Vimal Vasahi     1. Vimal Shah
B. Luna Vasahi      2. Vastupal and Tejpal
C. Pittalhar        3. Bhima Shah
D. Khartar Vasahi   4. Mandlik
questions.exp: Vimal Vasahi (1031) honours Adinath, Luna Vasahi (1230) honours Neminath, Pittalhar contains a large brass Adinath image, and Khartar Vasahi is dedicated to Parshvanath.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Palace)   List-II (City)
A. Sukh Mahal      1. Bundi
B. Padmini Mahal   2. Chittorgarh
C. Jag Mandir      3. Udaipur
D. Anup Mahal      4. Bikaner
questions.exp: Sukh Mahal at Bundi stands on Jait Sagar lake, Padmini Mahal is inside Chittorgarh fort, Jag Mandir is an island palace on Lake Pichola and Anup Mahal is in Junagarh, Bikaner.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Fort)   List-II (Type)
A. Jaisalmer    1. Dhanva durg
B. Gagron       2. Jal durg
C. Chittorgarh  3. Giri durg
D. Lohagarh     4. Parikh durg
questions.exp: Jaisalmer is ringed by desert (dhanva), Gagron by water (jal), Chittorgarh sits on a hill (giri) and Lohagarh is protected by a moat (parikh).

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Temple)   List-II (District)
A. Kiradu       1. Barmer
B. Osian        2. Jodhpur
C. Harshnath    3. Sikar
D. Baroli       4. Chittorgarh
questions.exp: Kiradu is in Barmer, Osian in Jodhpur, the Harshnath Shiva temple in Sikar and the Ghateshwar Mahadev temple of Baroli in Chittorgarh.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Stepwell)   List-II (Place)
A. Chand Baori          1. Abhaneri
B. Toorji ka Jhalra     2. Jodhpur
C. Raniji ki Baori      3. Bundi
D. Panna Meena ka Kund  4. Amber
questions.exp: Chand Baori is at Abhaneri in Dausa, Toorji ka Jhalra at Jodhpur, Raniji ki Baori at Bundi and Panna Meena ka Kund near Amber, Jaipur.

questions.q: Which one of the following fort-district pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Shergarh Fort, renovated by Sher Shah Suri, is in Baran district on the Parvan river; another Shergarh lies in Dholpur. Jhalawar's famous fort is Gagron.

questions.q: Which one of the following fort-type pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Ranthambore, standing on an isolated hill at the junction of the Aravalli and the Vindhyas, is a giri durg. Gagron is the classic jal durg of Rajasthan.

questions.q: Which one of the following monument-builder pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Jaigarh Fort - Sawai Jai Singh II
questions.exp: Lohagarh was built by Maharaja Suraj Mal of Bharatpur in 1733; his son Jawahar Singh raised the Jawahar Burj inside it.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT included among the six Hill Forts of Rajasthan inscribed by UNESCO?
questions.exp: The six are Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Amber, Jaisalmer and Gagron. Bhainsrorgarh in Chittorgarh district, at the Chambal-Bamani confluence, is not on the list.

questions.q: Which one of the following temple-district pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The Ambika Mata temple at Jagat, dated 961 CE and called the Khajuraho of Mewar, is in Udaipur district, not Rajsamand.

questions.q: Which one of the following haveli-place pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Salim Singh ki Haveli, with its distinctive peacock-shaped upper storey, is in Jaisalmer. Patwon ki Haveli, a cluster of five, is the largest haveli of Rajasthan.

questions.q:
Arrange the following monuments of Rajasthan in the correct chronological order of their construction:
I. Vijay Stambh, Chittorgarh
II. Hawa Mahal, Jaipur
III. Adhai Din ka Jhonpra, Ajmer
IV. Umaid Bhawan Palace, Jodhpur
questions.exp: Adhai Din ka Jhonpra dates from 1199, the Vijay Stambh was completed in 1448, Hawa Mahal was built in 1799 and Umaid Bhawan between 1929 and 1943.

questions.q: Chand Baori, one of the deepest stepwells in India, is located at Abhaneri in which district?
questions.exp: Built in the 8th-9th century by the Nikumbha ruler Chanda, Chand Baori has about 3,500 steps over 13 storeys and adjoins the Harshat Mata temple.

questions.q: Patwon ki Haveli, the largest haveli of Rajasthan and in fact a cluster of five havelis, is situated at
questions.exp: It was commissioned by the Jain trader Guman Chand Patwa in 1805. Jaisalmer's other famous havelis are Nathmal ki Haveli and Salim Singh ki Haveli.

questions.q: Lalgarh Palace at Bikaner, designed by Sir Samuel Swinton Jacob, was built by
questions.exp: Maharaja Ganga Singh named the red-sandstone palace after his father, Maharaja Lall Singh. Jacob also designed the Albert Hall Museum at Jaipur.

questions.q: Gaitor, the cenotaph complex of the Kachhwaha rulers, is located in
questions.exp: The chhatris of the Jaipur rulers from Sawai Jai Singh II onward stand at Gaitor below Nahargarh. The queens' cenotaphs are at Maharani ki Chhatri.

questions.q: The Chaurasi Khambon ki Chhatri, an eighty-four-pillared cenotaph, is located at
questions.exp: The cenotaph stands at Devpura in Bundi and was raised by Rao Anirudh Singh. Bundi is also famous for its Chaurasi Khambon step-wells and the Chitrashala murals.

questions.q: The fort standing at the confluence of the Chambal and the Bamani rivers, often called the 'Vellore of Rajasthan', is
questions.exp: Bhainsrorgarh in Chittorgarh district is a water-girt fort. Mandalgarh, Chittorgarh and Kumbhalgarh are together called the three sentinels of Mewar.

questions.q: The tenth-century Sun Temple, also known as the Padmanabh temple, stands at Jhalrapatan in which district?
questions.exp: Jhalrapatan, the 'city of temple bells', lies in Jhalawar district. The Sun Temple there is one of the finest examples of the Nagara style in Hadoti.

chapters.title: Painting Schools and Handicrafts
factsheet: Rajasthani painting grew out of the Western Indian Apabhramsa / Jain manuscript tradition; its miniatures are collectively called the Rajasthani or Rajput school.
Earliest dated Mewar set - Ragmala painted at Chawand in 1605 by Nisaruddin under Maharana Amar Singh I.
Mewar school - Sahibdin is its greatest master (Ragmala 1628, Rasikpriya, Bhagavata Purana, Yuddha Kanda of the Ramayana) under Maharana Jagat Singh I; other painter Manohar.
Bundi school - earliest work the Chunar Ragmala of 1591, painted for Rao Bhoj Singh; marked by lush vegetation, monsoon skies, elephants, red-brown ground; Chitrashala of Bundi palace.
Kota school - an offshoot of Bundi; famous for shikar (hunting) scenes in dense forest; flourished under Maharao Ram Singh and Umed Singh; painter Raghunath Das.

Kishangarh school - painter Nihal Chand under Raja Savant Singh (pen-name Nagari Das); the Bani Thani portrait is called the 'Indian Mona Lisa'; other painters Amar Chand, Sitaram, Soorajmal; Morchhal and Boat-scene themes.
Kishangarh features: elongated upturned eyes, arched eyebrows, pointed chin and nose, Krishna-Radha themes, panoramic Gundalao lake backgrounds.
Bikaner school - painters Ali Raza (Ustad), Ruknuddin, Shahadin, Nathu; patrons Rai Singh, Karan Singh, Anup Singh; strong Mughal-Deccani influence; artists signed and dated their work.
Marwar/Jodhpur school - Ragmala of 1623 painted at Pali by Virji; painters Shiv Das, Kishan Das, Dana, Amardas, Kalu; Dhola-Maru is its signature theme; Nath-sect subjects under Maharaja Man Singh.
Dhundhar (Amber-Jaipur) school - painter Sahib Ram, famed for life-size portraits; other artists Ghasi Ram, Hukma, Guman; patron Sawai Pratap Singh; work Bihari Satsai.
Alwar school - flourished under Maharao Raja Vinay Singh; painters Baldev, Ghasi Ram, Sali Ram, Jamna Das; noted for ivory painting and miniature Gulistan illustrations.
Nathdwara sub-school - Pichwai, large cloth paintings hung behind the Shrinathji image; Nathdwara is in Rajsamand district.
Phad painting - scroll narratives of Pabuji and Devnarayan; painted at Shahpura (Bhilwara) by the Joshi (Chhipa) family; Devnarayan ki Phad is the longest.
Uniara (Tonk) sub-school blends Bundi and Jaipur styles; other minor centres are Nagaur, Ghanerao, Deogarh, Shahpura and Sirohi.
Blue pottery - Jaipur; contains no clay at all (quartz powder, fuller's earth, borax, gum, glass); reached Jaipur through Persia and Kashmir; revived by Kripal Singh Shekhawat.
Molela (Rajsamand) - votive terracotta plaques, chiefly of the folk deity Devnarayan, made by Kumhar craftsmen; a GI-registered clay craft.
Thewa - Pratapgarh; sheet gold fused on to coloured glass; practised for generations by the Raj Soni family.
Kota Doria - woven at Kaithoon near Kota; the khat weave of cotton and silk yarns produces square check units; GI-registered.
Bandhej (tie-and-dye) centres: Jaipur, Sikar, Jodhpur, Udaipur, Nathdwara. Leheriya, with diagonal stripes, is associated with Jaipur, Jodhpur and Udaipur.
Sanganer - fine floral direct block printing on a white ground. Bagru (Jaipur district) - dabu (mud-resist) printing in earthy red and black; syahi-begar prints.
Ajrakh printing - Barmer and Balotra, by the Khatri community; geometric prints in indigo and madder.
Meenakari (enamelling) - Jaipur; introduced when Raja Man Singh I brought enamellers from Lahore. Koftgiri - gold and silver wire inlay on steel, at Udaipur, Alwar and Jaipur.
Usta art (munawwat) - Bikaner; gold embossing and painting on camel hide; the Usta family craft.
Kavad - a portable painted wooden shrine with hinged panels, made by Suthar craftsmen at Bassi (Chittorgarh); Bassi is also known for wooden toys and puppets.
Namda - felted woollen rugs of Tonk. Pattu - woollen shawl of Jaisalmer and Barmer. Jajam - block-printed floor spread of Chittorgarh (Akola) and Bhilwara.
Gotta-kinari - Khandela (Sikar), Ajmer and Jaipur. Danka work - Udaipur. Zari/Zardozi - Jaipur, Bikaner.
Pottery: blue pottery (Jaipur), black pottery (Sawai Madhopur, Kota), Kagzi (paper-thin) pottery (Alwar), terracotta (Molela).
Makrana (Nagaur) supplies the white marble of the Taj Mahal; marble carving is a major Jaipur craft. Rajasthali is the state handicraft emporium.

questions.q: The celebrated painting 'Bani Thani' of the Kishangarh school was executed by
questions.exp: Nihal Chand painted Bani Thani under the patronage of Raja Savant Singh. The work is popularly called the 'Indian Mona Lisa'.

questions.q: The Kishangarh ruler who patronised Nihal Chand wrote devotional poetry under the pen-name
questions.exp: Raja Savant Singh of Kishangarh (1748-57) composed Krishna-bhakti poetry as Nagari Das. Bani Thani, a singer at his court, was the model for the famous portrait.

questions.q: Sahibdin, the greatest painter of the Mewar school, worked chiefly under which ruler?
questions.exp: Sahibdin illustrated the Ragmala (1628), Rasikpriya, Bhagavata Purana and the Yuddha Kanda of the Ramayana under Maharana Jagat Singh I of Mewar.

questions.q: The earliest dated set of the Mewar school, a Ragmala of 1605, was painted at
questions.exp: The Ragmala of 1605 was painted at Chawand, then the Mewar capital, by the artist Nisaruddin during the reign of Maharana Amar Singh I.

questions.q: Ali Raza and Ruknuddin are the most celebrated painters of which school of Rajasthani painting?
questions.exp: The Bikaner school shows the strongest Mughal and Deccani influence, partly because its rulers served long terms in the Deccan. Bikaner artists customarily signed and dated their work.

questions.q: The painter Shiv Das is associated with which school of Rajasthani painting?
questions.exp: Shiv Das, along with Kishan Das, Dana and Amardas, belongs to the Marwar (Jodhpur) school, whose signature theme is the Dhola-Maru romance.

questions.q: The Chunar Ragmala of 1591, the earliest known work of its school, belongs to which school of painting?
questions.exp: The Chunar Ragmala was painted for Rao Bhoj Singh of Bundi by artists trained in the Mughal atelier. The Bundi style is known for lush vegetation and monsoon skies.

questions.q: Which school of Rajasthani painting is best known for its depiction of hunting (shikar) scenes set in dense forest?
questions.exp: The Kota school, an offshoot of Bundi, produced its finest work in tiger and boar hunts under Maharao Ram Singh and Umed Singh.

questions.q: The Alwar school of painting is particularly noted for
questions.exp: Alwar painting flourished under Maharao Raja Vinay Singh; its painters Baldev and Ghasi Ram executed miniatures on ivory as well as tiny illustrations for the Gulistan.

questions.q: Sahib Ram, famed for his life-size portraits, was the leading painter of which school?
questions.exp: Sahib Ram worked under Sawai Pratap Singh of Jaipur. The Dhundhar school is also associated with the illustrated Bihari Satsai.

questions.q: Pichwai paintings, large cloth hangings placed behind the deity's image, are associated with
questions.exp: Pichwais are hung behind the Shrinathji image at Nathdwara in Rajsamand district and change with the season and festival.

questions.q: Phad paintings of Rajasthan are traditionally produced by the Joshi family of
questions.exp: Shahpura in Bhilwara district is the home of phad painting. The Devnarayan ki Phad is the longest, and the Pabuji ki Phad the most widely performed.

questions.q: Blue pottery of Jaipur is distinguished by the fact that
opts: it is fired at very high temperature
no clay is used in its preparation
questions.exp: Blue pottery dough is made of quartz powder, fuller's earth, borax, gum and glass, with no clay at all. The craft reached Jaipur from Persia through Kashmir and Delhi.

questions.q: The revival of Jaipur blue pottery in the twentieth century is credited to
questions.exp: Kripal Singh Shekhawat, a Padma Shri awardee, revived and modernised the craft with the support of Rajmata Gayatri Devi and Kamladevi Chattopadhyay.

questions.q: Molela village, famous for votive terracotta plaques of folk deities, is located in which district?
questions.exp: Molela near Nathdwara in Rajsamand district produces terracotta plaques chiefly of Devnarayan, which Bhil and Gurjar devotees install in village shrines.

questions.q: Thewa, the craft of fusing sheet gold on to coloured glass, belongs to which town of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Thewa has been practised at Pratapgarh by the hereditary Raj Soni family. The gold sheet is engraved and then fused on molten glass.

questions.q: Kota Doria saris are woven at which centre?
questions.exp: Kaithoon near Kota is the traditional weaving centre. The khat weave of cotton and silk yarns produces the characteristic square check, and the fabric is GI-registered.

questions.q: Dabu, the mud-resist method of block printing, is chiefly associated with which centre of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Bagru in Jaipur district is famous for dabu resist printing in earthy reds and blacks; Sanganer specialises in fine floral direct printing on a white ground.

questions.q: Ajrakh printing, marked by geometric patterns in indigo and madder, is a traditional craft of
questions.exp: Ajrakh is printed by the Khatri community at Barmer and Balotra, where the water of the Luni is used in the dyeing process.

questions.q: The art of meenakari (enamelling) is said to have been introduced into Jaipur by
questions.exp: Raja Man Singh I brought enamellers from Lahore to Amber. Jaipur meenakari on gold, with its deep red and green, remains the finest in India.

questions.q: Usta art, the craft of gold embossing and painting on camel hide, is associated with which city?
questions.exp: The Usta or munawwat work of Bikaner decorates camel-hide vessels, doors and panels; the Junagarh fort's Anup Mahal displays it lavishly.

questions.q: Kavad, the portable painted wooden shrine with hinged panels, is made by Suthar craftsmen of
questions.exp: Bassi in Chittorgarh district makes the kavad, which a Kavadiya Bhat opens panel by panel while narrating the story. Bassi is also known for wooden toys and puppets.

questions.q: Namda, the craft of making felted woollen rugs, is chiefly associated with which district?
questions.exp: Tonk is the traditional centre for namda. Jaisalmer and Barmer are known instead for the woollen pattu shawl.

questions.q: Gotta-kinari work, the application of metallic ribbon on fabric, is traditionally associated with
questions.exp: Khandela in Sikar district, along with Ajmer and Jaipur, is the traditional gotta-kinari centre. Danka work is the corresponding Udaipur craft.

questions.q: Kagzi pottery, so thin that it is compared to paper, is a speciality of
questions.exp: Kagzi pottery is made at Alwar. Black pottery is associated with Sawai Madhopur and Kota, and blue pottery with Jaipur.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Kishangarh school of painting:
I. Its best-known painter was Nihal Chand.
II. Its figures have elongated, upturned eyes and arched eyebrows.
III. Its principal patron was Raja Savant Singh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The panoramic Gundalao lake at Kishangarh forms the background of many of its Krishna-Radha compositions.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Mewar school of painting:
I. Its earliest dated set is the Ragmala painted at Chawand in 1605.
II. Sahibdin illustrated the Yuddha Kanda of the Ramayana for this school.
III. Bani Thani is its most celebrated work.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Bani Thani belongs to the Kishangarh school, not Mewar. The Mewar style is marked by flat bright colour, oval faces and pointed noses.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Bikaner school of painting:
I. Its painters customarily signed and dated their work.
II. It shows strong Mughal and Deccani influence.
III. Ruknuddin was one of its leading painters.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Bikaner rulers such as Karan Singh and Anup Singh served long spells in the Deccan, which explains the Deccani influence.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about blue pottery:
I. It is chiefly made at Jaipur.
II. Clay is the principal raw material used in its dough.
III. The craft reached Rajasthan through Persian and Central Asian influence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: No clay is used in blue pottery; the dough is made of quartz powder, fuller's earth, borax, gum and glass. Sawai Ram Singh II encouraged the craft at Jaipur.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about phad painting:
I. It is painted on a long cloth scroll.
II. The Pabuji ki Phad is narrated by a Bhopa to the accompaniment of the Ravanhatha.
III. It is traditionally painted by the Joshi family of Shahpura.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Devnarayan ki Phad, the longest, is narrated to the accompaniment of the Jantar.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the textile crafts of Rajasthan:
I. Leheriya is characterised by diagonal stripes produced by resist dyeing.
II. Bandhej is a tie-and-dye craft associated with Jaipur, Sikar and Jodhpur.
III. Sanganeri printing is done with mud resist in earthy red and black.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Mud-resist (dabu) printing in earthy tones belongs to Bagru; Sanganer is known for fine floral direct printing on a white ground.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Kota school of painting:
I. It developed as an offshoot of the Bundi school.
II. Its most characteristic subject is the royal hunt.
III. It flourished under Maharao Ram Singh and Umed Singh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Kota's hunting scenes place tiny human figures against dense, dark forest, a treatment found in no other Rajasthani school.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Thewa art:
I. It involves fusing an engraved gold sheet on to coloured glass.
II. It is practised at Pratapgarh.
III. It is traditionally the craft of the Raj Soni family.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Thewa pieces are usually mounted in silver frames and made into pendants, boxes and plates.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Painting school)   List-II (Painter)
A. Kishangarh   1. Sahibdin
B. Bikaner      2. Nihal Chand
C. Mewar        3. Ali Raza
D. Marwar       4. Shiv Das
questions.exp: Nihal Chand belongs to Kishangarh, Ali Raza to Bikaner, Sahibdin to Mewar and Shiv Das to Marwar (Jodhpur).

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Craft)   List-II (Centre)
A. Thewa        1. Pratapgarh
B. Kota Doria   2. Kaithoon
C. Usta art     3. Bikaner
D. Kavad        4. Bassi
questions.exp: Thewa belongs to Pratapgarh, Kota Doria to Kaithoon, Usta art to Bikaner and the kavad shrine to Bassi in Chittorgarh.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (School)   List-II (Associated work)
A. Bundi       1. Chunar Ragmala
B. Mewar       2. Chawand Ragmala
C. Kishangarh  3. Bani Thani
D. Jaipur      4. Bihari Satsai
questions.exp: The Chunar Ragmala (1591) is Bundi's earliest work, the Chawand Ragmala (1605) Mewar's, Bani Thani is Kishangarh's masterpiece and the illustrated Bihari Satsai belongs to Jaipur.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Craft)   List-II (District/place)
A. Leheriya   1. Jodhpur
B. Ajrakh     2. Barmer
C. Bagru      3. Jaipur
D. Namda      4. Tonk
questions.exp: Leheriya is associated with Jodhpur and Jaipur, Ajrakh with Barmer, Bagru printing with Jaipur district and namda felting with Tonk.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Painter)   List-II (Patron)
A. Nihal Chand   1. Savant Singh
B. Sahib Ram     2. Sawai Pratap Singh
C. Sahibdin      3. Jagat Singh I
D. Ruknuddin     4. Karan Singh
questions.exp: Nihal Chand served Savant Singh of Kishangarh, Sahib Ram Sawai Pratap Singh of Jaipur, Sahibdin Maharana Jagat Singh I of Mewar and Ruknuddin Karan Singh of Bikaner.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Craft)   List-II (Technique)
A. Koftgiri    1. Inlay of gold wire on steel
B. Meenakari   2. Enamelling on metal
C. Thewa       3. Gold sheet fused on glass
D. Usta        4. Gold work on camel hide
questions.exp: Koftgiri inlays gold or silver wire into steel, meenakari is enamelling, thewa fuses gold sheet on glass and Usta art applies gold on camel hide.

questions.q: Which one of the following painting school-painter pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Sahib Ram was the leading painter of the Jaipur (Dhundhar) school and is famous for his life-size portraits.

questions.q: Which one of the following craft-district pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Kota Doria is woven at Kaithoon in Kota district. Bhilwara is associated with phad painting at Shahpura and with textile mills.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a school or sub-school of Rajasthani painting?
questions.exp: Basohli belongs to the Pahari group of painting in Jammu, not to the Rajasthani school. Uniara, Nagaur and Deogarh are recognised Rajasthani sub-schools.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about blue pottery is NOT correct?
opts: It is chiefly produced at Jaipur
Its dough contains quartz powder and fuller's earth
It is fired at a comparatively low temperature
