Terracotta clay forms its main ingredient
questions.exp: Blue pottery uses no clay whatsoever. The other three statements are correct; the low firing temperature is why the ware is fragile.

questions.q: Which one of the following pottery-place pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Blue pottery is the signature craft of Jaipur. Bikaner is known instead for Usta art on camel hide.

questions.q:
Arrange the following works of Rajasthani painting in the correct chronological order:
I. Chawand Ragmala of Mewar
II. Chunar Ragmala of Bundi
III. Sahibdin's Ragmala for Maharana Jagat Singh I
IV. Pali Ragmala of Marwar painted by Virji
questions.exp: The Chunar Ragmala dates from 1591, the Chawand Ragmala from 1605, the Pali (Marwar) Ragmala from 1623 and Sahibdin's Ragmala from 1628.

chapters.title: Performing Arts: Music, Dance, Theatre, Instruments
factsheet: Indian instrument classes: tat (chordophone/string), sushir (aerophone/wind), avanaddh (membranophone/drum), ghan (idiophone/solid).
Chautara - a four-stringed tanpura-like tat vadya used to accompany Ramdevji bhajans, chiefly by the Kamad community.
Kamaycha - bowed tat vadya of the Manganiyars of Jaisalmer-Barmer; about 17 strings, round leather-covered mango-wood resonator; exponent Sakar Khan.
Ravanhatha - bowed instrument with a half-coconut belly; used by Bhopas to recite the Pabuji ki Phad; regarded as an early ancestor of the violin.
Jantar - veena-like tat vadya with two gourds and 5-6 strings; played by Gurjar Bhopas of Devnarayan.
Sarangi - about 27 strings; the Sindhi Sarangi and Gujratan Sarangi are the Langa instruments. Surinda is another Langa bowed instrument.
Bhapang - single-stringed 'talking drum' of Mewat/Alwar, played by the Mewati Jogi; exponent Jahoor Khan Mewati. Chikara - three-stringed, Garasia and Meo.
Sushir vadya: Algoza (paired bamboo flutes), Poongi/Been (Kalbeliya snake charmers), Satara, Shehnai, Nad, Karna, Bankiya, Bhungal, Mashak, Morchang (jaw harp).
Avanaddh vadya: Nagara, Dhol, Dholak, Chang (daf), Damroo, Mridang/Pakhawaj, Khanjari, Maandal, Tasa, Dhaunsa, Naubat, Damama.
Chang (daf) is the Holi instrument of Shekhawati; Maandal is the clay drum of the Bhil Gavari; Nagara is the largest of the percussion instruments.
Ghan vadya: Khartal (wooden clappers; exponent Sadiq Khan Manganiyar), Manjira, Jhanjh, Thali, Ghara/Ghadwa, Chimta, Ghungroo, Lezim, Ghuraliyo.
Manganiyar - Muslim hereditary musicians of Jaisalmer-Barmer; play Kamaycha and Khartal; patrons Rajputs and Charans. Langa - play Sindhi Sarangi and Algoza; patrons Sindhi Sipahi.
Bhopa of Pabuji uses the Ravanhatha; Bhopa of Devnarayan uses the Jantar; Kamad sing Ramdevji bhajans; Dholi, Bhat, Dhadhi and Rawal are other performing communities.
Ghoomar - the most representative women's dance of Rajasthan; Bhil in origin, adopted by Rajput households; performed at Gangaur and Teej.
Gair - men's Holi dance of Mewar and Marwar; Dandi Gair of Jalore-Marwar and Geendad of Shekhawati are its variants.
Chari dance - Kishangarh and Ajmer; Gurjar and Saini women balance a brass chari with a lighted lamp; exponent Falku Bai.
Bhavai - Udaipur, Sirohi and Dungarpur; dancer balances seven to nine pots on the head and dances on a sword edge or glass; exponents Daulat Bai and Krishna Vyas.
Kalbeliya - dance of the Sapera community; inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in 2010; exponent Gulabo Sapera; forms Indoni, Shankaria, Panihari.
Terahtali - performed by Kamad women in honour of Baba Ramdev; thirteen manjiras tied to the body; centre Padarla/Ramdevra; exponents Mangi Bai and Moti Bai.
Gavari (Gavri) - Bhil ritual dance-drama of Mewar performed for about forty days after Rakshabandhan; only men perform, taking female roles too.
Walar and Loor - dances of the Garasia tribe of Sirohi and Pali. Chakri - Kanjar community of Hadoti (Baran, Kota).
Kachhi Ghodi - dummy-horse dance of the Shekhawati region, performed at weddings. Agni (fire) dance - Jasnathi sect at Katariyasar, Bikaner.
Kathputli (string puppetry) - performed by the Bhat/Nat community; the puppets are carved at Bassi in Chittorgarh.

Khyal theatre forms: Kuchamani Khyal (Lachhiram, Nagaur), Shekhawati Khyal (Nanuram), Turra-Kalangi (Nimbahera-Chittorgarh; Turra stands for Shiva, Kalangi for Parvati), Hela Khyal and Ali Baksh Khyal (Alwar).

Other theatre: Rammat (Bikaner, Jaisalmer, Phalodi - performed at Holi), Rasdhari (Mewar), Tamasha (Jaipur, Bhatt family, at Gangaur), Nautanki (Bharatpur-Dholpur belt), Swang (Chirawa, Mandal-Bhilwara), Gavari/Rai (Bhil).
Classical: Jaipur gharana of Kathak; Atrauli-Jaipur gharana of khayal founded by Alladiya Khan; Mewati gharana associated with Pandit Jasraj; Dhrupad tradition at Jaipur and Jodhpur courts.
Musical treatises: Maharana Kumbha wrote Sangeet Raj, Sangeet Mimansa and Sud Prabandh; Pundarik Vitthal wrote Nartan Nirnay; Radha Govind Sangeet Sar was compiled under Sawai Pratap Singh of Jaipur.
Folk songs: Panihari (at the well), Kurjan (crane as messenger), Olyun (Marwari song of longing), Peepli, Moriya, Hichki, Supna, Jachcha (birth), Halariya, Kaga, Papaiyo, Rasiya (Bharatpur), Bandola.

questions.q: The Chautara, used to accompany the bhajans of Ramdevji, belongs to which class of musical instruments?
questions.exp: The Chautara is a four-stringed instrument resembling the tanpura and is therefore a tat vadya. It is chiefly played by the Kamad community.

questions.q: The Kamaycha, a bowed string instrument, is played almost exclusively by which community?
questions.exp: The Manganiyars of the Jaisalmer-Barmer belt play the Kamaycha and the Khartal. Sakar Khan of Hamira was its best-known exponent.

questions.q: The Ravanhatha is traditionally played while narrating which phad?
questions.exp: Bhopas of Pabuji recite the phad to the Ravanhatha, a bowed instrument with a half-coconut resonator. The Devnarayan phad is narrated to the Jantar.

questions.q: The Jantar, a veena-like instrument with two gourd resonators, is played by the Bhopas of which folk deity?
questions.exp: Gurjar Bhopas of Devnarayan use the Jantar. It has five or six strings and is regarded as an early form of the veena.

questions.q: The Bhapang, a single-stringed instrument popularly called the 'talking drum', belongs to which region of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The Bhapang is played by the Mewati Jogis of Alwar and Bharatpur. Jahoor Khan Mewati was its most famous exponent.

questions.q: The Algoza is best described as
opts: a pair of bamboo flutes played simultaneously
a single bamboo flute with eight holes
questions.exp: One flute of the pair carries the melody while the other sustains a drone. It is played by the Langa, Bhil and Kalbeliya musicians.

questions.q: The Morchang, held between the lips and struck with a finger, is often called the
questions.exp: The Morchang is a small iron jaw harp classified among the sushir (wind) instruments in the Rajasthani tradition and is played by Langa and Manganiyar musicians.

questions.q: The Poongi (Been) is the characteristic instrument of which community?
questions.exp: The gourd-bodied Poongi is played by Kalbeliya snake charmers and accompanies the Kalbeliya dance along with the Khanjari and Dholak.

questions.q: The Khartal, a pair of hard wooden clappers, is classified as which type of instrument?
questions.exp: The Khartal is a ghan (idiophone) instrument. Sadiq Khan Manganiyar of Jaisalmer was its most celebrated player.

questions.q: The Chang, played during Holi in the Shekhawati region, belongs to which class of instruments?
questions.exp: The Chang, also called daf, is a single-membrane frame drum and hence an avanaddh vadya. Chang dancing is the signature Holi performance of Shekhawati.

questions.q: The Maandal, a baked-clay drum, is chiefly used in which dance?
questions.exp: Bhil performers of the Gavari dance-drama of Mewar use the Maandal along with the Thali. It has one small and one large mouth.

questions.q: Ghoomar, the best known women's folk dance of Rajasthan, is believed to have originated among
questions.exp: Ghoomar is Bhil in origin and was later adopted by Rajput households. It is performed at Gangaur, Teej and on wedding occasions.

questions.q: The Dandi Gair, a variant of the Gair dance, is particularly associated with which region?
questions.exp: Dandi Gair of the Jalore-Marwar area is performed with sticks; the Shekhawati variant of the Gair is called Geendad. The Gair is a men's Holi dance.

questions.q: In the Chari dance of the Kishangarh-Ajmer region, the dancer balances on her head
opts: a brass pot carrying a lighted lamp
questions.exp: Chari is performed by Gurjar and Saini women; Falku Bai of Kishangarh is its best-known exponent.

questions.q: The Bhavai dance, in which the performer balances several pots on the head and dances on a sword edge, is associated with which region?
questions.exp: Bhavai is performed in the Udaipur, Sirohi and Dungarpur belt. Daulat Bai and Krishna Vyas are among its noted performers.

questions.q: The Kalbeliya folk songs and dances of Rajasthan were inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in
questions.exp: Kalbeliya was inscribed in 2010. The dance is performed by the Sapera community and is popularly identified with the performer Gulabo Sapera.

questions.q: Terahtali dance is performed in honour of which folk deity?
questions.exp: Kamad women perform Terahtali before Baba Ramdev, with thirteen manjiras tied to the body. Mangi Bai Aryan is its best-known exponent.

questions.q: How many manjiras are tied to the body of a Terahtali performer?
questions.exp: Thirteen small brass cymbals, tied to the wrists, elbows, waist and arms, give the dance its name. The performer also balances a pot and holds a sword in her mouth.

questions.q: Gavari, the ritual dance-drama performed for about forty days after Rakshabandhan, belongs to which tribe?
questions.exp: The Bhils of the Mewar region perform Gavari; only men take part, playing female roles as well. It is dedicated to Gauri (Parvati).

questions.q: The Walar and Loor dances belong to which tribe of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Both are Garasia dances of the Sirohi and Pali region; the Walar is performed without any instrument and the Loor at Holi.

questions.q: The Chakri dance is associated with which community of the Hadoti region?
questions.exp: The Kanjar community of Baran and Kota performs the Chakri, in which women spin rapidly in wide skirts.

questions.q: The Agni (fire) dance of Rajasthan is performed by followers of which sect at Katariyasar?
questions.exp: Jasnathi Siddhs of Katariyasar in Bikaner district dance barefoot over live embers to the beat of the nagara during their jagran.

questions.q: Kathputli, the string-puppet theatre of Rajasthan, is traditionally performed by which community?
questions.exp: The Bhat or Nat community performs Kathputli; the wooden puppets themselves are carved at Bassi in Chittorgarh district.

questions.q: Kuchamani Khyal, one of the most popular forms of Rajasthani folk theatre, was developed by
questions.exp: Lachhiram of Kuchaman in Nagaur district gave the form its classic shape. Nanuram is associated with the Shekhawati Khyal.

questions.q: The Rammat form of folk theatre is chiefly performed at Holi in which region?
questions.exp: Rammat is staged in the open at Bikaner, Jaisalmer and Phalodi during Holi, with the nagara and dholak as its main instruments.

questions.q: Tamasha, the folk theatre performed at Jaipur during Gangaur, is associated with which family?
questions.exp: The Bhatt family, which settled in Jaipur under Sawai Pratap Singh, performs Tamasha. Unlike Khyal, it uses a fixed open-air stage.

questions.q: The musical treatise 'Sangeet Raj' was composed by
questions.exp: Maharana Kumbha of Mewar wrote Sangeet Raj, Sangeet Mimansa and Sud Prabandh, besides a commentary on the Gita Govinda called Rasik Priya.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Kalbeliya dance:
I. It is performed by the Sapera community.
II. The Poongi and the Khanjari accompany it.
III. It was inscribed on the UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Indoni, Shankaria and Panihari are recognised forms within the Kalbeliya repertoire.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Terahtali:
I. It is performed by women of the Kamad community.
II. Thirteen manjiras are tied to the dancer's body.
III. It is performed in honour of Gogaji.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Terahtali is performed before Baba Ramdev, not Gogaji. Male singers accompany it on the Chautara or Tandoora.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Manganiyars and the Langas:
I. The Manganiyars are chiefly associated with the Kamaycha.
II. The Langas play the Sindhi Sarangi and the Algoza.
III. Both are hereditary professional musician communities of western Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Manganiyars were patronised by Rajput and Charan families, the Langas by the Sindhi Sipahi.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the classification of Rajasthani folk instruments:
I. The Kamaycha is a tat vadya.
II. The Nagara is an avanaddh vadya.
III. The Manjira is a sushir vadya.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Manjira is a pair of small metal cymbals and is therefore a ghan (idiophone) instrument, not a wind instrument.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Gavari dance-drama:
I. It is performed by the Bhils of the Mewar region.
II. It begins the day after Rakshabandhan and continues for about forty days.
III. Women perform the female roles in it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Only men take part in the Gavari; female roles are also played by men. The performance is dedicated to Gauri and includes episodes such as Bhanwarya and Khetudiyar.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Rajasthani folk theatre:
I. Kuchamani Khyal is associated with Nagaur.
II. Turra-Kalangi Khyal developed in the Nimbahera-Chittorgarh area.
III. Rasdhari performances belong to the Mewar region.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. In Turra-Kalangi, the Turra represents Shiva and the Kalangi represents Parvati, and the two parties compete in verse.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Bhavai dance:
I. The performer balances a stack of pots on the head.
II. The dancer may perform on the edge of a sword or on broken glass.
III. It is chiefly performed in the Shekhawati region.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Bhavai belongs to the Udaipur-Sirohi-Dungarpur belt, not Shekhawati. Shekhawati is known instead for the Chang, Geendad and Kachhi Ghodi dances.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Ghoomar dance:
I. It is performed exclusively by women.
II. It takes its name from the circular movement (ghoomna) of the dancers.
III. It is performed on occasions such as Gangaur and Teej.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Ghoomar originated among the Bhils and was later adopted by Rajput households across Marwar, Mewar and Hadoti.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Rajasthani folk songs:
I. Panihari songs are sung by women drawing water at the well.
II. In the Kurjan, a woman sends a message to her absent husband through a crane.
III. Olyun is a Marwari song expressing the pangs of separation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Other well-known types are Jachcha (birth songs), Halariya, Supna, Moriya and Rasiya of the Bharatpur region.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Kathputli tradition:
I. It is a string-puppet form performed by the Bhat community.
II. The puppets are traditionally carved at Bassi in Chittorgarh.
III. Amar Singh Rathore is a favourite subject of its performances.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The puppeteer speaks through a bamboo-and-leather reed called the boli, while a companion interprets for the audience.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Instrument)   List-II (Class)
A. Kamaycha   1. Tat
B. Algoza     2. Sushir
C. Nagara     3. Avanaddh
D. Khartal    4. Ghan
questions.exp: The Kamaycha is a string (tat) instrument, the Algoza a wind (sushir) instrument, the Nagara a drum (avanaddh) and the Khartal an idiophone (ghan).

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Dance)   List-II (Community/tribe)
A. Terahtali   1. Kamad
B. Gavari      2. Bhil
C. Walar       3. Garasia
D. Chakri      4. Kanjar
questions.exp: Terahtali belongs to the Kamad, Gavari to the Bhil, Walar to the Garasia and Chakri to the Kanjar community.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Instrument)   List-II (Community/performer)
A. Kamaycha       1. Manganiyar
B. Sindhi Sarangi 2. Langa
C. Ravanhatha     3. Bhopa of Pabuji
D. Bhapang        4. Mewati Jogi
questions.exp: The Kamaycha belongs to the Manganiyar, the Sindhi Sarangi to the Langa, the Ravanhatha to the Bhopa of Pabuji and the Bhapang to the Mewati Jogi.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Theatre form)   List-II (Region)
A. Kuchamani Khyal   1. Nagaur
B. Rammat            2. Bikaner
C. Tamasha           3. Jaipur
D. Turra-Kalangi     4. Chittorgarh
questions.exp: Kuchamani Khyal comes from Kuchaman in Nagaur, Rammat from Bikaner, Tamasha from Jaipur and Turra-Kalangi from the Nimbahera area of Chittorgarh.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Dance)   List-II (Region/place)
A. Chari       1. Kishangarh
B. Agni        2. Katariyasar
C. Geendad     3. Shekhawati
D. Gavari      4. Mewar
questions.exp: Chari is danced at Kishangarh, the Agni dance at Katariyasar in Bikaner, the Geendad in Shekhawati and Gavari in Mewar.

questions.q: Which one of the following instrument-class pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The Manjira is a pair of small cymbals and is a ghan (idiophone) instrument. Avanaddh vadya are drums with a stretched membrane.

questions.q: Which one of the following dance-community pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The Chakri dance belongs to the Kanjar community of Baran and Kota. The Garasias perform the Walar, Loor and Jawara dances.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a wind (sushir) instrument?
questions.exp: The Surinda is a bowed string (tat) instrument used by the Langas. The Algoza, Satara and Bankiya are all wind instruments.

questions.q: Which one of the following theatre form-region pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Tamasha is the folk theatre of Jaipur, performed by the Bhatt family during Gangaur. Bikaner is associated with the Rammat.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Ghoomar dance is NOT correct?
opts: It is believed to have originated among the Bhils
It is performed at Gangaur and Teej
It is performed only by men during Holi
Its name derives from the circular movement of the dancers
questions.exp: Ghoomar is a women's dance. The men's Holi dance of Mewar and Marwar is the Gair.

questions.q:
Arrange the following Rajasthani instruments in descending order of the number of strings they carry:
I. Ektara
II. Sarangi
III. Chautara
IV. Kamaycha
questions.exp: The Sarangi carries about 27 strings, the Kamaycha about 17, the Chautara four and the Ektara one.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in the correct chronological order:
I. Nartan Nirnay by Pundarik Vitthal
II. Sangeet Raj by Maharana Kumbha
III. Inscription of Kalbeliya on the UNESCO list
IV. Radha Govind Sangeet Sar compiled under Sawai Pratap Singh
questions.exp: Sangeet Raj belongs to the fifteenth century, Nartan Nirnay to the late sixteenth, Radha Govind Sangeet Sar to the late eighteenth and the Kalbeliya inscription to 2010.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Manganiyars of western Rajasthan traditionally play the Kamaycha.
Reason (R): The Kamaycha is a bowed instrument whose round resonator is covered with goat skin.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: Both statements are factually correct, but the construction of the Kamaycha does not explain why the Manganiyars in particular play it; that is a matter of hereditary community practice.

chapters.title: Language, Dialects, Literature; Saints, Sects and Folk Deities
factsheet: Rajasthani descends from Maru-Gurjar (Gurjar) Apabhramsa; sequence Sanskrit > Pali > Prakrit > Apabhramsa > Rajasthani.
George Abraham Grierson (Linguistic Survey of India, 1908) gave the first scientific classification of Rajasthani dialects and popularised the name 'Rajasthani'.

Dingal - western Rajasthan, Charan poets, Marwari base, veer rasa (Dhola Maru ra Duha, Veli Krishan Rukmani Ri, Achaldas Khichi ri Vachanika). Pingal - eastern Rajasthan, Bhatt poets, Braj-mixed, shringar rasa (Prithviraj Raso, Vansh Bhaskar).
Marwari - widest dialect by area (Jodhpur, Pali, Nagaur, Bikaner, Jaisalmer); Mewari - Udaipur, Chittorgarh, Bhilwara, Rajsamand; Dhundhari - Jaipur, Tonk, Dausa.
Hadauti - Kota, Bundi, Baran, Jhalawar. Mewati - Alwar and Bharatpur (Mev community). Ahirwati/Rathi - Behror, Kotputli, Mundawar.
Bagri - Sri Ganganagar and Hanumangarh; Wagdi - Dungarpur and Banswara (Vagad); Godwadi - Pali, Sirohi, Jalore (Godwar); Shekhawati - Sikar, Churu, Jhunjhunu.
Malvi - Pratapgarh/Jhalawar; Rangdi - Pratapgarh (Marwari + Malvi mix); Nimadi - a Malvi sub-dialect; Devdawati - Sirohi; Khairadi - Shahpura-Bundi belt; Dhatki - Jaisalmer-Barmer border.
Riddles in Rajasthani are called Aadi, Hiyali and Bujh (asked RAS Pre 2024).
Kuvalayamala - Uddyotana Suri, 778 AD, composed at Jabalipur (Jalore) in Prakrit; names 18 desi languages including 'Maru'.
Bharateshwar Bahubali Ghor (Vajrasen Suri, 1168) - oldest available Jain work in Rajasthani; Hansawali - Asayit (RAS Pre 2016).
Prithviraj Raso - Chand Bardai (Pingal); Bisaldev Raso - Narpati Nalha; Khuman Raso - Dalpat Vijay; Shatrusal Raso - Dungarsi.
Hammir Mahakavya - Nayanchandra Suri (Sanskrit); Kanhadde Prabandh - Padmanabh (1455, Jalore); Achaldas Khichi ri Vachanika - Shivdas Gadan (1423, Gagron, Dingal).
Veli Krishan Rukmani Ri - Prithviraj Rathore 'Pithal'; Dursa Adha called it the 'fifth Veda' / 'nineteenth Purana'.
Rajprashasti - Ranchhod Bhatt Telang, on 25 black stone slabs at Rajsamand lake; the largest inscription in India. Vansh Bhaskar - Suryamal Mishran of Bundi.
Nainsi ri Khyat and Marwar ra Pargana ri Vigat - Muhnot Nainsi, 'the Abul Fazl of Rajasthan', Diwan of Maharaja Jaswant Singh of Marwar; Suraj Prakash - Karnidan.
Dhola Maru ra Duha - Kavi Kallol (Dingal); Padmavat - Malik Muhammad Jayasi (Awadhi, 1540); Bhakt Mal - Nabhadas.
First Sahitya Akademi Award in Rajasthani: Vijaydan Detha 'Bijji', 1974, for Bataan Ri Phulwari; Kanhaiyalal Sethia won it in 1976 for Leeltans.
Jasnathi sect - Jasnath (b. 1482) of Katariyasar, Bikaner; 36 rules; the Agni (fire) dance; followers largely Jats.
Vishnoi - Jambhoji born 1451 at Pipasar (Nagaur); sect founded 1485 at Samrathal Dhora; 29 rules; samadhi at Mukam (Nokha, Bikaner); Khejarli sacrifice of 1730 led by Amrita Devi, 363 martyrs.
Dadu Panth - Dadu Dayal (1544-1603), born at Ahmedabad, main seat Naraina (Jaipur); 52 'thambas'; branches Khalsa, Naga, Uttarade, Khaki, Virakt; disciples Rajjab (Sanganer), Sundardas, Garibdas.
Ramsnehi branches: Shahpura/Bhilwara (Ramcharan, main peeth, Phuldol festival), Rain/Nagaur (Daryavji), Khedapa/Jodhpur (Ramdas), Sinhthal/Bikaner (Haridas).
Nimbarka peeth - Salemabad (Kishangarh, Ajmer), philosophy Dvaitadvaita; Pushtimarg (Vallabh) centre - Nathdwara, Shrinathji installed under Rana Raj Singh, 1672.
Laldasi - Laldas (1540-1648), born Dholidoob (Alwar), Mev by birth; samadhi at Sherpur (Alwar); main seat Nagla (Bharatpur); greeting 'Jairam'.
Charandasi - Charandas, born Dehra (Alwar) 1703; the only Rajasthani sect whose principal seat is outside the state, at Delhi; women saints Sahjo Bai and Daya Bai (Daya Bodh, Vinay Malika).
Alakhiya sect - Lalgiri of Sulakhaniya (Churu), centre Bikaner. Meera Bai - married Bhojraj, son of Rana Sanga; guru Sant Raidas; 'Radha of Rajasthan'.
Panch Peer of Rajasthan: Pabuji, Harbhuji, Ramdevji, Mehaji and Gogaji.
Gogaji - born Dadrewa (Churu); 'Jahar Peer'; shrine Gogamedi (Nohar, Hanumangarh); Goga Navami on Bhadrapad Krishna Navami; the snake deity, revered by Hindus and Muslims alike.

Tejaji - Kharnal (Nagaur), Jat, mare Leelan, bitten on the tongue by the serpent, died at Sursura (Ajmer); Parbatsar cattle fair; invoked against snakebite. Pabuji - Kolu (Phalodi), mare Kesar Kalmi, 'god of camels', Pabuji ki Phad sung with the Ravanhatha.

Ramdevji - Ramdevra/Runicha (Jaisalmer), Tanwar Rajput, 'Ramsa Peer'; worshipped as footprints (pagalya); Kamdiya panth; Terahtali by Kamad women; fair Bhadrapad Shukla 2-11. Devnarayan - Asind/Malaseri (Bhilwara), Gurjar deity, phad sung with the Jantar.

Karni Mata - Deshnok (Bikaner), Charan kuldevi, white rats 'kaba'; Jeen Mata - Revasa (Sikar); Shila Devi - Amber; Kaila Devi - Karauli (Languriya songs); Aai Mata - Bilara (Sirvi kuldevi); Sundha Mata - Jalore (headless idol, Rajasthan's first ropeway).

questions.q: The Rajasthani language is generally held to have developed from which Apabhramsa?
questions.exp: Most scholars, following Dr Motilal Menariya, derive Rajasthani from Maru-Gurjar or Gurjar Apabhramsa. The line of descent runs Sanskrit - Pali - Prakrit - Apabhramsa - Rajasthani.

questions.q: Who gave the first scientific classification of the dialects of Rajasthani?
questions.exp: Grierson classified Rajasthani dialects in the Linguistic Survey of India (1908) and popularised the very name 'Rajasthani'. Tessitori did pioneering work on old Western Rajasthani but did not give the classification.

questions.q: 'Prithviraj Raso', the best-known Raso work of Rajasthan, was composed by
questions.exp: Chand Bardai, court poet of Prithviraj Chauhan III, composed the Prithviraj Raso in the Pingal style. Jayanak wrote the Sanskrit Prithviraj Vijay.

questions.q: 'Khuman Raso', which traces the Mewar line from Bappa Rawal onwards, was written by
questions.exp: Khuman Raso is attributed to Dalpat Vijay. Karnidan wrote Suraj Prakash; RPSC in 2024 used 'Khuman Raso - Karnidan' as the deliberately wrong pair.

questions.q: The Prakrit work 'Kuvalayamala', which mentions eighteen desi languages including 'Maru', was composed by
questions.exp: Uddyotana Suri completed the Kuvalayamala in 778 AD at Jabalipur (Jalore) during the reign of the Pratihara ruler Vatsaraja. It is a key source for the early form of Rajasthani.

questions.q: 'Achaldas Khichi ri Vachanika', regarded as the finest Vachanika of Rajasthani, was written by
questions.exp: Shivdas Gadan composed it in Dingal around 1423, describing Achaldas Khichi's fight for Gagron against Hoshang Shah of Malwa. Jagga Khidiya wrote the Vachanika Rathore Ratan Singh ji ri.

questions.q: 'Veli Krishan Rukmani Ri', praised by Dursa Adha as the 'fifth Veda', was composed by
questions.exp: Prithviraj Rathore of Bikaner, known as 'Pithal', wrote this Dingal classic. Dursa Adha called it the fifth Veda and the nineteenth Purana.

questions.q: The 'Rajprashasti', engraved on twenty-five black stone slabs at the Rajsamand lake, was composed by
questions.exp: Ranchhod Bhatt Telang composed the Rajprashasti in Sanskrit in the reign of Maharana Raj Singh of Mewar. It is the largest inscription in India.

questions.q: Which chronicler of Marwar, Diwan under Maharaja Jaswant Singh, is called the 'Abul Fazl of Rajasthan'?
questions.exp: Muhnot Nainsi wrote Nainsi ri Khyat and Marwar ra Pargana ri Vigat, the latter being an early statistical survey of Marwar. Dayaldas wrote the Bikaner khyat.

questions.q: 'Hansawali', an early work of Rajasthani literature, was written by
questions.exp: Hansawali is attributed to Asayit (Asaigu) and is counted among the earliest available works in Rajasthani. Vajrasen Suri's Bharateshwar Bahubali Ghor (1168) is the oldest surviving Jain work in the language.

questions.q: In Rajasthani, the words 'Aadi' and 'Hiyali' are used for
questions.exp: Aadi, Hiyali and Bujh are the Rajasthani terms for riddles. RPSC asked this directly in the 2024 Prelims.

questions.q: Who was the first recipient of the Sahitya Akademi Award in the Rajasthani language?
questions.exp: Vijaydan Detha 'Bijji' received the first Rajasthani Sahitya Akademi Award in 1974 for 'Bataan Ri Phulwari'. Kanhaiyalal Sethia won it in 1976 for 'Leeltans'.

questions.q: The Wagdi dialect of Rajasthani is spoken mainly in which region?
questions.exp: Wagdi is the speech of the Vagad region, i.e. Dungarpur and Banswara, and is heavily influenced by Gujarati and Mewari. Bagri belongs to Ganganagar-Hanumangarh.

questions.q: The Ahirwati (Rathi) dialect is spoken in which part of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Ahirwati, named after the Ahir community, is spoken in the Behror-Kotputli-Mundawar belt of the old Alwar-Jaipur border. Hadauti belongs to Kota, Bundi, Baran and Jhalawar.

questions.q: The Bagri dialect of Rajasthani is chiefly spoken in
questions.exp: Bagri is spoken in the Bagar tract of Sri Ganganagar and Hanumangarh and shows strong Punjabi and Haryanvi influence. Malvi belongs to Pratapgarh-Jhalawar.

questions.q: The principal seat of the Jasnathi sect, founded by Jasnath ji, is at
questions.exp: Jasnath was born at Katariyasar in Bikaner, which remains the sect's main seat. The Jasnathis observe 36 rules and are famous for the Agni (fire) dance.

questions.q: Guru Jambheshwar (Jambhoji) founded the Vishnoi sect in 1485 at which place?
questions.exp: Jambhoji, born at Pipasar in Nagaur in 1451, founded the sect at Samrathal Dhora in Bikaner in 1485 and laid down 29 rules. His samadhi is at Mukam (Nokha, Bikaner).

questions.q: The main seat (peeth) of the Dadu Panth is located at
questions.exp: Dadu Dayal, born at Ahmedabad in 1544, made Naraina near Dudu in Jaipur his principal centre; his followers are organised in the '52 thambas'. Rajjab, his disciple, belonged to Sanganer.

questions.q: The principal peeth of the Ramsnehi sect, where the Phuldol festival is celebrated, is at
questions.exp: Sant Ramcharan established the main Ramsnehi peeth at Shahpura in Bhilwara, where the Phuldol festival is held after Holi. Rain, Khedapa and Sinhthal are the other three branches.

questions.q: Salemabad in Ajmer district is the principal seat of which sect?
questions.exp: The Nimbarka sect, which teaches Dvaitadvaita and worships the Yugal form of Radha-Krishna, has its chief peeth at Salemabad near Kishangarh. Nathdwara is the centre of the Vallabh sect.

questions.q: Which sect founded in Rajasthan has its principal seat outside the state, at Delhi?
questions.exp: Charandas, born at Dehra in Alwar in 1703, established the Charandasi sect whose main seat is at Delhi. His women disciples Sahjo Bai and Daya Bai are celebrated saint-poets.

questions.q: Swami Lalgiri, born at Sulakhaniya in Churu, founded which sect whose centre is at Bikaner?
questions.exp: The Alakhiya sect founded by Lalgiri (Alakhgiri) worships the formless 'Alakh' and has its centre at Bikaner. Its texts include Alakh Stuti Prakash.

questions.q: Meera Bai was married to Bhojraj, the son of which ruler of Mewar?
questions.exp: Meera was married to Bhojraj, eldest son of Rana Sanga, in 1516. Sant Raidas is traditionally regarded as her guru, and she is called the 'Radha of Rajasthan'.

questions.q: The shrine of Gogaji, known as Gogamedi, is situated in which district?
questions.exp: Gogamedi lies in Nohar tehsil of Hanumangarh; Gogaji was born at Dadrewa in Churu. The Goga Navami fair falls on Bhadrapad Krishna Navami.

questions.q: The folk deity Tejaji was born at which village?
questions.exp: Tejaji was born at Kharnal in Nagaur to a Jat family. He is invoked against snakebite and his great cattle fair is held at Parbatsar.

questions.q: Ramdevji is worshipped at Ramdevra (Runicha), situated in which district?
questions.exp: Ramdevra near Pokhran in Jaisalmer is his samadhi sthal; the fair runs from Bhadrapad Shukla Dwitiya to Ekadashi. He is worshipped in the form of footprints (pagalya) rather than an idol.

questions.q: Which folk deity of Rajasthan is worshipped as the protector of camels and is honoured especially by the Raika-Rebari community?
questions.exp: Pabuji Rathore of Kolu (Phalodi) is credited with bringing camels to Marwar and is the 'god of camels'. The Pabuji ki Phad is sung by Nayak Bhopas to the Ravanhatha.

questions.q: The temple of Karni Mata, famous for its white rats called 'kaba', is at
questions.exp: Karni Mata's temple at Deshnok in Bikaner is the kuldevi shrine of the Charans and the aradhya devi of the Bikaner Rathores. She is credited with laying the foundation of Mehrangarh in 1459.

questions.q: The Kaila Devi temple, where the Lakhi fair is held on the banks of the Kalisil river, is in which district?
questions.exp: Kaila Devi's temple stands on the Trikut hills in Karauli. She is the kuldevi of the Jadaun (Yadav) rulers and is praised in the Languriya songs.

questions.q: Sundha Mata, worshipped in the form of a headless idol and served by Rajasthan's first ropeway, is located in which district?
questions.exp: The Sundha Mata temple is on Sundha hill in Jaswantpura tehsil of Jalore. Rajasthan's first ropeway was built here in 2006.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Dingal and Pingal styles of Rajasthani literature:
I. Dingal was mainly cultivated by Charan poets of western Rajasthan and is dominated by veer rasa.
II. Pingal carries a strong admixture of Braj and was mainly cultivated by Bhatt poets of eastern Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Both are correct. Dingal works include Dhola Maru ra Duha and Veli Krishan Rukmani Ri; Prithviraj Raso and Vansh Bhaskar belong to the Pingal tradition.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the dialects of Rajasthani:
I. Marwari covers the largest area among the dialects of Rajasthani.
II. The Dingal literary style is based on the Braj language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Only I is correct. Dingal is based on the western form of Marwari; it is Pingal that carries the Braj element.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Guru Jambheshwar and the Vishnoi sect:
I. The sect prescribes twenty-nine rules, several of which protect trees and wildlife.
II. The sect was founded in 1485 at Samrathal Dhora.
III. The samadhi of Jambhoji is at Pipasar in Nagaur.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. Pipasar was Jambhoji's birthplace; his samadhi is at Mukam in Nokha tehsil of Bikaner. The Khejarli sacrifice of 1730, led by Amrita Devi, was made by Vishnois to save khejri trees.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Sant Dadu Dayal:
I. He was born at Ahmedabad in Gujarat.
II. The principal seat of the Dadu Panth is at Sanganer.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Only I is correct. The main seat of the Dadu Panth is Naraina near Dudu in Jaipur; Sanganer was the birthplace of his disciple Rajjab. Sundardas, another disciple, is called the 'second Shankaracharya'.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Sant Laldas:
I. He was born at Dholidoob in Alwar and belonged to the Mev community.
II. The principal seat of the Laldasi sect is at Nagla in Bharatpur.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Both are correct. Laldas (1540-1648), a Muslim by birth, preached Nirgun devotion to Ram and Hindu-Muslim unity; his samadhi is at Sherpur in Alwar.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Ramsnehi sect:
I. It preaches Sagun devotion centred on the idol of Ram.
II. Its collection of sacred utterances is known as the Anabhai Vani.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Only II is correct. The Ramsnehi sect preaches Nirgun devotion to the formless Ram; its places of worship are called Ramdwaras and the Phuldol festival is its chief celebration.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the folk deity Ramdevji:
I. He is worshipped in the form of footprints rather than an idol.
II. The Terahtali dance is performed in his honour by women of the Kamad community.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Both are correct. Ramdevji, a Tanwar Rajput of Runicha, opposed untouchability; his followers form the Kamdiya panth and his fair at Ramdevra is a famous meeting ground of Hindus and Muslims.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the folk deity Gogaji:
I. He belonged to the Rathore clan.
II. He is popularly known as 'Jahar Peer' and is counted among the Panch Peer of Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Only II is correct. Gogaji was a Chauhan. He is revered by Hindus and Muslims alike, and farmers tie the 'Goga Rakhdi' before ploughing.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the folk deity Tejaji:
I. According to tradition he was bitten by a serpent on his tongue.
II. His largest cattle fair is held at Parbatsar in Nagaur district.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Both are correct. Tejaji is worshipped as a cure for snakebite; his mare was named Leelan and he died at Sursura in Ajmer.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Devnarayan ji:
I. He is chiefly worshipped by the Gurjar community.
II. His phad is sung to the accompaniment of the Ravanhatha.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Only I is correct. The Devnarayan phad is sung with the Jantar; the Ravanhatha accompanies the Pabuji ki Phad. His main shrines are at Asind and Malaseri Dungri in Bhilwara.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Karni Mata:
I. She is the kuldevi of the Charans and the aradhya devi of the Bikaner Rathores.
II. She is traditionally credited with laying the foundation stone of the Jaigarh fort.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Only I is correct. Tradition credits Karni Mata with laying the foundation of Mehrangarh at Jodhpur in 1459, not of Jaigarh.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Work)   List-II (Author)
A. Bisaldev Raso   1. Padmanabh
B. Kanhadde Prabandh   2. Narpati Nalha
C. Hammir Mahakavya   3. Kavi Kallol
D. Dhola Maru ra Duha   4. Nayanchandra Suri
questions.exp: Bisaldev Raso - Narpati Nalha; Kanhadde Prabandh - Padmanabh (1455); Hammir Mahakavya - Nayanchandra Suri; Dhola Maru ra Duha - Kavi Kallol.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Work)   List-II (Author)
A. Vansh Bhaskar   1. Muhnot Nainsi
B. Suraj Prakash   2. Suryamal Mishran
C. Marwar ra Pargana ri Vigat   3. Ranchhod Bhatt Telang
D. Rajprashasti   4. Karnidan
questions.exp: Vansh Bhaskar - Suryamal Mishran of Bundi; Suraj Prakash - Karnidan; Marwar ra Pargana ri Vigat - Muhnot Nainsi; Rajprashasti - Ranchhod Bhatt Telang.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Dialect)   List-II (Region)
A. Hadauti   1. Alwar and Bharatpur
B. Mewati   2. Kota and Jhalawar
C. Godwadi   3. Sikar and Jhunjhunu
D. Shekhawati   4. Pali and Sirohi
questions.exp: Hadauti - Kota, Bundi, Baran, Jhalawar; Mewati - Alwar and Bharatpur; Godwadi - the Godwar tract of Pali, Sirohi and Jalore; Shekhawati - Sikar, Churu and Jhunjhunu.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Sect)   List-II (Main seat)
A. Vishnoi   1. Salemabad
B. Nimbarka   2. Katariyasar
C. Jasnathi   3. Naraina
D. Dadu Panth   4. Mukam
questions.exp: Mukam (Nokha, Bikaner) holds Jambhoji's samadhi; Salemabad is the Nimbarka peeth; Katariyasar is the Jasnathi centre; Naraina is the Dadu Panth's headquarters.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Ramsnehi branch)   List-II (Founder)
A. Shahpura   1. Sant Daryavji
B. Rain   2. Sant Haridas
C. Khedapa   3. Sant Ramcharan
D. Sinhthal   4. Sant Ramdas
questions.exp: Shahpura (Bhilwara) - Ramcharan, the main peeth; Rain (Nagaur) - Daryavji; Khedapa (Jodhpur) - Ramdas; Sinhthal (Bikaner) - Haridas.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Folk deity)   List-II (Principal shrine)
A. Pabuji   1. Asind
B. Devnarayan   2. Tilwara
C. Mallinath   3. Bengti
D. Harbhuji   4. Kolu
questions.exp: Pabuji - Kolu (Phalodi); Devnarayan - Asind (Bhilwara); Mallinath - Tilwara on the Luni; Harbhuji - Bengti (Baingti) in Phalodi.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Folk goddess)   List-II (Place)
A. Jeen Mata   1. Amber
B. Shila Devi   2. Bilara
C. Aai Mata   3. Jhunjhunu
D. Rani Sati   4. Revasa
questions.exp: Jeen Mata - Revasa (Sikar); Shila Devi - Amber (Jaipur), brought by Man Singh I; Aai Mata - Bilara (Jodhpur), kuldevi of the Sirvis; Rani Sati - Jhunjhunu.

questions.q: Which one of the following work-author pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Khuman Raso was written by Dalpat Vijay; Karnidan is the author of Suraj Prakash. RPSC used exactly this pair in the 2024 Prelims.

questions.q: Which one of the following dialect-region pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Rangdi is spoken in the Pratapgarh area and is a mixture of Marwari and Malvi. Sri Ganganagar and Hanumangarh speak Bagri.

questions.q: Which one of the following saint-sect pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Charandas founded the Charandasi sect, whose seat is at Delhi. The Laldasi sect was founded by Sant Laldas of Alwar.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs relating to folk deities is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Ramdevji is associated with Runicha/Ramdevra in Jaisalmer; Kolu in Phalodi is the birthplace of Pabuji.

questions.q: Which one of the following folk goddess-district pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The Brahmani Mata temple, where the goddess is worshipped from the back and a donkey fair is held, is at Saursen in Baran district.

questions.q:
Arrange the following literary works in correct chronological order of composition (earliest first):
I. Kanhadde Prabandh
II. Kuvalayamala
III. Hammir Mahakavya
IV. Bharateshwar Bahubali Ghor
questions.exp: Kuvalayamala (778 AD), Bharateshwar Bahubali Ghor (1168), Hammir Mahakavya (c. 1403) and Kanhadde Prabandh (1455).

questions.q:
Arrange the following folk deities of Rajasthan in the correct chronological order of their traditionally accepted period (earliest first):
I. Ramdevji
II. Gogaji
III. Pabuji
IV. Tejaji
questions.exp: The traditional dates are Gogaji (10th century), Tejaji (11th century), Pabuji (13th century) and Ramdevji (14th-15th century).

chapters.title: Social Life: Fairs, Festivals, Customs, Dress, Ornaments, Tribes
factsheet: Pushkar fair (Ajmer) - Kartik Ekadashi to Kartik Purnima; camel fair; site of India's principal Brahma temple.
Chandrabhaga cattle fair - Jhalrapatan (Jhalawar), on the Chandrabhaga river, Kartik Purnima.
Beneshwar fair - Sabla/Navatapura, Dungarpur, at the Som-Mahi-Jakham confluence, Magh Purnima; called the 'Kumbh of the tribals (Bhils)'.
Mallinath cattle fair - Tilwara (Balotra) on the Luni, Chaitra; the oldest cattle fair of Rajasthan. Tejaji cattle fair - Parbatsar (Nagaur), Bhadrapad.
Ramdevra fair (Jaisalmer) Bhadrapad Shukla 2-11; Gogamedi fair (Nohar, Hanumangarh) Bhadrapad Krishna Navami; Kolayat fair (Bikaner) Kartik Purnima, sacred to Kapil Muni.
Kaila Devi 'Lakhi' mela - Karauli, Chaitra Shukla Ashtami, Kalisil river, Trikut hills. Karni Mata fair - Deshnok, Chaitra and Ashwin Navratri.
Khatu Shyamji fair - Sikar, Phalgun; Mahaveerji fair - Chandangaon (Hindaun, Karauli) on the Gambhir; Ghushmeshwar - Shivad (Sawai Madhopur), reckoned the twelfth jyotirlinga.
Urs of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti - Ajmer, 1-6 Rajab; Galiakot urs (Dungarpur) - of the Dawoodi Bohras, at the dargah of Syed Fakhruddin.
Sheetla Mata fair - Chaksu (Jaipur), Chaitra Krishna Ashtami; the goddess is worshipped in a broken idol, her vehicle is the donkey and her priests come from the Kumhar caste.
Sitabari fair - Kelwara (Baran), the great fair of the Sahariyas. Khejarli fair (Jodhpur) - Bhadrapad Shukla Dashami, memorial to the 363 Vishnoi tree-martyrs of 1730.
Gulabi (Pink) Gangaur - Nathdwara, Rajsamand. Dhinga Gavar - Jodhpur, in Vaishakh, where women in disguise dominate the streets. Ghudla - Marwar, Chaitra, girls carry perforated pots with lamps.
Gangaur - Chaitra Shukla Tritiya, worship of Isar and Gauri by women; the saying runs 'Teej tyoharan ri shuruat, Gangaur tyoharan ro ant'.
Hariyali Teej - Shravan Shukla Tritiya, the great Teej of Jaipur; Kajali (Badi) Teej - Bhadrapad Krishna Tritiya, the great Teej of Bundi.
Akha Teej / Akshaya Tritiya (Vaishakh Shukla 3) - an 'abuj' muhurat, traditionally the season of child marriages; Sanjhi - Ashwin Krishna Paksha, cow-dung wall art made by girls.

Customs: Jalwa Pujan (well worship after childbirth), Jadula/Mundan, Dhundh; Sagai/Tika, Bindoli, Toran, Pheras; Mausar (Mosar) and Nukta are death feasts; Nata pratha is remarriage by settlement; Dapa is bride-price among Garasia, Sahariya and Damor.
Men's dress: Dhoti, Angarkha/Angarkhi, Atamsukh (long winter coat), Dogla, Patka, Mojari. Pagri styles - Amarshahi, Shahjahani, Khidkidar, Udaishahi, Rajshahi, Jodhpuri safa.
Kasumal is a deep red/crimson colour, named from kusum (safflower), used in Rajasthani costume (RAS Pre 2024).

Women's dress: Ghaghra, Kanchli/Kurti, Kachhabu, Odhna/Chunari, Pomcha (yellow ground with lotus motifs, worn on the birth of a child), Lehariya (diagonal stripes, Teej wear), Mothra (crosswise lehariya producing checks).
Head ornaments - Rakhdi/Borla, Sheeshphool, Memand, Tikda; ear - Toti, Jhumka, Surliya, Bali; nose - Nath, Nathdi, Bhanwariya, Laung.
Neck - Timaniya, Hansli, Kanthi, Aad, Hamel, Madaliya; arm and hand - Bajuband, Chuda, Gajra, Pahunchi, Hathphool.
Waist - Kandora, Kardhani, Tagdi; foot - Payal, Nevari, Kadi, Anwala, Bichhiya, Rimjhol. Toti is an ear ornament (RAS Pre 2021).
Census 2011: Scheduled Tribes form 13.48% of Rajasthan's population. Meena is the largest ST (about 47% of the state's ST population), Bhil second (about 44%), Garasia third.
Bhil - Banswara, Dungarpur, Udaipur, Pratapgarh; village head 'Gameti', hamlet 'Phala', group of hamlets 'Pal'; shifting cultivation 'Walra' - 'Chimata' on hill slopes and 'Dajiya' on the plains.
Bhil dances - Gawari (Rai) performed in Shravan-Bhadrapad in Mewar, and Ghoomar; Bhils are called the 'bowmen of India'.
Mina - divided into Zamindar Mina and Chowkidar Mina; the most educated tribe of the state; Meena Kshatriya Mahasabha founded 1933; removed from the Criminal Tribes list in 1952.

Garasia - Abu Road and Pindwara (Sirohi), Bali (Pali), Gogunda and Kotra (Udaipur); marriage forms Mor Bandhiya, Peharavana and Tanana; bride-price 'Dapa'; house 'Gher', hamlet 'Faliya'; Valar/Gaur dance.

Sahariya - the only Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) of Rajasthan; Kishanganj and Shahbad tehsils of Baran; headman 'Kotwal'; huts called Topa, Korua or Gopna; Sitabari is their sacred fair.
Damor - Dungarpur (Simalwara, Aspur) and Banswara; headman 'Mukhi'; the Gyaras fair. Kathodi - Kotra and Jhadol in Udaipur, migrants from Maharashtra who make katha from khair; Mavlia dance.
Kanjar - Hadoti; deities Jogania Mata, Chauth Mata and Hanuman; Chakri and Dhakad dances. Sansi - Bharatpur; sub-groups Bija and Mala; kuldevi Sikodari Mata.

Gadia Lohar - nomadic blacksmiths who vowed not to return to Chittor after 1568; Jawaharlal Nehru led them into Chittorgarh fort in 1955. Rabari/Raika are the camel-breeders of Marwar. The Tribal Area Development (TAD) department has its headquarters at Udaipur.

questions.q: The Chandrabhaga cattle fair of Rajasthan is held at
questions.exp: The Chandrabhaga fair is held at Jhalrapatan in Jhalawar district on the banks of the Chandrabhaga river on Kartik Purnima.

questions.q: The Beneshwar fair, called the 'Kumbh of the tribals', is held in which district?
questions.exp: Beneshwar is held at Sabla in Dungarpur at the confluence of the Som, Mahi and Jakham rivers on Magh Purnima, and draws Bhils from Rajasthan, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh.

questions.q: The Pushkar fair of Ajmer culminates on which day?
questions.exp: The Pushkar fair runs from Kartik Ekadashi to Kartik Purnima. Pushkar has the country's principal temple of Brahma.

questions.q: The great cattle fair associated with the folk deity Tejaji is held at
questions.exp: The Tejaji cattle fair is held at Parbatsar in Nagaur district in Bhadrapad. Tejaji was born at Kharnal in the same district.

questions.q: The Kapil Muni fair held on Kartik Purnima takes place at Kolayat in which district?
questions.exp: Kolayat lies in Bikaner district and is associated with the sage Kapil. The fair coincides with the Pushkar fair on Kartik Purnima.

questions.q: The Sitabari fair at Kelwara in Baran district is chiefly the fair of which tribe?
questions.exp: Sitabari is the most important religious gathering of the Sahariyas, the only PVTG of Rajasthan, who live in the Kishanganj and Shahbad tehsils of Baran.

questions.q: The 'Gulabi Gangaur' is celebrated at which place in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Gulabi (Pink) Gangaur is the distinctive Gangaur of Nathdwara in Rajsamand district. Jodhpur is famous for the Dhinga Gavar.

questions.q: The Mallinath cattle fair, the oldest cattle fair of Rajasthan, is held at Tilwara on the bank of which river?
questions.exp: The Mallinath fair is held at Tilwara (Balotra) on the Luni in Chaitra. The Malani tract of western Rajasthan takes its name from Mallinath.

questions.q: Gangaur, the festival of Isar and Gauri, is celebrated on which day?
questions.exp: Gangaur falls on Chaitra Shukla Tritiya, eighteen days after Holi. The Rajasthani saying runs 'Teej tyoharan ri shuruat, Gangaur tyoharan ro ant'.

questions.q: 'Dhinga Gavar', in which women in disguise take over the streets, is a festival particularly of
questions.exp: Dhinga Gavar is celebrated at Jodhpur in Vaishakh, after Gangaur, and is one of the few Indian festivals in which women alone take the leading role.

questions.q: In the Marwar region, girls carry a perforated earthen pot with a lamp inside during which festival?
questions.exp: The Ghudla festival of Marwar is celebrated in Chaitra, when girls carry a perforated pot ('ghudla') lit from within and sing Ghudla songs.

questions.q: Kajali (Badi) Teej, celebrated on Bhadrapad Krishna Tritiya, is most famously observed at
questions.exp: Bundi's Kajali Teej falls on Bhadrapad Krishna Tritiya, while Jaipur's Hariyali Teej falls on Shravan Shukla Tritiya.

questions.q: The Sanjhi festival, in which girls make figures of cow dung on walls, is celebrated during
questions.exp: Sanjhi is observed during the Ashwin Krishna Paksha, the Pitru Paksha fortnight, and ends with the immersion of the Sanjhi figures.

questions.q: In Rajasthani social custom, 'Mausar' (Mosar) refers to
opts: A pre-wedding procession of the groom
A feast given after a death
Worship of a well after childbirth
The bride price paid to the bride's father
questions.exp: Mausar or Mosar is the community feast given after a death, also called Nukta. It has long been criticised as a source of rural indebtedness.

questions.q: The 'Nata' custom prevalent in parts of Rajasthan refers to
opts: Remarriage of a woman by mutual settlement
Exchange of brides between two families
questions.exp: Nata pratha allows a woman to live with another man after a settlement, usually with a money payment. Exchange marriage is separately called 'Aata-Sata'.

questions.q: 'Jalwa Pujan' in Rajasthani custom is performed
opts: Before setting out on a journey
At the time of laying a house foundation
After the birth of a child
On the death anniversary of an ancestor
questions.exp: Jalwa Pujan is the worship of a well or water source by the mother a few days after childbirth. Other birth customs include Jadula (mundan) and Dhundh.

questions.q: 'Kasumal', a colour used in the costumes of Rajasthan, is
questions.exp: Kasumal is a deep red or crimson, named after kusum (safflower) from which the dye was obtained. RPSC asked this in the 2024 Prelims.

questions.q: The 'Pomcha' worn by Rajasthani women is associated with which occasion?
opts: The death of a family elder
questions.exp: The Pomcha is a yellow odhni printed with lotus motifs, traditionally given to and worn by a woman on the birth of a child.

questions.q: 'Atamsukh' in Rajasthani dress is
opts: A man's long loose winter garment
A style of turban worn in Mewar
A printed waist-cloth worn at weddings
questions.exp: Atamsukh is a long, loose padded garment worn by men in winter. Angarkhi and Dogla are other traditional upper garments for men.

questions.q: The 'Amarshahi' style of turban is associated with which princely house of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The Amarshahi pagri is named after Maharana Amar Singh of Mewar (Udaipur). Other well-known styles include Shahjahani, Khidkidar and Udaishahi.

questions.q: 'Mothra' in Rajasthani textiles is produced when
opts: Cloth is block-printed with indigo at Bagru
Cloth is dyed in a single deep red shade
Gold thread is woven into a Kota Doria sari
Lehariya is tied in both directions to form checks
questions.exp: When lehariya stripes are tied diagonally in both directions, the criss-cross check pattern produced is called Mothra.

questions.q: On which part of the body is the ornament 'Toti' worn?
questions.exp: Toti is an ear ornament of Rajasthani women. Nathdi is worn on the nose, Kandora on the waist and Nevari on the foot.

questions.q: 'Rakhdi' (Borla) is an ornament worn on the
questions.exp: Rakhdi or Borla is the round head ornament worn on the forehead, regarded as a mark of a married woman in Rajasthan.

questions.q: The ornament 'Timaniya' is worn on which part of the body?
questions.exp: Timaniya is a neck ornament, in the same family as Hansli, Kanthi and Aad.

questions.q: 'Kandora' is an ornament worn on the
questions.exp: Kandora, also called Kardhani or Tagdi, is the waist girdle. Bajuband is worn on the upper arm.

questions.q: As per Census 2011, which is the largest Scheduled Tribe of Rajasthan by population?
questions.exp: Meenas account for about 47% of Rajasthan's ST population, ahead of the Bhils at about 44%. Garasia is third and Sahariya fifth.

questions.q: Which tribe of Rajasthan has been notified as a Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG)?
questions.exp: The Sahariyas of Kishanganj and Shahbad tehsils in Baran district are the only PVTG of Rajasthan. Their headman is called the Kotwal.

questions.q: Among the Bhils, the head of a village is known as
questions.exp: The Bhil village head is the Gameti; a hamlet is a 'Phala' and a group of hamlets a 'Pal'. Mukhi is used among the Damors and Kotwal among the Sahariyas.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Pushkar fair:
I. It is held in the month of Kartik and is famous as a camel fair.
II. Pushkar has the principal temple of Brahma in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Both are correct. The fair runs from Kartik Ekadashi to Kartik Purnima, when pilgrims bathe in the Pushkar lake.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Khejarli sacrifice and its fair:
I. It was made against the felling of khejri trees ordered by the ruler of Bikaner.
II. Khejarli village lies in Nagaur district.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Both are wrong. In 1730, 363 Vishnois led by Amrita Devi died resisting the men of Maharaja Abhay Singh of Jodhpur, and Khejarli lies in Jodhpur district. The Amrita Devi Bishnoi award is named after her.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sheetla Mata fair of Chaksu:
I. The goddess is worshipped in the form of a broken idol.
II. Her vehicle is the donkey and her priests are drawn from the Kumhar caste.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Both are correct. The fair is held at Sheel ki Doongri, Chaksu (Jaipur) on Chaitra Krishna Ashtami, when cold food cooked the previous day is eaten.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the festivals of Rajasthan:
I. Kajali Teej is celebrated at Jaipur in the month of Shravan.
II. In the Rajasthani saying, the festival cycle begins with Teej and ends with Gangaur.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Only II is correct. Kajali (Badi) Teej belongs to Bundi and falls on Bhadrapad Krishna Tritiya; Jaipur's Hariyali Teej falls in Shravan.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about shifting cultivation among the Bhils:
I. Cultivation practised on hill slopes is called 'Dajiya'.
II. Cultivation practised in the plains is called 'Chimata'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Both are wrong; the terms are reversed. Among the Bhils, cultivation on hill slopes is 'Chimata' and on the plains 'Dajiya'; shifting cultivation as a whole is called 'Walra'.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Rajasthani textiles:
I. Lehariya is distinguished by concentric circular patterns.
II. Bandhej is a tie-and-dye craft for which Jodhpur, Jaipur and Sikar are noted centres.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Only II is correct. Lehariya carries diagonal wave-like stripes and is traditionally worn in the Teej-Shravan season.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Garasia tribe:
I. It is the third largest Scheduled Tribe of Rajasthan.
II. It is concentrated mainly in Baran and Jhalawar districts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Only I is correct. The Garasias live in Abu Road and Pindwara (Sirohi), Bali (Pali) and Gogunda-Kotra (Udaipur). Their marriage forms include Mor Bandhiya, Peharavana and Tanana, and the bride price is called 'Dapa'.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Gadia Lohars:
I. Tradition holds that they vowed not to return to Jodhpur after its fall in 1568.
II. Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel led a group of them into the fort in 1955 to release them from that vow.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Both are wrong. The vow related to Chittorgarh, which fell to Akbar in 1568, and it was Jawaharlal Nehru who led them into Chittorgarh fort in 1955. They are a nomadic community of blacksmiths travelling in bullock carts.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sahariya tribe:
I. It is the second largest Scheduled Tribe of Rajasthan by population.
II. It is concentrated in the Kishanganj and Shahbad tehsils of Baran district.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Only II is correct. By Census 2011 the Sahariyas are only the fifth largest ST of Rajasthan; the Bhils are second. Their headman is called the 'Kotwal' and their huts Topa, Korua or Gopna.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Fair)   List-II (District)
A. Chandrabhaga   1. Karauli
B. Beneshwar   2. Jhalawar
C. Kaila Devi   3. Jaisalmer
D. Ramdevra   4. Dungarpur
questions.exp: Chandrabhaga - Jhalrapatan (Jhalawar); Beneshwar - Sabla (Dungarpur); Kaila Devi - Karauli; Ramdevra - Jaisalmer.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Fair)   List-II (District)
A. Sitabari   1. Sikar
B. Khatu Shyamji   2. Sawai Madhopur
C. Ghushmeshwar   3. Baran
D. Galiakot   4. Dungarpur
questions.exp: Sitabari - Kelwara (Baran); Khatu Shyamji - Sikar; Ghushmeshwar - Shivad (Sawai Madhopur); Galiakot - Dungarpur, the Dawoodi Bohra dargah of Syed Fakhruddin.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Ornament)   List-II (Part of the body)
A. Sheeshphool   1. Nose
B. Bhanwariya   2. Upper arm
C. Bajuband   3. Foot
D. Nevari   4. Head
questions.exp: Sheeshphool is a head ornament, Bhanwariya a nose ornament, Bajuband is worn on the upper arm and Nevari on the foot.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Tribe)   List-II (Main area)
A. Sahariya   1. Kotra and Jhadol, Udaipur
B. Kathodi   2. Bharatpur
C. Kanjar   3. Baran
D. Sansi   4. Hadoti region
questions.exp: Sahariya - Baran; Kathodi - Kotra and Jhadol in Udaipur; Kanjar - the Hadoti region; Sansi - Bharatpur.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Festival)   List-II (Time)
A. Gangaur   1. Bhadrapad Krishna Tritiya
B. Hariyali Teej   2. Vaishakh Shukla Tritiya
C. Kajali Teej   3. Chaitra Shukla Tritiya
D. Akha Teej   4. Shravan Shukla Tritiya
questions.exp: Gangaur - Chaitra Shukla Tritiya; Hariyali Teej - Shravan Shukla Tritiya; Kajali Teej - Bhadrapad Krishna Tritiya; Akha Teej - Vaishakh Shukla Tritiya.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Item of dress)   List-II (Description)
A. Kanchli   1. Yellow odhni printed with lotus motifs
B. Pomcha   2. Woman's upper bodice
C. Angarkhi   3. Woman's pleated lower garment
D. Ghaghra   4. Man's upper garment
questions.exp: Kanchli is a woman's bodice; Pomcha the yellow lotus-printed odhni; Angarkhi a man's upper garment; Ghaghra the woman's pleated skirt.

questions.q: Which one of the following fair-district pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The Mallinath cattle fair is held at Tilwara near Balotra in the Barmer region, on the bank of the Luni, not in Jaisalmer.

questions.q: Which one of the following ornament-body part pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Anwala is a hollow circular ornament worn on the foot. Ear ornaments include Toti, Jhumka, Surliya and Bali.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the tribes of Rajasthan is NOT correct?
opts: The Meenas are divided into Zamindar and Chowkidar groups
The Damors are concentrated in Dungarpur and Banswara
The Kathodis traditionally prepare katha from the khair tree
The Rabari-Raikas are the principal tribe of the Hadoti region
questions.exp: The Rabari or Raika are the camel-breeding community of Marwar in western Rajasthan. The Kanjars are the community associated with the Hadoti region.

questions.q: Which one of the following festival-related statements is NOT correct?
opts: Gangaur is celebrated eighteen days after Holi
Akha Teej is regarded as an abuj muhurat
Sanjhi is celebrated during the Pitru Paksha fortnight
Dhinga Gavar is celebrated at Bikaner in the month of Magh
questions.exp: Dhinga Gavar is a Jodhpur festival celebrated in Vaishakh, shortly after Gangaur.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs relating to Rajasthani dress is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Lehariya - a cloth patterned with diagonal wave stripes
Kachhabu - a style of turban worn in Marwar
Atamsukh - a man's long winter garment
questions.exp: Kachhabu is a traditional upper garment worn by women, not a turban style. Turban styles include Amarshahi, Shahjahani, Khidkidar and Udaishahi.

questions.q: Which one of the following custom-meaning pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Bindoli - the groom's ceremonial procession before marriage
Nukta - a feast given after a death
Dapa - bride price paid among the Garasias
Jadula - the worship of a well after childbirth
questions.exp: Jadula is the first tonsure (mundan) ceremony of a child. The worship of a well after childbirth is Jalwa Pujan.

questions.q:
Arrange the following festivals of Rajasthan in the order in which they occur in the Vikram Samvat year, beginning with Chaitra:
I. Hariyali Teej
II. Gangaur
III. Ramdevra fair
IV. Akha Teej
questions.exp: Gangaur falls in Chaitra, Akha Teej in Vaishakh, Hariyali Teej in Shravan and the Ramdevra fair in Bhadrapad.

chapters.title: Indus Valley Civilisation
factsheet: Harappa — Ravi river, Montgomery (now Sahiwal) district, Pakistan; excavated 1921 by Daya Ram Sahni under Director-General John Marshall; the civilisation is named after it.
Mohenjodaro ('mound of the dead') — Indus river, Larkana district, Sindh; discovered 1922 by R.D. Banerji; Great Bath, Great Granary, Pashupati seal, Dancing Girl, Priest-King.
Kalibangan — Ghaggar (Saraswati) river, Hanumangarh district, Rajasthan; excavated by B.B. Lal and B.K. Thapar (1961-69); earliest ploughed field, seven fire altars, camel bones, bangle factory.
Lothal — Bhogavo river, Ahmedabad district, Gujarat; S.R. Rao (1955-62); dockyard, rice husk, Persian Gulf seal, double burial, bead factory, ivory scale.
Dholavira — Khadir Bet island, Kutch district, Gujarat; R.S. Bisht (1989-2005); three-part town, giant water reservoirs, ten-sign 'signboard'; UNESCO World Heritage Site, 2021.
Chanhudaro — Sindh; N.G. Majumdar (1931) and Ernest Mackay (1935-36); the only major Harappan city without a citadel; bead-makers' workshop, inkpot, lipstick.
Banawali — Fatehabad district, Haryana; R.S. Bisht (1973-74); terracotta model of a plough, barley, radial street pattern.
Rakhigarhi — Hisar district, Haryana; the largest Harappan site found in India; excavated by Amarendra Nath, later by Vasant Shinde.
Ropar (Rupnagar) — Sutlej river, Punjab; Y.D. Sharma (1953); the first Harappan site excavated after independence; a dog buried with a human.
Surkotada — Kutch district, Gujarat; J.P. Joshi; the most debated report of horse bones; pot burials.
Boundary sites: Sutkagendor (west, Dasht river, Balochistan), Alamgirpur (east, Hindon river, Meerut), Manda (north, Chenab, Jammu), Daimabad (south, Pravara river, Maharashtra).
Mehrgarh (Bolan pass, Balochistan) — Neolithic; earliest evidence of wheat and barley cultivation and of cotton in the subcontinent.
Town planning: grid layout with streets crossing at right angles; citadel on a raised platform to the west, lower town to the east; covered drains with manholes and soak-pits.
Burnt bricks were laid in the standard ratio 4:2:1 (length : breadth : thickness); house doorways opened on to side lanes, not on the main street.
The Great Bath at Mohenjodaro measures about 11.88 x 7.01 m and is 2.43 m deep, made watertight with bitumen.
Seals are mostly of steatite, square, with a pictographic legend and an animal device; the 'unicorn' is by far the commonest animal.
The Indus script is pictographic, still undeciphered, and written boustrophedon (the first line right to left, the next left to right).
Weights are of chert and follow a binary system in the lower denominations (1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64) and a decimal system above; an ivory scale came from Lothal and a shell scale from Mohenjodaro.
Metals in use: copper, bronze (copper + tin), gold, silver and lead. Iron was completely unknown to the Harappans.
The bronze 'Dancing Girl' (made by the lost-wax process) and the steatite bearded 'Priest-King' are both from Mohenjodaro; the bronze chariot group is from Daimabad.
The Harappans were the first people in the world to produce cotton; the Greeks later called Indian cotton 'Sindon'.
Trade: Meluha was the Mesopotamian name for the Indus region; Dilmun is Bahrain and Magan the Makran/Oman coast; lapis lazuli came from Shortughai in Afghanistan.
Burials: Cemetery R-37 and Cemetery H at Harappa; extended north-south burial at Kalibangan; double burial at Lothal; pot burial at Surkotada.
Fire altars have been reported from Kalibangan, Lothal and Banawali; no structure anywhere has been positively identified as a temple.
Religion: terracotta mother-goddess figurines, the proto-Shiva 'Pashupati' seal, phallic (lingam-yoni) worship, the pipal tree, the humped bull and the swastika.
The mature (urban) Harappan phase is dated c. 2600-1900 BCE; the older ASI dating is 2500-1750 BCE.
Kot Diji (excavated by Fazal Ahmed Khan) and Amri are early/pre-Harappan cultures; Bhirrana in Fatehabad has yielded the earliest Hakra-ware levels.

Decline theories: Aryan invasion (Mortimer Wheeler), recurrent floods (Marshall, S.R. Rao, R.L. Raikes), increasing aridity (Gurdip Singh), tectonic disturbance (G.F. Dales), drying up of the Ghaggar.
The Great Granary is the largest single structure at Mohenjodaro; Harappa had two rows of six granaries with circular brick working-floors near by.
Order of first excavation: Harappa (1921), Mohenjodaro (1922), Chanhudaro (1931), Ropar (1953), Lothal (1955), Kalibangan (1961), Dholavira (1989).

questions.q: The Harappan site of Kalibangan is situated on the bank of which river?
questions.exp: Kalibangan stands on the left bank of the dried-up Ghaggar, widely identified with the Vedic Saraswati. The name Kalibangan means 'black bangles', after the fragments found on the mounds.

questions.q: Which Harappan site was excavated in 1921 by Daya Ram Sahni?
questions.exp: Harappa on the Ravi was the first site excavated, in 1921, by Daya Ram Sahni under John Marshall. The civilisation takes its alternative name from this type-site.

questions.q: Mohenjodaro was brought to light in 1922 by
questions.exp: Rakhal Das Banerji discovered Mohenjodaro in Larkana district of Sindh in 1922. The name means 'mound of the dead' in Sindhi.

questions.q: Kalibangan was excavated under the direction of
opts: Daya Ram Sahni and M.S. Vats
questions.exp: B.B. Lal and B.K. Thapar excavated Kalibangan for the ASI between 1961 and 1969. The mound had first been brought to notice by the Italian indologist Luigi Pio Tessitori early in the twentieth century.

questions.q: Surkotada in Kutch, which yielded the much-debated horse bones, was excavated by
questions.exp: J.P. Joshi of the ASI located and excavated Surkotada, a small fortified Harappan settlement in Rapar taluka of Kutch. The identification of the bones as true horse, argued by Sandor Bokonyi, remains disputed.

questions.q: Dholavira, inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2021, was excavated by
questions.exp: R.S. Bisht directed the long campaign at Dholavira between 1989 and 2005. It was the first Harappan site in India to be given World Heritage status.

questions.q: A brick-built structure identified as a dockyard has been found at
questions.exp: The large trapezoidal basin at Lothal in Ahmedabad district is generally interpreted as a tidal dockyard connected to the Bhogavo. Lothal also yielded rice husk and a Persian Gulf seal.

questions.q: The bronze figurine known as the 'Dancing Girl' was recovered from
questions.exp: The 'Dancing Girl' from Mohenjodaro was cast by the lost-wax (cire perdue) process and is now in the National Museum, New Delhi. The steatite 'Priest-King' bust is from the same site.

questions.q: Which Harappan city is distinguished by the complete absence of a citadel?
questions.exp: Chanhudaro in Sindh is the only major Harappan city that has no fortified citadel mound. It was an industrial town noted for bead-making, shell-working and an inkpot.

questions.q: The westernmost known site of the Indus Valley Civilisation is
questions.exp: Sutkagendor on the Dasht river in Balochistan marks the western limit of the civilisation. Alamgirpur on the Hindon marks the eastern limit.

questions.q: The largest Harappan site discovered within India is
questions.exp: Rakhigarhi in Hisar district of Haryana, spread over several mounds on a Ghaggar palaeochannel, is the largest Harappan settlement in India. Dholavira is the largest in Gujarat.

questions.q: The first Harappan site to be excavated after India's independence was
questions.exp: Ropar (Rupnagar) on the Sutlej was excavated by Y.D. Sharma in 1953, the first such excavation in independent India. It is also famous for a dog buried along with a human.

questions.q: The famous 'signboard' bearing ten large Indus signs was found at
questions.exp: The inlaid gypsum signboard of ten large characters was found near the north gate of the citadel at Dholavira. It is the largest known piece of Indus writing.

questions.q: Harappan burnt bricks were normally made in the ratio of
questions.exp: The standard Harappan brick had its length, breadth and thickness in the ratio 4:2:1, used consistently from Sindh to Gujarat. Such uniformity is a mark of the civilisation's standardisation.

questions.q: Harappan weights were made chiefly of
questions.exp: Cubical weights of chert are found across Harappan sites, following a binary scheme in the lower denominations. Scales of ivory (Lothal) and shell (Mohenjodaro) were used for linear measurement.

questions.q: The earliest evidence of a ploughed agricultural field in the subcontinent comes from
questions.exp: A pre-Harappan ploughed field with two sets of furrows crossing at right angles was found south-east of the settlement at Kalibangan. It suggests the cultivation of two crops together.

questions.q: In Mesopotamian records, the Indus region was referred to as
questions.exp: Mesopotamian texts call the Indus region Meluha; Dilmun is identified with Bahrain and Magan with the Makran-Oman coast. Both were intermediate stations on the sea route.

questions.q: The commonest animal device engraved on Harappan seals is the
questions.exp: The one-horned 'unicorn' with a ritual standard before it occurs on the majority of Harappan seals. Seals are typically square and made of steatite.

questions.q: A terracotta model of a plough has been reported from the Harappan site of
questions.exp: Banawali in Fatehabad district of Haryana yielded a terracotta model of a plough along with good quality barley. Kalibangan yielded the actual ploughed field.

questions.q: The earliest evidence of wheat and barley cultivation in the subcontinent comes from the Neolithic site of
questions.exp: Mehrgarh, near the Bolan pass in Balochistan, has yielded the earliest evidence of farming of wheat and barley and of cotton in South Asia. It represents the pre-urban ancestry of the Harappan tradition.

questions.q: Kalibangan is located in which district of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Kalibangan lies in Hanumangarh district, between Suratgarh and Hanumangarh town. It is the only major urban Harappan site in Rajasthan.

questions.q: Daimabad, generally regarded as the southernmost Harappan site, lies on the bank of the
questions.exp: Daimabad in Ahmednagar district of Maharashtra stands on the Pravara, a tributary of the Godavari. Its celebrated bronze hoard includes a chariot with a driver, a bull, an elephant and a rhinoceros.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Kalibangan:
I. It has yielded the earliest evidence of a ploughed agricultural field in the subcontinent.
II. A row of seven fire altars was found on a mud-brick platform in the citadel.
III. It lies on the bank of the Ghaggar, identified by many scholars with the Saraswati.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Kalibangan also yielded camel bones, a bangle-making industry and an unusual extended north-south burial practice.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Lothal:
I. It has yielded a brick-built structure widely identified as a dockyard.
II. Rice husk has been reported from the site.
III. It is situated in the Kutch district of Gujarat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Lothal is in Ahmedabad district, not Kutch, so statement III is wrong. Rice husk from Lothal and Rangpur is among the earliest evidence of rice in a Harappan context.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Mohenjodaro:
I. The Great Bath is situated within the citadel area.
II. The site lies on the left bank of the Ravi.
III. The so-called Pashupati seal was found here.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Mohenjodaro lies on the Indus, not the Ravi, so statement II is wrong. The Great Bath, the Great Granary and the college of priests are all on the citadel mound.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Harappan town planning:
I. Streets generally cut one another at right angles, producing a grid pattern.
II. The citadel usually lay to the west of the lower town and stood on a raised platform.
III. House doorways normally opened directly on to the main streets.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Doorways opened on to side lanes rather than the main streets, so statement III is wrong. Underground drains covered with stone slabs, fitted with manholes and soak-pits, ran along the streets.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Harappan metallurgy:
I. Copper, bronze, gold and silver were all in use.
II. Iron tools have been recovered from Mohenjodaro and Harappa.
III. Bronze was made by alloying copper with tin.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Iron was entirely unknown to the Harappans, so statement II is wrong. The Harappan age is therefore a Bronze Age culture; iron appears in India only in the later Vedic period.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Dholavira:
I. The settlement is divided into three parts - citadel, middle town and lower town.
II. It has the most elaborate series of water reservoirs found at any Harappan site.
III. It was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in 2021.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. Dholavira stands on Khadir Bet island between the Mansar and Manhar streams in the Rann of Kutch.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Harappan religion:
I. A large number of stone images of gods were installed in Harappan temples.
II. No structure at any Harappan site has been positively identified as a temple.
III. Fire altars have been reported from Kalibangan, Lothal and Banawali.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: No temples and no cult images have been identified, so statement I is wrong. Worship is inferred instead from terracotta mother-goddess figurines, the Pashupati seal, lingam-yoni stones and the pipal tree.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Indus script has been deciphered and is known to be an early form of Sanskrit.
II. Harappan weights follow a binary system in the lower denominations.
III. An ivory scale has been recovered from Lothal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Indus script remains undeciphered, so statement I is wrong. It is pictographic and was written boustrophedon, the first line running right to left.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Harappan site)   List-II (River)
A. Harappa       1. Indus
