questions.q: By the Treaty of Allahabad (1765), the East India Company obtained the Diwani of:
questions.exp: Shah Alam II granted the Diwani (revenue rights) of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa to the Company on 12 August 1765 against an annual pension of Rs 26 lakh.

questions.q: The Dual Government in Bengal, introduced by Robert Clive, was abolished in 1772 by:
questions.exp: Warren Hastings ended the dual system under which the Company held the Diwani while the Nawab retained the Nizamat, and brought Bengal under direct Company administration.

questions.q: Pitt's India Act of 1784 created which new body to control the civil, military and revenue affairs of the East India Company?
questions.exp: The Act set up a six-member Board of Control representing the Crown, creating a system of 'double government' alongside the Company's Court of Directors.

questions.q: Lord Macaulay's Minute on Education of 1835 recommended:
opts: Promotion of oriental learning through Sanskrit and Arabic
English as the medium of higher education in India
Vernacular languages as the medium of instruction at all levels
Compulsory primary education for all Indians
questions.exp: Macaulay's Minute of 2 February 1835 settled the Anglicist-Orientalist controversy in favour of English, and rested on the 'downward filtration theory'.

questions.q: Which of the following is called the 'Magna Carta of English education in India'?
questions.exp: Charles Wood's Despatch of 1854 laid down a graded system from vernacular primary schools to universities and led to the founding of Calcutta, Bombay and Madras universities in 1857.

questions.q: The Indian Education Commission of 1882, headed by W.W. Hunter, was appointed during the viceroyalty of:
questions.exp: The Hunter Commission was appointed by Lord Ripon and concentrated on primary and secondary education, recommending transfer of primary education to local bodies.

questions.q: The Mahalwari system of land revenue was introduced in 1822 through Regulation VII on the recommendation of:
questions.exp: Holt Mackenzie's scheme made the mahal (village estate) the unit of assessment. It was revised in 1833 under Bentinck by R.M. Bird and applied in the North-Western Provinces, Punjab and Central India.

questions.q: The first Indian ruler to accept Lord Wellesley's Subsidiary Alliance was the:
questions.exp: The Nizam of Hyderabad signed the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798. Awadh followed in 1801 and the Peshwa in 1802 by the Treaty of Bassein.

questions.q: Tipu Sultan was killed during the Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799) while defending:
questions.exp: Tipu died defending his capital Seringapatam on 4 May 1799. Mysore was then restored to the Wodeyar dynasty under a subsidiary alliance.

questions.q: Punjab was annexed to British India in 1849 after the Second Anglo-Sikh War by:
questions.exp: Dalhousie annexed Punjab in 1849; the young Maharaja Dalip Singh was pensioned off and the Koh-i-Noor diamond surrendered to the Crown.

questions.q: The 'drain of wealth' theory, which held that a part of India's national wealth was being exported to Britain without an equivalent return, was expounded by:
questions.exp: Dadabhai Naoroji first raised it in 'England's Debt to India' (1867) and elaborated it in 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901).

questions.q: The Government of India Act, 1858 created the office of:
opts: President of the Board of Trade
questions.exp: The Act abolished the East India Company and vested Indian administration in a Secretary of State for India assisted by a 15-member Council; the Governor-General also became Viceroy, Canning being the first.

questions.q: The sepoy mutiny that began the Revolt of 1857 at Meerut broke out on:
questions.exp: The Meerut sepoys revolted on 10 May 1857 and reached Delhi the next day. Mangal Pandey's earlier attack at Barrackpore was on 29 March 1857.

questions.q: Who commanded the rebel forces at Delhi in 1857 in the name of Bahadur Shah II?
questions.exp: Bakht Khan of the Bareilly troops became the effective military commander at Delhi. Khan Bahadur Khan led at Bareilly and Liaquat Ali at Allahabad.

questions.q: Queen Victoria's Proclamation transferring the government of India to the Crown was read out at Allahabad on 1 November 1858 by:
questions.exp: Canning, the last Governor-General and first Viceroy, read the Proclamation, which promised non-interference in religion and an end to annexations.

questions.q: The Child Marriage Restraint Act of 1929, which fixed the minimum age of marriage at 14 years for girls and 18 years for boys, is popularly known as the:
questions.exp: It is named after Har Bilas Sarda, who piloted the Bill. It came into force on 1 April 1930. The earlier Age of Consent Act of 1891 was associated with Behramji Malabari.

questions.q: Sati was declared illegal by Regulation XVII of 1829 during the governor-generalship of:
questions.exp: Bentinck acted on the sustained campaign of Raja Rammohan Roy. The Regulation applied first to Bengal Presidency and was extended to Bombay and Madras in 1830.

questions.q: Henry Louis Vivian Derozio, the inspiration behind the Young Bengal movement, taught at:
questions.exp: Derozio taught at Hindu College (1826-31) and encouraged radical free thinking among his students, who came to be called the Young Bengal or Derozians.

questions.q: The Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act of 1856 was passed largely due to the efforts of:
questions.exp: Vidyasagar marshalled scriptural authority in support of widow remarriage; the measure was enacted as Act XV of 1856.

questions.q: Kandukuri Veeresalingam, who performed the first widow remarriage in the Telugu region in 1881, worked chiefly at:
questions.exp: Veeresalingam organised the first widow remarriage at Rajahmundry on 11 December 1881 and later founded a widows' home there. He is called the father of the Telugu renaissance.

questions.q: The Ramakrishna Mission was founded in 1897 by:
questions.exp: Vivekananda founded the Mission on 1 May 1897 to combine spiritual practice with social service; its headquarters, Belur Math, was established in 1899.

questions.q: The Servants of India Society, founded in 1905 at Pune to train national missionaries for the service of India, was established by:
questions.exp: Gokhale founded the Society in June 1905. After his death in 1915 it was led by Srinivasa Sastri.

questions.q: The book 'The Indian War of Independence, 1857' was written by:
questions.exp: Savarkar's 1909 work first described 1857 as a planned war of national independence. S.N. Sen's 'Eighteen Fifty-Seven' and R.C. Majumdar's study were centenary-year histories.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Regulating Act of 1773:
I. It designated the Governor of Bengal as the Governor-General of Bengal.
II. It provided for the establishment of a Supreme Court at Calcutta.
III. It gave the British Cabinet direct control over the civil and military affairs of the Company.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Warren Hastings became the first Governor-General of Bengal and the Supreme Court was set up in 1774. Direct Crown control through the Board of Control came only with Pitt's India Act of 1784.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Doctrine of Lapse:
I. It was systematically applied by Lord Dalhousie.
II. Satara was the first state annexed under it, in 1848.
III. Awadh was annexed in 1856 under the Doctrine of Lapse.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Satara (1848), Jhansi (1853) and Nagpur (1854) lapsed for want of a natural heir. Awadh, however, was annexed in 1856 on the plea of misgovernance, not lapse.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the economic critique of colonial rule:
I. Dadabhai Naoroji developed the 'drain of wealth' theory in 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'.
II. R.C. Dutt wrote 'The Economic History of India'.
III. 'De-industrialisation' refers to the ruin of Indian handicrafts under British rule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Naoroji, Dutt and Ranade formed the core of the early nationalist economic critique of British rule.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Raja Rammohan Roy:
I. He founded the Atmiya Sabha at Calcutta.
II. He published the Persian journal Mirat-ul-Akhbar.
III. He opposed the introduction of Western scientific education in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Rammohan Roy actively favoured Western scientific and English education, opposing the proposal for a Sanskrit College in his 1823 letter to Lord Amherst.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Arya Samaj:
I. Its guiding slogan was 'Back to the Vedas'.
II. It launched the Shuddhi movement for reconversion.
III. The first Dayanand Anglo-Vedic (DAV) School was set up at Lahore in 1886.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Swami Dayanand founded the Arya Samaj at Bombay on 10 April 1875; his principal work is the Satyarth Prakash.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Permanent Settlement of 1793:
I. It was introduced in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa by Lord Cornwallis.
II. The zamindar retained one-eleventh of the rental and paid ten-elevenths to the state.
III. It was later extended to the whole of British India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Permanent Settlement covered about 19 per cent of British India; Ryotwari and Mahalwari were applied elsewhere.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about B.R. Ambedkar:
I. He started the fortnightly Mooknayak in 1920.
II. He founded the Bahishkrit Hitakarini Sabha in 1924.
III. He led the Mahad Satyagraha of 1927 for the right to use the Chavdar tank.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Ambedkar also led the Kalaram temple entry movement at Nashik in 1930 and started the journal Bahishkrit Bharat in 1927.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the aftermath of the Revolt of 1857:
I. The Revolt was declared suppressed by Lord Canning on 8 July 1858.
II. Bahadur Shah II was tried and exiled to Rangoon.
III. After 1857 the proportion of European troops in the Indian army was reduced.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The proportion of European to Indian troops was deliberately increased after 1857, and artillery was kept exclusively in European hands.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (System)   List-II (Associated with)
A. Permanent Settlement   1. Lord Cornwallis
B. Ryotwari Settlement   2. Thomas Munro
C. Mahalwari Settlement   3. Holt Mackenzie
D. Subsidiary Alliance   4. Lord Wellesley
questions.exp: Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement in 1793, Munro the Ryotwari in Madras, Mackenzie the Mahalwari in 1822 and Wellesley the Subsidiary Alliance from 1798.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (War)   List-II (Treaty)
A. First Anglo-Maratha War   1. Treaty of Salbai
B. Second Anglo-Mysore War   2. Treaty of Mangalore
C. First Anglo-Burmese War   3. Treaty of Yandabo
D. Third Anglo-Mysore War   4. Treaty of Seringapatam
questions.exp: Salbai (1782) ended the First Anglo-Maratha War, Mangalore (1784) the Second Anglo-Mysore War, Yandabo (1826) the First Anglo-Burmese War and Seringapatam (1792) the Third Anglo-Mysore War.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Centre of 1857)   List-II (Leader)
A. Kanpur   1. Nana Saheb
B. Lucknow   2. Begum Hazrat Mahal
C. Jhansi   3. Rani Lakshmibai
D. Jagdishpur   4. Kunwar Singh
questions.exp: Nana Saheb, assisted by Tatya Tope, led at Kanpur; Begum Hazrat Mahal at Lucknow; Rani Lakshmibai at Jhansi; and the octogenarian Kunwar Singh at Jagdishpur in Bihar.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Movement/Institution)   List-II (Founder)
A. Satyashodhak Samaj   1. Jyotiba Phule
B. Theosophical Society   2. Madame Blavatsky and Colonel Olcott
C. Aligarh Movement   3. Syed Ahmad Khan
D. Self-Respect Movement   4. E.V. Ramaswamy Naicker
questions.exp: Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873; the Theosophical Society was founded in New York in 1875; Syed Ahmad Khan led the Aligarh movement; Periyar started the Self-Respect Movement in 1925.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Institution)   List-II (Founder)
A. Prarthana Samaj   1. Atmaram Pandurang
B. SNDP Yogam   2. Narayana Guru
C. Gurukul Kangri   3. Swami Shraddhanand
D. Brahmo Samaj of India   4. Keshab Chandra Sen
questions.exp: Prarthana Samaj was founded at Bombay in 1867, the SNDP Yogam in Kerala in 1903, Gurukul Kangri at Haridwar in 1902 and the Brahmo Samaj of India in 1866.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs relating to the Charter Acts is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Charter Act, 1813 — Grant of one lakh rupees a year for education
Charter Act, 1833 — The Governor-General of Bengal became the Governor-General of India
Charter Act, 1853 — Introduction of open competition for the civil services
Charter Act, 1793 — End of the commercial functions of the East India Company
questions.exp: The Company's commercial functions were ended by the Charter Act of 1833, not 1793. The 1813 Act had already ended its trade monopoly except for tea and the China trade.

questions.q: Which one of the following states was NOT annexed under the Doctrine of Lapse?
questions.exp: Awadh was annexed by Dalhousie in 1856 on the ground of misgovernance. Satara (1848), Jhansi (1853) and Nagpur (1854) lapsed for want of a natural heir.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of 1857 centres and leaders is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Begum Hazrat Mahal led the revolt at Lucknow. At Gwalior the rebel forces were led by Tatya Tope and Rani Lakshmibai after they seized the fort in June 1858.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of reformers and their writings is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Bahishkrit Bharat was a Marathi fortnightly started by B.R. Ambedkar in 1927. Vivekananda's works include 'Rajayoga' and 'Karmayoga'.

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT a provision of the Government of India Act, 1858?
opts: Abolition of the East India Company
Creation of the office of Secretary of State for India
Transfer of the powers of the Board of Control to the Secretary of State
Introduction of dyarchy in the provinces
questions.exp: Dyarchy in the provinces was introduced by the Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms).

questions.q:
Arrange the following events in correct chronological order:
I. Battle of Wandiwash
II. Battle of Plassey
III. Battle of Buxar
IV. Treaty of Salbai
questions.exp: Plassey 1757, Wandiwash 1760 (Third Carnatic War), Buxar 1764 and the Treaty of Salbai 1782 ending the First Anglo-Maratha War.

questions.q:
Arrange the following socio-religious organisations in the correct chronological order of their founding:
I. Brahmo Samaj
II. Prarthana Samaj
III. Arya Samaj
IV. Ramakrishna Mission
questions.exp: Brahmo Samaj 1828, Prarthana Samaj 1867, Arya Samaj 1875 and Ramakrishna Mission 1897.

chapters.title: Freedom Struggle (1885-1947) and Nation Building to 2000
factsheet: Indian National Congress founded 28 December 1885 at the Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay; A.O. Hume the moving spirit; W.C. Bonnerjee president; 72 delegates.

Early presidents — 1886 Calcutta Dadabhai Naoroji; 1887 Madras Badruddin Tyabji (first Muslim); 1888 Allahabad George Yule (first Englishman); 1905 Benares G.K. Gokhale; 1906 Calcutta Dadabhai Naoroji (Swaraj declared the goal); 1907 Surat Rash Behari Ghosh (Surat split). Moderate phase 1885-1905 worked by 'prayer, petition and protest'; the Extremists were Lal-Bal-Pal and Aurobindo Ghosh.
Partition of Bengal announced 19 July 1905 by Curzon, effective 16 October 1905, annulled at the Delhi Durbar of 1911; Boycott resolution passed at Calcutta Town Hall, 7 August 1905.

All India Muslim League founded 30 December 1906 at Dhaka under Nawab Salimullah; Morley-Minto Reforms (Indian Councils Act) 1909 introduced separate electorates; Lucknow Pact 1916 brought Congress-League unity at the session presided over by Ambica Charan Mazumdar.
Home Rule Leagues 1916 — Tilak's launched from Belgaum in April, Annie Besant's from Adyar, Madras, in September; Besant became Congress president at Calcutta in 1917, the first woman to do so.
Gandhi's early satyagrahas — Champaran (indigo, tinkathia) 1917; Ahmedabad mill strike and Kheda 1918; Bardoli no-tax satyagraha under Sardar Patel 1928.
Rowlatt Act, March 1919 — 'no appeal, no vakil, no daleel'; Jallianwala Bagh massacre 13 April 1919 (General Dyer); Hunter Committee of inquiry; Tagore renounced his knighthood.

Nagpur session, December 1920 — president C. Vijayaraghavachariar; endorsed Non-Cooperation; new Congress constitution with a 15-member Working Committee, provincial committees on a linguistic basis and a membership fee of four annas.

Non-Cooperation launched 1 August 1920; withdrawn after the Chauri Chaura incident (Gorakhpur district) of 5 February 1922 by the Bardoli resolution of 12 February 1922; Swaraj Party formed in 1923 by C.R. Das (president) and Motilal Nehru (secretary) to contest council elections.
Simon Commission announced November 1927, arrived 3 February 1928; all-white; Lala Lajpat Rai fatally injured at Lahore. Nehru Report 1928 drafted under Motilal Nehru; Jinnah's Fourteen Points 1929.
Lahore session, December 1929 — Jawaharlal Nehru president; Purna Swaraj resolution; 26 January 1930 observed as the first Independence Day.
Dandi March 12 March to 6 April 1930 from Sabarmati Ashram, 78 volunteers, about 385 km; Gandhi-Irwin Pact 5 March 1931; Gandhi attended only the Second Round Table Conference (1931).

Communal Award 16 August 1932 by Ramsay MacDonald; Poona Pact 24 September 1932 at Yerwada Jail raised reserved seats for the Depressed Classes in provincial legislatures from 71 to 148 in place of separate electorates.

Government of India Act 1935 — All-India Federation (never formed), provincial autonomy replacing dyarchy in provinces, dyarchy at the Centre, Federal Court (1937), separation of Burma (1937). Individual Satyagraha October 1940 — first satyagrahi Vinoba Bhave, second Jawaharlal Nehru; Cripps Mission March 1942, called by Gandhi 'a post-dated cheque'.
Quit India resolution passed at Gowalia Tank, Bombay, 8 August 1942; 'Do or Die'; Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the flag; parallel governments at Ballia, Tamluk (Bengal) and Satara.

Women in the freedom struggle — Sarojini Naidu (first Indian woman Congress president, Kanpur 1925); Kanaklata Barua shot at Gohpur, Assam, 20 September 1942 aged 17 leading the Mrityu Bahini; Matangini Hazra killed at Tamluk 1942; Rama Devi of Odisha, called 'Maa', led the Salt Satyagraha there.

Revolutionary landmarks — Chapekar brothers 1897; Alipore Bomb Case 1908 (Khudiram Bose, Prafulla Chaki at Muzaffarpur); Delhi Conspiracy (Hardinge bomb) 23 December 1912 at Chandni Chowk, bomb thrown by Basanta Kumar Biswas, planned by Rash Behari Bose; Ghadar Party 1913 San Francisco (Sohan Singh Bhakna, Lala Hardayal).

Kakori Conspiracy 9 August 1925 — Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Rajendra Lahiri and Roshan Singh hanged; HSRA 1928; Central Assembly bomb 8 April 1929 (Bhagat Singh and B.K. Dutt); Bhagat Singh, Sukhdev, Rajguru hanged 23 March 1931; Chittagong Armoury Raid 18 April 1930 under Surya Sen. Kesari Singh Barhath of Shahpura was convicted in the Mahant Pyarelal murder case and jailed at Hazaribagh.

INA first raised 1942 under Captain Mohan Singh; Subhas Chandra Bose took charge at Singapore in July 1943 and proclaimed the Provisional Government of Free India there on 21 October 1943; Rani Jhansi Regiment led by Lakshmi Sahgal.

Cabinet Mission 1946 — Pethick-Lawrence, Stafford Cripps, A.V. Alexander; rejected Pakistan, proposed grouping of provinces; Direct Action Day 16 August 1946; Constituent Assembly first met 9 December 1946; Mountbatten Plan 3 June 1947; Indian Independence Act 18 July 1947; Radcliffe Line demarcated the Indo-Pakistan boundary.

Nationalist art and culture — Abanindranath Tagore painted Bharat Mata in 1905 (originally titled Banga Mata), the figure holding a book, sheaves of paddy, a piece of white cloth and a rudraksha mala; 'Vande Mataram' from Bankim Chandra Chatterjee's Anandamath (1882), first sung at the 1896 Calcutta Congress.

Integration of princely states — States Department created July 1947 under Sardar Patel with V.P. Menon as Secretary; Instrument of Accession; Junagadh plebiscite February 1948; Hyderabad by Operation Polo, September 1948; Jammu and Kashmir acceded 26 October 1947; Goa liberated by Operation Vijay, December 1961.

Linguistic reorganisation — Potti Sriramulu's fast led to Andhra State, 1 October 1953, the first linguistic state; Fazl Ali Commission appointed December 1953 (members H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar), reported 30 September 1955; States Reorganisation Act 1956 created 14 states and 6 union territories.

Five Year Plans — I (1951-56) Harrod-Domar, agriculture; II (1956-61) Mahalanobis, heavy industry; III (1961-66); Plan Holiday 1966-69; IV (1969-74) growth with stability; V (1974-79) Garibi Hatao; Rolling Plan 1978-80; VI (1980-85); VII (1985-90); VIII (1992-97) LPG.

Green Revolution — IADP launched 1960-61 in seven districts (including Pali in Rajasthan) with Ford Foundation support; High Yielding Varieties Programme 1966-67; Norman Borlaug's dwarf wheat; M.S. Swaminathan called the father of the Green Revolution in India.

Wars and accords — Sino-Indian War October-November 1962; Indo-Pak War 1965 followed by the Tashkent Declaration, 10 January 1966; Bangladesh Liberation War 1971 followed by the Shimla Agreement, 2 July 1972; Kargil conflict 1999 (Operation Vijay).

Emergency 25 June 1975 to 21 March 1977 under Article 352 on the ground of 'internal disturbance', following the Allahabad High Court verdict of 12 June 1975 in the Raj Narain case; 42nd Amendment 1976; Shah Commission 1977; 44th Amendment 1978 substituted 'armed rebellion'. Mandal Commission appointed 1979 under B.P. Mandal, reported December 1980, identified 3,743 backward castes and recommended 27 per cent reservation; implemented by V.P. Singh in 1990 and upheld in Indra Sawhney (1992).

Economic reforms 1991 — P.V. Narasimha Rao PM, Manmohan Singh Finance Minister; rupee devalued in two steps in July 1991; New Industrial Policy 24 July 1991 abolished licensing for most industries and cut public-sector reserved industries from 17 to 8; Narasimham Committee on banking reform.
Nuclear tests — Pokhran-I, 18 May 1974, code-named Smiling Buddha; Pokhran-II, Operation Shakti, five devices on 11 and 13 May 1998.

Education commissions — University Education Commission 1948-49 (S. Radhakrishnan); Secondary Education Commission appointed 23 September 1952 (A. Lakshmanaswami Mudaliar, Vice-Chancellor of Madras University), which recommended multipurpose schools and a three-year degree; Education Commission 1964-66 (D.S. Kothari, secretary J.P. Naik) which proposed the 10+2+3 pattern and raising education spending to 6 per cent of GDP; National Policy on Education 1968 and 1986.

questions.q: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 largely at the initiative of which retired British civil servant?
questions.exp: Allan Octavian Hume, a retired officer of the Bengal Civil Service, organised the first session and served as General Secretary for many years.

questions.q: The first session of the Indian National Congress in December 1885 was held at the Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in:
questions.exp: The session was shifted from Poona to Bombay because of a cholera outbreak. It was attended by 72 delegates and presided over by W.C. Bonnerjee.

questions.q: The Congress session of 1906 at Calcutta, which declared 'Swaraj' to be the goal of the Indian National Congress, was presided over by:
questions.exp: The Calcutta session of 1906, presided over by Dadabhai Naoroji, declared self-government or Swaraj on the model of the self-governing colonies to be the Congress goal.

questions.q: The Partition of Bengal, announced by Lord Curzon and given effect on 16 October 1905, was annulled in:
questions.exp: The partition was revoked at the Delhi Durbar of 1911; the capital was simultaneously shifted from Calcutta to Delhi.

questions.q: The Indian National Congress split into Moderates and Extremists at the session held in:
questions.exp: The Surat split occurred at the 1907 session presided over by Rash Behari Ghosh. The two wings reunited at the Lucknow session of 1916.

questions.q: The All India Muslim League was founded in December 1906 at:
questions.exp: The League was founded on 30 December 1906 at Dhaka under the leadership of Nawab Salimullah of Dhaka and Nawab Mohsin-ul-Mulk.

questions.q: Separate electorates for Muslims were first introduced in India by:
questions.exp: The Morley-Minto Reforms of 1909 introduced communal representation, for which Lord Minto is often called the father of communal electorates.

questions.q: Annie Besant's Home Rule League, founded in September 1916, had its headquarters at:
questions.exp: Besant's League worked from Adyar and covered the rest of India, while Tilak's League, started in April 1916 from Belgaum, worked in Maharashtra (excluding Bombay city), Karnataka, Central Provinces and Berar.

questions.q: Gandhi's first satyagraha in India, launched in 1917 against the tinkathia system of indigo cultivation, was at:
questions.exp: The Champaran satyagraha of 1917 in Bihar was undertaken at the request of Rajkumar Shukla and led to the Champaran Agrarian Act of 1918.

questions.q: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre took place on:
questions.exp: General Dyer's troops fired on an unarmed gathering at Amritsar on Baisakhi day, 13 April 1919. The Hunter Committee was appointed to inquire into it, and Rabindranath Tagore renounced his knighthood in protest.

questions.q: The Chauri Chaura incident of February 1922, which led to the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement, occurred in which district of the United Provinces?
questions.exp: A crowd set fire to a police station at Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur district on 5 February 1922. Gandhi withdrew the movement by the Bardoli resolution of 12 February 1922.

questions.q: The Simon Commission arrived in India in:
questions.exp: The all-white commission landed on 3 February 1928 and was met with black-flag demonstrations. Lala Lajpat Rai was fatally injured in a lathi charge at Lahore in October 1928.

questions.q: The resolution of Purna Swaraj was adopted at the Congress session of 1929 held at:
questions.exp: The Lahore session, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, adopted Purna Swaraj as the goal and 26 January 1930 was observed as the first Independence Day.

questions.q: Gandhi began the Dandi March on 12 March 1930 from:
questions.exp: Gandhi walked about 385 km with 78 volunteers from Sabarmati to Dandi, breaking the salt law on 6 April 1930 and launching the Civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.q: Under the Poona Pact of 1932, the number of seats reserved for the Depressed Classes in the provincial legislatures was fixed at:
questions.exp: The Communal Award had allotted 71 seats along with separate electorates. The Poona Pact of 24 September 1932 replaced separate electorates with joint electorates and raised reserved seats to 148.

questions.q: The Cabinet Mission that came to India in 1946 was headed by:
questions.exp: Secretary of State Pethick-Lawrence led the Mission, with Sir Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander as members. It rejected the demand for Pakistan and proposed a three-tier federal structure.

questions.q: The painting 'Bharat Mata', a defining image of the Swadeshi movement, was created in 1905 by:
questions.exp: Abanindranath Tagore, founder of the Bengal School, first titled the watercolour 'Banga Mata'. The four-armed figure holds a book, sheaves of paddy, a piece of white cloth and a rudraksha mala.

questions.q: Which revolutionary of Rajasthan was convicted in the Mahant Pyarelal murder case and sentenced to imprisonment at Hazaribagh?
questions.exp: Kesari Singh Barhath of Shahpura was convicted in the case and served a twenty-year sentence at Hazaribagh jail in Bihar, being released in 1920. His brother Jorawar Singh was linked to the Hardinge bomb attack.

questions.q: In the Delhi Conspiracy Case, the bomb thrown at Viceroy Lord Hardinge at Chandni Chowk on 23 December 1912 was hurled by:
questions.exp: Basanta Kumar Biswas threw the bomb during the state entry procession into the new capital; the plot was masterminded by Rash Behari Bose. Biswas was hanged at Ambala in 1915.

questions.q: Kanaklata Barua, who was shot dead in 1942 while leading a procession to hoist the national flag at the Gohpur police station, belonged to:
questions.exp: The seventeen-year-old Kanaklata Barua led a Mrityu Bahini procession on 20 September 1942 during the Quit India Movement and is honoured in Assam as 'Birangana'.

questions.q: Hyderabad was integrated into the Indian Union in September 1948 through a police action code-named:
questions.exp: Operation Polo (13-18 September 1948) ended the Nizam's resistance. Operation Vijay of December 1961 was the action that liberated Goa.

questions.q: The first state in independent India to be created on a linguistic basis was:
questions.exp: Andhra State was carved out of Madras on 1 October 1953 after the death of Potti Sriramulu on the 58th day of his fast.

questions.q: The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 reorganised the country into:
questions.exp: The Act was based on the report of the Fazl Ali Commission (1953-55), whose other members were H.N. Kunzru and K.M. Panikkar.

questions.q: The 'Plan Holiday' of 1966-69 was declared mainly because of:
opts: The failure of the Third Plan, the 1965 war and successive droughts
questions.exp: Three annual plans were adopted in place of a five year plan. The rupee was also devalued in June 1966.

questions.q: Who is described as the father of the Green Revolution in India?
questions.exp: M.S. Swaminathan adapted Norman Borlaug's dwarf Mexican wheat varieties to Indian conditions. Verghese Kurien is associated with the White Revolution.

questions.q: The Tashkent Declaration that ended the India-Pakistan war of 1965 was signed in January:
questions.exp: Lal Bahadur Shastri and Ayub Khan signed it on 10 January 1966 under Soviet mediation; Shastri died in Tashkent the same night.

questions.q: The National Emergency of 1975 was proclaimed under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.exp: The Emergency was proclaimed on 25 June 1975 on the ground of 'internal disturbance'. The 44th Amendment of 1978 replaced that ground with 'armed rebellion'.

questions.q: The commission appointed in 1979 to identify the socially and educationally backward classes was chaired by:
questions.exp: The Mandal Commission submitted its report in December 1980, identifying 3,743 backward castes and recommending 27 per cent reservation. It was implemented in 1990 by V.P. Singh.

questions.q: India's first nuclear test, conducted at Pokhran on 18 May 1974, was code-named:
questions.exp: Pokhran-I was described officially as a peaceful nuclear explosion. Pokhran-II of May 1998 was code-named Operation Shakti.

questions.q: The commission headed by Dr. A. Lakshmanaswami Mudaliar, appointed in September 1952, was the:
questions.exp: The Secondary Education Commission (1952-53) recommended multipurpose schools, diversified courses and a three-year degree. Mudaliar was Vice-Chancellor of the University of Madras.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Moderate phase of the Indian National Congress (1885-1905):
I. The Moderates relied on constitutional agitation through petitions, memorials and public meetings.
II. Dadabhai Naoroji, Pherozeshah Mehta and G.K. Gokhale were among its leading figures.
III. The Moderates demanded complete independence from British rule.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Moderates sought reform within the empire and greater Indian participation in administration; complete independence became the Congress goal only at Lahore in 1929.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Swadeshi Movement:
I. It began as a protest against the partition of Bengal.
II. The Boycott resolution was adopted at a public meeting in the Calcutta Town Hall on 7 August 1905.
III. Barisal was an important centre of the movement.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The movement popularised swadeshi enterprise, national education and samitis such as the Swadesh Bandhab Samiti of Ashwini Kumar Dutt at Barisal.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Nagpur session of the Indian National Congress (December 1920):
I. It was presided over by C. Vijayaraghavachariar.
II. A new Congress constitution provided for a Working Committee of fifteen members.
III. Provincial Congress Committees were reorganised on a linguistic basis.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Nagpur session endorsed the Non-Cooperation programme begun on 1 August 1920 and reduced the membership fee to four annas to widen the Congress base.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Civil Disobedience Movement:
I. It began with the breaking of the salt law at Dandi on 6 April 1930.
II. The Gandhi-Irwin Pact of March 1931 led to its suspension.
III. The Bardoli no-tax satyagraha led by Sardar Patel formed part of this movement.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Bardoli satyagraha took place in 1928, two years before the Civil Disobedience Movement, and won Vallabhbhai Patel the title 'Sardar'.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Government of India Act, 1935:
I. It provided for an All-India Federation that never came into existence.
II. It abolished dyarchy in the provinces and introduced provincial autonomy.
III. It provided for the establishment of a Federal Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Federal Court began functioning in 1937, the same year in which Burma was separated from India and provincial elections were held.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indian National Army:
I. It was first raised in 1942 under Captain Mohan Singh.
II. Subhas Chandra Bose took over its leadership in July 1943 at Singapore.
III. The Provisional Government of Free India was proclaimed at Rangoon in October 1943.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Provisional Government of Azad Hind was proclaimed at Singapore on 21 October 1943; its headquarters were later shifted to Rangoon.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Quit India Movement:
I. The Quit India resolution was passed at the Bombay session of the AICC on 8 August 1942.
II. Aruna Asaf Ali hoisted the Congress flag at the Gowalia Tank ground.
III. Parallel governments were established at Ballia, Tamluk and Satara.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Gandhi's call was 'Do or Die'; the entire Congress leadership was arrested on 9 August 1942 under Operation Zero Hour.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the integration of the princely states:
I. The States Department was set up in July 1947 under Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel.
II. V.P. Menon was the Secretary of the States Department.
III. Junagadh's accession to India was confirmed by a plebiscite held in February 1948.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Of the 562 princely states, all but Junagadh, Hyderabad and Jammu and Kashmir acceded before 15 August 1947.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the economic reforms of 1991:
I. The New Industrial Policy was announced on 24 July 1991.
II. The number of industries reserved for the public sector was reduced from seventeen to eight.
III. The Narasimham Committee of 1991 dealt with reform of the direct tax system.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Narasimham Committee dealt with reform of the financial and banking system; direct tax reform was examined by the Raja Chelliah Committee.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Emergency of 1975-77:
I. It was proclaimed under Article 352 on the ground of 'internal disturbance'.
II. The 44th Constitutional Amendment, passed during the Emergency, extended the term of the Lok Sabha from five to six years.
III. The Shah Commission was appointed in 1977 to inquire into the excesses committed during the Emergency.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: It was the 42nd Amendment of 1976 that extended the Lok Sabha term to six years; the 44th Amendment of 1978, passed after the Emergency, restored it to five years.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Green Revolution in India:
I. The High Yielding Varieties Programme was launched in 1966-67.
II. Norman Borlaug's dwarf Mexican wheat varieties were central to it.
III. Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh were its chief beneficiaries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The gains were largely confined to wheat and to irrigated regions, which widened regional and crop-wise disparities.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Congress session)   List-II (President)
A. 1885, Bombay   1. W.C. Bonnerjee
B. 1887, Madras   2. Badruddin Tyabji
C. 1888, Allahabad   3. George Yule
D. 1905, Benares   4. Gopal Krishna Gokhale
questions.exp: Badruddin Tyabji was the first Muslim and George Yule the first Englishman to preside over the Congress.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Congress session)   List-II (President)
A. 1920, Nagpur   1. C. Vijayaraghavachariar
B. 1925, Kanpur   2. Sarojini Naidu
C. 1929, Lahore   3. Jawaharlal Nehru
D. 1931, Karachi   4. Vallabhbhai Patel
questions.exp: Sarojini Naidu at Kanpur in 1925 was the first Indian woman to preside over the Congress. The Karachi session of 1931 adopted the resolution on Fundamental Rights and the National Economic Programme.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Revolutionary event)   List-II (Year)
A. Alipore Bomb Case   1. 1908
B. Delhi Conspiracy (Hardinge bomb) Case   2. 1912
C. Kakori Conspiracy Case   3. 1925
D. Chittagong Armoury Raid   4. 1930
questions.exp: Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Rajendra Lahiri and Roshan Singh were hanged in the Kakori case; the Chittagong raid of April 1930 was led by Surya Sen.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Act)   List-II (Provision)
A. Indian Councils Act, 1892   1. Indirect elections introduced
B. Indian Councils Act, 1909   2. Separate electorates for Muslims
C. Government of India Act, 1919   3. Dyarchy in the provinces
D. Government of India Act, 1935   4. Provincial autonomy
questions.exp: The 1919 Act divided provincial subjects into transferred and reserved; the 1935 Act ended that dyarchy and gave the provinces autonomy while introducing dyarchy at the Centre.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Woman freedom fighter)   List-II (Associated with)
A. Aruna Asaf Ali   1. Hoisting the Congress flag at Gowalia Tank, 1942
B. Kanaklata Barua   2. Shot dead at Gohpur, Assam, 1942
C. Matangini Hazra   3. Killed at Tamluk, Bengal, 1942
D. Rama Devi   4. Salt Satyagraha in Odisha
questions.exp: Rama Devi, called 'Maa' in Odisha, joined the Non-Cooperation, Salt Satyagraha and Quit India movements and later the Bhoodan movement.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Plan)   List-II (Feature)
A. First Five Year Plan   1. Harrod-Domar model; priority to agriculture
B. Second Five Year Plan   2. Mahalanobis model; priority to heavy industry
C. Fourth Five Year Plan   3. Growth with stability and self-reliance
D. Fifth Five Year Plan   4. Garibi Hatao and the minimum needs programme
questions.exp: The Fifth Plan (1974-79) was terminated a year early by the Janata government, which introduced the Rolling Plan for 1978-80.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Commission)   List-II (Chairman)
A. University Education Commission, 1948-49   1. S. Radhakrishnan
B. Secondary Education Commission, 1952-53   2. A. Lakshmanaswami Mudaliar
C. Education Commission, 1964-66   3. D.S. Kothari
D. States Reorganisation Commission, 1953-55   4. Fazl Ali
questions.exp: The Kothari Commission recommended the 10+2+3 pattern and raising educational expenditure to 6 per cent of GDP; its report was titled 'Education and National Development'.

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT a Moderate leader of the Indian National Congress?
questions.exp: Bipin Chandra Pal belonged to the Extremist or Garam Dal along with Lala Lajpat Rai and Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of publications and the persons associated with them is NOT correctly matched?
opts: The Indian Sociologist — Shyamji Krishna Varma
questions.exp: The Ghadar weekly was brought out by the Ghadar Party founded at San Francisco in 1913, whose leading figures were Sohan Singh Bhakna and Lala Hardayal.

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT a provision of the Government of India Act, 1919?
opts: A bicameral legislature at the Centre
Separation of provincial and central budgets
questions.exp: Provincial autonomy was introduced only by the Government of India Act, 1935, which simultaneously abolished dyarchy in the provinces.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs relating to the integration of princely states is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Jammu and Kashmir — Instrument of Accession signed in August 1947
questions.exp: Maharaja Hari Singh signed the Instrument of Accession on 26 October 1947 after the tribal invasion, not in August 1947.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of post-independence events and years is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Implementation of the Mandal Commission report — 1990
questions.exp: The Pokhran-II tests, code-named Operation Shakti, were conducted on 11 and 13 May 1998, five devices in all.

questions.q: Who among the following was NOT a member of the Cabinet Mission of 1946?
questions.exp: Lord Wavell was the Viceroy at the time and hosted the Mission, but was not one of its three members.

questions.q:
Arrange the following events of the freedom struggle in correct chronological order:
I. Jallianwala Bagh massacre
II. Chauri Chaura incident
III. Dandi March
IV. Quit India Movement
questions.exp: Jallianwala Bagh 1919, Chauri Chaura 1922, Dandi March 1930 and the Quit India Movement 1942.

chapters.title: Physical Geography: Mountains, Plateaus, Plains, Deserts
factsheet: Mount Everest (8,848.86 m), Great Himalaya, Nepal-China border - highest peak on earth and of Asia.
Aconcagua (about 6,960 m), Andes, Argentina - highest peak of South America and of the whole Western and Southern Hemisphere.
Denali (6,190 m), Alaska Range, USA - highest peak of North America; formerly called Mount McKinley.
Kilimanjaro (5,895 m), Tanzania - highest peak of Africa; a dormant stratovolcano. Mount Kenya (5,199 m) is second.
Mount Elbrus (5,642 m), Caucasus, Russia - highest peak of Europe. Mont Blanc (4,808 m), Alps, is highest in Western Europe.
Vinson Massif (4,892 m), Sentinel Range - highest peak of Antarctica.
Puncak Jaya / Carstensz Pyramid (4,884 m), New Guinea, Indonesia - highest of Oceania; Mount Kosciuszko (2,228 m) is highest on mainland Australia.
Descending order of continental highest peaks: Everest > Aconcagua > Denali > Kilimanjaro > Elbrus > Vinson Massif > Puncak Jaya.
K2 / Godwin Austen (8,611 m), Karakoram - world's second highest; Kangchenjunga (8,586 m) third.
Andes (about 7,000 km) - longest mountain range on land; the Mid-Oceanic Ridge (about 65,000 km) is the longest range overall.
Ural Mountains - conventional boundary between Europe and Asia. Atlas - north-west Africa; Drakensberg - South Africa; Great Dividing Range - eastern Australia.
Tibetan Plateau - highest and largest plateau, 'Roof of the World', average elevation above 4,500 m, between the Himalaya and the Kunlun.
Plateau types: intermontane (Tibet, Bolivia, Anatolia), lava/volcanic (Deccan, Columbia), dissected (Colorado - Grand Canyon), continental (Chotanagpur), piedmont, rain-shadow (Patagonia).
Plateau-country pairs: Katanga - DR Congo (copper); Anatolian - Turkey; Meseta - Spain; Mato Grosso - Brazil; Loess Plateau - China.
Earth's interior: crust-mantle boundary = Mohorovicic discontinuity; mantle-core = Gutenberg discontinuity. Layers by composition: SIAL, SIMA, NIFE.
S-waves travel only through solids; their shadow zone beyond 103 degrees proves the outer core is liquid. P-waves pass through solids and liquids.
Continental drift - Alfred Wegener (1912): Pangaea surrounded by Panthalassa, splitting into Laurasia and Gondwana across the Tethys Sea. Sea-floor spreading - Harry Hess.
Circum-Pacific belt or 'Ring of Fire' - about two-thirds of the world's active volcanoes and the great majority of earthquakes; dominated by subduction zones.
Ojos del Salado (Chile-Argentina) - world's highest volcano; Mauna Loa (Hawaii) - largest active volcano; Etna - Europe's most active; Stromboli - 'Lighthouse of the Mediterranean'.
Largest deserts: Antarctic (about 13.9 m sq km) and Arctic (about 13.7 m sq km) polar deserts; Sahara (over 8.5 m sq km) is the largest hot desert.

Desert-continent pairs: Gobi - Asia; Kalahari and Namib - southern Africa; Atacama and Patagonian - South America; Great Victoria and Great Sandy - Australia; Great Basin, Sonoran, Chihuahuan, Mojave - North America.

Atacama (Chile) - driest desert, kept arid by the cold Peru current and the Andean rain shadow; Namib - oldest desert; Patagonian - largest desert of the Americas; Great Victoria - largest in Australia.
Asian deserts: Arabian (with the Rub al-Khali), Karakum (Turkmenistan), Kyzylkum (Uzbekistan-Kazakhstan), Taklamakan (China), Thar (India-Pakistan), Kavir (Iran).
Wind erosion landforms: yardang, zeugen, inselberg, ventifact, mushroom rock, pediment. Wind deposition: barchan (crescent, horns downwind), seif/longitudinal dune, loess.
Glacial erosion: cirque, arete, horn, U-shaped valley, hanging valley, fjord (drowned glacial valley). Glacial deposition: moraine, drumlin, esker, outwash plain.

Atmosphere upward: troposphere (all weather; 18 km at equator, 8 km at poles) - stratosphere (ozone) - mesosphere (coldest, meteors burn) - thermosphere/ionosphere - exosphere. Normal lapse rate 6.5 C per km.
Pressure belts: equatorial low (doldrums), sub-tropical high (horse latitudes), sub-polar low, polar high. Planetary winds: Trades, Westerlies (Roaring Forties), Polar Easterlies.

Local winds: Chinook (Rockies, 'snow-eater'), Foehn (Alps), Mistral and Bora (cold), Sirocco (Sahara to Mediterranean), Harmattan (West Africa, 'the Doctor'), Santa Ana (California), Zonda (Argentina), Loo (north India).
Warm currents: Gulf Stream, North Atlantic Drift, Kuroshio, Brazil, Agulhas, East Australian. Cold currents: Labrador, Canary, Benguela, Peru (Humboldt), California, Oyashio, West Wind Drift.

Spring tides on new and full moon (syzygy); neap tides at quadrature. Bay of Fundy (Canada) has the world's highest tidal range. Great Barrier Reef (Coral Sea, Australia) is the largest coral reef system; reef types - fringing, barrier, atoll.

questions.q: Which of the following is the highest peak of the African continent?
questions.exp: Mount Kilimanjaro (5,895 m) in Tanzania is Africa's highest peak and a dormant stratovolcano. Mount Kenya (5,199 m) is the continent's second highest.

questions.q: Aconcagua, the highest peak of South America, lies in which mountain range?
questions.exp: Aconcagua (about 6,960 m) in Argentina is the highest peak of the Andes and the highest point of the entire Western and Southern Hemispheres.

questions.q: Mount Elbrus, the highest peak of Europe, is located in which mountain range?
questions.exp: Mount Elbrus (5,642 m) in Russia lies in the Caucasus range and is the highest point of Europe. Mont Blanc (4,808 m) in the Alps is the highest peak of Western Europe.

questions.q: Vinson Massif is the highest peak of which continent?
questions.exp: Vinson Massif (4,892 m) in the Sentinel Range of the Ellsworth Mountains is the highest peak of Antarctica.

questions.q: Denali, the highest mountain of North America, is situated in which country?
questions.exp: Denali (6,190 m), formerly called Mount McKinley, stands in the Alaska Range in the United States. Its officially accepted height was revised to 6,190 m in 2015.

questions.q: Which is the longest mountain range on the surface of the continents?
questions.exp: The Andes run about 7,000 km along the western edge of South America through seven countries. The Mid-Oceanic Ridge (about 65,000 km) is longer but lies almost entirely under the sea.

questions.q: Which mountain range is conventionally taken as the boundary between Europe and Asia?
questions.exp: The Ural Mountains, running roughly north to south across Russia, form the conventional dividing line between Europe and Asia.

questions.q: Which plateau of the world is known as the 'Roof of the World'?
questions.exp: The Tibetan Plateau, lying between the Himalaya and the Kunlun ranges, is the world's highest and largest plateau, with an average elevation above 4,500 m.

questions.q: The Grand Canyon has been cut by the Colorado river into which plateau?
questions.exp: The Grand Canyon is carved into the Colorado Plateau of the south-western United States, the classic example of a plateau dissected by river erosion.

questions.q: Which is the driest desert of the world?
questions.exp: The Atacama desert of northern Chile is the driest non-polar desert, kept arid by the cold Peru (Humboldt) current and by the rain shadow of the Andes.

questions.q: The Gobi desert is spread over which of the following?
questions.exp: The Gobi, a cold-winter desert of Asia, extends across southern Mongolia and northern China. The Karakum lies in Turkmenistan and the Kyzylkum in Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan.

questions.q: The Patagonian desert lies mainly in which country?
questions.exp: The Patagonian desert (about 6.73 lakh sq km) of southern Argentina is the largest desert of the Americas. It is a cold rain-shadow desert lying east of the Andes.

questions.q: Which of the following is the largest hot desert of the world?
questions.exp: The Sahara of northern Africa, over 8.5 million sq km in extent, is the world's largest hot desert. The Antarctic and Arctic polar deserts are larger overall.

questions.q: The surface of separation between the crust and the mantle of the earth is known as:
questions.exp: The Mohorovicic (Moho) discontinuity separates the crust from the mantle, while the Gutenberg discontinuity separates the mantle from the core.

questions.q: The theory of continental drift was propounded by:
questions.exp: Alfred Wegener put forward the continental drift theory in 1912, proposing a single supercontinent Pangaea surrounded by the ocean Panthalassa. Harry Hess later proposed sea-floor spreading.

questions.q: Which of the following seismic waves cannot pass through the liquid outer core of the earth?
questions.exp: Secondary (S) waves are transverse and travel only through solids. Their absence beyond about 103 degrees creates the shadow zone and proves that the outer core is liquid.

questions.q: Which of the following is the highest volcano in the world?
questions.exp: Nevado Ojos del Salado, on the Chile-Argentina border in the Andes, is the world's highest volcano. Mauna Loa in Hawaii is the largest active volcano by volume.

questions.q: The ozone layer of the atmosphere occurs in which layer?
questions.exp: The ozone layer lies within the stratosphere, roughly 15 to 35 km above the surface, and absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation from the sun.

questions.q: The local wind 'Chinook', known as the snow-eater, blows in which region?
opts: Eastern slopes of the Rocky Mountains
questions.exp: The Chinook is a warm dry descending wind on the eastern slopes of the Rockies in North America; it melts snow rapidly, hence 'snow-eater'. Its European counterpart is the Foehn of the Alps.

questions.q: The world's highest tidal range is recorded in the:
questions.exp: The Bay of Fundy in eastern Canada records the world's highest tidal range, exceeding 15 metres, because of its funnel shape and tidal resonance.

questions.q: The Great Barrier Reef, the world's largest coral reef system, lies off the coast of:
questions.exp: The Great Barrier Reef lies in the Coral Sea off the coast of Queensland in north-eastern Australia and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Circum-Pacific belt:
I. It is popularly known as the Ring of Fire.
II. About two-thirds of the world's active volcanoes lie along it.
III. It consists only of divergent plate boundaries.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Circum-Pacific belt or Ring of Fire is the world's greatest earthquake and volcano belt, but it is dominated by convergent boundaries and subduction zones, not by divergent boundaries.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Wegener's continental drift theory:
I. The single supercontinent was named Pangaea.
II. The ocean surrounding it was named Panthalassa.
III. Pangaea split into Laurasia in the north and Gondwana in the south.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. The narrow sea separating Laurasia from Gondwana was the Tethys, from whose sediments the Himalaya were later folded up.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sahara desert:
I. It is the largest hot desert of the world.
II. It lies in northern Africa.
III. The Nile flows through its eastern part.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. The Sahara spreads over more than 8.5 million sq km of northern Africa and is crossed in the east by the Nile, which sustains Egypt's settled agriculture.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about barchans:
I. They are crescent-shaped sand dunes.
II. Their horns extend in the direction towards which the wind blows.
III. They are landforms produced by glacial deposition.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Barchans are crescentic dunes formed by wind (aeolian) deposition, with horns pointing downwind; they have nothing to do with glaciers. Dunes aligned parallel to the wind are called seifs.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. A fjord is a drowned glacial valley invaded by the sea.
II. A cirque is an armchair-shaped hollow produced by glacial erosion.
III. A drumlin is a landform of glacial deposition.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. Norway, Chile, New Zealand and Greenland have the world's best developed fjord coasts.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Tibetan Plateau:
I. It is the highest plateau in the world.
II. It lies between the Himalaya and the Kunlun ranges.
III. It is an example of an intermontane plateau.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. An intermontane plateau is one enclosed by mountain ranges; the Tibetan, Bolivian and Anatolian plateaus are of this type.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about tides:
I. Spring tides occur on full moon and new moon days.
II. Neap tides occur when the sun and the moon are at right angles with respect to the earth.
III. Spring tides occur only during the spring season.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Spring tides are the highest tides and occur when the sun, earth and moon are in a line (syzygy); they have nothing to do with the spring season. Neap tides occur at quadrature.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the troposphere:
I. It contains almost all the water vapour and dust of the atmosphere.
II. Temperature in it falls at an average rate of about 6.5 degrees Celsius per kilometre.
III. It is thicker over the poles than over the equator.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The troposphere is about 18 km thick over the equator but only about 8 km over the poles, so the third statement is wrong. All weather phenomena occur in this lowest layer.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Mountain peak)   List-II (Continent)
A. Kilimanjaro   1. North America
B. Aconcagua     2. Europe
C. Denali        3. Africa
D. Elbrus        4. South America
questions.exp: Kilimanjaro is the highest peak of Africa, Aconcagua of South America, Denali of North America and Elbrus of Europe.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Desert)   List-II (Continent / region)
A. Gobi        1. Australia
B. Patagonia   2. Southern Africa
C. Victoria    3. Asia
D. Kalahari    4. South America
questions.exp: The Gobi lies in Asia (Mongolia and China), Patagonia in South America (Argentina), the Great Victoria in Australia and the Kalahari in southern Africa.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Local wind)   List-II (Region)
A. Mistral    1. West Africa
B. Harmattan  2. France
C. Santa Ana  3. Argentina
D. Zonda      4. California
questions.exp: The Mistral is a cold wind of southern France, the Harmattan a dry dusty wind of West Africa, the Santa Ana a hot dry wind of southern California and the Zonda a warm descending wind of Argentina.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Ocean current)   List-II (Description)

B. Benguela   2. Warm current off eastern Japan
C. Labrador   3. Warm current off south-eastern Africa
D. Agulhas    4. Cold current off south-western Africa
questions.exp: The Kuroshio is a warm Pacific current off Japan, the Benguela a cold current off south-western Africa, the Labrador a cold current off north-eastern North America and the Agulhas a warm current off south-eastern Africa.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Plateau)   List-II (Country)
A. Katanga      1. Turkey
B. Anatolian    2. Democratic Republic of the Congo
C. Meseta       3. Brazil
D. Mato Grosso  4. Spain
questions.exp: The Katanga (Shaba) plateau of the DR Congo is a great copper belt, the Anatolian plateau lies in Turkey, the Meseta is the central plateau of Spain and the Mato Grosso plateau is in Brazil.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of a mountain peak and its continent is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Mount Kosciuszko (2,228 m) is the highest peak of mainland Australia, not of Europe. The highest peak of Europe is Mount Elbrus in the Caucasus.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of a desert and its location is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The Namib is a coastal desert of south-western Africa, mainly in Namibia, and is regarded as the world's oldest desert. The chief South American deserts are the Atacama and the Patagonian.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a landform produced by glacial action?
questions.exp: A yardang is a wind-eroded ridge of a desert region. Cirques are landforms of glacial erosion, while eskers and drumlins are of glacial deposition.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the layers of the atmosphere is NOT correct?
opts: The stratosphere is the lowest layer of the atmosphere
The mesosphere is the layer in which most meteors burn up
The ionosphere reflects radio waves back to the earth
The exosphere is the outermost layer of the atmosphere
questions.exp: The troposphere, not the stratosphere, is the lowest layer of the atmosphere. The stratosphere lies above the tropopause and contains the ozone layer.

questions.q:
Arrange the following continental highest peaks in descending order of their height:
I. Mount Kilimanjaro
II. Denali
III. Mount Aconcagua
IV. Mount Elbrus
questions.exp: Aconcagua (about 6,960 m) > Denali (6,190 m) > Kilimanjaro (5,895 m) > Elbrus (5,642 m). Mount Everest (8,848.86 m) tops the list of continental highest peaks.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Atacama is one of the driest places on the earth.
Reason (R): It lies along a west coast washed by a cold ocean current and in the rain shadow of the Andes.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: The cold Peru (Humboldt) current chills the air over the coast and suppresses convection, while the Andes block moisture coming from the Amazon side; together they keep the Atacama extremely arid.

chapters.title: Rivers and Lakes of the World
factsheet: Nile (about 6,650 km) - longest river of the world and of Africa; rises in the East African highlands via the Kagera; drains into the Mediterranean Sea through a large delta in Egypt.
Amazon (about 6,400 km) - second longest but largest in discharge and basin area; rises in the Peruvian Andes, drains into the Atlantic Ocean.
Yangtze (about 6,300 km) - longest river of Asia and the longest flowing wholly within one country; drains into the East China Sea.
Mississippi-Missouri (about 6,275 km) - longest of North America; drains into the Gulf of Mexico with a bird's-foot delta.
Siberian rivers flowing north to the Arctic: Yenisei (5,539 km) to the Kara Sea, Ob-Irtysh (5,410 km) to the Gulf of Ob, Lena (4,400 km) to the Laptev Sea.
Huang He / Yellow river (5,464 km) - the 'Sorrow of China' because of its floods; carries a huge load of loess; drains into the Bohai Sea.

Volga (about 3,645 km) - longest river of Europe, entirely in Russia, drains into the Caspian Sea. Danube - second longest in Europe, passes through 10 countries and 4 capitals, drains into the Black Sea.
Congo (about 4,700 km) - the only major river crossing the Equator twice; the world's deepest river; drains into the Atlantic through an estuary, not a delta.
African outfalls: Niger - Gulf of Guinea; Zambezi - Indian Ocean (forms the Victoria Falls); Orange - Atlantic; Limpopo - Indian Ocean.
Murray-Darling - longest river system of Australia. Mekong - flows through China, Myanmar, Laos, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam into the South China Sea.
Tigris and Euphrates unite in southern Iraq to form the Shatt al-Arab, which enters the Persian Gulf.

European rivers and cities: Rhine - North Sea (Rotterdam); Rhone - Mediterranean; Elbe - Hamburg; Seine - Paris; Tiber - Rome; Thames - London; Vistula - Warsaw; Spree - Berlin; Danube - Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest, Belgrade.
The Blue Nile (from Lake Tana, Ethiopia) and the White Nile meet at Khartoum in Sudan.
North American outfalls: Mackenzie - Beaufort Sea (Arctic); Yukon - Bering Sea; Colorado - Gulf of California; St. Lawrence - Atlantic via the Great Lakes.
Parana-Rio de la Plata (about 4,880 km) - second longest of South America; Orinoco - Venezuela; Sao Francisco - Brazil.
Ganga-Brahmaputra delta (Sundarbans) is the world's largest delta. The Congo and the Amazon discharge through estuaries rather than true deltas.
Angel Falls (979 m), Venezuela - world's highest waterfall; plunges from the Auyan-tepui in Canaima National Park into a tributary of the Churun. Tugela Falls, South Africa, is second.

Victoria Falls - on the Zambezi, Zambia-Zimbabwe border, called Mosi-oa-Tunya, 'the smoke that thunders'. Niagara - USA-Canada; Iguazu - Argentina-Brazil; Boyoma (Congo) - greatest volume of any waterfall.
Suez Canal - opened 1869, about 193 km, joins the Mediterranean (Port Said) to the Red Sea (Suez); a sea-level canal with no locks; nationalised by Egypt in 1956.
Panama Canal - opened 1914, about 82 km, joins the Atlantic and the Pacific and works through a system of locks lifting ships to Gatun Lake. Kiel Canal - 1895, about 98 km, North Sea to Baltic Sea.
Caspian Sea (about 3.7 lakh sq km) - largest lake on earth, a landlocked salt lake bordered by Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan.
Lake Superior (82,100 sq km) - largest freshwater lake by area; Lake Victoria (about 69,000 sq km) - largest lake of Africa and second largest freshwater lake by area.

Lake Baikal - deepest lake (1,642 m) and largest freshwater lake by volume, holding about a fifth of the world's unfrozen surface fresh water; a tectonic rift lake in Siberia. Lake Tanganyika (1,470 m) is second deepest and the world's longest freshwater lake.

Lake Titicaca (3,812 m, Peru-Bolivia) - highest navigable lake. Dead Sea shore (about 430 m below sea level) - lowest exposed land surface on earth. Lake Eyre - lowest point and largest salt lake of Australia. Lake Ladoga - largest lake of Europe.
Aral Sea (Kazakhstan-Uzbekistan) shrank drastically after the Amu Darya and Syr Darya were diverted for cotton irrigation. Lake Chad is shared by Chad, Niger, Nigeria and Cameroon.
Sargasso Sea (North Atlantic) - the only sea without a coastline; it is bounded by ocean currents of the North Atlantic gyre.

Straits: Bering (Asia-North America), Gibraltar (Mediterranean-Atlantic; Europe-Africa), Malacca (Sumatra-Malay Peninsula), Hormuz (Persian Gulf-Gulf of Oman), Bab-el-Mandeb (Red Sea-Gulf of Aden), Bosphorus (Black Sea-Sea of Marmara), Magellan, Palk Strait (India-Sri Lanka).
Lake types: tectonic (Baikal, Tanganyika, Dead Sea), crater or caldera (Crater Lake, Toba), glacial (Great Lakes), ox-bow (fluvial), lagoon (coastal), artificial (Lake Volta, Lake Nasser).

questions.q: Which is the longest river in the world?
questions.exp: The Nile, about 6,650 km long, is conventionally reckoned the world's longest river. It rises in the East African highlands and drains into the Mediterranean Sea through a large delta in Egypt.

questions.q: Which river carries the largest volume of water to the sea?
questions.exp: The Amazon has by far the greatest discharge and the largest drainage basin of any river, accounting for roughly a fifth of the world's total river flow into the oceans.

questions.q: Which is the longest river of Asia?
questions.exp: The Yangtze, about 6,300 km long, is Asia's longest river and the longest river flowing entirely within a single country. It drains into the East China Sea.

questions.q: The Volga, the longest river of Europe, drains into which water body?
questions.exp: The Volga, about 3,645 km long, flows entirely within Russia and empties into the Caspian Sea, an inland basin with no outlet to the ocean.

questions.q: Which river of the world crosses the Equator twice?
questions.exp: The Congo crosses the Equator twice in its great arc through central Africa, which gives it a fairly even flow throughout the year. It is also the world's deepest river.

questions.q: Which river is known as the 'Sorrow of China'?
questions.exp: The Huang He or Yellow River earned this name from its disastrous floods. Its yellow colour and raised bed come from the enormous load of loess that it carries.

questions.q: The Victoria Falls are situated on which river?
questions.exp: The Victoria Falls, locally called Mosi-oa-Tunya or 'the smoke that thunders', lie on the Zambezi on the Zambia-Zimbabwe border.

questions.q: The Angel Falls, the highest waterfall of the world, is located in:
questions.exp: The Angel Falls (979 m) plunges from the Auyan-tepui in Canaima National Park, Venezuela, into a tributary of the Churun river. Tugela Falls in South Africa is the second highest.

questions.q: The Tigris and the Euphrates unite to form which waterway?
questions.exp: The Tigris and the Euphrates join in southern Iraq to form the Shatt al-Arab, which then flows into the Persian Gulf.

questions.q: The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea with the:
questions.exp: Opened in 1869 and about 193 km long, the Suez Canal joins the Mediterranean at Port Said with the Red Sea at Suez. Being a sea-level canal, it has no locks.

questions.q: Which of the following canals connects the Atlantic Ocean with the Pacific Ocean?
questions.exp: The Panama Canal, opened in 1914 and about 82 km long, links the Atlantic with the Pacific and works through a system of locks that lift ships up to Gatun Lake.

questions.q: Which is the largest lake in the world by surface area?
questions.exp: The Caspian Sea, bordered by Russia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, Iran and Azerbaijan, is a landlocked salt lake of roughly 3.7 lakh sq km, the largest lake on earth.

questions.q: Which is the deepest lake in the world?
questions.exp: Lake Baikal in Siberia reaches a depth of 1,642 m and holds about a fifth of the world's unfrozen surface fresh water. Lake Tanganyika (1,470 m) is the second deepest.

questions.q: Which is the largest freshwater lake in the world by surface area?
questions.exp: Lake Superior, about 82,100 sq km in area and one of the Great Lakes of North America, is the largest freshwater lake by surface area. Lake Victoria in Africa is second.

questions.q: Lake Titicaca, the highest navigable lake of the world, lies on the border of:
questions.exp: Lake Titicaca lies at about 3,812 m on the Altiplano of the Andes between Peru and Bolivia.

questions.q: The lowest exposed land surface on the earth is the shore of the:
questions.exp: The shore of the Dead Sea, between Israel and Jordan, lies about 430 m below sea level. Its extreme salinity makes bathers float easily.

questions.q: Which is the only sea in the world that has no coastline?
questions.exp: The Sargasso Sea in the North Atlantic is bounded not by land but by the ocean currents of the North Atlantic gyre, and is named after its floating Sargassum weed.

questions.q: The Bering Strait separates:
questions.exp: The Bering Strait separates Russia from Alaska and links the Bering Sea with the Arctic Ocean. The Strait of Gibraltar separates Europe from Africa.

questions.q: The Danube river drains into which sea?
questions.exp: The Danube, Europe's second longest river, rises in the Black Forest of Germany, passes through ten countries and four national capitals, and empties into the Black Sea.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Amazon river:
I. It has the largest drainage basin in the world.
II. It flows into the Pacific Ocean.
III. It rises in the Andes of Peru.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Amazon rises in the Peruvian Andes and flows eastward across Brazil into the Atlantic Ocean, not the Pacific. Its basin is the largest in the world.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Lake Baikal:
I. It is a tectonic rift lake.
II. It lies in Siberia in Russia.
III. It is the deepest lake in the world.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. Baikal occupies a continental rift valley, is more than 25 million years old and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Suez Canal:
I. It was opened for traffic in 1869.
II. It is a sea-level canal without locks.
III. It shortens the sea route between Europe and Asia by avoiding the Cape of Good Hope.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. Egypt nationalised the canal in 1956, an act that led to the Suez crisis of that year.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Nile:
I. The Blue Nile and the White Nile meet at Khartoum.
II. It drains into the Red Sea.
III. It is the longest river of Africa.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Nile drains into the Mediterranean Sea, not the Red Sea. The Blue Nile, rising from Lake Tana in Ethiopia, joins the White Nile at Khartoum in Sudan.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Aral Sea:
I. It lies between Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan.
II. It has shrunk drastically because the Amu Darya and the Syr Darya were diverted for irrigation.
III. It is a freshwater lake fed by the Volga.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Aral Sea is a saline lake fed by the Amu Darya and the Syr Darya, not by the Volga. Heavy diversion of these rivers for cotton irrigation caused one of the worst man-made ecological disasters of the last century.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Ganga-Brahmaputra delta is the largest delta in the world.
II. The Mississippi has a bird's-foot delta.
III. The Congo enters the Atlantic Ocean through a large delta.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Congo discharges through a deep estuary and submarine canyon rather than a delta, because strong currents and its steep gradient prevent deposition at the mouth.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

A. Lake Titicaca    1. Russia
B. Lake Eyre        2. Peru and Bolivia
C. Lake Ladoga      3. Canada

questions.q:

A. Strait of Hormuz     1. Red Sea and Gulf of Aden
B. Bab-el-Mandeb        2. Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman

questions.exp: About a fifth of the world's oil trade passes through the Strait of Hormuz, and the Bab-el-Mandeb is the southern gateway to the Red Sea and the Suez route.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Waterfall)   List-II (River)
A. Niagara Falls   1. Iguazu
B. Iguazu Falls    2. Niagara
C. Boyoma Falls    3. Zambezi
D. Victoria Falls  4. Congo
questions.exp: The Boyoma (formerly Stanley) Falls on the Congo carry the greatest volume of water of any waterfall in the world.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of a river and a country through which it flows is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The Tagus is the longest river of the Iberian Peninsula, flowing through Spain and Portugal and reaching the Atlantic at Lisbon. The chief river of Italy is the Po.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of a city and the river on which it stands is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Paris stands on the Seine. The Rhine passes Basel, Cologne and Rotterdam before entering the North Sea.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the lakes of the world is NOT correct?
opts: Lake Victoria is the largest lake of Africa
Lake Tanganyika is the longest freshwater lake in the world
Lake Chad is shared by Chad, Niger, Nigeria and Cameroon
Lake Malawi is the deepest lake in the world
questions.exp: Lake Baikal is the deepest lake in the world at 1,642 m, followed by Lake Tanganyika at 1,470 m. Lake Malawi is far shallower than either.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs relating to the canals of the world is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Panama Canal - a sea-level canal without locks
Kiel Canal - connects the North Sea with the Baltic Sea
questions.exp: The Panama Canal works through a system of locks that raise ships to Gatun Lake and lower them again. It is the Suez Canal that is a sea-level canal without locks.

questions.q:
Arrange the following rivers in descending order of their length:
I. Mississippi-Missouri
II. Nile
III. Yangtze
IV. Amazon
questions.exp: Nile (about 6,650 km) > Amazon (about 6,400 km) > Yangtze (about 6,300 km) > Mississippi-Missouri (about 6,275 km).

chapters.title: Natural Vegetation and Biomes
factsheet: Equatorial evergreen rainforest ('Selva') - Amazon basin, Congo basin and South-East Asia; multi-storeyed, dense canopy, lianas and epiphytes; no distinct leaf-shedding season.
Equatorial hardwoods: mahogany, ebony, rosewood, greenheart, cinchona; scattered occurrence makes commercial exploitation difficult.
Tropical deciduous or monsoon forest - teak, sal, sandalwood, bamboo; sheds leaves in the dry season; commercially the most useful forest of the monsoon lands.
Savanna (tropical grassland) - tall coarse grass with scattered acacia and baobab; called the 'big game country' for its lion, zebra, giraffe, elephant and wildebeest.
Tropical grassland names: Llanos (Orinoco basin, Venezuela), Campos (Brazilian highlands), Sudan/Sahel type (Africa), northern Australian savanna.

Temperate grassland-region pairs: Prairie - North America; Pampas - Argentina and Uruguay; Steppe - Eurasia; Veld - South Africa; Downs - Australia; Canterbury - New Zealand; Puszta - Hungary; Manchurian - north-east China.
Temperate grasslands are practically treeless, lie in continental interiors with 25-75 cm rainfall, and are the world's granaries and great ranching lands; herdsmen of the Pampas are called gauchos.

Mediterranean vegetation - hot dry summers and mild wet winters; sclerophyllous plants with thick bark, small waxy leaves and deep roots; citrus, olives, grapes and cork oak; the 'orchard lands' of the world.
Mediterranean scrub names: Maquis and Garrigue (Mediterranean basin), Chaparral (California), Matorral (central Chile), Fynbos (Cape region, South Africa), Mallee (south-western Australia).
Taiga or boreal coniferous forest - largest land biome, a continuous belt across Siberia, Canada and Scandinavia, confined almost wholly to the Northern Hemisphere.
Conifers - pine, fir, spruce, larch, cedar; evergreen, conical, needle-leaved; the world's chief source of softwood, pulp, newsprint and matchwood.
Tundra - beyond the tree line, underlain by permafrost; mosses, lichens (reindeer moss) and sedges; growing season only about two months; caribou/reindeer, musk ox, arctic fox, polar bear.
Temperate deciduous forest - oak, ash, beech, elm, maple; western Europe, eastern USA and eastern Asia; the most cleared of all forest belts.
Desert vegetation - xerophytes such as cactus, acacia, date palm and euphorbia; long roots, thick cuticle, spines in place of leaves, water-storing stems.
Mangrove or tidal forest - salt tolerant with stilt roots and pneumatophores; the Sundarbans of the Ganga-Brahmaputra delta is the world's largest mangrove forest.
World forest area is about 4.14 billion hectares, roughly 31-32 per cent of the global land area (FAO Global Forest Resources Assessment).
More than half of the world's forests are in five countries: Russia (about 832 million ha, one-fifth of the world total), Brazil, Canada, the United States and China.
Nearly half of the world's forests are tropical; TROPICAL FORESTS RECORD THE MAXIMUM GLOBAL DEFORESTATION.
