questions.exp: Odisha has the largest manganese reserves (about 34%), but Madhya Pradesh leads in production, followed by Maharashtra and then Odisha.

chapters.title: Location, Extent and Physiographic Divisions
factsheet: Area 3,42,239 sq km = 10.41% of India; largest Indian state by area since 1 November 2000 (Chhattisgarh carved out of Madhya Pradesh).
Latitudinal extent 23 deg 3' N to 30 deg 12' N (7 deg 9'); longitudinal extent 69 deg 30' E to 78 deg 17' E (8 deg 47').
North-south length 826 km; east-west length 869 km; difference 43 km. Shape roughly rhombus/kite.
Extreme points: N - Kona (Sri Ganganagar); S - Borkunda (Banswara); E - Silana (Dholpur); W - Katra (Jaisalmer).
Tropic of Cancer (23.5 deg N) grazes the extreme south - Banswara and Dungarpur districts only.
International border with Pakistan = 1,070 km (Radcliffe Line, 17 August 1947), from Hindumal Kot (Sri Ganganagar) to Shahgarh bulge (Barmer).
Jaisalmer has the longest international border (about 464 km); Sri Ganganagar, Bikaner and Barmer are the other border districts.
Inter-state boundaries: Madhya Pradesh longest (~1,600 km), Haryana ~1,262 km, Gujarat ~1,022 km, Uttar Pradesh ~877 km, Punjab shortest (~89 km).
Uttar Pradesh touches only Bharatpur and Dholpur; Punjab touches only Sri Ganganagar and Hanumangarh.
Administrative position 2025-26: 41 districts and 7 divisions (Jaipur, Jodhpur, Ajmer, Kota, Udaipur, Bikaner, Bharatpur).
2023: 19 new districts + 3 new divisions (Banswara, Pali, Sikar). December 2024: 9 districts and all 3 new divisions denotified on the Lalit K. Panwar committee's report.
Eight new districts retained: Balotra, Beawar, Deeg, Didwana-Kuchaman, Khairthal-Tijara, Kotputli-Behror, Phalodi, Salumbar.
Four physiographic divisions - Western Sandy Plain (~61% area, ~40% population), Aravalli Hilly region (~9%, ~10%), Eastern Plain (~23%, ~39%), South-Eastern Hadoti Plateau (~7%, ~11%).
Thar (Marusthali) is India's largest desert; in Rajasthan it runs about 640 km NE-SW and 300-360 km wide; 'desert triangle' = Jodhpur-Jaisalmer-Bikaner.
Dunes: barchan (crescentic, Shekhawati-Churu), longitudinal/seif (parallel to wind, maximum in Jaisalmer), transverse, parabolic (Bikaner), star (Pokhran-Mohangarh), coppice/nabkha.
Semi-arid Bangar sub-regions: Ghaggar plain (locally 'Nali'), Shekhawati-Torawati internal drainage, Nagauri upland, Luni basin (Godwar - Pali, Sirohi, Jalore).
Aravalli - oldest fold mountain range of India, trends SW-NE about 692 km from Palanpur (Gujarat) to Delhi; roughly 80% of it lies in Rajasthan; Great Boundary Fault marks its north-eastern margin.
Peaks: Guru Shikhar 1,722 m (Sirohi) highest; Ser 1,597 m (Sirohi); Delwara 1,442 m (Sirohi); Jarga 1,431 m (Udaipur); Achalgarh 1,380 m (Sirohi); Kumbhalgarh 1,224 m (Rajsamand).
Northern Aravalli peaks: Raghunathgarh 1,055 m (Sikar) highest in Shekhawati, Malkhet 1,052 m (Sikar), Khoh 920 m (Jaipur), Harshnath 820 m (Sikar), Bairath/Bhairach 792 m (Alwar).
Central Aravalli: Todgarh (Morarji) 934 m, Taragarh 873 m (Ajmer), Nag Pahar 795 m (Ajmer); Merwara hills divide Marwar from Mewar.
Bhorat plateau (about 1,225 m) lies between Gogunda and Kumbhalgarh - the highest plateau of Rajasthan; Girwa is the saucer-shaped basin around Udaipur.
Mount Abu (Sirohi) is Rajasthan's only hill station - a detached granite mass (inselberg) at the south-western end of the Aravalli, carrying Guru Shikhar and Nakki lake.
Aravalli passes (nal/dara): Desuri Nal, Haldighati, Som, Deobari, Kevada ki Nal, Pipli, Hathi Guda; most passes lie in the central Aravalli.
Eastern Plain sub-units: Banas basin (Mewar plain and Malpura-Karauli plain), Chambal basin with beehad/badlands (Dholpur, Karauli, Sawai Madhopur), Mahi basin.
Mahi basin regions: Chappan plain (56 streams/villages, Banswara-Pratapgarh), Vagad (Dungarpur-Banswara), Kanthal (Pratapgarh).

Hadoti (Pathar) plateau has two parts - Vindhyan scarpland (between the Banas and the Chambal; Karauli, Sawai Madhopur, Bundi, Kota; 350-550 m sandstone) and the Deccan lava plateau (black soil; Kota, Bundi, Baran, Jhalawar).
Dang - the ravine/badland tract of Dholpur, Karauli and Sawai Madhopur; Mukundara and Bundi hills are the arc-shaped ranges of Hadoti.

Cultural regions: Marwar (Jodhpur-Pali-Nagaur), Mewar (Udaipur-Bhilwara-Chittorgarh), Hadoti (Kota-Bundi-Baran-Jhalawar), Shekhawati (Sikar-Jhunjhunu-Churu), Dhundhar (Jaipur), Mewat (Alwar-Bharatpur), Braj (Bharatpur-Dholpur).
Malani igneous suite of Jodhpur-Barmer is among the oldest volcanic rock formations of India; Rajasthan's rocks span Pre-Cambrian Aravalli and Delhi Supergroups and Vindhyan sandstone.

questions.q: The total geographical area of Rajasthan is:
questions.exp: Rajasthan covers 3,42,239 sq km, which is 10.41% of India's area. The distractors are the areas of Madhya Pradesh (3,08,252), Uttar Pradesh (2,40,928) and Gujarat (1,96,024).

questions.q: Rajasthan became the largest State of India by area in the year:
questions.exp: Rajasthan overtook Madhya Pradesh on 1 November 2000, when Chhattisgarh was carved out of MP. Before that Rajasthan was the second largest state.

questions.q: Rajasthan accounts for what percentage of the total geographical area of India?
questions.exp: 3,42,239 sq km out of India's 32,87,263 sq km works out to about 10.41%. Rajasthan holds this area with only about 5.67% of India's population (Census 2011).

questions.q: The latitudinal extent of Rajasthan is:
questions.exp: Rajasthan lies between 23 deg 3' N and 30 deg 12' N, a spread of 7 deg 9'. The whole state therefore lies north of the Tropic of Cancer except its extreme southern fringe.

questions.q: The longitudinal extent of Rajasthan is:
questions.exp: Rajasthan extends from 69 deg 30' E to 78 deg 17' E, a spread of 8 deg 47'. The westernmost point is Katra village in Jaisalmer and the easternmost is Silana village in Dholpur.

questions.q: The north-to-south length of Rajasthan is approximately:
questions.exp: Rajasthan measures about 826 km from north to south and 869 km from east to west, a difference of 43 km.

questions.q: The difference between the east-west and the north-south extent of Rajasthan is:
questions.exp: East-west 869 km minus north-south 826 km = 43 km. This is a favourite RPSC one-liner because both figures look similar.

questions.q: The northernmost point of Rajasthan, Kona village, lies in which district?
questions.exp: Kona village in Sri Ganganagar district (30 deg 12' N) is Rajasthan's northernmost point. The southernmost is Borkunda in Banswara.

questions.q: The Tropic of Cancer passes through which districts of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The Tropic of Cancer clips only the extreme southern tip of Rajasthan, crossing Banswara and Dungarpur districts. Hence almost the whole state lies in the sub-tropical belt.

questions.q: The length of Rajasthan's international boundary with Pakistan is about:
questions.exp: The Radcliffe Line runs about 1,070 km along Rajasthan, from Hindumal Kot in Sri Ganganagar to the Shahgarh bulge in Barmer. 1,600 km is Rajasthan's boundary with Madhya Pradesh.

questions.q: Which district of Rajasthan shares the longest international border with Pakistan?
questions.exp: Jaisalmer accounts for about 464 km of the 1,070 km Radcliffe Line - by far the longest share of any Rajasthan district.

questions.q: The Radcliffe Line in Rajasthan begins in the north from:
questions.exp: Rajasthan's stretch of the Radcliffe Line runs from Hindumal Kot (Sri Ganganagar) in the north to the Shahgarh bulge (Barmer) in the south. Munabao is the railway crossing point on the Barmer border.

questions.q: With which of the following States does Rajasthan share its shortest boundary?
questions.exp: Rajasthan's border with Punjab is only about 89 km, touching Sri Ganganagar and Hanumangarh. Its longest inter-state boundary is with Madhya Pradesh (~1,600 km).

questions.q: Rajasthan shares its longest inter-State boundary with:
questions.exp: The Rajasthan-Madhya Pradesh boundary is about 1,600 km, the longest of the five states Rajasthan touches. Haryana follows with about 1,262 km.

questions.q: Which two districts of Rajasthan touch the boundary of Uttar Pradesh?
questions.exp: Only Bharatpur and Dholpur touch Uttar Pradesh. Karauli and Sawai Madhopur border Madhya Pradesh, not UP.

questions.q: As per the administrative position after the December 2024 review, Rajasthan has:
questions.exp: The 2023 reorganisation created 19 new districts and 3 new divisions; in December 2024 nine districts and all three new divisions were denotified, leaving 41 districts and 7 divisions (Jaipur, Jodhpur, Ajmer, Kota, Udaipur, Bikaner, Bharatpur).

questions.q: The committee whose report led to the denotification of nine newly created districts of Rajasthan in December 2024 was headed by:
questions.exp: A committee under retired IAS officer Dr Lalit K. Panwar reviewed the districts created in 2023; on its report nine districts and the Banswara, Pali and Sikar divisions were dissolved.

questions.q: Which physiographic division occupies the largest share of Rajasthan's area?
questions.exp: The Western Sandy Plain covers about 61% of the state but supports only about 40% of its population. The Eastern Plain, with 23% of the area, carries about 39% of the population.

questions.q: The 'Desert Triangle' of Rajasthan is formed by which three cities?
questions.exp: Jodhpur, Jaisalmer and Bikaner form the classic desert triangle of the Thar. The Thar is India's largest desert and covers roughly 61% of Rajasthan.

questions.q: Longitudinal (seif) sand dunes are found in maximum numbers in which district of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Longitudinal dunes lie parallel to the prevailing wind and are most extensive in Jaisalmer. Barchans dominate the Shekhawati-Churu tract and parabolic dunes are common around Bikaner.

questions.q: Barchan dunes are:
opts: Crescent-shaped dunes formed transverse to the prevailing wind
U-shaped dunes with horns pointing upwind
Long ridges lying parallel to the prevailing wind
Multi-armed dunes formed by winds from many directions
questions.exp: Barchans are crescent-shaped and develop across the wind direction, their horns pointing downwind; they are the most mobile dunes and are common in Churu, Jhunjhunu and Sikar. The other options describe parabolic, longitudinal and star dunes.

questions.q: In Rajasthan the Ghaggar plain is locally known as:
questions.exp: The flood plain of the Ghaggar in Hanumangarh-Sri Ganganagar is called 'Nali'. Godwar is the Luni basin of Pali-Sirohi-Jalore and Bagar the semi-arid Shekhawati tract.

questions.q: Guru Shikhar, the highest peak of Rajasthan, is located in which district and what is its height?
questions.exp: Guru Shikhar (1,722 m) on Mount Abu in Sirohi district is the highest point of Rajasthan and of the whole Aravalli range. Ser peak (1,597 m), also in Sirohi, is second.

questions.q: Which is the second highest peak of the Aravalli range?
questions.exp: Ser peak (1,597 m) in Sirohi district ranks second after Guru Shikhar (1,722 m). Delwara is 1,442 m, Jarga 1,431 m and Achalgarh 1,380 m.

questions.q: Raghunathgarh, the highest peak of the Shekhawati region, is situated in which district?
questions.exp: Raghunathgarh (1,055 m) in Sikar district is the highest peak of the northern Aravalli/Shekhawati tract. Malkhet (1,052 m) in the same district is a close second.

questions.q: The Bhorat plateau, the highest plateau of Rajasthan, lies between:
questions.exp: The Bhorat plateau (average height about 1,225 m) lies between Gogunda in Udaipur and Kumbhalgarh in Rajsamand. The Banas rises from the Khamnor hills on its slopes.

questions.q: The Chappan plain of Rajasthan lies in which districts?
questions.exp: The Chappan ('fifty-six') plain of Banswara and Pratapgarh is named after the 56 streams or villages of the Mahi basin that drain it. Vagad covers Dungarpur-Banswara and Kanthal covers Pratapgarh.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Aravalli range:
I. It is the oldest fold mountain range of India.
II. It runs in a south-west to north-east direction for about 692 km.
III. About 80 per cent of its length lies within Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Aravalli is a Pre-Cambrian fold range running from Palanpur in Gujarat to Delhi, and roughly four-fifths of it lies in Rajasthan; the Great Boundary Fault marks its north-eastern margin.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Thar desert:
I. It is the largest desert of India.
II. In Rajasthan it stretches about 640 km in a north-east to south-west direction.
III. It occupies roughly 61 per cent of the area of Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. The Thar or Marusthali is India's largest desert; its Rajasthan portion is about 640 km long and 300-360 km wide and forms the Western Sandy Plain, roughly 61% of the state.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Mount Abu:
I. It is the only hill station of Rajasthan.
II. It stands as a detached granite mass (inselberg) at the south-western end of the Aravalli.
III. Its highest point, Guru Shikhar, lies in Udaipur district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Guru Shikhar lies in Sirohi district, not Udaipur, so III is wrong. Mount Abu is Rajasthan's only hill station and its plateau carries Nakki lake and the Dilwara temples.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the physiographic divisions of Rajasthan:
I. The Western Sandy Plain has about 61 per cent of the area but only about 40 per cent of the population.
II. The Eastern Plain has about 23 per cent of the area and about 39 per cent of the population.
III. The South-Eastern Hadoti plateau is the smallest division by area.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Hadoti plateau covers only about 7% of Rajasthan with about 11% of its people, making it the smallest of the four divisions.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the reorganisation of districts in Rajasthan:
I. Nineteen new districts and three new divisions were created in 2023.
II. Banswara, Pali and Sikar were the three new divisions created.
III. All three new divisions were abolished in December 2024.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. After the December 2024 denotification Rajasthan reverted to 7 divisions, and the number of districts stands at 41.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Hadoti plateau:
I. The Vindhyan scarpland lies between the Banas and the Chambal rivers.
II. The Deccan lava plateau of Rajasthan is characterised by black soil.
III. The Mukundara hills form part of this division.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Vindhyan scarpland (350-550 m sandstone) spreads over Karauli, Sawai Madhopur, Bundi and Kota, while the Deccan lava plateau of Kota-Bundi-Baran-Jhalawar carries black cotton soil.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the sand dunes of Rajasthan:
I. Longitudinal dunes lie parallel to the direction of the prevailing wind.
II. Star dunes are formed where winds blow from several directions.
III. Parabolic dunes are crescent-shaped with their horns pointing downwind.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. In a parabolic dune the horns point upwind (the opposite of a barchan), so III is wrong. Star dunes occur around Pokhran and Mohangarh.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Luni basin of Rajasthan:
I. It is also known as the Godwar region.
II. It is the most humid part of the Western Sandy Plain.
III. It covers parts of Pali, Sirohi and Jalore districts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Luni basin or Godwar lies in the rain-shadow-free south-western foothills of the Aravalli and receives more rain than the rest of western Rajasthan.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the international boundary of Rajasthan:
I. It was drawn as part of the Radcliffe award of 1947.
II. Its total length in Rajasthan is about 1,070 km.
III. Jaisalmer accounts for the largest share of this boundary.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Jaisalmer alone accounts for about 464 km of the 1,070 km line, which runs from Hindumal Kot in Sri Ganganagar to the Shahgarh bulge in Barmer.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Eastern Plain of Rajasthan:
I. It is drained mainly by the Banas, Chambal and Mahi river systems.
II. The badland or beehad topography of this division is best developed in Dholpur, Karauli and Sawai Madhopur.
III. The Girwa is a saucer-shaped basin of this division lying around Udaipur.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. The Girwa around Udaipur belongs to the Aravalli hilly region, not the Eastern Plain, so III is wrong.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Peak)   List-II (District)
A. Jarga    1. Sirohi
B. Kumbhalgarh   2. Udaipur
C. Taragarh    3. Rajsamand
D. Delwara    4. Ajmer
questions.exp: Jarga (1,431 m) is in Udaipur, Kumbhalgarh (1,224 m) in Rajsamand, Taragarh (873 m) in Ajmer and Delwara (1,442 m) in Sirohi.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Peak)   List-II (Height in metres)
A. Guru Shikhar   1. 1,380
B. Ser     2. 1,722
C. Achalgarh    3. 1,055
D. Raghunathgarh   4. 1,597
questions.exp: Guru Shikhar 1,722 m, Ser 1,597 m, Achalgarh 1,380 m and Raghunathgarh 1,055 m. The first three are in Sirohi, Raghunathgarh is in Sikar.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Region)   List-II (Districts)
A. Vagad    1. Pratapgarh
B. Kanthal    2. Dungarpur and Banswara
C. Godwar    3. Sikar, Jhunjhunu and Churu
D. Shekhawati   4. Pali, Sirohi and Jalore
questions.exp: Vagad is the Dungarpur-Banswara tract, Kanthal is Pratapgarh, Godwar the Luni basin of Pali-Sirohi-Jalore, and Shekhawati covers Sikar, Jhunjhunu and Churu.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Extreme point of Rajasthan)   List-II (District)
A. Kona (north)   1. Banswara
B. Borkunda (south)  2. Dholpur
C. Silana (east)   3. Sri Ganganagar
D. Katra (west)   4. Jaisalmer
questions.exp: Kona is in Sri Ganganagar (30 deg 12' N), Borkunda in Banswara (23 deg 3' N), Silana in Dholpur (78 deg 17' E) and Katra in Jaisalmer (69 deg 30' E).

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Neighbouring State)   List-II (Approximate boundary length with Rajasthan)
A. Madhya Pradesh   1. 89 km
B. Punjab    2. 1,600 km
C. Uttar Pradesh   3. 1,022 km
D. Gujarat    4. 877 km
questions.exp: Madhya Pradesh ~1,600 km (longest), Punjab ~89 km (shortest), Uttar Pradesh ~877 km and Gujarat ~1,022 km. Haryana accounts for about 1,262 km.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Sub-region)   List-II (Physiographic division)
A. Bhorat plateau   1. South-Eastern Plateau
B. Chappan plain   2. Aravalli hilly region
C. Deccan lava plateau  3. Western Sandy Plain
D. Nagauri upland   4. Eastern Plain
questions.exp: The Bhorat plateau belongs to the Aravalli, the Chappan plain to the Mahi basin of the Eastern Plain, the Deccan lava plateau to the Hadoti division, and the Nagauri upland to the semi-arid Bangar of the Western Sandy Plain.

questions.q: Which one of the following peak-district pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Harshnath (about 820 m) is in Sikar district, not Alwar. Alwar's notable heights are Bhairach/Bairath (792 m) and Bilali (775 m).

questions.q: Which one of the following districts does NOT touch the international border with Pakistan?
questions.exp: Jodhpur has no international border. Taking the long-established districts, the border districts are Sri Ganganagar, Bikaner, Jaisalmer and Barmer; the 2023 reorganisation did not change Jodhpur's position on this point.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a part of the South-Eastern (Hadoti) plateau of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The Bhorat plateau lies in the Aravalli hilly region between Gogunda and Kumbhalgarh. The other three are parts of the Hadoti division.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about Rajasthan's location is NOT correct?
opts: It lies wholly to the north of the Equator and east of the Prime Meridian
The Tropic of Cancer passes through Banswara and Dungarpur districts
It shares boundaries with five Indian States and one country
Its easternmost point lies in Bharatpur district
questions.exp: The easternmost point of Rajasthan is Silana village in Dholpur district (78 deg 17' E), not Bharatpur. The other three statements are correct.

questions.q: Which one of the following districts was NOT retained after the December 2024 review of the districts created in 2023?
questions.exp: Anupgarh was one of the nine districts denotified in December 2024. Balotra, Beawar, Deeg, Didwana-Kuchaman, Khairthal-Tijara, Kotputli-Behror, Phalodi and Salumbar were retained.

questions.q:
Arrange the following peaks of Rajasthan in descending order of their height:
I. Jarga
II. Guru Shikhar
III. Kumbhalgarh
IV. Ser
questions.exp: Guru Shikhar 1,722 m > Ser 1,597 m > Jarga 1,431 m > Kumbhalgarh 1,224 m.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The western part of Rajasthan is far drier than the eastern part.
Reason (R): The Aravalli range lies parallel to the path of the south-west monsoon's Arabian Sea branch and fails to obstruct it.
Select the correct answer:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: The Aravalli runs south-west to north-east, roughly parallel to the Arabian Sea branch of the monsoon, so it does not force the moist air to rise; western Rajasthan therefore stays arid while the eastern side gets orographic rain.

chapters.title: Drainage: Rivers and Lakes of Rajasthan
factsheet: Drainage split: about 60% of Rajasthan has internal (inland) drainage; the Bay of Bengal system (Chambal-Banas-Kali Sindh-Parvati) drains the east and the Arabian Sea system (Luni, Mahi, Sabarmati, West Banas) the south and south-west.

Chambal - ancient name Charmanyavati; rises at Janapav hills (Mhow, Indore district, MP); enters Rajasthan at Chaurasigarh (Chittorgarh); joins the Yamuna in Etawah district, UP; the only perennial river of Rajasthan.
Chambal tributaries: Banas, Mej, Kali Sindh, Parvati, Parwan, Kural, Chhoti Kali Sindh, Brahmani, Aalaniya, Chakan, Retam, Shipra, Kunu.
Chambal projects upstream to downstream: Gandhi Sagar (MP) - Rana Pratap Sagar (Rawatbhata, Chittorgarh) - Jawahar Sagar (Kota-Bundi) - Kota Barrage.
Chulia waterfall lies on the Chambal near Bhainsrorgarh (Chittorgarh); the Chambal ravines (beehad) scar Dholpur, Karauli and Sawai Madhopur.
Banas - 'Van ki Asha'; rises in the Khamnor hills of the Aravalli (Rajsamand); 512 km, the longest river flowing entirely within Rajasthan; joins the Chambal at Rameshwar Ghat, Sawai Madhopur.
Banas tributaries: Berach, Kothari, Menali, Khari, Dai, Dheel, Sohadara, Morel, Bandi, Mansi.
Triveni Sangam at Bigod (Bhilwara) = Banas + Berach + Menali. The other Triveni is at Beneshwar (Dungarpur) = Som + Mahi + Jakham.
Bisalpur dam on the Banas at Todaraisingh (Tonk) supplies drinking water to Jaipur, Ajmer and Tonk; Isarda dam is also on the Banas.
Berach rises in the Gogunda hills (Udaipur), ancient name Ayad; Udai Sagar lies on it. Kothari rises at Diver (Rajsamand) and feeds Meja dam (Bhilwara).
Luni - ancient name Lavanavari; rises at Nag Pahar/Naga hills near Ajmer as the Sagarmati, joined by the Saraswati at Govindgarh; about 495 km; ends in the Rann of Kutch.
Luni turns saline downstream of Balotra, hence 'half sweet, half salty'. Jojri is its only left-bank tributary; others (Sukri, Mithri, Bandi, Jawai, Guhiya, Sagi, Khari) join from the right.
Jawai dam at Sumerpur (Pali) is the largest dam of western Rajasthan - the 'lifeline of Marwar'; Sardar Samand lies on the Sukri.
Mahi rises near Amjhera/Mehad in Dhar district, MP; 576 km total, about 171 km in Rajasthan; the only Indian river that crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice; empties into the Gulf of Khambhat.
Mahi tributaries: Som, Jakham, Anas, Eru, Chap, Moran. Mahi Bajaj Sagar dam is at Borkheda (Banswara), a joint Rajasthan-Gujarat project.
Jakham dam (Pratapgarh) is the highest dam of Rajasthan (about 81 m). Som-Kamla-Amba dam is in Dungarpur.
Sabarmati rises in the Padrada hills (Udaipur) and flows only about 45 km in Rajasthan; West Banas rises near Sirohi and ends in the Little Rann of Kutch.

Ghaggar - the 'mrit nadi' (dead river), identified with the Vedic Saraswati; rises in the Kalka/Shivalik hills (Himachal Pradesh); enters Rajasthan at Talwara jheel (Hanumangarh); locally called 'Nali'; Kalibangan stands on its bank.
Kantli rises in the Khandela hills (Sikar), flows through Sikar and Jhunjhunu and vanishes in the sands; Ganeshwar lies on it.
Kakni (Masurdi) of Jaisalmer is the shortest river of Rajasthan (about 17 km) and ends in the Bhuj jheel; Ruparel rises in the Udainath hills (Alwar) and dies out in Bharatpur.
Banganga ('Arjun ki Ganga') rises in the Bairath hills and disappears in the Bharatpur plains; Sabi/Sahibi rises in the Sewar hills (Jaipur) and flows to the Najafgarh jheel.
Sambhar-feeding rivers: Mentha, Rupangarh, Khari and Khandela. Kali Sindh joins the Chambal at Nonera (Kota); Parvati and Parwan enter from Madhya Pradesh.

Sambhar - India's largest inland saline lake, spread over the Jaipur-Ajmer-Nagaur tract; Ramsar site since 23 March 1990; about 190 sq km; run by Sambhar Salts Ltd; flamingo habitat; Shakambhari Devi temple.

Other saline lakes: Pachpadra (Balotra - best-quality salt, about 98% NaCl, 'mora' method), Didwana (sodium sulphate), Lunkaransar (Bikaner), Kuchaman, Phulera, Talchhapar (Churu), Rewasa (Sikar), Kawad (Jodhpur).
Jaisamand (Dhebar) on the Gomti river - built by Maharana Jai Singh (1685-91), traditionally called the largest artificial freshwater lake in Asia; has seven islands.
Rajsamand lake built by Maharana Raj Singh I (1662) on the Gomti; the Nauchowki embankment carries the Raj Prashasti, the largest inscription in India (25 slabs), composed by Ranchhod Bhatt.

Udaipur lakes: Pichola (dug in Rana Lakha's reign by a Banjara; Jag Mandir and Jag Niwas), Fateh Sagar (Maharana Fateh Singh; hosts the Udaipur Solar Observatory), Udai Sagar (Maharana Udai Singh, on the Berach), Swaroop Sagar, Badi (Jiyan Sagar).
Ajmer lakes: Ana Sagar (built by Arnoraj Chauhan; Jahangir's Daulat Bagh, Shah Jahan's baradari), Foy Sagar (1892 famine-relief work by engineer Foy), Pushkar (natural, 52 ghats, Brahma temple).

Nakki lake (Mount Abu, Sirohi) is the highest lake of Rajasthan and the only one that freezes; Jodhpur has Balsamand (1159) and Kaylana (Pratap Singh, 1872); Siliserh is in Alwar; Gadsisar in Jaisalmer; Kolayat and Gajner in Bikaner.
Ramgarh lake in Baran district occupies a meteorite impact crater and is a notified geo-heritage site.
Rajasthan has five Ramsar sites: Keoladeo Ghana (1981), Sambhar (1990), Menar (2025), Khichan (2025) and Siliserh Lake, Alwar (2025).
Waterfalls: Chulia (Chambal, Chittorgarh), Menal (Chittorgarh), Bhimlat (Bundi), Damoh (Dholpur), Apsara falls near Mount Abu.

questions.q: The Chambal river originates from:
opts: Janapav hills near Mhow, Madhya Pradesh
questions.exp: The Chambal rises in the Janapav hills of the Vindhyan range near Mhow in Indore district of Madhya Pradesh. Its ancient name is Charmanyavati.

questions.q: The ancient name of the Chambal river was:
questions.exp: The Chambal is the Charmanyavati of the Mahabharata. Varnasa is the old name of the Banas and Lavanavari of the Luni.

questions.q: The Chambal river enters Rajasthan at:
questions.exp: The Chambal enters Rajasthan at Chaurasigarh in Chittorgarh district. Bhainsrorgarh, further downstream, is famous for the Chulia waterfall.

questions.q: Which is the only perennial river of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The Chambal, fed by the heavier rainfall of the Malwa plateau and regulated by the Gandhi Sagar and Rana Pratap Sagar dams, is the only river in Rajasthan that flows through the year.

questions.q: The Chulia waterfall is situated on which river?
questions.exp: The Chulia falls lie on the Chambal near Bhainsrorgarh in Chittorgarh district. The Menal falls are on the Menali and the Bhimlat falls are in Bundi.

questions.q: The Rana Pratap Sagar dam on the Chambal river is located at:
questions.exp: Rana Pratap Sagar dam stands at Rawatbhata in Chittorgarh district, downstream of Gandhi Sagar. Rawatbhata also houses the Rajasthan Atomic Power Station.

questions.q: The Chambal river finally joins which river?
questions.exp: The Chambal merges with the Yamuna in Etawah district of Uttar Pradesh, at the Pachnada area where five streams meet.

questions.q: The Kali Sindh river joins the Chambal at:
questions.exp: The Kali Sindh, which enters Rajasthan from Madhya Pradesh through Jhalawar, joins the Chambal at Nonera in Kota district. Its own tributaries include the Ahu, Parwan and Chhoti Kali Sindh.

questions.q: Which is the longest river flowing entirely within Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The Banas, about 512 km long, rises and ends within Rajasthan and is therefore the longest river wholly inside the state. The Luni leaves Rajasthan for the Rann of Kutch.

questions.q: The Banas river originates from:
questions.exp: The Banas rises in the Khamnor hills of the Aravalli near Kumbhalgarh in Rajsamand district, on the Bhorat plateau. It is called 'Van ki Asha' - the hope of the forest.

questions.q: The Triveni Sangam at Bigod in Bhilwara district is formed by the confluence of which rivers?
questions.exp: At Bigod the Banas is joined by the Berach and the Menali. Rajasthan's other well-known Triveni is at Beneshwar in Dungarpur, where the Som, Mahi and Jakham meet.

questions.q: The Banas river merges with the Chambal at:
questions.exp: The Banas joins the Chambal at Rameshwar Ghat in Sawai Madhopur, where the Chambal, Banas and Seep meet - itself regarded as a Triveni.

questions.q: The Bisalpur dam, which supplies drinking water to Jaipur and Ajmer, is built on which river?
questions.exp: The Bisalpur dam stands on the Banas at Todaraisingh in Tonk district. The Meja dam on the Kothari serves Bhilwara.

questions.q: The Berach river, a tributary of the Banas, originates from:
questions.exp: The Berach rises in the Gogunda hills of Udaipur; in its upper course it is called the Ayad. Udai Sagar lake is built on it.

questions.q: The Meja dam of Bhilwara district is constructed on which river?
questions.exp: The Meja dam on the Kothari river is the main source of drinking water for Bhilwara city. The Kothari rises at Diver in Rajsamand and joins the Banas.

questions.q: The Luni river originates from:
questions.exp: The Luni rises on the western slope of the Naga hills (Nag Pahar) near Ajmer, where it is called the Sagarmati; after being joined by the Saraswati at Govindgarh it takes the name Luni.

questions.q: The Luni river becomes saline downstream of which town?
questions.exp: Up to Balotra the Luni carries sweet water; beyond it the gypsum-rich soils make it saline, which is why it is called 'half sweet, half salty'. Its old name Lavanavari also means salt-laden.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the only left-bank tributary of the Luni river?
questions.exp: The Jojri, rising in Nagaur, is the Luni's only left-bank tributary; all its other feeders - Sukri, Mithri, Bandi, Jawai, Guhiya, Sagi - come from the Aravalli on the right bank.

questions.q: The Jawai dam, called the lifeline of Marwar, is situated in which district?
questions.exp: The Jawai dam was built at Sumerpur in Pali district on the Jawai, a tributary of the Luni. It is the largest dam of western Rajasthan.

questions.q: The Luni river finally drains into:
questions.exp: After about 495 km the Luni empties into the Rann of Kutch in Gujarat. The Mahi and Sabarmati, by contrast, reach the Gulf of Khambhat.

questions.q: Which river is the only one in India that crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice?
questions.exp: The Mahi, which rises in Dhar district of Madhya Pradesh and loops through Banswara and Dungarpur before turning south into Gujarat, cuts the Tropic of Cancer twice.

questions.q: The Beneshwar Triveni in Dungarpur district is formed by the confluence of:
questions.exp: At Beneshwar the Som and the Jakham join the Mahi; the site hosts the Beneshwar fair, often called the 'kumbh of the tribals'.

questions.q: The highest dam of Rajasthan is built on which river?
questions.exp: The Jakham dam in Pratapgarh district, about 81 m high, is Rajasthan's highest dam. The Jakham is a tributary of the Mahi.

questions.q: The Ghaggar river enters Rajasthan in which district?
questions.exp: The Ghaggar enters Rajasthan at Talwara jheel in Hanumangarh district. It is called the 'mrit nadi' or dead river and is identified by many scholars with the Vedic Saraswati.

questions.q: The Kantli river of Rajasthan originates from:
questions.exp: The Kantli rises in the Khandela hills of Sikar, flows through Sikar and Jhunjhunu and vanishes in the sands - a classic inland drainage river. The Ganeshwar site lies on its bank.

questions.q: The shortest river of Rajasthan, the Kakni (Masurdi), flows in which district?
questions.exp: The Kakni rises at Kotri village in Jaisalmer, runs only about 17 km and spreads out into the Bhuj jheel - the shortest river of the state.

questions.q: Which river of Rajasthan flows towards Haryana and ends in the Najafgarh jheel?
questions.exp: The Sabi or Sahibi rises in the Sewar hills near Jaipur and flows north-east to the Najafgarh jheel in the Delhi-Haryana region. The Ruparel and Banganga die out inside Rajasthan.

questions.q: Jaisamand lake, traditionally described as the largest artificial freshwater lake of Asia, was built on which river?
questions.exp: Jaisamand or Dhebar lake was created by Maharana Jai Singh (1685-91) by damming the Gomti river. It has seven islands, the largest being Baba ka Bhagra. It lies in the erstwhile Udaipur district, now Salumbar.

questions.q: The Raj Prashasti, the largest inscription in India, is engraved on the Nauchowki embankment of which lake?
questions.exp: The Rajsamand lake, built by Maharana Raj Singh I in 1662, carries the Raj Prashasti on 25 marble slabs, composed by Ranchhod Bhatt Tailang.

questions.q: Nakki lake, the highest lake of Rajasthan, is located in which district?
questions.exp: Nakki lake lies at Mount Abu in Sirohi district at about 1,200 m - the highest lake in Rajasthan and the only one that freezes in winter.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Banas river:
I. It rises in the Khamnor hills of the Aravalli.
II. The Berach and the Kothari are among its tributaries.
III. It is a right-bank tributary of the Chambal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Banas joins the Chambal from the right at Rameshwar Ghat in Sawai Madhopur after a course of about 512 km, the longest run of any river confined to Rajasthan.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Chambal river:
I. It is a tributary of the Yamuna.
II. Gandhi Sagar, Rana Pratap Sagar and Jawahar Sagar dams are built on it.
III. It forms a long stretch of the boundary between Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Gandhi Sagar lies in Madhya Pradesh while Rana Pratap Sagar (Rawatbhata) and Jawahar Sagar (Kota-Bundi) are in Rajasthan, with the Kota Barrage last in the chain.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Luni river:
I. It is formed by the union of the Sagarmati and the Saraswati near Govindgarh in Ajmer.
II. It ends in the Gulf of Khambhat.
III. Its water is sweet in the upper course and saline in the lower course.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and III are correct. The Luni drains into the Rann of Kutch, not the Gulf of Khambhat, so II is wrong; the Mahi and Sabarmati reach the Gulf of Khambhat.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Mahi river:
I. It originates in Madhya Pradesh.
II. It crosses the Tropic of Cancer twice.
III. The Mahi Bajaj Sagar project is a joint venture of Rajasthan and Gujarat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Mahi rises near Amjhera in Dhar district (MP), enters Rajasthan through Banswara, and the Mahi Bajaj Sagar dam at Borkheda is shared with Gujarat.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Ghaggar river:
I. It rises in the Shivalik hills of Himachal Pradesh.
II. It is known as the 'mrit nadi' or dead river in Rajasthan.
III. The Harappan site of Kalibangan lies on its bank.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Ghaggar enters Rajasthan at Talwara jheel in Hanumangarh, is locally called 'Nali', and its dry bed carries Kalibangan.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Sambhar lake:
I. It is the largest inland saline lake of India.
II. It was designated a Ramsar site in 1990.
III. The Mentha and Rupangarh are among the rivers that feed it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Sambhar became a Ramsar site on 23 March 1990 and is fed by the Mentha, Rupangarh, Khari and Khandela; it is a major flamingo wintering ground.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Jaisamand lake:
I. It was built by Maharana Jai Singh in the late seventeenth century.
II. It is fed chiefly by the Gomti river.
III. It contains seven islands inhabited by the Bhil and Mina communities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Jaisamand, also called Dhebar lake, was completed between 1685 and 1691 and is traditionally described as Asia's largest artificial freshwater lake.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the inland drainage of Rajasthan:
I. Roughly 60 per cent of the area of Rajasthan has internal drainage.
II. The Kantli and the Kakni are rivers of internal drainage.
III. The Kantli finally empties into the Sambhar lake.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. The Kantli disappears in the sands of the Shekhawati region; it is the Mentha, Rupangarh, Khari and Khandela that drain into Sambhar, so III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the saline lakes of Rajasthan:
I. Pachpadra produces salt of the highest sodium chloride content.
II. Didwana lake is a source of sodium sulphate.
III. Lunkaransar lake lies in Churu district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. Lunkaransar lies in Bikaner district, not Churu; Talchhapar in Churu is the salt-affected flat famous for blackbuck.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Ramsar sites of Rajasthan:
I. Keoladeo Ghana was the first wetland of Rajasthan to be listed.
II. Menar and Khichan were added to the Ramsar list in 2025.
III. Rajasthan now has five Ramsar sites.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Keoladeo was listed in 1981 and Sambhar in 1990; Menar (Udaipur) and Khichan (Phalodi) were added in 2025, and Siliserh Lake (Alwar) later the same year, taking Rajasthan's total to five. Position as of September 2026.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (River)   List-II (Place of origin)
A. Luni    1. Khamnor hills
B. Banas    2. Janapav hills
C. Chambal    3. Naga hills
D. Sabarmati   4. Padrada hills
questions.exp: The Luni rises in the Naga hills (Ajmer), the Banas in the Khamnor hills (Rajsamand), the Chambal in the Janapav hills (MP) and the Sabarmati in the Padrada hills (Udaipur).

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Tributary)   List-II (Main river)
A. Jojri    1. Banas
B. Kothari    2. Mahi
C. Jakham    3. Luni
D. Parwan    4. Chambal system
questions.exp: Jojri is a tributary of the Luni, Kothari of the Banas, Jakham of the Mahi, and Parwan joins the Kali Sindh in the Chambal system.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Lake)   List-II (District)
A. Siliserh    1. Bikaner
B. Kaylana    2. Alwar
C. Kolayat    3. Baran
D. Ramgarh crater lake  4. Jodhpur
questions.exp: Siliserh is in Alwar, Kaylana in Jodhpur, Kolayat in Bikaner and the meteorite-crater lake of Ramgarh in Baran district.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Lake)   List-II (Builder)
A. Ana Sagar   1. Maharana Raj Singh I
B. Rajsamand   2. Arnoraj Chauhan
C. Udai Sagar   3. Maharana Fateh Singh
D. Fateh Sagar   4. Maharana Udai Singh
questions.exp: Ana Sagar (Ajmer) was built by Arnoraj Chauhan, Rajsamand by Maharana Raj Singh I, Udai Sagar by Maharana Udai Singh and Fateh Sagar by Maharana Fateh Singh.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Dam/Project)  List-II (River)
A. Meja    1. Jawai
B. Sumerpur dam   2. Kothari
C. Panchana    3. Gambhir
D. Som-Kamla-Amba   4. Som
questions.exp: Meja dam is on the Kothari (Bhilwara), the Jawai dam at Sumerpur is on the Jawai (Pali), Panchana in Karauli is on the Gambhir and the Som-Kamla-Amba project in Dungarpur is on the Som.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Saline lake)  List-II (District)
A. Pachpadra   1. Bikaner
B. Lunkaransar   2. Balotra
C. Talchhapar   3. Didwana-Kuchaman
D. Didwana    4. Churu
questions.exp: Pachpadra lies in Balotra (carved out of Barmer), Lunkaransar in Bikaner, Talchhapar in Churu and Didwana in Didwana-Kuchaman (carved out of Nagaur). The post-2023 district names are used here.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Waterfall)  List-II (District)
A. Chulia    1. Bundi
B. Bhimlat    2. Dholpur
C. Damoh    3. Chittorgarh
D. Menal    4. Chittorgarh-Bhilwara border area
questions.exp: Chulia falls are on the Chambal in Chittorgarh, Bhimlat in Bundi, Damoh in Dholpur and Menal on the Menali near the Chittorgarh-Bhilwara border.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a tributary of the Chambal river?
questions.exp: The Jojri is a tributary of the Luni, not of the Chambal. Mej, Parvati, Kali Sindh, Banas, Kural and Parwan all belong to the Chambal system.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a tributary of the Luni river?
questions.exp: The Menali joins the Banas at the Bigod Triveni Sangam in Bhilwara. Sukri, Bandi and Jawai are Luni tributaries.

questions.q: Which one of the following river-outfall pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The Sabi (Sahibi) flows north-east into the Najafgarh jheel. Sambhar is fed by the Mentha, Rupangarh, Khari and Khandela.

questions.q: Which one of the following lake-district pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Gadsisar (Gadisar) lake is in Jaisalmer, not Barmer. Foy Sagar and Pushkar are in Ajmer and Balsamand in Jodhpur.

questions.q: Which one of the following rivers does NOT belong to the inland drainage system of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The Berach is a tributary of the Banas and so belongs to the Bay of Bengal system through the Chambal and Yamuna. Kantli, Kakni and Ruparel all dissipate inland.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a Ramsar site of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Talchhapar in Churu is a wildlife sanctuary famous for blackbuck but is not a Ramsar site. Rajasthan's five Ramsar sites are Keoladeo Ghana National Park (Bharatpur, 1981), Sambhar Lake (1990), Menar (Udaipur, 2025), Khichan (Phalodi, 2025) and Siliserh Lake (Alwar, 2025).

questions.q:
Arrange the following dams on the Chambal river from upstream to downstream:
I. Jawahar Sagar
II. Gandhi Sagar
III. Kota Barrage
IV. Rana Pratap Sagar
questions.exp: Gandhi Sagar (MP) comes first, then Rana Pratap Sagar at Rawatbhata, then Jawahar Sagar, and the Kota Barrage last.

questions.q:
Arrange the following rivers in descending order of their total length:
I. Banas
II. Mahi
III. Sabarmati
IV. Luni
questions.exp: Mahi about 576 km, Banas 512 km, Luni about 495 km and Sabarmati about 416 km. The Banas is the longest river confined entirely to Rajasthan.

chapters.title: Climate of Rajasthan
factsheet: Rajasthan's climate is broadly arid to semi-arid; average annual rainfall about 58 cm against India's average of about 125 cm.
About 90 per cent of Rajasthan's rain falls in the south-west monsoon season (late June to mid-September); roughly 10 per cent comes from winter western disturbances.
The 50 cm isohyet runs broadly along the Aravalli axis and is the classic divide between the arid western desert and the semi-humid eastern plain.
Koppen Aw (tropical humid, savanna type) - Vagad region: Banswara, Dungarpur, Pratapgarh and adjoining south-east.
Koppen BWhw (hot desert, dry winter) - Jaisalmer, Bikaner, Churu, Sri Ganganagar, Hanumangarh, western Barmer and western Jodhpur.
Koppen BShw (semi-arid steppe) - Luni basin, Nagaur, Shekhawati (Sikar-Jhunjhunu), Ghaggar plain, Jalore, Pali.
Koppen Cwg (sub-humid, dry-winter monsoon type) - Jaipur, Alwar, Bharatpur, Ajmer, Bhilwara, Bundi, Chittorgarh, Udaipur, Kota.
Highest rainfall place in Rajasthan - Mount Abu (Sirohi); highest-rainfall district - Jhalawar.
Lowest rainfall - the Sam / Jaisalmer belt of the extreme west, roughly 10-20 cm a year.
Phalodi recorded 51.0 degrees C on 19 May 2016 - the highest air temperature ever recorded in India.
Churu is the classic extreme-continental station of Rajasthan, with among the highest annual temperature ranges in India.
Mount Abu is normally the coldest place of Rajasthan; Fatehpur (Sikar) and Churu frequently record sub-zero winter minima.
Loo - hot, dry, dust-laden westerly wind of May-June in western Rajasthan; Andhi - pre-monsoon dust storm.
Bhabulya - local dust whirlwind of the Bikaner-western Rajasthan tract; Mavath - winter rain from western disturbances, vital for rabi crops.
Western disturbances originate over the Mediterranean Sea and travel eastwards, entering India through the north-west.
The south-west monsoon normally enters Rajasthan in the last week of June through Banswara-Dungarpur and withdraws by about the end of September.
The Arabian Sea branch supplies most of western and southern Rajasthan's rain; the Bay of Bengal branch, weakened after crossing the Gangetic plain, reaches eastern Rajasthan.
The Aravalli range lies roughly parallel to the south-west monsoon current and therefore fails to obstruct it - a principal cause of western Rajasthan's aridity.
Rainfall regions of Rajasthan: arid (below 20 cm), semi-arid (20-40 cm), sub-humid (40-60 cm), humid (60-80 cm), very humid (80-150 cm).
Rainfall falls off sharply from the south-east to the north-west; rainfall variability exceeds 60 per cent in the west and is lowest in the south-east.
The Thar (Great Indian Desert) is India's largest desert; the arid western tract covers about 61 per cent of Rajasthan's area.
Chhappaniya Akal - the great famine of Vikram Samvat 1956 (1899-1900 CE), the most severe famine in Rajasthan's recorded history.
State Action Plans on Climate Change, including Rajasthan's (first prepared in 2010), sit under the National Action Plan on Climate Change, 2008.
The Tropic of Cancer passes through the extreme southern edge of Banswara district; almost the whole state lies in the sub-tropical belt.
Rajasthan has among India's highest diurnal and annual temperature ranges because of continentality, bare sandy surface and clear skies.
Only about 10 per cent of Rajasthan's area receives more than 80 cm of rain, and it lies almost entirely in the south and south-east.

questions.q: The highest air temperature ever recorded in India, 51.0 degrees Celsius on 19 May 2016, was registered at which place in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Phalodi (then part of Jodhpur district) touched 51.0 degrees C on 19 May 2016, the highest air temperature ever recorded in India. Churu, the usual runner-up, has touched 50.8 degrees C.

questions.q: Which Koppen climatic type is found in Jaisalmer, Bikaner and Churu districts?
questions.exp: BWhw denotes a hot desert climate with a dry winter, covering the extreme western districts. The 'w' suffix marks the dry winter and 'h' the hot type.

questions.q: The Vagad region comprising Banswara and Dungarpur falls under which Koppen climatic type?
questions.exp: Aw is the tropical humid savanna type with a dry winter, found in the wettest south of Rajasthan. It supports the state's highest rainfall after the Mount Abu tract.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Koppen type)   List-II (Region of Rajasthan)
A. Aw     1. Jaisalmer and Bikaner
B. BWhw   2. Shekhawati and Nagaur
C. BShw   3. Banswara and Dungarpur
D. Cwg    4. Jaipur and Alwar
questions.exp: Aw covers the humid Vagad south, BWhw the true desert, BShw the semi-arid steppe of Shekhawati and the Luni basin, and Cwg the sub-humid eastern plain.

questions.q: The 50 cm isohyet is important in the geography of Rajasthan chiefly because it broadly separates:
opts: The Banas basin from the Luni basin
The Chambal catchment from the internal drainage area
The Hadoti plateau from the Mewar plain
The arid western desert from the semi-humid eastern plain
questions.exp: The 50 cm annual rainfall line runs roughly along the Aravalli axis and is the conventional boundary between western arid Rajasthan and the eastern semi-humid plains.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about rainfall in Rajasthan:
I. Annual rainfall generally decreases from the south-east towards the north-west.
II. The 50 cm isohyet broadly coincides with the alignment of the Aravalli range.
III. The variability of annual rainfall is lowest in the western desert districts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Rainfall does fall off from the south-east to the north-west, and the 50 cm isohyet roughly follows the Aravalli axis. Variability is highest, not lowest, in the western desert, where it exceeds 60 per cent.

questions.q: Which district of Rajasthan receives the highest average annual rainfall?
questions.exp: Jhalawar in the Hadoti plateau records the highest district-level annual rainfall in Rajasthan. The single wettest station, however, is Mount Abu in Sirohi district.

questions.q: Which district of Rajasthan records the lowest average annual rainfall?
questions.exp: Jaisalmer, in the extreme west of the Thar, receives the least rain in Rajasthan, of the order of 10-20 cm a year. The Sam tract of the district is the driest point.

questions.q: The average annual rainfall of Rajasthan is approximately:
questions.exp: Rajasthan averages about 58 cm a year, well under half the national average of roughly 125 cm. Almost 90 per cent of it falls during the south-west monsoon.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs relating to the local winds and weather phenomena of Rajasthan is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Loo - hot dry summer wind of western Rajasthan
Mavath - rain from the retreating south-west monsoon
Bhabulya - dust whirlwind of the Bikaner region
questions.exp: Mavath is winter rainfall caused by western disturbances, not by the retreating monsoon, and is critical for the rabi crop.

questions.q: The hot, dry and dust-laden wind that blows over western Rajasthan during May and June is called:
questions.exp: The Loo is a scorching westerly of the pre-monsoon months and is a major cause of heat-stroke deaths in Barmer, Jaisalmer and Bikaner.

questions.q: In Rajasthan, winter rainfall caused by western disturbances is locally known as:
questions.exp: Mavath is the light winter rain of December-February brought by western disturbances. It is highly beneficial for wheat, mustard and gram.

questions.q: The local dust whirlwind of the Bikaner and adjoining western Rajasthan region is known as:
questions.exp: Bhabulya is a small, short-lived dust whirlwind of the arid western tract. Larger, more damaging dust storms of the pre-monsoon period are called Andhi.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the south-west monsoon in Rajasthan:
I. It normally enters the state in the last week of June through Banswara and Dungarpur.
II. It normally withdraws from the state by about the end of September.
III. The Bay of Bengal branch is the main rain-bearing current for western Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The monsoon enters through the humid south-east around the last week of June and withdraws by late September. Western Rajasthan draws mainly on the Arabian Sea branch, not the Bay of Bengal branch.

questions.q: Which is the single wettest station of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Mount Abu in Sirohi district, at over 1,200 m on the Aravalli crest, receives the state's heaviest rainfall through orographic lifting.

questions.q: The 'Chhappaniya Akal', the most severe famine in Rajasthan's recorded history, occurred in which year of the Vikram Samvat era?
questions.exp: The Chhappaniya Akal of Vikram Samvat 1956 corresponds to 1899-1900 CE. The earlier Trikal famine of VS 1868 is another landmark in the state's famine history.

questions.q:
Arrange the following districts of Rajasthan in DESCENDING order of average annual rainfall:
I. Jaisalmer
II. Jhalawar
III. Jaipur
IV. Banswara
questions.exp: Jhalawar and Banswara lie in the very humid south-east and south, Jaipur in the sub-humid eastern plain, and Jaisalmer in the arid extreme west.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Rainfall region)   List-II (Annual rainfall)
A. Arid          1. Below 20 cm
B. Semi-arid     2. 20-40 cm
C. Sub-humid     3. 40-60 cm
D. Very humid    4. Above 80 cm
questions.exp: Rajasthan is conventionally divided into five rainfall regions - arid, semi-arid, sub-humid, humid (60-80 cm) and very humid (above 80 cm).

questions.q: Approximately what proportion of Rajasthan's annual rainfall is received during the south-west monsoon season?
questions.exp: Roughly 90 per cent of the state's rain falls between late June and September. The remaining tenth comes mainly from winter western disturbances.

questions.q: Which one of the following Koppen climatic types is NOT found in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Am, the tropical monsoon type with a short dry season, does not occur in Rajasthan. The state has Aw, BWhw, BShw and Cwg types.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the influence of the Aravalli range on Rajasthan's climate:
I. The range runs roughly parallel to the direction of the south-west monsoon current.
II. Because of this alignment it fails to force the monsoon winds to rise significantly.
III. The area to the west of the range receives more rain than the area to its east.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The south-west to north-east alignment of the Aravallis keeps them parallel to the monsoon current, so little orographic lifting occurs. The eastern side, not the western, is the wetter flank.

questions.q: The Bay of Bengal branch of the south-west monsoon principally brings rainfall to which part of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The Bay of Bengal branch reaches eastern Rajasthan after crossing the Gangetic plain and is much weakened. Western and southern Rajasthan depend mainly on the Arabian Sea branch.

questions.q: Which of the following is normally the coldest place in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Mount Abu, the state's only hill station, is normally the coldest place. On the plains, Fatehpur in Sikar and Churu regularly record sub-zero minima during cold waves.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about climatic hazards in Rajasthan:
I. Heat waves are most frequent in the western districts during May and June.
II. Cold waves are caused by the incursion of cold northerly winds in winter.
III. Hailstorms in Rajasthan occur mainly during the south-west monsoon season.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Hailstorms in Rajasthan are associated with western disturbances in the winter and pre-monsoon months and are a major threat to the rabi crop, not with the south-west monsoon.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Western Rajasthan remains arid despite lying in the path of the south-west monsoon.
Reason (R): The Aravalli range is aligned roughly parallel to the monsoon current and does not obstruct it.
Select the correct answer:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: The south-west to north-east alignment of the Aravallis means the monsoon winds move along the range rather than across it, so they are not forced to rise and condense over western Rajasthan.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (District)   List-II (Climatic character)
A. Jaisalmer     1. Very humid
B. Nagaur        2. Semi-arid steppe
C. Jaipur        3. Arid, below 20 cm rainfall
D. Jhalawar      4. Sub-humid
questions.exp: Rainfall rises steadily from Jaisalmer in the arid west through Nagaur and Jaipur to Jhalawar in the very humid south-east.

questions.q: The arid western tract, that is, the Thar or Great Indian Desert region, covers approximately what share of Rajasthan's geographical area?
questions.exp: About 61 per cent of Rajasthan's area lies in the arid western tract, which is India's largest desert. It nonetheless supports a relatively dense population for a desert.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the seasons of Rajasthan:
I. The summer season extends from about March to mid-June.
II. The rainy season is associated with the advancing south-west monsoon from late June.
III. Winter rainfall in the state is associated with western disturbances.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Rajasthan's conventional seasons are summer (March to mid-June), the rainy season (late June to September), and winter (November to February), with a short transitional autumn.

questions.q: The Tropic of Cancer passes through the extreme southern part of which district of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The Tropic of Cancer clips the southern edge of Banswara district, so almost the whole of Rajasthan lies in the sub-tropical belt.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about Rajasthan's rainfall is NOT correct?
opts: Rainfall increases steadily from the south-east to the north-west
Almost 90 per cent of the rainfall occurs during the south-west monsoon
The 50 cm isohyet broadly divides the state into two rainfall halves
The rainfall of the state is highly variable from year to year
questions.exp: Rainfall decreases, not increases, from the south-east towards the north-west, falling from over 90 cm in Jhalawar to under 20 cm in Jaisalmer.

questions.q: The driest tract of Rajasthan, recording rainfall of the order of only 10-20 cm a year, lies around which place?
questions.exp: The Sam tract of Jaisalmer district, on the Indo-Pakistan frontier, is the driest part of Rajasthan and of India's mainland desert.

questions.q: In Rajasthan, the violent dust storms of the pre-monsoon months of May and June are locally called:
questions.exp: Andhi are dust storms raised by intense surface heating before the monsoon breaks. They reduce visibility sharply and often precede the first monsoon showers.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about western disturbances affecting Rajasthan:
I. They are extra-tropical systems that originate over the Mediterranean region.
II. They enter India from the north-west during the winter months.
III. They account for roughly half of Rajasthan's annual rainfall.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Western disturbances form over the Mediterranean and enter India from the north-west in winter, but they give only about a tenth of Rajasthan's annual rainfall.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about drought in Rajasthan:
I. Drought frequency is highest in the western desert districts.
II. High inter-annual rainfall variability is a principal cause of recurrent drought.
III. Jhalawar and Banswara are the most drought-prone districts of the state.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Jaisalmer, Barmer and Bikaner, not the humid south-eastern districts of Jhalawar and Banswara, are the most drought-prone parts of Rajasthan.

questions.q: Which station of Rajasthan is best known for an extreme continental climate, being among the hottest in summer and among the coldest in winter?
questions.exp: Churu, on the fringe of the Thar, has one of India's largest annual temperature ranges, crossing 50 degrees C in summer and falling below freezing in winter.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Bikaner falls in the hot desert BWhw type, not the semi-arid steppe BShw type. BShw covers Nagaur, Shekhawati, the Luni basin and the Ghaggar plain.

questions.q: The number of rainfall-based climatic regions into which Rajasthan is conventionally divided is:
questions.exp: Rajasthan is divided into five rainfall regions: arid, semi-arid, sub-humid, humid and very humid, running from the north-west to the south-east.

questions.q: Sub-zero winter minimum temperatures on the plains of Rajasthan are most frequently recorded at:
questions.exp: Fatehpur in Sikar district is the plains station that most often drops below freezing during cold waves, along with Churu. Mount Abu is colder but is a hill station.

questions.q: The State Action Plan on Climate Change of Rajasthan has been framed under the umbrella of:
opts: The National Action Plan on Climate Change, 2008
questions.exp: All states prepare State Action Plans on Climate Change consistent with the National Action Plan on Climate Change of 2008 and its national missions. Rajasthan's plan was first prepared in 2010.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about temperature conditions in Rajasthan:
I. The state records among the highest diurnal and annual temperature ranges in India.
II. Its distance from the sea and its bare sandy surface are the principal causes.
III. Clear skies and low humidity allow rapid heating by day and rapid cooling by night.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Continentality, a bare sandy surface and cloudless skies together give Rajasthan one of India's most extreme temperature regimes.

chapters.title: Natural Vegetation and Forests of Rajasthan
factsheet: As per the India State of Forest Report (ISFR) 2023, Rajasthan's forest cover is 16,548.21 sq km, which is 4.84 per cent of its geographical area.
ISFR 2023: Rajasthan's forest plus tree cover is 27,389.33 sq km, or 8.00 per cent of the state's geographical area.
ISFR 2023 canopy classes for Rajasthan - Very Dense Forest 223.20 sq km, Moderately Dense Forest 4,237.41 sq km, Open Forest 12,087.60 sq km; open forest dominates overwhelmingly.
ISFR 2023: Rajasthan gained about 394 sq km of forest and tree cover over 2021, the fourth-largest increase among Indian states (Chhattisgarh led with 684 sq km).

Recorded forest area of Rajasthan is about 32,700 sq km, roughly 9.6 per cent of the state; Protected Forest is the largest legal class (about 56 per cent), Reserved Forest about 38 per cent and Unclassed Forest about 6 per cent.
The governing state law is the Rajasthan Forest Act, 1953.
By Champion and Seth's classification, Rajasthan's forests belong mainly to Group 5 (Tropical Dry Deciduous, about 57 per cent of forest area) and Group 6 (Tropical Thorn, about 15 per cent).
Northern Dry Mixed Deciduous Forest is the single largest forest type of Rajasthan, covering roughly 40 per cent of its forest area.
Dhok (Anogeissus pendula) is the most widespread tree species of Rajasthan, dominating the Aravalli and eastern hill tracts; it is also the most numerous species by tree count.
Palash or Dhak (Butea monosperma), the 'Flame of the Forest', is the second most numerous tree species of the state.
Teak (Tectona grandis) forests occur in the south - Banswara, Udaipur, Chittorgarh, Pratapgarh, Dungarpur, Baran; the type is classed as Very Dry Teak Forest.
Salar (Boswellia serrata) grows on dry rocky Aravalli slopes and yields Indian frankincense resin; Khair (Acacia catechu) of riverine and ravine tracts yields katha (catechu).
Khejri (Prosopis cineraria) is the state tree - called the Kalp Vriksha of the desert; its pods are 'sangri' and its dried leaves 'loong'; it is also known as Shami or Jandi.
Rohida (Tecomella undulata) is the state flower, called 'Marwar Teak' or 'Desert Teak', prized for its timber in western Rajasthan.
Characteristic desert flora: Kair (Capparis decidua), Aak (Calotropis procera), Phog (Calligonum polygonoides) and Sewan grass (Lasiurus sindicus) of the Jaisalmer plains.
Bamboo (Dendrocalamus strictus, locally 'Bans') of Rajasthan is concentrated in Udaipur, Banswara, Dungarpur, Chittorgarh, Pratapgarh, Kota and Baran.
Sub-tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forest occurs in Rajasthan only in the Mount Abu tract of Sirohi district, the state's wettest hill area.
Salt-tolerant halophytic vegetation occurs around Sambhar, Pachpadra and Didwana salt basins.
As per ISFR 2021, Udaipur has the largest forest cover in Rajasthan (about 2,753 sq km), followed by Alwar, Pratapgarh, Baran and Chittorgarh.
As per ISFR 2021, the highest forest cover as a share of district area is in Udaipur (about 23.5 per cent) and Pratapgarh (about 23.2 per cent), then Sirohi, Karauli and Baran.
Lowest forest cover percentages are recorded in Jodhpur, Churu, Jaisalmer, Bikaner, Hanumangarh and Nagaur.
Khejarli (Jodhpur), 1730: Amrita Devi Bishnoi and 363 Bishnois were killed resisting the felling of Khejri trees by men of Maharaja Abhay Singh of Marwar.
11 September is observed as National Forest Martyrs Day in memory of the Khejarli sacrifice; the Amrita Devi Bishnoi Wildlife Protection Award honours courage in protecting wildlife.
The Bishnoi sect was founded by Guru Jambheshwar (Jambhoji) in 1485 at Samrathal Dhora near Bikaner; its 29 rules forbid felling green trees and killing animals.
Sacred groves of Rajasthan are called Oran, Kankad bani, Deo bani, Rakhat bani and Malvan; in December 2024 the Supreme Court directed that orans be treated as deemed forests.
Joint Forest Management in Rajasthan is implemented through Village Forest Protection and Management Committees; the state has a Forest Policy of 2010 and a Rajasthan Forest Policy 2023.
Rajasthan's forest policy target is to bring about 20 per cent of the geographical area under forest and tree cover.
The Aravalli Green Wall Project, launched in March 2023, aims to green a 5-km buffer along the Aravalli range across Rajasthan, Haryana, Gujarat and Delhi.

Desert afforestation relies on shelterbelt plantation along the Indira Gandhi Nahar, sand-dune stabilisation and species such as Khejri, Rohida, Phog and Sewan; CAZRI and AFRI, both at Jodhpur, are the lead research institutions.

questions.q: Which is the most widespread tree species in the forests of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Dhok (Anogeissus pendula) dominates the Aravalli and eastern hill forests and is the most widespread and most numerous tree species of Rajasthan.

questions.q: The botanical name of Dhok, the commonest tree of Rajasthan's forests, is:
questions.exp: Anogeissus pendula is Dhok. Boswellia serrata is Salar, Butea monosperma is Palash and Tecomella undulata is Rohida.

questions.q: Which tree has been declared the State Tree of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Khejri (Prosopis cineraria) is the state tree, revered as the Kalp Vriksha of the desert for its fodder, fuel, shade and edible pods known as sangri.

questions.q: Which is the State Flower of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Rohida (Tecomella undulata) is the state flower. The tree is known as Marwar Teak or Desert Teak and is valued for its durable timber.

questions.q: The botanical name of the Khejri tree is:
questions.exp: Prosopis cineraria is Khejri. Capparis decidua is Kair and Calligonum polygonoides is Phog, both characteristic desert shrubs.

questions.q: The Khejarli sacrifice of 1730, in which villagers gave up their lives to save trees, was led by:
questions.exp: Amrita Devi Bishnoi led the resistance at Khejarli near Jodhpur; 363 Bishnois died protecting Khejri trees from felling.

questions.q: How many Bishnois are said to have laid down their lives in the Khejarli incident of 1730?
questions.exp: 363 Bishnois, led by Amrita Devi, were killed while protecting Khejri trees at Khejarli in Jodhpur district.

questions.q: The Khejarli massacre of 1730 took place during the reign of which ruler of Marwar?
questions.exp: Trees were being felled at Khejarli to supply lime kilns for the palace of Maharaja Abhay Singh of Jodhpur when Amrita Devi and her companions resisted.

questions.q: National Forest Martyrs Day, commemorating the Khejarli sacrifice, is observed every year on:
questions.exp: 11 September is observed as National Forest Martyrs Day in memory of the 363 Bishnois of Khejarli and all who have died protecting forests.

questions.q: The Bishnoi sect, whose tenets underpin Rajasthan's tradition of tree and wildlife protection, was founded by:
questions.exp: Guru Jambheshwar, or Jambhoji, founded the Bishnoi sect in 1485 at Samrathal Dhora near Bikaner and laid down twenty-nine rules of conduct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Bishnoi tradition of Rajasthan:
I. The sect was founded by Guru Jambheshwar in the fifteenth century.
II. Its code of conduct consists of twenty-nine rules.
III. The rules include prohibitions on felling green trees and on killing animals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The name Bishnoi derives from 'bis' and 'noi', that is twenty-nine rules, laid down by Jambhoji in 1485.

questions.q: As per the India State of Forest Report 2023, the forest cover of Rajasthan as a percentage of its geographical area is approximately:
questions.exp: Rajasthan's forest cover in ISFR 2023 is 16,548.21 sq km, or 4.84 per cent of the state. 21.76 per cent is India's national forest cover in the same report.

questions.q: As per the India State of Forest Report 2023, the combined forest and tree cover of Rajasthan is about what percentage of its geographical area?
questions.exp: Forest cover 16,548.21 sq km plus tree cover gives 27,389.33 sq km, that is 8.00 per cent of Rajasthan's area, in ISFR 2023.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Rajasthan's forest cover as reported in the India State of Forest Report 2023:
I. Open forest accounts for the largest part of the state's forest cover.
II. Very dense forest covers less than 250 sq km in the state.
III. Rajasthan's forest cover exceeds the national average percentage.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Open forest (12,087.60 sq km) dominates and very dense forest is only 223.20 sq km. At 4.84 per cent, Rajasthan is far below the national figure of 21.76 per cent.

questions.q:
Arrange the following districts of Rajasthan in DESCENDING order of forest cover by area as per the India State of Forest Report 2021:
I. Alwar
II. Udaipur
III. Chittorgarh
IV. Pratapgarh
questions.exp: The order is Udaipur (about 2,753 sq km), Alwar (about 1,196), Pratapgarh (about 1,034) and Chittorgarh (about 990); Baran lies between Pratapgarh and Chittorgarh.

questions.q: Which legal class accounts for the largest share of Rajasthan's recorded forest area?
questions.exp: Protected Forest makes up roughly 56 per cent of Rajasthan's recorded forest area, Reserved Forest about 38 per cent and Unclassed Forest about 6 per cent.

questions.q: Forests in Rajasthan are governed principally by:
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Forest Act, 1953 is the principal state legislation for the constitution, protection and management of forests in Rajasthan.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Local name)   List-II (Botanical name)
A. Khejri    1. Butea monosperma
B. Rohida    2. Prosopis cineraria
C. Palash    3. Tecomella undulata
D. Salar     4. Boswellia serrata
questions.exp: Khejri is Prosopis cineraria, Rohida is Tecomella undulata, Palash is Butea monosperma and Salar is Boswellia serrata.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Species)   List-II (Chief area in Rajasthan)
A. Teak        1. Jaisalmer plains
B. Sewan grass 2. Aravalli and eastern hills
C. Dhok        3. Banswara and Udaipur
D. Rohida      4. Western arid districts
questions.exp: Teak is confined to the humid south, Sewan grass to the Jaisalmer plains, Dhok to the Aravalli belt and Rohida to the arid west.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of a tree and its principal product is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Salar - resin used as Indian frankincense
Khejri - sangri pods used as a vegetable
Palash - commercial timber for railway sleepers
questions.exp: Palash (Butea monosperma) is valued for its flowers, gum, leaves used as plates and for lac culture, not for commercial sleeper timber.

questions.q: The forest product 'katha' or catechu is obtained from which tree?
questions.exp: Khair (Acacia catechu) yields katha, used in paan and in tanning. It grows chiefly in riverine and ravine tracts of Rajasthan.

questions.q: Which tree of Rajasthan is popularly known as the 'Flame of the Forest'?
questions.exp: Palash or Dhak (Butea monosperma) is called the Flame of the Forest for its brilliant orange-red spring flowers. It is the second most numerous tree species of Rajasthan.

questions.q: Sewan, the important fodder grass of the Jaisalmer plains, has the botanical name:
questions.exp: Lasiurus sindicus, or Sewan grass, is the finest natural pasture grass of the Thar and sustains the sheep and cattle economy of Jaisalmer.

questions.q: Phog, a characteristic shrub of the sand dunes of western Rajasthan, has the botanical name:
questions.exp: Calligonum polygonoides, or Phog, is a dune-binding shrub of the Thar. Calotropis procera is Aak, Capparis decidua is Kair and Ziziphus nummularia is Jharber.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Khejri tree:
I. Its pods are known as sangri and are eaten as a vegetable.
II. Its dried leaves, used as fodder, are called loong.
III. It is also known as Shami or Jandi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Khejri's multiple uses in the desert economy earned it the name Kalp Vriksha of the desert.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Rohida:
I. It has been declared the state flower of Rajasthan.
II. It is known as Marwar Teak because of its valuable timber.
III. It is chiefly found in the humid south-eastern districts of the state.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Rohida is the state flower and is called Marwar Teak, but it is a tree of the arid and semi-arid west, not of the humid south-east.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a term used in Rajasthan for a sacred grove or community-protected forest?
questions.exp: Khadin is a traditional runoff-farming and water-harvesting structure of Jaisalmer, not a sacred grove. Oran, Kankad bani, Deo bani and Rakhat bani are sacred groves.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the orans of Rajasthan:
I. They are sacred groves protected by local communities in the name of a deity.
II. In December 2024 the Supreme Court directed that they be treated as deemed forests.
III. They are found mainly in western Rajasthan and provide habitat for the Great Indian Bustard.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Supreme Court's 2024 direction extended forest-conservation protection to oran lands.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Aravalli Green Wall Project:
I. It covers the Aravalli range across four states including Rajasthan.
II. Its object is to check land degradation and the eastward spread of the desert.
III. It was launched in 2023.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The project spans Rajasthan, Haryana, Gujarat and Delhi and forms part of India's wider land-restoration commitments.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Joint Forest Management in Rajasthan:
I. It is implemented through village-level forest protection and management committees.
II. It provides for sharing of usufruct benefits with participating villagers.
III. It replaces the Rajasthan Forest Act, 1953 as the legal basis of forest management.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Joint Forest Management is an administrative and participatory arrangement; it does not replace the Rajasthan Forest Act, 1953, which remains the governing statute.

questions.q: The forest policy of Rajasthan sets a target of bringing approximately what share of the state's geographical area under forest and tree cover?
questions.exp: Rajasthan's forest policy, restated in the Rajasthan Forest Policy 2023, targets about 20 per cent green cover, recognising that the national goal of 33 per cent is unattainable in a largely desert state.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the forest types of Rajasthan is NOT correct?
opts: Tropical dry deciduous forests occupy the largest share of the state's forest area
Tropical thorn forests occur in the arid west
Tropical wet evergreen forests occur along the Chambal valley
Northern dry mixed deciduous forest is the single largest forest type
questions.exp: Rajasthan has no tropical wet evergreen forest. Its only evergreen element is the sub-tropical evergreen patch at Mount Abu.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Forest type)   List-II (Characteristic)
A. Tropical dry deciduous   1. Confined to Mount Abu
B. Tropical thorn          2. Dominated by Dhok and teak; largest share of forest area
C. Sub-tropical evergreen  3. Around Sambhar and Pachpadra
D. Salt-tolerant vegetation 4. Desert thorn and dune scrub of the west
questions.exp: Group 5 dry deciduous forest is the largest, Group 6 thorn forest occupies the arid west, evergreen forest is confined to Mount Abu, and halophytes fringe the salt basins.
