questions.q: Under the Champion and Seth classification, the largest share of Rajasthan's forest area belongs to which group?
questions.exp: Group 5, the Tropical Dry Deciduous Forests, account for roughly 57 per cent of Rajasthan's forest area; Group 6 thorn forests account for about 15 per cent.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about tropical thorn forest in Rajasthan:
I. It occurs mainly in the arid western districts.
II. Desert thorn forest and desert dune scrub are among its sub-types.
III. It is dominated by teak and bamboo.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Thorn forest is dominated by Khejri, Kair, Rohida, Phog and Aak. Teak and bamboo belong to the moister dry deciduous forests of southern Rajasthan.

questions.q: The desert shrub Capparis decidua, whose berries are used to make the famous 'ker-sangri' preparation, is locally known as:
questions.exp: Kair (Capparis decidua) provides the ker berries which, with the sangri pods of the Khejri, make Rajasthan's celebrated ker-sangri dish.

questions.q: Which one of the following districts is NOT among those with the highest forest cover percentage in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Churu is among the districts with the lowest forest cover, under one per cent of its area. Udaipur, Pratapgarh, Sirohi, Karauli and Baran head the list.

questions.q: The Amrita Devi Bishnoi Award instituted in her memory is given for outstanding work in the field of:
questions.exp: The Amrita Devi Bishnoi Wildlife Protection Award honours individuals and communities showing exemplary courage in protecting wildlife and forests.

questions.q: Bamboo (Dendrocalamus strictus) in Rajasthan is concentrated chiefly in which districts?
questions.exp: Bamboo, locally called bans, grows in the moister southern districts of Udaipur, Banswara, Dungarpur, Chittorgarh, Pratapgarh, Kota and Baran.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Item)   List-II (Associated with)
A. State tree of Rajasthan       1. Khejri
B. State flower of Rajasthan     2. Rohida
C. Most widespread tree species  3. Dhok
D. Flame of the Forest           4. Palash
questions.exp: Khejri is the state tree, Rohida the state flower, Dhok the most widespread species and Palash the Flame of the Forest.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Khejri tree is NOT correct?
opts: It is the state tree of Rajasthan
It is called the Kalp Vriksha of the desert
Its felling was resisted at Khejarli in 1730
It is an evergreen conifer of the Aravalli highlands
questions.exp: Khejri is a hardy leguminous tree of the arid plains, not a conifer, and it is the mainstay of the desert agro-forestry system.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about desert afforestation in Rajasthan:
I. Shelterbelt plantations are raised along the Indira Gandhi Nahar to check dune movement and canal silting.
II. Sand-dune stabilisation makes use of species such as Phog and Sewan grass.
III. The Desert Development Programme is confined to the eastern plain of the state.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Desert Development Programme operates in the arid western districts, not in the eastern plain. Shelterbelts and dune stabilisation are the mainstays of desert afforestation.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Local name)   List-II (Botanical name)
A. Aak      1. Tectona grandis
B. Bamboo   2. Ziziphus mauritiana
C. Teak     3. Calotropis procera
D. Ber      4. Dendrocalamus strictus
questions.exp: Aak is Calotropis procera, the common desert milkweed; bamboo of Rajasthan is Dendrocalamus strictus; teak is Tectona grandis and ber is Ziziphus mauritiana.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Vegetation)   List-II (Chief area in Rajasthan)
A. Sub-tropical evergreen forest   1. Sambhar and Pachpadra
B. Teak forest                     2. Banswara
C. Sewan grassland                 3. Jaisalmer
D. Salt-tolerant vegetation        4. Mount Abu
questions.exp: Evergreen forest survives only on Mount Abu, teak in the humid south, Sewan grass on the Jaisalmer plains and halophytes around the saline basins.

questions.q: Which two Jodhpur-based institutions are the principal research bodies for arid-zone vegetation and desert afforestation in India?
questions.exp: The Central Arid Zone Research Institute (CAZRI) and the Arid Forest Research Institute (AFRI), both at Jodhpur, lead research on desert vegetation and afforestation.

chapters.title: Soils of Rajasthan
factsheet: Desert or arid sandy soil covers the largest area of Rajasthan - Jaisalmer, Barmer, Bikaner, Jodhpur, Churu, Nagaur; low in humus and nitrogen, calcareous, highly porous.
Brown (non-calcic brown) soil - Luni basin: Pali, Jalore, Sirohi, Ajmer and parts of Sikar and Jhunjhunu; comparatively rich in phosphate.
Red-yellow soil - Sawai Madhopur, Bhilwara, Udaipur, Rajsamand, Ajmer, Tonk; derived from granite and gneiss; deficient in nitrogen and calcium.
Red loamy soil - Banswara, Dungarpur, Pratapgarh, Udaipur and Chittorgarh in the humid south.
Mixed red and black soil - Chittorgarh, Pratapgarh, Bhilwara, Banswara and Jhalawar; potash-sufficient but deficient in nitrogen and phosphorus.
Black or medium-black soil - Hadoti: Kota, Bundi, Baran and Jhalawar; derived from Deccan lava; high clay content, strong moisture retention.
Alluvial soil - eastern plain: Bharatpur, Dholpur, Alwar, Jaipur, Dausa, Tonk, Karauli, Sawai Madhopur and the Ganganagar canal tract; the most fertile group.
Saline-alkaline soil (Reh, Kallar, Usar) - Sri Ganganagar, Hanumangarh, Barmer, Jalore, Pali and the Sambhar-Pachpadra belt; caused by capillary rise of salts and over-irrigation.
Lithosols and regosols are thin skeletal soils of the Aravalli slopes with little profile development.

USDA/ICAR soil orders in Rajasthan: Entisol (largest extent, western Rajasthan), Aridisol (Jaisalmer, Bikaner, Churu, Jhunjhunu), Inceptisol (Udaipur, Rajsamand, Chittorgarh, Banswara, Dungarpur), Vertisol (Kota, Bundi, Baran, Jhalawar), Alfisol (Alwar, Bharatpur, Dholpur, Karauli).

Vertisol is the order of the black cotton soil - self-mulching, swelling clays that crack deeply in summer; Entisol is the youngest order with no horizon development; Aridisol is the true desert order.
Wind erosion and sand-dune movement are the chief soil problems of western Rajasthan; sheet, rill and gully erosion (the Chambal ravines) dominate the east and south-east.
Waterlogging and secondary salinity are the chief soil problems of the Indira Gandhi Nahar command in Sri Ganganagar and Hanumangarh.

Reclamation measures: gypsum application for alkaline soils, sub-surface drainage for waterlogging, shelterbelts and dune stabilisation against wind erosion, contour bunding and check dams against water erosion.
Rajasthan has the largest area under land degradation and desertification of any Indian state, as mapped in ISRO's Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas.
Soil Health Cards, soil testing laboratories (static and mobile) in the districts, and the state Department of Agriculture support soil-fertility management.
Rajasthan is divided into 10 agro-climatic zones, delineated under the National Agricultural Research Project and grouped into five broad regions numbered I to V.
Zone I-A Arid Western Plain - Barmer and part of Jodhpur; about 200-370 mm rainfall; sandy soil.
Zone I-B Irrigated North-Western Plain - Sri Ganganagar and Hanumangarh; the only fully canal-irrigated zone; wheat, cotton, mustard.
Zone I-C Hyper Arid Partial Irrigated Zone - Bikaner, Churu and Jaisalmer; the driest zone of the state.
Zone II-A Transitional Plain of Inland Drainage - Sikar, Jhunjhunu, Nagaur and part of Churu (the Shekhawati tract).
Zone II-B Transitional Plain of Luni Basin - Jalore, Pali and parts of Sirohi and Jodhpur.
Zone III-A Semi-Arid Eastern Plain - Jaipur, Ajmer, Dausa and Tonk.
Zone III-B Flood Prone Eastern Plain - Alwar, Bharatpur, Dholpur, Karauli and Sawai Madhopur.
Zone IV-A Sub-Humid Southern Plain - Udaipur, Chittorgarh, Rajsamand, Bhilwara and part of Pratapgarh.
Zone IV-B Humid Southern Plain - Dungarpur and Banswara; among the highest-rainfall zones.
Zone V Humid South-Eastern Plain (Hadoti) - Kota, Bundi, Baran and Jhalawar; deep black soils and the state's most productive farmland.
Zones I-A, I-B and I-C together make up the arid western plain region; zones IV-A, IV-B and V cover the humid south and south-east.

questions.q: Which soil type covers the largest area of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Desert or arid sandy soil covers the largest part of the state, spreading over Jaisalmer, Barmer, Bikaner, Jodhpur, Churu and Nagaur. It is highly porous and poor in humus and nitrogen.

questions.q: The black soil of Rajasthan, derived from Deccan lava, is chiefly found in which region?
questions.exp: Black or medium-black soil occupies the Hadoti plateau - Kota, Bundi, Baran and Jhalawar. Its high clay content gives it excellent moisture retention.

questions.q: The most fertile soils of Rajasthan, found in the eastern plain districts of Bharatpur, Dholpur and Alwar, are:
questions.exp: The eastern plain carries alluvial soils deposited by the Banganga, Gambhir, Chambal and Banas systems, and these are the most productive soils of the state.

questions.q: Saline and alkaline soils, locally called Reh or Kallar, are a serious problem in which districts of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The canal-irrigated tract of Sri Ganganagar and Hanumangarh suffers from secondary salinity and alkalinity caused by over-irrigation and rising water tables.

questions.q: Red loamy soil in Rajasthan is chiefly found in which districts?
questions.exp: Red loamy soil occurs in the humid southern districts of Banswara, Dungarpur, Pratapgarh, Udaipur and Chittorgarh, where iron oxides give the characteristic colour.

questions.q: The brown or non-calcic brown soils of Rajasthan are chiefly associated with which basin?
questions.exp: Brown soils occupy the Luni basin - Pali, Jalore, Sirohi and Ajmer, extending into parts of Sikar and Jhunjhunu - and are comparatively rich in phosphate.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Soil type)   List-II (Districts)
A. Desert sandy soil   1. Banswara and Dungarpur
B. Black soil          2. Bharatpur and Dholpur
C. Alluvial soil       3. Kota and Jhalawar
D. Red loamy soil      4. Jaisalmer and Barmer
questions.exp: Sandy desert soil belongs to the western Thar, black soil to the Hadoti lava tract, alluvium to the eastern plain and red loam to the humid south.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of a soil type and a district of Rajasthan is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Churu lies in the arid Thar and carries desert sandy soil. Red loamy soil belongs to the humid southern districts such as Banswara and Dungarpur.

questions.q: In the USDA soil taxonomy adopted for Rajasthan, which order occupies the largest area of the state?
questions.exp: Entisols, the youngest soils showing almost no horizon development, cover the greatest extent in western Rajasthan. Aridisols occupy the true desert core.

questions.q: In soil taxonomy, the black cotton soils of Kota, Bundi, Baran and Jhalawar belong to which order?
questions.exp: Vertisols are deep, swelling clay soils that crack widely in the dry season and are self-mulching. In Rajasthan they occupy the Hadoti plateau.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Soil order)   List-II (Region of Rajasthan)
A. Aridisol    1. Kota and Jhalawar
B. Vertisol    2. Jaisalmer and Bikaner
C. Alfisol     3. Udaipur and Dungarpur
D. Inceptisol  4. Alwar and Bharatpur
questions.exp: Aridisols occupy the desert, Vertisols the Hadoti lava plateau, Alfisols the eastern plain and Inceptisols the southern Aravalli-Mewar-Vagad tract.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the desert soils of Rajasthan:
I. They are highly porous and have low water-holding capacity.
II. They are generally rich in humus and nitrogen.
III. They are usually calcareous and often contain a kankar layer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Desert soils are poor in humus and nitrogen because of sparse vegetation and rapid oxidation, but they are calcareous and frequently have a kankar or gypsum layer.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the black soils of Rajasthan:
I. They are derived from the weathering of Deccan lava.
II. They have a high clay content and retain moisture well.
III. They are the dominant soils of the Shekhawati region.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Black soils occupy the Hadoti plateau of the south-east, not Shekhawati, which carries sandy and brown soils.

questions.q: The chief soil problem of western Rajasthan is:
questions.exp: High wind velocity, loose sandy soil and sparse vegetation make wind erosion and shifting dunes the dominant soil hazard of the Thar.

questions.q: The extensive ravines and gully erosion of Rajasthan are chiefly associated with which river valley?
questions.exp: The Chambal ravines of Dholpur, Karauli and Sawai Madhopur are among India's most severely gullied badlands.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about waterlogging in Rajasthan:
I. It is most serious in the command area of the Indira Gandhi Nahar.
II. It is accompanied by secondary salinisation of the soil.
III. Sub-surface drainage is one of the recommended remedies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Over-irrigation without adequate drainage in the Sri Ganganagar and Hanumangarh canal tract has raised water tables and brought salts to the surface.

questions.q: Which amendment is most commonly used to reclaim alkaline soils in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Gypsum supplies calcium that displaces sodium from the soil complex, after which the sodium salts are leached out. Lime is used for acidic, not alkaline, soils.

questions.q: Into how many agro-climatic zones has Rajasthan been divided?
questions.exp: Rajasthan has ten agro-climatic zones, grouped into five broad regions numbered I to V, delineated on the basis of rainfall, soil, temperature and topography.

questions.q: Bikaner, Churu and Jaisalmer are included in which agro-climatic zone of Rajasthan?
opts: Zone I-C Hyper Arid Partial Irrigated Zone
Zone II-A Transitional Plain of Inland Drainage
questions.exp: Zone I-C, the Hyper Arid Partial Irrigated Zone, comprises Bikaner, Churu and Jaisalmer and is the driest agro-climatic zone of the state.

questions.q: Jaipur, Ajmer, Dausa and Tonk fall in which agro-climatic zone of Rajasthan?
opts: Zone III-B Flood Prone Eastern Plain
Zone II-B Transitional Plain of Luni Basin
questions.exp: Zone III-A, the Semi-Arid Eastern Plain, covers Jaipur, Ajmer, Dausa and Tonk, with rainfall of roughly 500-600 mm.

questions.q: Which agro-climatic zone of Rajasthan comprises Sri Ganganagar and Hanumangarh districts?
questions.exp: Zone I-B, the Irrigated North-Western Plain, comprises Sri Ganganagar and Hanumangarh. It is the only agro-climatic zone of the state that is fully canal-irrigated.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Agro-climatic zone)   List-II (Districts)
A. Zone II-A Transitional Plain of Inland Drainage   1. Kota and Jhalawar
B. Zone II-B Transitional Plain of Luni Basin        2. Sikar and Jhunjhunu
C. Zone IV-B Humid Southern Plain                    3. Jalore and Pali
D. Zone V Humid South-Eastern Plain                  4. Dungarpur and Banswara
questions.exp: Zone II-A is the Shekhawati inland-drainage tract, II-B the Luni basin, IV-B the humid Vagad south and Zone V the Hadoti plateau.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of an agro-climatic zone and its districts is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Zone I-B Irrigated North-Western Plain - Sri Ganganagar and Hanumangarh
Zone III-B Flood Prone Eastern Plain - Alwar and Bharatpur
Zone V Humid South-Eastern Plain - Kota and Baran
Zone IV-A Sub-Humid Southern Plain - Bikaner and Churu
questions.exp: Zone IV-A, the Sub-Humid Southern Plain, comprises Udaipur, Chittorgarh, Rajsamand and Bhilwara. Bikaner and Churu belong to the hyper-arid Zone I-C.

questions.q: Which agro-climatic zone of Rajasthan is known as the Humid South-Eastern Plain and covers the Hadoti districts?
questions.exp: Zone V, the Humid South-Eastern Plain, covers Kota, Bundi, Baran and Jhalawar. Its deep black soils make it the most productive farmland of Rajasthan.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Zone I-B of Rajasthan's agro-climatic classification:
I. It comprises Sri Ganganagar and Hanumangarh districts.
II. It receives the highest natural rainfall of all zones in the state.
III. It depends heavily on canal irrigation from the Gang and Indira Gandhi canal systems.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Zone I-B has low natural rainfall; its agricultural prosperity rests entirely on canal irrigation, which is why it is called the Irrigated North-Western Plain.

questions.q:
Arrange the following agro-climatic zones of Rajasthan in ASCENDING order of average annual rainfall:
I. Zone I-C Hyper Arid Partial Irrigated Zone
II. Zone III-A Semi-Arid Eastern Plain
III. Zone IV-B Humid Southern Plain
IV. Zone II-A Transitional Plain of Inland Drainage
questions.exp: Rainfall rises from the hyper-arid Zone I-C through the Shekhawati transitional plain and the semi-arid eastern plain to the humid southern plain of Dungarpur and Banswara.

questions.q: Mixed red and black soil in Rajasthan is chiefly found in which districts?
questions.exp: Mixed red and black soil occurs where the Aravalli metamorphics meet the Deccan lava, in Chittorgarh, Pratapgarh, Bhilwara, Banswara and Jhalawar.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Soil of Rajasthan)   List-II (Parent material or origin)
A. Black soil        1. Weathering of granite and gneiss
B. Red-yellow soil   2. River-borne deposits
C. Desert soil       3. Weathering of Deccan lava
D. Alluvial soil     4. Wind-blown sand
questions.exp: Black soils form on Deccan basalt, red-yellow soils on granites and gneisses of the Aravalli belt, desert soils from wind-blown sand and alluvium from river deposition.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about land degradation in Rajasthan:
I. Rajasthan has the largest area under desertification and land degradation among Indian states.
II. Wind erosion is the principal process of land degradation in the state.
III. The Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas of India is prepared by ISRO.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Wind erosion and vegetation degradation in the Thar make Rajasthan the most desertification-affected state in India.

questions.q: The thin, immature skeletal soils found on the steep slopes of the Aravalli range are called:
questions.exp: Lithosols, along with regosols, are shallow stony soils on Aravalli slopes with almost no profile development and very low agricultural value.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about soil conservation measures in Rajasthan:
I. Shelterbelt plantation and dune stabilisation are used against wind erosion.
II. Contour bunding and check dams are used against water erosion.
III. Gypsum application is used to reclaim alkaline soils.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are standard measures. In the IGNP command, sub-surface drainage is added to control waterlogging and secondary salinity.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a soil order recognised in the soil taxonomy of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Oxisols are deeply weathered tropical soils of humid equatorial regions and do not occur in Rajasthan. The state has Entisols, Aridisols, Inceptisols, Vertisols and Alfisols.

questions.q: The Alfisol order of soils in Rajasthan is chiefly found in which districts?
questions.exp: Alfisols, moderately leached soils with a clay-enriched subsoil, occupy the sub-humid eastern plain of Alwar, Bharatpur, Dholpur and Karauli.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the agro-climatic zoning of Rajasthan is NOT correct?
opts: The state has ten agro-climatic zones
Zone I-C is the driest zone of the state
Zone V comprises the Hadoti districts
Zone II-B covers Alwar, Bharatpur and Dholpur
questions.exp: Zone II-B is the Transitional Plain of the Luni Basin, covering Jalore, Pali and parts of Sirohi and Jodhpur. Alwar, Bharatpur and Dholpur belong to Zone III-B, the Flood Prone Eastern Plain.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Soil problem)   List-II (Area chiefly affected)
A. Wind erosion and dune movement   1. Sambhar and Pachpadra
B. Ravine and gully erosion         2. Dholpur and Karauli
C. Waterlogging and salinity        3. Sri Ganganagar and Hanumangarh
D. Soil salinity from saline lakes  4. Jaisalmer and Barmer
questions.exp: Wind erosion afflicts the Thar, ravines the Chambal tract, waterlogging the canal command, and salinity the surroundings of the saline lakes.

chapters.title: Biodiversity Conservation: Parks, Sanctuaries, Reserves
factsheet: Rajasthan has 5 national parks: Ranthambore (Sawai Madhopur), Keoladeo Ghana (Bharatpur), Sariska (Alwar), Desert NP (Jaisalmer-Barmer) and Mukundra Hills (Kota-Bundi-Jhalawar-Chittorgarh).
Desert National Park (about 3,162 sq km) is Rajasthan's largest national park; Keoladeo Ghana (28.73 sq km) is the smallest.
Keoladeo Ghana — bird sanctuary 1956, Ramsar site 1981, national park 1982, UNESCO World Heritage Site 1985; fed by the Gambhir and Banganga; Ajan Bandh built by Maharaja Suraj Mal of Bharatpur.
Ranthambore — Sawai Madhopur; one of the nine original Project Tiger reserves of 1973; national park 1980; Padam Talab, Raj Bagh, Jogi Mahal, Trinetra Ganesh temple.
Sariska (Alwar) — tiger reserve 1978, national park 1982; site of the world's first tiger relocation, June 2008, when tiger ST-1 was airlifted from Ranthambore.
Rajasthan's five notified tiger reserves: Ranthambore, Sariska, Mukundra Hills (2013), Ramgarh Vishdhari (2022, Bundi) and Dholpur-Karauli (2023) — position as of September 2026.
Dholpur-Karauli is India's 54th tiger reserve and Rajasthan's fifth and newest (2023).
Kumbhalgarh (Rajsamand-Udaipur-Pali-Ajmer-Sirohi, about 1,397 sq km) received in-principle central approval in August 2023 as Rajasthan's proposed sixth tiger reserve.
Rajasthan has 5 Ramsar sites (as of 2026): Keoladeo Ghana (1981), Sambhar Lake (1990), Khichan and Menar (5 June 2025) and Siliserh Lake, Alwar (2025).
Khichan (Phalodi) is famous for wintering demoiselle cranes (kurja); Menar (Udaipur) is the community-conserved 'bird village'.
Sanctuary to species: Tal Chhapar (Churu) blackbuck; Sitamata (Pratapgarh) flying squirrel and chausingha; National Chambal gharial, Gangetic dolphin and skimmer; Kumbhalgarh Indian wolf.

Sanctuary to district: Mount Abu-Sirohi; Shergarh-Baran; Bandh Baretha-Bharatpur; Kesarbagh, Van Vihar and Ram Sagar-Dholpur; Bassi and Bhainsrodgarh-Chittorgarh; Gajner-Bikaner; Dhawa (Doli)-Jodhpur.
Sajjangarh Wildlife Sanctuary (Udaipur) surrounds the Monsoon Palace and is the smallest sanctuary of Rajasthan.
Kailadevi (Karauli) and Sawai Man Singh (Sawai Madhopur) sanctuaries form part of the Ranthambore Tiger Reserve.
Todgarh-Raoli sanctuary spreads over Ajmer, Pali and Rajsamand; Kumbhalgarh WLS over Rajsamand, Udaipur and Pali; Jawahar Sagar over Kota, Bundi and Chittorgarh.
Bisalpur (Tonk, 2008) was Rajasthan's first conservation reserve; Jodbeed Gadhwala (Bikaner, 2008) is famous for migratory vultures.

Conservation reserve to district: Jawai Bandh leopard-Pali; Sundha Mata-Jalore and Sirohi; Gudha Vishnoi-Jodhpur; Rotu and Gogelav-Nagaur; Beed Jhunjhunu and Mansa Mata-Jhunjhunu; Ummedganj-Kota; Shakambhari-Sikar and Jhunjhunu; Baghdarrah crocodile-Udaipur; Shahbad and Sorsan-Baran.
State symbols: state bird Godawan / Great Indian Bustard (1981), state animal (wild) chinkara (1981), state animal (domestic) camel (2014), state tree khejri, state flower rohida.
Project Great Indian Bustard was launched by Rajasthan on 5 June 2013; GIB conservation breeding centres are at Sam-Sudasari and Ramdevra in Jaisalmer.
Jhalana (Jaipur, 2017) is India's first leopard reserve; Amagarh (Jaipur) is Rajasthan's second leopard reserve.
Sorsan (Baran) and Shokaliya (Ajmer) grasslands are lesser florican (kharmor) habitats; Kharmor Conservation Reserve is in Ajmer.
Khejarli (Jodhpur) — Amrita Devi Bishnoi and 362 Bishnois died in 1730 defending khejri trees; the Amrita Devi Bishnoi Award is Rajasthan's highest wildlife honour.
Kailash Sankhala of Jodhpur, the 'Tiger Man of India', was the first director of Project Tiger; Wildlife Week is observed 2-8 October.
Biological parks: Nahargarh (Jaipur), Sajjangarh (Udaipur), Machia (Jodhpur), Abheda (Kota); Jaipur Zoo (1876) is the oldest zoo of the state.
Akal Wood Fossil Park near Jaisalmer preserves 180-million-year-old fossilised tree trunks of the Jurassic period.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the largest national park of Rajasthan by area?
questions.exp: Desert National Park, spread over about 3,162 sq km in Jaisalmer and Barmer districts, is the largest national park of Rajasthan. Keoladeo Ghana (28.73 sq km) is the smallest.

questions.q: Keoladeo Ghana National Park is situated in which district of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Keoladeo Ghana lies in Bharatpur. It was declared a bird sanctuary in 1956, a Ramsar site in 1981 and a national park in 1982.

questions.q: Which national park of Rajasthan is inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List?
questions.exp: Keoladeo National Park was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985. Rajasthan's other World Heritage properties are the Hill Forts, Jantar Mantar and the walled city of Jaipur.

questions.q: How many national parks are there in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Rajasthan has five national parks: Ranthambore, Keoladeo Ghana, Sariska, Desert National Park and Mukundra Hills.

questions.q: The Indian giant flying squirrel is the best-known mammal of which wildlife sanctuary of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Sitamata Wildlife Sanctuary, chiefly in Pratapgarh and extending into Chittorgarh and Udaipur, is famous for the flying squirrel (uran gilheri) and the four-horned antelope (chausingha).

questions.q: Tal Chhapar Wildlife Sanctuary, noted for its blackbuck population, is located in which district?
questions.exp: Tal Chhapar is a flat saline grassland in Churu district. Besides blackbuck it is an important wintering ground for harriers.

questions.q: The gharial and the Gangetic dolphin are protected in which sanctuary of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The National Chambal Sanctuary (1979), extending over Kota, Bundi, Sawai Madhopur, Dholpur and Karauli, protects the gharial, mugger, Gangetic dolphin and Indian skimmer.

questions.q: Mount Abu Wildlife Sanctuary lies in which district of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Mount Abu Wildlife Sanctuary (1960) is in Sirohi district and contains Rajasthan's only sub-tropical evergreen forest patches.

questions.q: Which is the fifth and newest notified tiger reserve of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Dholpur-Karauli was notified in 2023 as Rajasthan's fifth tiger reserve and India's 54th. Position as of September 2026; Kumbhalgarh has only in-principle approval as the proposed sixth.

questions.q: Ramgarh Vishdhari Tiger Reserve is located in which district?
questions.exp: Ramgarh Vishdhari, in Bundi district, was notified in 2022 as Rajasthan's fourth tiger reserve. The Mej river flows through it.

questions.q: Mukundra Hills was declared a tiger reserve in which year?
questions.exp: Mukundra Hills became Rajasthan's third tiger reserve in 2013. Its national park was carved out of the erstwhile Darrah, Jawahar Sagar and Chambal sanctuaries.

questions.q: The world's first relocation of a wild tiger from one reserve to another was carried out in 2008 at:
questions.exp: After Sariska lost all its tigers by 2004-05, tiger ST-1 was airlifted from Ranthambore to Sariska in June 2008 — the world's first tiger relocation by air.

questions.q: Which area has received in-principle central approval to become Rajasthan's sixth tiger reserve?
questions.exp: The Kumbhalgarh-Todgarh Raoli landscape, spread over Rajsamand, Udaipur, Pali, Ajmer and Sirohi, received in-principle approval in August 2023 as the proposed sixth tiger reserve. Status as of September 2026.

questions.q: Which bird is the state bird of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The Great Indian Bustard, locally called godawan, was adopted as the state bird in 1981. Its main habitat is the Desert National Park.

questions.q: Which animal is the state animal (wild category) of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The chinkara (Indian gazelle) was declared the state animal in 1981; the camel was later added as the state animal in the domestic category.

questions.q: The camel was declared the state animal of Rajasthan in the domestic category in which year?
questions.exp: The camel was declared Rajasthan's state animal (domestic category) in 2014, and the Rajasthan Camel (Prohibition of Slaughter and Regulation of Temporary Migration or Export) Act followed in 2015.

questions.q: Which tree is the state tree of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Khejri (Prosopis cineraria), the 'kalpavriksha of the desert', is the state tree. Rohida (Tecomella undulata) is the state flower.

questions.q: Rohida is the state flower of Rajasthan. Its botanical name is:
questions.exp: Rohida (Tecomella undulata), also called the desert teak or 'marwar teak', is Rajasthan's state flower.

questions.q: Sambhar Lake was designated a Ramsar site in which year?
questions.exp: Sambhar, India's largest inland saline lake, became a Ramsar site in 1990. Keoladeo Ghana had been designated earlier, in 1981.

questions.q: As of 2026, how many Ramsar sites are located in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Rajasthan has five Ramsar sites as of 2026 — Keoladeo Ghana (1981), Sambhar Lake (1990), Khichan and Menar (June 2025) and Siliserh Lake, Alwar (2025).

questions.q: Khichan wetland, declared a Ramsar site in 2025, is famous for which migratory bird?
questions.exp: Khichan in Phalodi is world-renowned for the thousands of demoiselle cranes (kurja) that winter there and are fed by the local Jain community.

questions.q: Siliserh Lake, added to the Ramsar list in 2025, is situated in which district?
questions.exp: Siliserh Lake near Alwar became Rajasthan's fifth Ramsar site in 2025, after Keoladeo, Sambhar, Khichan and Menar.

questions.q: Which was the first conservation reserve to be notified in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Bisalpur Conservation Reserve in Tonk district, notified in 2008, was Rajasthan's first conservation reserve. Jodbeed Gadhwala (Bikaner) and Sundha Mata were notified the same year.

questions.q: Jawai Bandh Conservation Reserve in Pali district is best known for which animal?
questions.exp: The granite hills around Jawai Bandh in Pali support a remarkable density of leopards, which is why the area was notified as a leopard conservation reserve in 2013.

questions.q: Jodbeed Gadhwala Conservation Reserve in Bikaner is chiefly important for the conservation of:
questions.exp: Jodbeed Gadhwala, notified in 2008, hosts large congregations of migratory vultures, including Eurasian griffons, near Bikaner's carcass dumping ground.

questions.q: Kumbhalgarh Wildlife Sanctuary is particularly noted for which carnivore?
questions.exp: Kumbhalgarh Wildlife Sanctuary (Rajsamand, Udaipur and Pali) is known for the Indian wolf, besides leopard and chausingha.

questions.q: The Sorsan grassland of Baran district is an important habitat of which bird?
questions.exp: Sorsan in Baran is one of Rajasthan's principal breeding grasslands for the lesser florican (kharmor); Shokaliya in Ajmer is another.

questions.q: Which is India's first leopard reserve, notified in Rajasthan in 2017?
questions.exp: Jhalana in Jaipur was notified in 2017 as India's first leopard reserve. Amagarh, also in Jaipur, became Rajasthan's second.

questions.q: Kailadevi Wildlife Sanctuary, which forms part of the Ranthambore Tiger Reserve, lies mainly in which district?
questions.exp: Kailadevi Sanctuary (1983) lies chiefly in Karauli and extends into Sawai Madhopur; along with Sawai Man Singh Sanctuary it forms the buffer of the Ranthambore Tiger Reserve.

questions.q: Desert National Park is spread over which two districts?
questions.exp: Desert National Park covers parts of Jaisalmer and Barmer districts and is the principal refuge of the Great Indian Bustard.

questions.q: Shergarh Wildlife Sanctuary is located in which district of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Shergarh Sanctuary (1983) lies in Baran district on the Parvan river; Baran was carved out of Kota district in 1991.

questions.q: Who, born in Jodhpur and known as the 'Tiger Man of India', was the first director of Project Tiger?
questions.exp: Kailash Sankhala was the first director of Project Tiger (1973) and author of 'Tiger! The Story of the Indian Tiger'. Fateh Singh Rathore is associated with Ranthambore.

questions.q: Gajner Wildlife Sanctuary is situated in which district?
questions.exp: Gajner Sanctuary, around the Gajner lake and palace in Bikaner district, is famous for the imperial sandgrouse and blackbuck.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Ranthambore National Park:
I. It lies in Sawai Madhopur district.
II. It was among the nine reserves selected at the launch of Project Tiger in 1973.
III. The Trinetra Ganesh temple is situated within the reserve.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Ranthambore, in Sawai Madhopur, was one of the original nine Project Tiger reserves of 1973 and was declared a national park in 1980; the Trinetra Ganesh temple stands inside Ranthambore fort.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Keoladeo National Park:
I. It was created around the Ajan Bandh built by Maharaja Suraj Mal of Bharatpur.
II. It became a Ramsar site in 1981.
III. It was once the wintering ground of the Siberian crane.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Keoladeo was a duck-shooting preserve of the Bharatpur rulers, became a Ramsar site in 1981 and a national park in 1982; the Siberian crane was last recorded there in 2002.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Desert National Park:
I. It is the largest national park of Rajasthan.
II. It is the principal habitat of the Great Indian Bustard in India.
III. It lies wholly within Bikaner district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Desert National Park lies in Jaisalmer and Barmer districts, not Bikaner, so III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Sariska:
I. It was brought under Project Tiger in 1978.
II. It was declared a national park in 1982.
III. Tigers were reintroduced there from Ranthambore in 2008.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Sariska in Alwar became a tiger reserve in 1978 and a national park in 1982, and after local extinction it received relocated tigers from Ranthambore beginning June 2008.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the tiger reserves of Rajasthan:
I. Rajasthan has five notified tiger reserves.
II. Ramgarh Vishdhari Tiger Reserve is in Bundi district.
III. Dholpur-Karauli is the newest tiger reserve of the state.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct as of September 2026. Rajasthan's tiger reserves are Ranthambore, Sariska, Mukundra Hills, Ramgarh Vishdhari (Bundi, 2022) and Dholpur-Karauli (2023).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Ramsar sites of Rajasthan:
I. Keoladeo Ghana was designated in 1981.
II. Sambhar Lake is India's largest inland saline wetland.
III. Menar wetland lies in Udaipur district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Menar, the 'bird village' of Udaipur, and Khichan of Phalodi were designated Ramsar sites on 5 June 2025.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Tal Chhapar Sanctuary:
I. It is a flat saline grassland.
II. It is famous for the blackbuck.
III. It lies in Jhunjhunu district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Tal Chhapar is in Churu district, not Jhunjhunu, so III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about conservation reserves in Rajasthan:
I. Bisalpur Conservation Reserve is in Tonk district.
II. Sundha Mata Conservation Reserve extends over Jalore and Sirohi.
III. Ummedganj Conservation Reserve is in Kota.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Bisalpur (Tonk, 2008) was the state's first conservation reserve; Sundha Mata spans Jalore and Sirohi; Ummedganj Pakshi Vihar is in Kota.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Sitamata Wildlife Sanctuary:
I. It is known for the flying squirrel.
II. The four-horned antelope is found there.
III. It lies mainly in Bikaner district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Sitamata lies chiefly in Pratapgarh, extending into Chittorgarh and Udaipur, so III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the state symbols of Rajasthan:
I. The chinkara is the state animal in the wild category.
II. The godawan is the state bird.
III. The khejri is the state tree.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Rohida is the state flower and the camel is the state animal in the domestic category.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Chambal Sanctuary:
I. It was notified in 1979.
II. It is a tri-state sanctuary shared by Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.
III. The Indian skimmer is found there.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. In Rajasthan the sanctuary covers stretches of the Chambal in Kota, Bundi, Sawai Madhopur, Dholpur and Karauli, protecting gharial, dolphin and skimmer.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Wildlife Sanctuary)   List-II (District)
A. Tal Chhapar   1. Sirohi
B. Mount Abu     2. Churu
C. Shergarh      3. Bundi
D. Ramgarh Vishdhari   4. Baran
questions.exp: Tal Chhapar is in Churu, Mount Abu in Sirohi, Shergarh in Baran and Ramgarh Vishdhari in Bundi.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Wildlife Sanctuary)   List-II (District)
A. Bandh Baretha   1. Dholpur
B. Kesarbagh       2. Bharatpur
C. Sajjangarh      3. Sawai Madhopur
D. Sawai Man Singh 4. Udaipur
questions.exp: Bandh Baretha is in Bharatpur, Kesarbagh in Dholpur, Sajjangarh in Udaipur and Sawai Man Singh in Sawai Madhopur.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Conservation Reserve)   List-II (District)
A. Jawai Bandh   1. Jodhpur
B. Gudha Vishnoi 2. Nagaur
C. Rotu          3. Pali
D. Ummedganj     4. Kota
questions.exp: Jawai Bandh leopard conservation reserve is in Pali, Gudha Vishnoi in Jodhpur, Rotu in Nagaur and Ummedganj in Kota.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Tiger Reserve)   List-II (Year of notification)
A. Mukundra Hills   1. 1973
B. Ranthambore      2. 1978
C. Sariska          3. 2013
D. Ramgarh Vishdhari 4. 2022
questions.exp: Ranthambore came under Project Tiger in 1973, Sariska in 1978, Mukundra Hills in 2013 and Ramgarh Vishdhari in 2022; Dholpur-Karauli followed in 2023.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Protected area)   List-II (Flagship species)
A. Sitamata      1. Gharial
B. Tal Chhapar   2. Flying squirrel
C. National Chambal 3. Leopard
D. Jawai Bandh   4. Blackbuck
questions.exp: Sitamata is known for the flying squirrel, Tal Chhapar for blackbuck, National Chambal for gharial and Jawai Bandh for leopard.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (National Park)   List-II (District)
A. Ranthambore   1. Alwar
B. Sariska       2. Bharatpur
C. Keoladeo Ghana 3. Sawai Madhopur
D. Mukundra Hills 4. Kota
questions.exp: Ranthambore is in Sawai Madhopur, Sariska in Alwar, Keoladeo Ghana in Bharatpur and Mukundra Hills chiefly in Kota, extending into Bundi, Jhalawar and Chittorgarh.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Ramsar site)   List-II (District)
A. Keoladeo Ghana   1. Phalodi
B. Khichan          2. Udaipur
C. Menar            3. Bharatpur
D. Siliserh         4. Alwar
questions.exp: Keoladeo Ghana is in Bharatpur, Khichan in Phalodi, Menar in Udaipur and Siliserh in Alwar; Sambhar Lake spreads over Jaipur, Nagaur and Ajmer.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Wildlife Sanctuary)   List-II (District)
A. Bassi        1. Bikaner
B. Phulwari ki Naal 2. Jaipur
C. Jamwa Ramgarh 3. Chittorgarh
D. Gajner       4. Udaipur
questions.exp: Bassi is in Chittorgarh, Phulwari ki Naal in Udaipur, Jamwa Ramgarh in Jaipur and Gajner in Bikaner.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of wildlife sanctuary and district is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Todgarh-Raoli Sanctuary spreads over Ajmer, Pali and Rajsamand districts, not Bharatpur. The other three pairs are correct.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a tiger reserve of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Sitamata is a wildlife sanctuary in Pratapgarh, not a tiger reserve. Rajasthan's five tiger reserves are Ranthambore, Sariska, Mukundra Hills, Ramgarh Vishdhari and Dholpur-Karauli.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a national park of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Kumbhalgarh is a wildlife sanctuary (and a proposed tiger reserve), not a national park. Rajasthan's national parks are Ranthambore, Keoladeo Ghana, Sariska, Desert and Mukundra Hills.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of conservation reserve and district is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Beed Jhunjhunu Conservation Reserve is in Jhunjhunu district, not Barmer. Shakambhari extends over Sikar and Jhunjhunu, Baghdarrah crocodile reserve is in Udaipur and Gogelav is in Nagaur.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a Ramsar site of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Pushkar Lake is not a Ramsar site. Rajasthan's five Ramsar sites are Keoladeo Ghana, Sambhar Lake, Khichan, Menar and Siliserh (position as of 2026).

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of species and protected area is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Great Indian Bustard - Keoladeo National Park
questions.exp: The Great Indian Bustard is associated with the Desert National Park, Sorsan and Shokaliya grasslands, not with Keoladeo, which is a wetland bird park.

questions.q:
Arrange the following tiger reserves of Rajasthan in the correct chronological order of their notification, beginning with the earliest:
I. Mukundra Hills
II. Sariska
III. Dholpur-Karauli
IV. Ramgarh Vishdhari
questions.exp: Sariska (1978), Mukundra Hills (2013), Ramgarh Vishdhari (2022) and Dholpur-Karauli (2023). Ranthambore, notified in 1973, is the oldest of all.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Great Indian Bustard has been adopted as the state bird of Rajasthan.
Reason (R): The Desert National Park of Jaisalmer is among the last strongholds of the species in India.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: Both statements are factually true, but the bird was adopted as a state symbol in 1981 as a cultural and conservation emblem; the location of its surviving habitat is not the reason for that adoption.

chapters.title: Agriculture and Crops of Rajasthan
factsheet: Rajasthan ranks first in India in the production of bajra, rapeseed-mustard, guar (cluster bean), moth bean, isabgol and henna.
Bajra: Rajasthan is India's largest producer; Alwar leads in production while Barmer has the largest area under the crop.
Rapeseed-mustard: Rajasthan is the largest producer; Sriganganagar, Alwar and Bharatpur are leading districts; ICAR-Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research is at Sewar, Bharatpur.
Guar: Rajasthan accounts for the bulk of India's guar and guar gum output; Hanumangarh and Bikaner lead; guar gum is a major export earner.
Rajasthan ranks second in India in groundnut (Bikaner leads), third in soybean (Jhalawar leads) and third in total pulses (Nagaur leads).
Jowar: Rajasthan ranks third in India, Ajmer leading; barley is dominated by Jaipur district; gram by Bikaner.
Wheat and cotton are concentrated in the canal-irrigated north-west — Sriganganagar and Hanumangarh.
Seed spices: Rajasthan has the largest area in India under cumin (jeera); Nagaur is famous for fenugreek (methi), Jalore for isabgol, and Baran-Kota-Jhalawar for coriander.
Ramganj Mandi in Kota district is Asia's largest coriander (dhania) market.
Sojat (Pali) henna carries a Geographical Indication tag; Rajasthan supplies almost all of India's mehndi.
Horticulture: kinnow — Sriganganagar and Hanumangarh; orange — Jhalawar; Mathania (Jodhpur) red chilli; ber and aonla in the arid west.
Rajasthan pioneered olive cultivation through Rajasthan Olive Cultivation Ltd; India's first olive oil refinery is at Bassi in Jaipur district.
A Centre of Excellence for date palm has been set up at Sagra-Bhojka in Jaisalmer district.
Opium is grown under licence in Chittorgarh, Pratapgarh, Bhilwara and Jhalawar and is regulated by the Central Bureau of Narcotics.
Walra is the slash-and-burn shifting cultivation of the Bhils of southern Rajasthan; Chimata (plains/lower slopes) and Dajiya (hill slopes) are its two forms.
Maize hybrids associated with Rajasthan: Mahi Kanchan, Mahi Dhawal and the Pratap Makka series; bajra: RCB 911 and the RHB (Rajasthan Hybrid Bajra) series, besides HHB 67 Improved.
ICAR-National Research Centre on Seed Spices is at Tabiji, Ajmer (2000); the National Research Centre on Camel and the Central Institute for Arid Horticulture are both at Bikaner.
CAZRI (Central Arid Zone Research Institute), Jodhpur was set up in 1959; AFRI is also at Jodhpur; CSWRI is at Avikanagar (Malpura, Tonk), 1962.

Agricultural universities: SKRAU Bikaner (1987, the state's first), MPUAT Udaipur (1999), SKNAU Jobner, Agriculture University Jodhpur and Agriculture University Kota (2013); RAJUVAS Bikaner (2010) for veterinary sciences.
Rajasthan is divided into 10 agro-climatic zones out of the 126 identified for India by ICAR.
Rajasthan became the first Indian state to present a separate agriculture budget, in February 2022.
Kharif crops: bajra, jowar, maize, moth, guar, groundnut, cotton, sesame, soybean; rabi crops: wheat, barley, gram, mustard, taramira, isabgol, coriander.
Rajasthan Organic Farming Policy was announced in 2017; the Raj Kisan Saathi portal delivers farmer services online; crop insurance runs through PMFBY.
The Rajasthan State Agricultural Marketing Board (1974) runs the krishi upaj mandis; GRAM (Global Rajasthan Agritech Meet) was first held at Jaipur in 2016.
Sugarcane is confined to Bundi, Sriganganagar, Chittorgarh and Udaipur; the Keshoraipatan (Bundi) cooperative sugar mill is the best known unit.

questions.q: Rajasthan holds the first rank in India in the production of which of the following coarse cereals?
questions.exp: Rajasthan is India's largest producer of bajra (pearl millet). Alwar leads in production while Barmer has the largest area under the crop.

questions.q: Rajasthan is the largest producer in India of which of the following oilseeds?
questions.exp: Rajasthan leads India in rapeseed-mustard. It ranks second in groundnut and third in soybean.

questions.q: Which district leads Rajasthan in the production of guar (cluster bean)?
questions.exp: Hanumangarh leads in guar production, followed by Bikaner. Rajasthan accounts for the bulk of India's guar and guar-gum output, a major export item.

questions.q: Which district of Rajasthan is the leading producer of isabgol (psyllium)?
questions.exp: Jalore is the principal isabgol-producing district of Rajasthan, which is India's largest producer of the crop.

questions.q: Which place in Rajasthan is famous for henna (mehndi) cultivation and holds a Geographical Indication tag for it?
questions.exp: Sojat in Pali district is India's henna capital; Sojat mehndi received a GI tag. Rajasthan supplies almost the whole of India's henna.

questions.q: Ramganj Mandi, described as Asia's largest market for its produce, is associated with which crop?
questions.exp: Ramganj Mandi in Kota district is Asia's largest coriander (dhania) market. Coriander is grown mainly in Baran, Kota, Jhalawar and Bundi.

questions.q: Rajasthan has the largest area in India under which of the following seed spices?
questions.exp: Rajasthan has the largest area under cumin (jeera) in India, grown mainly in Jodhpur, Barmer, Jalore, Nagaur and Pali. Gujarat is the other major cumin state.

questions.q: Which district of Rajasthan is best known for the cultivation of fenugreek (methi)?
questions.exp: Nagaur is the leading fenugreek district of Rajasthan, which accounts for the largest share of India's methi production.

questions.q: Licensed cultivation of opium in Rajasthan is chiefly carried on in which group of districts?
questions.exp: Opium poppy is licensed in Chittorgarh, Pratapgarh, Bhilwara and Jhalawar in Rajasthan, under the Central Bureau of Narcotics; Mandsaur and Neemuch in Madhya Pradesh form the adjoining belt.

questions.q: Kinnow cultivation in Rajasthan is concentrated in which district?
questions.exp: Kinnow is grown mainly in Sriganganagar and Hanumangarh in the canal-irrigated north-west. Jhalawar is Rajasthan's orange belt.

questions.q: Which district of Rajasthan is known as the state's orange (santra) belt?
questions.exp: Jhalawar in the Hadoti region is Rajasthan's orange belt, supported by the humid south-eastern climate.

questions.q: Mathania, famous for its red chilli, is located in which district?
questions.exp: Mathania in Jodhpur district is renowned for its pungent red chilli, used in Rajasthani cuisine such as laal maas.

questions.q: India's first olive oil refinery was established at which place in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: India's first olive oil refinery was set up at Bassi in Jaipur district. Olive cultivation in Rajasthan is promoted through Rajasthan Olive Cultivation Ltd.

questions.q: 'Walra' in Rajasthan refers to:
opts: Shifting cultivation practised by the Bhils
questions.exp: Walra is the slash-and-burn shifting cultivation of the Bhils of southern Rajasthan (Udaipur, Dungarpur, Banswara, Sirohi). Chimata and Dajiya are its plain and hill-slope forms.

questions.q: 'Mahi Kanchan' is an improved variety of which crop?
questions.exp: Mahi Kanchan is a maize variety associated with Rajasthan's southern maize belt; Mahi Dhawal and the Pratap Makka series are other maize varieties.

questions.q: 'RCB 911' is a hybrid variety of which crop?
questions.exp: RCB 911 is a bajra (pearl millet) hybrid. The RHB series (Rajasthan Hybrid Bajra) and HHB 67 Improved are other well-known bajra hybrids grown in the state.

questions.q: The National Research Centre on Seed Spices is located at:
questions.exp: The ICAR-National Research Centre on Seed Spices is at Tabiji, Ajmer, established in 2000, reflecting Rajasthan's dominance in cumin, coriander, fenugreek and fennel.

questions.q: The National Research Centre on Camel is situated in which city of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The ICAR-National Research Centre on Camel is at Bikaner. The Central Institute for Arid Horticulture is also located at Bikaner.

questions.q: The Central Institute for Arid Horticulture is located at:
questions.exp: ICAR-Central Institute for Arid Horticulture (CIAH) is at Bikaner and works on ber, aonla, date palm, pomegranate and other arid fruits.

questions.q: The Central Arid Zone Research Institute (CAZRI) is located at:
questions.exp: CAZRI was established at Jodhpur in 1959 for research on desertification, arid farming systems and sand-dune stabilisation.

questions.q: The Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research is located at Sewar in which district?
questions.exp: ICAR-Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research is at Sewar, Bharatpur, in the heart of Rajasthan's mustard belt.

questions.q: Which was the first agricultural university established in Rajasthan?
opts: Maharana Pratap University of Agriculture and Technology, Udaipur
Sri Karan Narendra Agriculture University, Jobner
questions.exp: Rajasthan Agricultural University, Bikaner, founded in 1987, was the state's first agricultural university; it is now Swami Keshwanand Rajasthan Agricultural University (SKRAU).

questions.q: Maharana Pratap University of Agriculture and Technology is located at:
questions.exp: MPUAT was established at Udaipur in 1999 and serves the southern agro-climatic zones of Rajasthan.

questions.q: Sri Karan Narendra Agriculture University is situated at:
questions.exp: Sri Karan Narendra Agriculture University (SKNAU) is at Jobner in Jaipur district, created in 2013 along with the agriculture universities of Jodhpur and Kota.

questions.q: Which state was the first in India to present a separate agriculture budget?
questions.exp: Rajasthan presented India's first separate state agriculture budget in February 2022, for the financial year 2022-23.

questions.q: Into how many agro-climatic zones is Rajasthan divided?
questions.exp: Rajasthan is divided into 10 agro-climatic zones, out of the 126 zones identified for India by ICAR.

questions.q: Which district leads Rajasthan in soybean production?
questions.exp: Jhalawar leads Rajasthan in soybean, followed by Baran. Rajasthan ranks third in India in soybean after Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about bajra cultivation in Rajasthan:
I. Rajasthan is the largest producer of bajra in India.
II. It is a kharif crop.
III. Barmer has the largest area under bajra in the state.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Bajra is Rajasthan's principal kharif cereal; Barmer has the largest area while Alwar leads in production.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about rapeseed-mustard in Rajasthan:
I. It is a rabi crop.
II. Rajasthan is the largest producer in India.
III. The Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research is located at Bharatpur.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Mustard is sown in October-November and Rajasthan contributes the largest share of India's output; the ICAR directorate is at Sewar, Bharatpur.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about guar in Rajasthan:
I. It is a kharif legume.
II. Rajasthan produces the bulk of India's guar.
III. Guar gum is used in the oil and gas industry.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Guar gum extracted from the cluster bean is used as a fracturing agent in the petroleum industry, making it one of Rajasthan's major agricultural exports.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about seed spices in Rajasthan:
I. Rajasthan has the largest area under cumin in India.
II. Jalore is the leading district for isabgol.
III. The National Research Centre on Seed Spices is at Jodhpur.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. The National Research Centre on Seed Spices is at Tabiji in Ajmer, not Jodhpur, so III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Walra cultivation:
I. It is a form of shifting cultivation.
II. It is practised by the Bhils of southern Rajasthan.
III. Chimata and Dajiya are related forms of the same practice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Walra is slash-and-burn farming of forest patches; Chimata is practised on plains and lower slopes and Dajiya on hill slopes.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about agricultural universities of Rajasthan:
I. Maharana Pratap University of Agriculture and Technology is at Udaipur.
II. Sri Karan Narendra Agriculture University is at Jobner.
III. RAJUVAS, the veterinary university, is at Jaipur.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Rajasthan University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences (RAJUVAS) is at Bikaner, not Jaipur.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about cropping seasons in Rajasthan:
I. Moth, guar and sesame are kharif crops.
II. Taramira and isabgol are rabi crops.
III. Bajra is sown in the rabi season.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Bajra is a kharif crop sown with the onset of the monsoon, so III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about horticulture in Rajasthan:
I. India's first olive oil refinery was set up at Bassi in Jaipur district.
II. A Centre of Excellence for date palm has been established in Jaisalmer district.
III. Kinnow is grown mainly in Sriganganagar and Hanumangarh.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Rajasthan has promoted olive, date palm and citrus as high-value crops of the arid and canal-irrigated tracts.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about agricultural research institutions in Rajasthan:
I. CAZRI is located at Jodhpur.
II. The Central Institute for Arid Horticulture is at Bikaner.
III. The Central Sheep and Wool Research Institute is at Avikanagar in Tonk district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. CAZRI Jodhpur (1959), CIAH Bikaner and CSWRI Avikanagar (Malpura, Tonk) are the state's leading central research institutes.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about agricultural administration in Rajasthan:
I. Rajasthan was the first state in India to present a separate agriculture budget.
II. The Rajasthan Organic Farming Policy was announced in 2017.
III. Crop insurance in the state is implemented through the Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Rajasthan presented its first separate agriculture budget in February 2022 and runs the Raj Kisan Saathi portal for farmer services.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Crop)   List-II (Leading district in Rajasthan)
A. Guar      1. Jhalawar
B. Soybean   2. Hanumangarh
C. Isabgol   3. Bikaner
D. Groundnut 4. Jalore
questions.exp: Guar leads in Hanumangarh, soybean in Jhalawar, isabgol in Jalore and groundnut in Bikaner.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Research institution)   List-II (Location)
A. National Research Centre on Seed Spices   1. Bikaner
B. National Research Centre on Camel        2. Jodhpur
C. Central Arid Zone Research Institute     3. Bharatpur
D. Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research 4. Ajmer
questions.exp: NRC on Seed Spices is at Ajmer, NRC on Camel at Bikaner, CAZRI at Jodhpur and the Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research at Sewar, Bharatpur.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Agricultural produce)   List-II (Associated centre in Rajasthan)
A. Coriander   1. Bassi
B. Olive oil refinery   2. Sagra-Bhojka
C. Opium   3. Ramganj Mandi
D. Date palm Centre of Excellence   4. Chittorgarh
questions.exp: Ramganj Mandi (Kota) is Asia's largest coriander market, India's first olive oil refinery is at Bassi (Jaipur), opium is licensed in Chittorgarh, and the date palm Centre of Excellence is at Sagra-Bhojka in Jaisalmer.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (University)   List-II (Headquarters)
A. Swami Keshwanand Rajasthan Agricultural University   1. Udaipur
B. Maharana Pratap University of Agriculture and Technology  2. Jobner
C. Sri Karan Narendra Agriculture University  3. Bikaner
D. Agriculture University  4. Kota
questions.exp: SKRAU is at Bikaner, MPUAT at Udaipur, SKNAU at Jobner in Jaipur district, and a separate Agriculture University functions at Kota. RAJUVAS, the veterinary university, is also at Bikaner.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Horticultural produce)   List-II (District)
A. Kinnow   1. Jodhpur
B. Orange   2. Sriganganagar
C. Red chilli 3. Pali
D. Henna    4. Jhalawar
questions.exp: Kinnow is grown in Sriganganagar, orange in Jhalawar, Mathania red chilli in Jodhpur and henna at Sojat in Pali.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of crop and leading district of Rajasthan is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Cotton in Rajasthan is concentrated in the canal-irrigated north-west, led by Hanumangarh and Sriganganagar, not Udaipur.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a kharif crop of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Barley is a rabi crop sown in October-November. Moth, guar and sesame are kharif crops sown with the monsoon.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of institution and location is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Central Arid Zone Research Institute - Jodhpur
National Research Centre on Camel - Bikaner
National Research Centre on Seed Spices - Jaipur
Central Sheep and Wool Research Institute - Avikanagar
questions.exp: The National Research Centre on Seed Spices is at Tabiji, Ajmer, not Jaipur. The other three pairs are correct.

questions.q: Rajasthan is the largest producer in India of all the following EXCEPT:
questions.exp: Rajasthan ranks third in soybean, after Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra. It is the largest producer of bajra, guar and moth bean.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a rabi crop grown in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Moth bean is a kharif pulse of the arid districts. Taramira, isabgol and gram are rabi crops.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of variety and crop is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Mahi Kanchan is a maize variety, not a bajra variety. RCB 911 is a bajra hybrid.

questions.q:
Arrange the following institutions of Rajasthan in the correct chronological order of their establishment, beginning with the earliest:
I. National Research Centre on Seed Spices, Ajmer
II. Central Arid Zone Research Institute, Jodhpur
III. National Research Centre on Camel, Bikaner
IV. Central Sheep and Wool Research Institute, Avikanagar
questions.exp: CAZRI Jodhpur (1959), CSWRI Avikanagar (1962), NRC on Camel Bikaner (1984) and NRC on Seed Spices Ajmer (2000).

questions.q:
Arrange the following universities of Rajasthan in the correct chronological order of their establishment, beginning with the earliest:
I. Maharana Pratap University of Agriculture and Technology, Udaipur
II. Rajasthan Agricultural University, Bikaner
III. Agriculture University, Kota
IV. Rajasthan University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences, Bikaner
questions.exp: Rajasthan Agricultural University Bikaner (1987), MPUAT Udaipur (1999), RAJUVAS Bikaner (2010) and Agriculture University Kota (2013).

chapters.title: Livestock, Dairy and Fisheries of Rajasthan
factsheet: 20th Livestock Census (2019): Rajasthan 568 lakh livestock — 2nd in India after Uttar Pradesh; about 10.6% of the national herd; density about 166 animals per sq km.
Species share (20th Census): goat 36.7% > cattle 24.5% > buffalo 24.1% > sheep 13.9%.
Rajasthan's all-India ranks (20th Census): 1st in goat, camel and donkey; 2nd in buffalo; 4th in sheep; 6th in cattle; 17th in poultry.
Camel population fell about 35% between the 19th (2012) and 20th (2019) censuses to about 2.13 lakh — still roughly 85% of India's camels.
Rajasthan is India's largest wool producer, contributing about 48% of national output (47.85%, Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics 2025); Bikaner has Asia's largest wool market.
Cattle — Rathi (Bikaner, Sri Ganganagar, Hanumangarh, Jaisalmer): best milch breed of the state, called the 'Kamdhenu of Rajasthan'.
Tharparkar (Jodhpur, Jaisalmer, Barmer): dual-purpose; also called Thari, Malani or White Sindhi.
Nagauri (Nagaur): premier draught breed. Kankrej (Barmer, Jalore, Sirohi): also called Wadad/Wadhiar, famous for its 'sawai chaal' gait.

Gir (origin Gir forests, Saurashtra; in Rajasthan Ajmer, Bhilwara, Chittorgarh) also called Renderi/Ajmeri; Mewati or Kosi (Alwar, Bharatpur); Malvi (Jhalawar, Kota, Baran); Hariana (Sikar, Jhunjhunu, Alwar).

Buffalo — Rajasthan has no indigenous buffalo breed. Murrah (highest milk yield, 'black gold') in Alwar-Bharatpur-Shekhawati; Surti in Udaipur-Banswara; Bhadawari (highest milk fat, up to about 13%) in eastern Rajasthan; Jafarabadi is India's heaviest buffalo.
Sheep — Chokla (Churu, Jhunjhunu, Sikar): finest carpet wool in India; called the 'Jewel of Rajasthan' and the 'Indian Merino'.
Magra, also called Bikaneri (Bikaner, Nagaur, Jaisalmer, Churu): the only lustrous white carpet-wool breed of the region.
Marwari sheep (Jodhpur, Pali, Barmer, Jalore, Nagaur): black face, small tubular ears; the most numerous sheep breed of Rajasthan.
Nali (Sri Ganganagar, Hanumangarh, Churu, Jhunjhunu): densest and heaviest fleece of Rajasthan's breeds. Pugal (Bikaner-Jaisalmer border): black face with brown stripes above the eyes.

Jaisalmeri (Jaisalmer, Barmer, Jodhpur): largest-bodied sheep breed, Roman nose. Malpura (Jaipur, Tonk, Sawai Madhopur). Sonadi or Chanothar (Udaipur, Dungarpur, Chittorgarh): large drooping ears, also milked.
Goat — Sirohi (Sirohi, Pali, Ajmer): leading meat breed; Jakhrana (Jakhrana village, Behror, Alwar): highest milk-yielding goat of Rajasthan.
Marwari goat (Jodhpur, Barmer, Jaisalmer, Pali): black, long-haired. Barbari (Alwar, Bharatpur, Dholpur): small, stall-fed. Jamunapari (Chambal ravines of Dholpur-Karauli): tallest Indian goat breed.
Camel — declared the state animal of Rajasthan on 30 June 2014; the Rajasthan Camel (Prohibition of Slaughter and Regulation of Temporary Migration or Export) Act, 2015 protects it.
Camel breeds: Bikaneri (heavy draught/load), Jaisalmeri and Nachna (fast riding breeds), Gomat (Jaisalmer-Jodhpur), Mewari (Udaipur-Rajsamand, best milker), Kachchhi (Barmer-Jalore).
Horses — Marwari (inward-curving ear tips), Malani (Barmer), Kathiawari (Jalore-Barmer); the Equine Production Campus of NRC on Equines is at Bikaner.

Institutions — RAJUVAS, Bikaner (veterinary university, 2010); National Research Centre on Camel, Jorbeed, Bikaner (1984); Central Sheep and Wool Research Institute, Avikanagar (Malpura, Tonk district, 1962); Central Wool Development Board headquarters, Jodhpur.
Bikaner hosts Asia's largest wool market; Bikaner and Jodhpur are the state's main wool-scouring and pressing centres.
Dairy — Rajasthan Co-operative Dairy Federation (RCDF) set up in 1977, headquarters Jaipur, markets milk under the brand SARAS.

RCDF follows the three-tier Anand (Amul) pattern: village dairy co-operative society, district milk producers' union, state federation; NDDB Anand and Operation Flood (Verghese Kurien) are the parent model.

Fisheries — Rajasthan is landlocked, so only inland fisheries exist; Chambal-basin reservoirs (Rana Pratap Sagar, Jawahar Sagar, Kota Barrage), Mahi Bajaj Sagar and Jaisamand are the main fishery waters; PMMSY (2020) is the central umbrella scheme.

Schemes — Bhamashah Pashu Bima Yojana, Avika Kavach (sheep insurance), Mangla Pashu Bima Yojana (announced 2024-25, free livestock insurance), Gopal Credit Card (2024-25); central Rashtriya Gokul Mission (2014) and National Livestock Mission.
Livestock fairs — Pushkar (Ajmer) camel fair, Ramdeoji cattle fair Nagaur, Mallinath fair Tilwara (Barmer) famous for horses, Gogamedi (Hanumangarh) and Baldev pashu mela Merta (Nagaur).

questions.q: As per the 20th Livestock Census (2019), what is Rajasthan's rank in India in total livestock population?
questions.exp: Rajasthan had about 568 lakh livestock in the 20th Livestock Census (2019), second only to Uttar Pradesh. This is roughly 10.6% of India's livestock.

questions.q: Which species accounts for the largest share of Rajasthan's livestock as per the 20th Livestock Census (2019)?
questions.exp: Goats made up about 36.7% of Rajasthan's livestock, ahead of cattle (24.5%) and buffalo (24.1%). Rajasthan also has the largest goat population of any Indian state.

questions.q: As per the 20th Livestock Census (2019), Rajasthan ranks FIRST in India in the population of which of the following?
questions.exp: Rajasthan holds the country's largest camel population (about 2.13 lakh, roughly 85% of India's camels). In the same census it ranked 4th in sheep, 6th in cattle and 17th in poultry.

questions.q: Rajasthan's rank in India in wool production is:
questions.exp: Rajasthan is India's largest wool producer, contributing about 48% of national output (47.85% as per Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics 2025); Jammu & Kashmir is a distant second. Bikaner has Asia's largest wool market.

questions.q: In milk production Rajasthan stands at which position among Indian states?
questions.exp: Rajasthan is the second largest milk producing state in India after Uttar Pradesh, as reported in the Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics. It is first in goat milk production.

questions.q: Which cattle breed of Rajasthan is popularly called the 'Kamdhenu of Rajasthan'?
questions.exp: The Rathi, whose home tract is Bikaner, Sri Ganganagar, Hanumangarh and Jaisalmer, is the state's best milch breed and is named after the Rath community.

questions.q: The Nagauri breed of cattle is chiefly valued for:
questions.exp: The Nagauri, from Nagaur district, is a premier draught breed used for ploughing and cart work; it is a poor milker.

questions.q: The cattle breed of Rajasthan also known as 'Wadad' or 'Wadhiar' is:
questions.exp: Kankrej, found in Barmer, Jalore and Sirohi, is locally called Wadad, Waged or Wadhiar and is famous for its 'sawai chaal' walking gait. It is a dual-purpose breed.

questions.q: Which is the highest milk-yielding buffalo breed reared in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Murrah, of Haryana origin and reared mainly in Alwar, Bharatpur and the Shekhawati belt, is India's highest milk-yielding buffalo breed and is nicknamed 'black gold'.

questions.q: The buffalo breed known for the highest fat content in its milk is:
questions.exp: Bhadawari buffalo milk carries the highest fat percentage (up to about 13%). In Rajasthan it is kept in the eastern districts such as Dholpur and Karauli.

questions.q: Which sheep breed of Rajasthan produces the finest carpet wool in India and is called the 'Jewel of Rajasthan'?
questions.exp: Chokla, whose home tract is Churu, Jhunjhunu and Sikar, yields the finest carpet-grade wool in the country and is also called the 'Indian Merino'.

questions.q: The Magra breed of sheep, noted for its extremely white and lustrous fleece, belongs primarily to which district?
questions.exp: Magra, also called Bikaneri, is centred on the eastern and southern parts of Bikaner district and extends into Nagaur, Jaisalmer and Churu. It is the only lustrous carpet-wool breed of the region.

questions.q: Which is the largest-bodied sheep breed of Rajasthan, marked by a Roman nose and long drooping ears?
questions.exp: Jaisalmeri sheep, found in Jaisalmer, western Barmer and Jodhpur, are the tallest and heaviest of the state's sheep breeds and give medium carpet-quality wool.

questions.q: The sheep breed of Rajasthan yielding the densest and heaviest fleece is:
questions.exp: Nali sheep of Sri Ganganagar, Hanumangarh, Churu and Jhunjhunu have a dense, long-stapled coarse fleece, the heaviest among Rajasthan's breeds.

questions.q: Which goat breed, named after a village in Alwar district, is the highest milk-yielding goat of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Jakhrana, named after Jakhrana village near Behror in Alwar district, is the state's best dairy goat. It is black with white spots on the ears and muzzle.

questions.q: The Sirohi breed of goat is primarily reared in which group of districts?
questions.exp: Sirohi goats, brown with white patches, are concentrated in Sirohi, Pali, Ajmer and adjoining Udaipur. It is Rajasthan's leading meat goat and is widely used for upgrading elsewhere in India.

questions.q: In which year was the camel declared the state animal of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The camel was notified as Rajasthan's state animal on 30 June 2014, followed by the Rajasthan Camel (Prohibition of Slaughter and Regulation of Temporary Migration or Export) Act, 2015.

questions.q: The Nachna breed of camel, prized as a fast riding camel, belongs to which district?
questions.exp: Nachna, named after the Nachna area of Jaisalmer, is a light, swift riding breed, as is the Jaisalmeri. Bikaneri camels, by contrast, are heavy draught animals.

questions.q: The National Research Centre on Camel is located at:
questions.exp: The National Research Centre on Camel was set up in 1984 at Jorbeed, Bikaner. Bikaner also houses the Central Institute for Arid Horticulture and RAJUVAS.

questions.q: Avikanagar, the seat of the Central Sheep and Wool Research Institute, lies in which district of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The Central Sheep and Wool Research Institute (1962) is at Avikanagar in Malpura tehsil of Tonk district, within the home tract of the Malpura sheep.

questions.q: The Rajasthan University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences (RAJUVAS) is located at:
questions.exp: RAJUVAS was established at Bikaner in 2010. Rajasthan's first veterinary college was also founded at Bikaner.

questions.q: The headquarters of the Central Wool Development Board is situated at:
questions.exp: The Central Wool Development Board, under the Union Ministry of Textiles, has its headquarters at Jodhpur. Bikaner, however, hosts Asia's largest wool market.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajasthan Co-operative Dairy Federation:
I. It was set up in 1977.
II. It markets milk and milk products under the brand name SARAS.
III. It follows the three-tier Anand pattern of co-operative organisation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: RCDF, headquartered at Jaipur, was set up in 1977, sells under the SARAS brand and works on the three-tier Anand (Amul) pattern of village society, district union and state federation.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Chokla sheep:
I. Its home tract lies in Churu, Jhunjhunu and Sikar districts.
II. It yields the finest carpet-quality wool among Indian sheep breeds.
III. It is also known as the Indian Merino.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Chokla is a light, reddish-brown-faced, polled breed of the Shekhawati tract whose dense fine fleece has earned it the names 'Jewel of Rajasthan' and 'Indian Merino'.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about camels in Rajasthan:
I. Rajasthan has the largest camel population among Indian states.
II. The camel population of Rajasthan increased between the 19th and 20th Livestock Censuses.
III. The Mewari camel is valued mainly for milk.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and III are correct. Statement II is wrong: the camel population fell by about 35% between the 19th (2012) and 20th (2019) censuses, which is why the state animal has been given legal protection.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Tharparkar cattle:
I. It is a purely draught breed with negligible milk yield.
II. Its home tract in Rajasthan lies in Jodhpur, Jaisalmer and Barmer.
III. It is also known as Thari or White Sindhi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements II and III are correct. Tharparkar is a dual-purpose breed valued for both milk and draught, so statement I is wrong; the true draught specialist of Rajasthan is the Nagauri.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Marwari sheep:
I. It is distinguished by a black face and very small tubular ears.
II. Its home tract includes Jodhpur, Pali, Barmer, Jalore and Nagaur.
III. It is the most numerous sheep breed of Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. The hardy Marwari, adapted to the arid Marwar tract, carries a white, non-dense fleece and is the state's most widely distributed sheep breed.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about fisheries in Rajasthan:
I. Being a landlocked state, Rajasthan has only inland fisheries.
II. Reservoirs of the Chambal basin are among the state's principal fishery waters.
III. The Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana is the central umbrella scheme for fisheries development.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Rajasthan has no coastline, so its fish output comes from reservoirs and tanks such as Rana Pratap Sagar, Jawahar Sagar, Kota Barrage, Mahi Bajaj Sagar and Jaisamand. PMMSY was launched in 2020.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about goats in Rajasthan:
I. Rajasthan has the largest goat population among Indian states.
II. The Jamunapari is the tallest goat breed found in India.
III. The Barbari goat is a large-bodied breed of the western desert.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Statement III is wrong: the Barbari is a small, stall-fed goat of the eastern districts such as Alwar, Bharatpur and Dholpur.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements based on the 20th Livestock Census (2019) for Rajasthan:
I. Goats form the single largest species group in the state's livestock.
II. Rajasthan ranks second in India in buffalo population.
III. Rajasthan ranks first in India in cattle population.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Rajasthan ranked sixth, not first, in cattle population in the 20th Livestock Census; goats accounted for about 36.7% of its livestock.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Cattle breed)   List-II (Home tract)
A. Rathi   1. Nagaur
B. Nagauri   2. Bikaner and Sri Ganganagar
C. Mewati   3. Barmer and Jalore
D. Kankrej   4. Alwar and Bharatpur
questions.exp: Rathi belongs to the Bikaner-Sri Ganganagar belt, Nagauri to Nagaur, Mewati (Kosi) to the Mewat tract of Alwar-Bharatpur and Kankrej to Barmer-Jalore-Sirohi.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Sheep breed)   List-II (Home tract)
