A. Chokla   1. Udaipur and Dungarpur
B. Magra   2. Churu, Jhunjhunu and Sikar
C. Sonadi   3. Jaipur, Tonk and Sawai Madhopur
D. Malpura   4. Bikaner
questions.exp: Chokla is the Shekhawati breed, Magra is the Bikaneri breed, Sonadi (Chanothar) belongs to the southern districts and Malpura to the Jaipur-Tonk tract where CSWRI Avikanagar is located.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Goat breed)   List-II (Speciality or tract)
A. Jakhrana   1. Leading meat breed of southern Rajasthan
B. Sirohi   2. Highest milk yield, Alwar district
C. Barbari   3. Black, long-haired goat of the Marwar desert
D. Marwari   4. Small stall-fed goat of eastern Rajasthan
questions.exp: Jakhrana of Alwar is the best dairy goat of the state, Sirohi the leading meat breed, Barbari a small stall-fed eastern breed and Marwari the black long-haired goat of the desert districts.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Camel breed)   List-II (Principal tract)
A. Bikaneri   1. Udaipur and Rajsamand
B. Nachna   2. Bikaner
C. Mewari   3. Barmer and Jalore
D. Kachchhi   4. Jaisalmer
questions.exp: Bikaneri is the heavy draught camel of Bikaner, Nachna the swift riding camel of Jaisalmer, Mewari the hill camel of the Mewar districts and best milker, and Kachchhi is reared in Barmer-Jalore.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Institution)   List-II (Location)
A. Central Sheep and Wool Research Institute   1. Jodhpur
B. National Research Centre on Camel   2. Jaipur
C. Central Wool Development Board   3. Avikanagar (Tonk)
D. Rajasthan Co-operative Dairy Federation headquarters   4. Bikaner
questions.exp: CSWRI is at Avikanagar in Tonk district, NRC on Camel at Jorbeed in Bikaner, the Central Wool Development Board at Jodhpur and RCDF at Jaipur.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a sheep breed of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Jakhrana is a goat breed of Alwar district, not a sheep breed. Pugal, Sonadi and Malpura are all recognised sheep breeds of Rajasthan.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of buffalo breed and its place of origin is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Bhadawari - Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh
questions.exp: Jafarabadi originates in the Gir forest region of Saurashtra in Gujarat, not Punjab. It is India's heaviest buffalo breed.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of cattle breed and district is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The Gir, originally of the Gir forests of Saurashtra, is reared in Rajasthan mainly in Ajmer, Bhilwara, Chittorgarh and the Hadoti area, not in Hanumangarh.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about animal husbandry in Rajasthan is NOT correct?
opts: Rajasthan is the largest wool producing state of India
Bikaner has Asia's largest wool market
Rajasthan has its own indigenous buffalo breed named Murrah
The camel is the state animal of Rajasthan
questions.exp: Rajasthan has no indigenous buffalo breed; Murrah is a Haryana breed widely reared in eastern Rajasthan. The other three statements are correct.

questions.q:
Arrange the following species in the descending order of their share in Rajasthan's livestock as per the 20th Livestock Census (2019):
I. Buffalo
II. Goat
III. Sheep
IV. Cattle
questions.exp: The order is goat (about 36.7%), cattle (24.5%), buffalo (24.1%) and sheep (13.9%).

chapters.title: Irrigation Projects and Canal Systems of Rajasthan
factsheet: IGNP was conceived by Kanwar Sen, Chief Engineer of Bikaner, on 29 October 1948; originally called the Rajasthan Canal Project and renamed Indira Gandhi Nahar Pariyojana in 1984.
Foundation stone of the Rajasthan Canal was laid on 31 March 1958 by Union Home Minister Govind Ballabh Pant.
IGNP draws water from the Harike Barrage at the Sutlej-Beas confluence in Ferozepur district, Punjab.
Rajasthan Feeder 204 km (about 170 km in Punjab-Haryana and 35 km in Rajasthan) plus the Indira Gandhi Main Canal 445 km gives a total of about 649 km.

Stage-I main canal is 189 km, commanding Sri Ganganagar, Hanumangarh and northern Bikaner; Stage-II runs the remaining 256 km up to Mohangarh in Jaisalmer, commanding Bikaner, Jodhpur, Jaisalmer, Barmer, Churu and Nagaur.
Gravity branches of IGNP leave the right bank (Rawatsar branch is the exception on the left bank); all seven lift canals take off from the left bank.
Kanwar Sen Lift Canal (old name Lunkaransar Lift), head at Gharsana — benefits Sri Ganganagar and Bikaner.
Pannalal Barupal Lift Canal (old Gajner Lift) — Bikaner and Nagaur; Veer Tejaji Lift Canal (old Bangarsar Lift) — Bikaner.
Chaudhary Kumbha Ram Lift Canal (old Gandheli-Sahwa Lift) — Hanumangarh, Churu, Jhunjhunu and Bikaner; the main drinking-water lifeline of Churu and Jhunjhunu.

Dr. Karni Singh Lift Canal (old Kolayat Lift) — Bikaner and Jodhpur; Guru Jambheshwar Lift Canal (old Phalodi Lift) — Jodhpur, Jaisalmer, Bikaner; Jai Narayan Vyas Lift Canal (old Pokaran Lift) — Jaisalmer and Jodhpur.
Rajiv Gandhi Lift Canal carries IGNP water for drinking to Jodhpur city; waterlogging and salinity ('sem') in the Stage-I command of Sri Ganganagar-Hanumangarh is IGNP's principal criticism.

Gang Canal is Rajasthan's oldest canal — built by Maharaja Ganga Singh of Bikaner after the Chhappaniya famine, opened 26 October 1927; about 129 km long with only 17 km in Rajasthan; draws Sutlej water at the Ferozepur (Hussainiwala) headworks and irrigates Sri Ganganagar.

Bhakra-Nangal is on the Sutlej at Bhakra (Bilaspur, Himachal Pradesh); its reservoir is Gobind Sagar; a joint Punjab-Haryana-Rajasthan project in which Rajasthan's share is about 15.2%; it irrigates Hanumangarh and Sri Ganganagar.

Chambal Valley Project is a 50:50 Rajasthan-Madhya Pradesh venture; upstream to downstream the structures are Gandhi Sagar (Mandsaur, MP), Rana Pratap Sagar (Rawatbhata, Chittorgarh), Jawahar Sagar (Kota) and Kota Barrage.
Kota Barrage generates no power; it only diverts water into the Right and Left Main Canals which irrigate Kota, Bundi, Baran, Sawai Madhopur and Tonk.
Bisalpur dam is on the Banas at Bisalpur village, Todaraisingh tehsil, Tonk district — the state's biggest drinking-water project, supplying Jaipur, Ajmer, Tonk, Beawar, Kishangarh and Nasirabad.

Jawai dam is on the Jawai, a tributary of the Luni, at Sumerpur in Pali district — the largest dam of western Rajasthan and the 'lifeline of Marwar'; begun by Maharaja Umaid Singh in 1946 and completed in 1957; benefits Pali and Jalore.

Mahi Bajaj Sagar is on the Mahi at Borkheda in Banswara district — a joint Rajasthan-Gujarat project and the longest dam of Rajasthan (about 3.1 km); benefits Banswara and Dungarpur, with the Kagdi pick-up weir feeding its canals.
Parwan Vrihad Pariyojana is on the Parwan, a tributary of the Kali Sindh, in Jhalawar district and benefits Jhalawar, Baran and Kota.

Narmada Canal: Rajasthan is the tail-end beneficiary of the Sardar Sarovar; 74 km of the canal lies in Rajasthan (532 km with Gujarat's stretch), entering near Sanchore in Jalore and irrigating Jalore and Barmer; it is India's first canal command with 100% sprinkler and drip irrigation.
Sidhmukh-Nohar project uses Ravi-Beas water and benefits Hanumangarh (Nohar, Bhadra) and Churu (Sidhmukh, Taranagar); it was assisted by the European Union and later NABARD.

Yamuna water: the 1994 MoU among Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, Himachal Pradesh and Delhi governs Rajasthan's share; the Gurgaon Canal serves Bharatpur, and a 2024 Haryana-Rajasthan MoU covers Yamuna water for Churu, Sikar and Jhunjhunu.

ERCP became PKC-ERCP after the tripartite MoU of 28 January 2024 among the Centre, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh, and was renamed the Ram Jal Setu Link Project on 22 January 2025; it had been given national-project status in December 2022.

Ram Jal Setu (PKC-ERCP) transfers surplus monsoon flows of the Chambal and its tributaries Parvati, Kali Sindh, Mej and Chakan to the deficit Banas, Banganga, Gambhiri and Parbati sub-basins, serving 17 eastern districts and about 40% of Rajasthan's population.

Other dams: Jakham (Pratapgarh, highest dam of Rajasthan at about 81 m), Panchana (Karauli, biggest earthen dam, built at the confluence of five rivers), Som-Kamla-Amba (Dungarpur), Meja (Bhilwara, on the Kothari), Morel (Sawai Madhopur), Gudha (Bundi, on the Mej), Chhapi (Jhalawar), Orai (Chittorgarh), Sardar Samand (Pali), Bandh Baretha (Bharatpur, on the Kakund) and Isarda (Tonk-Sawai Madhopur, on the Banas).

Wells and tube-wells irrigate the largest share of Rajasthan's net irrigated area; canals rank second and are concentrated in the Sri Ganganagar-Hanumangarh belt. The Chambal is the state's only perennial river.
Khadin (Jaisalmer) — developed by Paliwal Brahmins in the 15th century; an earthen bund across the lower slope of a rocky catchment on which crops are raised on residual moisture; also called Dhora.

Tanka — a covered underground tank in a house courtyard for drinking water (Bikaner, Barmer, Jaisalmer, Churu). Kund or Kundi — a circular covered underground well whose saucer-shaped catchment is called the agor.

Nadi (village pond), Toba (natural depression with a catchment in the Thar), Kui or Beri (narrow deep seepage pit dug beside a paar or tank), Paar (percolation area tapped through kuis), Jhalara (rectangular stepped tank fed by seepage, used for community bathing — Jodhpur, Udaipur), Baori (stepwell; Chand Baori at Abhaneri in Dausa, Bundi the city of stepwells).

Johad — earthen check dam of the Alwar region, revived by Rajendra Singh and Tarun Bharat Sangh (Arvari river); Bandha (embankment, Alwar-Bharatpur); Chauka system of Laporiya village, Dudu, Jaipur; Naada and Saza Kuva of southern Rajasthan. Mukhyamantri Jal Swavlamban Abhiyan was launched on 27 January 2016 at Nimbi Jodha (Nagaur); Jal Jeevan Mission began on 15 August 2019.

questions.q: The Indira Gandhi Nahar Pariyojana was originally conceived in 1948 by:
questions.exp: Kanwar Sen, then Chief Engineer of Bikaner state, conceived the scheme on 29 October 1948. It was first called the Rajasthan Canal Project and renamed after Indira Gandhi in 1984.

questions.q: The Indira Gandhi Canal takes off from which of the following?
opts: Harike Barrage at the Sutlej-Beas confluence
questions.exp: IGNP draws its water from the Harike Barrage, built at the confluence of the Sutlej and the Beas in Ferozepur district of Punjab.

questions.q: The length of the Rajasthan Feeder canal of the Indira Gandhi Nahar Pariyojana is about:
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Feeder is about 204 km long, of which roughly 170 km lies in Punjab and Haryana and about 35 km in Rajasthan. The Indira Gandhi Main Canal that follows it is 445 km long.

questions.q: The total length of the Indira Gandhi Main Canal is:
questions.exp: The Indira Gandhi Main Canal is 445 km long and lies entirely in Rajasthan. Adding the 204 km Rajasthan Feeder gives a total main course of about 649 km.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Canal Project was renamed the Indira Gandhi Nahar Pariyojana in the year:
questions.exp: The project was renamed in 1984 in memory of Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. Its foundation stone had been laid in 1958.

questions.q: The foundation stone of the Rajasthan Canal was laid on 31 March 1958 by:
questions.exp: Union Home Minister Govind Ballabh Pant laid the foundation stone of the Rajasthan Canal on 31 March 1958.

questions.q: The Indira Gandhi Main Canal terminates at:
questions.exp: The main canal of Stage-II ends at Mohangarh in Jaisalmer district; a further extension towards Gadra Road in Barmer has long been proposed.

questions.q: The Kanwar Sen Lift Canal of the Indira Gandhi Nahar Pariyojana was earlier known as:
questions.exp: The Kanwar Sen Lift Canal, named after IGNP's originator and headed at Gharsana, was formerly the Lunkaransar Lift Canal. It benefits Sri Ganganagar and Bikaner districts.

questions.q: The Chaudhary Kumbha Ram Lift Canal, earlier called the Gandheli-Sahwa Lift Canal, principally supplies drinking water to which districts?
questions.exp: The Chaudhary Kumbha Ram Lift Canal carries IGNP water to Hanumangarh, Churu, Jhunjhunu and Bikaner, and is the drinking-water lifeline of the Churu-Jhunjhunu belt.

questions.q: The Pannalal Barupal Lift Canal was formerly known as the:
questions.exp: The Pannalal Barupal Lift Canal is the renamed Gajner Lift Canal and serves Bikaner and Nagaur districts.

questions.q: The Jai Narayan Vyas Lift Canal of IGNP was earlier called the:
questions.exp: The Jai Narayan Vyas Lift Canal is the renamed Pokaran Lift Canal, benefiting Jaisalmer and Jodhpur districts.

questions.q: Which lift canal carries Indira Gandhi Canal water for drinking purposes to Jodhpur city?
questions.exp: The Rajiv Gandhi Lift Canal was built specifically to carry IGNP water to Jodhpur city for drinking supply.

questions.q: The oldest canal irrigation project of Rajasthan is:
questions.exp: The Gang Canal, opened on 26 October 1927, is Rajasthan's oldest canal. It was built by Maharaja Ganga Singh of Bikaner after the Chhappaniya famine of 1899-1900.

questions.q: The Gang Canal principally irrigates which district of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The Gang Canal draws Sutlej water at the Ferozepur headworks and irrigates Sri Ganganagar district, which owes its agricultural prosperity to it.

questions.q: The reservoir created by the Bhakra Dam on the Sutlej is called:
questions.exp: The Bhakra Dam in Bilaspur district of Himachal Pradesh impounds Gobind Sagar. Rajasthan, with a share of about 15.2% in the Bhakra-Nangal project, uses the water in Hanumangarh and Sri Ganganagar.

questions.q: Which is the uppermost (most upstream) dam of the Chambal Valley Project?
questions.exp: Gandhi Sagar, in Mandsaur district of Madhya Pradesh, is the first and largest reservoir of the Chambal Valley Project, followed downstream by Rana Pratap Sagar, Jawahar Sagar and Kota Barrage.

questions.q: The Rana Pratap Sagar dam is situated at Rawatbhata in which district?
questions.exp: Rana Pratap Sagar was built on the Chambal at Rawatbhata in Chittorgarh district; the Rajasthan Atomic Power Station stands at the same site.

questions.q: Which structure of the Chambal Valley Project does NOT generate hydroelectric power and serves only to divert water into canals?
questions.exp: Kota Barrage, the last structure of the series, has no power house. It diverts water into the Right and Left Main Canals which irrigate Kota, Bundi, Baran, Sawai Madhopur and Tonk.

questions.q: The Bisalpur dam is constructed on which river?
questions.exp: Bisalpur dam stands on the Banas river at Bisalpur village in Todaraisingh tehsil of Tonk district and is the state's largest drinking-water project, supplying Jaipur, Ajmer and Tonk.

questions.q: The Jawai dam, called the 'lifeline of Marwar', is located in which district?
questions.exp: Jawai dam was built on the Jawai, a tributary of the Luni, at Sumerpur in Pali district. It is the largest dam of western Rajasthan and benefits Pali and Jalore.

questions.q: The Mahi Bajaj Sagar project is a joint venture of Rajasthan with which state?
questions.exp: Mahi Bajaj Sagar, built on the Mahi at Borkheda in Banswara district, is a joint Rajasthan-Gujarat project. It is the longest dam of Rajasthan and benefits Banswara and Dungarpur.

questions.q: The Parwan Vrihad Pariyojana is designed to benefit which group of districts?
questions.exp: The Parwan project on the Parwan river, a tributary of the Kali Sindh, is located in Jhalawar district and provides irrigation and drinking water to Jhalawar, Baran and Kota.

questions.q: Narmada canal water reaches Rajasthan and irrigates which pair of districts?
questions.exp: Rajasthan is the tail-end beneficiary of the Sardar Sarovar project; the Narmada Canal enters near Sanchore in Jalore and irrigates Jalore and Barmer districts. About 74 km of the canal lies in Rajasthan.

questions.q: The Narmada Canal command in Rajasthan is notable for being the first in India where:
opts: Water is supplied entirely by lift
Sprinkler and drip irrigation are 100% compulsory
The canal is fully lined with concrete
Irrigation is charged on a volumetric basis
questions.exp: Micro-irrigation, that is sprinkler and drip, was made mandatory over the entire Narmada Canal command in Rajasthan, a first for any canal command in the country.

questions.q: The Sidhmukh-Nohar irrigation project benefits which districts of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The Sidhmukh-Nohar project uses Ravi-Beas water to irrigate the Nohar and Bhadra areas of Hanumangarh and the Sidhmukh and Taranagar areas of Churu. It received European Union and later NABARD assistance.

questions.q: The Eastern Rajasthan Canal Project, integrated with the Parvati-Kalisindh-Chambal link, was renamed as:
questions.exp: The PKC-ERCP was renamed the Ram Jal Setu Link Project by the Rajasthan government on 22 January 2025. As of September 2026 the project is under implementation under this name.

questions.q: The Jakham dam, the highest dam of Rajasthan, is located in which district?
questions.exp: The Jakham dam near Anuppura in Pratapgarh district (formerly part of Udaipur district) stands about 81 metres high, the tallest in Rajasthan. It is built on the Jakham, a tributary of the Som.

questions.q: The khadin system of water harvesting was developed by which community?
questions.exp: Khadins, also called dhoras, were developed by the Paliwal Brahmins of Jaisalmer in the 15th century. An earthen bund across the lower slope of a rocky catchment holds run-off, and crops are grown on the residual soil moisture.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indira Gandhi Nahar Pariyojana:
I. Stage-I of the main canal is 189 km long.
II. The command of Stage-I lies mainly in Sri Ganganagar, Hanumangarh and northern Bikaner.
III. Stage-II extends the canal up to Mohangarh in Jaisalmer district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Stage-I covers the first 189 km of the 445 km main canal, and the remaining 256 km of Stage-II reaches Mohangarh in Jaisalmer.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indira Gandhi Nahar Pariyojana:
I. Excessive seepage has caused waterlogging and salinity in parts of its Stage-I command.
II. All its lift canals take off from the left bank of the main canal.
III. The canal system has helped stabilise shifting sand dunes along its course.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. Waterlogging or 'sem' in Sri Ganganagar and Hanumangarh is IGNP's best-known ecological criticism, while afforestation along the canal has helped fix dunes.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Ram Jal Setu Link Project:
I. It was earlier known as the Eastern Rajasthan Canal Project.
II. A tripartite memorandum of understanding for it was signed in January 2024 by the Union government, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh.
III. It aims to serve the eastern districts of Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. As of September 2026 the project, formed by integrating ERCP with the Parvati-Kalisindh-Chambal link and renamed on 22 January 2025, is being executed for about 17 eastern districts holding roughly 40% of the state's population.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Bisalpur project:
I. It is built on the Banas river.
II. It lies in Sawai Madhopur district.
III. It supplies drinking water to Jaipur and Ajmer.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and III are correct. The dam is located at Bisalpur village in Todaraisingh tehsil of Tonk district, not Sawai Madhopur.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Chambal Valley Project:
I. It is a joint project of Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh on an equal-share basis.
II. Jawahar Sagar dam lies between Rana Pratap Sagar and Kota Barrage.
III. Gandhi Sagar dam is located in Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Gandhi Sagar lies in Mandsaur district of Madhya Pradesh, so statement III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about traditional water structures of Rajasthan:
I. A tanka is a covered underground tank built in a house courtyard to store rainwater for drinking.
II. The saucer-shaped catchment of a kund is called the agor.
III. A jhalara is a rectangular stepped tank fed by seepage and used for community bathing.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Tanka, kund and jhalara are distinct structures: the first two store rainwater for drinking, while jhalaras such as those of Jodhpur draw seepage from upstream tanks and serve religious and community use.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Mukhyamantri Jal Swavlamban Abhiyan was launched in January 2016.
II. The Jal Jeevan Mission was launched on 15 August 2019.
III. Wells and tube-wells account for the largest share of Rajasthan's net irrigated area.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. MJSA was launched on 27 January 2016 at Nimbi Jodha in Nagaur; the Jal Jeevan Mission was announced on 15 August 2019; and groundwater sources irrigate the bulk of Rajasthan's irrigated land, with canals second.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Gang Canal:
I. It was built during the reign of Maharaja Ganga Singh of Bikaner.
II. It draws water from the Sutlej river.
III. The greater part of its length lies in Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Of the canal's roughly 129 km, only about 17 km lies in Rajasthan and the rest in Punjab, so statement III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Mahi Bajaj Sagar project:
I. The dam is built on the Mahi river in Banswara district.
II. The Kagdi pick-up weir forms part of the project.
III. It benefits Banswara and Dungarpur districts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Mahi Bajaj Sagar at Borkheda in Banswara is the longest dam of Rajasthan, with the Kagdi pick-up weir downstream feeding its canal system in Banswara and Dungarpur.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Project)   List-II (River)
A. Bisalpur   1. Kothari
B. Meja   2. Banas
C. Jawai   3. Mahi
D. Bajaj Sagar   4. Luni tributary
questions.exp: Bisalpur is on the Banas, Meja on the Kothari in Bhilwara, Jawai on the Jawai which is a tributary of the Luni, and Bajaj Sagar on the Mahi in Banswara.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Irrigation project)   List-II (Chief beneficiary districts)
A. Jawai   1. Jhalawar, Baran and Kota
B. Parwan   2. Jalore and Barmer
C. Narmada Canal   3. Pali and Jalore
D. Som-Kamla-Amba   4. Dungarpur and Udaipur
questions.exp: Jawai serves Pali and Jalore, Parwan serves Jhalawar, Baran and Kota, the Narmada Canal serves Jalore and Barmer, and Som-Kamla-Amba serves the tribal belt of Dungarpur and Udaipur.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Present name of lift canal)   List-II (Former name)
A. Kanwar Sen Lift Canal   1. Kolayat Lift Canal
B. Pannalal Barupal Lift Canal   2. Gandheli-Sahwa Lift Canal
C. Dr. Karni Singh Lift Canal   3. Lunkaransar Lift Canal
D. Chaudhary Kumbha Ram Lift Canal   4. Gajner Lift Canal
questions.exp: Kanwar Sen was the Lunkaransar Lift, Pannalal Barupal the Gajner Lift, Dr. Karni Singh the Kolayat Lift and Chaudhary Kumbha Ram the Gandheli-Sahwa Lift.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Lift canal)   List-II (Districts benefited)
A. Guru Jambheshwar   1. Sri Ganganagar and Bikaner
B. Kanwar Sen   2. Jodhpur, Jaisalmer and Bikaner
C. Pannalal Barupal   3. Hanumangarh, Churu and Jhunjhunu
D. Chaudhary Kumbha Ram   4. Bikaner and Nagaur
questions.exp: Guru Jambheshwar (old Phalodi Lift) serves Jodhpur, Jaisalmer and Bikaner; Kanwar Sen serves Sri Ganganagar and Bikaner; Pannalal Barupal serves Bikaner and Nagaur; Chaudhary Kumbha Ram serves Hanumangarh, Churu and Jhunjhunu.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Water harvesting structure)   List-II (Description)
A. Khadin   1. Narrow deep pit dug to collect seepage water
B. Kui   2. Earthen bund across a rocky slope for crop raising
C. Toba   3. Earthen check dam of the Alwar region
D. Johad   4. Natural depression with a catchment in the Thar
questions.exp: Khadin traps run-off behind a bund for cropping, kui or beri is a narrow seepage pit, toba is a natural depression with its own catchment, and johad is the earthen check dam of Alwar revived by Rajendra Singh.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Dam)   List-II (District)
A. Panchana   1. Bundi
B. Gudha   2. Karauli
C. Bandh Baretha   3. Bharatpur
D. Sardar Samand   4. Pali
questions.exp: Panchana, the state's biggest earthen dam, is in Karauli; Gudha is on the Mej in Bundi; Bandh Baretha is on the Kakund in Bharatpur; and Sardar Samand lies in Pali.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of project and river is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The Orai dam in Chittorgarh is built on the Orai river; the Kothari river carries the Meja dam in Bhilwara district.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of lift canal and beneficiary district is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Jai Narayan Vyas Lift Canal - Jaisalmer
Dr. Karni Singh Lift Canal - Bikaner
questions.exp: The Kanwar Sen Lift Canal serves Sri Ganganagar and Bikaner in the north-west; Banswara lies in the southern Mahi basin and is entirely outside the IGNP command.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a component of the Chambal Valley Project?
questions.exp: Bisalpur is an independent project on the Banas in Tonk district. The Chambal Valley Project comprises Gandhi Sagar, Rana Pratap Sagar, Jawahar Sagar and Kota Barrage.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Indira Gandhi Nahar Pariyojana is NOT correct?
opts: It obtains its water from the Harike Barrage
Its entire command lies in the Chambal basin
Its main canal is 445 km long
It was originally known as the Rajasthan Canal Project
questions.exp: IGNP commands the north-western desert districts drained by no perennial river; the Chambal basin lies in south-eastern Rajasthan and is served by a separate project.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a traditional water harvesting structure of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Zing is a meltwater collection tank of Ladakh. Khadin, tanka and johad are all Rajasthani systems.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of dam and district is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The Isarda dam is being built on the Banas on the Tonk-Sawai Madhopur boundary to supply Dausa and Sawai Madhopur; it has no connection with Alwar.

questions.q:
Arrange the following structures of the Chambal Valley Project in order from upstream to downstream:
I. Jawahar Sagar
II. Gandhi Sagar
III. Kota Barrage
IV. Rana Pratap Sagar
questions.exp: Going downstream along the Chambal the order is Gandhi Sagar (Mandsaur, MP), Rana Pratap Sagar (Rawatbhata), Jawahar Sagar (Kota) and finally Kota Barrage.

chapters.title: Population, Urbanisation and Tribes of Rajasthan
factsheet: Census 2011: Rajasthan population 6,85,48,437 (6.85 crore) = 5.66% of India; 8th most populous state, 1st in area.
Decadal growth 2001-11: 21.31% (India 17.70%) — highest Barmer (32.5%), lowest Sri Ganganagar (about 10%).
Density 200 persons/sq km (India 382; Rajasthan was 165 in 2001) — highest Jaipur (595), lowest Jaisalmer (17).
Sex ratio 928 (India 943) — highest Dungarpur (994), then Rajsamand (990), Pali (987); lowest Dholpur (846), then Karauli/Jaisalmer.
Child sex ratio (0-6) 888 (India 919) — highest Banswara (934), lowest Jhunjhunu (837).
Literacy 66.11% (India 74.04%) — male 79.19%, female 52.12%; gender gap about 27 points, the widest among major states.
Literacy: highest district Kota (76.56%), lowest Jalore (54.86%); highest male literacy Jhunjhunu (86.9%), lowest male literacy Pratapgarh.
Female literacy: highest Kota (about 65.9%), lowest Jalore (about 38.5%).
Most populous district Jaipur (66.26 lakh), then Jodhpur (36.87 lakh) and Alwar (36.74 lakh); least populous Jaisalmer (6.69 lakh).
Largest district by area Jaisalmer (38,401 sq km); smallest Dholpur (about 3,034 sq km).
Urban population 24.89% (about 1.70 crore); rural 75.11% — Rajasthan is far less urbanised than India (31.16%).
Most urbanised district Kota (about 60.3%), then Jaipur (52.4%) and Ajmer (40.1%); least urbanised Dungarpur (about 6.4%), then Banswara and Pratapgarh.
Million-plus cities in Census 2011: Jaipur, Jodhpur and Kota (Jaipur is the only one above 30 lakh).
Scheduled Castes 17.83% (1.22 crore); Scheduled Tribes 13.48% (92.38 lakh) of the state population.
ST share: highest Banswara, second Dungarpur, then Pratapgarh and Udaipur; lowest Nagaur, then Bikaner.
ST absolute numbers: highest in Udaipur district; SC absolute numbers highest in Jaipur; SC share highest in Sri Ganganagar, lowest in Dungarpur.
Religion (2011): Hindu 88.49%, Muslim 9.07%, Sikh 1.27%, Jain 0.91%, Christian 0.14%.
Meena (Mina) is the most populous Scheduled Tribe of Rajasthan; Bhil second; Garasia third; Sahariya the smallest but most vulnerable.
Bhil — Banswara, Dungarpur, Udaipur, Pratapgarh; hamlet 'palli/phala'; shifting cultivation 'Chimata' (hill slope) and 'Dajiya' (plain); dance-drama Gavri.
Garasia — Sirohi (Abu Road, Pindwara), Udaipur (Kotra, Jhadol), Pali (Bali); shifting cultivation 'Walra'; marriages Mor-bandiya, Peharavani, Taanana; Gol-Gadheda fair.
Sahariya — the ONLY Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) of Rajasthan; Kishanganj and Shahbad tehsils of Baran district; headman 'Kotwal'.
Damor — Simalwara and Aspur (Dungarpur) and parts of Banswara; village/panchayat head called 'Mukhi'; Chadwa Tirth fair.
Kathodi — Kotra, Jhadol and Sarada (Udaipur); migrants from Maharashtra; prepare 'katha' (catechu) from khair wood.
Rabari/Raika — camel and sheep herders of Pali, Jodhpur, Nagaur and Sirohi; Gadia Lohar — nomadic blacksmiths tracing descent to Chittorgarh.
Kanjar and Sansi are denotified nomadic communities; Bhil-Mina, Dhanka, Naik, Patelia and Seharia are also notified STs of Rajasthan.
Tribal Area Development (TAD) department headquarters — Udaipur; Tribal Sub-Plan began in the Fifth Five Year Plan (1974-75); MADA covers scattered tribal pockets.
Rajasthan announced its State Population Policy in 2000; the state is a net out-migration state, chiefly to Gujarat, Maharashtra and Delhi.
After the December 2024 reorganisation Rajasthan has 41 districts in 7 divisions — Jaipur, Jodhpur, Ajmer, Kota, Bikaner, Bharatpur and Udaipur.
Work participation rate of Rajasthan in Census 2011 was above the all-India average; female work participation is high in western districts.
Rajasthan's population growth has decelerated: 28.41% (1991-2001) fell to 21.31% (2001-2011).

questions.q: As per Census 2011, Rajasthan's rank among Indian states in terms of population is:
questions.exp: Rajasthan had 6,85,48,437 persons in Census 2011, making it the 8th most populous state, while it is the largest state by area.

questions.q: The decadal growth rate of population of Rajasthan during 2001-2011, as per Census 2011, was:
questions.exp: Rajasthan grew 21.31% against the national 17.70%. 28.41% was Rajasthan's growth in the previous decade (1991-2001).

questions.q: As per Census 2011, the population density of Rajasthan is:
questions.exp: Rajasthan's density rose from 165 (2001) to 200 persons per sq km in 2011, well below the all-India figure of 382.

questions.q: The sex ratio of Rajasthan as per Census 2011 is:
questions.exp: Rajasthan's sex ratio is 928 females per 1000 males, below the all-India 943.

questions.q: As per Census 2011, the child sex ratio (0-6 years) of Rajasthan is:
questions.exp: Rajasthan's 0-6 child sex ratio was 888, against the all-India figure of 919.

questions.q: The overall literacy rate of Rajasthan as per Census 2011 is:
questions.exp: Rajasthan's literacy was 66.11% in 2011 (60.41% in 2001); the all-India figure was 74.04%.

questions.q: As per Census 2011, the female literacy rate of Rajasthan is:
questions.exp: Female literacy in Rajasthan was 52.12% against male literacy of 79.19% — a gap of about 27 percentage points, the widest among major states.

questions.q: Which district of Rajasthan recorded the highest sex ratio in Census 2011?
questions.exp: Dungarpur recorded 994 females per 1000 males, followed by Rajsamand (990) and Pali (987).

questions.q: As per Census 2011, the lowest sex ratio in Rajasthan was recorded in the district of:
questions.exp: Dholpur had the lowest sex ratio at 846 females per 1000 males; Jaisalmer and Karauli are also at the bottom of the list.

questions.q: Which district of Rajasthan had the highest child sex ratio (0-6 years) in Census 2011?
questions.exp: Banswara recorded the highest child sex ratio (934). The southern tribal districts generally show better child sex ratios than the Shekhawati belt.

questions.q: The lowest child sex ratio (0-6 years) in Census 2011 among Rajasthan's districts was recorded in:
questions.exp: Jhunjhunu recorded 837, the lowest child sex ratio in the state, despite having the state's highest male literacy.

questions.q: Which district of Rajasthan had the highest literacy rate as per Census 2011?
questions.exp: Kota led with 76.56% literacy; Kota also had the state's highest female literacy (about 65.9%).

questions.q: As per Census 2011, the lowest literacy rate in Rajasthan was recorded in the district of:
questions.exp: Jalore recorded 54.86% literacy, the lowest in Rajasthan; it also had the lowest female literacy (about 38.5%).

questions.q: The highest male literacy rate in Rajasthan as per Census 2011 was recorded in:
questions.exp: Jhunjhunu recorded the highest male literacy (about 86.9%), reflecting the Shekhawati region's strong schooling tradition.

questions.q: Which district of Rajasthan had the largest population as per Census 2011?
questions.exp: Jaipur district had 66.26 lakh persons, followed by Jodhpur (36.87 lakh) and Alwar (36.74 lakh).

questions.q: As per Census 2011, the least populous district of Rajasthan was:
questions.exp: Jaisalmer had only about 6.69 lakh persons though it is the largest district by area (38,401 sq km).

questions.q: The district of Rajasthan with the lowest population density (about 17 persons per sq km) in Census 2011 is:
questions.exp: Jaisalmer's density of 17 persons per sq km is the lowest in Rajasthan; the highest is Jaipur at 595.

questions.q: Which is the smallest district of Rajasthan by geographical area?
questions.exp: Dholpur, with about 3,034 sq km, is the smallest district by area; Jaisalmer is the largest.

questions.q: The highest decadal growth rate of population (2001-2011) in Rajasthan was recorded in the district of:
questions.exp: Barmer recorded about 32.5% decadal growth, the highest in the state; Sri Ganganagar recorded the lowest (about 10%).

questions.q: As per Census 2011, the lowest decadal growth rate of population in Rajasthan was recorded in:
questions.exp: Sri Ganganagar recorded roughly 10% decadal growth, the lowest among Rajasthan's districts.

questions.q: The share of urban population in Rajasthan as per Census 2011 is approximately:
questions.exp: About 24.89% of Rajasthan's population lived in urban areas in 2011, against 31.16% for India as a whole.

questions.q: Which is the most urbanised district of Rajasthan as per Census 2011?
questions.exp: Kota district was about 60.3% urban, ahead of Jaipur (52.4%) and Ajmer (40.1%).

questions.q: As per Census 2011, the least urbanised district of Rajasthan was:
questions.exp: Dungarpur was only about 6.4% urban, the lowest in the state; Banswara and Pratapgarh follow.

questions.q: How many cities of Rajasthan had a population of more than ten lakh as per Census 2011?
questions.exp: Jaipur, Jodhpur and Kota crossed the ten-lakh mark in Census 2011; Jaipur alone exceeded 30 lakh.

questions.q: The Scheduled Caste population of Rajasthan as a share of the state's total population in Census 2011 is about:
questions.exp: SCs form 17.83% (about 1.22 crore) of Rajasthan's population, while STs form 13.48%.

questions.q: As per Census 2011, Scheduled Tribes form what percentage of Rajasthan's population?
questions.exp: STs numbered about 92.38 lakh, i.e. 13.48% of Rajasthan's population.

questions.q: Which district of Rajasthan has the highest percentage of Scheduled Tribe population as per Census 2011?
questions.exp: Banswara has the highest ST share, followed by Dungarpur. In absolute numbers, however, Udaipur has the largest ST population.

questions.q: The largest Scheduled Tribe population in absolute numbers in Rajasthan (Census 2011) is found in the district of:
questions.exp: Udaipur has the largest number of tribal persons, though Banswara has the highest tribal proportion.

questions.q: As per Census 2011, the lowest proportion of Scheduled Tribe population in Rajasthan is found in:
questions.exp: Nagaur has the lowest ST share (about 0.2%), followed by Bikaner. The tribal belt is concentrated in the south of the state.

questions.q: Which is the most populous Scheduled Tribe of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The Meena (Mina) are the most numerous ST of Rajasthan, followed by the Bhil; together the two account for the bulk of the state's tribal population.

questions.q: The only Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) of Rajasthan is:
questions.exp: The Sahariya of Baran district are Rajasthan's sole PVTG (earlier 'primitive tribal group'), concentrated in Kishanganj and Shahbad tehsils.

questions.q: The Sahariya tribe of Rajasthan is mainly concentrated in the Kishanganj and Shahbad tehsils of which district?
questions.exp: Sahariyas live in the Shahbad and Kishanganj tehsils of Baran district in the Dang region; their village headman is called 'Kotwal'.

questions.q: 'Walra', a form of shifting cultivation practised in Rajasthan, is associated with which tribe?
questions.exp: Walra is the slash-and-burn cultivation of the Garasia of the Sirohi-Udaipur-Pali hills. The Bhils' shifting cultivation is called Chimata and Dajiya.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Rajasthan as per Census 2011:
I. The state's population density is 200 persons per sq km.
II. The state's sex ratio is 928 females per 1000 males.
III. The state's decadal growth rate was lower than the all-India average.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Density 200 and sex ratio 928 are correct. Rajasthan's decadal growth (21.31%) was HIGHER than India's (17.70%), so III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about literacy in Rajasthan as per Census 2011:
I. Male literacy was 79.19% and female literacy 52.12%.
II. Kota district recorded the highest literacy rate.
III. Barmer district recorded the lowest literacy rate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. The lowest literacy district was Jalore (54.86%), not Barmer.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the tribal population of Rajasthan:
I. Scheduled Tribes constitute about 13.5% of the state's population.
II. Banswara district has the highest proportion of Scheduled Tribes.
III. The Bhil are numerically the largest tribe of Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct as per Census 2011. The largest tribe of Rajasthan is the Meena, not the Bhil, so III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Bhil tribe of Rajasthan:
I. They are concentrated in Banswara, Dungarpur, Udaipur and Pratapgarh.
II. Their small hamlet is called 'palli' or 'phala'.
III. Their form of shifting cultivation on hill slopes is called 'Chimata'.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Bhil shifting cultivation on level land is called 'Dajiya' and on hill slopes 'Chimata'; Gavri is their famous dance-drama.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Garasia tribe:
I. They are found mainly in the Abu Road and Pindwara tehsils of Sirohi district.
II. 'Mor bandiya' is one of their recognised forms of marriage.
III. They are the largest tribe of Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. The Garasia are the third largest tribe of Rajasthan after the Meena and the Bhil, so III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sahariya tribe of Rajasthan:
I. They are the only Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group notified in the state.
II. Their traditional village headman is called 'Kotwal'.
III. They are concentrated in the Dungarpur-Banswara belt.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. The Sahariya live in Baran district (Shahbad and Kishanganj), not in Dungarpur-Banswara, so III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements on urbanisation in Rajasthan as per Census 2011:
I. About one-fourth of the state's population lives in urban areas.
II. Kota is the most urbanised district of the state.
III. Rajasthan's level of urbanisation is higher than the all-India average.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Urban share was 24.89% and Kota the most urbanised district. India's urban share (31.16%) is higher than Rajasthan's, so III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Scheduled Caste population of Rajasthan (Census 2011):
I. SCs form about 17.8% of the state's population.
II. Sri Ganganagar has one of the highest proportions of SC population.
III. Dungarpur has one of the lowest proportions of SC population.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. In absolute numbers the largest SC population is in Jaipur district.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Meena tribe of Rajasthan:
I. They are numerically the largest Scheduled Tribe of the state.
II. They are concentrated in Jaipur, Dausa, Sawai Madhopur and Karauli.
III. 'Zamindar' and 'Chowkidar' are recognised divisions among them.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Meena are concentrated in the eastern plains, unlike the Bhil who occupy the southern hills.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the administrative divisions of Rajasthan:
I. The state at present has 41 districts.
II. The state at present has 7 divisions.
III. Banswara and Pali are among the current divisional headquarters.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: After the December 2024 reorganisation Rajasthan has 41 districts and 7 divisions — Jaipur, Jodhpur, Ajmer, Kota, Bikaner, Bharatpur and Udaipur. The Banswara, Pali and Sikar divisions created in 2023 were abolished. (Position as of 2026.)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about population policy and migration in Rajasthan:
I. Rajasthan announced its State Population Policy in the year 2000.
II. Rajasthan is a net out-migration state.
III. Gujarat and Maharashtra are among the major destinations of migrants from Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Out-migration is heaviest from the eastern and southern districts towards Gujarat, Maharashtra and Delhi.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below (Census 2011):
List-I (Indicator)   List-II (District with the highest value)
A. Sex ratio   1. Kota
B. Literacy rate   2. Jaipur
C. Population   3. Dungarpur
D. Child sex ratio   4. Banswara
questions.exp: Highest sex ratio Dungarpur (994), highest literacy Kota (76.56%), largest population Jaipur (66.26 lakh), highest child sex ratio Banswara (934).

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below (Census 2011, lowest values):
List-I (Indicator)   List-II (District)
A. Sex ratio   1. Jaisalmer
B. Literacy rate   2. Jhunjhunu
C. Population density   3. Dholpur
D. Child sex ratio   4. Jalore
questions.exp: Lowest sex ratio Dholpur (846), lowest literacy Jalore (54.86%), lowest density Jaisalmer (17), lowest child sex ratio Jhunjhunu (837).

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Tribe)   List-II (Principal district)
A. Sahariya   1. Udaipur
B. Kathodi   2. Baran
C. Damor   3. Sirohi
D. Garasia   4. Dungarpur
questions.exp: Sahariya - Baran; Kathodi - Kotra/Jhadol in Udaipur; Damor - Simalwara and Aspur in Dungarpur; Garasia - Abu Road and Pindwara in Sirohi.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Tribal term)   List-II (Meaning/association)
A. Palli   1. Garasia shifting cultivation
B. Walra   2. Bhil hamlet
C. Kotwal   3. Damor village head
D. Mukhi   4. Sahariya village head
questions.exp: Palli is the Bhil hamlet, Walra the Garasia slash-and-burn cultivation, Kotwal the Sahariya headman and Mukhi the Damor village head.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below (Census 2011 population):
List-I (District)   List-II (Approximate population)
A. Jaipur   1. 6.69 lakh
B. Jodhpur   2. 36.87 lakh
C. Alwar   3. 66.26 lakh
D. Jaisalmer   4. 36.74 lakh
questions.exp: Jaipur 66.26 lakh, Jodhpur 36.87 lakh, Alwar 36.74 lakh and Jaisalmer 6.69 lakh — the state's most and least populous districts.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Community)   List-II (Traditional occupation)
A. Gadia Lohar   1. Camel and sheep rearing
B. Rabari (Raika)   2. Preparation of katha from khair
C. Kathodi   3. Itinerant blacksmithy
D. Sansi   4. Denotified nomadic community of the Bharatpur region
questions.exp: Gadia Lohars are wandering blacksmiths who trace their origin to Chittorgarh; Rabaris are camel herders; Kathodis make catechu; the Sansi are a denotified community.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below (Census 2011, level of urbanisation):
List-I (District)   List-II (Approximate urban share)
A. Kota   1. 6.4%
B. Jaipur   2. 40.1%
C. Ajmer   3. 60.3%
D. Dungarpur   4. 52.4%
questions.exp: Kota (60.3%) is the most urbanised district, followed by Jaipur (52.4%) and Ajmer (40.1%); Dungarpur (6.4%) is the least urbanised.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of Census 2011 indicator and district is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The lowest population density in Rajasthan is in Jaisalmer (17 persons per sq km), not Barmer. Barmer did record the highest decadal growth (about 32.5%).

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about Rajasthan as per Census 2011 is NOT correct?
opts: The state's child sex ratio was 888
The state's urban population share was about 24.89%
The state ranked first in India in population
questions.exp: Rajasthan ranks first in AREA, but eighth in population as per Census 2011. The other three figures are correct.

questions.q: Which one of the following tribe-district pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The Damor are found in Simalwara and Aspur tehsils of Dungarpur and adjoining Banswara, not in Jhalawar.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a Scheduled Tribe notified in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The Toda are a tribe of the Nilgiris in Tamil Nadu. Damor, Patelia and Dhanka are all notified STs of Rajasthan.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Sahariya tribe is NOT correct?
opts: They are the only PVTG of Rajasthan
They are concentrated in the Dang region of Baran district
Collection of minor forest produce is among their traditional occupations
questions.exp: The Sahariya headman is called 'Kotwal'; 'Mukhi' is the village head among the Damor.

questions.q: Which one of the following cities of Rajasthan did NOT have a population above ten lakh as per Census 2011?
questions.exp: Only Jaipur, Jodhpur and Kota crossed ten lakh in Census 2011; Ajmer's city population was well below that mark.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched with reference to tribal administration in Rajasthan?
opts: Headquarters of the Tribal Area Development department - Udaipur
Tribal Sub-Plan - began in the Fifth Five Year Plan
MADA - approach for scattered tribal pockets
questions.exp: The Sahariya development effort is focused on Baran district (Shahbad and Kishanganj), not Dungarpur.

questions.q:
Arrange the following districts of Rajasthan in descending order of their population as per Census 2011:
I. Alwar
II. Jaipur
III. Nagaur
IV. Jodhpur
questions.exp: Jaipur (66.26 lakh) > Jodhpur (36.87 lakh) > Alwar (36.74 lakh) > Nagaur (about 33.07 lakh).

questions.q:
Arrange the following districts of Rajasthan in descending order of sex ratio as per Census 2011:
I. Pali
II. Dungarpur
III. Rajsamand
IV. Dholpur
questions.exp: Dungarpur (994) > Rajsamand (990) > Pali (987) > Dholpur (846, the lowest in the state).

chapters.title: Minerals, Energy, Tourism and Transport of Rajasthan
factsheet: Rajasthan is India's SOLE producer of lead-zinc ore, wollastonite, selenite and jasper; it leads India in gypsum, rock phosphate, silver, marble, calcite, soapstone, ball clay and sandstone.
Jhamar Kotra (Udaipur) — India's largest rock phosphate deposit, worked by RSMML; other deposits Maton and Kanpur-Dakan Kotra (Udaipur), Birmania (Jaisalmer).
Gypsum — Got-Manglodh and Bhadwasi (Nagaur), also Bikaner, Sri Ganganagar, Hanumangarh, Barmer; Rajasthan produces the bulk of India's gypsum.
Copper — Khetri-Singhana, Madan-Kudan and Kolihan (Jhunjhunu), worked by the Khetri Copper Complex of Hindustan Copper Ltd; also Kho-Dariba (Alwar), Deri-Basantgarh (Sirohi).

Lead-zinc — Zawar (Udaipur, world's oldest known zinc-smelting site), Rampura-Agucha (Bhilwara, India's largest zinc mine), Rajpura-Dariba and Sindesar Khurd (Rajsamand); operator Hindustan Zinc Ltd, HQ Udaipur.
Sindesar Khurd (Rajsamand) is India's largest silver-producing mine; HZL smelters at Debari (Udaipur), Chanderiya (Chittorgarh) and Dariba.
Tungsten — Degana (Nagaur, Rewat hill); gold — Bhukia-Jagpura (Banswara); uranium — Rohil in the Khandela belt (Sikar) and Jahaj (Bhilwara).
Iron ore — Morija-Banola (Jaipur), Neemla-Rajpura (Dausa), Nathara-ki-Pal and Dalani (Udaipur); manganese — Kalakhunta, Lilwani, Timamori (Banswara).
Marble — Makrana (Nagaur region; white marble of the Taj Mahal), Rajsamand (largest producing district), Andhi (Jaipur, green), Babarmal (Udaipur, pink).
Limestone — Sanu (Jaisalmer, high-grade SMS variety for steel plants), Gotan and Mundwa (Nagaur), Chittorgarh, Bundi, Jhunjhunu (cement grade).
Sandstone — Dholpur and Karauli (red), Jodhpur (chhitar), Bansi Paharpur (Bharatpur/Deeg); granite — Jalore, the 'granite city of Rajasthan'.
Fluorite — Mando ki Pal (Dungarpur); wollastonite — Khera and Belka Pahar (Sirohi); asbestos — Rikhabdeo/Kherwara (Udaipur), Ajmer, Dungarpur, Rajsamand.
Emerald — Kaliguman-Tekhi belt (Rajsamand-Ajmer); garnet — Rajmahal (Tonk); bentonite — Barmer and Jaisalmer; ball clay — Bikaner; selenite — Nagaur.
Lignite — Palana and Barsingsar (Bikaner), Kapurdi, Jalipa and Giral (Barmer), Matasukh and Kasnau (Nagaur). Palana is Rajasthan's oldest worked lignite field.

Petroleum — Barmer-Sanchore basin: Mangala (discovered 2004, India's largest onshore find in decades), Bhagyam, Aishwariya, Raageshwari, Saraswati; block RJ-ON-90/1, operator Cairn/Vedanta; production from 2009.
Natural gas — Jaisalmer basin: Tanot, Dandewala, Bagitibba, Bhagewala (ONGC); this gas feeds the Ramgarh gas-based power station.

HPCL Rajasthan Refinery (HRRL), Pachpadra in Balotra district — 9 MMTPA refinery with a 2.4 MMTPA petrochemical complex; HPCL 74% and Government of Rajasthan 26%; commercial operations declared in June 2026.

RSMML (Rajasthan State Mines and Minerals Ltd), HQ Udaipur — rock phosphate, limestone, gypsum, lignite and fluorite; Rajasthan is India's third largest salt producer (Sambhar, Didwana, Pachpadra, Lunkaransar).
Thermal power: Suratgarh (Sri Ganganagar) is the largest thermal station of the state and is called Rajasthan's 'thermal power house'; Kota Super Thermal (Kota) was its first coal-based station.
Other stations — Chhabra (Baran), Kalisindh (Jhalawar), Giral lignite (Barmer), Barsingsar lignite of NLC (Bikaner), Ramgarh gas (Jaisalmer), Dholpur combined-cycle gas (Dholpur).

Rawatbhata Atomic Power Station (Chittorgarh) on the Chambal — India's second nuclear power station, Unit-1 built with Canadian collaboration; hydel at Rana Pratap Sagar, Jawahar Sagar and Mahi Bajaj Sagar (Banswara).

Bhadla Solar Park — Bhadla village, Phalodi district (earlier Jodhpur district), about 2,245 MW over roughly 56 sq km; India's largest solar park (long described as the world's largest, since overtaken; position as of 2026).
Rajasthan ranks FIRST among Indian states in installed solar capacity (about 41.7 GW as of April 2026) and second in total renewable capacity after Gujarat.

RRECL — Rajasthan Renewable Energy Corporation Ltd (Jaipur) is the state nodal agency for renewable energy; key policies: Rajasthan Solar Energy Policy 2019 and Rajasthan Integrated Clean Energy Policy 2024.

PM-KUSUM (2019, MNRE) — Component A: small grid-connected plants on barren land; Component B: standalone solar pumps; Component C: solarisation of existing grid-connected pumps. PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana (Feb 2024) gives up to 300 free units a month.
Power utilities: RVUNL (generation), RVPNL (transmission) and three discoms — Jaipur, Ajmer and Jodhpur Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. Wind hubs: Jaisalmer, Jodhpur and Barmer.
UNESCO World Heritage Sites in Rajasthan (4): Keoladeo National Park, Bharatpur (1985, natural); Jantar Mantar, Jaipur (2010); Hill Forts of Rajasthan (2013); Jaipur walled city (2019).
The six Hill Forts of Rajasthan: Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh (Rajsamand), Ranthambore (Sawai Madhopur), Gagron (Jhalawar), Amber (Jaipur) and Jaisalmer.

Tourism: RTDC runs state tourism; Palace on Wheels launched 26 January 1982, Royal Rajasthan on Wheels in 2009; slogan 'Padharo Mhare Desh'; Rajasthan Tourism Policy 2020; tourism given industry status in 2021.

Transport: North Western Railway, HQ Jaipur, created 1 October 2002; Jaipur Metro (Mansarovar-Chandpole) opened 3 June 2015, the state's first metro; the longest state stretch of the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway (about 373 km) lies in Rajasthan; Jaipur is the state's main international airport and Kishangarh (Ajmer) its greenfield airport.

questions.q: Jhamar Kotra, the largest deposit of its kind in India, is associated with which mineral?
questions.exp: Jhamar Kotra in Udaipur district is India's largest rock phosphate deposit and is worked by RSMML.

questions.q: The Got-Manglodh mines of Rajasthan are famous for the production of:
questions.exp: Got-Manglodh in Nagaur district is a major gypsum belt; Bhadwasi (Nagaur) is another. Rajasthan is India's largest gypsum producer.

questions.q: The Khetri copper belt of Rajasthan lies in which district?
questions.exp: Khetri-Singhana, Madan-Kudan and Kolihan mines lie in Jhunjhunu district and are worked by Hindustan Copper Ltd's Khetri Copper Complex.

questions.q: Rampura-Agucha, India's largest zinc mine, is located in which district of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Rampura-Agucha in Bhilwara district is operated by Hindustan Zinc Ltd and is India's largest zinc-producing mine.

questions.q: Zawar, the world's oldest known site of zinc smelting, is situated in which district?
questions.exp: The Zawar mines near Udaipur show evidence of zinc distillation from about the 13th century CE; they are still worked by Hindustan Zinc.

questions.q: Degana in Rajasthan is known for the mining of which mineral?
questions.exp: The Rewat hill deposit at Degana (Nagaur) is India's best-known tungsten (wolframite) occurrence.

questions.q: Makrana, famous for white marble, lies in which region of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Makrana lies in the Nagaur region (placed in Didwana-Kuchaman district after the 2023 reorganisation); its white marble was used in the Taj Mahal.

questions.q: The Sanu deposit of Jaisalmer district is important for which mineral?
questions.exp: Sanu supplies high-grade (SMS) limestone used by steel plants; it is worked by RSMML.

questions.q: Mando ki Pal, the principal fluorite deposit of Rajasthan, lies in which district?
questions.exp: Mando ki Pal in Dungarpur district is India's leading fluorite (fluorspar) deposit and is worked by RSMML.

questions.q: The Rohil uranium deposit of Rajasthan is located in which district?
questions.exp: Rohil in the Khandela belt of Sikar district is Rajasthan's most important uranium find; Jahaj in Bhilwara is another.

questions.q: The Bhukia-Jagpura gold deposit of Rajasthan is situated in which district?
questions.exp: Bhukia-Jagpura in Banswara district is Rajasthan's principal gold prospect.

questions.q: Rajasthan is the only producer in India of which of the following minerals?
questions.exp: Wollastonite, mined at Khera and Belka Pahar in Sirohi district, is produced only in Rajasthan; the state is also India's sole producer of lead-zinc ore, selenite and jasper.

questions.q: Sindesar Khurd, India's largest silver-producing mine, is located in which district of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Sindesar Khurd, near Rajpura-Dariba in Rajsamand district, is operated by Hindustan Zinc and makes Rajasthan India's leading silver producer.

questions.q: The Mangala oil field of Rajasthan lies in which basin?
questions.exp: Mangala, discovered in 2004 in the Barmer-Sanchore basin, was India's largest onshore oil discovery in decades; Bhagyam and Aishwariya lie in the same basin.

questions.q: Palana and Barsingsar, well-known lignite fields of Rajasthan, are located in which district?
questions.exp: Palana and Barsingsar lie in Bikaner district; Palana is the oldest worked lignite field of Rajasthan and Barsingsar has an NLC lignite power station.

questions.q: The Kapurdi and Jalipa lignite fields of Rajasthan lie in which district?
questions.exp: Kapurdi and Jalipa in Barmer district feed the Barmer lignite thermal power project; Giral, also in Barmer, is another lignite field.

questions.q: Rajasthan State Mines and Minerals Limited (RSMML) has its headquarters at:
questions.exp: RSMML, headquartered at Udaipur, mines rock phosphate, limestone, gypsum, lignite and fluorite for the state.

questions.q: Hindustan Zinc Limited, the operator of Rajasthan's lead-zinc mines, has its headquarters at:
questions.exp: Hindustan Zinc Ltd is headquartered at Udaipur; its smelters are at Debari, Chanderiya (Chittorgarh) and Dariba.

questions.q: Nathara-ki-Pal, an iron ore deposit of Rajasthan, is located in which district?
questions.exp: Nathara-ki-Pal and Dalani lie in Udaipur district; Morija-Banola (Jaipur) and Neemla-Rajpura (Dausa) are the other iron ore belts.

questions.q: Which district of Rajasthan is known as the 'granite city' of the state?
questions.exp: Jalore is called the granite city of Rajasthan because of its extensive granite quarrying and processing.

questions.q: Bansi Paharpur, the source of the red sandstone used in several major national monuments, lies in which district?
questions.exp: Bansi Paharpur red sandstone comes from the Bharatpur region (now in Deeg district after reorganisation); Dholpur and Karauli are the other red sandstone belts.

questions.q: Which district of Rajasthan is the largest producer of marble in the state?
questions.exp: Rajsamand leads Rajasthan in marble production; Makrana is famous for white marble, Andhi (Jaipur) for green and Babarmal (Udaipur) for pink marble.

questions.q: The Bhadla Solar Park of Rajasthan is located in which district?
questions.exp: Bhadla village lies in Phalodi district, carved out of the erstwhile Jodhpur district in 2023. The park has about 2,245 MW over roughly 56 sq km.

questions.q: Which state of India has the highest installed solar power capacity?
questions.exp: Rajasthan leads India in installed solar capacity (about 41.7 GW as of April 2026); Gujarat is second in solar but first in total renewable capacity.

questions.q: The state nodal agency for the promotion of renewable energy in Rajasthan is:
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Renewable Energy Corporation Ltd (RRECL), Jaipur, is the nodal agency for solar, wind and biomass projects in the state.

questions.q: Which is the largest thermal power station of Rajasthan in terms of installed capacity?
questions.exp: Suratgarh in Sri Ganganagar district, often called Rajasthan's 'thermal power house', is the state's largest thermal station.

questions.q: Which was the first coal-based thermal power station established in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The Kota Super Thermal Power Station on the Chambal was Rajasthan's first coal-based thermal power station.

questions.q: The Chhabra Thermal Power Plant of Rajasthan is situated in which district?
questions.exp: Chhabra lies in Baran district and includes both subcritical and supercritical units.

questions.q: The Kalisindh Thermal Power Station of Rajasthan is located in which district?
questions.exp: The Kalisindh station stands near Jhalawar; each of its two units is of 600 MW.

questions.q: The Rawatbhata Atomic Power Station of Rajasthan is located in which district?
questions.exp: Rawatbhata, on the Chambal in Chittorgarh district, is India's second nuclear power station; its first unit was built with Canadian collaboration.

questions.q: The Ramgarh gas-based thermal power station of Rajasthan is located in which district?
questions.exp: The Ramgarh station in Jaisalmer district runs on gas from the Tanot and Dandewala fields of the Jaisalmer basin.

questions.q: Under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana, how many units of electricity per month are provided free to eligible households?
questions.exp: The scheme, launched in February 2024, offers rooftop solar with up to 300 free units a month and targets one crore households nationally.

questions.q: Under the PM-KUSUM scheme, Component-B provides for:
opts: Grid-connected solar plants on barren land
Installation of standalone solar agriculture pumps
questions.exp: Component-A covers decentralised grid-connected plants on barren land, Component-B standalone solar pumps and Component-C solarisation of existing grid-connected pumps.

questions.q: Which organisation is responsible for the transmission of electricity in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Rajasthan Rajya Vidyut Prasaran Nigam Ltd (RVPNL) handles transmission; RVUNL generates and the three Vidyut Vitran Nigams distribute.

questions.q: How many properties in Rajasthan are inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List?
questions.exp: Four: Keoladeo National Park (1985), Jantar Mantar Jaipur (2010), the Hill Forts of Rajasthan (2013) and the walled city of Jaipur (2019). Position as of 2026.

questions.q: The walled city of Jaipur was inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List in which year?
questions.exp: Jaipur's walled city was inscribed in 2019, becoming India's second city after Ahmedabad to receive World Heritage city status.

questions.q: Which of the following hill forts inscribed by UNESCO is located in Jhalawar district?
questions.exp: Gagron, a jal-durg at the confluence of the Ahu and Kali Sindh, lies in Jhalawar district and is one of the six inscribed Hill Forts of Rajasthan.

questions.q: The luxury tourist train 'Palace on Wheels' was started in which year?
questions.exp: The Palace on Wheels was flagged off on 26 January 1982 by RTDC and Indian Railways; the Royal Rajasthan on Wheels followed in 2009.

questions.q: The headquarters of the North Western Railway zone is located at:
questions.exp: The North Western Railway, created on 1 October 2002, has its headquarters at Jaipur with divisions at Jaipur, Jodhpur, Ajmer and Bikaner.

questions.q: The first corridor of the Jaipur Metro, opened in 2015, runs between:
questions.exp: Phase 1A of the Pink Line, from Mansarovar to Chandpole, was opened on 3 June 2015; the underground stretch to Badi Chaupar came later.

questions.q: The greenfield airport at Kishangarh in Rajasthan lies in which district?
questions.exp: Kishangarh airport is in Ajmer district and began commercial operations in 2017; Jaipur is the state's main international airport.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about minerals of Rajasthan:
I. Rajasthan is the sole producer of lead-zinc ore in India.
II. Rajasthan is the leading producer of gypsum in India.
III. Rajasthan is the leading producer of bauxite in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Rajasthan is India's only source of lead-zinc ore and its largest gypsum producer. Bauxite comes chiefly from Odisha, Gujarat and Jharkhand.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Jhamar Kotra:
I. It is India's largest rock phosphate deposit.
II. It is located in Udaipur district.
III. It is worked by Rajasthan State Mines and Minerals Ltd.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. RSMML also works the Sanu limestone and Mando ki Pal fluorite deposits.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the lead-zinc mines of Rajasthan:
I. Rampura-Agucha is located in Bhilwara district.
II. Rajpura-Dariba is located in Rajsamand district.
III. Zawar is located in Chittorgarh district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Rampura-Agucha (Bhilwara) and Rajpura-Dariba (Rajsamand) are correctly placed; Zawar is in Udaipur district, not Chittorgarh.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the lignite resources of Rajasthan:
I. Palana lignite field lies in Bikaner district.
II. Kapurdi and Jalipa lignite fields lie in Barmer district.
III. Matasukh lignite field lies in Nagaur district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Giral, also in Barmer, is another lignite field with an associated power project.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about petroleum in Rajasthan:
I. The Mangala field was discovered in the Barmer-Sanchore basin.
II. Tanot and Dandewala are gas fields of the Jaisalmer basin.
III. Commercial crude oil production from the Barmer basin began in the 1980s.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Mangala was discovered in 2004 and production began in 2009, so III is wrong. Tanot and Dandewala are indeed Jaisalmer basin gas fields.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the HPCL Rajasthan Refinery at Pachpadra:
I. It is a joint venture of HPCL and the Government of Rajasthan.
II. It is located in Balotra district.
III. Its refining capacity is 9 MMTPA.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. HPCL holds 74% and the state 26%; the complex includes a 2.4 MMTPA petrochemical unit and was declared commercially operational in June 2026.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the marble of Rajasthan:
I. Makrana is famous for white marble.
II. Andhi in Jaipur district yields green marble.
III. Rajsamand is the largest marble-producing district of the state.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Babarmal in Udaipur district is known for pink marble.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Bhadla Solar Park:
I. It is spread over roughly 56 square kilometres.
II. Its installed capacity is about 2,245 MW.
III. It lies in Barmer district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Bhadla is in Phalodi district (earlier Jodhpur district), not Barmer, so III is wrong. It is India's largest solar park.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about renewable energy in Rajasthan:
I. RRECL is the state nodal agency for renewable energy.
II. Rajasthan ranks first among Indian states in installed solar capacity.
III. The Rajasthan Solar Energy Policy was announced in 2019.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct as of 2026; the Rajasthan Integrated Clean Energy Policy was subsequently announced in 2024.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about thermal power in Rajasthan:
I. The Suratgarh station lies in Sri Ganganagar district.
II. The Chhabra station lies in Baran district.
III. The Kalisindh station lies in Kota district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Suratgarh (Sri Ganganagar) and Chhabra (Baran) are correct; the Kalisindh station is in Jhalawar district, not Kota.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rawatbhata Atomic Power Station:
I. It stands on the Chambal river in Chittorgarh district.
II. Its first unit was built with Canadian collaboration.
III. It was India's first nuclear power station.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Rawatbhata was India's SECOND nuclear power station; Tarapur in Maharashtra was the first. Statements I and II are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the UNESCO World Heritage properties of Rajasthan:
I. Keoladeo National Park was inscribed as a natural site.
II. The Jantar Mantar of Jaipur was inscribed in 2010.
III. The Hill Forts of Rajasthan comprise six forts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct: Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Gagron, Amber and Jaisalmer make up the serial Hill Forts property inscribed in 2013.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about tourism in Rajasthan:
I. The Palace on Wheels was launched in 1982.
II. RTDC is the state tourism development corporation.
III. Rajasthan's tourism slogan is 'Padharo Mhare Desh'.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Rajasthan also announced a new Tourism Policy in 2020 and accorded industry status to tourism in 2021.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about transport in Rajasthan:
I. The North Western Railway zone has its headquarters at Jaipur.
II. Jaipur was the first city of Rajasthan to get a metro rail system.
III. The longest state stretch of the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway lies in Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct; roughly 373 km of the 1,386 km Delhi-Mumbai Expressway passes through Rajasthan.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Mineral)   List-II (District)
A. Rock phosphate   1. Jhunjhunu
B. Gypsum   2. Udaipur
C. Copper   3. Jaisalmer
D. Limestone (SMS grade)   4. Nagaur
questions.exp: Rock phosphate - Jhamar Kotra (Udaipur); gypsum - Got-Manglodh (Nagaur); copper - Khetri (Jhunjhunu); SMS-grade limestone - Sanu (Jaisalmer).

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Mine)   List-II (Mineral)
A. Jhamar Kotra   1. Tungsten
B. Got-Manglodh   2. Rock phosphate
C. Zawar   3. Gypsum
D. Degana   4. Lead-zinc
questions.exp: Jhamar Kotra - rock phosphate; Got-Manglodh - gypsum; Zawar - lead-zinc; Degana - tungsten. This is among the most frequently repeated matching sets in RAS.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Lignite field)   List-II (District)
A. Palana   1. Barmer
B. Kapurdi   2. Nagaur
C. Matasukh   3. Bikaner
D. Giral   4. Barmer
questions.exp: Palana lies in Bikaner; Kapurdi and Giral both lie in Barmer; Matasukh lies in Nagaur.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Field)   List-II (Product/Basin)
A. Mangala   1. Gas, Jaisalmer basin
B. Tanot   2. Crude oil, Barmer-Sanchore basin
C. Aishwariya   3. Crude oil, Barmer-Sanchore basin
D. Dandewala   4. Gas, Jaisalmer basin
questions.exp: Mangala and Aishwariya are crude oil fields of the Barmer-Sanchore basin; Tanot and Dandewala are gas fields of the Jaisalmer basin.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Power station)   List-II (District)
A. Suratgarh   1. Jhalawar
B. Chhabra   2. Chittorgarh
C. Kalisindh   3. Sri Ganganagar
D. Rawatbhata   4. Baran
questions.exp: Suratgarh - Sri Ganganagar; Chhabra - Baran; Kalisindh - Jhalawar; Rawatbhata atomic station - Chittorgarh.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Mineral)   List-II (Deposit)
A. Fluorite   1. Khera-Belka Pahar (Sirohi)
B. Wollastonite   2. Rajmahal (Tonk)
C. Emerald   3. Mando ki Pal (Dungarpur)
D. Garnet   4. Kaliguman (Rajsamand)
questions.exp: Fluorite - Mando ki Pal (Dungarpur); wollastonite - Khera and Belka Pahar (Sirohi); emerald - Kaliguman belt (Rajsamand); garnet - Rajmahal (Tonk).

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (UNESCO World Heritage property in Rajasthan)   List-II (Year of inscription)
A. Keoladeo National Park   1. 2019
B. Jantar Mantar, Jaipur   2. 1985
C. Hill Forts of Rajasthan   3. 2010
D. Jaipur walled city   4. 2013
questions.exp: Keoladeo 1985, Jantar Mantar 2010, Hill Forts 2013 and the walled city of Jaipur 2019.

questions.q:

B. Gagron   2. Rajsamand
C. Ranthambore   3. Jaipur
D. Amber   4. Jhalawar
questions.exp: Kumbhalgarh - Rajsamand; Gagron - Jhalawar; Ranthambore - Sawai Madhopur; Amber - Jaipur. Chittorgarh and Jaisalmer complete the six inscribed Hill Forts.

Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

A. Chanderiya   1. Copper smelting
B. Khetri   2. Zinc smelting
C. Makrana   3. Salt production

questions.exp: Chanderiya (Chittorgarh) has a Hindustan Zinc smelter; Khetri has the copper complex; Makrana is a marble centre; Sambhar is India's largest inland salt source.

questions.q: Which one of the following mineral-district pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Rajasthan's principal fluorite deposit is Mando ki Pal in Dungarpur district; Sirohi is associated with wollastonite.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a lignite field of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Jhamar Kotra (Udaipur) is a rock phosphate deposit. Kapurdi and Jalipa are in Barmer and Barsingsar in Bikaner.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Bhadla Solar Park is NOT correct?
opts: It has an installed capacity of about 2,245 MW
It is India's largest solar park
It is operated solely by the Rajasthan Renewable Energy Corporation
questions.exp: Bhadla was developed in four phases by several agencies and developers including NTPC, SECI, ACME, Fortum and Avaada — not by RRECL alone.

questions.q: Which one of the following power station-district pairs of Rajasthan is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The Giral lignite power project is in Barmer district; Barsingsar is the lignite station located in Bikaner.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a UNESCO World Heritage property located in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Rani ki Vav is a stepwell at Patan in Gujarat, inscribed in 2014. Rajasthan has four inscribed properties.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT one of the six Hill Forts of Rajasthan inscribed by UNESCO?
questions.exp: Mehrangarh (Jodhpur) is not part of the inscribed serial property. The six are Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Gagron, Amber and Jaisalmer.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the HPCL Rajasthan Refinery is NOT correct?
opts: It is located at Pachpadra in Balotra district
The Government of Rajasthan holds a 26% equity stake
It has a refining capacity of 9 MMTPA
It is India's first refinery based entirely on imported crude
questions.exp: The refinery is designed to process both imported crude and crude from the Barmer basin, so it is not based entirely on imported crude. The other three statements are correct (position as of 2026).

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Morija-Banola in Jaipur district is an iron ore belt; manganese in Rajasthan comes chiefly from Banswara district.

questions.q:
Arrange the following World Heritage properties of Rajasthan in the chronological order of their inscription by UNESCO, starting with the earliest:
I. Jantar Mantar, Jaipur
II. Keoladeo National Park
III. Jaipur walled city
IV. Hill Forts of Rajasthan
questions.exp: Keoladeo 1985, Jantar Mantar 2010, Hill Forts 2013 and Jaipur walled city 2019.

questions.q:
Arrange the following power projects of Rajasthan in the chronological order of their commissioning, starting with the earliest:
I. Kota Super Thermal Power Station
II. Rawatbhata Atomic Power Station Unit-1
III. Bhadla Solar Park (full capacity)
IV. Suratgarh Super Thermal Power Station
questions.exp: Rawatbhata Unit-1 came on line in the 1970s, Kota Super Thermal in the 1980s, Suratgarh in the late 1990s and Bhadla reached full capacity around 2020.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Rajasthan leads all Indian states in installed solar power capacity.
Reason (R): Western Rajasthan combines very high solar insolation with extensive tracts of low-value barren land.
Select the correct answer:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: Both statements are true and the high insolation plus cheap barren land of the Thar directly explains the state's lead (about 41.7 GW of solar as of April 2026).

subjects.subject: Indian Constitution, Political System and Governance

chapters.title: Making of the Constitution, Preamble, Salient Features, Sources
factsheet: Idea of a Constituent Assembly for India first mooted by M. N. Roy in 1934; INC made it an official demand in 1935; conceded in principle by the British in the August Offer, 1940.

Constituent Assembly constituted in November 1946 under the Cabinet Mission Plan; members chosen indirectly by provincial assemblies through proportional representation with a single transferable vote.

Total strength 389 = 296 from British India (292 provinces + 4 chief commissioners' provinces, including Ajmer-Merwara) + 93 from princely states; reduced to 299 after Partition; roughly one seat per million population, provincial seats split among Muslim, Sikh and General communities.
First sitting 9 December 1946; Dr. Sachchidananda Sinha temporary (provisional) President; Dr. Rajendra Prasad elected permanent President on 11 December 1946.
Vice-Presidents of the Assembly: H. C. Mukherjee and V. T. Krishnamachari (who represented Jaipur and was later Deputy Chairman of the Planning Commission).
