Art. 352 National Emergency - grounds war, external aggression or armed rebellion; 'armed rebellion' replaced 'internal disturbance' by the 44th Amendment, 1978.

Art. 352 procedure - written recommendation of the Union Cabinet; approval by both Houses within one month by special majority; continues 6 months at a time; Lok Sabha can revoke by simple majority (notice of 1/10th members).
National Emergency proclaimed thrice - 1962 (Chinese aggression), 1971 (Pakistan war), 1975 (internal disturbance).

Art. 358 - Art. 19 automatically suspended, and only when the emergency is on grounds of war/external aggression (44th Amendment). Art. 359 - President may suspend enforcement of other FRs, but never Art. 20 and Art. 21.
Art. 355 - duty of the Union to protect States against external aggression and internal disturbance.

Art. 356 President's Rule - approval within 2 months, 6 months at a time, maximum 3 years; beyond 1 year only if a National Emergency is in force and the Election Commission certifies that elections cannot be held (44th Amendment).
President's Rule has been imposed in Rajasthan 4 times: 1967, 1977, 1980 and 1992-93 (the last being the longest, about a year).
S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) - Art. 356 proclamation is subject to judicial review; majority is to be tested on the floor of the House; secularism is part of the basic structure.
Art. 360 Financial Emergency - never proclaimed in India.
Art. 368 - amendment procedure; Bill may start in either House, needs special majority, no joint sitting; 24th Amendment (1971) made the President's assent obligatory.

Ratification by half the State legislatures (simple majority) is needed for: election of the President, extent of executive power of Union/States, Supreme Court and High Courts, distribution of legislative powers, any List of the 7th Schedule, representation of States in Parliament, and Art. 368 itself.

Amendment landmarks: 1st (1951) 9th Schedule and Art. 15(4); 7th (1956) States reorganisation; 24th (1971) Parliament's power over FRs; 26th (1971) abolition of privy purses; 42nd (1976) 'mini-Constitution'.
44th (1978) right to property made a legal right under Art. 300A; 52nd (1985) anti-defection, 10th Schedule; 61st (1988) voting age 21 to 18; 69th (1991) Delhi as NCT (Art. 239AA).
73rd and 74th (1992) panchayats and municipalities; 86th (2002) Art. 21A right to education; 91st (2003) Council of Ministers capped at 15%; 97th (2011) co-operative societies, Art. 43B, Part IX-B.

101st (2016) GST; 102nd (2018) NCBC constitutional status (Art. 338B, 342A); 103rd (2019) 10% EWS reservation (Art. 15(6), 16(6)); 104th (2019) SC/ST reservation extended to 2030 and Anglo-Indian nomination discontinued; 105th (2021) States' power to identify SEBCs; 106th (2023) one-third reservation for women (Art. 330A, 332A, 334A).

Schedules: 1 States and UTs; 2 emoluments; 3 oaths; 4 Rajya Sabha seats; 5 Scheduled Areas; 6 tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, Mizoram; 7 three Lists; 8 languages (22); 9 land-reform laws (1st Amendment); 10 anti-defection; 11 panchayats (29 items); 12 municipalities (18 items).

Art. 371 series: 371A Nagaland, 371B Assam, 371C Manipur, 371D/E Andhra Pradesh, 371F Sikkim, 371G Mizoram, 371H Arunachal Pradesh, 371I Goa, 371J Karnataka (Hyderabad-Karnataka, 98th Amendment 2012).

questions.q: Residuary powers of legislation are vested in the Parliament by which Article of the Constitution?
questions.exp: Article 248, read with Entry 97 of the Union List, vests residuary powers of legislation in Parliament. In the Canadian model residuary power lies with the Centre, in the US model with the states.

questions.q: Parliament can legislate on a subject of the State List in the national interest if the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution to that effect under which Article?
questions.exp: Under Article 249 a Rajya Sabha resolution supported by two-thirds of the members present and voting empowers Parliament to make law on a State List subject for one year, renewable.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 249 of the Constitution:
I. The resolution must be passed by the Rajya Sabha by a majority of two-thirds of the members present and voting.
II. The law so made remains in force for one year and the resolution can be renewed.
III. Such a law can also be made by Parliament on a resolution of the Lok Sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Only the Rajya Sabha, as the House representing the States, can pass a resolution under Article 249; the Lok Sabha has no such role. Statement III is therefore wrong.

questions.q: Under which Article can Parliament legislate on a State List subject when two or more State Legislatures pass resolutions requesting it to do so?
questions.exp: Article 252 covers legislation by consent of States; such a law can be amended or repealed only by Parliament. Article 253 is for implementing international treaties and agreements.

questions.q: Which one of the following subjects was transferred from the State List to the Concurrent List by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976?
questions.exp: The 42nd Amendment moved five subjects to the Concurrent List: education, forests, weights and measures, protection of wild animals and birds, and administration of justice. Police and public order remain in the State List.

questions.q: Which one of the following subjects is NOT included in the Union List of the Seventh Schedule?
questions.exp: Public order and police are Entries 1 and 2 of the State List. Atomic energy, citizenship and banking are Union List subjects.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Article)   List-II (Subject)
A. Article 268   1. Finance Commission
B. Article 275   2. Duties levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States
C. Article 280   3. Discretionary grants by the Union
D. Article 282   4. Statutory grants-in-aid to States
questions.exp: Article 268 covers stamp duties levied by the Union but collected and appropriated by the States; Article 275 provides statutory grants-in-aid charged on the Consolidated Fund of India; Article 280 the Finance Commission; Article 282 discretionary grants.

questions.q: Statutory grants-in-aid to needy States, charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, are provided under which Article?
questions.exp: Article 275 provides statutory grants-in-aid on the recommendation of the Finance Commission. Article 282 allows both the Union and the States to make discretionary grants for any public purpose.

questions.q: The Goods and Services Tax Council has been constituted under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.exp: Article 279A, inserted by the 101st Amendment Act, 2016, creates the GST Council with the Union Finance Minister as Chairperson. Article 246A gives concurrent taxing power on GST.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Goods and Services Tax Council:
I. The Union Finance Minister is its Chairperson.
II. Decisions are taken by a majority of not less than three-fourths of the weighted votes of the members present and voting.
III. The vote of the Central Government has a weightage of one-half of the total votes cast.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Centre's vote carries a weightage of one-third and the States together two-thirds, not one-half. The quorum is one-half of the total members.

questions.q: Adjudication of disputes relating to the waters of inter-State rivers is provided for under which Article?
questions.exp: Article 262 empowers Parliament to provide for adjudication of inter-State river water disputes and to bar the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court and other courts in such matters.

questions.q: The Inter-State Council was set up in 1990 by a Presidential Order on the recommendation of which body?
questions.exp: The Sarkaria Commission (appointed 1983, report 1988) recommended a permanent Inter-State Council under Article 263; it was established on 28 May 1990 with the Prime Minister as Chairman.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Zonal Councils is NOT correct?
opts: They were created by the States Reorganisation Act, 1956
They are statutory and not constitutional bodies
The Union Home Minister is the common chairman of all Zonal Councils
Rajasthan is a member of the Central Zonal Council
questions.exp: Rajasthan belongs to the Northern Zonal Council along with Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Delhi, Chandigarh, Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh. The Central Zonal Council covers Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.

questions.q: Freedom of trade, commerce and intercourse throughout the territory of India is guaranteed by which Article?
questions.exp: Article 301 guarantees this freedom, subject to restrictions under Articles 302-305. Under Article 304(b) a State can impose reasonable restrictions only with the previous sanction of the President.

questions.q: Which Article imposes a duty on the Union to protect every State against external aggression and internal disturbance?
questions.exp: Article 355 is the constitutional basis on which the Centre acts under Article 356. It also requires the Union to ensure that the government of every State is carried on in accordance with the Constitution.

questions.q: After the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978, a National Emergency under Article 352 can be proclaimed on which of the following grounds?
opts: War, external aggression or internal disturbance
War, external aggression or armed rebellion
War, armed rebellion or failure of constitutional machinery
External aggression, armed rebellion or financial instability
questions.exp: The 44th Amendment substituted 'armed rebellion' for the vaguer 'internal disturbance', which had been used to justify the 1975 Emergency.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the proclamation of a National Emergency:
I. The President can proclaim it only on the written recommendation of the Union Cabinet.
II. It must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within one month by a special majority.
III. Once approved, it continues for six months at a time.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Before the 44th Amendment the approval period was two months and only a simple majority was needed. The Lok Sabha alone can force revocation by a simple-majority resolution.

questions.q: A National Emergency has been proclaimed in India on how many occasions?
questions.exp: Three times: in 1962 (Chinese aggression), 1971 (war with Pakistan) and 1975 (internal disturbance). A Financial Emergency has never been proclaimed.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Articles 358 and 359:
I. Article 19 is automatically suspended only when the National Emergency is declared on grounds of war or external aggression.
II. Article 359 empowers the President to suspend the enforcement of Articles 20 and 21 as well.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: The 44th Amendment provided that Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended, and restricted the automatic suspension of Article 19 to emergencies declared on grounds of war or external aggression.

questions.q: What is the maximum period for which President's Rule under Article 356 can normally continue in a State?
questions.exp: President's Rule is approved for six months at a time and can extend to a maximum of three years. Beyond one year it needs a National Emergency in force and an Election Commission certificate that elections cannot be held.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about President's Rule under Article 356:
I. The proclamation must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within two months.
II. Extension beyond one year requires that a National Emergency be in operation and that the Election Commission certify that elections cannot be held.
III. Approval of the proclamation requires a special majority in both Houses.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Approval of a proclamation under Article 356 needs only a simple majority in both Houses, unlike a National Emergency, which needs a special majority. Statement III is therefore wrong.

questions.q: How many times has President's Rule been imposed in the State of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: President's Rule has been imposed in Rajasthan four times: 1967, 1977, 1980 and December 1992 to December 1993. The 1992-93 spell was the longest, lasting about a year.

questions.q: President's Rule was imposed in Rajasthan in all of the following years EXCEPT:
questions.exp: The four impositions were in 1967, 1977, 1980 and 1992. No proclamation was made in 1985; the first, in March 1967, followed an indecisive assembly election.

questions.q: In which year was President's Rule imposed in Rajasthan for the first time?
questions.exp: The first spell ran from 13 March to 26 April 1967, following an inconclusive assembly election. Nationally, the first use of Article 356 was in Punjab in 1951.

questions.q: In which case did the Supreme Court hold that a proclamation under Article 356 is subject to judicial review and that the majority of a government must be tested on the floor of the House?
questions.exp: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India (1994) laid down these principles and also held secularism to be part of the basic structure of the Constitution.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about a Financial Emergency is correct?
opts: It has been proclaimed once, in 1991
It is declared under Article 360 and has never been proclaimed
It can be proclaimed only on the advice of the Finance Commission
questions.exp: Article 360 provides for a Financial Emergency; it has never been invoked. During such an emergency salaries of government servants, including judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts, may be reduced.

questions.q:
Arrange the following Constitutional Amendment Acts in correct chronological order of their enactment:
I. Anti-defection (Tenth Schedule)
II. Fundamental Duties
III. Reduction of voting age to 18 years
IV. Right to property made a legal right
questions.exp: 42nd Amendment (1976) added Fundamental Duties, 44th (1978) made property a legal right under Article 300A, 52nd (1985) added the Tenth Schedule, and 61st (1988) lowered the voting age.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the procedure for amending the Constitution under Article 368:
I. An amendment Bill can be introduced in either House of Parliament.
II. There is no provision for a joint sitting in case of a deadlock between the two Houses.
III. The President is bound to give assent to a Constitution Amendment Bill.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The 24th Amendment Act, 1971 made the President's assent to a Constitution Amendment Bill obligatory. An amendment Bill cannot be introduced in a State Legislature.

questions.q: Which one of the following amendments does NOT require ratification by the legislatures of half of the States?
opts: An amendment affecting the election of the President
An amendment altering the Seventh Schedule
An amendment to the Fundamental Rights
An amendment altering the representation of States in Parliament
questions.exp: Amendments to Fundamental Rights need only a special majority of Parliament. Ratification by half the States is required for federal provisions listed in the proviso to Article 368(2).

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Amendment Act)   List-II (Subject)
A. 1st Amendment   1. Anti-defection
B. 52nd Amendment   2. Ninth Schedule
C. 61st Amendment   3. Right to education
D. 86th Amendment   4. Voting age lowered to 18 years
questions.exp: 1st Amendment (1951) created the Ninth Schedule, 52nd (1985) added the Tenth Schedule on defection, 61st (1988) reduced the voting age, and 86th (2002) inserted Article 21A.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Amendment Act)   List-II (Subject)
A. 73rd Amendment   1. Goods and Services Tax
B. 91st Amendment   2. Panchayati Raj institutions
C. 101st Amendment   3. Ten per cent reservation for economically weaker sections
D. 103rd Amendment   4. Size of the Council of Ministers limited to 15 per cent
questions.exp: 73rd (1992) panchayats; 91st (2003) capped the Council of Ministers at 15 per cent of the House strength; 101st (2016) GST; 103rd (2019) EWS reservation under Articles 15(6) and 16(6).

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Amendment Act)   List-II (Subject)
A. 26th Amendment   1. Delhi made the National Capital Territory
B. 42nd Amendment   2. Abolition of privy purses
C. 44th Amendment   3. Fundamental Duties added
D. 69th Amendment   4. Right to property made a legal right
questions.exp: 26th (1971) abolished privy purses; 42nd (1976) inserted Part IVA; 44th (1978) deleted Article 31 and inserted Article 300A; 69th (1991) inserted Article 239AA for Delhi.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act gave constitutional status to co-operative societies by inserting Part IX-B and Article 43B?
questions.exp: The 97th Amendment Act, 2011 (effective 2012) made forming co-operative societies a fundamental right under Article 19(1)(c), added Article 43B in the Directive Principles and inserted Part IX-B.

questions.q: The National Commission for Backward Classes was granted constitutional status by which amendment?
questions.exp: The 102nd Amendment Act, 2018 inserted Articles 338B and 342A. The 105th Amendment Act, 2021 restored the power of States to identify socially and educationally backward classes.

questions.q: The 106th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2023 relates to which of the following?
opts: One-third reservation of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies
Constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes
Extension of Scheduled Caste reservation to 2030
questions.exp: Popularly called the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam, it inserted Articles 330A, 332A and 334A; the reservation is to operate after a census and delimitation exercise and is to last 15 years.

questions.q: Which Constitutional Amendment Act discontinued the nomination of Anglo-Indian members to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies?
questions.exp: The 104th Amendment Act, 2019 ended Anglo-Indian nomination and extended reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in legislatures up to 2030.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of amendment and subject is NOT correctly matched?
opts: 24th Amendment - Power of Parliament to amend Fundamental Rights
71st Amendment - Addition of Konkani, Manipuri and Nepali to the Eighth Schedule
questions.exp: The 92nd Amendment Act, 2003 added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali to the Eighth Schedule, raising the number of scheduled languages to 22. Right to education came through the 86th Amendment.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Schedule)   List-II (Subject)
A. Second Schedule   1. Allocation of seats in the Rajya Sabha
B. Fourth Schedule   2. Emoluments of the President, Governors and Judges
C. Ninth Schedule   3. Anti-defection provisions
D. Tenth Schedule   4. Land reform and other laws immune from challenge
questions.exp: The Ninth Schedule was created by the 1st Amendment, 1951; after I.R. Coelho (2007), laws added to it after 24 April 1973 are open to judicial review on basic-structure grounds.

questions.q: Which Schedule of the Constitution contains provisions for the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes?
questions.exp: The Fifth Schedule applies to Scheduled Areas in States other than Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram, and provides for a Tribes Advisory Council and an annual report by the Governor to the President.

questions.q: The Sixth Schedule of the Constitution applies to the tribal areas of which group of States?
opts: Assam, Arunachal Pradesh, Meghalaya and Tripura
questions.exp: The Sixth Schedule provides for Autonomous District Councils in these four States. Nagaland is instead covered by the special provisions of Article 371A.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Fifth Schedule:
I. The Governor of a State having Scheduled Areas must submit an annual report to the President.
II. A Tribes Advisory Council is to be established, with three-fourths of its members drawn from the Scheduled Tribe representatives in the Legislative Assembly.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Both are correct. The Tribes Advisory Council may have up to twenty members. Parliament can amend the Fifth Schedule by a simple majority, and this is not treated as an amendment under Article 368.

questions.q: Special provisions with respect to the State of Nagaland, protecting Naga customary law and ownership of land and resources, are contained in which Article?
questions.exp: Article 371A was inserted by the 13th Amendment Act, 1962. Article 371G contains similar provisions for Mizoram and Article 371C for Manipur.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Article)   List-II (State)
A. Article 371D   1. Sikkim
B. Article 371F   2. Andhra Pradesh
C. Article 371G   3. Karnataka
D. Article 371J   4. Mizoram
questions.exp: Article 371D provides for an Administrative Tribunal in Andhra Pradesh; 371F for Sikkim (36th Amendment, 1975); 371G for Mizoram; 371J for the Hyderabad-Karnataka region (98th Amendment, 2012).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Constitution originally had eight Schedules.
II. The Eighth Schedule at present recognises 22 languages.
III. The Ninth Schedule was added by the First Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Constitution now has twelve Schedules; the 11th and 12th were added by the 73rd and 74th Amendments in 1992.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about Article 254 is correct?
opts: It deals with the residuary power of legislation
It provides that in case of repugnancy between a Union law and a State law on a Concurrent List subject, the Union law prevails
It empowers the Governor to reserve any Bill for the President
It restricts the taxing power of the States
questions.exp: Article 254 deals with inconsistency between laws made by Parliament and by State Legislatures. If a repugnant State law has been reserved for and received the President's assent, it prevails in that State.

chapters.title: Local Government: Rural and Urban
factsheet: Article 40 (DPSP) directs the State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government; Lord Ripon's Resolution of 1882 earned him the title 'Father of local self-government in India'.
Royal Commission on Decentralisation, 1907 (report 1909) recommended strengthening village panchayats; Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms 1919 made local self-government a transferred subject.
Balwant Rai Mehta Committee - appointed January 1957, reported November 1957; recommended 'democratic decentralisation' and a three-tier system: Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti, Zila Parishad.
Rajasthan was the first State to implement Panchayati Raj - inaugurated by Jawaharlal Nehru at Nagaur on 2 October 1959; Andhra Pradesh was the second (1 November 1959).

Ashok Mehta Committee - appointed 1977, reported August 1978; recommended a two-tier system of Zila Parishad and Mandal Panchayat (for 15,000-20,000 population) and open participation of political parties.

G.V.K. Rao Committee, 1985 (Planning Commission) - called the system 'grass without roots'; recommended the Zila Parishad as the pivotal body and creation of the post of District Development Commissioner.
L.M. Singhvi Committee, 1986 - first recommended constitutional status for panchayats, treated the Gram Sabha as the embodiment of direct democracy and revived Nyaya Panchayats.

Other committees: Hanumantha Rao (1983), P.K. Thungon (1988), V.N. Gadgil (1988). The 64th Constitutional Amendment Bill, 1989 (Rajiv Gandhi) was passed by the Lok Sabha but defeated in the Rajya Sabha.
73rd Amendment Act, 1992 - added Part IX (Articles 243 to 243-O) and the Eleventh Schedule; came into force 24 April 1993, now observed as National Panchayati Raj Day.
74th Amendment Act, 1992 - added Part IX-A (Articles 243P to 243ZG) and the Twelfth Schedule; came into force 1 June 1993.
Eleventh Schedule - 29 functional items for panchayats, linked to Article 243G. Twelfth Schedule - 18 items for municipalities, linked to Article 243W.
Article 243A Gram Sabha; 243B constitution of panchayats (a State with population not exceeding 20 lakh need not constitute the intermediate level); 243C composition; 243D reservation.

Article 243E five-year term (fresh elections within six months of dissolution); 243F disqualifications, minimum age 21 years; 243H taxes and funds; 243I State Finance Commission; 243J audit; 243K State Election Commission; 243M non-application; 243-O bar on courts in electoral matters.
Article 243Q - three types of urban bodies: Nagar Panchayat (transitional area), Municipal Council (smaller urban area), Municipal Corporation (larger urban area).
Article 243S - Ward Committees are mandatory in municipalities with a population of three lakh or more; 243T reservation (States may also reserve for backward classes); 243U duration; 243W powers.

Article 243ZD District Planning Committee - four-fifths of members elected by elected members of the district panchayat and the municipalities from among themselves, in proportion to rural-urban population.

Article 243ZE Metropolitan Planning Committee - for a metropolitan area of population ten lakh or more; two-thirds of members elected by elected members of municipalities and chairpersons of panchayats in that area.
Reservation: seats for SCs and STs in proportion to population, and not less than one-third of total seats (including of SC/ST seats) reserved for women; offices of chairperson also reserved.
State Election Commission (Art. 243K/243ZA) - State Election Commissioner appointed by the Governor, removable only in the manner and on the grounds of a High Court judge.
State Finance Commission (Art. 243I/243Y) - constituted by the Governor every five years to review the finances of panchayats and municipalities.
PESA, the Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act, was enacted in December 1996 on the recommendations of the Bhuria Committee (1995, chaired by Dilip Singh Bhuria).
PESA applies to Fifth Schedule areas in ten States: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha and Rajasthan.

Under PESA the Gram Sabha approves plans and beneficiaries, owns minor forest produce, is consulted before land acquisition, controls minor water bodies and minor minerals, and may prohibit intoxicants.

Bikaner was the first princely state in Rajasthan to enact its own Gram Panchayat Act, in 1928; Jodhpur, Jaipur, Udaipur, Sirohi, Bharatpur and Karauli also legislated on panchayats before independence.

Rajasthan Panchayat Act, 1953 and the Rajasthan Panchayat Samitis and Zila Parishads Act, 1959 preceded the present Rajasthan Panchayati Raj Act, 1994; Mount Abu (1864) had Rajasthan's first municipality.

15th Finance Commission recommended Rs 4.36 lakh crore for local governments for 2021-26 - Rs 2.36 lakh crore for rural and Rs 1.21 lakh crore for urban local bodies, plus Rs 70,051 crore of health grants.
15th Finance Commission grants to local bodies are distributed among States on population (90 per cent weight) and area (10 per cent weight); the vertical devolution share of States is 41 per cent.
Article 280(3)(bb) and (c) require the Central Finance Commission to recommend measures to augment a State's Consolidated Fund to supplement the resources of panchayats and municipalities.
In a Municipal Corporation the Mayor is the ceremonial/deliberative head while the Municipal Commissioner, usually an IAS or State service officer, is the executive head.
Panchayat elections and municipal electoral rolls are outside the jurisdiction of ordinary courts by virtue of Articles 243-O and 243ZG; challenges lie only by election petition.

questions.q: Which Directive Principle of State Policy requires the State to organise village panchayats as units of self-government?
questions.exp: Article 40 is the Gandhian Directive Principle on village panchayats; it was the constitutional basis for the 73rd Amendment. Article 43B, added in 2011, deals with co-operative societies.

questions.q: Which committee first recommended a three-tier structure of Panchayati Raj and the concept of 'democratic decentralisation'?
questions.exp: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee, appointed in January 1957 to review the Community Development Programme, reported in November 1957 and proposed Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee's recommendations:
I. The Gram Panchayat was to be directly elected.
II. The Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad were to be indirectly constituted.
III. The District Collector was to be the Chairman of the Zila Parishad.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Committee also recommended that real transfer of power and resources be made to these bodies, with the Panchayat Samiti as the executive body.

questions.q: Panchayati Raj was first inaugurated in India on 2 October 1959 at which place?
questions.exp: Jawaharlal Nehru inaugurated Panchayati Raj at Nagaur in Rajasthan, making Rajasthan the first State to adopt it. Andhra Pradesh followed on 1 November 1959.

questions.q: The Ashok Mehta Committee, which reported in 1978, recommended which pattern of Panchayati Raj?
opts: A single-tier system at the district level
A two-tier system of Zila Parishad and Mandal Panchayat
A three-tier system with the Panchayat Samiti as the pivot
A four-tier system including a State-level council
questions.exp: The Ashok Mehta Committee proposed the district as the first point of decentralisation, with Mandal Panchayats covering a population of 15,000 to 20,000, and open participation by political parties.

questions.q: Which committee described the Panchayati Raj institutions of the time as 'grass without roots' and recommended creating the post of District Development Commissioner?
questions.exp: The G.V.K. Rao Committee (1985), appointed by the Planning Commission on administrative arrangements for rural development, held that bureaucratisation had weakened the panchayats and made the Zila Parishad the pivot.

questions.q: Which committee was the first to recommend constitutional status for Panchayati Raj institutions?
questions.exp: The L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986) recommended constitutional recognition, treated the Gram Sabha as the embodiment of direct democracy and urged the revival of Nyaya Panchayats.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Committee)   List-II (Year of appointment/report)
A. Balwant Rai Mehta Committee   1. 1986
B. Ashok Mehta Committee   2. 1957
C. G.V.K. Rao Committee   3. 1977
D. L.M. Singhvi Committee   4. 1985
questions.exp: Balwant Rai Mehta 1957, Ashok Mehta appointed 1977 (report 1978), G.V.K. Rao 1985 and L.M. Singhvi 1986.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Committee)   List-II (Key recommendation)
A. Balwant Rai Mehta   1. Nyaya Panchayats and constitutional status
B. Ashok Mehta   2. District Development Commissioner
C. G.V.K. Rao   3. Democratic decentralisation in three tiers
D. L.M. Singhvi   4. Mandal Panchayat as the base unit
questions.exp: Balwant Rai Mehta gave the three-tier design, Ashok Mehta the two-tier Mandal Panchayat model, G.V.K. Rao the District Development Commissioner and L.M. Singhvi constitutional status.

questions.q: The 64th Constitutional Amendment Bill on Panchayati Raj, introduced in 1989, met which fate?
opts: It was passed and became the 64th Amendment Act
It was passed by the Lok Sabha but defeated in the Rajya Sabha
It was struck down by the Supreme Court
questions.exp: The Bill, introduced by the Rajiv Gandhi government, was passed by the Lok Sabha but failed to secure passage in the Rajya Sabha. Constitutional status finally came through the 73rd Amendment in 1992.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act came into force on 24 April 1993.
II. The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act came into force on 1 June 1993.
III. National Panchayati Raj Day is observed on 2 October every year.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: National Panchayati Raj Day is observed on 24 April, the date the 73rd Amendment took effect, not on 2 October. Both Amendments received the President's assent on 20 April 1993.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Part IX of the Constitution, relating to panchayats, comprises Articles 243 to 243-O.
II. Part IX-A, relating to municipalities, comprises Articles 243P to 243ZG.
III. Part IX-B, relating to co-operative societies, comprises Articles 243ZH to 243ZT.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Part IX-B was inserted by the 97th Amendment Act, 2011; in 2021 the Supreme Court struck it down insofar as it applied to co-operative societies operating within a single State.

questions.q: The Eleventh Schedule of the Constitution contains how many functional items for panchayats?
questions.exp: The Eleventh Schedule, added by the 73rd Amendment and linked to Article 243G, lists 29 subjects. The Twelfth Schedule, linked to Article 243W, lists 18 subjects for municipalities.

questions.q: Which one of the following subjects is NOT included in the Eleventh Schedule of the Constitution?
questions.exp: Fire services is an item of the Twelfth Schedule, meant for municipalities. Minor forest produce, fisheries and rural electrification including distribution of electricity are all Eleventh Schedule items.

questions.q: Which one of the following subjects is NOT included in the Twelfth Schedule of the Constitution?
opts: Urban forestry and protection of the environment
Regulation of slaughter houses and tanneries
questions.exp: Minor irrigation, water management and watershed development is item 3 of the Eleventh Schedule. The Twelfth Schedule's 18 items begin with urban planning including town planning.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Provision)   List-II (Article)
A. Gram Sabha   1. Article 243K
B. State Finance Commission for panchayats   2. Article 243A
C. State Election Commission   3. Article 243ZD
D. District Planning Committee   4. Article 243I
questions.exp: Article 243A defines the Gram Sabha's powers, 243I the State Finance Commission, 243K the State Election Commission and 243ZD the District Planning Committee.

questions.q: Under Article 243B, which States may choose not to constitute panchayats at the intermediate level?
opts: States having a population not exceeding ten lakh
States having a population not exceeding twenty lakh
States having fewer than five districts
States with more than sixty per cent urban population
questions.exp: A State whose population does not exceed twenty lakh need not constitute panchayats at the intermediate (block) level; the village and district levels are compulsory everywhere.

questions.q: What is the minimum age prescribed for being chosen as a member of a panchayat?
questions.exp: Article 243F provides that a person who has attained 21 years of age is eligible for membership of a panchayat, even though the voting age is 18. The same age applies to municipalities under Article 243V.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the duration of panchayats:
I. Every panchayat continues for five years from the date appointed for its first meeting unless dissolved earlier.
II. If a panchayat is dissolved before the expiry of its term, fresh elections must be completed within six months.
III. A panchayat constituted after dissolution serves a fresh full term of five years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Under Article 243E the panchayat constituted after premature dissolution serves only the remainder of the original term. No fresh election is held if the remainder is less than six months.

questions.q: The superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of all elections to panchayats is vested in the State Election Commission under which Article?
questions.exp: Article 243K vests these powers in the State Election Commission; the State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor and can be removed only in the manner and on the grounds of a High Court judge.

questions.q: The State Finance Commission for reviewing the financial position of panchayats is constituted by the Governor at what interval?
questions.exp: Article 243I requires the Governor to constitute a State Finance Commission every five years. Article 243Y extends its remit to municipalities.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about reservation in panchayats under Article 243D:
I. Seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in proportion to their population in the panchayat area.
II. Not less than one-third of the total number of seats is reserved for women.
III. Reservation for women applies also within the seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Offices of chairpersons are also reserved. Reservation for backward classes is optional and left to the State legislature.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Type of urban body)   List-II (Area)
A. Nagar Panchayat   1. A larger urban area
B. Municipal Council   2. An area in transition from rural to urban
C. Municipal Corporation   3. A metropolitan area of ten lakh or more population
D. Metropolitan Planning Committee   4. A smaller urban area
questions.exp: Article 243Q defines the three types of municipalities; the Governor specifies the area having regard to population, density, revenue, non-agricultural employment and economic importance. Article 243ZE covers metropolitan areas.

questions.q: Under Article 243S, the constitution of Ward Committees is mandatory in municipalities having a population of:
questions.exp: Ward Committees consisting of one or more wards are compulsory within the territorial area of a municipality having a population of three lakh or more.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the District Planning Committee:
I. It is provided for under Article 243ZD.
II. Four-fifths of its members are elected by the elected members of the district panchayat and the municipalities in the district from amongst themselves.
III. Its seats are filled in proportion to the ratio of rural and urban population in the district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The DPC consolidates the plans prepared by panchayats and municipalities and forwards the draft development plan for the district to the State Government.

questions.q: A Metropolitan Planning Committee is constituted under Article 243ZE for a metropolitan area having a population of:
questions.exp: A metropolitan area is one with a population of ten lakh or more comprising two or more municipalities or panchayats. Two-thirds of the Committee's members are elected by elected representatives of the local bodies in that area.

questions.q: The Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act was enacted in which year?
questions.exp: PESA was enacted in December 1996 to extend Part IX of the Constitution, with modifications, to the Fifth Schedule areas, which the 73rd Amendment had left out under Article 243M.

questions.q: PESA, 1996 was enacted largely on the recommendations of which committee?
questions.exp: The committee headed by Dilip Singh Bhuria submitted its report in 1995, recommending self-governance for tribal areas through empowered Gram Sabhas.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the powers of the Gram Sabha under PESA, 1996:
I. It has ownership of minor forest produce.
II. It must be consulted before land acquisition in Scheduled Areas.
III. Its recommendation is mandatory for grant of prospecting licences for minor minerals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Gram Sabha under PESA also approves plans and beneficiaries, manages village markets and can enforce prohibition on the sale of intoxicants.

questions.q: PESA, 1996 currently applies to the Fifth Schedule areas of how many States?
questions.exp: Ten States have Fifth Schedule areas covered by PESA: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha and Rajasthan.

questions.q: Which one of the following States does NOT have Scheduled Areas covered by PESA, 1996?
questions.exp: West Bengal has no Fifth Schedule area. Rajasthan's Scheduled Areas lie mainly in the southern districts such as Banswara, Dungarpur, Pratapgarh and parts of Udaipur, Sirohi and Chittorgarh.

questions.q: Which was the first princely state in Rajasthan to enact its own Gram Panchayat Act?
questions.exp: Bikaner state enacted a Gram Panchayat Act as early as 1928. Jodhpur, Jaipur, Udaipur, Sirohi, Bharatpur and Karauli also passed panchayat legislation before independence.

questions.q: Which one of the following princely states of Rajasthan is NOT usually listed among those that enacted panchayat legislation before independence?
questions.exp: Jodhpur, Bharatpur, Jaipur, Sirohi, Udaipur and Karauli enacted laws on panchayats before independence, in addition to Bikaner's Act of 1928. Dholpur is not part of that list.

questions.q: Lord Ripon's Resolution of 1882, regarded as the Magna Carta of local self-government in India, is associated with which of the following?
opts: Creation of the first Municipal Corporation in India
Introduction of elected local boards with non-official chairmen
Transfer of local self-government to Indian ministers
Constitution of the Royal Commission on Decentralisation
questions.exp: Ripon's Resolution provided for local boards with a majority of elected non-official members and non-official chairmen, earning him the title 'Father of local self-government in India'.

questions.q: Which Article bars the interference of courts in electoral matters relating to panchayats?
questions.exp: Article 243-O bars courts from questioning the validity of any law relating to delimitation of constituencies or allotment of seats, and provides that panchayat elections can be challenged only by an election petition. Article 243ZG does the same for municipalities.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 15th Finance Commission's grants to local governments for 2021-26:
I. The total recommended amount is about Rs 4.36 lakh crore.
II. Rural local bodies were allotted a larger share than urban local bodies.
III. Health grants were also to be channelled through local governments.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct: about Rs 2.36 lakh crore for rural and Rs 1.21 lakh crore for urban local bodies, plus Rs 70,051 crore of health grants. The States' share in central taxes was fixed at 41 per cent.

questions.q: Grants recommended by the 15th Finance Commission for local bodies are distributed among the States on the basis of population and area with what weightage?
opts: Population 60 per cent and area 40 per cent
Population 75 per cent and area 25 per cent
Population 90 per cent and area 10 per cent
questions.exp: The weightage is 90 per cent for population and 10 per cent for area. The Commission also recommended that States constitute State Finance Commissions and act upon their reports.

questions.q: In a Municipal Corporation, who is the executive head responsible for implementing the decisions of the corporation?
opts: The Chairman of the Standing Committee
questions.exp: The Municipal Commissioner, usually an IAS or senior State service officer appointed by the State Government, is the executive head, while the Mayor is the ceremonial and deliberative head.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in correct chronological order:
I. Balwant Rai Mehta Committee report
II. Ashok Mehta Committee report
III. L.M. Singhvi Committee report
IV. 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act
questions.exp: Balwant Rai Mehta reported in 1957, Ashok Mehta in 1978, L.M. Singhvi in 1986 and the 73rd Amendment was enacted in 1992, coming into force in 1993.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act made it obligatory for States to hold panchayat elections at fixed intervals.
Reason (R): Article 243E provides a fixed five-year term for every panchayat and requires elections to be completed before the expiry of that term.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: Article 243E fixes the five-year term and mandates completion of elections before expiry, which is precisely why regular elections became obligatory after 1993.

chapters.title: Constitutional, Statutory and Executive Bodies
factsheet: Election Commission of India - Article 324; came into existence 25 January 1950; became a permanent multi-member body (CEC + 2 ECs) from 1 October 1993.
CEC is removed in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court; other Election Commissioners are removed by the President only on the recommendation of the CEC.

CEC and Other ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 - Selection Committee = Prime Minister (chair) + a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM + Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha; a Search Committee headed by the Cabinet Secretary sends a panel of five names.
EC tenure 6 years or 65 years, whichever earlier; no re-appointment. Elections to panchayats and municipalities are conducted by the State Election Commission (Art. 243K/243ZA), not the ECI.

Art. 325 - no exclusion from electoral rolls on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex; Art. 326 - adult suffrage, voting age lowered 21 to 18 by the 61st Amendment, 1988; Art. 329 - bar to interference by courts in electoral matters.

Model Code of Conduct is non-statutory (evolved from Kerala, 1960); EVMs first used at Paravur, Kerala (1982); VVPAT first used at the Noksen (Nagaland) bye-election, 2013; NOTA introduced in 2013 after PUCL v. Union of India.

Delimitation Commission is a statutory (not constitutional) body - four so far: 1952, 1963, 1973, 2002. The 84th Amendment froze seat allocation till 2026; the 87th Amendment (2003) shifted delimitation to the 2001 Census.

UPSC - Articles 315-323. Chairman and members appointed by the President; term 6 years or 65 years (State PSC: 6 years or 62 years). At least one-half of the members must have held office for at least ten years under the Union or a State.

Art. 316 appointment; Art. 317 removal (only by the President on a report of the Supreme Court after inquiry); Art. 318 conditions of service; Art. 320 functions; Art. 321 extension of functions; Art. 322 expenses charged on the Consolidated Fund; Art. 323 reports.

UPSC is NOT consulted on reservations for backward classes (Art. 320(4) proviso). UPSC Chairman is ineligible for any further government employment; a UPSC member may become UPSC Chairman or Chairman of a State PSC.

Joint State Public Service Commission (Art. 315(2)) - created by Parliament by law on the request of two or more state legislatures; its chairman and members are appointed and removed by the President.

CAG - Art. 148; appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal; term 6 years or 65 years; removed like a Supreme Court judge; salary equal to a Supreme Court judge and charged on the Consolidated Fund of India; ineligible for further office under the Union or any State.

Art. 149 - duties and powers prescribed by Parliament (CAG's Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service Act, 1971); Art. 150 - form of accounts prescribed by the President on the advice of the CAG; Art. 151 - Union reports to the President, State reports to the Governor.

First CAG of India: V. Narahari Rao. Ambedkar called the CAG probably the most important officer under the Constitution. Accounts and audit were separated in 1976. CAG is the friend, philosopher and guide of the Public Accounts Committee.

Finance Commission - Art. 280; constituted by the President every fifth year or earlier; Chairman + 4 other members; qualifications fixed by the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951; recommendations are advisory only.

FC functions: distribution of net proceeds of taxes between Union and States and inter se among States; principles of grants-in-aid out of the Consolidated Fund of India (Art. 275); measures to augment State funds to supplement panchayat and municipality resources (added by the 73rd and 74th Amendments); any other matter referred by the President. State borrowing limits (Art. 293) are NOT its mandate.

First FC (1951) - Chairman K.C. Neogy. 14th FC (Y.V. Reddy) raised devolution to 42%; 15th FC (N.K. Singh) recommended 41%. 16th FC constituted 31 December 2023 under Arvind Panagariya; report for 2026-27 to 2030-31 submitted 17 November 2025.

Attorney General - Art. 76; appointed by the President; must be qualified to be a Supreme Court judge; holds office during the pleasure of the President; right of audience in all courts and to speak in both Houses without a vote. First AG: M.C. Setalvad. Advocate General of a State - Art. 165.

National Commission for SCs - Art. 338; National Commission for STs - Art. 338A (both by the 89th Amendment, 2003; NCST effective 19 February 2004); National Commission for Backward Classes - Art. 338B (102nd Amendment, 2018). Each: Chairperson, Vice-Chairperson and three other members appointed by the President.
Art. 350B - Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, inserted by the 7th Amendment, 1956 on the recommendation of the States Reorganisation Commission; appointed by the President.

NHRC - Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993. Chairperson: a person who has been Chief Justice of India OR a Judge of the Supreme Court (widened by the 2019 Amendment). Term 3 years or 70 years (reduced from 5 years in 2019).

NHRC composition after 2019: Chairperson + 5 full-time members (one serving/retired SC judge, one serving/retired HC Chief Justice, three members of whom at least one woman) + deemed members (chairpersons of NCSC, NCST, NCW, NCBC, NCPCR and the Chief Commissioner for Persons with Disabilities).

NHRC selection committee: Prime Minister (chair), Speaker of the Lok Sabha, Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, Leaders of Opposition in both Houses, Union Home Minister. NHRC cannot inquire into a violation more than one year old; its recommendations are not binding; it cannot punish.

CVC - recommended by the Santhanam Committee on Prevention of Corruption; set up by executive resolution on 11 February 1964; made statutory by the CVC Act, 2003 following Vineet Narain (1997). First CVC: Nittoor Srinivasa Rau.

CVC composition: Central Vigilance Commissioner (chairperson) + not more than two Vigilance Commissioners; appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee of the Prime Minister, the Union Home Minister and the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha; term 4 years or 65 years. CVC exercises superintendence over the CBI in Prevention of Corruption Act cases.

CBI - set up 1 April 1963 by a Home Ministry resolution; derives police powers from the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946; needs State consent under Section 6; under the Ministry of Personnel (DoPT). Director appointed on the recommendation of the PM, the LoP in Lok Sabha and the CJI or an SC judge nominated by him; minimum tenure 2 years, extendable up to 5 years (2021 amendment).

Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 (assent 1 January 2014, in force 16 January 2014) - Lokpal = Chairperson + maximum 8 members, at least half judicial; term 5 years or 70 years. Selection Committee: PM, Speaker of Lok Sabha, LoP in Lok Sabha, CJI or his nominee, one eminent jurist. First Lokpal: Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose (2019).

NITI Aayog - executive resolution of 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission (set up 15 March 1950 by a Cabinet resolution). PM is ex officio Chairperson; Governing Council = all Chief Ministers + Lieutenant Governors of UTs; CEO of the rank of Secretary to the Government of India. First Vice-Chairman: Arvind Panagariya. It is a think tank and allocates no funds.

National Development Council - set up 6 August 1952; neither constitutional nor statutory; chaired by the Prime Minister. Law Commission of India - a non-statutory executive body; the first Law Commission of independent India (1955) was chaired by M.C. Setalvad.

NGT - National Green Tribunal Act, 2010; established 18 October 2010, principal bench at New Delhi; India was the third country in the world (after Australia and New Zealand) to set up such a body. CCI - Competition Act, 2002, established 14 October 2003. NCW - National Commission for Women Act, 1990 (functioning from 31 January 1992). NCPCR - Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005 (set up March 2007).

questions.q: The Election Commission of India is constituted under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.exp: Article 324 vests the superintendence, direction and control of the preparation of electoral rolls and the conduct of all elections to Parliament, State Legislatures and the offices of President and Vice-President in the Election Commission.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Election Commission of India:
I. The Chief Election Commissioner can be removed from office in the same manner and on the same grounds as a Judge of the Supreme Court.
II. An Election Commissioner other than the Chief Election Commissioner can be removed by the President only on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner.
III. The Election Commission conducts elections to panchayats and municipalities in the States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Elections to panchayats and municipalities are conducted by the State Election Commission under Articles 243K and 243ZA, not by the Election Commission of India.

questions.q: Under the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023, the Selection Committee that recommends names for appointment consists of
opts: The Prime Minister, a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister and the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha
The Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and the Chief Justice of India
The President, the Prime Minister and the Chief Justice of India
The Vice-President, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha and the Prime Minister
questions.exp: The 2023 Act replaced the Chief Justice of India (directed by the Supreme Court in Anoop Baranwal, 2023) with a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister. A Search Committee headed by the Cabinet Secretary first prepares a panel of five names.

questions.q: The voting age in India was reduced from 21 years to 18 years by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
questions.exp: The 61st Amendment Act, 1988 amended Article 326 to lower the voting age to 18 years. It took effect from 28 March 1989.

questions.q: NOTA (None of the Above) was introduced as an option for voters in 2013 following the Supreme Court's judgment in
opts: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
Indra Sawhney v. Union of India
People's Union for Civil Liberties v. Union of India
questions.exp: In PUCL v. Union of India (2013) the Supreme Court directed the Election Commission to provide a NOTA button on EVMs to protect the secrecy of a negative vote.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Article)   List-II (Subject)
A. Article 324   1. No person to be ineligible for inclusion in electoral rolls on grounds of religion, race, caste or sex
B. Article 325   2. Superintendence, direction and control of elections vested in the Election Commission
C. Article 326   3. Bar to interference by courts in electoral matters
D. Article 329   4. Elections to the House of the People and State Legislative Assemblies on the basis of adult suffrage
questions.exp: Article 324 - Election Commission; 325 - one general electoral roll with no discrimination; 326 - adult suffrage; 329 - bar to interference by courts in electoral matters.

questions.q: The Delimitation Commission of India is
opts: a statutory body constituted under an Act of Parliament
a body constituted by an executive order of the Union Cabinet
a constitutional body appointed under Article 82
a standing committee of the Election Commission of India
questions.exp: Delimitation Commissions are set up by Acts of Parliament; four have been constituted so far - 1952, 1963, 1973 and 2002. The 84th Amendment froze the allocation of seats till 2026.

questions.q: The Union Public Service Commission is dealt with in which group of Articles of the Constitution?
questions.exp: Part XIV of the Constitution, Articles 315 to 323, deals with the Public Service Commissions for the Union and the States.

questions.q: A member of the Union Public Service Commission holds office for a term of six years or until he attains the age of
questions.exp: The age limit for UPSC is 65 years; for a State Public Service Commission and a Joint State PSC it is 62 years.

questions.q: A member of a State Public Service Commission can be removed on the ground of misbehaviour by
opts: the Governor, after an inquiry by the High Court
the Governor, on the advice of the State Council of Ministers
the State Legislature by a resolution passed by a special majority
the President, after an inquiry held by the Supreme Court
questions.exp: Under Article 317, the chairman or a member of any Public Service Commission - Union, State or Joint - can be removed only by the President on a report of the Supreme Court after inquiry. Though appointed by the Governor, a State PSC member is removed by the President.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Union Public Service Commission:
I. Not less than one-half of the members of the Commission must be persons who have held office for at least ten years under the Government of India or a State Government.
II. The expenses of the Commission are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
III. The Chairman of the UPSC is eligible for re-appointment as Chairman on the expiry of his term.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Under Article 319 the Chairman of the UPSC is not eligible for any further employment either under the Government of India or under a State Government, including re-appointment.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a function of the Union Public Service Commission?
opts: Conducting examinations for appointment to the services of the Union
Advising on disciplinary matters affecting a person serving under the Government of India
Advising on claims for reimbursement of legal expenses incurred by a civil servant in defending legal proceedings
Making reservations of appointments in favour of any backward class of citizens
questions.exp: The proviso to Article 320(4) expressly excludes the UPSC from being consulted on reservations in appointments for backward classes. The other three are duties listed in Article 320.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Article)   List-II (Provision relating to Public Service Commissions)
A. Article 315   1. Removal and suspension of a member of a Public Service Commission
B. Article 317   2. Constitution of Public Service Commissions for the Union and the States
C. Article 320   3. Expenses charged on the Consolidated Fund
D. Article 322   4. Functions of Public Service Commissions
questions.exp: Article 315 - constitution; 317 - removal and suspension; 320 - functions; 322 - expenses charged on the Consolidated Fund of India or of the State.

questions.q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India is appointed by the President under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.exp: Article 148 provides for the appointment of the CAG by the President by warrant under his hand and seal, and for his removal in the same manner as a Judge of the Supreme Court.

questions.q: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India holds office for a term of six years or until he attains the age of
questions.exp: The CAG holds office for six years or up to the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier, and is thereafter ineligible for any further office under the Government of India or of any State.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Comptroller and Auditor General of India:
I. He can be removed from office by the President in the same manner as a Judge of the Supreme Court.
II. His salary is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
III. He is eligible for further office under the Government of India after ceasing to hold office.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Article 148(4) bars the CAG from holding any further office under the Government of India or of any State after he ceases to hold office.

questions.q: The duties and powers of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India are prescribed by Parliament under
questions.exp: Article 149 empowers Parliament to prescribe the CAG's duties and powers; this was done by the Comptroller and Auditor General's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Comptroller and Auditor General of India is NOT correct?
opts: He exercises control over the issue of money from the Consolidated Fund at the time of expenditure.
He is the head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department.
He audits the accounts of government companies.
He audits all expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India and of each State.
questions.exp: Unlike his British counterpart, the Indian CAG is only an auditor and not a comptroller - he has no control over the issue of money from the Consolidated Fund, and his audit is entirely post-facto.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Article)   List-II (Provision relating to the CAG)
A. Article 148   1. Form of accounts of the Union and the States
B. Article 149   2. Audit reports to be laid before the legislature
C. Article 150   3. Appointment, oath and conditions of service
D. Article 151   4. Duties and powers as prescribed by Parliament
questions.exp: Article 148 - appointment and service conditions; 149 - duties and powers; 150 - form of accounts; 151 - audit reports.

questions.q: The Finance Commission is constituted by the President of India under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.exp: Article 280 requires the President to constitute a Finance Commission every fifth year, or earlier if he considers it necessary. Article 275 deals with statutory grants-in-aid to States.

questions.q: The Finance Commission consists of a Chairman and
questions.exp: Article 280(1) provides for a Chairman and four other members. Their qualifications and the manner of selection are laid down in the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a function assigned to the Finance Commission under Article 280 of the Constitution?
opts: Recommending the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States
Recommending the principles governing grants-in-aid to the States out of the Consolidated Fund of India
Fixing the annual borrowing limits of State Governments under Article 293
Recommending measures needed to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of panchayats and municipalities
questions.exp: Borrowing limits of States under Article 293 are decided by the Union Government, not the Finance Commission. The clauses relating to panchayats and municipalities were added to Article 280(3) by the 73rd and 74th Amendments.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Finance Commission of India:
I. The qualifications of its members are determined by Parliament by law.
II. Its recommendations are binding on the Government of India.
III. The recommendations relating to panchayats and municipalities were added to its terms of reference by the 73rd and 74th Amendments.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Finance Commission's recommendations are advisory only; the Union Government lays them before Parliament with an explanatory memorandum on the action taken.

questions.q: The Sixteenth Finance Commission, which submitted its report for the award period 2026-27 to 2030-31, was chaired by
questions.exp: The 16th Finance Commission was constituted on 31 December 2023 under Dr. Arvind Panagariya and submitted its report to the President on 17 November 2025. N.K. Singh headed the 15th and Y.V. Reddy the 14th Finance Commission.

questions.q: The Fifteenth Finance Commission recommended that the share of the States in the divisible pool of central taxes be
questions.exp: The 15th Finance Commission recommended 41 per cent, one percentage point lower than the 42 per cent recommended by the 14th Finance Commission, to account for the conversion of Jammu and Kashmir into Union Territories.

questions.q: The Attorney General of India is appointed by the President under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.exp: Article 76 provides for the Attorney General of India, the highest law officer of the Union. Article 165 provides for the Advocate General of a State.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Attorney General of India:
I. He must be a person qualified to be appointed a Judge of the Supreme Court.
II. He has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of both Houses of Parliament, but without a right to vote.
III. He holds office for a fixed term of five years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Attorney General holds office during the pleasure of the President and has no fixed tenure. M.C. Setalvad was independent India's first Attorney General.

questions.q: The National Commission for Backward Classes was given constitutional status by inserting Article 338B through the
questions.exp: The 102nd Amendment Act, 2018 inserted Articles 338B and 342A, giving the NCBC constitutional status. The 105th Amendment, 2021 restored the power of States to identify socially and educationally backward classes.

questions.q: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes was created as a separate body by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
questions.exp: The 89th Amendment Act, 2003 bifurcated the erstwhile combined commission, retaining the NCSC under Article 338 and creating the NCST under Article 338A, which came into existence on 19 February 2004.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Body)   List-II (Constitutional provision)
A. National Commission for Scheduled Castes   1. Article 338A
B. National Commission for Scheduled Tribes   2. Article 350B
C. National Commission for Backward Classes   3. Article 338
D. Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities   4. Article 338B
questions.exp: NCSC - Article 338; NCST - Article 338A; NCBC - Article 338B; Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities - Article 350B.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a constitutional body?
questions.exp: The National Commission for Women is a statutory body set up under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990 and began functioning on 31 January 1992. The other three are constitutional bodies.

questions.q: The National Human Rights Commission was established under
opts: the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955
the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
questions.exp: The NHRC is a statutory body constituted under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, which also provides for State Human Rights Commissions and Human Rights Courts.

questions.q: After the Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019, who among the following is eligible to be appointed Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission?
opts: Only a person who has been Chief Justice of India
Any person who has been Chief Justice of a High Court
A person who has been Chief Justice of India or a Judge of the Supreme Court
Any person of eminence in the field of human rights
questions.exp: The 2019 Amendment widened the eligibility, which was earlier confined to a retired Chief Justice of India, to include a retired Judge of the Supreme Court. Similarly, a State Human Rights Commission may now be headed by a former Chief Justice or Judge of a High Court.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Human Rights Commission:
I. Its Chairperson and members are appointed by the President on the recommendation of a six-member committee headed by the Prime Minister.
II. The term of the Chairperson and members is three years or until the age of seventy years, whichever is earlier.
III. The Commission can inquire into a violation of human rights that occurred more than one year before the complaint.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Section 36(2) of the Act bars the NHRC from inquiring into a matter after the expiry of one year from the date on which the act constituting the violation is alleged to have been committed. The 2019 Amendment reduced the term from five to three years.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the National Human Rights Commission is NOT correct?
opts: Its recommendations are advisory and not binding on the government.
It has the powers of a civil court while inquiring into complaints.
It can intervene in any proceeding involving an allegation of violation of human rights pending before a court.
It can itself punish a public servant found guilty of violating human rights.
questions.exp: The NHRC has no power to punish; it can only recommend action, compensation or prosecution to the concerned government or authority, which must report the action taken within one month.

questions.q: As per the Protection of Human Rights Act as amended in 2019, apart from the Chairperson, how many full-time members does the National Human Rights Commission have?
questions.exp: The 2019 Amendment raised the number of members from four to five - one serving or retired Judge of the Supreme Court, one serving or retired Chief Justice of a High Court, and three members having knowledge of human rights, of whom at least one must be a woman.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a member of the committee that recommends appointments to the National Human Rights Commission?
questions.exp: The selection committee consists of the Prime Minister (chairperson), the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, the Leaders of Opposition in both Houses and the Union Home Minister.

questions.q: The Central Vigilance Commission was set up in 1964 on the recommendation of
questions.exp: The Committee on Prevention of Corruption headed by K. Santhanam recommended the creation of the CVC, which was set up by a government resolution on 11 February 1964. Nittoor Srinivasa Rau was the first Central Vigilance Commissioner.

questions.q: The Central Vigilance Commission was conferred statutory status by an Act of Parliament in the year
questions.exp: The CVC Act, 2003 made the Commission statutory, giving effect to the Supreme Court's directions in the Vineet Narain (Jain Hawala) case of 1997.

questions.q: The Central Vigilance Commissioner is appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee consisting of the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and
opts: the Union Minister of Home Affairs
the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.exp: The three-member committee under the CVC Act, 2003 comprises the Prime Minister as Chairperson, the Minister of Home Affairs and the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Central Vigilance Commission:
I. It consists of a Central Vigilance Commissioner and not more than two Vigilance Commissioners.
II. Its members hold office for a term of four years or until they attain the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
III. It exercises superintendence over the functioning of the Central Bureau of Investigation in matters relating to the Prevention of Corruption Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. The Central Vigilance Commissioner and Vigilance Commissioners are removed by the President on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity after an inquiry by the Supreme Court.

questions.q: The Central Bureau of Investigation derives its police powers from
opts: the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946
questions.exp: The CBI was created by a Home Ministry resolution on 1 April 1963 and has no separate statute of its own; it draws its powers from the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946 and needs the consent of a State under Section 6 of that Act to investigate there.

questions.q: The Director of the Central Bureau of Investigation is appointed on the recommendation of a committee comprising the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and
opts: the Chief Justice of India or a Supreme Court Judge nominated by him
questions.exp: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 amended the DSPE Act to provide this three-member collegium. The Director has a minimum tenure of two years, extendable up to five years under the 2021 amendment.

questions.q: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act was enacted by Parliament in the year
questions.exp: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 received presidential assent on 1 January 2014 and came into force on 16 January 2014. Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose became India's first Lokpal in March 2019.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Lokpal:
I. The Lokpal consists of a Chairperson and a maximum of eight members.
II. Not less than fifty per cent of the members shall be judicial members.
III. The Chairperson and members hold office for a term of five years or until the age of seventy years, whichever is earlier.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Selection Committee consists of the Prime Minister, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, the Chief Justice of India or a Judge nominated by him, and one eminent jurist.

questions.q: NITI Aayog was constituted on
questions.exp: NITI Aayog was set up by an executive resolution of the Union Cabinet on 1 January 2015, replacing the Planning Commission which had itself been created by a Cabinet resolution in March 1950.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about NITI Aayog:
I. The Prime Minister is its ex officio Chairperson.
II. Its Governing Council comprises the Chief Ministers of all States and the Lieutenant Governors of Union Territories.
III. It is a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: NITI Aayog is neither constitutional nor statutory; it was created by an executive resolution. Its full-time organisational framework includes a Vice-Chairperson, full-time and part-time members, ex officio members and a Chief Executive Officer of the rank of Secretary to the Government of India.

questions.q: The National Development Council was set up in the year
questions.exp: The NDC was constituted on 6 August 1952 by an executive resolution and is neither a constitutional nor a statutory body. It is chaired by the Prime Minister.

questions.q:
Arrange the following bodies in the chronological order of their establishment, beginning with the earliest:
I. Central Vigilance Commission
II. National Human Rights Commission
III. Central Information Commission
IV. NITI Aayog
questions.exp: Central Vigilance Commission 1964; National Human Rights Commission 1993; Central Information Commission 2005; NITI Aayog 2015.

questions.q:
Arrange the following Acts in the chronological order of their enactment, beginning with the earliest:
I. Protection of Human Rights Act
II. Delhi Special Police Establishment Act
III. Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act
IV. Central Vigilance Commission Act
questions.exp: Delhi Special Police Establishment Act 1946; Protection of Human Rights Act 1993; Central Vigilance Commission Act 2003; Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Body)   List-II (Authority that appoints its head)
A. Comptroller and Auditor General   1. President, on the recommendation of a committee of the PM, Home Minister and Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha
B. Central Vigilance Commissioner   2. President, by warrant under his hand and seal
C. Chief Information Commissioner   3. President, on the recommendation of a committee of the PM, Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the PM
D. Chairperson of NITI Aayog   4. Holds office ex officio as Prime Minister
questions.exp: The CAG is appointed directly by warrant; the CVC and the CIC each have a statutory three-member selection committee; the Prime Minister is ex officio Chairperson of NITI Aayog.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of a body and the year of its establishment is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The Central Information Commission was constituted in 2005 under Section 12 of the Right to Information Act, 2005; the Act came fully into force on 12 October 2005.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Body)   List-II (Statute or provision under which it is set up)
A. National Commission for Women   1. Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
B. National Commission for Protection of Child Rights   2. Right to Information Act, 2005
C. Central Information Commission   3. National Commission for Women Act, 1990
D. National Green Tribunal   4. National Green Tribunal Act, 2010
questions.exp: NCW - Act of 1990; NCPCR - Act of 2005; CIC - Section 12 of the RTI Act, 2005; NGT - Act of 2010.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Office)   List-II (First incumbent in India)
