A. Comptroller and Auditor General   1. Nittoor Srinivasa Rau
B. Central Vigilance Commissioner   2. Wajahat Habibullah
C. Chief Information Commissioner   3. Pinaki Chandra Ghose
D. Lokpal   4. V. Narahari Rao
questions.exp: V. Narahari Rao was the first CAG of independent India, Nittoor Srinivasa Rau the first Central Vigilance Commissioner (1964), Wajahat Habibullah the first Chief Information Commissioner (2005) and Justice Pinaki Chandra Ghose the first Lokpal (2019).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Scheduled Castes:
I. While investigating any matter it has all the powers of a civil court trying a suit.
II. It presents an annual report to the President, who causes it to be laid before both Houses of Parliament.
III. Before the 89th Amendment Act, 2003 there was a single National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. The 89th Amendment bifurcated the combined commission into the NCSC under Article 338 and the NCST under Article 338A.

chapters.title: Governance: Public Policy, Citizen Charter, Social Audit, Grievance Redressal, RTI
factsheet: Public policy - Thomas Dye: 'whatever governments choose to do or not to do'. Harold Lasswell is regarded as the father of the policy sciences.
Stages of the policy process: problem identification and agenda setting - policy formulation - policy adoption/legitimation - policy implementation - policy evaluation.

Policy models: rational-comprehensive and bounded rationality (Herbert Simon), incrementalism or 'muddling through' (Charles Lindblom), mixed scanning (Amitai Etzioni), garbage-can model (Cohen, March and Olsen), systems model (David Easton - inputs, conversion, outputs, feedback).
Citizen's Charter originated in the United Kingdom in 1991 under Prime Minister John Major; its six principles are Quality, Choice, Standards, Value, Accountability and Transparency.

India adopted the Citizen's Charter after the Conference of Chief Ministers on 24 May 1997, which approved the 'Action Plan for Effective and Responsive Government'; DARPG is the nodal agency and the first charters were issued in 1997.

Components of a Citizen's Charter: (1) Vision and Mission statement, (2) details of business transacted by the organisation, (3) details of clients, (4) details of services provided to each client group, (5) details of the grievance redress mechanism and how to access it, (6) expectations from the clients.

A Citizen's Charter is NOT legally enforceable or justiciable; penalty or punishment for defaulting officials is not one of its components. Its main criticism is that it is drafted without consulting the citizens it serves.

Sevottam - DARPG's service delivery excellence model; three modules: Citizen's Charter, Public Grievance Redress, and Service Delivery Capability. Its assessment standard is IS 15700:2005 of the Bureau of Indian Standards.

Second ARC - constituted 31 August 2005; chairman Veerappa Moily (later V. Ramachandran); submitted 15 reports. First report: 'Right to Information - Master Key to Good Governance' (2006); 4th 'Ethics in Governance'; 11th 'Promoting e-Governance - The SMART Way Forward'; 12th 'Citizen Centric Administration - The Heart of Governance'.
First ARC - constituted 1966, chairman Morarji Desai and later K. Hanumanthaiah; submitted 20 reports; recommended the setting up of Lokpal and Lokayuktas (1966).
SMART governance = Simple, Moral, Accountable, Responsive and Transparent. The World Bank popularised the term 'good governance' in its 1992 report 'Governance and Development'.

The United Nations lists eight attributes of good governance: participation, rule of law, transparency, responsiveness, consensus orientation, equity and inclusiveness, effectiveness and efficiency, and accountability.

Social audit - first given a statutory mandate in India by Section 17 of MGNREGA, 2005, which requires the Gram Sabha to conduct social audits of all works in the Gram Panchayat; the MGNREGA Audit of Scheme Rules, 2011 were framed in consultation with the CAG.
Meghalaya was the first state to enact a dedicated social audit law - the Meghalaya Community Participation and Public Services Social Audit Act, 2017.

Rajasthan's Jan Sunwai (public hearing) tradition grew out of the Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan founded in 1990 at Devdungri, Rajsamand (Aruna Roy, Nikhil Dey, Shankar Singh); slogan 'Hamara Paisa, Hamara Hisab'. It led the national campaign for the right to information.

CPGRAMS - Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System, the online grievance portal run by DARPG (Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions). The redressal timeline was cut from 30 days to 21 days in August 2024; an appeal lies to the Appellate Authority within 30 days.

RTI Act, 2005 - assent 15 June 2005; came fully into force 12 October 2005; replaced the Freedom of Information Act, 2002; extends to the whole of India (Jammu and Kashmir's separate RTI Act was repealed in 2019).

RTI preamble: 'to provide for setting out the practical regime of right to information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority'.

Section 4 - suo motu / proactive disclosure by every public authority; Section 6 - request for information (no reason need be given, only contact details); Section 5 - designation of PIOs and Assistant PIOs.

Section 7 time limits: 30 days ordinarily; 48 hours where the information concerns the life or liberty of a person; 35 days if the application is filed with an Assistant PIO; 40 days where third-party interest is involved; free information if the deadline is missed.

Section 8 - ten grounds of exemption; Section 8(2) - public interest override; Section 8(3) - information more than 20 years old ordinarily to be supplied; Section 9 - rejection on copyright grounds; Section 10 - severability; Section 11 - third-party information.
Section 19 - first appeal to the officer senior to the PIO within 30 days; second appeal to the CIC or SIC within 90 days; the burden of proving that a refusal was justified lies on the PIO.
Section 20 - penalty of Rs. 250 per day of delay, subject to a maximum of Rs. 25,000, imposed on the Public Information Officer, plus recommendation for disciplinary action for persistent default.

Section 22 - the RTI Act overrides the Official Secrets Act, 1923 and any inconsistent law; Section 23 - bar on the jurisdiction of courts; Section 24 - intelligence and security organisations listed in the Second Schedule are exempt, except for allegations of corruption and human rights violations.

Central Information Commission (Section 12) - Chief Information Commissioner and not more than ten Information Commissioners, appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee of the Prime Minister (chair), the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister. First CIC: Wajahat Habibullah.

State Information Commission (Section 15) - State Chief Information Commissioner and up to ten State Information Commissioners appointed by the Governor on the recommendation of a committee of the Chief Minister (chair), the Leader of Opposition in the Legislative Assembly and a State Cabinet Minister nominated by the Chief Minister.

RTI (Amendment) Act, 2019 amended Sections 13, 16 and 27: the term and salary of the CIC, ICs and their state counterparts are no longer fixed in the statute but are 'as prescribed by the Central Government'. The RTI Rules, 2019 fix the term at three years (earlier five years); the upper age limit of 65 years remains.

Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014 (assent 9 May 2014) - allows public interest disclosures to the Central or State Vigilance Commission and protects the complainant's identity; it followed the murder of Satyendra Dubey (2003) and the 2nd ARC's 'Ethics in Governance' report. It is still not fully operational.

Right to public services: Madhya Pradesh was the first state (Public Service Guarantee Act, 2010, effective 25 September 2010), followed by Bihar (2011). Rajasthan enacted the Guaranteed Delivery of Public Services Act, 2011 and the Rajasthan Right to Hearing Act, 2012 - the first such law in India.

E-governance: National e-Governance Plan approved 18 May 2006 with 27 Mission Mode Projects (later 31); e-Kranti (NeGP 2.0) approved March 2015 with 44 MMPs; Digital India launched 1 July 2015 with nine pillars and three vision areas; UMANG launched 2017; DBT launched 1 January 2013; UIDAI set up January 2009 and made statutory by the Aadhaar Act, 2016 (first Aadhaar issued 29 September 2010 at Tembhli, Nandurbar, Maharashtra). Interaction types: G2C, G2B, G2G and G2E.

questions.q: Public policy has been defined as 'whatever governments choose to do or not to do' by
questions.exp: This widely quoted definition is by Thomas R. Dye. Harold Lasswell is regarded as the father of the policy sciences and gave a seven-stage model of the policy process.

questions.q: The incremental model of public policy making, popularly described as 'the science of muddling through', is associated with
questions.exp: Charles Lindblom's 1959 article 'The Science of Muddling Through' argued that policy makers make small incremental changes to existing policy rather than comprehensive rational choices.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Model of policy making)   List-II (Thinker)
A. Bounded rationality   1. David Easton
B. Incrementalism   2. Amitai Etzioni
C. Mixed scanning   3. Herbert Simon
D. Systems model   4. Charles Lindblom
questions.exp: Herbert Simon gave bounded rationality, Lindblom incrementalism, Etzioni mixed scanning and David Easton the systems model of the political and policy process.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the public policy process:
I. Agenda setting is the stage at which a problem is recognised as requiring government action.
II. Policy evaluation assesses whether a policy has achieved its stated objectives.
III. Policy implementation is carried out mainly by the legislature.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Implementation is essentially an executive and administrative function; the legislature's role is to legitimise and oversee policy, not to implement it.

questions.q: The concept of the Citizen's Charter was first introduced in 1991 in
questions.exp: The Citizen's Charter was launched in the United Kingdom in 1991 by Prime Minister John Major as a national programme to improve public services.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a component of a Citizen's Charter?
opts: Vision and mission statement of the organisation
Details of the grievance redress mechanism and how to access it
Provision of penalty and punishment for officials who fail to meet the declared standards
Expectations of the organisation from its clients
questions.exp: A Citizen's Charter is a voluntary, non-justiciable declaration of service standards; it contains no penal provision against officials. Its recognised components are the vision and mission statement, details of business transacted, details of clients, details of services to each client group, the grievance redress mechanism, and expectations from clients.

questions.q: In India, the decision to formulate Citizen's Charters for central and state government departments was taken at the Conference of Chief Ministers held in
questions.exp: The Conference of Chief Ministers held on 24 May 1997 adopted the 'Action Plan for Effective and Responsive Government'. The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances is the nodal agency for Citizen's Charters in India.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Citizen's Charter in India:
I. It is a legally enforceable document and a citizen can sue for its breach.
II. The Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances is the nodal agency for Citizen's Charters.
III. A common criticism is that charters are drafted without consulting the citizens and staff concerned.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: A Citizen's Charter is not a legally enforceable or justiciable document; it is a declaration of commitment to service standards.

questions.q: The three modules of the Sevottam model of service delivery excellence are
opts: Citizen's Charter, Public Grievance Redress and Service Delivery Capability
Right to Information, Right to Services and Right to Hearing
questions.exp: Sevottam, developed by DARPG, has three modules - Citizen's Charter, Public Grievance Redress and Service Delivery Capability - and is assessed against the standard IS 15700:2005.

questions.q: The Indian Standard against which an organisation's compliance with the Sevottam model is certified is
questions.exp: IS 15700:2005 of the Bureau of Indian Standards lays down the requirements for a quality management system for service quality by public service organisations.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): A Citizen's Charter does not create legally enforceable rights in favour of a citizen.
Reason (R): A Citizen's Charter is a voluntary declaration by an organisation of the standards of service it commits itself to deliver, and is not a statute.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: Both statements are true and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion. This is why the 2nd ARC recommended that charters be made more meaningful by adding measurable standards and an effective grievance redress mechanism.

questions.q: Social audit was given a statutory basis in India for the first time by
opts: the Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996
questions.exp: Section 17 of the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 makes the Gram Sabha responsible for conducting social audits of all works executed within the Gram Panchayat. The Audit of Scheme Rules were framed in 2011 in consultation with the CAG.

questions.q: Which State became the first in India to enact a dedicated law providing for social audit of public services?
questions.exp: The Meghalaya Community Participation and Public Services Social Audit Act, 2017 was the first state legislation in India to mandate social audit across government schemes and departments.

questions.q: The Jan Sunwai (public hearing) movement that led to the national campaign for the right to information originated in Rajasthan with
questions.exp: The Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan, founded in 1990 at Devdungri in Rajsamand district by Aruna Roy, Nikhil Dey and Shankar Singh, used public hearings to audit muster rolls under the slogan 'Hamara Paisa, Hamara Hisab'.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about social audit:
I. It is an audit of the social and community impact of a programme conducted with the participation of the beneficiaries.
II. Under MGNREGA it is to be conducted by the Gram Sabha at least once in every six months.
III. It replaces the financial audit conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Social audit supplements, and does not replace, the statutory financial audit. MGNREGA requires the Gram Sabha to conduct a social audit of all projects at least once in every six months.

questions.q: In August 2024 the Government of India reduced the timeline for redressal of public grievances received on CPGRAMS to
questions.exp: The timeline was progressively reduced from 60 days to 30 days and then to 21 days in August 2024. A citizen dissatisfied with the disposal may file an appeal before the Appellate Authority within 30 days.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the grievance redress machinery of the Government of India:
I. The Directorate of Public Grievances functions under the Cabinet Secretariat.
II. Every Ministry and Department has a designated Public Grievance Officer.
III. An appeal against the disposal of a grievance on CPGRAMS lies to the Appellate Authority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Directorate of Public Grievances in the Cabinet Secretariat and DARPG in the Ministry of Personnel are the two nodal agencies for public grievances at the central level.

questions.q: The Right to Information Act, 2005 came fully into force with effect from
questions.exp: The Act received presidential assent on 15 June 2005 and came into force in full on 12 October 2005, 120 days after enactment. It replaced the Freedom of Information Act, 2002.

questions.q: Under Section 7 of the Right to Information Act, 2005, information concerning the life or liberty of a person must be supplied within
questions.exp: The normal time limit is 30 days, but where the information sought concerns the life or liberty of a person it must be provided within 48 hours of the receipt of the request.

questions.q: Under Section 20 of the Right to Information Act, 2005, the maximum penalty that can be imposed on a Public Information Officer is
questions.exp: The Information Commission may impose a penalty of Rs. 250 for each day of delay, subject to a maximum of Rs. 25,000, and may also recommend disciplinary action against the PIO.

questions.q: Under Section 19 of the Right to Information Act, 2005, a second appeal to the Central or State Information Commission must be filed within
questions.exp: The first appeal lies to an officer senior to the Public Information Officer within 30 days; the second appeal lies to the Information Commission within 90 days. The burden of proving that a refusal was justified rests on the PIO.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Right to Information Act, 2005:
I. An applicant is not required to give any reason for requesting information.
II. The Act has an overriding effect over the Official Secrets Act, 1923.
III. Intelligence and security organisations listed in the Second Schedule are wholly outside the Act even in respect of allegations of corruption.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Section 6(2) bars asking for reasons and Section 22 gives the Act overriding effect. Under the proviso to Section 24, information relating to allegations of corruption and human rights violations must be furnished even by exempted organisations.

questions.q: The Central Information Commission consists of the Chief Information Commissioner and
opts: not more than five Information Commissioners
not more than eight Information Commissioners
not more than ten Information Commissioners
not more than twelve Information Commissioners
questions.exp: Section 12 of the RTI Act provides for a Chief Information Commissioner and not more than ten Information Commissioners; the same numerical limit applies to a State Information Commission under Section 15.

questions.q: The Chief Information Commissioner is appointed by the President on the recommendation of a committee consisting of the Prime Minister, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and
opts: a Union Cabinet Minister nominated by the Prime Minister
the Speaker of the Lok Sabha
questions.exp: The three-member committee under Section 12(3) of the RTI Act is chaired by the Prime Minister. Wajahat Habibullah was India's first Chief Information Commissioner.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the State Information Commission:
I. Its members are appointed by the Governor.
II. The recommending committee is headed by the Chief Minister and includes the Leader of Opposition in the Legislative Assembly.
III. It consists of a State Chief Information Commissioner and not more than ten State Information Commissioners.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. The third member of the recommending committee is a State Cabinet Minister nominated by the Chief Minister.

questions.q: As a result of the Right to Information (Amendment) Act, 2019 and the RTI Rules, 2019, the term of office of the Chief Information Commissioner is
opts: five years or until the age of 65 years
three years or until the age of 65 years
six years or until the age of 65 years
five years or until the age of 62 years
questions.exp: The 2019 Amendment removed the fixed five-year term from the statute and left the term, salary and service conditions to be prescribed by the Central Government; the RTI Rules, 2019 fix the term at three years. The upper age limit of 65 years remains.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Right to Information (Amendment) Act, 2019 is NOT correct?
opts: It amended Sections 13, 16 and 27 of the principal Act.
It removed the right of a citizen to file a second appeal before the Information Commission.
It empowered the Central Government to prescribe the salaries of Information Commissioners.
It empowered the Central Government to prescribe the term of office of Information Commissioners.
questions.exp: The 2019 Amendment did not touch the appeal mechanism under Section 19; it dealt only with the tenure, salaries and service conditions of the Chief Information Commissioner, Information Commissioners and their state counterparts.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Section of the RTI Act, 2005)   List-II (Subject)
A. Section 4   1. Exemptions from disclosure of information
B. Section 6   2. Constitution of the Central Information Commission
C. Section 8   3. Suo motu disclosure by public authorities
D. Section 12   4. Request for obtaining information
questions.exp: Section 4 - proactive disclosure; Section 6 - request for information; Section 8 - exemptions; Section 12 - constitution of the Central Information Commission.

questions.q: The Whistle Blowers Protection Act was passed by Parliament in the year
questions.exp: The Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014 received presidential assent on 9 May 2014. It provides for public interest disclosures to the Central or State Vigilance Commission and for protecting the identity of the complainant.

questions.q: Which State was the first in India to enact a law guaranteeing the time-bound delivery of public services to citizens?
questions.exp: The Madhya Pradesh Public Service Guarantee Act, 2010 was the first such law in India. Rajasthan followed with the Guaranteed Delivery of Public Services Act, 2011 and became the first state to enact a Right to Hearing Act in 2012.

questions.q: The National e-Governance Plan was approved by the Government of India in the year
questions.exp: The NeGP was approved on 18 May 2006 with 27 Mission Mode Projects, later expanded to 31. It was subsumed in 2015 into e-Kranti, or NeGP 2.0, which has 44 Mission Mode Projects.

questions.q: The Digital India programme was launched on
questions.exp: Digital India was launched on 1 July 2015 and rests on nine pillars with three vision areas - digital infrastructure as a utility to every citizen, governance and services on demand, and digital empowerment of citizens.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about e-governance in India:
I. e-Kranti, also called NeGP 2.0, was approved in 2015 with 44 Mission Mode Projects.
II. UMANG is a single mobile platform providing access to a range of central and state government services.
III. The Direct Benefit Transfer programme was launched on 1 January 2013.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. UMANG - Unified Mobile Application for New-age Governance - was launched in 2017.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Initiative)   List-II (Year of launch)
A. Direct Benefit Transfer   1. 2006
B. National e-Governance Plan   2. 2017
C. Digital India   3. 2013
D. UMANG   4. 2015
questions.exp: DBT was launched on 1 January 2013, the NeGP was approved in 2006, Digital India was launched in 2015 and UMANG in 2017.

questions.q: The first report of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission was titled
opts: Right to Information: Master Key to Good Governance
Citizen Centric Administration: The Heart of Governance
Promoting e-Governance: The SMART Way Forward
questions.exp: The 2nd ARC's first report, submitted in June 2006, was 'Right to Information - Master Key to Good Governance'. 'Ethics in Governance' was its fourth and 'Citizen Centric Administration' its twelfth report.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Second Administrative Reforms Commission:
I. It was constituted in 2005.
II. Its first chairman was Veerappa Moily.
III. It submitted a total of fifteen reports.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The 2nd ARC was constituted on 31 August 2005 under Veerappa Moily, who was succeeded by V. Ramachandran, and it submitted fifteen reports. The First ARC of 1966, headed by Morarji Desai and later K. Hanumanthaiah, had submitted twenty reports.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT among the attributes of good governance identified by the United Nations?
questions.exp: The eight attributes of good governance are participation, rule of law, transparency, responsiveness, consensus orientation, equity and inclusiveness, effectiveness and efficiency, and accountability. The World Bank popularised the term in its 1992 report 'Governance and Development'.

questions.q:
Arrange the following legislations in chronological order of their enactment, beginning with the earliest:
I. Freedom of Information Act
II. Right to Information Act
III. Whistle Blowers Protection Act
IV. Meghalaya Community Participation and Public Services Social Audit Act
questions.exp: Freedom of Information Act 2002; Right to Information Act 2005; Whistle Blowers Protection Act 2014; Meghalaya Social Audit Act 2017.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Social audit - First mandated in India by the Right to Information Act, 2005
Sevottam - Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances
questions.exp: Social audit was first statutorily mandated in India by Section 17 of MGNREGA, 2005, not by the RTI Act. The other three pairs are correctly matched.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Report of the Second Administrative Reforms Commission)   List-II (Report number)
A. Right to Information: Master Key to Good Governance   1. Fourth report
B. Ethics in Governance   2. Eleventh report
C. Promoting e-Governance: The SMART Way Forward   3. Twelfth report
D. Citizen Centric Administration: The Heart of Governance   4. First report
questions.exp: The 2nd ARC's first report (2006) was on the Right to Information, the fourth on Ethics in Governance, the eleventh on e-Governance and the twelfth on Citizen Centric Administration.

subjects.subject: Political and Administrative System of Rajasthan

chapters.title: Governor of Rajasthan
factsheet: Article 153 — there shall be a Governor for each State; Article 154 — executive power of the State vested in the Governor.
Article 155 — Governor appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal; Article 156 — holds office during the President's pleasure, normal term 5 years.
Article 157 — qualifications: citizen of India, completed 35 years of age; Article 158 — conditions of office (no office of profit, not an MP/MLA).
Article 159 — oath administered by the Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court (or, in his absence, the senior-most available judge).
Governor's emoluments are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State and cannot be diminished during his term.

Key Articles: 161 pardon; 163 aid and advice; 164 appointment of CM/Ministers; 165 Advocate General; 166 conduct of business; 167 CM's duties; 174 summon/prorogue/dissolve; 175 address and messages; 176 special address; 200 assent to Bills; 201 Bills reserved for the President; 213 ordinances; 356 report leading to President's Rule.
Rajpramukh of Matsya Union (18 Mar 1948) — Maharaja Udaibhan Singh of Dholpur.
Rajpramukh of Rajasthan Union (25 Mar 1948) — Maharao Bhim Singh II of Kota.
Rajpramukh of Sanyukt Rajasthan (18 Apr 1948) — Maharana Bhupal Singh of Udaipur (later Maharajpramukh).
Rajpramukh of Vrihad (Greater) Rajasthan from 30 Mar 1949 to 31 Oct 1956 — Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II of Jaipur; the last Rajpramukh.
The post of Rajpramukh was abolished by the Seventh Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956, which also allowed one person to be Governor of two or more States.
First Governor of Rajasthan — Gurmukh Nihal Singh, 1 Nov 1956 to 16 Apr 1962; earlier Chief Minister of Delhi; his 5 years 166 days is the longest gubernatorial tenure in Rajasthan.
Second Governor — Dr Sampurnanand (16 Apr 1962 – 16 Apr 1967), former Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh.
Sardar Hukam Singh (1967–70, 1970–72) — a former Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
First acting Governor of Rajasthan — Justice Jagat Narain (Nov–Dec 1970).
Justice Jagdish Sharan Verma served as acting Governor (1987–88, 1989) and later became Chief Justice of India.
Air Chief Marshal Om Prakash Mehra (1982–85) — the only former Chief of the Air Staff to be Governor of Rajasthan.
Vasantdada Patil (1985–87) — a former Chief Minister of Maharashtra.
Bali Ram Bhagat (1993–98) — a former Speaker of the Lok Sabha and Union External Affairs Minister.
Governors who died in office include Darbara Singh (1998), Nirmal Chandra Jain (2003) and Prabha Rau (2010).
Pratibha Patil (8 Nov 2004 – 23 Jun 2007) — first woman Governor of Rajasthan; resigned to contest and win the office of President of India.
Women Governors of Rajasthan: Pratibha Patil (2004–07), Prabha Rau (2009–10), Margaret Alva (2012–14).
Kalyan Singh (2014–19) — former Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh; Kalraj Mishra (2019–24) — Governor during the 2020 Rajasthan political crisis.
Current Governor — Haribhau Kisanrao Bagde, sworn in 31 July 2024; formerly Speaker of the Maharashtra Legislative Assembly (as of 4 September 2026).

President's Rule has been imposed in Rajasthan four times: 1967 (Sukhadia), 1977 (Hari Dev Joshi), 1980 (Bhairon Singh Shekhawat) and 1992–93 (Bhairon Singh Shekhawat); 1992–93 was the longest at about 354 days.
The Governor is ex-officio Chancellor of the State universities of Rajasthan and appoints the Advocate General, RPSC Chairman/members, the State Election Commissioner and the Lokayukta.

Article 161 lets the Governor grant pardons for offences against State law, but he cannot pardon a death sentence or deal with court-martial sentences — those belong to the President under Article 72.
Article 163(2) makes the Governor's own decision on what falls within his discretion final and non-justiciable; Article 361 gives him immunity from court proceedings during his term.

questions.q: Under which Article of the Constitution is it provided that there shall be a Governor for each State?
questions.exp: Article 153 provides that there shall be a Governor for each State. Article 154 vests the executive power of the State in the Governor.

questions.q: Who was the first Governor of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Gurmukh Nihal Singh became the first Governor of Rajasthan on 1 November 1956 after the post of Rajpramukh was abolished. He had earlier been Chief Minister of Delhi.

questions.q: Gurmukh Nihal Singh assumed office as the first Governor of Rajasthan on:
questions.exp: He took office on 1 November 1956, the day Rajasthan attained its present form under the States Reorganisation Act and the office of Rajpramukh ceased.

questions.q: The post of Rajpramukh was abolished by which Constitutional Amendment Act?
questions.exp: The Seventh Amendment Act, 1956 abolished the classification of States into Parts A, B, C and D and with it the office of Rajpramukh; it also permitted one person to be Governor of two or more States.

questions.q: Who was the Rajpramukh of Vrihad (Greater) Rajasthan formed on 30 March 1949?
opts: Maharao Bhim Singh II of Kota
Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II of Jaipur
questions.exp: Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II of Jaipur was Rajpramukh from 30 March 1949 until the office was abolished on 31 October 1956, making him the last Rajpramukh of Rajasthan.

questions.q: The Governor of Rajasthan is appointed by:
questions.exp: Under Article 155 the Governor is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal. There is no direct or indirect election to the office.

questions.q: The minimum age prescribed under Article 157 for appointment as Governor is:
questions.exp: Article 157 requires that the Governor be a citizen of India who has completed 35 years of age. The same minimum applies to the President under Article 58.

questions.q: The oath of office to the Governor of Rajasthan is administered by:
opts: The Speaker of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly
The Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court
questions.exp: Article 159 provides that the Governor's oath is administered by the Chief Justice of the High Court of the State, or in his absence the senior-most judge available.

questions.q: The pardoning power of the Governor is contained in which Article?
questions.exp: Article 161 empowers the Governor to grant pardons, reprieves, respites and remissions of punishment for offences against laws relating to State subjects. Article 72 is the President's corresponding power.

questions.q: The Governor's power to promulgate ordinances when the Legislature is not in session is derived from:
questions.exp: Article 213 gives the Governor ordinance-making power; Article 123 is the President's equivalent. An ordinance has the same force as an Act of the State Legislature.

questions.q: The Governor of Rajasthan holds office during the pleasure of:
questions.exp: Article 156(1) states that the Governor holds office during the pleasure of the President; his normal term of five years is subject to this.

questions.q: Who was the first woman Governor of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Pratibha Patil was Governor of Rajasthan from 8 November 2004 to 23 June 2007 and then became the first woman President of India. Prabha Rau and Margaret Alva were the other women Governors of the State.

questions.q: Which Governor of Rajasthan has had the longest tenure in the office?
questions.exp: Gurmukh Nihal Singh served 5 years and 166 days (1956-1962), the longest for any Governor of Rajasthan. Kalyan Singh and Sampurnanand each completed almost exactly five years.

questions.q: Who is the Governor of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Haribhau Kisanrao Bagde was sworn in as Governor of Rajasthan on 31 July 2024, succeeding Kalraj Mishra, and continues in office as of 4 September 2026.

questions.q: Before being appointed Governor of Rajasthan, Haribhau Kisanrao Bagde had held which office?
opts: Speaker of the Maharashtra Legislative Assembly
questions.exp: Haribhau Bagde was Speaker of the Maharashtra Legislative Assembly (2014-2019) before becoming Governor of Rajasthan on 31 July 2024.

questions.q: Who was the first person to hold charge as acting Governor of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Justice Jagat Narain held charge as acting Governor from 20 November to 23 December 1970, between the two spells of Sardar Hukam Singh.

questions.q: Who was the Governor of Rajasthan during the political crisis of July-August 2020?
questions.exp: Kalraj Mishra (September 2019 - July 2024) was Governor when the dispute over summoning the Assembly arose during the 2020 crisis; the session finally met on 14 August 2020.

questions.q: Which former Governor of Rajasthan later became the President of India?
questions.exp: Pratibha Patil resigned as Governor of Rajasthan in June 2007 and was elected President of India the following month, becoming the first woman to hold that office.

questions.q: Which Governor of Rajasthan had earlier served as Chief of the Air Staff of the Indian Air Force?
opts: Air Chief Marshal Om Prakash Mehra
questions.exp: Air Chief Marshal O.P. Mehra, a former Chief of the Air Staff, was Governor of Rajasthan from 1982 to 1985 and later Governor of Maharashtra.

questions.q: Vasantdada Patil, Governor of Rajasthan from 1985 to 1987, had earlier served as:
opts: Chief Justice of the Bombay High Court
questions.exp: Vasantdada Patil was a four-time Chief Minister of Maharashtra before his term as Governor of Rajasthan (1985-1987).

questions.q: The Governor of Rajasthan is the ex-officio Chancellor of:
opts: all central universities located in the State
the Board of Secondary Education, Rajasthan
questions.exp: By the statutes of the State universities the Governor is their Chancellor; this is a statutory, not a constitutional, function.

questions.q: President's Rule in a State is imposed under which Article, usually on a report of the Governor?
questions.exp: Article 356 permits the President to assume the functions of a State government on receipt of a report from the Governor or otherwise. Article 352 is national emergency and Article 360 financial emergency.

questions.q: How many times has President's Rule been imposed in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: President's Rule has been imposed four times in Rajasthan: 1967, 1977, 1980 and 1992-93. The government of Bhairon Singh Shekhawat was dismissed on two of these occasions.

questions.q: The longest spell of President's Rule in Rajasthan was imposed in:
questions.exp: The proclamation of 15 December 1992, following the Babri Masjid demolition, lasted until 4 December 1993 - about 354 days, the longest of the four spells.

questions.q: The emoluments and allowances of the Governor of Rajasthan are charged on the:
questions.exp: Article 158(3) provides that the Governor's emoluments and allowances are charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State and cannot be diminished during his term of office.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the pardoning power of the Governor under Article 161:
I. He can grant pardon in respect of offences against laws relating to State subjects.
II. He can grant pardon in a case where the sentence is one of death.
III. His pardoning power extends to sentences awarded by a court martial.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Only statement I is correct. The Governor cannot pardon a death sentence and has no power over court-martial sentences; both belong exclusively to the President under Article 72. The Governor may, however, suspend, remit or commute a death sentence.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the office of the Governor:
I. He must have completed thirty-five years of age.
II. He must not be a member of either House of Parliament or of a House of the State Legislature.
III. His normal term is five years from the date on which he enters upon his office.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Article 157 lays down the age and citizenship requirement, Article 158 the conditions of office, and Article 156(3) the five-year term, subject always to the President's pleasure.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the transition from Rajpramukh to Governor in Rajasthan:
I. The Rajpramukh was the constitutional head of a Part B State under the original Constitution.
II. The office was abolished by the Seventh Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956.
III. Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II was thereafter appointed the first Governor of Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Man Singh II was the last Rajpramukh, not the first Governor; Gurmukh Nihal Singh became the first Governor on 1 November 1956. Man Singh II was later appointed Rajpramukh emeritus and then Ambassador to Spain.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Gurmukh Nihal Singh:
I. He had earlier been Chief Minister of Delhi.
II. He held the office of Governor of Rajasthan from 1 November 1956 to 16 April 1962.
III. His was the longest tenure of any Governor of Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. His tenure of 5 years and 166 days remains the longest for a Governor of Rajasthan.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Pratibha Patil:
I. She was the first woman Governor of Rajasthan.
II. She resigned the Governorship in 2007 to contest the presidential election.
III. She was the first woman Chief Minister of Maharashtra.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Pratibha Patil was never Chief Minister of Maharashtra; she held State ministerial office and was Deputy Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha before becoming Governor of Rajasthan.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the ordinance-making power of the Governor under Article 213:
I. An ordinance can be promulgated only when the Legislative Assembly is not in session.
II. Every such ordinance must be laid before the Legislature and ceases to operate six weeks from its reassembly.
III. In certain specified cases the Governor must obtain instructions from the President before promulgating an ordinance.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The proviso to Article 213(1) requires the Governor to obtain the President's instructions where a Bill containing the same provisions would have needed the President's prior sanction or reservation.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about President's Rule in Rajasthan:
I. It has been imposed on four occasions.
II. The government headed by Bhairon Singh Shekhawat was dismissed on two of these occasions.
III. The first imposition, in 1967, came during the tenure of Mohan Lal Sukhadia.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Shekhawat's governments were dismissed in February 1980 and December 1992, and the first proclamation of March 1967 followed the post-election deadlock during Sukhadia's tenure.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the discretionary powers of the Governor:
I. Article 163(2) makes the Governor's decision on what falls within his discretion final.
II. Recommending the imposition of President's Rule is exercised in his discretion.
III. The Governor appoints the Advocate General of the State in his discretion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. The Advocate General is appointed under Article 165 on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers, not in the Governor's discretion.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 200 of the Constitution:
I. The Governor may withhold assent to a Bill passed by the State Legislature.
II. The Governor may reserve a Bill for the consideration of the President.
III. If the Governor returns a Money Bill for reconsideration, the House is bound to accept his suggestions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Under the proviso to Article 200 the Governor may return only a Bill other than a Money Bill, and even then the House is not bound to accept his suggestions.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Governor of Rajasthan)   List-II (Period)
A. Gurmukh Nihal Singh   1. 1993-1998
B. Dr Sampurnanand       2. 1956-1962
C. Bali Ram Bhagat       3. 2014-2019
D. Kalyan Singh          4. 1962-1967
questions.exp: Gurmukh Nihal Singh 1956-62, Sampurnanand 1962-67, Bali Ram Bhagat 1993-98 and Kalyan Singh 2014-19.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Article)   List-II (Subject)
A. Article 155   1. Pardoning power of the Governor
B. Article 161   2. Appointment of the Governor
C. Article 213   3. Special address by the Governor
D. Article 176   4. Ordinance-making power of the Governor
questions.exp: Article 155 appointment, 161 pardon, 213 ordinances and 176 the Governor's special address at the first session after a general election and at the first session of each year.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Governor of Rajasthan)   List-II (Office held earlier)
A. Sardar Hukam Singh       1. Chief of the Air Staff
B. Om Prakash Mehra         2. Speaker of the Lok Sabha
C. Kalyan Singh             3. Chief Minister of Delhi
D. Madan Lal Khurana        4. Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh
questions.exp: Sardar Hukam Singh was Speaker of the Lok Sabha, O.P. Mehra Chief of the Air Staff, Kalyan Singh Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh and Madan Lal Khurana Chief Minister of Delhi.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Union)   List-II (Rajpramukh)
A. Matsya Union        1. Maharao Bhim Singh II of Kota
B. Rajasthan Union     2. Maharana Bhupal Singh of Udaipur
C. Sanyukt Rajasthan   3. Maharaja Udaibhan Singh of Dholpur
D. Vrihad Rajasthan    4. Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II of Jaipur
questions.exp: Matsya Union (18 March 1948) was headed by Udaibhan Singh of Dholpur, the Rajasthan Union (25 March 1948) by Bhim Singh II of Kota, Sanyukt Rajasthan (18 April 1948) by Bhupal Singh of Udaipur and Vrihad Rajasthan (30 March 1949) by Sawai Man Singh II.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Governor of Rajasthan)   List-II (Year of assuming office)
A. Margaret Alva      1. 2019
B. Kalyan Singh       2. 2024
C. Kalraj Mishra      3. 2012
D. Haribhau Bagde     4. 2014
questions.exp: Margaret Alva took office in May 2012, Kalyan Singh in September 2014, Kalraj Mishra in September 2019 and Haribhau Bagde on 31 July 2024.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs relating to the office of the Governor of Rajasthan is NOT correctly matched?
opts: First Governor of Rajasthan - Gurmukh Nihal Singh
First woman Governor of Rajasthan - Pratibha Patil
Rajpramukh of Vrihad Rajasthan - Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II
Governor of Rajasthan with the longest tenure - Kalraj Mishra
questions.exp: The longest tenure belongs to Gurmukh Nihal Singh (5 years 166 days). Kalraj Mishra served from September 2019 to July 2024, about 4 years 326 days.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a discretionary power of the Governor of Rajasthan?
opts: Reserving a Bill for the consideration of the President
Recommending the imposition of President's Rule
Appointing the Chief Minister when no party has a clear majority
Appointing the Chairman of the Rajasthan Public Service Commission
questions.exp: The Chairman and members of the RPSC are appointed by the Governor under Article 316, but on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers - it is not a discretionary function.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Governor of Rajasthan is NOT correct?
opts: He is appointed by the President by warrant under his hand and seal
He must be a citizen of India who has completed thirty-five years of age
He can be removed by a resolution of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly
He is not entitled to hold any other office of profit
questions.exp: There is no procedure by which a State Legislature can remove a Governor; he holds office during the pleasure of the President and may be transferred or asked to resign.

questions.q: Which one of the following Article-subject pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Article 157 - Qualifications for appointment as Governor
Article 159 - Oath of office of the Governor
Article 160 - Discharge of the Governor's functions in certain contingencies
Article 162 - Pardoning power of the Governor
questions.exp: Article 162 deals with the extent of the executive power of the State. The pardoning power of the Governor is in Article 161.

questions.q: Which one of the following has NOT served as Governor of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Ram Naresh Yadav was Governor of Madhya Pradesh. Sukhdev Prasad (1988-90), Marri Chenna Reddy (1992-93) and Darbara Singh (1998) all held the office in Rajasthan.

questions.q:
Arrange the following Governors of Rajasthan in the correct chronological order of assuming office:
I. Bali Ram Bhagat
II. Dr Sampurnanand
III. Margaret Alva
IV. Raghukul Tilak
questions.exp: Sampurnanand 1962, Raghukul Tilak 1977, Bali Ram Bhagat 1993 and Margaret Alva 2012.

chapters.title: Chief Minister and the Council of Ministers of Rajasthan
factsheet: Article 163 - Council of Ministers with the Chief Minister at the head to aid and advise the Governor, except where he acts in his discretion; Article 163(2) makes his view on discretion final.
Article 164(1) - the Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor and other Ministers are appointed by the Governor on the CM's advice; Ministers hold office during the Governor's pleasure.

Article 164(1A), inserted by the 91st Amendment Act, 2003 - total Ministers including the CM must not exceed 15% of the Assembly's strength and must not be fewer than 12; for Rajasthan the ceiling is 30.
Article 164(2) collective responsibility to the Legislative Assembly; 164(3) oath by the Governor; 164(4) a non-member Minister must become a member within six consecutive months.

Article 165 Advocate General; Article 166 conduct of business of the State Government; Article 167 duties of the Chief Minister towards the Governor; Article 177 right of Ministers to speak in the House.
Heera Lal Shastri - first Chief Minister of Rajasthan, 7 April 1949 to 5 January 1951; a Jaipur Prajamandal leader, nominated by the Rajpramukh.
C.S. Venkatachari - second CM (6 January 1951 to 25 April 1951), an administrator brought in from outside the legislature.
Jai Narayan Vyas - CM twice (26 April 1951 - 3 March 1952 and 1 November 1952 - 12 November 1954); lost from two seats in the 1952 election.
Tika Ram Paliwal - first elected Chief Minister of Rajasthan (3 March 1952 - 31 October 1952); he had earlier been the first Deputy Chief Minister.
Mohan Lal Sukhadia - CM from 13 November 1954 to 9 July 1971 (with the 1967 break), the longest-serving Chief Minister of Rajasthan at about seventeen years.
Barkatullah Khan - CM 9 July 1971 to 11 October 1973; the only Muslim Chief Minister of Rajasthan; died in office.
Hari Dev Joshi - Chief Minister three times (1973-77, 1985-88, 1989-90); later Governor of Assam and Meghalaya.
Bhairon Singh Shekhawat - first non-Congress Chief Minister (1977-80, 1990-92, 1993-98); elected Vice-President of India in 2002.
Jagannath Pahadia - Chief Minister 1980-81; the first Scheduled Caste Chief Minister of Rajasthan.
Shiv Charan Mathur - Chief Minister twice (1981-85 and 1988-89).
Hira Lal Devpura - Chief Minister for about a fortnight (23 February to 10 March 1985), the shortest tenure; he became Speaker of the Assembly later the same month.
Ashok Gehlot - Chief Minister three times (1998-2003, 2008-2013, 2018-2023).
Vasundhara Raje - first woman Chief Minister of Rajasthan; two terms (2003-2008 and 2013-2018).
Bhajan Lal Sharma - Chief Minister since 15 December 2023; MLA from Sanganer; a first-time MLA when chosen.
Deputy Chief Ministers appointed in December 2023 - Diya Kumari (Vidhyadhar Nagar) and Prem Chand Bairwa (Dudu); Sachin Pilot was Deputy CM from 2018 to 2020.

President's Rule in Rajasthan - four times: 13 March-26 April 1967 (Sukhadia), 30 April-21 June 1977 (Hari Dev Joshi), 17 February-5 June 1980 (Shekhawat) and 15 December 1992-3 December 1993 (Shekhawat).
Bhairon Singh Shekhawat is thus the Chief Minister whose government was dismissed most often - twice.
The Chief Minister is Leader of the House in the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly and chairman of the State Planning Board and the State Disaster Management Authority.

Article 167 requires the CM to communicate decisions of the Council of Ministers, furnish information called for by the Governor, and place before the Council any matter decided by a single Minister when the Governor so requires.
Ministers are of three ranks - Cabinet Minister, Minister of State and Deputy Minister; only Cabinet Ministers attend Cabinet meetings.
The 91st Amendment also bars a member disqualified on the ground of defection from being appointed a Minister for the duration of that disqualification.
Rajasthan's Chief Minister's Office (CMO) and the Cabinet Secretariat within the State Secretariat at Jaipur service the Council of Ministers; the Chief Secretary is secretary to the Cabinet.

questions.q: Who was the first Chief Minister of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Heera Lal Shastri, a leader of the Jaipur Prajamandal, took office on 7 April 1949 when Vrihad Rajasthan was inaugurated, and served until 5 January 1951.

questions.q: Heera Lal Shastri became the first Chief Minister of Rajasthan on:
questions.exp: Vrihad Rajasthan was formed on 30 March 1949 and its first ministry under Heera Lal Shastri was sworn in on 7 April 1949 by Rajpramukh Sawai Man Singh II.

questions.q: Who was the first elected Chief Minister of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: After the first general election of 1952 Tika Ram Paliwal became Chief Minister on 3 March 1952, the first to hold the office as an elected member of the Assembly.

questions.q: Which Chief Minister of Rajasthan has had the longest total tenure in office?
questions.exp: Mohan Lal Sukhadia was Chief Minister from November 1954 to July 1971, about seventeen years, the longest in the State's history.

questions.q: Who succeeded Heera Lal Shastri as Chief Minister of Rajasthan in January 1951?
questions.exp: C.S. Venkatachari, an administrator, headed the government from 6 January to 25 April 1951, after which Jai Narayan Vyas took over.

questions.q: Barkatullah Khan, Chief Minister of Rajasthan from 1971 to 1973, is remembered as:
opts: the only Muslim Chief Minister of Rajasthan
the first Scheduled Caste Chief Minister
the youngest Chief Minister of Rajasthan
questions.exp: Barkatullah Khan is the only Muslim to have been Chief Minister of Rajasthan. He died in office on 11 October 1973.

questions.q: Who was the first non-Congress Chief Minister of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Bhairon Singh Shekhawat headed the Janata Party government sworn in on 22 June 1977, the first non-Congress ministry in Rajasthan.

questions.q: Who was the first Scheduled Caste Chief Minister of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Jagannath Pahadia, Chief Minister from 6 June 1980 to 13 July 1981, was the first Chief Minister of Rajasthan from a Scheduled Caste.

questions.q: Which Chief Minister of Rajasthan had the shortest tenure?
questions.exp: Hira Lal Devpura was Chief Minister from 23 February to 10 March 1985, about a fortnight. He was elected Speaker of the Assembly later that month.

questions.q: Who was the first woman Chief Minister of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Vasundhara Raje became the first woman Chief Minister of Rajasthan on 8 December 2003 and served a second term from 2013 to 2018.

questions.q: Vasundhara Raje first became Chief Minister of Rajasthan in:
questions.exp: She was sworn in on 8 December 2003 after the BJP's victory in the 2003 Assembly election, and served until 11 December 2008.

questions.q: Which Chief Minister of Rajasthan later became the Vice-President of India?
questions.exp: Bhairon Singh Shekhawat resigned as Chief Minister in 2002 on being elected Vice-President of India, an office he held until 2007.

questions.q: Who is the Chief Minister of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Bhajan Lal Sharma of the BJP has been Chief Minister since 15 December 2023 and continues in office as of 4 September 2026.

questions.q: Bhajan Lal Sharma was sworn in as Chief Minister of Rajasthan on:
questions.exp: The 2023 results were declared on 3 December, he was chosen leader of the BJP legislature party on 12 December, and he took the oath of office on 15 December 2023.

questions.q: Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma represents which Assembly constituency?
questions.exp: He was elected from Sanganer in Jaipur district in 2023. Vidhyadhar Nagar is represented by Deputy Chief Minister Diya Kumari and Dudu by Deputy Chief Minister Prem Chand Bairwa.

questions.q: Which Article deals with the appointment of the Chief Minister and other Ministers of a State?
questions.exp: Article 164 provides for the appointment of the Chief Minister by the Governor and of other Ministers on the Chief Minister's advice, and also contains the collective responsibility and oath provisions.

questions.q: Under Article 163, the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister aids and advises the Governor except when the Governor:
opts: is presiding over the Legislative Assembly
questions.exp: Article 163(1) excludes those functions which the Governor is required by the Constitution to exercise in his discretion; Article 163(2) makes his own decision on that question final.

questions.q: The maximum permissible size of the Council of Ministers in Rajasthan, including the Chief Minister, is:
questions.exp: Article 164(1A) caps the Council of Ministers at 15 per cent of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly; 15 per cent of 200 is 30.

questions.q: The ceiling of 15 per cent on the size of a State Council of Ministers was introduced by which Constitutional Amendment?
questions.exp: The 91st Amendment Act, 2003 inserted Article 164(1A). The 52nd Amendment (1985) had introduced the anti-defection law in the Tenth Schedule.

questions.q: The minimum number of Ministers in a State Council of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, is:
questions.exp: Article 164(1A) provides a floor of twelve Ministers including the Chief Minister, so that very small States are not left with token ministries.

questions.q: The Council of Ministers of Rajasthan is collectively responsible to:
questions.exp: Article 164(2) makes the Council of Ministers collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly of the State, which is the basis of the no-confidence motion.

questions.q: A Minister in Rajasthan who is not a member of the State Legislature must become a member within:
opts: the remaining term of the Assembly
questions.exp: Article 164(4) provides that a Minister who is not a member of the Legislature for six consecutive months ceases to be a Minister at the end of that period.

questions.q: The oath of office and secrecy to Ministers of the Rajasthan Government is administered by:
opts: the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
the Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court
questions.exp: Article 164(3) requires the Governor to administer the oaths of office and secrecy to Ministers in the forms set out in the Third Schedule.

questions.q: Which Article lays down the duties of the Chief Minister with respect to furnishing information to the Governor?
questions.exp: Article 167 requires the CM to communicate all decisions of the Council of Ministers, to furnish information the Governor calls for, and to place before the Council any matter decided by a single Minister when the Governor so requires.

questions.q: Who were appointed the two Deputy Chief Ministers of Rajasthan in December 2023?
opts: Diya Kumari and Prem Chand Bairwa
Kirodi Lal Meena and Prem Chand Bairwa
questions.exp: Diya Kumari (Vidhyadhar Nagar) and Prem Chand Bairwa (Dudu) were sworn in as Deputy Chief Ministers along with Bhajan Lal Sharma on 15 December 2023.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Mohan Lal Sukhadia:
I. He became Chief Minister of Rajasthan in November 1954.
II. He held the office for about seventeen years in all.
III. President's Rule was imposed in Rajasthan for the first time during his tenure, in 1967.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. He took office on 13 November 1954 and, apart from the President's Rule interlude of March-April 1967, continued until 9 July 1971.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about President's Rule in Rajasthan:
I. It has been imposed on four occasions.
II. The government of Bhairon Singh Shekhawat was dismissed on two of these occasions.
III. The imposition of 1980 followed the dismissal of the government of Hari Dev Joshi.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. The 1980 proclamation dismissed Bhairon Singh Shekhawat's first government; Hari Dev Joshi's government had been dismissed in 1977.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 164:
I. The Chief Minister is appointed by the Governor.
II. Other Ministers are appointed by the Governor on the advice of the Chief Minister.
III. Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Legislative Assembly.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Governor, though the Council as a whole is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003:
I. It caps the State Council of Ministers at 15 per cent of the strength of the Legislative Assembly.
II. It provides that the number of Ministers in a State shall not be less than twelve.
III. It bars a member disqualified on the ground of defection from being appointed a Minister.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The 91st Amendment inserted Articles 75(1A)-(1B) for the Union and 164(1A)-(1B) for the States, and also amended the Tenth Schedule by deleting the split provision.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Hira Lal Devpura:
I. He was Chief Minister of Rajasthan for about a fortnight in 1985.
II. He later served as Speaker of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly.
III. He belonged to the Bharatiya Janata Party.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Devpura was a Congress leader; he was Chief Minister from 23 February to 10 March 1985 and became Speaker on 20 March 1985.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Bhairon Singh Shekhawat:
I. He was the first non-Congress Chief Minister of Rajasthan.
II. He held the office of Chief Minister on three separate occasions.
III. He was elected Vice-President of India in 2002.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. His three terms were 1977-80, 1990-92 and 1993-98; he was Vice-President from 2002 to 2007.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the relationship of the Chief Minister with the Governor:
I. The Chief Minister communicates to the Governor all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to the administration of the State.
II. The Governor may require any matter decided by a single Minister to be placed before the Council of Ministers.
III. Article 166 deals with the conduct of business of the Government of a State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Clauses (a) and (c) of Article 167 cover statements I and II, and Article 166 provides that executive action is expressed in the name of the Governor and allows rules of business to be made.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajasthan Council of Ministers:
I. Ministers are of three ranks - Cabinet Ministers, Ministers of State and Deputy Ministers.
II. Portfolios are allocated among Ministers by the Chief Minister.
III. A Minister may vote in either House of the State Legislature.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Under Article 177 a Minister may speak in and take part in the proceedings of either House but may vote only in the House of which he is a member; in any case Rajasthan has only one House.

A. Heera Lal Shastri   1. First woman Chief Minister of Rajasthan

questions.exp: Heera Lal Shastri was the first CM, Tika Ram Paliwal the first elected CM, Barkatullah Khan the only Muslim CM and Vasundhara Raje the first woman CM.

questions.exp: The four spells displaced Sukhadia (1967), Hari Dev Joshi (1977) and Bhairon Singh Shekhawat twice (1980 and 1992-93).

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs relating to the Chief Ministers of Rajasthan is NOT correctly matched?
opts: First Chief Minister of Rajasthan - Heera Lal Shastri
First elected Chief Minister of Rajasthan - Tika Ram Paliwal
Longest-serving Chief Minister of Rajasthan - Mohan Lal Sukhadia
Shortest-serving Chief Minister of Rajasthan - Jagannath Pahadia
questions.exp: The shortest tenure was that of Hira Lal Devpura, about a fortnight in 1985. Jagannath Pahadia was Chief Minister for over a year (1980-81).

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a function of the Chief Minister of Rajasthan?
opts: Recommending the allocation of portfolios among Ministers
Advising the Governor on the summoning of the Assembly
Appointing the Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court
Recommending the dissolution of the Legislative Assembly
questions.exp: Judges of the High Court, including the Chief Justice, are appointed by the President under Article 217 on the recommendation of the collegium; the Chief Minister has no such power.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Rajasthan Council of Ministers is NOT correct?
opts: It is collectively responsible to the Legislative Assembly
Its total strength cannot exceed thirty including the Chief Minister
Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Legislative Assembly
The Governor administers the oath of secrecy to Ministers
questions.exp: Ministers hold office during the pleasure of the Governor under Article 164(1); it is the collective responsibility that runs to the Assembly.

questions.q: Which one of the following has NOT served as Chief Minister of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Ram Niwas Mirdha was the longest-serving Speaker of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly and later a Union Minister, but he was never Chief Minister.

questions.q: Which one of the following Chief Ministers of Rajasthan did NOT hold the office on more than one occasion?
questions.exp: Jagannath Pahadia was Chief Minister only once (1980-81). Hari Dev Joshi held office three times, Shiv Charan Mathur twice and Vasundhara Raje twice.

questions.q:

II. Tika Ram Paliwal
III. Jagannath Pahadia
IV. Mohan Lal Sukhadia
questions.exp: Tika Ram Paliwal 1952, Mohan Lal Sukhadia 1954, Barkatullah Khan 1971 and Jagannath Pahadia 1980.

questions.q:
Arrange the following Chief Ministers of Rajasthan in the correct chronological order of first assuming office:
I. Ashok Gehlot
II. Bhairon Singh Shekhawat
III. Bhajan Lal Sharma
IV. Vasundhara Raje
questions.exp: Bhairon Singh Shekhawat first took office in 1977, Ashok Gehlot in 1998, Vasundhara Raje in 2003 and Bhajan Lal Sharma in 2023.

chapters.title: Rajasthan Legislative Assembly
factsheet: The Rajasthan Legislative Assembly has 200 seats - 34 reserved for Scheduled Castes and 25 for Scheduled Tribes.
Jaipur district returns the largest number of members (19) and Jaisalmer and Pratapgarh the fewest (2 each).
The first Assembly was constituted in February 1952 with 160 members and first met on 29 March 1952 at the Sawai Man Singh Town Hall, Jaipur.
Strength grew to 176 after the merger of Ajmer State in 1956, to 184 in 1967, and to the present 200 from 1977.
The present Vidhan Sabha building at Jyoti Nagar, Jaipur was inaugurated on 6 November 2001 by President K.R. Narayanan.
Rajasthan is unicameral; before the Assembly, the interim legislature was the Rajasthan Pratinidhi Sabha constituted in 1949.
Article 168 constitution of State Legislatures; 170 composition of the Assembly (not more than 500, not less than 60); 172 duration of five years; 174 sessions, prorogation and dissolution.

Article 169 - Parliament may create or abolish a Legislative Council if the Assembly passes a resolution by a majority of its total membership and by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting; such a law is not deemed an amendment under Article 368.

On 18 April 2012 the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly passed a resolution under Article 169 for a 66-member Legislative Council; the Rajasthan Legislative Council Bill, 2013 was introduced in Parliament but has not been enacted.
Article 173 - qualification for membership: citizen of India, at least 25 years of age for the Assembly, and an oath before the Election Commission's nominee.

Article 178 Speaker and Deputy Speaker; 179 vacation and removal (14 days' notice, resolution by a majority of all the then members); 181 the Speaker does not preside when his own removal is being considered.
Article 189 - quorum is one-tenth of the total membership, i.e. 20 members in Rajasthan; the Speaker has only a casting vote.

Article 191 disqualifications; Article 192 the Governor decides questions of disqualification after obtaining the Election Commission's opinion; Article 190 - a seat falls vacant on 60 days' unexcused absence.

Article 194 privileges; Article 199 definition of a Money Bill; Article 200 assent; Article 202 annual financial statement; Article 208 rules of procedure; Article 212 courts not to inquire into proceedings.
First Speaker of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly - Narottam Lal Joshi (31 March 1952 to 25 April 1957).
Longest-serving Speaker - Ram Niwas Mirdha (1957-1967, second and third Assemblies).
First woman Speaker - Sumitra Singh, of the Twelfth Assembly (2004-2009), from Jhunjhunu.

Other Speakers include Niranjan Nath Acharya, Ram Kishore Vyas, Laxman Singh, Poonam Chand Vishnoi, Hira Lal Devpura, Giriraj Prasad Tiwari, Hari Shankar Bhabhra, Shanti Lal Chaplot, Samrath Lal Meena, Parasram Maderna, Deependra Singh Shekhawat, Kailash Chandra Meghwal and C.P. Joshi.
Current Speaker - Vasudev Devnani (BJP, Ajmer North), elected 21 December 2023 for the Sixteenth Assembly.
Leader of the Opposition - Tika Ram Jully (Congress, Alwar Rural), since January 2024.
A no-confidence motion needs the support of at least one-fifth of the total membership - 40 members in Rajasthan - to be admitted; no such motion has ever been carried in Rajasthan.
Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot won a confidence motion in the Assembly by voice vote on 14 August 2020 during the political crisis of that year.
The Assembly has four financial committees - Public Accounts, Public Undertakings and Estimates Committees A and B; committee membership is capped at 15 and Ministers cannot be members.
Other committees include Subordinate Legislation, Privileges, Petitions, Government Assurances, Rules, Women and Children, and the Committee on the Welfare of Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Assembly, only on the Governor's recommendation, and is certified by the Speaker; the Governor cannot return a Money Bill for reconsideration.
The maximum gap between two sessions of the Assembly is six months (Article 174); the Governor's special address is under Article 176.
The Sixteenth Assembly was constituted after the election of 25 November 2023, results declared on 3 December 2023, in which the BJP won 115 seats.
The Assembly Secretariat is headed by the Secretary appointed under Article 187; Rajasthan has adopted the National e-Vidhan Application (NeVA) for paperless proceedings.

questions.q: What is the total strength of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly?
questions.exp: The Assembly has 200 members, a strength it attained in 1977. Earlier it had 160 seats (1952), 176 (1957) and 184 (1967).

questions.q: How many seats in the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly are reserved for Scheduled Castes?
questions.exp: 34 of the 200 seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes and 25 for Scheduled Tribes.

questions.q: How many seats in the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly are reserved for Scheduled Tribes?
questions.exp: 25 seats are reserved for Scheduled Tribes, mainly in the southern tribal belt of Udaipur, Dungarpur, Banswara and Pratapgarh.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Legislative Assembly attained its present strength of 200 seats in:
questions.exp: The strength rose from 184 to 200 with the 1977 general election and has remained unchanged since.

questions.q: The strength of the first Rajasthan Legislative Assembly constituted in 1952 was:
questions.exp: The first Assembly had 160 members; the number rose to 176 after Ajmer State was merged into Rajasthan in 1956.

questions.q: The first Rajasthan Legislative Assembly held its first sitting on 29 March 1952 at:
opts: Sawai Man Singh Town Hall, Jaipur
the Vidhan Sabha Bhawan, Jyoti Nagar
questions.exp: The Assembly met in the Sawai Man Singh Town Hall, Jaipur, which housed it until the new Vidhan Sabha Bhawan at Jyoti Nagar was occupied in 2001.

questions.q: The present Rajasthan Vidhan Sabha building at Jyoti Nagar, Jaipur was inaugurated in November 2001 by:
questions.exp: President K.R. Narayanan inaugurated the new Vidhan Sabha Bhawan on 6 November 2001.

questions.q: Who was the first Speaker of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly?
questions.exp: Narottam Lal Joshi was Speaker of the first Assembly from 31 March 1952 to 25 April 1957.

questions.q: Who was the first woman Speaker of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly?
questions.exp: Sumitra Singh presided over the Twelfth Assembly from January 2004 to January 2009 and remains the only woman to have been Speaker in Rajasthan.

questions.q: Who has been the longest-serving Speaker of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly?
questions.exp: Ram Niwas Mirdha was Speaker for about ten years (1957-1967), covering the second and third Assemblies.

questions.q: Who is the Speaker of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly?
questions.exp: Vasudev Devnani, MLA from Ajmer North, was elected Speaker of the Sixteenth Assembly on 21 December 2023 and continues in office as of 4 September 2026.

questions.q: Who is the Leader of the Opposition in the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly?
questions.exp: Tika Ram Jully of the Congress, MLA from Alwar Rural, has been Leader of the Opposition since January 2024 and holds the post as of 4 September 2026.

questions.q: Under which Article of the Constitution may Parliament create or abolish a State Legislative Council?
questions.exp: Article 169 empowers Parliament to create or abolish a Legislative Council if the Assembly of the State first passes a resolution by a special majority. Rajasthan remains unicameral.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Legislative Assembly passed its resolution for the creation of a Legislative Council on:
questions.exp: The resolution under Article 169(1) was adopted on 18 April 2012 during the Ashok Gehlot government; the Council has still not been constituted.

questions.q: The Legislative Council proposed for Rajasthan in the 2012 resolution was to consist of how many members?
questions.exp: The resolution proposed a 66-member Council - a Council cannot exceed one-third of the Assembly's strength or be fewer than 40 members under Article 171.

questions.q: The normal term of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly under Article 172 is:
opts: five years, automatically extendable by two years
questions.exp: Article 172 fixes a five-year term from the date of the Assembly's first meeting, extendable by one year at a time during a national emergency.

questions.q: The minimum age for membership of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly is:
questions.exp: Article 173 requires a candidate for a Legislative Assembly seat to be at least 25 years old; the minimum for a Legislative Council is 30.

questions.q: The quorum for a sitting of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly is:
questions.exp: Article 189(3) fixes the quorum at one-tenth of the total membership, which for a 200-member House is 20.

questions.q: The maximum permissible interval between two sessions of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly is:
questions.exp: Article 174(1) provides that six months shall not intervene between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next.

questions.q: A Money Bill in the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly is certified as such by:
questions.exp: The Speaker's certificate that a Bill is a Money Bill is final and cannot be questioned; the Bill can be introduced only in the Assembly and only on the Governor's recommendation.

questions.q: Article 199 of the Constitution defines:
questions.exp: Article 199 defines a Money Bill for the purposes of a State Legislature; the corresponding provision for Parliament is Article 110.

questions.q: A no-confidence motion in the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly can be admitted only if it is supported by at least:
questions.exp: The rules require the support of not less than one-fifth of the total membership, i.e. 40 of the 200 members, before the motion is admitted.

questions.q: How many no-confidence motions moved in the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly have so far been carried?
questions.exp: No no-confidence motion has ever been passed in the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly; the last one moved was against the Hari Dev Joshi government in 1985.

questions.q: Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot won a confidence motion in the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly on:
questions.exp: After a month-long crisis, the Assembly met on 14 August 2020 and the confidence motion moved by the Gehlot government was carried by a voice vote.

questions.q: Which district of Rajasthan returns the largest number of members to the Legislative Assembly?
questions.exp: Jaipur district has 19 Assembly constituencies, the most of any district; Jaisalmer and Pratapgarh have only 2 each.

questions.q: How many financial committees does the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly have?
questions.exp: There are four: the Public Accounts Committee, the Committee on Public Undertakings and the two Estimates Committees, A and B.

questions.q: The removal of the Speaker of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly requires a resolution passed by:
opts: a simple majority of members present and voting
a majority of all the then members of the Assembly
two-thirds of the members present and voting
the prior approval of the Governor
questions.exp: Article 179(c) requires a resolution passed by a majority of all the then members of the Assembly, after at least fourteen days' notice of intention to move it.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the composition of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly:
I. It has 200 seats.
II. 34 seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes.
III. 25 seats are reserved for Scheduled Tribes.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The 200-seat strength dates from 1977 and the reservations follow the delimitation based on the Census.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 169:
I. Parliament may by law create or abolish a Legislative Council in a State.
II. The State Legislative Assembly must first pass a resolution by a majority of its total membership and by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.
III. Such a law is deemed to be an amendment of the Constitution for the purposes of Article 368.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Article 169(3) expressly provides that such a law shall not be deemed to be an amendment of the Constitution for the purposes of Article 368.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Speaker of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly:
