I. The Speaker is chosen by the Assembly from among its own members.
II. He continues in office until immediately before the first meeting of the Assembly after a dissolution.
III. He can be removed only with the prior approval of the Governor.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Removal is by a resolution of the Assembly passed by a majority of all the then members after fourteen days' notice; the Governor has no role.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the history of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly:
I. The first Assembly was constituted in 1952 with 160 members.
II. Its strength rose to 176 after the merger of Ajmer State in 1956.
III. The strength became 200 with the general election of 1977.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct; the intermediate figure was 184 members between 1967 and 1977.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about a Legislative Council for Rajasthan:
I. Rajasthan at present has a bicameral legislature.
II. The Legislative Assembly passed a resolution in 2012 for the creation of a Legislative Council.
III. The Rajasthan Legislative Council Bill, 2013 was introduced in Parliament but has not been enacted.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements II and III are correct. Rajasthan remains unicameral; only six States - Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh - have Legislative Councils.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Money Bills in the Rajasthan Legislature:
I. A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Legislative Assembly.
II. It can be introduced only on the recommendation of the Governor.
III. The Governor may return a Money Bill to the Assembly for reconsideration.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Under the proviso to Article 200 the Governor may return only a Bill other than a Money Bill; on a Money Bill he must give or withhold assent, or reserve it for the President.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Sumitra Singh:
I. She was the first woman Speaker of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly.
II. She held the office during the Twelfth Assembly.
III. She represented a constituency in Jhunjhunu district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Sumitra Singh, a long-serving legislator from the Jhunjhunu region, was Speaker from January 2004 to January 2009.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the powers and proceedings of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly:
I. Article 194 deals with the powers and privileges of the Houses of State Legislatures and their members.
II. Article 212 bars courts from inquiring into the proceedings of the Legislature.
III. Article 208 empowers the House to make rules for regulating its procedure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Article 212 also protects the validity of proceedings from challenge on the ground of alleged irregularity of procedure.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the committees of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly:
I. A Minister cannot be a member of a financial committee.
II. The Public Accounts Committee and the Committee on Estimates are financial committees.
III. The maximum strength of a committee is fifteen members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The committees are normally reconstituted every year and Ministers can neither chair nor sit on them.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the first Rajasthan Legislative Assembly:
I. It was constituted in February 1952.
II. Its first sitting was held at the Sawai Man Singh Town Hall in Jaipur.
III. Tika Ram Paliwal was elected its first Speaker.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Tika Ram Paliwal was the first elected Chief Minister; the first Speaker was Narottam Lal Joshi.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Speaker)   List-II (Period)
A. Narottam Lal Joshi   1. 2019-2023
B. Ram Niwas Mirdha     2. 1952-1957
C. Sumitra Singh        3. 1957-1967
D. C.P. Joshi           4. 2004-2009
questions.exp: Narottam Lal Joshi 1952-57, Ram Niwas Mirdha 1957-67, Sumitra Singh 2004-09 and C.P. Joshi 2019-23.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Article)   List-II (Subject)
A. Article 168   1. Duration of State Legislatures
B. Article 170   2. Constitution of Legislatures in States
C. Article 172   3. Sessions, prorogation and dissolution
D. Article 174   4. Composition of the Legislative Assemblies
questions.exp: Article 168 constitution of State Legislatures, 170 composition of the Assembly, 172 duration and 174 sessions, prorogation and dissolution.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Office)   List-II (First holder)
A. Speaker of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly   1. Sumitra Singh
B. Woman Speaker of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly   2. Narottam Lal Joshi
C. Governor of Rajasthan   3. Heera Lal Shastri
D. Chief Minister of Rajasthan   4. Gurmukh Nihal Singh
questions.exp: Narottam Lal Joshi was the first Speaker, Sumitra Singh the first woman Speaker, Gurmukh Nihal Singh the first Governor and Heera Lal Shastri the first Chief Minister.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Assembly)   List-II (Year of constitution)
A. First Assembly       1. 2018
B. Twelfth Assembly     2. 2023
C. Fifteenth Assembly   3. 1952
D. Sixteenth Assembly   4. 2003
questions.exp: The first Assembly was constituted in 1952, the twelfth after the 2003 election, the fifteenth after 2018 and the sixteenth after the December 2023 election.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Term)   List-II (Meaning)
A. Prorogation          1. Ending of a session of the House by the Governor
B. Adjournment sine die 2. Termination of a sitting without naming a day for reassembly
C. Dissolution          3. Ending the life of the existing Legislative Assembly
D. Quorum               4. Minimum number of members required to transact business
questions.exp: Prorogation ends a session, adjournment sine die ends a sitting without a fixed date, dissolution ends the House itself and the quorum in Rajasthan is 20 members.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Parliamentary device)   List-II (Description)
A. No-confidence motion   1. Moved by the Chief Minister to demonstrate the majority of his government
B. Confidence motion      2. Moved against the Council of Ministers; needs the support of 40 members for admission
C. Adjournment motion     3. Raises a definite matter of urgent public importance and carries an element of censure
D. Calling attention      4. A member calls the attention of a Minister to a matter of urgent public importance
questions.exp: A no-confidence motion needs one-fifth support for admission, a confidence motion is moved by the government itself, an adjournment motion involves censure, and a calling-attention notice does not.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Speaker)   List-II (Assembly presided over)
A. Hari Shankar Bhabhra      1. Fourteenth Assembly
B. Parasram Maderna          2. Ninth Assembly
C. Kailash Chandra Meghwal   3. Sixteenth Assembly
D. Vasudev Devnani           4. Eleventh Assembly
questions.exp: Hari Shankar Bhabhra became Speaker in 1990 (Ninth Assembly), Parasram Maderna in 1999 (Eleventh), Kailash Chandra Meghwal in 2014 (Fourteenth) and Vasudev Devnani in 2023 (Sixteenth).

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs relating to the Speakers of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly is NOT correctly matched?
opts: First Speaker of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly - Narottam Lal Joshi
First woman Speaker of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly - Sumitra Singh
Longest-serving Speaker of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly - Ram Niwas Mirdha
Speaker of the Fifteenth Assembly - Kailash Chandra Meghwal
questions.exp: C.P. Joshi was Speaker of the Fifteenth Assembly (2019-2023); Kailash Chandra Meghwal presided over the Fourteenth Assembly (2014-2019).

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a financial committee of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly?
questions.exp: The Committee on Privileges is a House committee. The four financial committees are Public Accounts, Public Undertakings and Estimates Committees A and B.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly is NOT correct?
opts: Its normal term is five years
It has a Legislative Council as its second chamber
The quorum for its sitting is twenty members
questions.exp: Rajasthan has a unicameral legislature. A resolution for a Legislative Council was passed in 2012 but Parliament has not enacted the necessary law under Article 169.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a disqualification for membership of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly under Article 191?
opts: Holding an office of profit under the State Government
Being of unsound mind as declared by a competent court
Being less than thirty years of age
questions.exp: The minimum age for the Legislative Assembly is 25 years, not 30; thirty is the minimum for a Legislative Council. The other three are disqualifications under Article 191.

questions.q: Which one of the following has NOT held the office of Speaker of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly?
questions.exp: Jagannath Pahadia was Chief Minister of Rajasthan and later a Governor, but never Speaker. The other three all presided over the Assembly.

questions.q:
Arrange the following Speakers of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly in the correct chronological order of assuming office:
I. Parasram Maderna
II. Ram Niwas Mirdha
III. C.P. Joshi
IV. Sumitra Singh
questions.exp: Ram Niwas Mirdha 1957, Parasram Maderna 1999, Sumitra Singh 2004 and C.P. Joshi 2019.

chapters.title: Rajasthan High Court and Subordinate Judiciary
factsheet: Rajasthan High Court — inaugurated 29 August 1949 at Jodhpur; created by the Rajasthan High Court Ordinance, 1949 (promulgated 21 June 1949).
The Ordinance abolished the separate High Courts of the covenanting princely states (Jaipur, Jodhpur, Bikaner, Mewar/Udaipur and the Matsya/Kota unit) and created one High Court for the whole state.
Inaugurated by the Rajpramukh, Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II of Jaipur; twelve judges including the Chief Justice took oath on the inaugural day.
First Chief Justice — Justice Kamal Kant Verma (29 August 1949 – January 1950).
Principal seat — Jodhpur; the only Bench is at Jaipur. Motto: Satyameva Jayate ('Truth alone triumphs').
The Bench that functioned at Jaipur after the 1956 reorganisation was abolished in 1958 on the recommendation of the P. Satyanarayana Rao Committee.
Permanent Jaipur Bench re-created by a Presidential order and began functioning on 31 January 1977.
Sanctioned strength of judges — 50 (38 permanent + 12 additional). New Jodhpur High Court building inaugurated in 2019 by the President of India.
Rajasthan High Court Rules, 1952 came into force on 1 October 1952. Rajasthan has 36 judicial districts and over 1,250 subordinate courts.
Art. 214 — a High Court for each State; Art. 215 — High Court is a court of record with power to punish for contempt.
Art. 216 — composition (Chief Justice + such other judges as the President may appoint); no fixed maximum strength in the Constitution.

Art. 217 — appointment of a High Court judge by the President after consultation with the CJI, the Governor of the State, and (for a judge other than the Chief Justice) the Chief Justice of that High Court.
Qualification for High Court judge — citizen of India; 10 years' judicial office in India OR 10 years as an advocate of a High Court. No minimum age is prescribed.
Retirement age of a High Court judge — 62 years (raised from 60 by the 15th Constitutional Amendment, 1963).
Art. 219 — oath administered by the Governor of the State; Art. 220 — bar on practice after being a permanent judge (except in the Supreme Court and other High Courts).
Art. 221 — salaries of judges charged on the Consolidated Fund of the State; pensions charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.

Art. 222 — transfer of a judge from one High Court to another by the President after consultation with the CJI; Art. 223 — acting Chief Justice; Art. 224 — additional and acting judges; Art. 224A — retired judges at sittings.

Removal of a High Court judge — by Presidential order after an address by both Houses of Parliament with special majority, on proved misbehaviour or incapacity; procedure under the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968.

Art. 226 — writ jurisdiction for fundamental rights 'and for any other purpose' — wider than Art. 32; Art. 227 — superintendence over all courts and tribunals; Art. 228 — transfer of cases involving a substantial question of constitutional law.
Art. 229 — appointments of officers and servants of the High Court (Registrar General, Registrars, staff) are made by the Chief Justice or a judge/officer directed by him — a repeat RPSC favourite.
The Rajasthan High Court has no ordinary original civil jurisdiction (that exists only in the chartered High Courts).

Collegium: for High Court appointments — CJI + two senior-most Supreme Court judges; the High Court collegium is the Chief Justice + two senior-most judges of that High Court. Second Judges Case 1993 and Third Judges Case 1998 govern the consultation process; the NJAC (99th Amendment) was struck down in 2015.

Advocate General of Rajasthan — Art. 165; appointed by the Governor; must be qualified to be a High Court judge; holds office during the Governor's pleasure; under Art. 177 he may speak in either House but cannot vote.

Subordinate judiciary — Art. 233 district judges appointed by the Governor in consultation with the High Court; Art. 233(2) direct recruitment of an advocate of 7 years' standing recommended by the High Court; Art. 234 other judicial officers (Governor + State PSC + High Court); Art. 235 control over subordinate courts vested in the High Court.
Rajasthan Judicial Service (Civil Judge cadre) is recruited through an examination conducted by the Rajasthan High Court; the district judge cadre is the Rajasthan Higher Judicial Service (RHJS).
Rajasthan State Judicial Academy — established 16 November 2001 at Jodhpur.

Lok Adalat — Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987; its award is deemed a decree of a civil court and is final, no appeal lies. Permanent Lok Adalat (Sec. 22B) handles public utility service disputes. NALSA at the Centre, Rajasthan State Legal Services Authority in the state, with the Chief Justice as Patron-in-Chief.
Family Courts Act 1984; Legal Services Authorities Act 1987; Gram Nyayalayas Act 2008; Commercial Courts Act 2015.
Board of Revenue for Rajasthan — Ajmer; the highest court of appeal in revenue matters. Rajasthan Tax Board — Ajmer. Rajasthan Civil Services Appellate Tribunal — Jaipur.
Justice Rajendra Mal Lodha, elevated from the Rajasthan High Court, became the 41st Chief Justice of India (2014).

questions.q: The Rajasthan High Court was established on:
questions.exp: The Rajasthan High Court was inaugurated at Jodhpur on 29 August 1949, following the Rajasthan High Court Ordinance, 1949. 30 March 1949 is Rajasthan Day (formation of Greater Rajasthan), not the High Court's date.

questions.q: The principal seat of the Rajasthan High Court is at:
questions.exp: Jodhpur is the principal seat; Jaipur has the only Bench. The seat was fixed at Jodhpur by the Rajasthan High Court Ordinance, 1949.

questions.q: Who was the first Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court?
questions.exp: Justice Kamal Kant Verma took oath as the first Chief Justice on 29 August 1949 along with eleven other judges. Justice R.M. Lodha, who rose from this Court, later became the 41st Chief Justice of India.

questions.q: The Rajasthan High Court was created by which of the following?
questions.exp: The Rajasthan High Court Ordinance, 1949 (promulgated 21 June 1949) abolished the High Courts of the former covenanting states and created a single High Court for Rajasthan.

questions.q: The Rajasthan High Court at Jodhpur was inaugurated in 1949 by:
opts: Rajpramukh Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II
questions.exp: Maharaja Sawai Man Singh II of Jaipur, then Rajpramukh of Rajasthan, inaugurated the Court. Gurumukh Nihal Singh became Rajasthan's first Governor only in 1956, after the Rajpramukh's office was abolished.

questions.q: The permanent Jaipur Bench of the Rajasthan High Court began functioning on:
questions.exp: The permanent Bench at Jaipur was created by a Presidential order and started work on 31 January 1977. An earlier Jaipur Bench had been abolished in 1958.

questions.q: The Jaipur Bench of the Rajasthan High Court was abolished in 1958 on the recommendation of which committee?
questions.exp: The P. Satyanarayana Rao Committee recommended a single seat, and the Jaipur Bench was abolished in 1958. It was revived as a permanent Bench in 1977.

questions.q: The sanctioned strength of judges of the Rajasthan High Court is:
questions.exp: The sanctioned strength is 50 judges — 38 permanent and 12 additional. The Constitution fixes no maximum; strength is determined by the President under Article 216.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides that there shall be a High Court for each State?
questions.exp: Article 214 provides for a High Court for each State. Article 231 permits a common High Court for two or more States.

questions.q: Under which Article is every High Court a court of record with power to punish for contempt of itself?
questions.exp: Article 215 makes every High Court a court of record. Article 129 makes the same provision for the Supreme Court.

questions.q: A judge of the Rajasthan High Court holds office until he attains the age of:
questions.exp: High Court judges retire at 62; the age was raised from 60 by the 15th Constitutional Amendment, 1963. Supreme Court judges retire at 65.

questions.q: A judge of the Rajasthan High Court is appointed by the President after consultation with the Chief Justice of India, the Governor of Rajasthan and:
opts: the Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court
questions.exp: Under Article 217(1), for the appointment of a judge other than the Chief Justice, the Chief Justice of that High Court is also consulted. Since the Second and Third Judges Cases, 'consultation' with the CJI means concurrence of the collegium.

questions.q: The oath of office to a judge of the Rajasthan High Court is administered by:
opts: The Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court
questions.exp: Article 219 requires a High Court judge to take the oath before the Governor of the State or a person appointed by him. Supreme Court judges take oath before the President.

questions.q: The power of a High Court to issue writs for the enforcement of fundamental rights and 'for any other purpose' flows from:
questions.exp: Article 226 gives High Courts writ jurisdiction for fundamental rights and for any other legal right, making it wider than the Supreme Court's Article 32 jurisdiction.

questions.q: Article 227 of the Constitution confers on the High Court:
opts: Power of superintendence over all courts and tribunals within its territorial jurisdiction
Power to transfer cases to itself
questions.exp: Article 227 gives the High Court administrative and judicial superintendence over all courts and tribunals in its territory (except military tribunals). Article 228 covers transfer of cases involving a substantial question of constitutional law.

questions.q: Appointments of officers and servants of the Rajasthan High Court, including the Registrar General, are made by:
opts: The Chief Justice of the High Court, or a judge or officer of the Court directed by him
The Department of Personnel, Government of Rajasthan
questions.exp: Article 229 vests appointment of High Court staff in the Chief Justice or his nominee, securing the independence of the Registry. The Registrar General is the administrative head of the Registry.

questions.q: The Advocate General of Rajasthan is appointed by the Governor under which Article?
questions.exp: Article 165 provides for the Advocate General of a State; Article 76 is the Attorney General of India. He must be qualified to be a High Court judge.

questions.q: District judges in Rajasthan are appointed by the Governor in consultation with:
questions.exp: Article 233 requires the Governor to consult the High Court for the appointment, posting and promotion of district judges. Article 234 brings in the State Public Service Commission for the lower judicial service.

questions.q: Control over district courts and subordinate courts, including posting, promotion and grant of leave to members of the judicial service, is vested in the High Court by:
questions.exp: Article 235 vests control over the subordinate judiciary in the High Court — a core guarantee of judicial independence at the district level.

questions.q: The Rajasthan State Judicial Academy is located at:
questions.exp: The Rajasthan State Judicial Academy was established on 16 November 2001 at Jodhpur, the seat of the High Court, and trains judicial officers of the state.

questions.q: Lok Adalats in India derive their statutory status from:
questions.exp: The Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 gave Lok Adalats statutory backing and created NALSA and the State Legal Services Authorities, including the Rajasthan State Legal Services Authority.

questions.q: The highest court of appeal in revenue matters in Rajasthan is the Board of Revenue, whose headquarters is at:
questions.exp: The Board of Revenue for Rajasthan sits at Ajmer and is the apex revenue court of the state, hearing appeals from Divisional Commissioners and Collectors.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Tax Board has its headquarters at:
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Tax Board, the appellate authority in commercial tax matters, functions from Ajmer — the same city as the Board of Revenue and the RPSC.

questions.q: The transfer of a judge from the Rajasthan High Court to another High Court is made by the President after consultation with:
opts: The Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court
questions.exp: Article 222 empowers the President to transfer a judge from one High Court to another after consultation with the Chief Justice of India. The consent of the judge is not constitutionally required.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the establishment of the Rajasthan High Court:
I. It was created under the Rajasthan High Court Ordinance, 1949, which abolished the separate High Courts of the former covenanting states.
II. It was formally inaugurated at Jodhpur on 29 August 1949.
III. Kamal Kant Verma was sworn in as its first Chief Justice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Ordinance of 21 June 1949 merged the High Courts of Jaipur, Jodhpur, Bikaner, Mewar and the Matsya unit into one High Court seated at Jodhpur.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Jaipur Bench of the Rajasthan High Court:
I. The Bench that functioned at Jaipur after the reorganisation of states was abolished in 1958.
II. A permanent Bench at Jaipur was created by an order of the President and began functioning on 31 January 1977.
III. The principal seat of the High Court continues to be at Jodhpur.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Jodhpur remains the principal seat and Jaipur is the only Bench of the Rajasthan High Court.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the qualifications for appointment as a judge of a High Court:
I. The person must be a citizen of India.
II. He must have held a judicial office in the territory of India for at least ten years, or have been an advocate of a High Court for at least ten years.
III. The Constitution prescribes a minimum age of 40 years for appointment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II reproduce Article 217(2). The Constitution prescribes no minimum age for a High Court judge — only a retirement age of 62 years.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the appointment of High Court judges:
I. The collegium that initiates a recommendation for a High Court consists of the Chief Justice of that High Court and its two senior-most judges.
II. The Supreme Court collegium for High Court appointments consists of the Chief Justice of India and the two senior-most judges of the Supreme Court.
III. The National Judicial Appointments Commission created by the 99th Constitutional Amendment was struck down by the Supreme Court in 2015.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The collegium system rests on the Second Judges Case (1993) and the Third Judges Case (1998); the NJAC was struck down in the Fourth Judges Case, 2015.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the removal of a judge of the Rajasthan High Court:
I. He can be removed by an order of the President on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity.
II. The removal requires an address by each House of Parliament supported by a special majority.
III. The Rajasthan Legislative Assembly must also pass a resolution recommending his removal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: High Court judges are removed by the same process as Supreme Court judges under Article 217(1)(b) read with Article 124(4) and the Judges (Inquiry) Act, 1968. The State Legislature has no role.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 226 and Article 32:
I. Article 226 can be invoked only for the enforcement of fundamental rights.
II. The writ jurisdiction of a High Court is wider in scope than that of the Supreme Court under Article 32.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Article 226 covers fundamental rights 'and for any other purpose', that is, ordinary legal rights as well — hence it is wider than Article 32, which is confined to fundamental rights.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Lok Adalats:
I. An award of a Lok Adalat is deemed to be a decree of a civil court.
II. No appeal lies against an award of a Lok Adalat.
III. A Permanent Lok Adalat is constituted for disputes relating to public utility services.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987. The award is final and binding; the only remedy against it is a writ petition, not an appeal.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the subordinate judiciary in Rajasthan:
I. Recruitment to the Rajasthan Judicial Service (Civil Judge cadre) is made through an examination conducted by the Rajasthan High Court.
II. An advocate of at least seven years' standing recommended by the High Court is eligible for direct appointment as a district judge.
III. Persons other than district judges are appointed to the judicial service by the Governor in accordance with rules framed after consulting the State Public Service Commission and the High Court.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct — statement II reflects Article 233(2) and statement III Article 234. The district judge cadre in the state is the Rajasthan Higher Judicial Service.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Advocate General of Rajasthan:
I. He must be qualified to be appointed a judge of a High Court.
II. He holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.
III. He has the right to speak in and take part in the proceedings of the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly and to vote therein.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Under Article 177 the Advocate General may speak in and take part in the proceedings of either House and its committees, but he has no right to vote.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Article)   List-II (Provision)
A. Article 214   1. High Court to be a court of record
B. Article 215   2. High Court for each State
C. Article 226   3. Power of superintendence over courts and tribunals
D. Article 227   4. Power to issue writs
questions.exp: Article 214 — High Court for each State; 215 — court of record; 226 — writs; 227 — superintendence. Article 228 covers transfer of cases involving constitutional questions.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Year)   List-II (Event relating to the Rajasthan High Court)
A. 1949   1. Abolition of the Jaipur Bench on a committee's recommendation
B. 1958   2. Inauguration of the High Court at Jodhpur
C. 1977   3. Establishment of the Rajasthan State Judicial Academy
D. 2001   4. Commencement of the permanent Jaipur Bench
questions.exp: 1949 inauguration at Jodhpur, 1958 abolition of the Jaipur Bench on the P. Satyanarayana Rao Committee's recommendation, 31 January 1977 permanent Jaipur Bench, 16 November 2001 Judicial Academy at Jodhpur.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Institution)   List-II (Governing Act)
A. Family Court   1. Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987
B. Lok Adalat   2. Family Courts Act, 1984
C. Gram Nyayalaya   3. Commercial Courts Act, 2015
D. Commercial Court   4. Gram Nyayalayas Act, 2008
questions.exp: Family Courts Act 1984, Legal Services Authorities Act 1987 (Lok Adalats), Gram Nyayalayas Act 2008 and Commercial Courts Act 2015 are the four governing statutes.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Article)   List-II (Subject)
A. Article 233   1. Control over subordinate courts vested in the High Court
B. Article 234   2. Appointment of district judges
C. Article 235   3. Definition of 'district judge'
D. Article 236   4. Recruitment of persons other than district judges to the judicial service
questions.exp: Articles 233 to 237 form Chapter VI on subordinate courts: 233 appointment of district judges, 234 other judicial officers, 235 High Court's control, 236 definitions.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Article)   List-II (Provision)
A. Article 217   1. Transfer of a judge from one High Court to another
B. Article 219   2. Appointment of judges of a High Court
C. Article 222   3. Appointment of additional and acting judges
D. Article 224   4. Oath or affirmation by judges of a High Court
questions.exp: Article 217 appointment, 219 oath before the Governor, 222 transfer by the President after consulting the CJI, 224 additional and acting judges (224A allows retired judges to sit).

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Rajasthan High Court is NOT correct?
opts: It was inaugurated at Jodhpur on 29 August 1949.
Its sanctioned strength of judges is 50.
Its permanent Jaipur Bench started functioning in 1977.
It exercises ordinary original civil jurisdiction over the city of Jaipur.
questions.exp: Ordinary original civil jurisdiction exists only in the chartered High Courts such as Calcutta, Bombay, Madras and Delhi. The Rajasthan High Court has no such jurisdiction.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of a Constitutional Article and its subject is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Article 214 — High Court for each State
Article 226 — Writ jurisdiction of the High Court
Article 229 — Appointment of officers and servants of the High Court
Article 231 — Retirement age of a High Court judge
questions.exp: Article 231 provides for a common High Court for two or more States. The retirement age of 62 years is prescribed in Article 217(1).

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Advocate General of Rajasthan is NOT correct?
opts: He is appointed by the Governor of Rajasthan.
He must be qualified to be appointed a judge of a High Court.
He is entitled to vote in the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly.
He holds office during the pleasure of the Governor.
questions.exp: Article 177 gives the Advocate General the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of either House, but expressly denies him a vote.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the subordinate judiciary in Rajasthan is NOT correct?
opts: District judges are appointed by the Governor in consultation with the High Court.
Control over district and subordinate courts is vested in the State Government.
An advocate of seven years' standing recommended by the High Court may be directly appointed a district judge.
Recruitment to the Rajasthan Judicial Service (Civil Judge cadre) is made through an examination conducted by the Rajasthan High Court.
questions.exp: Article 235 vests control over district and subordinate courts in the High Court, not in the State Government — this is the constitutional guarantee of judicial independence at the district level.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about Lok Adalats is NOT correct?
opts: They function under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987.
Their awards are deemed to be decrees of a civil court.
An appeal against an award of a Lok Adalat lies to the District Court.
A Permanent Lok Adalat deals with disputes relating to public utility services.
questions.exp: No appeal lies against a Lok Adalat award; it is final and binding on the parties. Only a writ petition to the High Court is possible in exceptional cases.

questions.q:
Arrange the following events relating to the Rajasthan High Court in correct chronological order:
I. Establishment of the Rajasthan State Judicial Academy
II. Inauguration of the High Court at Jodhpur
III. Commencement of the permanent Jaipur Bench
IV. Abolition of the Jaipur Bench on the recommendation of the Satyanarayana Rao Committee
questions.exp: Inauguration 1949, abolition of the Jaipur Bench 1958, permanent Jaipur Bench 31 January 1977, Judicial Academy 16 November 2001.

questions.q:
Arrange the following Central enactments in the correct chronological order of their enactment:
I. Legal Services Authorities Act
II. Family Courts Act
III. Commercial Courts Act
IV. Gram Nyayalayas Act
questions.exp: Family Courts Act 1984, Legal Services Authorities Act 1987, Gram Nyayalayas Act 2008, Commercial Courts Act 2015.

chapters.title: State Secretariat, Chief Secretary and Directorates
factsheet: State Secretariat (Shasan Sachivalaya), Jaipur — the apex office of the state government; houses the Chief Minister, ministers, the Chief Secretary and departmental secretaries.
Secretariat = staff / policy-making agency; Directorate = line / executing agency. This distinction is a classic RPSC discriminator.
Secretariat functions: policy formulation, assisting ministers, legislative and budget work, coordination between departments, service and financial rules, supervision of directorates.
Directorate functions: field execution, technical advice, supervision of district-level staff; headed by a Director (also called Head of Department, HoD), usually a technical or specialist officer.

Secretariat hierarchy: Chief Secretary > Additional Chief Secretary > Principal Secretary > Secretary > Special Secretary > Joint Secretary > Deputy Secretary > Assistant Secretary > Section Officer (Anubhag Adhikari).

Art. 166(1) — all executive action of the state is expressed in the name of the Governor; 166(2) authentication of orders; 166(3) — the Governor makes Rules of Business for the more convenient transaction of business and allocates it among ministers.
Art. 167 — duty of the Chief Minister to communicate decisions of the Council of Ministers to the Governor and to furnish information he calls for.
Chief Secretary — administrative head of the whole state administration; normally the senior-most IAS officer of the Rajasthan cadre; appointed by the Chief Minister; no fixed constitutional tenure.

Chief Secretary's roles: chief adviser to the Chief Minister, Secretary to the Council of Ministers, head of the Secretariat, head of the Department of Personnel and General Administration, chief of the state civil services, chairman of the state's Civil Services Board and of numerous state-level committees.
First Chief Secretary of Rajasthan — K. Radhakrishnan (13 April 1949 – 2 May 1950). A recurring RPSC question.

Recent Chief Secretaries: Niranjan Kumar Arya (Nov 2020 – Jan 2022), Usha Sharma (Feb 2022 – Dec 2023), Sudhansh Pant (Jan 2024 – 16 Nov 2025), V. Srinivas (from 17 November 2025; incumbent as of September 2026).

Department of Personnel (DoP) — held by the Chief Minister; cadre controlling authority for the IAS and the Rajasthan Administrative Service; handles service rules, postings and transfers. Raj Kaj is its integrated e-office and employee service application.

Administrative Reforms Department — nodal for administrative reform, e-governance, citizen's charters, the Rajasthan Guaranteed Delivery of Public Services Act 2011 and the Rajasthan Right to Hearing Act 2012.

General Administration Department — inter-departmental coordination and Secretariat establishment; Finance Department — budget and financial control; Planning Department — plan formulation and statistics.
Directorate of Elementary Education and Directorate of Secondary Education — Bikaner. Directorate of Mines and Geology — Udaipur. Directorate of Ayurved — Ajmer.
Rajasthan Public Service Commission — Ajmer (1949); Board of Secondary Education Rajasthan — Ajmer; Board of Revenue for Rajasthan — Ajmer.

HCM Rajasthan State Institute of Public Administration (HCM RIPA), Jaipur — established 1957; the apex civil services training institute of the state, popularly called OTS; named after parliamentarian Harish Chandra Mathur.

HCM RIPA conducts foundation and in-service training for RAS, RPS, RAcS and other state services and for IAS officers of the Rajasthan cadre; it has regional training centres at Udaipur, Bikaner, Jodhpur and Kota.

Rajasthan Administrative Service (RAS) — the premier state civil service; direct recruits selected by the RPSC through the RAS & RTS Combined Competitive Examination; a part of the cadre is filled by promotion from subordinate services such as Tehsildars.
The combined examination is held under the Rajasthan State and Subordinate Services (Direct Recruitment by Combined Competitive Examinations) Rules, 1999 — Prelims, Mains and Interview.

RAS career path: Assistant Collector / Sub-Divisional Magistrate > Additional District Collector / Additional Divisional Commissioner / Deputy Secretary; grades run from junior scale to higher super-time scale. Seniority follows the year of allotment and merit position.

RAS to IAS: promotion on the recommendation of a Selection Committee under the IAS (Appointment by Promotion) Regulations, 1955, chaired by the Chairman or a Member of the UPSC; not more than one-third (33 1/3 per cent) of the senior duty posts of the state IAS cadre may be filled by promotion and selection; minimum eight years of continuous service in the State Civil Service for inclusion in the select list; the appointment order is issued by the Central Government.
Rajasthan Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1958 — classification of services, disciplinary authorities, inquiry procedure, penalties and appeals.

CCA Rules — minor penalties: censure, withholding of promotion, recovery of pecuniary loss, withholding of increments. Major penalties: reduction in rank/pay, compulsory retirement, removal from service, dismissal from service.

Rajasthan Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1971 — absolute integrity and devotion to duty, bar on accepting gifts beyond limits, no trade or business without sanction, no unauthorised criticism of government policy, property returns, no speculation in stocks.

Constitutional backing: Art. 308-314 (Services); Art. 309 recruitment and conditions of service; Art. 310 doctrine of pleasure; Art. 311 safeguards — 311(1) no dismissal by an authority subordinate to the appointing authority, 311(2) inquiry with reasonable opportunity of being heard.

E-governance in the Secretariat: Raj Kaj (e-file / employee services), IFMS (Integrated Financial Management System), SSO Rajasthan single sign-on, Rajasthan Sampark grievance portal, e-Mitra service delivery kiosks, Jan Soochna portal (2019).
Board of Revenue for Rajasthan (Ajmer) is the apex revenue court, functioning outside the Secretariat-Directorate chain.

questions.q: Who was the first Chief Secretary of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: K. Radhakrishnan served as Rajasthan's first Chief Secretary from 13 April 1949 to 2 May 1950. Hiralal Shastri was the first Chief Minister, Gurumukh Nihal Singh the first Governor and Man Singh II the first (and only) Rajpramukh.

questions.q: As of September 2026, the Chief Secretary of Rajasthan is:
questions.exp: V. Srinivas (Voruganti Srinivas), IAS, took charge as Chief Secretary of Rajasthan on 17 November 2025, succeeding Sudhansh Pant; he is the incumbent as of September 2026.

questions.q: The State Secretariat of Rajasthan is located at:
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Secretariat (Shasan Sachivalaya) functions from Jaipur, the state capital. The Rajasthan High Court's principal seat is at Jodhpur and the RPSC is at Ajmer.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Government Rules of Business, which allocate business among ministers, are made by:
questions.exp: Article 166(3) empowers the Governor to make rules for the more convenient transaction of the business of the state government and for its allocation among ministers, on the advice of the Chief Minister.

questions.q: Under Article 166(1) of the Constitution, all executive action of the Government of Rajasthan is expressed to be taken in the name of:
questions.exp: Article 166(1) requires all executive action of a state to be expressed in the name of the Governor; Article 166(2) provides for authentication of such orders so that their validity cannot be questioned.

questions.q: In the Government of Rajasthan, the Department of Personnel is normally held by:
questions.exp: The Department of Personnel is retained by the Chief Minister; the Chief Secretary is its administrative head. It is the cadre controlling authority for the IAS and the Rajasthan Administrative Service.

questions.q: The State Secretariat is best described as:
opts: A line agency that executes government programmes in the field
A staff agency that assists ministers in policy formulation
A technical agency headed by a Director
A statutory body created by an Act of the state legislature
questions.exp: The Secretariat is a staff agency for policy formulation, coordination and control; execution in the field is left to the directorates, which are line agencies.

questions.q: A Directorate in the Rajasthan administrative system is headed by:
questions.exp: A Directorate is headed by a Director, who is also the Head of the Department (HoD) and is usually a technical or specialist officer, unlike the generalist Secretary in the Secretariat.

questions.q: The Directorate of Elementary Education of Rajasthan is located at:
questions.exp: Both the Directorate of Elementary Education and the Directorate of Secondary Education of Rajasthan function from Bikaner, while the Board of Secondary Education is at Ajmer.

questions.q: The Directorate of Mines and Geology, Rajasthan, has its headquarters at:
questions.exp: The Directorate of Mines and Geology is located at Udaipur, in the heart of Rajasthan's mineral belt. The Rajasthan State Mines and Minerals Limited (RSMML) is also headquartered at Udaipur.

questions.q: HCM Rajasthan State Institute of Public Administration (RIPA) was established in the year:
questions.exp: HCM RIPA, Jaipur was set up in 1957 and is the apex training institute of the Rajasthan Government for state civil services and for IAS officers of the state cadre.

questions.q: HCM RIPA, the apex training institute of the Rajasthan Government at Jaipur, is named after:
questions.exp: The institute is named after Harish Chandra Mathur, a noted parliamentarian from Rajasthan. It is popularly known in Jaipur as OTS (Officers' Training School).

questions.q: Recruitment to the Rajasthan Administrative Service is made through a competitive examination conducted by:
questions.exp: The RPSC, Ajmer conducts the RAS & RTS Combined Competitive Examination for direct recruitment to the Rajasthan Administrative Service and allied state services.

questions.q: Disciplinary proceedings and penalties against Rajasthan state government servants are governed by:
opts: The Rajasthan Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1958
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1958 lay down disciplinary authorities, inquiry procedure, minor and major penalties, and appeals.

questions.q: Restrictions on a Rajasthan government servant regarding acceptance of gifts, criticism of government policy and submission of property returns are contained in:
opts: The Rajasthan Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1958
The Rajasthan Transparency in Public Procurement Act, 2012
The Rajasthan Right to Hearing Act, 2012
questions.exp: The Conduct Rules, 1971 prescribe standards of behaviour — integrity, devotion to duty, restrictions on gifts, trade, speculation and public criticism of government policy. The CCA Rules, 1958 deal with punishing their breach.

questions.q: Which Article of the Constitution provides that no civil servant shall be dismissed, removed or reduced in rank except after an inquiry in which he has been informed of the charges and given a reasonable opportunity of being heard?
questions.exp: Article 311(2) is the principal safeguard for civil servants. Article 311(1) adds that no one may be dismissed or removed by an authority subordinate to that which appointed him.

questions.q: The power to regulate the recruitment and conditions of service of persons appointed to state services is conferred by:
questions.exp: Article 309 allows the appropriate legislature to regulate recruitment and service conditions and, until it does so, permits the Governor to make rules — the source of the Rajasthan Civil Services Rules.

questions.q: The 'doctrine of pleasure', under which members of the state civil services hold office during the pleasure of the Governor, is embodied in:
questions.exp: Article 310 embodies the doctrine of pleasure for state services, subject to the safeguards in Article 311. Article 308 is only the definition clause of Part XIV.

questions.q: The maximum share of senior duty posts in the IAS cadre of a State that may be filled by promotion from the State Civil Service and by selection from other sources is:
questions.exp: Under the IAS (Cadre) Rules, not more than one-third (33 1/3 per cent) of the senior duty posts may be filled by promotion from the State Civil Service and selection from non-state-civil-service officers.

questions.q: The Selection Committee that prepares the select list for promotion of State Civil Service officers to the Indian Administrative Service is chaired by:
opts: The Chief Secretary of the State
The Chairman or a Member of the Union Public Service Commission
The Chairman of the State Public Service Commission
questions.exp: Under the IAS (Appointment by Promotion) Regulations, 1955, the Selection Committee is chaired by the Chairman or a Member of the UPSC, with the state's Chief Secretary and senior officers as members.

questions.q: 'Raj Kaj' in the Rajasthan administrative system refers to:
opts: A scheme for employment of rural youth
A grievance redressal helpline of the Rajasthan Police
A skill development mission of the state
An integrated e-governance and e-file application used by Rajasthan government employees and offices
questions.exp: Raj Kaj is the state's integrated e-office platform covering electronic files, employee service records, leave and transfer processes. Related state platforms include IFMS, SSO Rajasthan and Rajasthan Sampark.

questions.q: In the Government of Rajasthan, the nodal department for administrative reforms, citizen's charters and guaranteed delivery of public services is:
questions.exp: The Administrative Reforms Department is the nodal agency for administrative reform, e-governance, citizen's charters and the Rajasthan Guaranteed Delivery of Public Services Act, 2011.

questions.q: The RAS and RTS Combined Competitive Examination is conducted under:
opts: The Rajasthan State and Subordinate Services (Direct Recruitment by Combined Competitive Examinations) Rules, 1999
The Rajasthan Public Service Commission (Conditions of Service) Regulations, 1950
questions.exp: The 1999 Rules govern direct recruitment through the combined competitive examination to the state and subordinate services, prescribing the Preliminary, Main and Interview stages.

questions.q: In relation to the Council of Ministers of Rajasthan, the Chief Secretary functions as:
opts: The Chairman of the Cabinet Committee on Appointments
The Secretary to the Council of Ministers
A member of the Council of Ministers
The presiding officer of Cabinet meetings
questions.exp: The Chief Secretary acts as Secretary to the Council of Ministers, preparing agenda, recording decisions and ensuring their implementation. He is a civil servant and never a member of the Council.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Chief Secretary of Rajasthan:
I. He is normally the senior-most IAS officer serving in the state cadre.
II. He is appointed by the Chief Minister.
III. The Constitution prescribes a fixed tenure of two years for the office.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The office of Chief Secretary is not a constitutional office and has no fixed tenure; the Chief Minister selects the incumbent, usually the senior-most IAS officer of the state cadre.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements distinguishing the Secretariat from the Directorates in Rajasthan:
I. The Secretariat is primarily concerned with policy formulation, while the Directorate is concerned with execution.
II. A Directorate is generally headed by a technical or specialist officer designated as Head of the Department.
III. The Secretariat is a field agency, whereas the Directorate works only at the state headquarters.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statement III inverts the true position: the Secretariat is the headquarters staff agency and the Directorate is the executing agency with a field establishment across districts.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajasthan Administrative Service:
I. Its cadre controlling authority is the Department of Personnel, Government of Rajasthan.
II. Direct recruits are selected through a competitive examination held by the Rajasthan Public Service Commission.
III. Foundation and professional training of RAS officers is imparted at HCM RIPA, Jaipur.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. A part of the RAS cadre is additionally filled by promotion from subordinate services such as the Tehsildar cadre.

questions.q:
Consider the following penalties under the Rajasthan Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1958:
I. Censure
II. Compulsory retirement
III. Dismissal from service
Which of the above are major penalties?
questions.exp: Censure is a minor penalty. Compulsory retirement, removal and dismissal, along with reduction in rank or pay, are major penalties requiring a formal departmental inquiry.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajasthan Civil Services (Conduct) Rules, 1971:
I. A government servant is required to maintain absolute integrity and devotion to duty.
II. A government servant may not, except with prior sanction, engage in any trade or business.
III. The Rules permit a government servant to criticise the policies of the State Government in the press.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Conduct Rules bar a government servant from making any adverse public criticism of the policies or actions of the government. Statements I and II are core obligations under the Rules.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. K. Radhakrishnan was the first Chief Secretary of Rajasthan.
II. The Chief Secretary is the administrative head of the State Secretariat.
III. The Chief Secretary is the ex-officio Chairman of the Board of Revenue for Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Board of Revenue for Rajasthan at Ajmer has its own Chairman and is independent of the Chief Secretary. K. Radhakrishnan held office as the first Chief Secretary from 1949 to 1950.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Article 166 provides for the conduct of business of the Government of a State.
II. Article 167 makes it the duty of the Chief Minister to communicate to the Governor all decisions of the Council of Ministers relating to the administration of the state.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Both are correct. Article 166 also empowers the Governor to make Rules of Business, and Article 167 further obliges the Chief Minister to furnish any information the Governor calls for.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about promotion of Rajasthan Administrative Service officers to the Indian Administrative Service:
I. Promotion is made on the recommendation of a Selection Committee constituted under the IAS (Appointment by Promotion) Regulations, 1955.
II. An officer must ordinarily have completed at least eight years of continuous service in the State Civil Service to be eligible for inclusion in the select list.
III. The final appointment order to the Indian Administrative Service is issued by the Government of Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Appointment to the IAS by promotion is notified by the Central Government (Department of Personnel and Training), not by the state government, so statement III is wrong.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Office)   List-II (Headquarters)
A. Directorate of Elementary Education   1. Ajmer
B. Directorate of Mines and Geology   2. Bikaner
C. Rajasthan Public Service Commission   3. Jaipur
D. HCM RIPA   4. Udaipur
questions.exp: Elementary Education Directorate — Bikaner; Mines and Geology — Udaipur; RPSC — Ajmer; HCM RIPA — Jaipur.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Department)   List-II (Principal function)
A. Department of Personnel   1. Preparation of the state budget and financial control
B. Administrative Reforms Department   2. Cadre management and service rules of state services
C. Finance Department   3. Inter-departmental coordination and Secretariat establishment
D. General Administration Department   4. Citizen's charters, e-governance and public service delivery reform
questions.exp: The Department of Personnel handles cadres and service rules, the Administrative Reforms Department handles reform and service delivery, Finance handles the budget and GAD handles coordination.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Article)   List-II (Provision)
A. Article 166   1. Doctrine of pleasure
B. Article 167   2. Conduct of business of the Government of a State
C. Article 309   3. Duties of the Chief Minister towards the Governor
D. Article 310   4. Recruitment and conditions of service of persons serving the State
questions.exp: Article 166 conduct of business, 167 duties of the Chief Minister, 309 recruitment and service conditions, 310 doctrine of pleasure.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Rule or Act)   List-II (Year)
A. Rajasthan Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules   1. 1999
B. Rajasthan Civil Services (Conduct) Rules   2. 2011
C. Rajasthan State and Subordinate Services (Direct Recruitment by Combined Competitive Examinations) Rules   3. 1958
D. Rajasthan Guaranteed Delivery of Public Services Act   4. 1971
questions.exp: CCA Rules 1958, Conduct Rules 1971, Combined Competitive Examination Rules 1999, Guaranteed Delivery of Public Services Act 2011.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Functionary)   List-II (Role)
A. Chief Secretary   1. Head of a Directorate and technical head of a department
B. Principal Secretary   2. Administrative head of the entire state administration
C. Director   3. Unit head in the Secretariat responsible for initial handling of files
D. Section Officer   4. Administrative head of a department within the Secretariat
questions.exp: The Chief Secretary heads the state administration, the Principal Secretary heads a Secretariat department, the Director heads a Directorate, and the Section Officer heads a section within the Secretariat.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Body)   List-II (Nature)
A. State Secretariat   1. Line agency for field execution
B. Directorate   2. Staff agency for policy formulation
C. Rajasthan Public Service Commission   3. Training institution
D. HCM RIPA   4. Constitutional body for recruitment
questions.exp: The Secretariat is a staff agency, the Directorate a line agency, the RPSC a constitutional body under Article 315, and HCM RIPA a training institute.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Chief Secretary of Rajasthan is NOT correct?
opts: He is the administrative head of the State Secretariat.
He acts as the chief adviser to the Chief Minister.
He is appointed by the Governor on the recommendation of the Union Public Service Commission.
He is generally the senior-most IAS officer serving in the state.
questions.exp: The Chief Secretary is chosen by the Chief Minister from among senior IAS officers of the state cadre; the UPSC has no role in the appointment.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a characteristic of the State Secretariat?
opts: It assists the ministers in the formulation of policy.
It exercises direct field-level execution of departmental programmes.
It coordinates the work of different departments of the government.
It is headed administratively by the Chief Secretary.
questions.exp: Field-level execution is the work of the directorates and the district administration. The Secretariat formulates policy, coordinates, and supervises.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of an office and its headquarters is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Directorate of Mines and Geology — Jodhpur
questions.exp: The Directorate of Mines and Geology is at Udaipur, not Jodhpur. The other three pairs are correctly matched.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a major penalty under the Rajasthan Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1958?
questions.exp: Censure is a minor penalty. Major penalties include reduction in rank or pay, compulsory retirement, removal and dismissal from service.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Rajasthan Administrative Service is NOT correct?
opts: Direct recruitment to it is made by the Rajasthan Public Service Commission.
Its members are appointed to the service by the Union Public Service Commission on the advice of the Central Government.
A part of its cadre is filled by promotion from subordinate services.
Its officers are trained at HCM RIPA, Jaipur.
questions.exp: The RAS is a state service; appointments are made by the Government of Rajasthan on the RPSC's recommendation. The UPSC's role arises only later, in promotion of RAS officers to the IAS.

questions.q:
Arrange the following Chief Secretaries of Rajasthan in the correct chronological order of their assuming office:
I. Sudhansh Pant
II. Usha Sharma
III. V. Srinivas
IV. Niranjan Kumar Arya
questions.exp: Niranjan Kumar Arya (November 2020), Usha Sharma (February 2022), Sudhansh Pant (January 2024) and V. Srinivas (17 November 2025), who is the incumbent as of September 2026.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The State Secretariat of Rajasthan does not itself implement government programmes in the field.
Reason (R): Implementation is entrusted to the Directorates, which are the executive agencies headed by Directors.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: Both statements are true and the Reason explains the Assertion: the Secretariat is a staff agency for policy, and the Directorates are the line agencies that execute policy through their field establishments.

chapters.title: Divisional and District Administration; Board of Revenue
factsheet: Rajasthan has 7 divisions (sambhag) and 41 districts as of January 2025, after the cabinet decision of 28 December 2024 scrapped 9 of the 17 districts and all 3 of the divisions created in 2023.
The seven divisions are Jaipur, Jodhpur, Udaipur, Bikaner and Kota (all 1949), Ajmer (1987) and Bharatpur (2005) — each division is named after its headquarters town.
Divisions abolished in December 2024: Banswara, Pali and Sikar (all created in 2023 under CM Ashok Gehlot).
Nine districts abolished in December 2024: Dudu, Kekri, Shahpura, Neem Ka Thana, Gangapur City, Jaipur Rural, Jodhpur Rural, Anupgarh and Sanchore.
Eight of the 2023 districts were retained: Balotra, Beawar, Deeg, Didwana-Kuchaman, Kotputli-Behror, Khairthal-Tijara, Phalodi and Salumbar.
The office of Divisional Commissioner was ABOLISHED in 1962 by the Rajasthan Divisional Commissioner (Office Abolition) Act, 1962, under CM Mohan Lal Sukhadia.
The office of Divisional Commissioner was RESTORED on 26 January 1987 under CM Haridev Joshi; Ajmer was simultaneously made the sixth division.
The Divisional Commissioner is a senior IAS officer; he supervises district administration, is an appellate revenue authority above the Collector, and coordinates development in the division.

The District Collector is appointed by the State Government from the IAS cadre; he is simultaneously Collector (revenue), District Magistrate (law and order), District Election Officer, Chairman of the District Disaster Management Authority, and District Registrar of births and deaths.

Revenue hierarchy in descending order: Board of Revenue → Divisional Commissioner → Collector → Revenue Appellate Authority (parallel appellate) → Sub-Divisional Officer / Assistant Collector → Tehsildar → Naib Tehsildar → Girdawar (Kanungo) → Patwari.
The Patwari is the lowest revenue functionary; his jurisdiction is the patwar circle; he maintains the khasra and carries out girdawari (crop inspection).
The Girdawar (Kanungo) supervises a group of patwar circles; the Naib Tehsildar heads a sub-tehsil; the Tehsildar heads a tehsil and exercises the powers of an Assistant Collector.
The Sub-Divisional Officer (SDO/SDM) heads a sub-division and is the link between the district and the tehsil.
Jamabandi = the record of rights of a village; Khasra = the field-wise register; Girdawari = periodical crop inspection; Bandobast = settlement operations.
The Board of Revenue for Rajasthan was created by Ordinance No. 22 of 1949 on 7 April 1949 and enforced on 1 November 1949; its seat is at AJMER.

The Board of Revenue is the highest court of appeal, revision and reference in revenue matters in Rajasthan; under the Rajasthan Land Revenue Act, 1956 it consists of a Chairman and not more than 20 members.
Key revenue legislation: Rajasthan Land Revenue Act, 1956 and Rajasthan Tenancy Act, 1955 (in force 15 October 1955).
The Rajasthan Tax Board (Ajmer) hears appeals in commercial-tax matters; the Rajasthan Civil Services Appellate Tribunal (Jaipur) hears service appeals of state employees.
District Planning Committee: constitutional basis Article 243ZD; in Rajasthan it is provided for by Section 121 of the Rajasthan Panchayati Raj Act, 1994; its chairperson is the ZILA PRAMUKH.
Article 243ZD requires that not less than FOUR-FIFTHS of the members of a District Planning Committee be elected from among the elected members of the panchayats and municipalities of the district.
The Chief Executive Officer of the Zila Parishad (an IAS/RAS officer) is its executive head and ex-officio secretary; the Zila Pramukh is its elected political head.
The Superintendent of Police (an IPS officer) heads the district police and works under the general direction of the District Magistrate; police commissionerates operate in Jaipur and Jodhpur.
District police hierarchy outside commissionerates: DGP → ADGP → IG → DIG → SP → Additional SP → Deputy SP → Inspector → Sub-Inspector.

Under the Disaster Management Act, 2005 the District Disaster Management Authority is chaired by the District Collector; at the state level the Rajasthan State Disaster Management Authority is chaired by the Chief Minister.
The District Rural Development Agency (DRDA) is the district-level agency for implementation of centrally sponsored rural development schemes.
Section 163 of the BNSS (formerly Section 144 CrPC) is the prohibitory-order power exercised by the District Magistrate.
The Collector is the custodian of government land in the district and the district-level authority for arms and explosives licensing.
Kota, Bikaner, Jaipur, Jodhpur and Udaipur were the five original divisions constituted in 1949 at the time of the formation of Greater Rajasthan.

questions.q: As of January 2025, how many administrative divisions (sambhag) does Rajasthan have?
questions.exp: Rajasthan has 7 divisions and 41 districts as of January 2025. The three divisions created in 2023 (Banswara, Pali, Sikar) were abolished by the state cabinet decision of 28 December 2024.

questions.q: The Board of Revenue for Rajasthan has its headquarters at
questions.exp: The Board of Revenue for Rajasthan sits at Ajmer. It is the highest court of appeal, revision and reference in revenue matters in the state.

questions.q: The office of Divisional Commissioner in Rajasthan was abolished in the year
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Divisional Commissioner (Office Abolition) Act, 1962 abolished the post during the chief ministership of Mohan Lal Sukhadia. It was restored only in 1987.

questions.q: The office of Divisional Commissioner was restored in Rajasthan on 26 January 1987 during the chief ministership of
questions.exp: The Haridev Joshi government restored the divisional set-up on 26 January 1987 and simultaneously created Ajmer as the sixth division.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the most recently created division of Rajasthan that survives today?
questions.exp: Bharatpur was made a division in 2005 and is the seventh and newest surviving division. The divisions created in 2023 (Banswara, Pali, Sikar) were abolished in December 2024.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Division)   List-II (Year of creation)
A. Bikaner   1. 1949
B. Ajmer     2. 1987
C. Bharatpur 3. 2005
D. Banswara  4. 2023
questions.exp: Bikaner is one of the five original 1949 divisions, Ajmer was added in 1987, Bharatpur in 2005 and Banswara in 2023 (abolished December 2024).

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of division and year of creation is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Kota was one of the five divisions constituted in 1949, not in 1987. Ajmer is the division that dates from 1987.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the recent reorganisation of Rajasthan's administrative units:
I. Nineteen new districts and three new divisions were notified in 2023.
II. In December 2024 the state cabinet abolished nine of the newly created districts and all three new divisions.
III. Rajasthan consequently has 41 districts and 7 divisions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct as of January 2025. Nineteen new districts and three new divisions were notified in 2023, taking the state to 50 districts; the December 2024 cabinet decision scrapped nine of them - Dudu, Kekri, Shahpura, Neem Ka Thana, Gangapur City, Jaipur Rural, Jodhpur Rural, Anupgarh and Sanchore - leaving 41 districts and 7 divisions.

questions.q: Which one of the following districts created in 2023 was abolished by the Rajasthan cabinet decision of December 2024?
questions.exp: Sanchore was among the nine districts scrapped. Balotra, Beawar and Phalodi were retained along with Deeg, Didwana-Kuchaman, Kotputli-Behror, Khairthal-Tijara and Salumbar.

questions.q: Which one of the following districts created in the 2023 reorganisation continues to exist after the December 2024 review?
questions.exp: Deeg was one of the eight new districts retained. Dudu, Kekri and Anupgarh were among the nine abolished.

questions.q: The Board of Revenue for Rajasthan was established in the year
questions.exp: The Board of Revenue was created by Ordinance No. 22 of 1949 (7 April 1949) and came into force on 1 November 1949, with its seat at Ajmer.

questions.q: Under the Rajasthan Land Revenue Act, 1956, the Board of Revenue consists of a Chairman and not more than how many members?
questions.exp: The Act provides for a Chairman and a maximum of 20 members, appointed by the State Government. The Board normally functions through single-member and division benches.

questions.q: The highest court of appeal in revenue matters in Rajasthan is the
questions.exp: The Board of Revenue at Ajmer is the apex revenue court of the state, hearing appeals, revisions and references from subordinate revenue courts.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Land Revenue Act was enacted in the year
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Land Revenue Act, 1956 consolidated the land revenue laws of the merged princely states. Tenancy matters are governed by the separate Rajasthan Tenancy Act, 1955.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Tenancy Act came into force in the year
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Tenancy Act, 1955 came into force on 15 October 1955 and governs the rights of khatedar and other tenants.

questions.q:
Arrange the following revenue functionaries of Rajasthan in descending order of hierarchy:
I. Tehsildar
II. Patwari
III. Sub-Divisional Officer
IV. Girdawar
questions.exp: The descending order is Sub-Divisional Officer → Tehsildar → Girdawar (Kanungo) → Patwari. The Patwari is the lowest revenue functionary.

questions.q: The smallest unit of revenue administration in Rajasthan, placed in the charge of a Patwari, is called the
questions.exp: A patwar circle, comprising a group of villages, is the smallest revenue unit. The Patwari maintains the khasra and carries out girdawari there.

questions.q: In the revenue administration of Rajasthan, the officer who directly supervises the work of Patwaris is the
questions.exp: The Girdawar, also called Kanungo, supervises a group of patwar circles and checks the girdawari and land records prepared by Patwaris.

questions.q: A sub-tehsil in Rajasthan is headed by the
questions.exp: The Naib Tehsildar heads a sub-tehsil and assists the Tehsildar in revenue collection and record maintenance.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Tehsildar in Rajasthan:
I. He is the head of revenue administration at the tehsil level.
II. He exercises the powers of an Assistant Collector.
III. He is the ex-officio chairperson of the District Planning Committee.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. The District Planning Committee in Rajasthan is chaired by the Zila Pramukh, not by the Tehsildar.

questions.q: The officer who constitutes the link between the district and the tehsil in Rajasthan is the
questions.exp: The Sub-Divisional Officer (SDO/SDM) heads a sub-division and forms the administrative link between the Collector and the tehsils under him.

questions.q: In his capacity as District Magistrate, the Collector is primarily responsible for
opts: preparation of the district development plan
questions.exp: Revenue collection is the Collector's function; law and order, including prohibitory orders and licensing of arms, is exercised in the capacity of District Magistrate.

questions.q: In a district of Rajasthan, the District Election Officer for the conduct of elections is normally the
questions.exp: The District Collector doubles as District Election Officer and, for parliamentary and assembly constituencies, as Returning Officer or supervisor of Returning Officers.

questions.q: Under the Disaster Management Act, 2005, the District Disaster Management Authority is chaired by the
questions.exp: The District Collector (District Magistrate) is the ex-officio chairperson of the District Disaster Management Authority; at the state level the Chief Minister chairs the SDMA.

questions.q: Who is the chairperson of the District Planning Committee in Rajasthan?
opts: Minister in charge of the district
questions.exp: In Rajasthan the Zila Pramukh, the elected head of the Zila Parishad, chairs the District Planning Committee constituted under Section 121 of the Rajasthan Panchayati Raj Act, 1994.

questions.q: District Planning Committees are provided for under which Article of the Constitution of India?
questions.exp: Article 243ZD, inserted by the 74th Amendment, provides for a District Planning Committee in every state to consolidate the plans of panchayats and municipalities. Article 243ZE deals with the Metropolitan Planning Committee.

questions.q: Under Article 243ZD, what proportion of the members of a District Planning Committee must be elected from among the elected members of the panchayats and municipalities of the district?
questions.exp: Not less than four-fifths of the members of a District Planning Committee must be so elected, in proportion to the ratio of the rural and urban population of the district.

questions.q: The executive head and ex-officio secretary of a Zila Parishad in Rajasthan is the
questions.exp: The Chief Executive Officer, an IAS or senior RAS officer, is the executive head of the Zila Parishad, while the Zila Pramukh is its elected political head.

questions.q: Outside the commissionerate areas, the head of the district police in Rajasthan is the
questions.exp: The Superintendent of Police, an IPS officer, heads the district police and works under the general direction and control of the District Magistrate.

questions.q: The police commissionerate system in Rajasthan operates in which of the following pairs of cities?
questions.exp: Police commissionerates were introduced in Jaipur and Jodhpur, where a Police Commissioner exercises the magisterial powers otherwise held by the District Magistrate.

questions.q: Which of the following is an appellate authority interposed in the revenue court hierarchy between the Collector and the Board of Revenue?
questions.exp: The Revenue Appellate Authority hears appeals from orders of Sub-Divisional Officers and Collectors, from which a further appeal or revision lies to the Board of Revenue.

questions.q: The record of rights maintained for a village in Rajasthan revenue administration is known as
questions.exp: The jamabandi is the record of rights showing owners, tenants and their holdings. The khasra is the field-wise register and girdawari is periodic crop inspection.

questions.q: The periodic crop inspection carried out by the Patwari in Rajasthan is called
questions.exp: Girdawari is the season-wise inspection and recording of standing crops; bandobast refers to settlement operations for fixing land revenue.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a function performed by the District Collector in Rajasthan?
opts: Chairing the District Disaster Management Authority
Presiding over the Zila Parishad as its elected head
Licensing of arms in the district
questions.exp: The Zila Parishad is presided over by the elected Zila Pramukh. The Collector performs the other three functions in his revenue, magisterial and election capacities.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Functionary)   List-II (Territorial jurisdiction)
A. Divisional Commissioner   1. Patwar circle
B. Sub-Divisional Officer    2. Division
C. Naib Tehsildar            3. Sub-division
D. Patwari                   4. Sub-tehsil
questions.exp: Divisional Commissioner heads a division, the SDO a sub-division, the Naib Tehsildar a sub-tehsil and the Patwari a patwar circle.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Board of Revenue for Rajasthan:
I. Its seat is at Ajmer.
II. It was constituted in 1949.
III. It is the highest court of appeal in revenue matters in the state.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. The Board was created by Ordinance No. 22 of 1949 and enforced on 1 November 1949 with its seat at Ajmer.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Divisional Commissioner in Rajasthan:
I. The post was abolished in 1962 and revived in 1987.
II. He is an appellate authority in revenue matters above the Collector.
III. He is elected by the Zila Parishads of the division.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. The Divisional Commissioner is a senior IAS officer appointed by the State Government, never elected.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Tax Board, which hears appeals in commercial tax matters, is located at
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Tax Board sits at Ajmer, the same town as the Board of Revenue. The Rajasthan Civil Services Appellate Tribunal, by contrast, sits at Jaipur.

questions.q:
Arrange the following divisions of Rajasthan in the chronological order of their creation, beginning with the earliest:
I. Ajmer
II. Bharatpur
III. Udaipur
IV. Banswara
questions.exp: Udaipur (1949) → Ajmer (1987) → Bharatpur (2005) → Banswara (2023, abolished December 2024).

questions.q: Which one of the following officers does NOT form part of the land revenue hierarchy of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The Vikas Adhikari (Block Development Officer) belongs to the panchayati raj development set-up at the panchayat samiti level, not to the revenue hierarchy.

questions.q: The agency created in each district for the implementation of centrally sponsored rural development programmes is the
questions.exp: The District Rural Development Agency (DRDA) is the district-level body for planning and implementation of rural development schemes.

questions.q: The District Collector in Rajasthan is appointed by the
opts: Governor on the advice of the Board of Revenue
State Government from the Indian Administrative Service
