questions.exp: The Collector is an IAS officer posted by the State Government. The Divisional Commissioner supervises but does not appoint him.

questions.q: As of January 2025, the number of districts in Rajasthan is
questions.exp: Rajasthan has 41 districts as of January 2025 — the pre-2023 total of 33 plus the eight new districts retained after the December 2024 review.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (District)   List-II (Division)
A. Jaisalmer    1. Kota
B. Jhalawar     2. Udaipur
C. Banswara     3. Bikaner
D. Hanumangarh  4. Jodhpur
questions.exp: Jaisalmer falls in Jodhpur division, Jhalawar in Kota division, Banswara in Udaipur division and Hanumangarh in Bikaner division.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the District Collector in Rajasthan:
I. He is the custodian of government land in the district.
II. He is the District Registrar of births and deaths.
III. He is the appointing authority of the Superintendent of Police.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. The Superintendent of Police is an IPS officer appointed by the State Government; the Collector only exercises general direction over him in law-and-order matters.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the District Planning Committee is NOT correct?
opts: It is provided for by Article 243ZD of the Constitution.
In Rajasthan it is chaired by the Zila Pramukh.
It consolidates the plans of panchayats and municipalities of the district.
All of its members are nominated by the State Government.
questions.exp: Not less than four-fifths of its members must be elected from among the elected members of the panchayats and municipalities of the district; only a minority may be nominated.

questions.q: Settlement operations for the assessment of land revenue in Rajasthan are technically known as
questions.exp: Bandobast refers to settlement operations under which land is surveyed, classified and land revenue assessed; the Settlement Department works under the Board of Revenue.

questions.q: The District Planning Committee in Rajasthan is constituted under which provision of the Rajasthan Panchayati Raj Act, 1994?
questions.exp: Section 121 of the Rajasthan Panchayati Raj Act, 1994, read with Rules 350-352 of the Rajasthan Panchayati Raj Rules, 1996, governs the District Planning Committee.

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT among the five original divisions of Rajasthan constituted in 1949?
questions.exp: The five original divisions of 1949 were Jaipur, Jodhpur, Udaipur, Bikaner and Kota. Ajmer became a division only in 1987.

questions.q: The prohibitory-order power exercised by the District Magistrate in Rajasthan to prevent apprehended danger is now contained in which provision?
questions.exp: Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 replaces the former Section 144 of the CrPC as the District Magistrate's prohibitory-order power.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the divisions of Rajasthan:
I. Every division of Rajasthan is named after its headquarters town.
II. Bharatpur division was created in 2005.
III. Pali and Sikar divisions were abolished in December 2024.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. Pali, Sikar and Banswara divisions, created in 2023, were scrapped by the cabinet decision of 28 December 2024.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Patta — periodic settlement of land revenue
questions.exp: A patta is a title or lease document conferring rights on a holding; the periodic settlement of land revenue is called bandobast.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Board of Revenue for Rajasthan:
I. Its members are appointed by the State Government.
II. It exercises superintendence over all subordinate revenue courts in the state.
III. Appeals from its orders lie to the Rajasthan Tax Board.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. The Rajasthan Tax Board is a separate appellate body for commercial tax matters and is in no way superior to the Board of Revenue.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The District Collector in Rajasthan performs both revenue and magisterial functions.
Reason (R): The offices of Collector and District Magistrate are held by the same officer in the district.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: In Rajasthan the same IAS officer is Collector for revenue purposes and District Magistrate for law and order, which is precisely why both sets of functions vest in him.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sub-Divisional Officer in Rajasthan:
I. He exercises the powers of an Assistant Collector.
II. He is also a Sub-Divisional Magistrate.
III. He is elected by the panchayat samitis of his sub-division.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. The SDO is a member of the IAS or RAS posted by the State Government and is never elected.

chapters.title: State Commissions and Statutory Bodies of Rajasthan
factsheet: RPSC — constituted 22 December 1949 (Ordinance No. 28 of 1949); first sat at Jaipur, shifted to AJMER on 21 August 1958; first Chairman Sir S.K. Ghosh; constitutional basis Articles 315-323 (Part XIV).
RPSC chairman and members are appointed by the GOVERNOR; they hold office for 6 years or until the age of 62 years, whichever is earlier; resignation is addressed to the Governor.
An RPSC member can be REMOVED only by the PRESIDENT on the ground of misbehaviour, and only after the Supreme Court holds an inquiry under Article 317 — the Governor cannot remove him.
Article 316 requires that at least one-half of the members of a Public Service Commission be persons who have held office under the Government of India or a State for at least ten years.
The RPSC submits its ANNUAL REPORT to the Governor, who causes it to be laid before the State Legislature together with a memorandum explaining any non-acceptance of its advice (Article 323).
Rajasthan State Election Commission — constituted 1 July 1994 under Article 243K read with Section 120 of the Rajasthan Panchayati Raj Act, 1994; it is a CONSTITUTIONAL, single-member body.

First State Election Commissioner of Rajasthan: Amar Singh Rathore (1994); appointed by the Governor, removable only in the same manner as a High Court judge; the Commission conducts panchayati raj (Art. 243K) and urban local body (Art. 243ZA) elections and prepares their rolls, but NOT Lok Sabha or Vidhan Sabha elections.

Rajasthan State Information Commission — constituted 13 April 2006 under the Right to Information Act, 2005; became functional 18 April 2006; seat at Jaipur; first State Chief Information Commissioner M.D. Kaurani.

SIC composition: one State Chief Information Commissioner plus not more than TEN State Information Commissioners, appointed by the Governor on the recommendation of a committee of the CHIEF MINISTER (chairperson), the Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly and one Cabinet Minister nominated by the Chief Minister.
After the RTI (Amendment) Act, 2019 the term of the State Chief Information Commissioner and State Information Commissioners is 3 years (earlier 5 years) or 65 years of age, whichever is earlier.
Rajasthan State Human Rights Commission — constituted 18 January 1999 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993; began functioning in March 2000; headquarters Jaipur.
RSHRC composition after the Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019: a Chairperson and TWO members.
RSHRC Chairperson must be a retired Chief Justice OR a retired Judge of a High Court (widened by the 2019 amendment, which earlier required a former Chief Justice of a High Court).

RSHRC members: one who is or has been a Judge of a High Court or a District Judge with at least seven years' experience as District Judge, and one person having knowledge of or practical experience in human rights.

RSHRC selection committee: Chief Minister (chairperson), Speaker of the Legislative Assembly, Minister in charge of the Home Department, and the Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly; the Governor makes the appointment.
A member of a State Human Rights Commission can be removed only by the PRESIDENT of India, on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity after a Supreme Court inquiry.
RSHRC tenure after the 2019 amendment: 3 years or 70 years of age, whichever is earlier (earlier 5 years); reappointment is permitted.
RSHRC powers and limits: it has the powers of a CIVIL COURT under the CPC, 1908; it cannot inquire into a matter more than ONE YEAR old; its recommendations are advisory, not binding.

RSHRC chairpersons: Justice Kanta Kumari Bhatnagar (first, from 23 March 2000), Justice S. Saghir Ahmad, Justice N.K. Jain (16 July 2005 - 15 July 2010, a full five-year term), Justice Prakash Chandra Tatia, Justice Gangaram Moolchandani.
Rajasthan Lokayukta and Up-Lokayuktas Act, 1973 (Act No. 9 of 1973) — assented 26 March 1973 and deemed in force from 3 February 1973; seat at Jaipur.

First Lokayukta of Rajasthan: Justice I.N. Modi. The Lokayukta is appointed by the GOVERNOR after consultation with the Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court and the Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly; Up-Lokayuktas are appointed in consultation with the Lokayukta.

Matters NOT subject to investigation by the Lokayukta include: any action for which a formal public inquiry is directed under the Public Servants (Inquiries) Act, 1850; any matter referred for inquiry under the Commissions of Inquiry Act, 1952; and any complaint made more than FIVE YEARS after the action complained of.

The Lokayukta may be removed by the Governor for misbehaviour or incapacity only after an inquiry by a Supreme Court judge or a High Court Chief Justice and an address by the Assembly supported by a majority of its total membership and two-thirds of the members present and voting; the annual report goes to the Governor.

Rajasthan State Commission for Women — Act of 1999 (notified 15 May 1999); first chairperson Kanta Khaturia; a chairperson, three members and a member secretary; term 3 years; civil court powers. Rajasthan State Commission for Protection of Child Rights — 23 February 2010, under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005; both sit at Jaipur.

Rajasthan State Disaster Management Authority — under the Disaster Management Act, 2005, chaired by the CHIEF MINISTER; the State Executive Committee is chaired by the Chief Secretary; the District Disaster Management Authority is chaired by the Collector.

Rajasthan State Legal Services Authority — under the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987; the Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court is Patron-in-Chief and a sitting High Court judge nominated by him is the Executive Chairman; District Legal Services Authorities are chaired by the District Judge.

Rajasthan Guaranteed Delivery of Public Services Act, 2011 (enacted 14 November 2011) — Madhya Pradesh was the first state (2010) to enact such a law, but Rajasthan was the first to prescribe a penalty for delay (Rs 250 per day, minimum Rs 500, maximum Rs 5,000); the citizen applies to a Designated Officer, first appeal within 30 days and second appeal within 60 days, with no fee.

Rajasthan Right to Hearing Act, 2012 (Sunwai ka Adhikar Adhiniyam) — Rajasthan was the first state in India to legislate a right to be heard; the Rajasthan Transparency in Public Procurement Act, 2012 governs state procurement.

Rajasthan Civil Services Appellate Tribunal (Jaipur) hears service appeals of state employees; the Rajasthan Tax Board sits at Ajmer; the Rajasthan Subordinate and Ministerial Services Selection Board (Jaipur) is now the Rajasthan Staff Selection Board (RSSB).

RIICO (Jaipur) is the state industrial development corporation, renamed in 1980 from the Rajasthan Industrial and Mineral Development Corporation of 1969; RSMML (Udaipur) is the state PSU for rock phosphate, lignite and limestone.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Public Service Commission has its headquarters at
questions.exp: The RPSC first sat at Jaipur and was shifted to Ajmer on 21 August 1958; it has functioned from the Ghooghra Ghati building since 21 October 2000.

questions.q: The Chairman and members of the Rajasthan Public Service Commission are appointed by the
opts: Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court
questions.exp: Under Article 316, members of a State Public Service Commission are appointed by the Governor of the state. Their removal, however, lies only with the President.

questions.q: A member of the Rajasthan Public Service Commission can be removed from office by the
opts: Governor, on the recommendation of the Chief Minister
President, after an inquiry by the Supreme Court
Governor, after an inquiry by the Rajasthan High Court
State Legislature, by a two-thirds majority
questions.exp: Under Article 317, a member of a State Public Service Commission can be removed only by the President on the ground of misbehaviour, and only after the Supreme Court has inquired into the matter and recommended removal.

questions.q: A member of the Rajasthan Public Service Commission holds office for a term of six years or until he attains the age of
questions.exp: For a State Public Service Commission the limit is 62 years; for the Union Public Service Commission it is 65 years.

questions.q: The annual report of the Rajasthan Public Service Commission on its work is submitted to the
questions.exp: Under Article 323 the report is presented to the Governor, who causes it to be laid before the State Legislature along with a memorandum explaining any case where the Commission's advice was not accepted.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Office)   List-II (Manner of appointment)
A. State Chief Information Commissioner, Rajasthan   1. Appointed by the Governor on the recommendation of a committee of the Chief Minister, the Speaker, the Home Minister and the Leader of the Opposition
B. Chairperson, Rajasthan State Human Rights Commission   2. Appointed by the Governor after consultation with the Chief Justice of the High Court and the Leader of the Opposition
C. Lokayukta of Rajasthan   3. Appointed by the Governor on the recommendation of a committee of the Chief Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and a Cabinet Minister
D. Chairman, Rajasthan Public Service Commission   4. Appointed by the Governor
questions.exp: The Information Commission's committee is the CM, the Leader of the Opposition and a Cabinet Minister; the Human Rights Commission's committee adds the Speaker and the Home Minister; the Lokayukta is appointed after consulting the Chief Justice and the Leader of the Opposition.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajasthan Public Service Commission:
I. Its chairman is appointed by the Governor.
II. Its chairman can be removed by the Governor on the ground of misbehaviour.
III. It submits its annual report to the Governor.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and III are correct. Removal of a chairman or member is exclusively the President's power under Article 317, exercised after a Supreme Court inquiry.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Rajasthan Public Service Commission is NOT correct?
opts: It is a constitutional body under Part XIV of the Constitution.
Its members hold office for six years or until the age of 62 years.
It conducts recruitment to all subordinate and ministerial posts of the state.
Its chairman submits his resignation to the Governor.
questions.exp: Recruitment to subordinate and ministerial posts is done by the Rajasthan Staff Selection Board (formerly RSMSSB), not by the RPSC.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Article)   List-II (Subject)
A. Article 315   1. Removal of a member of a Public Service Commission
B. Article 316   2. Constitution of Public Service Commissions
C. Article 317   3. Report of a Public Service Commission
D. Article 323   4. Appointment and term of office of members
questions.exp: Article 315 constitutes the Commissions, 316 governs appointment and term, 317 removal and suspension, and 323 the annual report.

questions.q: The State Election Commission of Rajasthan was constituted in the year
questions.exp: The Rajasthan State Election Commission was constituted on 1 July 1994 under Article 243K read with Section 120 of the Rajasthan Panchayati Raj Act, 1994.

questions.q: The State Election Commission of a state is provided for by which Article of the Constitution?
questions.exp: Article 243K, inserted by the 73rd Amendment, provides for a State Election Commission for panchayat elections; Article 243ZA extends the same body to municipal elections.

questions.q: The Rajasthan State Election Commission is
opts: a statutory body created by state legislation only
a constitutional body consisting of a single member
a constitutional body consisting of a chairman and two members
an executive body constituted by the Governor's order
questions.exp: It is a constitutional body under Article 243K and is a single-member commission headed by the State Election Commissioner.

questions.q: Which of the following elections is conducted by the State Election Commission of Rajasthan?
opts: Election to the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly
Election to the Lok Sabha from Rajasthan
Election to the municipal bodies of Rajasthan
questions.exp: The State Election Commission conducts panchayati raj and urban local body elections and prepares their electoral rolls. Assembly and Lok Sabha elections are conducted by the Election Commission of India.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the State Election Commission of Rajasthan:
I. It is a single-member commission.
II. It was constituted in 1994.
III. It conducts elections to the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Assembly elections are conducted by the Election Commission of India, not by the State Election Commission.

questions.q: The Rajasthan State Information Commission was constituted in the year
questions.exp: The Rajasthan State Information Commission was constituted on 13 April 2006 under the Right to Information Act, 2005 and became functional on 18 April 2006.

questions.q: Who was the first State Chief Information Commissioner of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: M.D. Kaurani took office as the first State Chief Information Commissioner of Rajasthan on 18 April 2006.

questions.q: The State Information Commission of Rajasthan consists of the State Chief Information Commissioner and not more than how many State Information Commissioners?
questions.exp: The Right to Information Act, 2005 allows a State Chief Information Commissioner and a maximum of ten State Information Commissioners.

questions.q: The committee that recommends the appointment of the State Chief Information Commissioner in Rajasthan is headed by the
opts: Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court
questions.exp: The committee consists of the Chief Minister as chairperson, the Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly, and a Cabinet Minister nominated by the Chief Minister; the Governor makes the appointment.

questions.q:
Consider the following as members of the committee that recommends appointments to the Rajasthan State Information Commission:
I. The Chief Minister
II. The Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly
III. A Cabinet Minister nominated by the Chief Minister
Which of the above are members of that committee?
questions.exp: All three are members. The Chief Minister chairs the committee and the Governor makes the formal appointment on its recommendation.

questions.q: The Rajasthan State Human Rights Commission was constituted on
questions.exp: The Commission was constituted on 18 January 1999 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993, and began functioning in March 2000 when its first chairperson took office.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Body)   List-II (Governing law or provision)
A. Rajasthan Public Service Commission        1. Right to Information Act, 2005
B. Rajasthan State Election Commission        2. Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993
C. Rajasthan State Information Commission     3. Article 243K of the Constitution
D. Rajasthan State Human Rights Commission    4. Articles 315-323 of the Constitution
questions.exp: The RPSC rests on Articles 315-323, the State Election Commission on Article 243K, the Information Commission on the RTI Act, 2005 and the Human Rights Commission on the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.

questions.q: After the Protection of Human Rights (Amendment) Act, 2019, the Rajasthan State Human Rights Commission consists of a chairperson and
questions.exp: A State Human Rights Commission now consists of a chairperson and two members: one who is or has been a High Court judge or a District Judge of at least seven years' standing, and one person with knowledge of human rights.

questions.q: After the 2019 amendment to the Protection of Human Rights Act, who is eligible to be appointed chairperson of a State Human Rights Commission?
opts: Only a retired Chief Justice of a High Court
A retired Chief Justice or a retired Judge of a High Court
Only a retired Judge of the Supreme Court
Any retired District Judge of seven years' standing
questions.exp: The 2019 amendment widened the eligibility from a former Chief Justice of a High Court to also include a former Judge of a High Court.

questions.q: The chairperson of the Rajasthan State Human Rights Commission is appointed by the Governor on the recommendation of a committee headed by the
opts: Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court
questions.exp: The selection committee comprises the Chief Minister as chairperson, the Speaker of the Legislative Assembly, the Minister in charge of the Home Department and the Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly.

questions.q:
Consider the following members of the selection committee for the Rajasthan State Human Rights Commission:
I. Chief Minister
II. Speaker of the Legislative Assembly
III. Minister in charge of the Home Department
IV. Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly
Which of the above are members of the committee?
questions.exp: All four are members of the selection committee. In states with a Legislative Council, its Chairman and its Leader of the Opposition are added.

questions.q: A member of a State Human Rights Commission can be removed from office by the
opts: Chief Justice of the High Court
questions.exp: Although appointed by the Governor, a chairperson or member of a State Human Rights Commission can be removed only by the President on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity after a Supreme Court inquiry.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the powers of the Rajasthan State Human Rights Commission is NOT correct?
opts: It has the powers of a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
It can inquire into a violation of human rights on its own motion.
Its recommendations to the state government are legally binding.
It cannot inquire into a matter after the expiry of one year from the date of the alleged violation.
questions.exp: The Commission's recommendations are advisory. The authority concerned must report the action taken, but it is not bound to accept the recommendation.

questions.q: The Rajasthan State Human Rights Commission cannot inquire into a complaint of human rights violation made after the expiry of
opts: six months from the date of the violation
one year from the date of the violation
two years from the date of the violation
three years from the date of the violation
questions.exp: Section 36(2) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 bars inquiry into any matter after one year from the date on which the act constituting the violation is alleged to have been committed.

questions.q: Justice N.K. Jain, who served as chairperson of the Rajasthan State Human Rights Commission from 2005 to 2010, is notable because he
opts: was the first chairperson of the Commission
completed a full five-year tenure as chairperson
was later appointed to the National Human Rights Commission as chairperson
was removed from office by the Governor
questions.exp: Justice Nagendra Kumar Jain held office from 16 July 2005 to 15 July 2010, completing the full five-year term then prescribed for the office.

questions.q: Who was the first chairperson of the Rajasthan State Human Rights Commission?
questions.exp: Justice Kanta Kumari Bhatnagar became the first chairperson of the Commission on 23 March 2000. Justice S. Saghir Ahmad, Justice N.K. Jain and Justice Prakash Chandra Tatia followed later.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajasthan State Human Rights Commission:
I. Its headquarters is at Jaipur.
II. Its chairperson is appointed by the Governor.
III. Justice Prakash Chandra Tatia has served as its chairperson.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. Justice Prakash Chandra Tatia, a former Chief Justice of the Jharkhand High Court, headed the Commission from 2015.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Lokayukta and Up-Lokayuktas Act was passed in the year
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Lokayukta and Up-Lokayuktas Act, 1973 (Act No. 9 of 1973) received assent on 26 March 1973 and is deemed to have come into force on 3 February 1973.

questions.q: Who was the first Lokayukta of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Justice I.N. Modi was appointed the first Lokayukta of Rajasthan under the Act of 1973. The Lokayukta's office is at Jaipur.

questions.q: Before appointing the Lokayukta of Rajasthan, the Governor is required to consult
opts: the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court and the Chief Minister
the Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court and the Leader of the Opposition
the Speaker and the Chief Secretary
the Chairman of the Rajasthan Public Service Commission
questions.exp: Section 3 of the Act requires consultation with the Chief Justice of the High Court and the Leader of the Opposition in the Legislative Assembly. Up-Lokayuktas are appointed in consultation with the Lokayukta.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT subject to investigation by the Lokayukta of Rajasthan?
opts: An allegation of corruption against a minister of the state
An action for which a formal public inquiry has been directed under the Public Servants (Inquiries) Act, 1850
A grievance against the Pradhan of a panchayat samiti
A complaint against an officer of a state government company
questions.exp: Actions for which a formal public inquiry has been ordered under the Public Servants (Inquiries) Act, 1850 are expressly excluded, as are matters referred under the Commissions of Inquiry Act, 1952.

questions.q: A complaint to the Lokayukta of Rajasthan is barred if it is made after the expiry of how many years from the date of the action complained against?
questions.exp: The Act bars investigation of any complaint made more than five years after the date on which the action complained against is alleged to have taken place.

questions.q:
Consider the following matters:
I. A matter referred for inquiry under the Commissions of Inquiry Act, 1952.
II. A complaint made six years after the action complained against.
III. An allegation of maladministration against a Municipal Mayor.
Which of the above are outside the jurisdiction of the Lokayukta of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Items I and II are expressly excluded by the Act. A Mayor is a public servant covered by the Act and complaints against him are maintainable.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Lokayukta of Rajasthan:
I. Up-Lokayuktas are appointed by the Governor in consultation with the Lokayukta.
II. The Chief Minister of the state is within the Lokayukta's jurisdiction.
III. The Lokayukta is a constitutional authority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. The Lokayukta is a statutory authority created by the Act of 1973, not a constitutional one.

questions.q: Who was the first chairperson of the Rajasthan State Commission for Women?
questions.exp: Smt. Kanta Khaturia was the first chairperson of the Rajasthan State Commission for Women.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Office)   List-II (Term of office)
A. Member, Rajasthan Public Service Commission            1. 3 years or 70 years of age
B. State Information Commissioner, Rajasthan              2. 6 years or 62 years of age
C. Chairperson, Rajasthan State Human Rights Commission   3. 5 years or 65 years of age
D. State Election Commissioner, Rajasthan                 4. 3 years or 65 years of age
questions.exp: RPSC member: 6 years or 62; State Information Commissioner: 3 years or 65 (after the 2019 amendment); RSHRC chairperson: 3 years or 70 (after the 2019 amendment); State Election Commissioner: 5 years or 65.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajasthan State Commission for Women:
I. It has the powers of a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
II. Its members are appointed by the State Government.
III. It is a constitutional body.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. The Commission is a statutory body created by the Rajasthan State Commission for Women Act, 1999.

questions.q: The Rajasthan State Commission for Protection of Child Rights was established under which Act?
opts: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
questions.exp: The Commission was established on 23 February 2010 under the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005, with its headquarters at Jaipur.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about disaster management institutions in Rajasthan:
I. The State Disaster Management Authority is chaired by the Chief Minister.
II. The District Disaster Management Authority is chaired by the District Collector.
III. Both are constituted under the Disaster Management Act, 2005.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. The Act of 2005 provides a three-tier structure at national, state and district levels.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Body)   List-II (Person who heads it)
A. Rajasthan State Disaster Management Authority                 1. District Judge
B. State Executive Committee under the Disaster Management Act   2. Chief Minister
C. District Legal Services Authority                             3. Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court, as Patron-in-Chief
D. Rajasthan State Legal Services Authority                      4. Chief Secretary
questions.exp: The Chief Minister chairs the SDMA, the Chief Secretary the State Executive Committee, the District Judge the District Legal Services Authority, and the Chief Justice is Patron-in-Chief of the State Legal Services Authority.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Guaranteed Delivery of Public Services Act was enacted in the year
questions.exp: The Act was enacted on 14 November 2011 to guarantee the delivery of notified public services within stipulated time limits.

questions.q: Which state was the first in India to enact a law guaranteeing the delivery of public services within a fixed time?
questions.exp: Madhya Pradesh enacted the first such law in 2010. Rajasthan followed in 2011 but was the first state to provide a penalty for failure or delay in delivering a notified service.

questions.q: Under the Rajasthan Guaranteed Delivery of Public Services Act, 2011, a first appeal against non-delivery of a notified service must be filed within
questions.exp: The first appeal lies within 30 days of the expiry of the stipulated time limit; a second appeal lies within 60 days of the first appellate authority's decision. No fee is charged.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajasthan Guaranteed Delivery of Public Services Act, 2011:
I. It provides for a penalty on a Designated Officer who fails to deliver a notified service in time.
II. Public holidays are excluded while computing the stipulated time limit.
III. A fee is payable for filing an appeal under the Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. No fee is charged for an appeal or revision under the Act; the penalty ranges from Rs 500 to Rs 5,000.

questions.q: Rajasthan was the first state in India to enact which of the following laws?
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Right to Hearing Act, 2012 (Sunwai ka Adhikar Adhiniyam) made Rajasthan the first state to give citizens a statutory right to be heard by public authorities.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Rajasthan legislation)   List-II (Year)
A. Rajasthan Lokayukta and Up-Lokayuktas Act          1. 1999
B. Rajasthan State Commission for Women Act           2. 1973
C. Rajasthan Guaranteed Delivery of Public Services Act  3. 2012
D. Rajasthan Right to Hearing Act                     4. 2011
questions.exp: Lokayukta Act 1973, State Commission for Women Act 1999, Guaranteed Delivery of Public Services Act 2011 and Right to Hearing Act 2012.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Rajasthan legislation)   List-II (Subject)
A. Rajasthan Guaranteed Delivery of Public Services Act, 2011   1. Right of a citizen to be heard by a public authority
B. Rajasthan Right to Hearing Act, 2012                         2. Government purchases and tendering
C. Rajasthan Transparency in Public Procurement Act, 2012       3. Complaints against ministers and public servants
D. Rajasthan Lokayukta and Up-Lokayuktas Act, 1973              4. Time-bound delivery of notified public services
questions.exp: The 2011 Act guarantees time-bound service delivery, the 2012 Right to Hearing Act a statutory hearing, the Procurement Act governs government purchases and the Lokayukta Act complaints against public servants.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Subordinate and Ministerial Services Selection Board has been renamed as the
questions.exp: The Jaipur-based RSMSSB now functions as the Rajasthan Staff Selection Board (RSSB), recruiting to subordinate and ministerial posts outside the RPSC's purview.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Body)   List-II (Year of constitution)
A. Rajasthan Public Service Commission   1. 1949
B. Rajasthan State Election Commission   2. 1994
C. Rajasthan State Human Rights Commission   3. 1999
D. Rajasthan State Information Commission   4. 2006
questions.exp: RPSC 1949, State Election Commission 1994, State Human Rights Commission 1999 and State Information Commission 2006.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Body)   List-II (Head/first holder)
A. Rajasthan Public Service Commission   1. Amar Singh Rathore
B. Rajasthan Lokayukta                   2. S.K. Ghosh
C. Rajasthan State Election Commission   3. Kanta Kumari Bhatnagar
D. Rajasthan State Human Rights Commission  4. I.N. Modi
questions.exp: S.K. Ghosh was the first RPSC chairman, I.N. Modi the first Lokayukta, Amar Singh Rathore the first State Election Commissioner and Kanta Kumari Bhatnagar the first RSHRC chairperson.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Office)   List-II (Manner of removal)
A. Member, Rajasthan Public Service Commission   1. By the President, after an inquiry by the Supreme Court
B. State Chief Information Commissioner, Rajasthan   2. By the Governor, after an inquiry by the Supreme Court
C. State Election Commissioner, Rajasthan   3. In the same manner as a Judge of a High Court
D. Lokayukta of Rajasthan   4. By the Governor, after an inquiry and an address by the Legislative Assembly
questions.exp: A PSC member is removed only by the President after a Supreme Court inquiry; the State Chief Information Commissioner by the Governor after a Supreme Court inquiry; the State Election Commissioner like a High Court judge; the Lokayukta by the Governor after an address by the Assembly.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of body and headquarters is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Rajasthan State Human Rights Commission — Jaipur
Rajasthan State Mines and Minerals Limited — Jaipur
questions.exp: RSMML is headquartered at Udaipur, not Jaipur. The other three pairs are correctly matched.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a CONSTITUTIONAL body in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The State Election Commission derives its existence from Article 243K of the Constitution. The other three are statutory bodies created by legislation.

questions.q:
Arrange the following bodies of Rajasthan in the chronological order of their establishment, beginning with the earliest:
I. Rajasthan State Human Rights Commission
II. Rajasthan Public Service Commission
III. Rajasthan State Information Commission
IV. Rajasthan Lokayukta
questions.exp: RPSC 1949 → Lokayukta 1973 → State Human Rights Commission 1999 → State Information Commission 2006.

questions.q:
Arrange the following Rajasthan legislations in the chronological order of their enactment, beginning with the earliest:
I. Rajasthan Guaranteed Delivery of Public Services Act
II. Rajasthan Lokayukta and Up-Lokayuktas Act
III. Rajasthan Right to Hearing Act
IV. Rajasthan State Commission for Women Act
questions.exp: Lokayukta Act 1973 → Women's Commission Act 1999 → Guaranteed Delivery of Public Services Act 2011 → Right to Hearing Act 2012.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Rajasthan Lokayukta was established before the Rajasthan State Human Rights Commission.
II. The Rajasthan State Information Commission was established after the Rajasthan State Election Commission.
III. The Rajasthan Public Service Commission is the oldest of these four bodies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct: RPSC 1949, Lokayukta 1973, State Election Commission 1994, State Human Rights Commission 1999 and State Information Commission 2006.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Rajasthan Lokayukta is NOT correct?
opts: He is appointed by the Governor.
He submits his annual report to the Governor.
He is empowered to punish a public servant found guilty of corruption.
He can investigate allegations against ministers of the state.
questions.exp: The Lokayukta only reports his findings to the competent authority, which must communicate the action taken within three months; he has no power to impose punishment himself.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Rajasthan State Election Commission is NOT correct?
opts: It prepares the electoral rolls for panchayat elections.
The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor.
Its conditions of service can be varied to the disadvantage of the State Election Commissioner after his appointment.
questions.exp: Article 243K expressly protects the State Election Commissioner: his conditions of service cannot be varied to his disadvantage after appointment.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajasthan State Human Rights Commission:
I. It can inquire into a complaint suo motu.
II. It has the power of a civil court to summon witnesses and require production of documents.
III. It can award compensation directly to a victim, and the award is binding on the state.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. The Commission may recommend payment of compensation, but its recommendations are not legally binding on the state government.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a ground on which the Lokayukta of Rajasthan declines to investigate a complaint?
opts: The complaint was made more than five years after the action complained against.
The matter has been referred for inquiry under the Commissions of Inquiry Act, 1952.
A formal public inquiry has been directed under the Public Servants (Inquiries) Act, 1850.
The complaint is against a minister of the state government.
questions.exp: Ministers are squarely within the Lokayukta's jurisdiction. The other three are express exclusions under the Act of 1973.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajasthan Public Service Commission:
I. Its headquarters was shifted from Jaipur to Ajmer in 1958.
II. Its first chairman was Sir S.K. Ghosh.
III. It was constituted in 1949.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. The Commission moved to Ajmer on 21 August 1958 and to its present Ghooghra Ghati building in October 2000.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about statutory bodies in Rajasthan:
I. The Rajasthan State Commission for Women was set up in 1999.
II. The Rajasthan State Commission for Protection of Child Rights was set up in 2010.
III. Both derive their existence from the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Both are statutory bodies — the former under a state Act of 1999 and the latter under the central Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Body)   List-II (Headquarters)
A. Rajasthan Public Service Commission   1. Udaipur
B. Rajasthan State Information Commission  2. Ajmer
C. Rajasthan State Mines and Minerals Ltd  3. Jaipur
D. Rajasthan High Court (principal seat)   4. Jodhpur
questions.exp: The RPSC and the Board of Revenue sit at Ajmer, the State Information Commission at Jaipur, RSMML at Udaipur and the principal seat of the Rajasthan High Court is at Jodhpur.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Authority)   List-II (Appointing/heading authority)
A. Chairman, Rajasthan Public Service Commission  1. Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court is Patron-in-Chief
B. Rajasthan State Legal Services Authority        2. Chaired by the Chief Minister
C. Rajasthan State Disaster Management Authority   3. Appointed by the Governor
D. District Disaster Management Authority          4. Chaired by the District Collector
questions.exp: The RPSC chairman is appointed by the Governor, the High Court Chief Justice is Patron-in-Chief of RSLSA, the CM chairs the SDMA and the Collector chairs the DDMA.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajasthan Lokayukta:
I. He is appointed under the Rajasthan Lokayukta and Up-Lokayuktas Act, 1973.
II. His office is located at Jaipur.
III. Employees of state government companies in which the state holds at least 51 per cent of the shares fall within his jurisdiction.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. The Act's definition of public servant covers employees of state corporations and government companies with at least 51 per cent state shareholding.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Rajasthan Guaranteed Delivery of Public Services Act, 2011 is NOT correct?
opts: It applies to notified services of scheduled departments.
It provides for first and second appeals.
It requires the applicant to be given a dated acknowledgement.
It creates a State Public Services Commission to hear appeals.
questions.exp: Appeals lie to departmental first and second appellate authorities; the Act creates no separate commission for the purpose.

chapters.title: Panchayati Raj in Rajasthan
factsheet: Panchayati Raj was inaugurated in India on 2 October 1959 at Bagdari village, Nagaur district, Rajasthan, by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru — the first in the country.
Andhra Pradesh was the second state, on 11 October 1959 (Shadnagar, then Mahbubnagar district).
Balwant Rai Mehta Committee (report 1957) recommended 'democratic decentralisation' and the three-tier structure; the National Development Council approved it in January 1958.
Bikaner princely state had a village panchayat Act as early as 1928 — the earliest in the Rajasthan region.
Pre-independence panchayat legislation also existed in Jodhpur, Jaipur, Udaipur, Sirohi, Bharatpur and Karauli states.
Rajasthan Panchayat Act, 1953 — provided uniform gram panchayats for the whole state.
Rajasthan Panchayat Samitis and Zila Parishads Act, 1959 — created the intermediate and district tiers.
73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 came into force on 24 April 1993; it added Part IX (Articles 243 to 243-O) and the Eleventh Schedule (29 subjects).
Rajasthan Panchayati Raj Act, 1994 (Act No. 13 of 1994) came into force on 23 April 1994; Rajasthan Panchayati Raj Rules were made in 1996.
Three tiers: Gram Panchayat (Sarpanch), Panchayat Samiti (Pradhan), Zila Parishad (Zila Pramukh).
Minimum strength: Gram Panchayat 9 wards; Panchayat Samiti 15 members; Zila Parishad 17 members.
Gram Sabha (Art. 243(b), 243A) = all persons registered in the electoral rolls of a village within a Gram Panchayat area; it is the only permanent body of the system.
Term of every panchayat = 5 years from the date of its first meeting; if dissolved earlier, fresh elections within 6 months (Art. 243E).
Minimum age to contest a panchayat election = 21 years (Art. 243F).
Reservation: SC/ST in proportion to population; not less than one-third of SC/ST seats for women of those categories; in Rajasthan 50 per cent of all seats are reserved for women.
Rajasthan State Election Commission (Art. 243K, constituted 1994) conducts all panchayat elections; the Commissioner can be removed only like a High Court judge.
The Village Level Worker / Gram Sevak was redesignated Gram Vikas Adhikari (Village Development Officer) — secretary of the Gram Panchayat. [asked in RAS Pre 2021 and 2023]
Vikas Adhikari (Block Development Officer) is the executive officer of the Panchayat Samiti; the Chief Executive Officer heads the Zila Parishad secretariat.

Article map: 243A Gram Sabha, 243B constitution, 243C composition, 243D reservation, 243E duration, 243F disqualifications, 243G powers, 243H taxes and funds, 243-I State Finance Commission, 243J audit, 243K elections, 243M non-application, 243N continuance of laws, 243-O bar to court interference.
State Finance Commission under Article 243-I, constituted every five years.
Rajasthan SFCs: 1st Krishna Kumar Goyal (1994), 2nd Hira Lal Devpura, 3rd Manik Chand Surana, 4th Dr. B.D. Kalla, 5th Dr. Jyoti Kiran, 6th Pradhyuman Singh (award period 2020-25).

Review committees: Sadiq Ali Committee (1964) and Girdharilal Vyas Committee (1973) in Rajasthan; nationally Ashok Mehta (1977, two-tier Mandal Panchayat + Zila Parishad), G.V.K. Rao (1985, district as pivot), L.M. Singhvi (1986, constitutional status).
PESA Act, 1996 extends Part IX to Scheduled Areas; Rajasthan notified its PESA Rules in 2011.
Fully Scheduled Areas districts in Rajasthan: Banswara, Dungarpur and Pratapgarh, with parts of Udaipur, Rajsamand, Chittorgarh, Sirohi and Pali.
Rajiv Gandhi Seva Kendras were built at gram panchayat and panchayat samiti level largely with MGNREGA funds.

MGNREGA, 2005 guaranteed 100 days of unskilled manual work per rural household per year and was implemented in Rajasthan through the panchayati raj institutions; it was repealed by the Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025 (assent 21 Dec 2025), which raises the guarantee to 125 days.
A minimum educational qualification for panchayat candidates was introduced by ordinance in December 2014 and removed by the Rajasthan Panchayati Raj (Amendment) Act, 2019.
eGramSwaraj is the Ministry of Panchayati Raj's unified planning, accounting and monitoring application; the Ministry also confers the national panchayat awards.

questions.q: Panchayati Raj in India was formally inaugurated on 2 October 1959 in which district of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru inaugurated the country's first Panchayati Raj system at Bagdari village in Nagaur district on 2 October 1959.

questions.q: Who inaugurated the Panchayati Raj system at Nagaur on 2 October 1959?
questions.exp: Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru performed the inauguration; Mohanlal Sukhadia was then the Chief Minister of Rajasthan.

questions.q: Which was the second State in India to introduce the Panchayati Raj system, on 11 October 1959?
questions.exp: Andhra Pradesh followed Rajasthan on 11 October 1959; Maharashtra adopted the system only in 1962.

questions.q: The recommendation for a three-tier Panchayati Raj structure based on 'democratic decentralisation' was made by the:
questions.exp: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee, appointed to study Community Development, recommended the three-tier structure of Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad.

questions.q: The Balwant Rai Mehta Committee submitted its report in the year:
questions.exp: The report was submitted in 1957 and approved by the National Development Council in January 1958, paving the way for the Nagaur launch in 1959.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Panchayat Samitis and Zila Parishads Act was enacted in the year:
questions.exp: This 1959 Act created the intermediate and district tiers and made the Nagaur inauguration possible; gram panchayats already existed under the 1953 Act.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Panchayat Act, which provided for uniform gram panchayats throughout the State, was passed in:
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Panchayat Act, 1953 unified the varied panchayat laws inherited from the princely states.

questions.q: Which princely state of the Rajasthan region had enacted a village panchayat Act as early as 1928?
questions.exp: Bikaner state's village panchayat legislation of 1928 is the earliest in the Rajasthan region; Jodhpur, Jaipur, Udaipur, Sirohi, Bharatpur and Karauli followed before independence.

questions.q: Under the Rajasthan Panchayati Raj Act, 1994, the elected head of a Zila Parishad is designated as:
questions.exp: The Zila Pramukh is the elected chairperson of the Zila Parishad; the Chief Executive Officer is the appointed administrative head.

questions.q: The elected head of a Panchayat Samiti in Rajasthan is called the:
questions.exp: The Pradhan heads the Panchayat Samiti; the Up-Pradhan is the deputy and the Vikas Adhikari is the executive officer.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Panchayati Raj Act, 1994 came into force on:
questions.exp: The Act (No. 13 of 1994) came into force on 23 April 1994, giving effect in Rajasthan to the 73rd Constitutional Amendment.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Panchayati Raj Rules were framed in the year:
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Panchayati Raj Rules, 1996 operationalise the 1994 Act, covering elections, meetings, committees and the conduct of business.

questions.q: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act came into force on:
questions.exp: The 73rd Amendment (panchayats) took effect on 24 April 1993, which is observed as National Panchayati Raj Day; the 74th Amendment for municipalities took effect on 1 June 1993.

questions.q: Provisions relating to Panchayats were inserted into the Constitution as:
questions.exp: Part IX (Articles 243 to 243-O) deals with Panchayats; Part IXA deals with Municipalities.

questions.q: The Eleventh Schedule of the Constitution lists how many subjects for devolution to panchayats?
questions.exp: The Eleventh Schedule contains 29 subjects; the Twelfth Schedule for municipalities contains 18.

questions.q: Under Article 243E, if a panchayat is dissolved before the expiry of its term, elections to constitute it must be completed within:
questions.exp: Article 243E requires that a dissolved panchayat be reconstituted within six months; the new body serves only the remainder of the original five-year term.

questions.q: The minimum age prescribed for contesting an election to a panchayat is:
questions.exp: Article 243F fixes 21 years as the minimum age for membership of a panchayat, although the voting age is 18.

questions.q: In Rajasthan, which officer functions as the secretary of a Gram Panchayat following the redesignation of the Village Level Worker?
questions.exp: The Village Level Worker (Gram Sevak) was redesignated Gram Vikas Adhikari (Village Development Officer) and serves as secretary of the Gram Panchayat.

questions.q: In Rajasthan, the Village Level Worker (Gram Sevak) has been redesignated as:
questions.exp: The post is now Gram Vikas Adhikari. Note that the Vikas Adhikari is a different, block-level officer (the BDO).

questions.q: The executive officer of a Panchayat Samiti in Rajasthan is the:
questions.exp: The Vikas Adhikari, equivalent to the Block Development Officer, is the executive officer and ex-officio secretary of the Panchayat Samiti.

questions.q: Who is the administrative head of the Zila Parishad establishment in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The Chief Executive Officer, usually an IAS or senior RAS officer, heads the Zila Parishad establishment; the Zila Pramukh is its elected political head.

questions.q: Elections to the panchayati raj institutions of Rajasthan are conducted by the:
questions.exp: Superintendence, direction and control of panchayat elections vests in the State Election Commission under Article 243K; Rajasthan's Commission was constituted in 1994.

questions.q: The State Election Commission derives its authority in respect of panchayat elections from:
questions.exp: Article 243K covers panchayat elections and Article 243ZA covers municipal elections; both are handled by the same State Election Commission in Rajasthan.

questions.q: The proportion of seats reserved for women in the panchayati raj institutions of Rajasthan is:
questions.exp: Rajasthan raised women's reservation in panchayats from the constitutional minimum of one-third to 50 per cent, and applies it to the offices of chairpersons as well.

questions.q: The State Finance Commission for panchayats is constituted under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.exp: Article 243-I requires the Governor to constitute a Finance Commission every five years to review the financial position of panchayats; Article 243Y extends its review to municipalities.

questions.q: Who was the chairman of the First State Finance Commission of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The First SFC of Rajasthan was constituted in 1994 under the chairmanship of Krishna Kumar Goyal, with an award period of 1995-2000.

questions.q: The Sixth State Finance Commission of Rajasthan covered which award period?
questions.exp: The Sixth SFC of Rajasthan, chaired by Pradhyuman Singh, made recommendations for the period 1 April 2020 to 31 March 2025.

questions.q: Which committee was appointed to review the working of Panchayati Raj in Rajasthan in 1964?
questions.exp: The Sadiq Ali Committee (1964) examined the functioning of panchayati raj in Rajasthan; the Girdharilal Vyas Committee followed in 1973.

questions.q: The Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) recommended which structure for panchayati raj?
opts: Two-tier — Mandal Panchayat and Zila Parishad
Three-tier as recommended by Balwant Rai Mehta
questions.exp: The Ashok Mehta Committee proposed a two-tier system with the Mandal Panchayat covering a cluster of villages and the Zila Parishad as the executive body.

questions.q: Which committee recommended that panchayati raj institutions be given constitutional status?
questions.exp: The L.M. Singhvi Committee (1986) recommended constitutional recognition for panchayats and Nyaya Panchayats; this led eventually to the 73rd Amendment.

questions.q: The Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act, generally called PESA, was enacted in:
questions.exp: PESA, 1996 extends Part IX of the Constitution to the Fifth Schedule areas with modifications that give primacy to the Gram Sabha.

questions.q: Rajasthan notified its PESA Rules in which year?
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Panchayat Raj (Modification of Provisions in their Application to the Scheduled Areas) Rules were notified in 2011.

questions.q: MGNREGA, 2005 guaranteed how many days of unskilled manual work to a rural household in a financial year?
questions.exp: The statutory guarantee under MGNREGA was 100 days per household per financial year, delivered in Rajasthan through the panchayati raj institutions. MGNREGA was repealed by the VB-G RAM G Act, 2025, which raises the guarantee to 125 days.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding panchayat legislation in the princely states of the Rajasthan region:
I. Bikaner state had a village panchayat Act as early as 1928.
II. Jodhpur, Jaipur, Udaipur and Sirohi states had enacted panchayat legislation before independence.
III. No princely state of Rajputana had any panchayat legislation before 1947.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct; III contradicts them. Bharatpur and Karauli also had panchayat legislation before independence.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Gram Sabha:
I. It consists of persons registered in the electoral rolls of a village within the area of a Gram Panchayat.
II. It is recognised by the Constitution under Article 243A.
III. Its powers and functions are those which the State Legislature may by law provide.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Gram Sabha is the only permanent body in the panchayati raj system, since it is not elected for a fixed term.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about PESA in Rajasthan:
I. Banswara, Dungarpur and Pratapgarh are fully covered by the Scheduled Areas of the State.
II. PESA extends the provisions of Part IX of the Constitution to the Scheduled Areas with modifications.
III. Rajasthan framed its PESA Rules in 2011.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Parts of Udaipur, Rajsamand, Chittorgarh, Sirohi and Pali districts are also included in the Scheduled Areas.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the implementation of MGNREGA (2005-2025) through panchayati raj institutions in Rajasthan:
I. The Gram Sabha recommends the works to be taken up.
II. The Gram Panchayat is the principal authority for planning and implementation at the village level.
III. Not more than 25 per cent of the works by cost may be executed through Gram Panchayats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. At least 50 per cent of works by value are to be executed through Gram Panchayats, so III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the minimum educational qualification for panchayat candidates in Rajasthan:
I. It was introduced through an ordinance in December 2014.
II. The Supreme Court upheld a comparable Haryana law in Rajbala v. State of Haryana (2015).
III. Rajasthan removed the requirement by an amendment Act in 2019.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Rajasthan was the first state to impose such a qualification, and among the first to withdraw it.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about reservation in panchayats:
I. Seats are reserved for the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in proportion to their population in the panchayat area.
II. Not less than one-third of the seats reserved for the SCs and STs must be reserved for women of those categories.
III. The Constitution does not permit reservation of the offices of chairpersons of panchayats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. Article 243D expressly provides for reservation of the offices of chairpersons, so III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following as sources of income of a Gram Panchayat in Rajasthan:
I. Devolution recommended by the State Finance Commission
II. Grants recommended by the Central Finance Commission
III. Income from panchayat land, ponds and other property
Which of the above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are sources. Panchayats also levy taxes, duties and fees that the State Legislature authorises them to impose under Article 243H.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Zila Parishad in Rajasthan:
I. Its members are directly elected from Zila Parishad constituencies in the district.
II. Members of Parliament and members of the State Legislative Assembly representing the area are members of the Zila Parishad.
III. The District Collector is the ex-officio chairperson of the Zila Parishad.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. The elected chairperson is the Zila Pramukh; the Collector is not the chairperson.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about a Gram Panchayat in Rajasthan:
I. The Sarpanch is directly elected by the voters of the whole Gram Panchayat area.
II. The Up-Sarpanch is elected by the ward panchs from among themselves.
III. The normal term of the Gram Panchayat is five years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Ward panchs are elected from single-member wards, of which there must be at least nine in a Gram Panchayat.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act:
I. It inserted Part IX into the Constitution.
II. Panchayats at the intermediate level are compulsory only in states with a population above twenty lakh.
III. It added the Twelfth Schedule to the Constitution.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. The 73rd Amendment added the Eleventh Schedule; the Twelfth Schedule came with the 74th Amendment.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the State Election Commissioner of Rajasthan:
I. He is appointed by the Governor.
II. He can be removed only in the manner and on the grounds prescribed for the removal of a judge of a High Court.
III. The Rajasthan State Election Commission was constituted in 1994.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Article 243K also bars any reduction in the Commissioner's conditions of service after appointment.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Article)   List-II (Subject)
A. Article 243A   1. Elections to the Panchayats
B. Article 243D   2. Gram Sabha
C. Article 243-I   3. Reservation of seats
D. Article 243K   4. Constitution of the Finance Commission
questions.exp: 243A Gram Sabha, 243D reservation of seats, 243-I State Finance Commission, 243K elections to panchayats.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (State Finance Commission of Rajasthan)   List-II (Chairman)
A. Second   1. Manik Chand Surana
B. Third   2. Hira Lal Devpura
C. Fourth   3. Dr. Jyoti Kiran
D. Fifth   4. Dr. B.D. Kalla
questions.exp: Second SFC — Hira Lal Devpura; Third — Manik Chand Surana; Fourth — Dr. B.D. Kalla; Fifth — Dr. Jyoti Kiran, the first woman to chair a Rajasthan SFC.

Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

B. Article 243C   2. Constitution of Panchayats
C. Article 243E   3. Composition of Panchayats
D. Article 243-O   4. Bar to interference by courts in electoral matters
questions.exp: 243B constitution, 243C composition, 243E duration, 243-O bar to interference by courts in electoral matters.

Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

questions.exp: 243H taxes and funds, 243J audit, 243M non-application to certain areas including Nagaland, Meghalaya and Mizoram, 243N continuance of existing laws.

Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a tier of the panchayati raj system in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Rajasthan has a three-tier system of Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad. Ward committees belong to urban local bodies.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The Chief Executive Officer belongs to the Zila Parishad; the Panchayat Samiti's executive officer is the Vikas Adhikari.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Rajasthan Panchayati Raj Act, 1994 is NOT correct?
opts: It gave effect in Rajasthan to the 73rd Constitutional Amendment
It provides for a two-tier panchayati raj structure
It came into force on 23 April 1994
It replaced the earlier Acts of 1953 and 1959
questions.exp: The 1994 Act retains the three-tier structure of Gram Panchayat, Panchayat Samiti and Zila Parishad; the two-tier idea was the Ashok Mehta Committee's proposal.

questions.q: Which one of the following subjects is NOT included in the Eleventh Schedule of the Constitution?
opts: Minor irrigation, water management and watershed development
questions.exp: Fire services is a Twelfth Schedule (municipal) subject. The Eleventh Schedule lists 29 rural subjects.

questions.q: Which one of the following Articles does NOT relate to panchayats?
questions.exp: Article 243ZA falls in Part IXA and deals with elections to municipalities.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Gram Sabha in Rajasthan is NOT correct?
opts: Its members are elected for a term of five years
It is the only permanent body of the panchayati raj system
Its members are the registered voters of the Gram Panchayat area
Its meetings are ordinarily presided over by the Sarpanch
questions.exp: The Gram Sabha is not elected at all — every registered voter of the area is automatically a member, which is why it is a permanent body.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of committee and year is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The L.M. Singhvi Committee reported in 1986; 1992 is the year of the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act itself.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in correct chronological order:
I. Balwant Rai Mehta Committee report
II. Inauguration of Panchayati Raj at Nagaur
III. Rajasthan Panchayat Act
IV. Rajasthan Panchayati Raj Act
questions.exp: Rajasthan Panchayat Act 1953, Balwant Rai Mehta report 1957, Nagaur inauguration 2 October 1959, Rajasthan Panchayati Raj Act 1994.

questions.q:
Arrange the following chairpersons of the State Finance Commissions of Rajasthan in the order in which their Commissions were constituted, beginning with the earliest:
I. Dr. Jyoti Kiran
II. Hira Lal Devpura
III. Manik Chand Surana
IV. Krishna Kumar Goyal
questions.exp: First Krishna Kumar Goyal (1994), Second Hira Lal Devpura, Third Manik Chand Surana, then the Fourth under Dr. B.D. Kalla and the Fifth under Dr. Jyoti Kiran.

chapters.title: Municipal Administration in Rajasthan; Rajasthan Public Examination Act 2022
factsheet: Mount Abu, established in 1864, was the first municipality of the Rajasthan region.
74th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992 came into force on 1 June 1993; it added Part IXA (Articles 243P to 243ZG) and the Twelfth Schedule of 18 municipal subjects.
Article 243Q provides three kinds of urban bodies: Nagar Panchayat for a transitional area, Municipal Council for a smaller urban area and Municipal Corporation for a larger urban area.
Rajasthan Municipalities Act, 2009 (Act No. 18 of 2009, assent 11 September 2009) governs urban local bodies; it replaced the Rajasthan Municipalities Act, 1959.
Rajasthan's three categories are Municipal Board, Municipal Council and Municipal Corporation; a municipality must have at least 13 seats, all filled by direct election from wards.

Nominated members: 6 in a Municipal Corporation, 5 in a Municipal Council and 4 in a Municipal Board — persons with special knowledge or experience of municipal administration; they have NO right to vote.
The MLA representing the municipal area is a member and does have the right to vote.
Security deposit for a general-category candidate for the office of Mayor is Rs. 30,000. [asked in RAS Pre 2021 and 2024]
Minimum age for membership of a municipality is 21 years; the term of a municipality is 5 years from the date fixed for its first meeting.
Heads: Mayor and Deputy Mayor in a Municipal Corporation; Chairman and Vice-Chairman in a Municipal Council and Municipal Board.
Chief municipal officers: CEO-cum-Commissioner (Corporation), Commissioner (Council) and Executive Officer (Board).
Ward Committees are provided under section 54 and the Executive Committee under section 55 of the 2009 Act.
Municipal elections are conducted by the State Election Commission under Article 243ZA; municipal finances are reviewed by the State Finance Commission under Article 243Y.
District Planning Committee — Article 243ZD; Metropolitan Planning Committee — Article 243ZE, for metropolitan areas of ten lakh or more population.
Main own-source revenue of Rajasthan's urban bodies is the Urban Development (UD) tax, along with fees, user charges, rents, licence fees, State and Central Finance Commission grants.
Urban Improvement Trusts are constituted under the Rajasthan Urban Improvement Act, 1959; the Jaipur Development Authority was created by a separate Act of 1982.
RUIDP is the ADB-assisted Rajasthan Urban Infrastructure Development Project; RUDSICO is the state nodal agency for AMRUT, the Smart Cities Mission and PMAY (Urban).
Smart Cities Mission cities from Rajasthan: Jaipur, Udaipur, Kota and Ajmer. AMRUT was launched in 2015 and the Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban) on 2 October 2014.
The Rajasthan Guaranteed Delivery of Public Services Act, 2011 made Rajasthan an early mover in statutory time-bound service delivery; the Rajasthan Right to Hearing Act followed in 2012.

Rajasthan Public Examination (Measures for Prevention of Unfair Means in Recruitment) Act, 2022 — Act No. 6 of 2022; assent 5 April 2022; published 6 April 2022; extends to the whole of Rajasthan; 20 sections and 2 Schedules.

Schedule-I lists the examination authorities (RPSC, Rajasthan High Court, Rajasthan Staff Selection Board, Police Recruitment Board, state-funded universities, RBSE, state PSUs and local bodies); Schedule-II lists the public examinations covered — recruitment examinations.

Section 2 defines 'conduct of public examination' to cover preparation, printing, coding, storage, transport, distribution, collection, evaluation and declaration of results; 'examinee' includes an authorised scribe.

'Unfair means' has two limbs — section 2(f)(i) taking unauthorised help or using unauthorised electronic or mechanical gadgets, and section 2(f)(ii) impersonation, leaking or conspiring to leak, procuring, possessing or solving question papers.
Section 10(1): an examinee using unfair means — imprisonment up to 3 years and fine of not less than Rs. 1 lakh; default in payment attracts up to 9 months' further imprisonment.
Section 10(2) as originally enacted: 5 to 10 years' imprisonment with fine of Rs. 10 lakh to Rs. 10 crore; default in payment attracts 2 years' further imprisonment.

Rajasthan Public Examination (Amendment) Act, 2023 (Act No. 17 of 2023, assent 5 August 2023) raised the section 10(2) punishment to not less than 10 years extending to imprisonment for life; the fine range was left unchanged.
Section 11: a convicted examinee is debarred from any public examination for 2 years. Section 13: a convicted institution pays the entire cost of the examination and is banned forever.

Section 12: proceeds of the offence may be seized or attached with prior written approval of the State Government; the Designated Court must be informed within 48 hours; on conviction property is confiscated to the State Government free from all encumbrances.
Section 14: all offences are cognizable, non-bailable and non-compoundable. Section 15: investigation only by an officer not below the rank of Additional Superintendent of Police.

Sections 16-17: offences are tried exclusively by Designated Courts, which are Courts of Session designated by the State Government in consultation with the Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court. The central Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 covers only UPSC, SSC, Railway Recruitment Boards, IBPS and NTA examinations, not state recruitment.

questions.q: The first municipality established in the region of present-day Rajasthan was at:
questions.exp: Mount Abu got the region's first municipality in 1864, then the summer headquarters of the Rajputana Agency.

questions.q: The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act came into force on:
questions.exp: The 74th Amendment, dealing with municipalities, took effect on 1 June 1993; the 73rd Amendment on panchayats had taken effect on 24 April 1993.

questions.q: Provisions relating to Municipalities were inserted into the Constitution as:
questions.exp: Part IXA covers Articles 243P to 243ZG. Part IX deals with panchayats.

questions.q: The Twelfth Schedule of the Constitution lists how many subjects for municipalities?
questions.exp: The Twelfth Schedule has 18 municipal subjects, including urban planning, water supply, fire services, slum improvement and urban forestry.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Municipalities Act, 2009 is:
questions.exp: It is Act No. 18 of 2009 and received the Governor's assent on 11 September 2009.

questions.q: Urban local bodies in Rajasthan are at present governed by the:
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Municipalities Act, 2009 replaced the 1959 Act; the Rajasthan Urban Improvement Act, 1959 governs Urban Improvement Trusts, which are separate bodies.

questions.q: Under Article 243Q of the Constitution, a Municipal Council is constituted for a:
questions.exp: A Nagar Panchayat is for a transitional area, a Municipal Council for a smaller urban area and a Municipal Corporation for a larger urban area; in Rajasthan the transitional-area body is called a Municipal Board.

questions.q: Under the Rajasthan Municipalities Act, 2009, how many members may be nominated to a Municipal Corporation?
questions.exp: Six persons may be nominated to a Municipal Corporation, five to a Municipal Council and four to a Municipal Board, all being persons with special knowledge or experience of municipal administration.

questions.q: A nominated member of a municipality in Rajasthan:
opts: Has the right to vote in all meetings
May vote only in the election of the Mayor
May vote only on financial matters
Has no right to vote in the meetings of the municipality
questions.exp: Nominated members participate in deliberations but have no right to vote in the meetings of the municipality.

questions.q: What is the amount of security deposit for a general-category candidate contesting the election to the office of Mayor in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: A general-category mayoral candidate must deposit Rs. 30,000 as security; a lower deposit is prescribed for reserved-category and women candidates.

questions.q: The minimum age prescribed for membership of a municipality in Rajasthan is:
questions.exp: A candidate must have attained the age of 21 years, the same as for panchayat membership.

questions.q: The term of a municipality in Rajasthan is five years reckoned from:
opts: The date of notification of the election result
The date appointed for its first meeting
The first day of the financial year following the election
The date of oath of the Mayor or Chairman
questions.exp: Article 243U and the 2009 Act both count the five-year term from the date appointed for the municipality's first meeting.

questions.q: Under the Rajasthan Municipalities Act, 2009, the minimum number of seats in a municipality is:
questions.exp: A municipality must have at least 13 seats, all of which are filled by direct election from single-member wards.

questions.q: The chief municipal officer of a Municipal Board in Rajasthan is designated as the:
questions.exp: A Municipal Board has an Executive Officer, a Municipal Council a Commissioner and a Municipal Corporation a Chief Executive Officer-cum-Commissioner.

questions.q: Elections to municipalities are conducted under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.exp: Article 243ZA vests superintendence of municipal elections in the State Election Commission; the corresponding provision for panchayats is Article 243K.

questions.q: A Metropolitan Planning Committee is constituted under Article 243ZE for a metropolitan area having a population of:
questions.exp: A metropolitan area under Article 243P means an area with a population of ten lakh or more comprised in one or more districts and two or more municipalities or panchayats.

questions.q: The principal own-source tax revenue of urban local bodies in Rajasthan is the:
questions.exp: The Urban Development (UD) tax on urban property is the main own-source tax of Rajasthan's municipal bodies; octroi has been abolished.

questions.q: The Jaipur Development Authority was constituted under an Act of the year:
questions.exp: The Jaipur Development Authority Act, 1982 created the JDA for the planned development of the Jaipur region, replacing the earlier Urban Improvement Trust arrangement there.

questions.q: Which organisation is the State nodal agency in Rajasthan for AMRUT, the Smart Cities Mission and PMAY (Urban)?
questions.exp: RUDSICO — the Rajasthan Urban Drinking Water, Sewerage and Infrastructure Corporation — is the state nodal agency; RUIDP is the ADB-assisted urban infrastructure project.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about nominated members of municipalities in Rajasthan:
I. Six may be nominated to a Municipal Corporation, five to a Municipal Council and four to a Municipal Board.
II. They must be persons having special knowledge or experience of municipal administration.
III. They have the right to vote in the meetings of the municipality.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct; nominated members have no right to vote, so III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the head of a municipality in Rajasthan:
I. Every municipality has a Chairperson and a Vice-Chairperson.
II. In a Municipal Corporation they are designated Mayor and Deputy Mayor.
III. The Mayor is the chief executive officer of the Municipal Corporation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. The chief executive officer of a Municipal Corporation is the CEO-cum-Commissioner, not the Mayor, who is its elected political head.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 74th Constitutional Amendment Act:
I. It inserted Part IXA containing Articles 243P to 243ZG.
