II. It added the Twelfth Schedule containing eighteen subjects.
III. It provided for District Planning Committees and Metropolitan Planning Committees.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. District Planning Committees come under Article 243ZD and Metropolitan Planning Committees under Article 243ZE.

questions.q:
Consider the following as sources of revenue of a municipality in Rajasthan:
I. Urban Development tax
II. Devolution recommended by the State Finance Commission
III. Income tax collected from the residents of the municipal area
Which of the above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. Income tax is a Union levy and no share of it is collected by a municipality, so III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about urban missions in Rajasthan:
I. AMRUT was launched in 2015.
II. Jaipur, Udaipur, Kota and Ajmer were selected from Rajasthan under the Smart Cities Mission.
III. The Swachh Bharat Mission (Urban) was launched on 2 October 2014.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. AMRUT and the Smart Cities Mission were both launched in June 2015.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about urban development bodies in Rajasthan:
I. Urban Improvement Trusts are constituted under the Rajasthan Urban Improvement Act, 1959.
II. The Jaipur Development Authority was created by a separate Act of the State Legislature.
III. The Jaipur Development Authority is a wing of the Jaipur Municipal Corporation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. The JDA is an independent statutory development authority, not a wing of the municipal corporation.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Body)   List-II (Chief officer)
A. Municipal Corporation   1. Executive Officer
B. Municipal Council   2. Commissioner
C. Municipal Board   3. Chief Executive Officer-cum-Commissioner
D. Zila Parishad   4. Chief Executive Officer
questions.exp: Corporation — CEO-cum-Commissioner; Council — Commissioner; Board — Executive Officer; Zila Parishad — Chief Executive Officer.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Article)   List-II (Subject)
A. Article 243P   1. Definitions
B. Article 243Q   2. Constitution of Municipalities
C. Article 243ZA   3. Elections to the Municipalities
D. Article 243ZE   4. Metropolitan Planning Committee
questions.exp: 243P definitions, 243Q constitution of municipalities, 243ZA elections, 243ZE Metropolitan Planning Committee.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I   List-II (Number)
A. Nominated members in a Municipal Corporation   1. 4
B. Nominated members in a Municipal Council   2. 6
C. Nominated members in a Municipal Board   3. 5
D. Minimum seats in a municipality   4. 13
questions.exp: Corporation 6, Council 5, Board 4 nominated members; a municipality must have at least 13 seats.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Body / Project)   List-II (Description)
A. RUIDP   1. ADB-assisted urban infrastructure development project
B. RUDSICO   2. State nodal agency for AMRUT and the Smart Cities Mission
C. JDA   3. Development authority for the Jaipur region
D. UIT   4. Urban Improvement Trust under the 1959 Act
questions.exp: RUIDP is the ADB-assisted project, RUDSICO the nodal agency for central urban missions, JDA the Jaipur development authority, and UITs are trusts under the 1959 Act.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Article)   List-II (Subject)
A. Article 243-I   1. State Finance Commission for panchayats
B. Article 243Y   2. Finance Commission review of municipal finances
C. Article 243ZD   3. District Planning Committee
D. Article 243K   4. State Election Commission for panchayats
questions.exp: 243-I State Finance Commission, 243Y its review of municipal finances, 243ZD District Planning Committee, 243K State Election Commission for panchayats.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a subject listed in the Twelfth Schedule of the Constitution?
opts: Urban forestry and protection of the environment
questions.exp: Minor forest produce is an Eleventh Schedule (panchayat) subject. The Twelfth Schedule contains 18 municipal subjects.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of an urban local body and its officer is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: A Municipal Council's chief officer is the Commissioner; the Chief Executive Officer-cum-Commissioner belongs to a Municipal Corporation.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about nominated members of a municipality in Rajasthan is NOT correct?
opts: They are nominated by the State Government
They must have special knowledge or experience of municipal administration
They have the right to vote in the meetings of the municipality
Four such members may be nominated to a Municipal Board
questions.exp: Nominated members have no right to vote in municipal meetings, although they may take part in the proceedings.

questions.q: Which one of the following cities of Rajasthan was NOT selected under the Smart Cities Mission?
questions.exp: Rajasthan's four Smart Cities are Jaipur, Udaipur, Kota and Ajmer.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in correct chronological order:
I. Establishment of the first municipality of the Rajasthan region at Mount Abu
II. Rajasthan Municipalities Act, 1959
III. 74th Constitutional Amendment Act
IV. Rajasthan Municipalities Act, 2009
questions.exp: Mount Abu 1864, Rajasthan Municipalities Act 1959, 74th Amendment 1992 (in force 1993), Rajasthan Municipalities Act 2009.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Public Examination (Measures for Prevention of Unfair Means in Recruitment) Act, 2022 is:
questions.exp: It is Act No. 6 of 2022. Act No. 17 of 2023 is the amending Act that later enhanced the punishment under section 10(2). (Position as of September 2026.)

questions.q: The Rajasthan Public Examination (Measures for Prevention of Unfair Means in Recruitment) Act, 2022 received the Governor's assent on:
questions.exp: Assent was given on 5 April 2022 and the Act was published in the Rajasthan Gazette (Extraordinary) on 6 April 2022. It extends to the whole of the State of Rajasthan.

questions.q: Under section 10(1) of the Rajasthan Public Examination Act, 2022, an examinee who uses unfair means is punishable with imprisonment which may extend to:
questions.exp: Section 10(1) prescribes imprisonment up to three years with a fine of not less than one lakh rupees; default in payment of the fine attracts further imprisonment up to nine months. (Position as of September 2026.)

questions.q: The minimum fine imposable on an examinee convicted under section 10(1) of the Rajasthan Public Examination Act, 2022 is:
questions.exp: The fine shall not be less than one lakh rupees; failure to pay attracts a further term of imprisonment up to nine months.

questions.q: The maximum fine that may be imposed under section 10(2) of the Rajasthan Public Examination Act, 2022 is:
questions.exp: Section 10(2) prescribes a fine of not less than ten lakh rupees which may extend to ten crore rupees; the 2023 amendment did not alter the fine range. (Position as of September 2026.)

questions.q: After the amendment of 2023, the maximum punishment prescribed under section 10(2) of the Rajasthan Public Examination Act, 2022 is:
questions.exp: The Amendment Act of 2023 raised section 10(2) to imprisonment of not less than ten years, extending to imprisonment for life. (Position as of September 2026.)

questions.q: Under section 11 of the Rajasthan Public Examination Act, 2022, an examinee convicted under the Act is debarred from taking any public examination for a period of:
questions.exp: The debarment is for two years and follows conviction, not mere accusation. A convicted institution, by contrast, is banned forever under section 13.

questions.q: Under the Rajasthan Public Examination Act, 2022, an offence may be investigated only by a police officer not below the rank of:
questions.exp: Section 15 restricts investigation to officers of at least the rank of Additional Superintendent of Police. The central Act of 2024 sets this bar at Deputy Superintendent of Police.

questions.q: Offences under the Rajasthan Public Examination Act, 2022 are tried by:
opts: Any Judicial Magistrate of the first class
Designated Courts constituted from Courts of Session
A special tribunal set up by the RPSC
questions.exp: Sections 16 and 17 provide for trial exclusively by Designated Courts, which the State Government designates from among Courts of Session in consultation with the Chief Justice of the Rajasthan High Court.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Public Examination (Amendment) Act that enhanced the punishment under section 10(2) was passed in the year:
questions.exp: Act No. 17 of 2023 received assent on 5 August 2023 and came into force at once; it raised the minimum sentence from five to ten years and the maximum from ten years to imprisonment for life.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajasthan Public Examination (Measures for Prevention of Unfair Means in Recruitment) Act, 2022:
I. It extends to the whole of the State of Rajasthan.
II. Offences under the Act are cognizable, non-bailable and non-compoundable.
III. It applies to the Class X and Class XII board examinations of the Board of Secondary Education, Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. The 2022 Act deals with recruitment examinations; board and university examinations are covered by the Rajasthan Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 1992.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about section 10(2) of the Rajasthan Public Examination Act, 2022 as it stands after the 2023 amendment:
I. The minimum imprisonment is ten years.
II. The punishment may extend to imprisonment for life.
III. The fine ranges from ten lakh rupees to ten crore rupees.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct as of September 2026. The court may award less than the minimum only for adequate and special reasons recorded in the judgment.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the attachment and confiscation of property under the Rajasthan Public Examination Act, 2022:
I. Seizure or attachment requires the prior approval in writing of the State Government.
II. The Designated Court must be informed of the seizure or attachment within seven days.
III. On conviction, the Designated Court may declare the property confiscated to the State Government free from all encumbrances.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and III are correct. Section 12 requires that the Designated Court be informed within 48 hours, not seven days.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about penalties on institutions under the Rajasthan Public Examination Act, 2022:
I. A convicted management or institution must pay all costs and expenditure of the examination as determined by the Designated Court.
II. Such a management or institution is banned forever.
III. A convicted examinee is debarred from public examinations for five years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct under section 13. The debarment for a convicted examinee under section 11 is two years, not five.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajasthan Public Examination Act, 2022:
I. Where an offence is committed by a company or institution, every person in charge of its business at the time is deemed guilty.
II. Such a person escapes liability if he proves that the offence was committed without his knowledge or that he exercised all due diligence.
III. The provisions of the Act are in addition to, and not in derogation of, any other law in force.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Section 9 casts a reverse burden of proof on officers of the institution, and section 18 preserves the operation of other laws.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Section of the Rajasthan Public Examination Act, 2022)   List-II (Subject)
A. Section 10(1)   1. Debarment of a convicted examinee
B. Section 11   2. Punishment of an examinee using unfair means
C. Section 12   3. Offences to be cognizable and non-bailable
D. Section 14   4. Attachment and confiscation of property
questions.exp: Section 10(1) punishment of an examinee, section 11 debarment, section 12 attachment and confiscation, section 14 cognizable and non-bailable offences.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Provision of the Rajasthan Public Examination Act, 2022)   List-II (Quantum)
A. Minimum fine on an examinee under section 10(1)   1. Ten crore rupees
B. Minimum fine under section 10(2)   2. One lakh rupees
C. Maximum fine under section 10(2)   3. Two years
D. Default imprisonment for non-payment of fine under section 10(2)   4. Ten lakh rupees
questions.exp: Examinee's minimum fine one lakh rupees; section 10(2) fine ranges from ten lakh to ten crore rupees; default imprisonment there is up to two years.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Rajasthan Public Examination Act, 2022 is NOT correct?
opts: Offences under the Act are bailable and compoundable
The Act extends to the whole of the State of Rajasthan
A convicted examinee is debarred from public examinations for two years
Investigation is restricted to officers of and above the rank of Additional Superintendent of Police
questions.exp: Section 14 makes every offence under the Act cognizable, non-bailable and non-compoundable.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT among the examination authorities specified in Schedule-I of the Rajasthan Public Examination Act, 2022?
questions.exp: The UPSC is covered by the central Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, which applies to UPSC, SSC, Railway Recruitment Boards, IBPS and NTA examinations, not by the Rajasthan Act.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Rajasthan Public Examination (Measures for Prevention of Unfair Means in Recruitment) Act, 2022 was amended in 2023 to provide for imprisonment for life.
Reason (R): As originally enacted, section 10(2) of the Act prescribed a maximum punishment of only ten years' imprisonment.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: Repeated paper leaks led the State to conclude that the original maximum of ten years was inadequate; the 2023 amendment therefore raised the sentence to a minimum of ten years extending to life. (Position as of September 2026.)

chapters.title: Basic Concepts: Growth, Development, Sustainability, National Income
factsheet: Economic growth = quantitative rise in real national output/income; economic development = growth PLUS structural, qualitative and distributional improvement in welfare.
Amartya Sen — capability approach, 'Development as Freedom' (1999); Mahbub ul Haq — architect of the Human Development Index, first Human Development Report 1990.
Sustainable development defined by the Brundtland Commission (World Commission on Environment and Development) in 'Our Common Future', 1987.
SDGs: 17 goals, 169 targets, 'Transforming our World: the 2030 Agenda', adopted September 2015, in force 1 January 2016; replaced the 8 Millennium Development Goals (2000-2015).
NITI Aayog publishes the SDG India Index (first edition December 2018) with MoSPI and UN India.
Green GDP = GDP adjusted for depletion of natural resources and cost of environmental degradation. Circular economy = reduce-reuse-recycle, opposite of the linear take-make-dispose model.
First estimate of India's national income: Dadabhai Naoroji, 1867-68, in 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (per capita Rs 20). First scientific estimate: V.K.R.V. Rao, 1931-32.
National Income Committee, 1949 — chairman P.C. Mahalanobis; members D.R. Gadgil and V.K.R.V. Rao; first report 1951, final report 1954.
CSO set up 1951, NSSO 1950; merged into the National Statistical Office (NSO) in 2019 under MoSPI. National Statistical Commission set up 2005 (first chairman S.D. Tendulkar).
GVA at basic prices = GVA at factor cost + production taxes - production subsidies.
GDP at market prices = GVA at basic prices + product taxes - product subsidies.
NDP = GDP - depreciation (consumption of fixed capital). GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA). NNP = GNP - depreciation.
National Income = NNP at factor cost. Per capita income = NNP at factor cost / mid-year population.
GNI (Gross National Income) is the income concept corresponding to GNP; GNI per capita (PPP $) is the income indicator used in the HDI.
Three methods of estimating national income: production/value-added method, income method (wages + rent + interest + profit), expenditure method (C + I + G + (X - M)).
Value added = value of output - intermediate consumption. Double counting is avoided by counting only value added or only final goods.
Nominal GDP is at current prices; real GDP is at constant (base-year) prices. GDP deflator = (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) x 100 — the broadest price index, with no fixed basket.
GDP base-year series in India: 1993-94, 1999-2000, 2004-05, 2011-12 (introduced January 2015), and 2022-23 (released 27 February 2026 by MoSPI).

The 2022-23 series uses double deflation in manufacturing and agriculture, a Supply-Use Table framework, and GST, PFMS, e-Vahan, ASUSE and PLFS data. Advisory Committee on National Accounts Statistics (ACNAS) guides MoSPI.
Under the new series, real GDP growth was 7.2% in 2023-24 and 7.1% in 2024-25 (MoSPI, as of February 2026).
Since January 2015 India's headline growth is reported as GDP at constant market prices; sectoral performance is reported through GVA at basic prices.
Transfer payments (pensions, scholarships, subsidies to households), sale of second-hand goods and purely financial transactions are excluded from national income.
By PPP, India is the third largest economy in the world (after the USA and China); by nominal GDP in US dollars it is the fourth largest (IMF World Economic Outlook).

Sectors: primary (agriculture, mining), secondary (manufacturing, construction, electricity), tertiary/services. Services contribute the largest share (about 55%) of India's GVA; agriculture employs the largest share of workers (43.0% in PLFS 2025).

Growth models: Harrod-Domar (savings rate / capital-output ratio), Rostow's five stages (traditional, pre-conditions, take-off, drive to maturity, high mass consumption), Lewis dual-sector model, Rosenstein-Rodan's 'big push', Nurkse's vicious circle of poverty, Hirschman's unbalanced growth.

Economic Survey is prepared by the Economic Division of the Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance, under the Chief Economic Adviser, and is tabled a day before the Union Budget. First Economic Survey: 1950-51.
India follows a mixed economy; the framework was laid by the Industrial Policy Resolutions of 1948 and 1956 and the concept of a 'socialistic pattern of society'.

questions.q: Economic growth is best described as
opts: an increase in the nominal value of goods and services produced
an improvement in the distribution of income among all sections of society
a rise in literacy, life expectancy and standard of living
a sustained increase in the real national output of a country over time
questions.exp: Growth is a purely quantitative concept — a sustained rise in real (inflation-adjusted) national output. Improvements in distribution, literacy and longevity belong to the wider concept of economic development.

questions.q: The book 'Development as Freedom', which treats development as the expansion of human capabilities, was written by
questions.exp: Amartya Sen's 'Development as Freedom' (1999) argues that development means removing 'unfreedoms' and expanding capabilities. Sen also assisted Mahbub ul Haq in designing the Human Development Index.

questions.q: The definition of sustainable development as 'development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs' was given in the report
questions.exp: 'Our Common Future' (1987) was the report of the World Commission on Environment and Development, chaired by Gro Harlem Brundtland; hence it is popularly called the Brundtland Report.

questions.q: The Sustainable Development Goals adopted by the United Nations in 2015 consist of
questions.exp: The 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development contains 17 goals and 169 targets; 232 refers to the number of unique global indicators, not targets. The SDGs replaced the 8 Millennium Development Goals.

questions.q: The first estimate of India's national income was prepared by
questions.exp: Dadabhai Naoroji made the first estimate for 1867-68 in 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India', placing per capita income at Rs 20. The first scientific estimate was made by V.K.R.V. Rao for 1931-32.

questions.q: The National Income Committee constituted in 1949 was chaired by
questions.exp: P.C. Mahalanobis chaired the National Income Committee (1949), with V.K.R.V. Rao and D.R. Gadgil as members. Its first report came in 1951 and the final report in 1954.

questions.q: Gross National Product (GNP) is obtained as
opts: GDP minus net factor income from abroad
GDP plus indirect taxes minus subsidies
GDP plus net factor income from abroad
questions.exp: GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA). NFIA is factor income earned by residents abroad minus factor income earned by non-residents within the country.

questions.q: In national income accounting, 'National Income' refers specifically to
opts: Gross Domestic Product at market prices
Net Domestic Product at factor cost
Net National Product at factor cost
Gross Value Added at basic prices
questions.exp: National Income is defined as Net National Product at factor cost (NNP-FC). Per capita income is NNP at factor cost divided by the mid-year population.

questions.q: India's new series of National Accounts released by MoSPI in February 2026 uses which base year?
questions.exp: MoSPI released the new GDP series with base year 2022-23 on 27 February 2026, replacing the 2011-12 base year that had been in use since January 2015. As of February 2026, 2022-23 was chosen as a post-COVID 'normal' year with robust data.

questions.q: Per capita income of a country is calculated by dividing which aggregate by its population?
opts: Gross Domestic Product at market prices
Net Domestic Product at market prices
Gross National Product at market prices
Net National Product at factor cost
questions.exp: Per capita income = National Income (NNP at factor cost) / mid-year population. Using GDP instead would ignore depreciation and net factor income from abroad.

questions.q: Net Domestic Product is arrived at by deducting which item from Gross Domestic Product?
questions.exp: NDP = GDP - depreciation, which in national accounts is called consumption of fixed capital. Deducting NFIA from GDP would instead move from GNP to GDP.

questions.q: Which sector currently contributes the largest share to India's Gross Value Added?
questions.exp: The services (tertiary) sector contributes roughly 55% of India's GVA, well ahead of industry and agriculture. Agriculture, however, still absorbs the largest share of the workforce (43.0% in PLFS 2025).

questions.q: The method of estimating national income that adds together wages, rent, interest and profit is called the
questions.exp: The income method sums factor payments — compensation of employees, rent, interest, and profit (plus mixed income). The other two approaches are the production/value-added method and the expenditure method.

questions.q: The Economic Survey of India is prepared by the
opts: Department of Economic Affairs, Ministry of Finance
questions.exp: The Economic Survey is prepared by the Economic Division of the Department of Economic Affairs under the Chief Economic Adviser and is tabled in Parliament a day before the Union Budget. The first Economic Survey was for 1950-51.

questions.q: The National Statistical Office (NSO) was formed in 2019 by merging
opts: the CSO and the Office of the Economic Adviser
the CSO and the National Statistical Commission
the NSSO and the Labour Bureau
questions.exp: NSO was created in 2019 by merging the Central Statistics Office (CSO) and the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) under MoSPI. The National Statistical Commission, set up in 2005, remains a separate advisory body.

questions.q: Gross Value Added at basic prices is obtained from GVA at factor cost by
opts: adding product taxes and deducting product subsidies
adding net factor income from abroad
adding production taxes and deducting production subsidies
questions.exp: GVA at basic prices = GVA at factor cost + production taxes - production subsidies. Product taxes and subsidies are then adjusted to move from GVA at basic prices to GDP at market prices.

questions.q: The Harrod-Domar growth model explains the rate of growth primarily in terms of
opts: the savings rate and the capital-output ratio
questions.exp: In the Harrod-Domar model, growth rate = savings rate / capital-output ratio. It highlights capital accumulation as the engine of growth and was influential in India's Second Five Year Plan thinking.

questions.q: 'Green GDP' is best described as
opts: GDP generated by the renewable energy sector
GDP measured at purchasing power parity
GDP of the agriculture and forestry sectors combined
GDP adjusted for the depletion of natural resources and environmental degradation
questions.exp: Green GDP subtracts the monetary value of resource depletion and environmental damage from conventional GDP, a form of green or environmental accounting.

questions.q: A 'circular economy' is one in which
opts: output is produced entirely by the public sector
the economy moves through repeated cycles of boom and recession
materials are kept in use through reduction, reuse, recycling and recovery
all goods are produced and consumed within a single region
questions.exp: The circular economy keeps materials and products in circulation instead of the linear 'take-make-dispose' model. India promotes it through Extended Producer Responsibility and the Vehicle Scrappage Policy.

questions.q: The SDG India Index, which ranks States and Union Territories on progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals, is published by
opts: the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
questions.exp: NITI Aayog publishes the SDG India Index in collaboration with MoSPI and the UN in India; the first edition was released in December 2018.

questions.q: The Millennium Development Goals, which preceded the Sustainable Development Goals, comprised
questions.exp: The MDGs consisted of 8 goals covering 2000-2015. They were succeeded by the 17 SDGs, which came into force on 1 January 2016.

questions.q: In India, the headline rate of economic growth is officially reported as the growth of
questions.exp: Since the January 2015 revision, India reports headline growth as real GDP (constant market prices), while sectoral performance is reported through GVA at basic prices.

questions.q: In terms of purchasing power parity, India is currently the
opts: second largest economy in the world
fourth largest economy in the world
third largest economy in the world
fifth largest economy in the world
questions.exp: By PPP-adjusted GDP India ranks third, after the United States and China. In nominal US-dollar terms India is the fourth largest economy (IMF World Economic Outlook).

questions.q: In Rostow's stages of economic growth, the stage at which growth becomes a normal, self-sustaining condition is called
opts: the age of high mass consumption
questions.exp: W.W. Rostow's five stages are traditional society, pre-conditions for take-off, take-off, drive to maturity, and the age of high mass consumption. Take-off marks the point where growth becomes self-sustaining.

questions.q: Value added by a firm is calculated as
opts: value of output minus intermediate consumption
sales revenue minus wages and salaries
questions.exp: Value added = value of output - intermediate consumption. Summing value added across all producing units avoids the problem of double counting in national income estimation.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about economic growth and economic development:
I. Economic growth is a narrower concept than economic development.
II. Economic development necessarily accompanies economic growth.
III. Economic development includes qualitative changes such as improvement in health and education.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Growth is narrower than development, and development includes qualitative and distributional change. Statement II is wrong — growth can occur without development if its benefits are not widely shared ('growth without development').

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding GDP and GVA:
I. GDP at market prices equals GVA at basic prices plus product taxes minus product subsidies.
II. GVA measures the supply side of the economy, while GDP at market prices reflects the demand side.
III. A rise in indirect taxes raises GVA even if output is unchanged.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. III is wrong — GVA is measured net of product taxes, so it is unaffected by an indirect tax increase, whereas GDP at market prices would rise.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about sustainable development:
I. It was defined by the World Commission on Environment and Development.
II. It requires that the needs of the present be met without compromising those of future generations.
III. It rests on the three pillars of economic, social and environmental sustainability.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Brundtland Commission (WCED) definition of 1987 and the three-pillar framework of economic, social and environmental sustainability are both standard.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's new National Accounts series with base year 2022-23:
I. It replaced the series with base year 2011-12.
II. It introduces double deflation for manufacturing and agriculture.
III. It uses GST returns and the e-Vahan database as new data sources.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The series released by MoSPI on 27 February 2026 also adopts the Supply-Use Table framework and draws on ASUSE and PLFS for the household sector.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about nominal and real GDP:
I. Real GDP is measured at constant prices of a base year.
II. Nominal GDP can rise even when physical output falls.
III. In the base year, nominal GDP and real GDP are equal.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Because the base-year deflator equals 100, nominal and real GDP coincide in the base year; in later years nominal GDP can rise purely on account of price increases.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Net Factor Income from Abroad (NFIA):
I. It is the difference between factor income received from abroad and factor income paid abroad.
II. For India, NFIA is generally negative.
III. Gross National Income is obtained by adding NFIA to Gross Domestic Product.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. India's NFIA is usually negative because payments of investment income to foreigners exceed factor income earned by Indians abroad; hence India's GNI is normally slightly smaller than its GDP.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sustainable Development Goals:
I. They came into force on 1 January 2016.
II. SDG-1 relates to No Poverty and SDG-13 to Climate Action.
III. They are legally binding on member states of the United Nations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. III is wrong — the SDGs are voluntary, non-binding commitments monitored through Voluntary National Reviews at the UN High-Level Political Forum.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Economic Survey:
I. It is a constitutional requirement to lay it before Parliament.
II. It is normally presented a day before the Union Budget.
III. It is prepared under the guidance of the Chief Economic Adviser.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: II and III are correct. The Economic Survey is a convention, not a constitutional or statutory obligation, unlike the Annual Financial Statement required by Article 112.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the estimation of national income:
I. Only the value of final goods and services is counted under the expenditure method.
II. Transfer payments such as old-age pensions are included in national income.
III. The sale of a second-hand car is not counted in the national income of the year of resale.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and III are correct. Transfer payments involve no corresponding production and are therefore excluded; second-hand sales were already counted when the good was first produced.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Aggregate)   List-II (Expression)
A. NDP at market prices   1. GDP + NFIA
B. GNP at market prices   2. GDP - depreciation
C. National Income        3. GNP - depreciation
D. NNP at market prices   4. NNP at factor cost
questions.exp: NDP = GDP - depreciation; GNP = GDP + NFIA; National Income = NNP at factor cost; NNP at market prices = GNP - depreciation.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Economist)   List-II (Concept)
A. Ragnar Nurkse        1. Big Push theory
B. P.N. Rosenstein-Rodan 2. Unbalanced growth
C. Arthur Lewis         3. Vicious circle of poverty
D. A.O. Hirschman       4. Dual-sector model with unlimited supply of labour
questions.exp: Nurkse gave the vicious circle of poverty and balanced growth; Rosenstein-Rodan the Big Push; Lewis the dual-sector model; Hirschman the unbalanced growth strategy.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Body)   List-II (Function)
A. NSO, MoSPI        1. Preparation of the Economic Survey
B. Department of Economic Affairs   2. Compilation of national accounts statistics
C. NITI Aayog        3. Compilation of the Wholesale Price Index
D. Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT   4. Publication of the SDG India Index
questions.exp: NSO compiles national accounts; the DEA prepares the Economic Survey; NITI Aayog publishes the SDG India Index; the Office of the Economic Adviser under DPIIT compiles the WPI.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Goal)   List-II (Sustainable Development Goal number)
A. Zero Hunger        1. SDG-3
B. Good Health and Well-being   2. SDG-2
C. Quality Education  3. SDG-5
D. Gender Equality    4. SDG-4
questions.exp: SDG-1 No Poverty, SDG-2 Zero Hunger, SDG-3 Good Health and Well-being, SDG-4 Quality Education, SDG-5 Gender Equality.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Term)   List-II (Meaning)
A. Demographic dividend   1. GDP corrected for environmental costs
B. Green GDP              2. Growth benefits reaching the poor indirectly through the market
C. Trickle-down           3. Growth potential from a rising share of working-age population
D. Circular economy       4. Keeping materials in use through reuse and recycling
questions.exp: Demographic dividend arises from a rising working-age share; green GDP nets out environmental costs; trickle-down is indirect benefit transmission; circular economy focuses on material retention.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a method of estimating national income?
questions.exp: The three recognised methods are the production (value added), income and expenditure methods. 'Input-output substitution method' is not a national income estimation method.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT included while computing the national income of India?
opts: Salary of a government school teacher
Old-age pension paid by the State
Profit earned by a private company
questions.exp: Old-age pension is a transfer payment — money is transferred without any corresponding production of goods or services — and is therefore excluded from national income.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of national income concepts is NOT correctly matched?
opts: GNP  —  GDP plus net factor income from abroad
GDP deflator  —  ratio of real GDP to nominal GDP multiplied by 100
National income  —  NNP at factor cost
questions.exp: The GDP deflator is (Nominal GDP / Real GDP) x 100, not the reverse. The other three pairs are correct.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the new National Accounts series with base year 2022-23?
opts: Use of double deflation in manufacturing and agriculture
Use of the Supply-Use Table framework
Replacement of GDP by GVA as the headline growth indicator
Use of GST and PFMS administrative data
questions.exp: The new series retains GDP at constant market prices as the headline growth measure; GVA at basic prices continues to be used for sectoral analysis. The other three are genuine features.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a part of the tertiary sector of the economy?
questions.exp: Electricity, gas and water supply are classified under the secondary sector in Indian national accounts. Banking, transport and trade are all tertiary (services) activities.

questions.q:
Arrange the following base years of India's National Accounts series in correct chronological order of their adoption:
I. 2011-12
II. 1999-2000
III. 2004-05
IV. 1993-94
questions.exp: India's national accounts base years moved 1993-94, then 1999-2000, then 2004-05, then 2011-12 (adopted January 2015), and most recently 2022-23 (released February 2026).

chapters.title: Measurement of Development: HDI, Indices, Poverty and Inequality
factsheet: Human Development Index — conceived by Mahbub ul Haq with Amartya Sen; first Human Development Report published by UNDP in 1990.

HDI has 3 dimensions and 4 indicators: life expectancy at birth (health); mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling (education); GNI per capita in PPP dollars (standard of living). Since 2010 it is computed as a geometric mean.
HDI classes: Very high 0.800 and above; High 0.700-0.799; Medium 0.550-0.699; Low below 0.550.

Human Development Report 2025 (released May 2025, theme 'A matter of choice: people and possibilities in the age of AI'): India ranked 130 out of 193 countries with an HDI of 0.685 — the medium human development category. Iceland ranked first.

IHDI — inequality-adjusted HDI (introduced 2010). GDI — ratio of female HDI to male HDI. GII — Gender Inequality Index (reproductive health, empowerment, labour market); a lower GII value is better. MPI — Multidimensional Poverty Index.

Global MPI is published jointly by UNDP and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative (OPHI): 3 dimensions, 10 indicators; a person is multidimensionally poor if deprived in at least one-third (33.33%) of the weighted indicators.

NITI Aayog's National MPI uses 3 dimensions and 12 indicators — the 10 global indicators plus maternal health and bank account. Alkire-Foster methodology; MPI = Headcount ratio (H) x Intensity of deprivation (A).
NITI Aayog's 'National MPI: A Progress Review 2023' found multidimensional poverty falling from 24.85% (2015-16) to 14.96% (2019-21).
PQLI (Physical Quality of Life Index) — Morris David Morris, 1979: infant mortality rate, life expectancy at age one, and basic literacy rate; scaled 0-100; income is deliberately excluded.
Gross National Happiness is the development philosophy of Bhutan, with four pillars and nine domains.

World Happiness Report 2026: Finland ranked first for the ninth consecutive year; India ranked 116 out of 147 countries, up from 118 in the 2025 edition; Afghanistan ranked last. (As of the March 2026 edition.)
India's earlier World Happiness Report ranks: 139 (2021 edition), 126 (2023 and 2024 editions), 118 (2025), 116 (2026).

The World Happiness Report is based on Gallup World Poll life evaluations using the Cantril ladder (0-10); six explanatory variables are GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom to make life choices, generosity, and perceptions of corruption.

Global Hunger Index — published by Concern Worldwide (Ireland) and Welthungerhilfe (Germany); four indicators: undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting, child mortality. India ranked 102nd in the GHI 2025.
Global Innovation Index — published by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO); India ranked 38th in GII 2025.

World Bank's Doing Business report (Ease of Doing Business rank) was discontinued in September 2021; India's last rank was 63rd out of 190 in Doing Business 2020. It is being replaced by the Business Ready (B-READY) report.

DPIIT (Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, Ministry of Commerce and Industry) runs the Business Reform Action Plan (BRAP), under which States and UTs are ranked on ease of doing business.

Poverty committees: Working Group 1962; Dandekar and Rath 1971 (2250 calories); Y.K. Alagh Task Force 1979 (2400 kcal rural, 2100 kcal urban); D.T. Lakdawala 1993 (state-specific poverty lines, CPI-IW urban and CPI-AL rural); Suresh Tendulkar 2009; C. Rangarajan 2014.
Tendulkar Committee: poverty ratio 21.9% in 2011-12 (rural 25.7%, urban 13.7%); poverty lines Rs 816 (rural) and Rs 1000 (urban) per capita per month.
Rangarajan Committee (report submitted June 2014): poverty ratio 29.5% in 2011-12; poverty lines Rs 972 (rural) and Rs 1407 (urban) per capita per month.
Gini coefficient ranges from 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (perfect inequality); it is derived from the Lorenz curve, given by Max O. Lorenz in 1905.

Kuznets curve — an inverted-U relationship between per capita income and inequality, proposed by Simon Kuznets in 1955. The Environmental Kuznets Curve applies the same shape to income and environmental degradation.
Unemployment types: structural, frictional, cyclical, seasonal, disguised (marginal productivity near zero, typical of Indian agriculture), and educated/open unemployment.

Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) was launched by the NSO in April 2017, replacing the quinquennial Employment-Unemployment Surveys of the NSSO; it uses Usual Status (ps+ss) and Current Weekly Status.
LFPR = labour force / population x 100. WPR (Worker Population Ratio, also called Work Participation Rate) = employed persons / population x 100. Unemployment Rate = unemployed / labour force x 100.
PLFS Annual Report 2025 (January-December 2025, released March 2026), usual status, age 15 and above: LFPR 59.3%, WPR 57.4%, Unemployment Rate 3.1%; youth (15-29) unemployment 9.9%.
PLFS 2025: male WPR 76.6% and female WPR 38.8%; agriculture's share of employment fell from 44.8% (2024) to 43.0% (2025); self-employed 56.2% and regular wage/salaried 23.6%.

questions.q: The Human Development Index was developed by
opts: Mahbub ul Haq with the assistance of Amartya Sen
questions.exp: The Pakistani economist Mahbub ul Haq designed the HDI, assisted by Amartya Sen, and it first appeared in the UNDP Human Development Report of 1990.

questions.q: Which one of the following is used as the standard-of-living indicator in the Human Development Index?
opts: Gross Domestic Product per capita at market exchange rates
Net National Product at factor cost per capita
Gross National Income per capita at purchasing power parity
questions.exp: Since 2010 the HDI uses GNI per capita in PPP dollars; before 2010 it used GDP per capita (PPP). The other two dimensions are life expectancy at birth and the two schooling indicators.

questions.q: In the Human Development Report 2025, India's rank was
questions.exp: The UNDP's Human Development Report 2025 placed India 130th out of 193 countries with an HDI value of 0.685 (as of the report released in May 2025). Iceland topped the index.

questions.q: India's Human Development Index value as reported in the Human Development Report 2025 places it in which category?
questions.exp: India's HDI value of 0.685 in HDR 2025 falls in the medium human development band (0.550-0.699). The high band begins at 0.700.

questions.q: Which country topped the Human Development Index in the Human Development Report 2025?
questions.exp: Iceland ranked first in the HDR 2025 released by UNDP in May 2025, followed by other very high human development economies of Northern and Western Europe.

questions.q: According to the World Happiness Report 2026, India's rank among the countries covered was
questions.exp: India was ranked 116th of 147 countries in the World Happiness Report 2026 (released March 2026), improving from 118th in the 2025 edition and 126th in the 2024 edition.

questions.q: Which country was ranked the happiest in the world for the ninth consecutive year in the World Happiness Report 2026?
questions.exp: Finland retained the top position for the ninth year in a row in the World Happiness Report 2026; Afghanistan was placed last among the 147 countries ranked.

questions.q: The country rankings in the World Happiness Report are based primarily on
opts: per capita income and life expectancy data of the World Bank
household survey data collected by national statistical offices
an index of mental health services computed by the WHO
self-reported life evaluations on the Cantril ladder from the Gallup World Poll
questions.exp: Rankings rest on average life evaluations on the Cantril ladder (0 to 10) from the Gallup World Poll. Six variables — GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom, generosity and perceptions of corruption — are used to explain, not to compute, the scores.

questions.q: The Global Multidimensional Poverty Index is published jointly by UNDP and
opts: the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative
questions.exp: The Global MPI is produced by UNDP with OPHI at the University of Oxford. It uses 3 dimensions and 10 indicators, with a deprivation cut-off of one-third of weighted indicators.

questions.q: India's National Multidimensional Poverty Index prepared by NITI Aayog uses
questions.exp: The National MPI retains the 3 global dimensions but uses 12 indicators — the 10 global ones plus maternal health and bank account, reflecting national priorities.

questions.q: The Multidimensional Poverty Index is computed using the Alkire-Foster methodology as the product of
opts: headcount ratio and intensity of deprivation
headcount ratio and the Gini coefficient
poverty gap and squared poverty gap
incidence of poverty and the depth of income shortfall
questions.exp: MPI = H x A, where H is the proportion of people who are multidimensionally poor and A is the average share of weighted deprivations they suffer.

questions.q: The Physical Quality of Life Index developed by Morris David Morris combines the infant mortality rate, the basic literacy rate and
questions.exp: PQLI (1979) uses infant mortality, life expectancy at age one and basic literacy, each scaled 0-100. It deliberately excludes income, unlike the HDI.

questions.q: Gross National Happiness as a formal measure of development is associated with which country?
questions.exp: Bhutan adopted Gross National Happiness as its guiding development philosophy; it is built on four pillars and nine domains and is written into Bhutan's Constitution.

questions.q: The Global Hunger Index is published annually by
opts: the Food and Agriculture Organization and the World Food Programme
the UNDP and the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative
the World Bank and the International Food Policy Research Institute
questions.exp: The GHI is published by Concern Worldwide (Ireland) and Welthungerhilfe (Germany). India was ranked 102nd in the Global Hunger Index 2025.

questions.q: The Global Hunger Index is computed from four indicators — undernourishment, child stunting, child wasting and
questions.exp: The fourth GHI indicator is child mortality, that is the under-five mortality rate. Undernourishment carries a one-third weight, child mortality one-third, and stunting and wasting one-sixth each.

questions.q: The Gini coefficient measures
opts: the rate of growth of per capita income
the proportion of population below the poverty line
the degree of inequality in the distribution of income
questions.exp: The Gini coefficient measures income (or consumption) inequality on a scale of 0 (perfect equality) to 1 (perfect inequality) and is derived from the Lorenz curve.

questions.q: The Kuznets curve depicts the relationship between
opts: savings rate and the growth rate
per capita income and income inequality
questions.exp: Simon Kuznets (1955) proposed an inverted-U relationship in which inequality first rises and then falls as per capita income increases. The Environmental Kuznets Curve applies the same shape to environmental degradation.

questions.q: According to the Tendulkar Committee, the poverty ratio in India in 2011-12 was
questions.exp: The Tendulkar methodology placed poverty at 21.9% in 2011-12 (rural 25.7%, urban 13.7%). The Rangarajan Committee, using a different basket, put it at 29.5% for the same year.

questions.q: The Rangarajan Committee, which submitted its report in 2014, was constituted to review the methodology for the measurement of
questions.exp: The Expert Group under C. Rangarajan reviewed the poverty measurement methodology and recommended monthly per capita poverty lines of Rs 972 (rural) and Rs 1407 (urban) at 2011-12 prices.

questions.q: The Worker Population Ratio is defined as the
opts: number of persons employed per 1000 persons in the labour force
percentage of employed persons in the total population
percentage of persons in the labour force in the total population
percentage of unemployed persons in the labour force
questions.exp: WPR (Worker Population Ratio, also called Work Participation Rate) is the percentage of employed persons in the population. LFPR uses the labour force in the numerator, and the unemployment rate uses the labour force in the denominator.

questions.q: According to the PLFS Annual Report for January-December 2025, the Worker Population Ratio in India for persons aged 15 years and above (usual status) was about
questions.exp: The PLFS Annual Report 2025, released in March 2026, reported WPR at 57.4%, LFPR at 59.3% and the unemployment rate at 3.1% for persons aged 15 and above on usual status.

questions.q: The Ease of Doing Business ranking of countries was published by the World Bank in a report that was discontinued in 2021. That report was titled
questions.exp: The World Bank's 'Doing Business' report was discontinued in September 2021 after data irregularities; India's last rank was 63rd out of 190 in Doing Business 2020. It is being replaced by the Business Ready (B-READY) report.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Human Development Index:
I. It uses life expectancy at birth as the health indicator.
II. Education is measured by mean years of schooling and expected years of schooling.
III. Since 2010 the index is computed as the arithmetic mean of the three dimension indices.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. Since the 2010 Human Development Report the HDI has been computed as the geometric mean, not the arithmetic mean, of the three dimension indices, so that poor performance in one dimension cannot be fully offset by another.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about UNDP's composite indices:
I. The Inequality-adjusted HDI equals the HDI when there is no inequality across people.
II. The Gender Development Index is the ratio of the female HDI to the male HDI.
III. A higher value of the Gender Inequality Index indicates better performance.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. In the Gender Inequality Index a lower value is better, since the index measures loss in achievement due to gender disparity in reproductive health, empowerment and the labour market.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the World Happiness Report:
I. It is based on data from the Gallup World Poll.
II. India's rank improved from the 2025 edition to the 2026 edition.
III. Finland has topped the report in every edition since 2018.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct as of the 2026 edition: India moved from 118th (2025) to 116th (2026), and Finland has led the ranking for nine consecutive editions since 2018.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Multidimensional Poverty Index:
I. The Global MPI uses three dimensions and ten indicators.
II. NITI Aayog's National MPI adds maternal health and bank account as indicators.
III. A person is identified as multidimensionally poor if deprived in at least one-half of the weighted indicators.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. The deprivation cut-off in the MPI is one-third (33.33%) of the weighted indicators, not one-half.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about poverty estimation in India:
I. The Y.K. Alagh Task Force of 1979 fixed calorie norms of 2400 kcal for rural and 2100 kcal for urban areas.
II. The Lakdawala Committee recommended state-specific poverty lines.
III. The Rangarajan Committee estimated a lower poverty ratio for 2011-12 than the Tendulkar Committee.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. The Rangarajan Committee's estimate for 2011-12 was 29.5%, higher than the Tendulkar Committee's 21.9%.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Lorenz curve and the Gini coefficient:
I. The further the Lorenz curve lies from the line of equality, the greater is the inequality.
II. A Gini coefficient of zero indicates perfect equality.
III. The Gini coefficient can exceed one when inequality is extreme.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. The Gini coefficient is bounded between 0 and 1 (or 0 and 100 when expressed as an index) and cannot exceed one.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about types of unemployment:
I. Disguised unemployment occurs when the marginal productivity of an additional worker is nearly zero.
II. Frictional unemployment arises during the time taken to move between jobs.
III. Cyclical unemployment is characteristic of Indian agriculture.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. Indian agriculture is characterised by disguised and seasonal unemployment; cyclical unemployment is a feature of industrial economies during recessions.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Periodic Labour Force Survey:
I. It is conducted by the National Statistical Office.
II. It replaced the quinquennial Employment-Unemployment Surveys of the NSSO.
III. It reports estimates on Usual Status and Current Weekly Status.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. PLFS was launched by the NSO in April 2017 and since 2025 also produces monthly estimates for both rural and urban areas.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Index)   List-II (Publishing organisation)
A. Human Development Index   1. World Intellectual Property Organization
B. Global Hunger Index       2. UNDP
C. Global Innovation Index   3. World Economic Forum
D. Global Competitiveness Report   4. Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe
questions.exp: HDI is published by UNDP, GHI by Concern Worldwide and Welthungerhilfe, GII by WIPO, and the Global Competitiveness Report by the World Economic Forum.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Committee/Task Force)   List-II (Year of report)
A. Dandekar and Rath study   1. 1993
B. Y.K. Alagh Task Force      2. 2009
C. D.T. Lakdawala Committee   3. 1971
D. Suresh Tendulkar Committee   4. 1979
questions.exp: Dandekar and Rath 1971, Alagh Task Force 1979, Lakdawala Committee 1993, Tendulkar Committee 2009. The Rangarajan Expert Group reported in 2014.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Index)   List-II (A key component)
A. Physical Quality of Life Index   1. Adolescent birth rate
B. Gender Inequality Index          2. Infant mortality rate
C. Human Development Index         3. Child wasting
D. Global Hunger Index             4. Expected years of schooling
questions.exp: PQLI uses the infant mortality rate; the GII uses the adolescent birth rate under reproductive health; the HDI uses expected years of schooling; the GHI uses child wasting.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Type of unemployment)   List-II (Description)
A. Structural   1. Unemployment during the period of job search
B. Frictional   2. Mismatch between skills available and skills demanded
C. Seasonal     3. Employment available only in certain parts of the year
D. Disguised    4. More persons employed than are actually required
questions.exp: Structural unemployment arises from a skills mismatch, frictional from job search, seasonal from the crop or tourist calendar, and disguised where the marginal product of extra workers is near zero.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a component of the Human Development Index?
questions.exp: The HDI uses life expectancy at birth, mean and expected years of schooling, and GNI per capita (PPP). The infant mortality rate is a component of the PQLI, not the HDI.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of an index and its publishing organisation is NOT correctly matched?
opts: World Happiness Report  —  Gallup World Poll data
Global Innovation Index  —  World Intellectual Property Organization
Multidimensional Poverty Index  —  International Monetary Fund
questions.exp: The Global MPI is published by UNDP together with the Oxford Poverty and Human Development Initiative, not by the IMF. The other three pairs are correct.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT an indicator used in NITI Aayog's National Multidimensional Poverty Index?
questions.exp: The National MPI has 12 non-monetary indicators across health, education and standard of living. Income is deliberately excluded — the MPI is a measure of non-monetary deprivation.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about employment indicators is NOT correct?
opts: The Labour Force Participation Rate includes both employed and unemployed persons in the numerator
The Worker Population Ratio takes total population in the denominator
The Unemployment Rate is expressed as a percentage of the total population
The Usual Status approach uses a reference period of 365 days
questions.exp: The unemployment rate is the number of unemployed persons as a percentage of the labour force, not of the total population. The other three statements are correct.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in correct chronological order of their first introduction:
I. Human Development Index
II. Physical Quality of Life Index
III. Millennium Development Goals
IV. Global Multidimensional Poverty Index
questions.exp: PQLI was proposed by Morris in 1979, the HDI appeared in the first Human Development Report of 1990, the MDGs were adopted in 2000, and the Global MPI was introduced in the Human Development Report of 2010.

questions.q:
Arrange the following poverty-related committees in correct chronological order of their reports:
I. Suresh Tendulkar Committee
II. D.T. Lakdawala Committee
III. C. Rangarajan Expert Group
IV. Y.K. Alagh Task Force
questions.exp: Alagh Task Force 1979, Lakdawala Committee 1993, Tendulkar Committee 2009, Rangarajan Expert Group 2014.

chapters.title: Money, Banking, RBI, Monetary Policy and Inflation
factsheet: Reserve Bank of India was established on 1 April 1935 under the RBI Act, 1934, on the recommendation of the Hilton Young Commission (Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance, 1926). Nationalised on 1 January 1949.

RBI's original headquarters was Kolkata; shifted permanently to Mumbai in 1937. First Governor Sir Osborne Smith; first Indian Governor C.D. Deshmukh. Sanjay Malhotra took charge as the 26th Governor on 11 December 2024.
RBI issues all currency notes except the Re 1 note, which is issued by the Government of India and bears the signature of the Finance Secretary. Coins are also minted by the Government of India.
Minimum Reserve System, in force since 1957: RBI must hold assets worth at least Rs 200 crore, of which at least Rs 115 crore must be in gold.

Money supply: M0 (reserve money) = currency in circulation + bankers' deposits with RBI + other deposits with RBI. M1 = currency with the public + demand deposits + other deposits with RBI. M2 = M1 + post office savings deposits. M3 (broad money) = M1 + time deposits with the banking system. M4 = M3 + total post office deposits (excluding NSCs). Liquidity: M1 > M2 > M3 > M4.

CRR is prescribed under Section 42(1) of the RBI Act, 1934; it is kept in cash with the RBI and earns no interest. SLR is prescribed under Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949; it is held by the bank itself in cash, gold or unencumbered approved securities, with a statutory maximum of 40%.
Policy rates as of the August 2026 MPC review: repo rate 5.25%, Standing Deposit Facility 5.00%, Marginal Standing Facility 5.50%, Bank Rate 5.50%, CRR 3.00%, SLR 18.00%; stance neutral.

The Standing Deposit Facility, introduced in April 2022, is uncollateralised and forms the floor of the LAF corridor; the MSF is collateralised and forms the ceiling. The corridor is symmetric at 25 basis points around the repo rate.
The fixed-rate reverse repo is no longer the operational floor; the SDF replaced it in April 2022.

Monetary Policy Committee: constituted under Section 45ZB of the RBI Act (inserted by the Finance Act, 2016). Six members — the Governor (ex officio Chairperson), the Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy, one officer nominated by the Central Board, and three external members appointed by the Central Government for four years (not eligible for re-appointment). Quorum four; the Governor has a casting vote in case of a tie; it must meet at least four times a year.

Inflation target: 4% CPI (Combined) with a tolerance band of +/- 2 per cent, i.e. 2% to 6%, notified by the Central Government under Section 45ZA. First notified for 5 August 2016 to 31 March 2021, renewed for 2021-2026, and retained for 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031.
A 'failure' of monetary policy is deemed to occur if average inflation is outside the 2-6% band for three consecutive quarters; the RBI must then report to the Central Government.

Quantitative (general) credit control tools: CRR, SLR, repo, SDF, MSF, Bank Rate, Open Market Operations. Qualitative (selective) tools: margin requirements, credit rationing, moral suasion, direct action, regulation of consumer credit.
Headline inflation covers all items in the index, including food and fuel; core inflation is headline inflation excluding food and fuel, which are the volatile components.

Demand-pull inflation arises when aggregate demand exceeds aggregate supply — 'too much money chasing too few goods'. Cost-push inflation arises from a rise in input costs such as wages, fuel or raw materials, and can produce stagflation.

Deflation is a sustained fall in the general price level; disinflation is a fall in the rate of inflation while it remains positive; reflation is a deliberate policy-induced price rise after deflation; stagflation is high inflation combined with stagnant output and high unemployment.
The Phillips curve, given by A.W. Phillips (1958), shows an inverse short-run relationship between the rate of inflation and the rate of unemployment.

Consumer Price Index (Combined) is the headline inflation measure in India; the new CPI series with base year 2024=100 was released on 12 February 2026, replacing base 2012=100. Weights come from the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey 2023-24; items rose from 299 to 358 and groups from 6 to 12. CPI is compiled by the NSO, MoSPI.

Wholesale Price Index is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser, Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT). Base year revised from 2011-12 to 2022-23, with the new WPI series and the Producer Price Index launched on 15 June 2026; the basket expanded from 697 to 957 items. WPI excludes services; the PPI covers them.
CPI-IW is compiled by the Labour Bureau (base 2016=100) and is used for indexing dearness allowance; CPI-AL and CPI-RL are also compiled by the Labour Bureau.
GDP deflator is the broadest measure of inflation as it covers all goods and services and has no fixed basket.

Bank nationalisation: 14 banks with deposits of Rs 50 crore or more on 19 July 1969; 6 more banks with deposits of Rs 200 crore or more on 15 April 1980. Imperial Bank of India became the State Bank of India in 1955.

Regional Rural Banks were set up under an Ordinance of 26 September 1975 (RRB Act, 1976) on the recommendation of the Narasimham Working Group; the first RRB was Prathama Bank, Moradabad, on 2 October 1975. Shareholding: Centre 50%, sponsor bank 35%, State 15%. Under 'One State One RRB', the number of RRBs was reduced to 28 from 1 May 2025.
NABARD was set up on 12 July 1982 on the recommendation of the B. Sivaraman Committee (CRAFICARD); SIDBI in 1990; EXIM Bank in 1982.

Payments banks may accept deposits up to Rs 2 lakh per individual customer but cannot lend or issue credit cards; small finance banks must lend 40% (raised to 75%) of adjusted net bank credit to priority sectors, with at least 50% of loans up to Rs 25 lakh. Both were recommended by the Nachiket Mor Committee (2013).

Priority Sector Lending target for domestic scheduled commercial banks: 40% of Adjusted Net Bank Credit, with sub-targets of 18% for agriculture, 7.5% for micro enterprises and 12% for weaker sections.

An asset becomes a Non-Performing Asset when interest or instalment of principal remains overdue for more than 90 days. Deposit insurance under DICGC is Rs 5 lakh per depositor per bank (raised from Rs 1 lakh in February 2020).

Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016: NCLT is the adjudicating authority for corporate insolvency and the DRT for individuals and partnership firms; the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India was set up on 1 October 2016. The corporate insolvency resolution process must be completed within 330 days including litigation.
SEBI was set up as a non-statutory body in 1988 and made statutory by the SEBI Act, 1992 (headquarters Mumbai). IRDAI was constituted under the IRDA Act, 1999 (headquarters Hyderabad).

Financial inclusion: PMJDY launched 28 August 2014 (zero-balance account, RuPay card with Rs 2 lakh accident cover for cards issued after 28 August 2018, overdraft up to Rs 10,000). PMMY (MUDRA) launched 8 April 2015 — Shishu up to Rs 50,000, Kishore Rs 50,000 to Rs 5 lakh, Tarun Rs 5-10 lakh, Tarun Plus Rs 10-20 lakh. UPI was launched by NPCI in April 2016.

questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India was established on
questions.exp: The RBI commenced operations on 1 April 1935 under the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. It was nationalised on 1 January 1949.

questions.q: The establishment of the Reserve Bank of India was recommended by the
questions.exp: The Hilton Young Commission, formally the Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance (1926), recommended a central bank for India, leading to the RBI Act, 1934.

questions.q: The Reserve Bank of India was nationalised with effect from
questions.exp: The RBI was nationalised on 1 January 1949 under the Reserve Bank (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948. Commercial bank nationalisation came much later, in 1969 and 1980.

questions.q: In India, the one rupee note is issued by
opts: the Security Printing and Minting Corporation
questions.exp: The Re 1 note is issued by the Government of India and bears the signature of the Finance Secretary; all other currency notes are issued by the RBI over the Governor's signature. Coins are also issued by the Government of India.

questions.q: Under the Minimum Reserve System followed by the Reserve Bank of India, the minimum value of gold that must be held as backing for note issue is
questions.exp: Since 1957 the RBI must maintain assets of at least Rs 200 crore, of which at least Rs 115 crore must be in gold and the remainder in foreign securities.

questions.q: Reserve money (M0) consists of currency in circulation, other deposits with the RBI and
opts: time deposits with the banking system
questions.exp: M0 = currency in circulation + bankers' deposits with the RBI + other deposits with the RBI. It is the monetary base created by the RBI, distinct from M1 (narrow money).

questions.q: Broad money (M3) in India is defined as
opts: M1 plus savings deposits with post office savings banks
M1 plus time deposits with the banking system
M0 plus demand deposits with the banking system
M2 plus all deposits with post office savings banks
questions.exp: M3 = M1 + time deposits with the banking system. M2 adds post office savings deposits to M1, and M4 adds all post office deposits (excluding NSCs) to M3.

questions.q: The Cash Reserve Ratio is the proportion of a bank's net demand and time liabilities that it must maintain
opts: in cash with itself in its own vaults
as a deposit with the Reserve Bank of India
in the form of unencumbered government securities
as a deposit with the State Bank of India
questions.exp: CRR is maintained as a cash balance with the RBI under Section 42(1) of the RBI Act, 1934, and earns no interest. SLR, by contrast, is held by the bank itself in cash, gold or approved securities.

questions.q: The Statutory Liquidity Ratio in India is prescribed under
opts: Section 42(1) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949
Section 45ZB of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934
the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007
questions.exp: SLR is governed by Section 24 of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, with a statutory ceiling of 40%. Section 42(1) of the RBI Act governs the CRR, and Section 45ZB deals with the Monetary Policy Committee.

questions.q: What was the policy repo rate of the Reserve Bank of India following the Monetary Policy Committee review of August 2026?
questions.exp: The MPC left the policy repo rate unchanged at 5.25% with a neutral stance in August 2026. The corresponding SDF rate was 5.00% and the MSF and Bank Rate 5.50%.

questions.q: The Standing Deposit Facility introduced by the Reserve Bank of India in April 2022
opts: allows banks to borrow overnight against government securities
allows the RBI to absorb liquidity from banks without offering collateral
is the ceiling of the liquidity adjustment facility corridor
questions.exp: The SDF is an uncollateralised liquidity absorption facility and forms the floor of the LAF corridor, replacing the fixed-rate reverse repo in that role. The MSF remains the ceiling.

questions.q: The Monetary Policy Committee of the Reserve Bank of India consists of
opts: four members, of whom two are from the RBI
six members, of whom three are from the RBI
six members, all appointed by the Central Government
five members, of whom two are external experts
questions.exp: The MPC has six members — the Governor (ex officio Chairperson), the Deputy Governor in charge of monetary policy and one RBI officer nominated by the Central Board, plus three external members appointed by the Central Government for four years. The Governor has a casting vote.

questions.q: Under India's flexible inflation targeting framework, the inflation target and tolerance band notified by the Central Government are
opts: 2 per cent with a band of +/- 2 per cent
4 per cent with a band of +/- 2 per cent
5 per cent with a band of +/- 1 per cent
6 per cent with a band of +/- 2 per cent
questions.exp: The target is 4% CPI (Combined) inflation with a tolerance band of +/- 2 per cent, that is 2% to 6%. It was first notified in August 2016 and has been retained for the period 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031.

questions.q: Core inflation is defined as
opts: inflation measured by the Wholesale Price Index only
headline inflation excluding food and fuel
inflation in the prices of essential commodities only
the difference between the CPI and the WPI inflation rates
questions.exp: Core inflation strips out food and fuel, the most volatile components, to reveal the underlying persistent price trend. Headline inflation includes all items of the index.

questions.q: Inflation caused by an increase in aggregate demand beyond the economy's capacity to produce is called
questions.exp: Demand-pull inflation is the classic case of 'too much money chasing too few goods'. Cost-push inflation, in contrast, originates in a rise in input costs such as wages or fuel.

questions.q: The Phillips curve depicts the relationship between
opts: inflation and the rate of interest
inflation and the rate of unemployment
money supply and the price level
questions.exp: A.W. Phillips (1958) showed an inverse short-run relationship between the rate of unemployment and the rate of wage or price inflation. Stagflation in the 1970s challenged this relationship.

questions.q: The new Consumer Price Index series released by MoSPI in February 2026 uses which base year?
questions.exp: The new CPI series with base 2024=100 was released on 12 February 2026, replacing base 2012=100. Its weights are derived from the Household Consumption Expenditure Survey 2023-24, and the number of items rose from 299 to 358.

questions.q: The Wholesale Price Index in India is compiled by the
opts: Labour Bureau, Ministry of Labour and Employment
Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT
questions.exp: The WPI is compiled by the Office of the Economic Adviser under DPIIT. Its base year was revised from 2011-12 to 2022-23, and the new WPI series along with the Producer Price Index was launched on 15 June 2026.

questions.q: How many commercial banks were nationalised in India on 19 July 1969?
questions.exp: Fourteen banks with deposits of Rs 50 crore or more were nationalised on 19 July 1969; six more with deposits of Rs 200 crore or more followed on 15 April 1980.

questions.q: The first Regional Rural Bank established in India on 2 October 1975 was
questions.exp: Prathama Bank, sponsored by Syndicate Bank at Moradabad, was the first RRB. RRBs were set up under an Ordinance of 26 September 1975, later replaced by the RRB Act, 1976.

questions.q: An advance is classified as a Non-Performing Asset when interest or instalment of principal remains overdue for a period of more than
questions.exp: The RBI's income recognition and asset classification norms treat an account as an NPA when dues remain overdue for more than 90 days. Special Mention Accounts (SMA-0, 1, 2) flag stress before that.

questions.q: Under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, the adjudicating authority for insolvency of companies is the
questions.exp: NCLT is the adjudicating authority for corporate insolvency, while the DRT handles individuals and partnership firms. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India, set up on 1 October 2016, is the regulator.

questions.q: The Unified Payments Interface was launched in 2016 by
opts: the National Payments Corporation of India
the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology
questions.exp: UPI was launched by the National Payments Corporation of India in April 2016. NPCI was set up in 2008 as the umbrella organisation for retail payments under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.

questions.q: The Priority Sector Lending target for domestic scheduled commercial banks is what percentage of Adjusted Net Bank Credit?
questions.exp: Domestic scheduled commercial banks must lend 40% of Adjusted Net Bank Credit to the priority sector, with sub-targets of 18% for agriculture, 7.5% for micro enterprises and 12% for weaker sections. Small finance banks have a higher target of 75%.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the functions of the Reserve Bank of India:
I. It acts as banker to the Central and State Governments.
II. It is the lender of last resort to commercial banks.
III. It regulates the securities market in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. Regulation of the securities market is the function of SEBI, not the RBI. The RBI is also the manager of public debt and custodian of foreign exchange reserves.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Cash Reserve Ratio and the Statutory Liquidity Ratio:
I. CRR is maintained with the RBI while SLR is maintained by the bank itself.
II. Banks earn interest on the CRR balances kept with the RBI.
III. SLR can be maintained in the form of gold and unencumbered approved securities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and III are correct. No interest is paid on CRR balances. The statutory maximum for SLR is 40%; there has been no statutory floor or ceiling for the CRR since the 2006 amendment.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the liquidity adjustment facility:
I. The repo rate is the rate at which the RBI lends to banks against government securities.
II. The Marginal Standing Facility rate forms the ceiling of the corridor.
III. The Standing Deposit Facility requires the RBI to provide collateral to banks.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and II are correct. The SDF is an uncollateralised facility — that is precisely why it was introduced in April 2022, since the RBI's stock of securities constrained collateralised absorption.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Monetary Policy Committee:
I. It was constituted under the Reserve Bank of India Act as amended by the Finance Act, 2016.
II. External members hold office for a term of four years and are eligible for re-appointment.
III. In the event of a tie, the Governor has a second or casting vote.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: I and III are correct. External members are appointed for four years and are NOT eligible for re-appointment. The quorum for a meeting is four members and the MPC must meet at least four times a year.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's monetary policy framework:
