questions.q: Operation Flood, launched in 1970 under the National Dairy Development Board, was led by:
questions.exp: Verghese Kurien, the 'Milkman of India', built the Anand pattern of dairy cooperatives. NDDB was established at Anand in 1965, and Operation Flood ran in three phases up to 1996.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. India is the world's largest producer of milk.
II. Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana was launched in 2020 with an outlay of about Rs 20,050 crore.
III. India is the world's largest producer of rice.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: China is the largest producer of rice; India is the second largest producer but the largest exporter. India is also the world's largest producer of pulses and the second largest producer of fish.

questions.q: PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana, approved by the Union Cabinet in 2025, covers:
opts: 50 districts, with an annual outlay of Rs 10,000 crore
250 districts, with an annual outlay of Rs 50,000 crore
100 blocks, with an annual outlay of Rs 24,000 crore
100 districts, with an annual outlay of Rs 24,000 crore
questions.exp: Announced in the Union Budget 2025-26, the scheme runs for six years from 2025-26, converges 36 existing schemes of 11 Ministries and selects districts on low productivity, low cropping intensity and poor credit access, with at least one district from every State and Union Territory.

questions.q:
Arrange the following schemes in the correct chronological order of their launch:
I. Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana
II. Soil Health Card scheme
III. National Agriculture Market (eNAM)
IV. PM-KISAN
questions.exp: Soil Health Card - 19 February 2015; PMFBY - 18 February 2016; eNAM - 14 April 2016; PM-KISAN - 24 February 2019.

chapters.title: Industry: Growth, LPG Reforms, MSME and Industrial Policy
factsheet: Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR) 1948 — 6 April 1948; first industrial policy of independent India; four-fold classification of industries; accepted a mixed economy.
IPR 1956 — 30 April 1956; called the 'Economic Constitution of India'; basis of the Second Five Year Plan (Mahalanobis model); aimed at a 'socialistic pattern of society'.
IPR 1956 schedules — Schedule A: 17 industries exclusively for the State; Schedule B: 12 industries progressively state-owned; Schedule C: all the rest, left to the private sector.
Industrial Policy Statement 1977 — Janata Government; top priority to the tiny and small sector; created District Industries Centres (DICs); expanded SSI reservation.
Industrial Policy Statement 1980 — Indira Gandhi government; concept of 'economic federalism' through nucleus plants in industrially backward districts; stress on capacity regularisation.
New Industrial Policy — 24 July 1991; PM P. V. Narasimha Rao, FM Manmohan Singh; the LPG package (Liberalisation, Privatisation, Globalisation).

NIP 1991 — industrial licensing abolished for all but 18 industries; public-sector reserved list cut from 17 to 8; MRTP asset limit (Rs 100 crore) scrapped; FDI up to 51% automatic in 34 high-priority industries.

Compulsory industrial licensing today survives for only a handful of items — alcoholic drinks (distillation/brewing), cigars and cigarettes, electronic aerospace and defence equipment, industrial explosives.
Rupee devalued in two steps on 1 and 3 July 1991 by about 18-19% cumulatively; gold pledged with the Bank of England and Bank of Japan in mid-1991.

MRTP Act 1969 replaced by the Competition Act, 2002 (CCI); FERA 1973 replaced by FEMA, 1999 (in force 1 June 2000); SICA/BIFR replaced by the IBC, 2016. Disinvestment is handled by DIPAM (Ministry of Finance), renamed from the Department of Disinvestment in April 2016.
IIP base year 2011-12, compiled by NSO/MoSPI; sectoral weights — manufacturing 77.63%, mining 14.37%, electricity 7.99%.
Index of Eight Core Industries (base 2011-12), released by the Office of the Economic Adviser, Ministry of Commerce and Industry — combined weight 40.27% of IIP.
ICI weights — Refinery products 28.04, Electricity 19.85, Steel 17.92, Coal 10.33, Crude oil 8.98, Natural gas 6.88, Cement 5.37, Fertilizers 2.63.
MSMED Act, 2006 — came into force 2 October 2006; created the National Board for MSME and the delayed-payment remedy (Section 15: payment within 45 days).

MSME classification revised by notification S.O. 2119(E) dated 26 June 2020, effective 1 July 2020 — composite investment-and-turnover criterion; manufacturing/service distinction removed. Micro Rs 1 cr / Rs 5 cr; Small Rs 10 cr / Rs 50 cr; Medium Rs 50 cr / Rs 250 cr.

MSME classification revised again by S.O. 1364(E) dated 21 March 2025, effective 1 April 2025 (Budget 2025-26: investment limits x2.5, turnover x2) — Micro Rs 2.5 cr / Rs 10 cr; Small Rs 25 cr / Rs 100 cr; Medium Rs 125 cr / Rs 500 cr.

Exports are excluded while computing turnover for MSME classification; Udyam Registration portal launched 1 July 2020 — free, paperless, PAN- and Aadhaar-based; Udyam Assist Platform (2023) for informal micro enterprises.

MSME schemes — PMEGP (2008, national nodal agency KVIC), CGTMSE (2000, GoI + SIDBI), MSME Samadhaan (delayed payments), MSME Sambandh, ZED certification, RAMP (World Bank-assisted, Rs 6,062 crore), Self-Reliant India Fund Rs 50,000 crore.
PM Vishwakarma — launched 17 September 2023, Ministry of MSME; 18 traditional trades; collateral-free credit of Rs 1 lakh then Rs 2 lakh at 5% concessional interest.
Make in India — launched 25 September 2014, initially 25 sectors; Make in India 2.0 covers 27 sectors; administered by DPIIT.
PLI schemes — 14 sectors, total outlay about Rs 1.97 lakh crore; first three sectors approved in March 2020 (large-scale electronics/mobiles, bulk drugs-KSM/API, medical devices).

Startup India — launched 16 January 2016 (National Startup Day); Fund of Funds for Startups Rs 10,000 crore operated by SIDBI; Startup India Seed Fund Scheme Rs 945 crore. DPIIT recognition: entity up to 10 years old with turnover not above Rs 100 crore in any financial year.
Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan — announced 12 May 2020; package of Rs 20 lakh crore, about 10% of GDP; five pillars — Economy, Infrastructure, System, Vibrant Demography, Demand.

Industrial corridors — DMIC (2006, Japanese collaboration, along the Western DFC), Chennai-Bengaluru (CBIC), Amritsar-Kolkata (AKIC), Bengaluru-Mumbai (BMEC); implementing agency NICDC (formerly DMICDC).
SEZ Act, 2005 (rules effective 10 February 2006); Kandla (1965) was India's and Asia's first Export Processing Zone; EXIM Policy 2000 first introduced the SEZ scheme.
National Manufacturing Policy 2011 — target of raising manufacturing to 25% of GDP and creating 100 million jobs; introduced National Investment and Manufacturing Zones (NIMZ).

CPSE status — Maharatna needs Navratna status, listing, 3-year average turnover above Rs 25,000 crore, net worth above Rs 15,000 crore, net profit above Rs 5,000 crore and global presence; Navratna needs a composite score of 60 out of 100; Miniratna-I needs pre-tax profit of Rs 30 crore or more in at least one of the last three years.

National Monetisation Pipeline — NITI Aayog, announced 23 August 2021; Rs 6 lakh crore of core assets over FY2022-25; ownership stays with government, only brownfield assets. Budget 2025-26 announced a second Asset Monetisation Plan of Rs 10 lakh crore for 2025-30.

Ease of Doing Business — India ranked 63rd of 190 in the World Bank's Doing Business 2020 (77th in 2019, 100th in 2018, 142nd in 2015). The Doing Business report was discontinued in September 2021 and is being replaced by B-READY. DPIIT (Ministry of Commerce and Industry) runs the Business Reform Action Plan ranking of states.

Labour codes — four codes subsuming 29 central labour laws, made effective from 21 November 2025: Code on Wages 2019 (4 Acts), Industrial Relations Code 2020 (3 Acts), Code on Social Security 2020 (9 Acts), OSH and Working Conditions Code 2020 (13 Acts).

questions.q: The first Industrial Policy Resolution of independent India was announced in the year
questions.exp: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 6 April 1948 was the first industrial policy statement of independent India; it accepted a mixed economy and divided industries into four categories.

questions.q: Which industrial policy of India is popularly described as the 'Economic Constitution of India'?
questions.exp: The IPR of 30 April 1956, which laid the framework for a 'socialistic pattern of society', is called the Economic Constitution of India. It provided the basis for the Second Five Year Plan.

questions.q: Under the Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956, the number of industries placed in Schedule A, reserved exclusively for the State, was
questions.exp: Schedule A listed 17 industries as an exclusive state monopoly, Schedule B listed 12 in which the State would progressively take the initiative, and Schedule C left the remainder to the private sector.

questions.q: The Industrial Policy Resolution of 1956 provided the framework for which Five Year Plan?
questions.exp: IPR 1956 gave effect to the heavy-industry strategy of the Second Five Year Plan, drafted on the Mahalanobis model.

questions.q: District Industries Centres (DICs) were introduced under which industrial policy?
questions.exp: The Industrial Policy Statement of 1977, announced by the Janata Government, gave the highest priority to the tiny and small sector and set up District Industries Centres as a single agency for small enterprises.

questions.q: The concept of 'nucleus plants' in industrially backward districts was introduced by the
questions.exp: The 1980 statement promoted 'economic federalism' by proposing nucleus plants in each industrially backward district to generate ancillary and small units around them.

questions.q: The New Industrial Policy that launched the LPG reforms was announced on 24 July 1991 when the Prime Minister of India was
questions.exp: The New Industrial Policy of 24 July 1991 was announced by the Narasimha Rao government, with Dr Manmohan Singh as Finance Minister, alongside the 1991-92 budget.

questions.q: Under the New Industrial Policy, 1991 industrial licensing was abolished for all industries except
questions.exp: The 1991 policy retained compulsory licensing for only 18 industries, chiefly on grounds of security, strategy, environment and social concern. The list has since been pruned to a handful.

questions.q: Which one of the following activities still requires a compulsory industrial licence in India?
opts: Distillation and brewing of alcoholic drinks
questions.exp: Compulsory licensing survives for only a few items, including distillation and brewing of alcoholic drinks, cigars and cigarettes, electronic aerospace and defence equipment and industrial explosives.

questions.q: The Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices (MRTP) Act, 1969 was replaced by the
questions.exp: The MRTP Act was repealed and replaced by the Competition Act, 2002, under which the Competition Commission of India functions. The MRTP asset limit of Rs 100 crore had already been scrapped in 1991.

questions.q: As part of the 1991 stabilisation measures the Indian rupee was devalued in two steps on 1 and 3 July 1991 by a cumulative
questions.exp: The RBI devalued the rupee against major currencies in two steps totalling roughly 18-19 per cent to correct the external imbalance during the balance of payments crisis.

questions.q: The Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM) functions under which ministry?
questions.exp: DIPAM, renamed from the Department of Disinvestment in April 2016, is a department of the Ministry of Finance and handles disinvestment and management of the government's equity in CPSEs.

questions.q: The current base year of the Index of Industrial Production (IIP) in India is
questions.exp: The IIP series has 2011-12 as its base year and is compiled and released monthly by the National Statistical Office under MoSPI.

questions.q: In the Index of Industrial Production (base 2011-12), the highest weight is assigned to
questions.exp: Manufacturing carries a weight of 77.63 per cent, mining 14.37 per cent and electricity 7.99 per cent. Construction is not covered by the IIP.

questions.q: In the Index of Eight Core Industries, the highest weight is assigned to
questions.exp: Refinery products have the highest weight at 28.04 per cent, followed by electricity 19.85 and steel 17.92. Fertilizers has the lowest weight at 2.63.

questions.q: The department that prepares the Business Reform Action Plan ranking of states for ease of doing business is
opts: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
questions.exp: DPIIT, under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry and renamed from DIPP in 2019, runs the Business Reform Action Plan exercise; since 2019 states are placed in categories such as Top Achievers and Achievers instead of numerical ranks.

questions.q: The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act was enacted in the year
questions.exp: The MSMED Act, 2006 came into force on 2 October 2006. It first gave a statutory definition of micro, small and medium enterprises and created the delayed-payment remedy under Section 15.

questions.q: Under the classification of MSMEs effective from 1 April 2025, a micro enterprise is one with investment in plant and machinery and annual turnover not exceeding
opts: Rs 1 crore and Rs 5 crore respectively
Rs 2 crore and Rs 8 crore respectively
Rs 2.5 crore and Rs 10 crore respectively
Rs 5 crore and Rs 20 crore respectively
questions.exp: Notification S.O. 1364(E) of 21 March 2025, effective 1 April 2025, raised the micro limits to Rs 2.5 crore investment and Rs 10 crore turnover (the 2020 limits were Rs 1 crore and Rs 5 crore).

questions.q: Under the revised MSME classification effective 1 April 2025, a medium enterprise is one with investment up to Rs 125 crore and turnover up to
questions.exp: The 2025 revision fixed medium enterprises at investment up to Rs 125 crore and turnover up to Rs 500 crore, against Rs 50 crore and Rs 250 crore under the 2020 definition.

questions.q: The Udyam Registration portal for MSMEs was launched on
questions.exp: Udyam Registration began on 1 July 2020 along with the revised composite classification. It is free, paperless and based on self-declaration linked to PAN and Aadhaar.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the national nodal implementing agency for the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)?
opts: Small Industries Development Bank of India
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
questions.exp: PMEGP, launched in 2008 by merging PMRY and REGP, is implemented at the national level by the KVIC under the Ministry of MSME, with State KVIBs, DICs and banks at the field level.

questions.q: India's rank in the World Bank's 'Doing Business 2020' report, the last edition of that report, was
questions.exp: India stood 63rd among 190 economies in Doing Business 2020, up from 77th in 2019 and 142nd in 2015. The World Bank discontinued the Doing Business report in September 2021 and is replacing it with the B-READY assessment.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the revision of the MSME definition notified in June 2020:
I. The distinction between manufacturing and service enterprises was removed.
II. A composite criterion of investment in plant and machinery and annual turnover was adopted.
III. Exports are included while computing turnover for classification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The 2020 revision merged manufacturing and services into one composite investment-plus-turnover criterion. Exports are specifically excluded from turnover so that export growth does not push a unit out of the MSME bracket.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the economic reforms of 1991:
I. Industrial licensing was abolished for all but eighteen industries.
II. The asset limit under the MRTP Act was abolished.
III. The number of industries reserved for the public sector was raised from eight to seventeen.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The 1991 policy reduced the public-sector reserved list from 17 industries to 8, not the other way round. Delicensing and the scrapping of the MRTP asset limit were both central to the reform.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes:
I. They currently cover fourteen sectors.
II. The total outlay approved for them is about Rs 1.97 lakh crore.
III. The incentive is paid on incremental sales of goods manufactured in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The PLI schemes span 14 sectors with an approved outlay of about Rs 1.97 lakh crore, and pay incentives on incremental sales of domestically manufactured goods over a base year. The first three PLI schemes, approved in March 2020, covered mobiles and electronic components, bulk drugs and medical devices.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Startup India initiative:
I. It was launched on 16 January 2016.
II. The Fund of Funds for Startups is operated by SIDBI.
III. For DPIIT recognition an entity may be up to fifteen years old.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Startup India was launched on 16 January 2016, now observed as National Startup Day, and the Rs 10,000 crore Fund of Funds is operated by SIDBI. The age limit for DPIIT recognition is ten years, with turnover not exceeding Rs 100 crore in any financial year.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the four Labour Codes:
I. They subsume twenty-nine central labour laws.
II. The Code on Wages was enacted in 2019 and the other three in 2020.
III. They were brought into force across the country from 21 November 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Code on Wages, 2019 and the Industrial Relations, Social Security and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Codes of 2020 together replace 29 central labour laws and were made effective from 21 November 2025.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Monetisation Pipeline:
I. It was prepared by NITI Aayog.
II. It covers greenfield infrastructure assets awaiting construction.
III. Ownership of the assets remains with the government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The NMP, announced on 23 August 2021 for Rs 6 lakh crore over FY2022-25, was prepared by NITI Aayog and covers only brownfield, revenue-generating assets; ownership is retained by the government and only the right to operate is transferred for a defined period.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Special Economic Zones in India:
I. The SEZ Act was passed in 2005.
II. Kandla was the first Export Processing Zone in Asia.
III. The SEZ scheme was first announced in the EXIM Policy of 2000.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Kandla Free Trade Zone of 1965 was Asia's first EPZ; the SEZ scheme was announced in the EXIM Policy 2000 and given statutory backing by the SEZ Act, 2005, whose rules came into effect in February 2006.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Maharatna status for central public sector enterprises:
I. The enterprise must already have Navratna status.
II. It must be listed on an Indian stock exchange with the prescribed minimum public shareholding.
III. Its average annual turnover in the last three years must exceed Rs 5,000 crore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: A Maharatna candidate must be a listed Navratna with average annual turnover above Rs 25,000 crore, net worth above Rs 15,000 crore and average annual net profit after tax above Rs 5,000 crore for three years, besides a significant global presence.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Industrial policy)   List-II (Distinctive feature)

questions.exp: IPR 1948 was the first policy statement; IPR 1956 introduced Schedules A, B and C; the 1977 statement created District Industries Centres; the 1980 statement proposed nucleus plants.

Match List-I with List-II with reference to the MSME classification effective from 1 April 2025 and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

B. Fund of Funds for Startups   2. DPIIT

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II with reference to the Index of Eight Core Industries (base 2011-12) and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Industry)   List-II (Weight in per cent)

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:

A. DMIC   1. Amritsar and Kolkata
B. CBIC   2. Bengaluru and Mumbai

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of the New Industrial Policy of 1991?
opts: Abolition of industrial licensing for most industries
Removal of the MRTP asset limit
Automatic approval of foreign direct investment up to 51 per cent in high-priority industries
Reservation of 807 items exclusively for the small-scale sector
questions.exp: Reservation of items for exclusive manufacture by the small-scale sector was a pre-reform device that the 1991 policy and later governments progressively dismantled; the last reserved items were dereserved in 2015.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of an economic legislation and its year of enactment is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: FEMA was enacted in 1999 (in force from 1 June 2000), replacing FERA, 1973. The other three pairs are correct.

questions.q: Which one of the following central public sector enterprises does NOT have Maharatna status?
questions.exp: NHPC was upgraded to Navratna status; BHEL, Coal India and NTPC are among the Maharatna CPSEs. Maharatna status carries the highest investment autonomy, up to Rs 5,000 crore or 15 per cent of net worth in a single project.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT one of the four Labour Codes enacted by Parliament?
opts: Code on Industrial Disputes and Trade Unions, 2020
questions.exp: The four codes are the Code on Wages 2019 and the Industrial Relations, Social Security and Occupational Safety, Health and Working Conditions Codes of 2020. Trade unions and industrial disputes are dealt with inside the Industrial Relations Code.

questions.q:
Arrange the following enactments in correct chronological order of their enactment:
I. Monopolies and Restrictive Trade Practices Act
II. Competition Act
III. Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act
IV. Foreign Exchange Management Act
questions.exp: MRTP Act 1969, FEMA 1999, Competition Act 2002 and MSMED Act 2006 is the correct sequence.

chapters.title: Services, Infrastructure, External Sector, Employment and Skills
factsheet: Services contribute the largest share of India's gross value added (roughly 55 per cent) and India is among the world's largest exporters of commercial services.
India's total exports in FY 2024-25 were a record US$ 820.93 billion — merchandise US$ 437.42 billion and services US$ 383.51 billion; merchandise imports US$ 720.24 billion.
The United States has been India's largest trading partner in recent years, while China is the largest source of India's imports; crude petroleum is the single largest import item.

Electricity Act, 2003 unbundled generation, transmission and distribution; UDAY (Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana) was launched in November 2015 to restore DISCOM finances; the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) followed in 2021.
At COP26 (Glasgow, 2021) India committed under 'Panchamrit' to 500 GW of non-fossil energy capacity by 2030 and net zero by 2070.
PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana — launched 13 February 2024; rooftop solar for one crore households with up to 300 units of free electricity a month.
Bharatmala Pariyojana — Phase-I approved in 2017 for about 34,800 km, covering economic corridors, border and international connectivity roads and expressways; implemented mainly through NHAI.

Golden Quadrilateral (5,846 km) links Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata; the North-South corridor runs Srinagar to Kanyakumari and the East-West corridor Silchar to Porbandar — the two corridors cross at Jhansi.
Dedicated Freight Corridors — Eastern DFC (Ludhiana to Sonnagar) and Western DFC (Jawaharlal Nehru Port to Dadri); implemented by DFCCIL, incorporated in 2006.
The first Vande Bharat Express (Train 18) was flagged off on 15 February 2019 on the New Delhi-Varanasi route; Kavach is the indigenous train collision avoidance system.

Sagarmala (2015) is the port-led development programme of the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways; the Major Port Authorities Act, 2021 replaced the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963 and gave major ports greater autonomy.

UDAN (Ude Desh ka Aam Naagrik), the Regional Connectivity Scheme, was launched on 21 October 2016; the first flight was Shimla-Delhi in April 2017; airfares on RCS seats are capped and airlines get viability gap funding.

Telecommunications Act, 2023 replaced the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885 and the Indian Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933; TRAI was set up under the TRAI Act, 1997; BharatNet (originally NOFN, 2011) targets broadband to every gram panchayat; 5G services were launched on 1 October 2022.

PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan — launched 13 October 2021; a GIS-based digital platform built with BiSAG-N integrating 16 ministries; nodal department DPIIT; institutional structure of Network Planning Group and an Empowered Group of Secretaries.

Budget 2022-23 named the seven engines of PM Gati Shakti: roads, railways, airports, ports, mass transport, waterways and logistics infrastructure. The National Logistics Policy was released on 17 September 2022.
National Infrastructure Pipeline — task force chaired by Atanu Chakraborty; projects worth about Rs 111 lakh crore for FY2020-25; projects are showcased on the India Investment Grid.

PPP models — BOT (Toll) puts traffic risk on the concessionaire; BOT (Annuity) puts it on the authority; Hybrid Annuity Model has the government funding 40 per cent of project cost during construction and the rest as annuities; TOT monetises operational highways; EPC is not a PPP model. VGF is administered by the Department of Economic Affairs; the Kelkar Committee (2015) reviewed PPPs.

Balance of Payments — current account (merchandise trade plus invisibles: services, primary income and transfers) and capital account (FDI, FPI, ECBs, banking capital). The BoP always balances by construction; a deficit is financed by reserves.

Foreign exchange reserves comprise foreign currency assets, gold, SDRs and the reserve tranche position with the IMF; India's reserves crossed US$ 700 billion for the first time in September 2024 and India is among the top four reserve holders.
FDI implies a lasting interest, conventionally 10 per cent or more of equity; below that it is foreign portfolio investment. FPI is volatile 'hot money'; FDI brings technology and management.

Exchange rate regime — LERMS (dual rate) in 1992, unified in March 1993 into a managed float. India accepted current account convertibility under Article VIII of the IMF in August 1994; the Tarapore Committees of 1997 and 2006 examined capital account convertibility, which India has not adopted fully.

WTO — established 1 January 1995 under the Marrakesh Agreement (1994), successor to GATT 1947; headquarters Geneva; decisions by consensus; 166 members after Comoros and Timor-Leste joined at MC13 in Abu Dhabi (2024).

India's trade agreements — CEPA with the UAE (2022), ECTA with Australia (2022), TEPA with EFTA (signed 2024, in force 2025, with a US$ 100 billion investment commitment) and CETA with the United Kingdom (signed July 2025). India walked out of RCEP negotiations in November 2019.
Foreign Trade Policy 2023 came into effect on 1 April 2023 and is open-ended (no fixed end date); it is administered by the DGFT under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
Periodic Labour Force Survey — launched by NSO in April 2017; annual reports on usual status and quarterly (now monthly) urban bulletins on current weekly status.
PLFS 2023-24 (usual status, age 15 years and above): LFPR 60.1 per cent, Worker Population Ratio 58.2 per cent, unemployment rate 3.2 per cent; female LFPR rose from 37.0 to 41.7 per cent.
Work Participation Ratio (Worker Population Ratio) = number of employed persons divided by total population, expressed as a percentage; LFPR counts workers plus those seeking work.

About 90 per cent of India's workforce is in the unorganised or informal sector; the e-Shram portal (26 August 2021, Ministry of Labour and Employment) is the national database of unorganised workers, with over 30 crore registrations.

Skill ecosystem — Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship created 9 November 2014; NSDC incorporated in 2008 as a PPP with 49 per cent government and 51 per cent private equity; NSQF notified in December 2013 with 10 levels; National Skill Development Mission, PMKVY and the National Policy on Skill Development and Entrepreneurship were all launched on 15 July 2015 (World Youth Skills Day). NAPS (2016) promotes apprenticeship under the Apprentices Act, 1961.

Gig economy — the Code on Social Security, 2020 was the first Indian law to define 'gig worker' and 'platform worker'; NITI Aayog's 2022 report projected the gig workforce rising from about 77 lakh in 2020-21 to 2.35 crore by 2029-30.

questions.q: Which sector currently contributes the largest share to India's gross value added?
questions.exp: The services sector accounts for roughly 55 per cent of India's gross value added, far ahead of industry and agriculture, and is also the largest recipient of FDI.

questions.q: India's services exports in the financial year 2024-25 were of the order of
questions.exp: As per the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, services exports were US$ 383.51 billion in FY 2024-25, growing 12.45 per cent, while merchandise exports were US$ 437.42 billion, taking total exports to a record US$ 820.93 billion.

questions.q: The unbundling of electricity generation, transmission and distribution in India was mandated by the
questions.exp: The Electricity Act, 2003 consolidated earlier laws, delicensed generation, mandated open access and required unbundling of state electricity boards into separate generation, transmission and distribution entities.

questions.q: Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana (UDAY) was launched in 2015 for the financial and operational turnaround of
questions.exp: UDAY, launched in November 2015, allowed states to take over a large part of the debt of their distribution companies and tied further support to loss-reduction milestones. It was later succeeded by the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme, 2021.

questions.q: Under the 'Panchamrit' commitments announced at COP26, India's target for non-fossil fuel based energy capacity by 2030 is
questions.exp: India committed at Glasgow in 2021 to 500 GW of non-fossil fuel energy capacity by 2030, meeting 50 per cent of energy requirements from renewables and reaching net zero by 2070.

questions.q: Under the PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana launched in February 2024, the free electricity offered to a beneficiary household every month is up to
questions.exp: The scheme targets rooftop solar in one crore households with up to 300 units of free electricity a month, and is implemented by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.

questions.q: Phase-I of the Bharatmala Pariyojana, approved in 2017, envisaged the development of about
questions.exp: Bharatmala Phase-I covers about 34,800 km, comprising economic corridors, inter-corridor and feeder routes, border and international connectivity roads, coastal and port connectivity roads and expressways.

questions.q: The total length of the Golden Quadrilateral highway network connecting Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Kolkata is about
questions.exp: The Golden Quadrilateral is about 5,846 km long. The North-South corridor (Srinagar to Kanyakumari) is about 4,076 km and the East-West corridor (Silchar to Porbandar) about 3,640 km.

questions.q: The North-South and East-West corridors of the National Highways Development Project intersect at
questions.exp: The Srinagar-Kanyakumari and Silchar-Porbandar corridors cross at Jhansi in Uttar Pradesh, making it the junction of the two longest NHDP corridors.

questions.q: The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor runs between
questions.exp: The Western DFC connects Jawaharlal Nehru Port near Mumbai with Dadri in Uttar Pradesh, while the Eastern DFC runs from Ludhiana in Punjab to Sonnagar in Bihar. Both are executed by DFCCIL, set up in 2006.

questions.q: The first Vande Bharat Express in India was flagged off in February 2019 on which route?
questions.exp: Train 18, later named Vande Bharat Express, began commercial service on the New Delhi-Varanasi route on 15 February 2019. It is India's first indigenously designed semi-high-speed train set.

questions.q: The Sagarmala programme for port-led development is implemented by the
opts: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
questions.exp: Sagarmala, approved in 2015, rests on port modernisation, port connectivity, port-led industrialisation and coastal community development, and is run by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways.

questions.q: The Major Port Authorities Act, 2021 replaced which earlier legislation?
questions.exp: The 2021 Act replaced the Major Port Trusts Act, 1963, converting port trusts into port authorities with greater autonomy in tariff fixation and land use.

questions.q: The acronym UDAN in India's Regional Connectivity Scheme stands for
questions.exp: UDAN, launched on 21 October 2016 under the National Civil Aviation Policy 2016, caps fares on regional connectivity seats and gives airlines viability gap funding; the first UDAN flight was Shimla-Delhi in April 2017.

questions.q: The Telecommunications Act, 2023 replaced which of the following colonial-era legislations?
questions.exp: The Telecommunications Act, 2023 replaced the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885 and the Indian Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933. Sector regulation continues under TRAI, created by the TRAI Act, 1997.

questions.q: The PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan for multi-modal connectivity was launched on
questions.exp: PM Gati Shakti was launched on 13 October 2021 as a GIS-based digital platform integrating the infrastructure plans of 16 ministries, developed with BiSAG-N and coordinated by DPIIT.

questions.q: The National Infrastructure Pipeline announced by the Government of India envisaged investment of about
questions.exp: The task force under Atanu Chakraborty projected infrastructure investment of about Rs 111 lakh crore over FY2020-25 across more than 9,000 projects, showcased on the India Investment Grid.

questions.q: Under the Hybrid Annuity Model of highway development, the share of project cost provided by the government during the construction period is
questions.exp: In HAM the authority pays 40 per cent of the project cost in instalments during construction and the balance 60 per cent as annuities over the concession period; the concessionaire does not bear traffic or toll risk.

questions.q: An investment in the equity of an Indian company is conventionally treated as foreign direct investment rather than portfolio investment when the stake is at least
questions.exp: The 10 per cent threshold reflects a 'lasting interest' and management participation. Below it the flow is classified as foreign portfolio investment, which is far more volatile.

questions.q: The World Trade Organization came into existence on
questions.exp: The WTO was established on 1 January 1995 under the Marrakesh Agreement signed in April 1994, replacing GATT 1947. Its headquarters are at Geneva and it works by consensus.

questions.q: In the financial year 2024-25 India's largest trading partner was
questions.exp: The United States remained India's largest trading partner in FY 2024-25, while China continued to be the largest single source of India's imports.

questions.q: The e-Shram portal, the national database of unorganised workers, functions under the
opts: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
questions.exp: e-Shram was launched on 26 August 2021 by the Ministry of Labour and Employment; registration is Aadhaar-seeded and more than 30 crore unorganised workers have enrolled, of whom over half are women.

questions.q: The National Skills Qualifications Framework (NSQF) in India has how many levels?
questions.exp: The NSQF, notified in December 2013, organises qualifications in ten levels graded by learning outcomes, so that vocational and general education can be equated and credits transferred.

questions.q: The Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship was created in the year
questions.exp: The Ministry was carved out in November 2014 to coordinate skilling efforts spread across more than twenty ministries; the National Policy on Skill Development and Entrepreneurship followed in 2015.

questions.q: The Work Participation Ratio of a population is defined as
opts: the ratio of the labour force to the total population
the ratio of employed persons to the total population
the ratio of unemployed persons to the labour force
the ratio of employed persons to the labour force
questions.exp: The Worker Population Ratio or Work Participation Rate is the percentage of employed persons in the population. The labour force to population ratio is the LFPR, and unemployed as a share of the labour force is the unemployment rate.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan:
I. It was launched in October 2021.
II. It is a GIS-based digital platform integrating the infrastructure plans of sixteen ministries.
III. The nodal department for its implementation is the Ministry of Railways.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The nodal department is the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade, which houses the Logistics Division, the Network Planning Group and the secretariat of the Empowered Group of Secretaries chaired by the Cabinet Secretary.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Infrastructure Pipeline:
I. It was drawn up by a task force chaired by Atanu Chakraborty.
II. It covers the period 2020-21 to 2024-25.
III. Its projects are displayed on the India Investment Grid.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct: the NIP task force was headed by Atanu Chakraborty, then Secretary in the Department of Economic Affairs; the pipeline covers FY2020-25 with an outlay of about Rs 111 lakh crore, and projects are hosted on the India Investment Grid.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's balance of payments:
I. The current account records trade in goods and services along with primary income and transfers.
II. Foreign direct investment is recorded in the capital account.
III. The balance of payments as a whole can show a permanent surplus or deficit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The BoP always balances by construction because any current account gap is settled through capital flows and reserve movements; only individual accounts can be in surplus or deficit.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's foreign exchange reserves:
I. They include the reserve tranche position with the International Monetary Fund.
II. Special Drawing Rights form a component of the reserves.
III. Foreign currency assets form the smallest component.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Reserves comprise foreign currency assets, gold, SDRs and the reserve tranche position; foreign currency assets are by far the largest component. India's reserves crossed US$ 700 billion for the first time in September 2024.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements based on the Periodic Labour Force Survey Annual Report for 2023-24 (usual status, persons aged 15 years and above):
I. The labour force participation rate was 60.1 per cent.
II. The worker population ratio was 58.2 per cent.
III. The unemployment rate was 6.1 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: As per PLFS 2023-24, LFPR was 60.1 per cent, WPR 58.2 per cent and the unemployment rate 3.2 per cent for persons aged 15 years and above in usual status. Female LFPR rose to 41.7 per cent.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's skill development architecture:
I. The National Skill Development Mission and the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana were both launched on 15 July 2015.
II. The National Skill Development Corporation is a public sector undertaking wholly owned by the Government of India.
III. The National Apprenticeship Promotion Scheme operates under the Apprentices Act, 1961.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: NSDC is a public-private partnership incorporated in 2008, in which the Government holds 49 per cent and the private sector 51 per cent, so statement II is wrong. NSDM, PMKVY and the National Policy on Skill Development and Entrepreneurship were all launched on World Youth Skills Day, 15 July 2015.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the UDAN Regional Connectivity Scheme:
I. It was launched in 2016 under the National Civil Aviation Policy.
II. Selected airlines receive viability gap funding on regional connectivity seats.
III. The fare on regional connectivity seats is capped.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: UDAN, launched on 21 October 2016, combines a cap on airfares for a fixed share of seats with viability gap funding financed partly by a levy on major routes, in order to make small-airport routes commercially viable.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's trade agreements:
I. India signed a Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement with the United Arab Emirates in 2022.
II. India signed a Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement with the EFTA countries.
III. India is a founder member of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: India walked out of the RCEP negotiations in November 2019 and is not a member. The India-UAE CEPA came into force in May 2022 and the India-EFTA TEPA, signed in March 2024, carries a US$ 100 billion investment commitment.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (PPP model)   List-II (Feature)
A. BOT (Toll)   1. Government funds 40 per cent of cost during construction
B. BOT (Annuity)   2. Concessionaire recovers investment from user charges
C. Hybrid Annuity Model   3. Operational public asset leased out for a fixed period
D. Toll-Operate-Transfer   4. Authority pays fixed semi-annual payments, bearing traffic risk
questions.exp: In BOT (Toll) the concessionaire bears traffic risk and recovers cost through tolls; in BOT (Annuity) the authority pays fixed annuities; HAM splits the cost 40:60 between grant and annuity; TOT monetises an already operational asset.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Programme)   List-II (Sector)
A. Sagarmala   1. Regional air connectivity
B. Bharatmala   2. Rural broadband
C. UDAN   3. Ports
D. BharatNet   4. Highways
questions.exp: Sagarmala is the port-led development programme, Bharatmala the highways programme, UDAN the regional air connectivity scheme and BharatNet the optical fibre programme for gram panchayats.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Scheme or portal)   List-II (Ministry)
A. UDAY   1. Ministry of Labour and Employment
B. e-Shram   2. Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
C. PMKVY   3. Ministry of Power
D. Sagarmala   4. Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways
questions.exp: UDAY belongs to the Ministry of Power, e-Shram to Labour and Employment, PMKVY to Skill Development and Entrepreneurship, and Sagarmala to Ports, Shipping and Waterways.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Committee)   List-II (Subject)
A. Tarapore Committee   1. National Infrastructure Pipeline
B. Atanu Chakraborty Task Force   2. Revitalising public private partnerships
C. Vijay Kelkar Committee   3. Capital account convertibility
D. Rangarajan Committee   4. Measurement of poverty
questions.exp: The Tarapore Committees of 1997 and 2006 examined capital account convertibility, the Chakraborty task force framed the NIP, the Kelkar Committee of 2015 reviewed the PPP framework and the Rangarajan Committee re-examined poverty estimation.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Trade agreement)   List-II (Partner)
A. CEPA   1. United Kingdom
B. ECTA   2. EFTA countries
C. TEPA   3. United Arab Emirates
D. CETA   4. Australia
questions.exp: India signed the CEPA with the UAE in February 2022, the ECTA with Australia in 2022, the TEPA with the EFTA bloc in March 2024 and the CETA with the United Kingdom in July 2025.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a part of the current account of India's balance of payments?
questions.exp: External commercial borrowings are a capital account item. The current account records merchandise trade and invisibles, namely services, primary income and current transfers such as remittances.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT among the seven engines of growth identified for PM Gati Shakti in the Union Budget 2022-23?
questions.exp: The seven engines are roads, railways, airports, ports, mass transport, waterways and logistics infrastructure. Power transmission, though critical infrastructure, is not one of the named seven engines.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs relating to infrastructure and trade is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Foreign Trade Policy 2023 - effective from 1 April 2023
Sagarmala programme - Ministry of Commerce and Industry
questions.exp: Sagarmala is implemented by the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways, not the Ministry of Commerce and Industry. The Foreign Trade Policy 2023 is administered by DGFT under the Commerce Ministry and, unusually, has no end date.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about employment in India is NOT correct?
opts: About ninety per cent of the workforce is in the unorganised sector
The Periodic Labour Force Survey is conducted by the National Statistical Office
The Code on Social Security, 2020 defines gig and platform workers
The e-Shram portal registers only workers of the organised sector
questions.exp: e-Shram is a database of unorganised workers, including migrant, construction, gig and platform workers. It was launched in August 2021 and has more than 30 crore registrations.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a skill development or apprenticeship initiative of the Government of India?
questions.exp: PM-KUSUM is a solar energy scheme for farmers under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy. PMKVY, NAPS and SANKALP are all skilling programmes under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in correct chronological order of their launch or enactment:
I. Electricity Act
II. Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana
III. Bharatmala Pariyojana Phase-I
IV. PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan
questions.exp: Electricity Act 2003, UDAY 2015, Bharatmala Phase-I 2017 and PM Gati Shakti 2021 is the correct sequence.

questions.q:
Arrange the following events in correct chronological order:
I. Establishment of the World Trade Organization
II. India accepts current account convertibility under Article VIII of the IMF
III. India-UAE Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement comes into force
IV. India signs the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement with the United Kingdom
questions.exp: India accepted Article VIII obligations in August 1994, the WTO came into existence on 1 January 1995, the India-UAE CEPA entered into force in May 2022 and the India-UK CETA was signed in July 2025.

chapters.title: Macro Overview and the Rajasthan State Budget
factsheet: Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 was presented in the State Assembly in February 2026 by Deputy Chief Minister and Finance Minister Diya Kumari - the third budget of the present government.
Budget 2026-27: total expenditure Rs 6,10,956 crore; total receipts Rs 6,01,480 crore (2025-26 total budget size was Rs 5,37,068 crore).
Budget 2026-27: expenditure excluding debt repayment Rs 4,05,632 crore (+13%); receipts excluding borrowings Rs 3,26,140 crore (+14%).
Revenue deficit 2026-27 = Rs 24,314 crore = 1.1% of GSDP (2025-26 RE Rs 32,983 crore = 1.8%).
Outstanding liabilities (debt) projected at 36.8% of GSDP in 2026-27, down from 38% in 2025-26 (RE).
GSDP 2026-27 at current prices estimated at Rs 21,52,100 crore; 2025-26 RE Rs 18,75,413 crore (a 15% rise).
Capital outlay 2026-27 Rs 53,978 crore - a 37% jump, the sharpest rise among the major expenditure heads.
Revenue receipts 2026-27 Rs 3,25,740 crore: own tax revenue 50% (Rs 1,62,668 cr), share in central taxes 28% (Rs 90,446 cr), grants-in-aid 14% (Rs 44,191 cr), own non-tax 8% (Rs 28,435 cr).
Own tax heads 2026-27: State GST Rs 72,500 cr > Sales Tax/VAT Rs 33,800 cr > State Excise Rs 21,000 cr > Stamp Duty & Registration Rs 18,750 cr > Taxes on Vehicles Rs 11,000 cr.
Committed expenditure (salaries, pensions, interest) Rs 1,68,403 crore = 52% of revenue receipts.
Top sector allocations 2026-27: Education/Sports/Art & Culture Rs 68,989 cr > Energy Rs 42,752 cr > Rural Development Rs 32,948 cr > Health Rs 32,526 cr > Social Welfare & Nutrition Rs 26,495 cr.
Urban Development saw the largest percentage rise in 2026-27 (+58%), followed by Water Supply & Sanitation (+34%) and Energy (+24%).
Thematic budgets 2026-27: Agriculture Rs 1,19,408 cr, Gender Rs 74,312 cr, Child Rs 51,138 cr, Green Rs 33,475 cr.
Rajasthan was the FIRST Indian state to present a separate Agriculture Budget - from 2022-23, presented on 23 February 2022 by then Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot.

Budget 2026-27 headline schemes: Mukhyamantri Yuva Swarojgar Yojana (100% interest subsidy on loans up to Rs 10 lakh, Rs 1,000 crore), Lakhpati Didi loan limit raised Rs 1 lakh to Rs 1.5 lakh, Cooperative Dairy Infrastructure Development Fund doubled to Rs 2,000 crore, Rs 5,000 crore for tourism.
Budget 2025-26 announcements: Vivekanand Employment Assistance Fund Rs 500 crore, Gig and Unorganised Workers Development Fund Rs 350 crore, CM Amrut Aahar Yojana Rs 200 crore.
Rajasthan Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2005 - Act No. 7 of 2005; the 2011 amendment fixed zero revenue deficit from 2011-12 and a fiscal deficit of 3% of GSDP.

FRBM Second Amendment (2011) laid a debt-to-GSDP glide path: 39.3% (2011-12), 38.3%, 37.3%, 36.5% (2014-15); the 2021 amendment allowed an extra 0.50% of GSDP borrowing for 2021-22 to 2024-25 linked to power-sector reform.
Rajasthan Economic Review 2025-26: GSDP about Rs 18.75 lakh crore; growth 8.66% at constant prices and 10.24% at current prices.
Rajasthan Economic Review 2025-26 per capita income: Rs 2,02,349 at current prices and Rs 1,03,189 at constant prices; per capita GSDP for 2023-24 was Rs 1,87,454.
GSVA composition (2025-26): Services 47.7% > Industry 26.5% > Agriculture & allied 25.7% - services is the largest, agriculture the smallest of the three.
Rajasthan contributes roughly 5% of India's GDP; it is India's largest state by area and the 8th most populous (Census 2011).

Rajasthan's state Wholesale Price Index has base year 1999-2000 = 100, effective 1 January 2005 (replacing 1952-53 = 100), covering 154 commodities - 75 primary articles, 69 manufactured products, 10 fuel & power.
State WPI group weights: Manufactured Products 49.853, Primary Articles 33.894, Fuel-Power-Light-Lubricants 16.253; compiled by the Directorate of Economics & Statistics, Rajasthan.
All-India WPI base year revised from 2011-12 to 2022-23, effective 15 June 2026; the item basket rose from 697 to 957.
CPI-IW base 2016 = 100 (Labour Bureau, Shimla) with Rajasthan centres at Jaipur, Alwar and Bhilwara; CPI-AL/RL base 1986-87 = 100; general CPI (rural/urban/combined) base 2012 = 100.

State Finance Commissions are constituted under Articles 243-I (panchayats) and 243-Y (municipalities): Rajasthan's 1st SFC 1994 (Krishna Kumar Goyal), 2nd Hira Lal Devpura, 3rd Manik Chand Surana, 4th Dr. B.D. Kalla, 5th Dr. Jyoti Kiran (award 2015-20), 6th Pradhyuman Singh (constituted 12 April 2021, award 2020-25).
Census 2011 Rajasthan: population 6.85 crore, decadal growth 21.31%, density 200 per sq km, sex ratio 928, literacy 66.11%, urban population 24.89%.

questions.q: The total size (total expenditure) of the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 is approximately:
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 has a total expenditure of about Rs 6,10,956 crore against Rs 5,37,068 crore in 2025-26. Rs 4,05,632 crore is expenditure excluding debt repayment. As of the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 documents (data as of September 2026).

questions.q: As per the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27, the fiscal deficit is estimated at what percentage of GSDP?
questions.exp: Fiscal deficit for 2026-27 is Rs 79,493 crore, i.e. 3.7% of GSDP, against 3.9% in the 2025-26 revised estimates and 4.3% in the 2025-26 budget estimates. As of the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 documents (data as of September 2026).

questions.q: The revenue deficit projected in the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 is:
questions.exp: Revenue deficit for 2026-27 is Rs 24,314 crore, or 1.1% of GSDP, down 26% from the 2025-26 revised figure of Rs 32,983 crore. Rs 79,493 crore is the fiscal deficit. As of the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 documents (data as of September 2026).

questions.q: As per the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27, the state's GSDP at current prices is estimated at about:
questions.exp: GSDP for 2026-27 is projected at Rs 21,52,100 crore at current prices, about 15% higher than the 2025-26 revised estimate of Rs 18,75,413 crore. As of the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 documents (data as of September 2026).

questions.q: The capital outlay provided in the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 is approximately:
questions.exp: Capital outlay in 2026-27 is Rs 53,978 crore, a rise of about 37% over the 2025-26 revised estimate - the sharpest increase among the major expenditure categories. As of the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 documents (data as of September 2026).

questions.q: In the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27, the largest single component of the state's revenue receipts is:
questions.exp: Own tax revenue of Rs 1,62,668 crore makes up 50% of the Rs 3,25,740 crore revenue receipts; share in central taxes is 28%, grants-in-aid 14% and own non-tax revenue 8%. As of the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 documents (data as of September 2026).

questions.q: Rajasthan's share in central taxes in the Budget 2026-27 is about what proportion of its revenue receipts?
questions.exp: Share in central taxes is Rs 90,446 crore, roughly 28% of revenue receipts. Grants-in-aid account for about 14% and own non-tax revenue about 8%. As of the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 documents (data as of September 2026).

questions.q: Which of the following yields the largest amount of own tax revenue to Rajasthan in 2026-27?
questions.exp: State GST is budgeted at Rs 72,500 crore in 2026-27, well ahead of Sales Tax/VAT (Rs 33,800 crore), State Excise (Rs 21,000 crore), stamp duty and registration (Rs 18,750 crore) and vehicle taxes (Rs 11,000 crore). As of the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 documents (data as of September 2026).

questions.q: Which sector received the largest allocation in the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27?
questions.exp: Education (with sports, art and culture) received Rs 68,989 crore, ahead of Energy (Rs 42,752 crore), Rural Development (Rs 32,948 crore) and Health (Rs 32,526 crore). As of the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 documents (data as of September 2026).

questions.q: As per the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27, the state's outstanding liabilities (debt) are projected at about what percentage of GSDP?
questions.exp: Outstanding liabilities are projected at 36.8% of GSDP for 2026-27, down from about 38% in the 2025-26 revised estimates. As of the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 documents (data as of September 2026).

questions.q: The size of Rajasthan's separate Agriculture Budget for 2026-27 is approximately:
questions.exp: The Agriculture Budget 2026-27 is about Rs 1,19,408 crore. The figure is far larger than the departmental head 'Agriculture and Allied Activities' (Rs 18,212 crore) because the agriculture budget also pools irrigation, farm power subsidy, cooperatives and animal husbandry. As of the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 documents (data as of September 2026).

questions.q: Rajasthan became the first state in India to present a separate Agriculture Budget in the financial year:
questions.exp: The first separate Agriculture Budget of Rajasthan - and of any Indian state - was presented on 23 February 2022 for 2022-23 by the then Chief Minister Ashok Gehlot, and it has been presented every year since.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 was presented in the State Legislative Assembly by:
opts: The Deputy Chief Minister who holds the Finance portfolio
The Minister of State for Planning
questions.exp: Diya Kumari, Deputy Chief Minister holding the Finance portfolio, presented the Budget 2026-27 - the third budget of the present government. As of the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 documents (data as of September 2026).

questions.q: Committed expenditure (salaries, pensions and interest payments) in the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 accounts for approximately what share of revenue receipts?
questions.exp: Committed expenditure of Rs 1,68,403 crore is about 52% of revenue receipts in 2026-27, leaving limited fiscal space for development spending. As of the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 documents (data as of September 2026).

questions.q: The Rajasthan Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act was enacted in the year:
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act, 2005 (Act No. 7 of 2005) is the state's fiscal rule statute; it was amended in 2011 and again in 2021.

questions.q: Under the Rajasthan FRBM (Amendment) Act, 2011, the fiscal deficit was to be brought down to what percentage of GSDP?
questions.exp: The 2011 amendment required Rajasthan to achieve a fiscal deficit of 3% of GSDP and a zero revenue deficit from the financial year 2011-12 onwards.

questions.q: The Rajasthan FRBM (Amendment) Act, 2011 required the state to achieve a zero revenue deficit from the financial year:
questions.exp: The amendment mandated zero revenue deficit from 2011-12 and its maintenance or conversion into a revenue surplus thereafter.

questions.q: The 2021 amendment to the Rajasthan FRBM Act permitted additional borrowing of what proportion of GSDP, linked to power-sector performance?
questions.exp: The 2021 amendment allowed additional borrowing of 0.50% of GSDP for the years 2021-22 to 2024-25, conditional on meeting power-sector reform criteria - a window created following the Fifteenth Finance Commission's recommendations.

questions.q: State Finance Commissions for panchayati raj institutions are constituted under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.exp: Article 243-I requires the Governor to constitute a State Finance Commission every five years for panchayats; Article 243-Y extends its scope to municipalities. Article 280 relates to the (central) Finance Commission.

questions.q: Who was the chairperson of the Sixth State Finance Commission of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The Sixth State Finance Commission of Rajasthan, constituted on 12 April 2021 with an award period of 2020-25, was chaired by Pradhyuman Singh. Dr. Jyoti Kiran chaired the Fifth SFC.

questions.q: Dr. Jyoti Kiran was the chairperson of which State Finance Commission of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Dr. Jyoti Kiran chaired the Fifth State Finance Commission of Rajasthan (constituted 2014) whose award period was April 2015 to March 2020.

questions.q: The First State Finance Commission of Rajasthan was constituted in the year:
questions.exp: Rajasthan's First State Finance Commission was constituted in 1994 under the chairmanship of Krishna Kumar Goyal; its award period ran from April 1995 to March 2000.

questions.q: The base year of Rajasthan's state Wholesale Price Index is:
questions.exp: Rajasthan's state WPI uses base 1999-2000 = 100, effective from 1 January 2005, replacing the earlier 1952-53 = 100 series. It is compiled by the Directorate of Economics and Statistics.

questions.q: How many commodities are covered in Rajasthan's state Wholesale Price Index series?
questions.exp: The state WPI covers 154 commodities - 75 from primary articles, 69 from manufactured products and 10 from fuel and power.

questions.q: In Rajasthan's state Wholesale Price Index, which group carries the highest weight?
questions.exp: Manufactured Products carry the highest weight (49.853), followed by Primary Articles (33.894) and Fuel, Power, Light and Lubricants (16.253).

questions.q: The base year of the all-India Wholesale Price Index has been revised to:
questions.exp: The all-India WPI base year was revised from 2011-12 to 2022-23, effective 15 June 2026, and the item basket was expanded from 697 to 957 items.

questions.q: The Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW) currently uses which base year?
questions.exp: CPI-IW was shifted to base 2016 = 100 from September 2020 by the Labour Bureau, Shimla. Its centres in Rajasthan are Jaipur, Alwar and Bhilwara.

questions.q: As per the Rajasthan Economic Review 2025-26, the per capita income of Rajasthan at current prices is approximately:
questions.exp: The Economic Review 2025-26 puts per capita income at Rs 2,02,349 at current prices and Rs 1,03,189 at constant prices. Per capita GSDP for 2023-24 was Rs 1,87,454.

questions.q: As per the Rajasthan Economic Review 2025-26, the share of the services sector in the state's Gross State Value Added is approximately:
questions.exp: Services contribute about 47.7% of Rajasthan's GSVA, industry 26.5% and agriculture and allied activities 25.7%.

questions.q: As per the Rajasthan Economic Review 2025-26, the share of agriculture and allied activities in the state's GSVA is about:
questions.exp: Agriculture and allied activities account for roughly 25.7% of Rajasthan's GSVA - a much higher share than the all-India average, and the smallest of the state's three broad sectors.

questions.q: As per the Rajasthan Economic Review 2025-26, the growth rate of the state's GSDP at constant prices is about:
questions.exp: GSDP growth is estimated at 8.66% at constant prices and 10.24% at current prices in the Economic Review 2025-26.

questions.q: Rajasthan's approximate share in India's Gross Domestic Product is:
questions.exp: Rajasthan accounts for roughly 5% of India's GDP, though it holds 10.4% of the country's area and about 5.7% of its population.

questions.q: As per Census 2011, Rajasthan's rank among Indian states by population is:
questions.exp: Rajasthan was the eighth most populous state in Census 2011 with 6.85 crore people, even though it is the largest state by area.

questions.q:

questions.exp: Fiscal deficit is 3.7% and revenue deficit 1.1% of GSDP in 2026-27. Outstanding liabilities are projected to FALL to about 36.8% of GSDP, so statement III is wrong. As of the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 documents (data as of September 2026).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Rajasthan's separate Agriculture Budget:
I. Rajasthan was the first state in India to present a separate agriculture budget.
II. It was first presented for the financial year 2022-23.
III. It has since been discontinued.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Rajasthan pioneered the separate agriculture budget in 2022-23 and has continued the practice every year, including 2026-27 (about Rs 1.19 lakh crore). Statement III is therefore incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Rajasthan FRBM Act:
I. It was enacted in 2005.
II. Its 2011 amendment set a fiscal deficit target of 3 per cent of GSDP.
III. Its 2011 second amendment prescribed a declining debt-to-GSDP path ending at 36.5 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Rajasthan FRBM Act, 2005 was amended in 2011 to fix a 3% fiscal deficit and zero revenue deficit from 2011-12, and a second 2011 amendment laid a debt-GSDP glide path of 39.3% to 36.5% between 2011-12 and 2014-15.

questions.q:

questions.exp: Services 47.7% > Industry 26.5% > Agriculture and allied 25.7%. Statement III is wrong because agriculture's share is well above 15%.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Rajasthan's state Wholesale Price Index:

questions.exp: The state WPI (base 1999-2000 = 100) covers 154 commodities and is compiled by the Directorate of Economics and Statistics, Rajasthan - not the RBI.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about State Finance Commissions in Rajasthan:

questions.exp: All three statements are correct. Under Article 243-I the Governor constitutes an SFC at the expiry of every fifth year; Rajasthan's Sixth SFC, chaired by Pradhyuman Singh, covered 2020-25.

questions.exp: Own tax revenue is about 50% of revenue receipts. Share in central taxes (Rs 90,446 crore, 28%) is far larger than grants-in-aid (Rs 44,191 crore, 14%), so statement II is wrong. As of the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 documents (data as of September 2026).

questions.q:

II. Rajasthan contributes about 5 per cent of India's GDP.

questions.exp: All three are correct. Rajasthan holds 10.41% of India's area, contributes roughly 5% of national GDP and ranked eighth in population in Census 2011.
