chapters.title: Agriculture and Allied Sector of Rajasthan
factsheet: Agriculture and allied activities contribute about 25.7% of Rajasthan's GSVA (Rajasthan Economic Review 2025-26) and support the largest share of the state's workforce.
Foodgrain production in 2025-26 is estimated at 283.98 lakh tonnes (Rajasthan Economic Review 2025-26).
Rajasthan ranks FIRST in India in bajra (about 39% of national output), mustard/rapeseed (about 47%), guar or cluster bean (about 87%) and total oilseeds (about 22%).
Rajasthan is also India's leading producer of moth bean, isabgol, coriander, fenugreek (methi), henna (mehndi) and taramira.
Leading districts: bajra - Alwar (Barmer has the largest area under bajra); mustard - Sri Ganganagar; guar - Hanumangarh; maize - Chittorgarh; jowar - Ajmer; cotton - Hanumangarh.
Sojat in Pali district is India's henna (mehndi) capital; Ramganj Mandi in Kota district is Asia's largest coriander market.
Crop-place pairs: Mathania (Jodhpur) red chilli, Nagauri methi, Jhalawar oranges, Chittorgarh and Pratapgarh opium, Bharatpur mustard belt.
Rajasthan ranks second in India in groundnut (after Gujarat) and third in soybean (after Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra).
Wool: Rajasthan is India's largest producer with 47.85% of national output (Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics 2025, reference year 2024-25); India's total wool output was 34.57 million kg.
Milk: Rajasthan ranks SECOND in India with 14.82% of output, behind Uttar Pradesh (15.66%); India's total milk production was 247.87 million tonnes (BAHS 2025).
Rajasthan has India's largest camel population; the camel was declared the state animal (domestic category) in 2014.
Wells and tube-wells are the largest source of irrigation in Rajasthan; the Indira Gandhi Nahar Pariyojana is the largest canal system.
Improved bajra varieties: Raj-171, RHB-30, RCB-2, RCB-911, Pusa Composite 383, Moti, HB-3.
Improved maize varieties: Mahi Kanchan, Mahi Dhawal, Navjot, Megha, Moti Composite, Ganga-11.
CAZRI - Central Arid Zone Research Institute, Jodhpur, established 1959, the premier desert-agriculture institute.
CSWRI - Central Sheep and Wool Research Institute, Avikanagar (Malpura tehsil, Tonk district), established 1962.
National Research Centre on Camel, Bikaner (1984); Central Institute for Arid Horticulture (CIAH), Bikaner (1993); National Research Centre on Seed Spices, Tabiji, Ajmer (2000).
Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research (DRMR), Bharatpur - started in 1993 as the National Research Centre on Rapeseed-Mustard and upgraded to a Directorate in 2009.

Agricultural universities: SKRAU Bikaner (1987), MPUAT Udaipur (1999), and the 2013 trio - Agriculture University Jodhpur, Agriculture University Kota and Sri Karan Narendra Agriculture University, Jobner (Jaipur).
Rajasthan presented India's first separate Agriculture Budget in 2022-23; the 2026-27 agriculture budget is about Rs 1.19 lakh crore.
Rajasthan Kisan Kalyan Kosh was created in the 2020-21 budget with a corpus of Rs 1,000 crore.
Mukhyamantri Kisan Mitra Urja Yojana (2021) gives metered agricultural consumers an electricity-bill subsidy of up to Rs 1,000 a month, subject to a maximum of Rs 12,000 a year.
Rajasthan Agro-Processing, Agri-Business and Agri-Export Promotion Policy was notified in 2019.
Rajasthan Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1961 governs the mandi system; the Rajasthan State Agricultural Marketing Board (RSAMB) was constituted in 1974.

RCDF - Rajasthan Cooperative Dairy Federation (1977) markets milk and milk products under the SARAS brand; the Budget 2026-27 doubled the Cooperative Dairy Infrastructure Development Fund to Rs 2,000 crore.
Mukhyamantri Krishak Sathi Yojana (2019) compensates farmers and mandi workers for accidental death or injury during agricultural work.
Budget 2026-27 agriculture targets: 50,000 solar pumps under PM-KUSUM and micro-irrigation coverage of about 3 lakh hectares.
The average operational landholding in Rajasthan is about 2.73 hectares - among the largest in India, reflecting extensive dryland farming.

questions.q: Rajasthan's rank in India in the production of bajra (pearl millet) is:
questions.exp: Rajasthan is India's largest producer of bajra, contributing roughly 39% of national output. Alwar is the leading producing district while Barmer has the largest area under the crop.

questions.q: Which district of Rajasthan is the leading producer of bajra?
questions.exp: Alwar leads in bajra production, followed by Jaipur. Barmer, however, has the largest area sown under bajra - area and production leadership differ because of yield differences.

questions.q: Rajasthan contributes approximately what share of India's total mustard (rapeseed-mustard) production?
questions.exp: Rajasthan produces roughly 46-47% of India's mustard, making it the country's largest producer. Sri Ganganagar is the leading district, followed by Alwar.

questions.q: Which district of Rajasthan leads in the production of mustard?
questions.exp: Sri Ganganagar is the leading mustard-producing district of Rajasthan, followed by Alwar. Bharatpur, though a major mustard belt, is better known as the seat of the Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research.

questions.q: Rajasthan accounts for roughly what proportion of India's guar (cluster bean) production?
questions.exp: Rajasthan produces close to 87-88% of India's guar, and guar gum from Rajasthan is a major agricultural export used by the oil-drilling industry. Hanumangarh is the leading producing district.

questions.q: Which district of Rajasthan is the leading producer of guar?
questions.exp: Hanumangarh leads in guar production, followed by Bikaner. Guar is a hardy kharif legume suited to the state's arid north-west.

questions.q: Rajasthan's rank in India in the production of total oilseeds is:
questions.exp: Rajasthan is India's largest oilseed producing state, accounting for about 22% of national output, driven mainly by mustard, groundnut, soybean and taramira.

questions.q: As per the Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics 2025, Rajasthan's share in India's wool production is approximately:
questions.exp: Rajasthan is India's largest wool producer with about 47.85% of national output (reference year 2024-25). India's total wool production was 34.57 million kg.

questions.q: As per the Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics 2025, Rajasthan's rank in India in milk production is:
questions.exp: Rajasthan ranks second with about 14.82% of national milk output, behind Uttar Pradesh (15.66%) and ahead of Madhya Pradesh. India's total milk production was 247.87 million tonnes.

questions.q: Which place in Rajasthan is known as India's henna (mehndi) capital?
questions.exp: Sojat in Pali district is the country's principal henna growing and processing centre, and Sojat mehndi has been granted a Geographical Indication.

questions.q: Ramganj Mandi, described as Asia's largest market for its commodity, deals principally in:
questions.exp: Ramganj Mandi in Kota district is Asia's largest coriander (dhania) market. Rajasthan is India's leading coriander producer.

questions.q: India's largest producer of isabgol (psyllium husk) is:
questions.exp: Rajasthan is India's largest isabgol producer, the crop being concentrated in the western districts such as Jalore, Barmer and Nagaur. Isabgol is a major medicinal export crop.

questions.q: Rajasthan's rank in India in the production of groundnut is:
questions.exp: Rajasthan ranks second in groundnut production after Gujarat. Bikaner and the Sri Ganganagar-Hanumangarh belt are the main producing areas.

questions.q: Rajasthan's rank in India in the production of soybean is:
questions.exp: Rajasthan is the third largest soybean producer after Madhya Pradesh and Maharashtra; the crop is concentrated in the Hadoti region - Kota, Baran, Jhalawar and Bundi.

questions.q: Which district of Rajasthan leads in the production of maize?
questions.exp: Chittorgarh is the leading maize producing district, followed by Bhilwara. Maize is grown mainly in the southern and south-eastern districts.

questions.q: Which of the following is a variety of maize developed for Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Mahi Kanchan is a maize variety; Raj-171, RCB-2 and RHB-30 are bajra varieties.

questions.q: Which one of the following is an improved variety of bajra?
questions.exp: RHB-30 is a bajra hybrid. Mahi Dhawal, Navjot and Ganga-11 are maize varieties.

questions.q: The Central Arid Zone Research Institute (CAZRI) is located at:
questions.exp: CAZRI, established in 1959, is at Jodhpur and is India's premier institute for desert and dryland agriculture research.

questions.q: The Central Sheep and Wool Research Institute is situated at:
questions.exp: The Central Sheep and Wool Research Institute (CSWRI), established in 1962, is at Avikanagar in Malpura tehsil of Tonk district.

questions.q: The National Research Centre on Camel is located in which district of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The National Research Centre on Camel, set up in 1984, is at Jorbeer in Bikaner. Rajasthan has India's largest camel population and the camel was declared the state animal in 2014.

questions.q: The National Research Centre on Seed Spices is located at:
questions.exp: The National Research Centre on Seed Spices at Tabiji, Ajmer, was established in 2000 and works on cumin, coriander, fenugreek and fennel.

questions.q: The Central Institute for Arid Horticulture is located at:
questions.exp: The Central Institute for Arid Horticulture (CIAH) at Bichhwal, Bikaner, was set up in 1993 for research on ber, khejri, bael, aonla and other arid fruits.

questions.q: The Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research of the ICAR is located at:
questions.exp: The Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research (DRMR) is at Bharatpur; it began in 1993 as the National Research Centre on Rapeseed-Mustard and was upgraded to a Directorate in 2009.

questions.q: Maharana Pratap University of Agriculture and Technology is located at:
questions.exp: Maharana Pratap University of Agriculture and Technology (MPUAT) was established at Udaipur in 1999. Swami Keshwanand Rajasthan Agricultural University (1987) is at Bikaner.

questions.q: Swami Keshwanand Rajasthan Agricultural University is located at:
questions.exp: Swami Keshwanand Rajasthan Agricultural University, established in 1987, is at Bikaner. Sri Karan Narendra Agriculture University is at Jobner in Jaipur district.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Cooperative Dairy Federation markets its milk and milk products under which brand name?
questions.exp: RCDF, established in 1977, markets under the SARAS brand. Amul belongs to Gujarat, Verka to Punjab and Vita to Haryana.

questions.q: Under the Mukhyamantri Kisan Mitra Urja Yojana, the maximum annual electricity-bill subsidy available to an eligible farmer is:
questions.exp: The scheme, launched in 2021, gives metered agricultural consumers a grant of up to Rs 1,000 per month subject to a ceiling of Rs 12,000 per year.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Kisan Kalyan Kosh was set up with an initial corpus of:
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Kisan Kalyan Kosh was announced in the 2020-21 state budget with a corpus of Rs 1,000 crore to fund farmer welfare interventions.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Agro-Processing, Agri-Business and Agri-Export Promotion Policy was notified in the year:
questions.exp: The policy was notified in 2019 to promote food processing units, agri-export zones and value addition in the state's farm produce.

questions.q: The Rajasthan State Agricultural Marketing Board, which regulates the state's mandi system, was constituted in:
questions.exp: The Rajasthan State Agricultural Marketing Board (RSAMB) was constituted in 1974 under the Rajasthan Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1961.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Rajasthan's position in Indian agriculture:
I. Rajasthan is the largest producer of bajra in India.
II. Rajasthan is the largest producer of mustard in India.
III. Rajasthan is the largest producer of guar in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Rajasthan leads India in all three - bajra (about 39%), mustard (about 47%) and guar (about 87% of national output).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about livestock production in Rajasthan:
I. Rajasthan is India's largest producer of wool.
II. Rajasthan is India's largest producer of milk.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: As per the Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics 2025, Rajasthan leads in wool (47.85%) but is second in milk (14.82%) behind Uttar Pradesh (15.66%).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about agricultural research institutions in Rajasthan:
I. The National Research Centre on Camel is at Bikaner.
II. The National Research Centre on Seed Spices is at Ajmer.
III. The Central Institute for Arid Horticulture is at Jodhpur.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Central Institute for Arid Horticulture is at Bichhwal in Bikaner, not Jodhpur; Jodhpur hosts CAZRI. Statements I and II are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the separate Agriculture Budget of Rajasthan:
I. It was first presented in 2022-23.
II. Rajasthan was the first state in India to adopt the practice.
III. The Agriculture Budget 2026-27 is of the order of Rs 1.19 lakh crore.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The agriculture budget pools spending on farming, irrigation, farm power subsidy, cooperatives and animal husbandry, which is why it is far larger than the departmental agriculture head. As of the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 documents (data as of September 2026).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Mukhyamantri Kisan Mitra Urja Yojana:
I. It provides a subsidy on agricultural electricity bills.
II. The maximum benefit is Rs 12,000 per year.
III. It was launched in 2021.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct - metered agricultural consumers receive up to Rs 1,000 a month, capped at Rs 12,000 a year, under this 2021 scheme.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about irrigation in Rajasthan:
I. Wells and tube-wells are the largest source of irrigation.
II. The Indira Gandhi Nahar Pariyojana is the state's largest canal system.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Both are correct. Groundwater through wells and tube-wells irrigates the largest share of Rajasthan's net irrigated area, while the IGNP is the largest surface irrigation system.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about crop varieties used in Rajasthan:
I. RCB-2 is a variety of bajra.
II. Mahi Dhawal is a variety of maize.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Both are correct. RCB-2 and RCB-911 are bajra varieties, while Mahi Dhawal and Mahi Kanchan are maize varieties developed for Rajasthan's conditions.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Rajasthan's agriculture sector:
I. Agriculture and allied activities account for roughly one-fourth of the state's GSVA.
II. The average operational landholding in Rajasthan is among the largest in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Both are correct. Agriculture and allied activities contributed about 25.7% of GSVA in 2025-26, and the average holding of about 2.73 hectares is among the largest in the country because of extensive dryland farming.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the marketing of agricultural produce in Rajasthan:
I. The mandi system operates under the Rajasthan Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1961.
II. The Rajasthan State Agricultural Marketing Board was constituted in 1974.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Both are correct. The 1961 Act provides the legal framework for regulated markets and the Board, set up in 1974, develops and supervises mandi infrastructure.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about agriculture proposals in the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27:
I. About 50,000 solar pumps are targeted under PM-KUSUM.
II. The Cooperative Dairy Infrastructure Development Fund was doubled to Rs 2,000 crore.
III. Micro-irrigation is to be extended to about 3 lakh hectares.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are announcements of the Budget 2026-27, alongside a 100% interest waiver for colonisation-area farmers clearing outstanding dues. As of the Rajasthan Budget 2026-27 documents (data as of September 2026).

questions.exp: Rajasthan is second in milk production, behind Uttar Pradesh (Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics 2025). It does lead in bajra, guar and wool.
