chapters.title: Industry, MSME and Industrial Policy of Rajasthan
factsheet: RIICO (Rajasthan State Industrial Development and Investment Corporation) - incorporated 28 March 1969 as RSIMDC; renamed RIICO on 1 January 1980 when the mineral wing was hived off as RSMML; head office Udyog Bhawan, Tilak Marg, Jaipur.
RIICO has developed more than 400 industrial areas (415 as reported on the state investment portal) over about 93,000 acres; it is the nodal agency for industrial land in Rajasthan.

RSMML (Rajasthan State Mines and Minerals Ltd) - headquarters Udaipur; RFC (Rajasthan Financial Corporation) - set up 1955 under the State Financial Corporations Act 1951, head office Jaipur; RAJSICO markets handicrafts and small-industry products.

RIICO specialised parks: MedTech Medical Device Park - Boranada (Jodhpur); Sports Goods and Toys Zone - Khushkhera (Bhiwadi region); Integrated Resource Recovery Park - Tholai, Jamwa Ramgarh (Jaipur); Rajasthan Petro Zone - Balotra (about 700 hectares); Fintech Park - Jaipur.

Japanese Zone - Neemrana (erstwhile Alwar district), India's first country-specific investment zone; Rajasthan's second Japanese zone and its Korean investment zone are at Ghiloth (erstwhile Alwar district).

RAS Pre 2024 asked which park RIICO has NOT developed - answer: Agro Food Park, Udaipur (MedTech Boranada, Sports Goods and Toys Khushkhera and Integrated Resource Recovery Jamwa Ramgarh are all RIICO parks).
Mahindra World City, Jaipur - multi-product SEZ, a joint venture of the Mahindra Group with RIICO; Gem and Jewellery SEZ - Sitapura, Jaipur.
DMIC in Rajasthan: the largest share of the corridor alignment (about 39%) falls in the state; two nodes - Khushkhera-Bhiwadi-Neemrana (KBNIA) and Jodhpur-Pali-Marwar (JPMIA).

HPCL Rajasthan Refinery Ltd (HRRL), Pachpadra (Balotra, erstwhile Barmer district) - JV of HPCL (74%) and Government of Rajasthan (26%), refining capacity 9 MMTPA; Rajasthan Petro Zone at Balotra supports its downstream industry.
Textiles: Bhilwara - 'Textile City', largest centre of polyester/suiting fabric; Pali and Balotra - dyeing and printing; Sanganer and Bagru - hand block printing; Kaithun (Kota) - Kota Doria (GI).

Cement: first plant of Rajasthan at Lakheri (Bundi), 1915; J.K. Cement - Nimbahera (Chittorgarh); Birla Cement Works - Chittorgarh; Shree Cement - Beawar; Binani Cement and J.K. Lakshmi Cement - Pindwara/Jaykaypuram (Sirohi); Mangalam Cement - Morak (Kota).

Marble and stone: Makrana (erstwhile Nagaur, now Didwana-Kuchaman) - white marble of the Taj Mahal; Kishangarh (Ajmer) - largest marble market/processing hub; Bhainslana (Jaipur) - black marble; Dholpur and Jodhpur - sandstone.

Glass industry - Dholpur (silica sand base). Salt - Sambhar (Sambhar Salts Ltd, a JV of Hindustan Salts Ltd and the State), Didwana (Rajasthan State Chemical Works), Pachpadra, Lunkaransar; Rajasthan is India's third largest salt producer after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.

Fertiliser: Chambal Fertilisers and Chemicals - Gadepan (Kota); Shriram Fertilisers and Chemicals - Kota. Sugar: The Ganganagar Sugar Mills (Sri Karanpur, Sriganganagar) in the state sector and Keshoraipatan Sahakari Sugar Mill (Bundi) in the co-operative sector.

Zinc and lead: Hindustan Zinc Ltd (registered office Udaipur) - smelters at Chanderiya (Chittorgarh, one of the world's largest single-location zinc-lead smelting complexes), Debari (Udaipur) and Dariba (Rajsamand); Zawar (Udaipur) - among India's oldest zinc mines.
Wool: Bikaner is the state's principal wool trading and processing centre; Central Wool Development Board - Jodhpur; Central Sheep and Wool Research Institute - Avikanagar (Tonk).

Gems and jewellery: Jaipur is a world centre for cutting and polishing coloured gemstones, especially emerald. Leather: RIICO leather complex at Manpura-Macheri (Bassi, Jaipur). Wooden handicraft exports: Jodhpur.
Handicrafts: Thewa - Pratapgarh; blue pottery - Jaipur; Molela terracotta - Rajsamand; Usta/Munawwat work - Bikaner; Namda - Tonk; handmade paper - Sanganer.

Rajasthan MSME (Facilitation of Establishment and Operation) Act, 2019 - a new enterprise may start on a mere declaration of intent and an acknowledgement certificate, exempt from approvals/inspections/NOCs for three years; the 2023 amendment raised the period to five years.
Raj Udyog Mitra portal issues the acknowledgement certificate under the MSME Act; Udyam Registration Portal (Ministry of MSME) is the all-India MSME registration platform.

RIPS 2024 (Rajasthan Investment Promotion Scheme) - notified 8 October 2024, replacing RIPS-2019; offers SGST reimbursement, asset creation/investment subsidy, employment generation subsidy and exemption from stamp duty, land conversion charges and electricity duty.

Policy package announced in 2024 ahead of the summit: Rajasthan Industrial Development Policy, RIPS-2024, Rajasthan MSME Policy 2024, One District One Product (ODOP) Policy 2024 and Export Promotion Policy 2024.

Rajasthan M-Sand Policy 2024 - announced 30 December 2024; target to raise manufactured sand output to 30 million tonnes by 2028-29; incentives include stamp duty exemption and seven-year electricity duty exemption, with assured government procurement of M-sand.

Rising Rajasthan Global Investment Summit - held 9-11 December 2024 at JECC, Sitapura, Jaipur; inaugurated by the Prime Minister; MoUs of the order of about Rs 35 lakh crore reported; Pravasi Rajasthani Conclave and MSME Conclave were part of it.

Bureau of Investment Promotion (BIP) is the single-window investment facilitation agency of the Industries and Commerce Department; RAJ NIVESH is the online single window clearance portal for investors.

Ease of Doing Business: the States' assessment under the Business Reform Action Plan (BRAP) is done by DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry; BRAP 2020 used the categories Top Achievers, Achievers, Aspirers and Emerging Business Ecosystems (Rajasthan was placed in 'Aspirers'). Asked in RAS Pre 2021 and 2024.

Rajasthan Startup Policy 2022 replaced the Startup Policy 2015; iStart Rajasthan (DoIT&C) is the startup platform, QRate its startup evaluation/rating mechanism, and iStart Nest the incubation network.
Industry (secondary sector) contributes about 26.5% of Rajasthan's Gross State Value Added (Rajasthan Economic Review 2025-26), against services 47.7% and agriculture and allied 25.7%.

Bhiwadi (Khairthal-Tijara region) is Rajasthan's largest industrial town in the National Capital Region; Boranada (Jodhpur), Sitapura and Bais Godam (Jaipur), Ghiloth and Neemrana are among the state's leading RIICO industrial areas.

questions.q: As per the Rajasthan Economic Review 2025-26, the share of the industry (secondary) sector in the Gross State Value Added of Rajasthan is approximately:
questions.exp: Industry accounts for about 26.5% of Rajasthan's GSVA; services (47.7%) is the largest sector and agriculture and allied activities contribute about 25.7%.

questions.q: The Rajasthan State Industrial and Mineral Development Corporation was given its present name, RIICO, in which year?
questions.exp: Incorporated on 28 March 1969 as RSIMDC, the corporation was renamed the Rajasthan State Industrial Development and Investment Corporation on 1 January 1980, when its mineral wing was separated as RSMML.

questions.q: The head office of RIICO, the nodal agency for industrial infrastructure in Rajasthan, is located at:
questions.exp: RIICO functions from Udyog Bhawan, Tilak Marg, Jaipur. It acquires, develops and allots industrial land across the state.

questions.q: According to the State Government's investment portal, the number of industrial areas developed by RIICO in Rajasthan is more than:
questions.exp: RIICO has developed 415 industrial areas over about 93,000 acres of land, making it the largest developer of industrial infrastructure in the state.

questions.q: The MedTech Medical Device Park developed by RIICO is located at:
questions.exp: RIICO's MedTech Medical Device Park is at Boranada Extension, Jodhpur. It was one of the options in the RAS Pre 2024 question on parks developed by RIICO.

questions.q: The Sports Goods and Toys Zone developed by RIICO has come up at:
questions.exp: The Sports Goods and Toys Zone is at Khushkhera in the Bhiwadi industrial region. Khushkhera is also one of the DMIC node locations of Rajasthan.

questions.q: RIICO's Integrated Resource Recovery Park at Tholai is located in which district?
questions.exp: The Integrated Resource Recovery Park is at Tholai in the Jamwa Ramgarh area of Jaipur district; it is designed for recycling and recovery of waste resources.

questions.q: India's first country-specific investment zone, the Japanese Zone, was developed by RIICO at:
questions.exp: The Japanese Zone at Neemrana (erstwhile Alwar district) was India's first dedicated country-specific industrial zone and hosts several Japanese manufacturing units.

questions.q: Rajasthan's second Japanese investment zone, as well as its Korean investment zone, have been developed by RIICO at:
questions.exp: Ghiloth industrial area (erstwhile Alwar district) hosts the state's second Japanese zone and the Korean investment zone. Neemrana holds the first Japanese zone.

questions.q: Mahindra World City, Jaipur - a multi-product Special Economic Zone - is a joint venture of the Mahindra Group with:
questions.exp: Mahindra World City, Jaipur is a joint venture between the Mahindra Group and RIICO, and is Rajasthan's largest multi-product SEZ.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of locations constitute the two investment nodes of the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The two DMIC nodes in Rajasthan are the Khushkhera-Bhiwadi-Neemrana Investment Region and the Jodhpur-Pali-Marwar Industrial Area. The largest share of the DMIC alignment falls in Rajasthan.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Petro Zone being developed at Balotra is meant to attract downstream industries linked to:
opts: the HPCL Rajasthan Refinery at Pachpadra
the Barmer lignite thermal power plants
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Petro Zone (about 700 hectares) at Balotra is planned around the HPCL Rajasthan Refinery at Pachpadra for petrochemical and downstream units.

questions.q: The annual crude oil refining capacity of the HPCL Rajasthan Refinery at Pachpadra is:
questions.exp: HPCL Rajasthan Refinery Limited (HRRL) is a joint venture of HPCL (74%) and the Government of Rajasthan (26%) with a capacity of 9 MMTPA, integrated with a petrochemical complex.

questions.q: Rajasthan's first crude oil refinery-cum-petrochemical complex at Pachpadra is located in which district?
questions.exp: Pachpadra lies in Balotra district, carved out of the erstwhile Barmer district. The crude is drawn largely from the Barmer-Sanchore basin.

questions.q: Which district of Rajasthan, the state's largest centre of polyester and suiting fabric, is known as the 'Textile City'?
questions.exp: Bhilwara is the largest producer of synthetic suiting fabric in Rajasthan and is called the Textile City. Pali and Balotra are known mainly for dyeing and printing of cloth.

questions.q: Rajasthan's first cement factory, established in 1915, is located at:
questions.exp: The cement works at Lakheri in Bundi district, set up in 1915, was the first cement plant of Rajasthan. Chittorgarh, Sirohi, Nagaur and Kota are the state's other cement districts.

questions.q: Makrana, the source of the white marble used in the Taj Mahal, lies in which district?
questions.exp: Makrana is in the erstwhile Nagaur district (now part of Didwana-Kuchaman district). Its calcite white marble was used in the Taj Mahal and the Victoria Memorial.

questions.q: Kishangarh, the largest marble processing and trading centre of Rajasthan, is situated in which district?
questions.exp: Kishangarh in Ajmer district hosts the state's biggest marble mandi and slab-processing cluster; Makrana supplies white marble and Rajsamand is a major quarrying belt.

questions.q: Bhainslana, well known for black marble, is located in which district of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Bhainslana in Jaipur district is the state's noted source of black marble. Jaisalmer yields yellow limestone/marble and Rajsamand green and white varieties.

questions.q: Which district is the principal centre of the glass industry in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Dholpur, with locally available silica sand, is the main centre of the glass industry in Rajasthan; the district is also famous for its red sandstone.

questions.q: The urea plant of Chambal Fertilisers and Chemicals Limited at Gadepan is located in which district?
questions.exp: Gadepan in Kota district hosts the Chambal Fertilisers urea complex. Kota also has the Shriram Fertilisers and Chemicals unit.

questions.q: The Chanderiya lead-zinc smelter complex, among the world's largest single-location zinc-lead smelting complexes, is situated in which district?
questions.exp: Chanderiya in Chittorgarh district is Hindustan Zinc Limited's largest smelting complex. HZL also runs smelters at Debari (Udaipur) and Dariba (Rajsamand).

questions.q: Rajasthan State Chemical Works, engaged in the manufacture of salt and allied chemicals, is located at:
questions.exp: Rajasthan State Chemical Works functions at Didwana. Sambhar Lake is worked by Sambhar Salts Limited, a joint venture of Hindustan Salts Limited and the State Government.

questions.q: The Central Sheep and Wool Research Institute is located at Avikanagar in which district?
questions.exp: The Central Sheep and Wool Research Institute (ICAR) is at Avikanagar in Tonk district. The Central Wool Development Board functions from Jodhpur.

questions.q: The Central Wool Development Board of the Government of India has its headquarters in which city of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The Central Wool Development Board, under the Ministry of Textiles, is headquartered at Jodhpur. Rajasthan is India's largest wool-producing state.

questions.q: The Gem and Jewellery Special Economic Zone of Rajasthan has been developed at:
questions.exp: The Gem and Jewellery SEZ is in the Sitapura industrial area of Jaipur, the country's leading centre for cutting and polishing of coloured gemstones.

questions.q: Under the Rajasthan Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (Facilitation of Establishment and Operation) Act, 2019, as originally enacted, a new enterprise was exempted from approvals, inspections and no-objection certificates for a period of:
questions.exp: The 2019 Act allowed a new MSME to start on a mere declaration of intent, with exemption for three years; an amendment in 2023 extended the acknowledgement certificate's validity and the exemption to five years.

questions.q: Under the Rajasthan MSME Act, 2019, the acknowledgement certificate for a new enterprise is obtained through which portal?
questions.exp: The Raj Udyog Mitra portal issues the acknowledgement certificate to an entrepreneur who files a declaration of intent under the Rajasthan MSME Act, 2019.

questions.q: Registration of micro, small and medium enterprises anywhere in India is presently done on which portal of the Ministry of MSME?
questions.exp: Udyam Registration replaced the earlier Udyog Aadhaar Memorandum as the all-India MSME registration system; Raj Udyog Mitra is Rajasthan's own facilitation portal.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Investment Promotion Scheme (RIPS) 2024 was notified in:
questions.exp: RIPS-2024 was notified on 8 October 2024, replacing RIPS-2019, and forms the core incentive framework offered to investors in the state. (As of September 2026.)

questions.q: The Rajasthan M-Sand Policy, 2024 sets a target of raising the state's manufactured sand production by 2028-29 to:
questions.exp: The M-Sand Policy announced in December 2024 targets 30 million tonnes of manufactured sand by 2028-29 to reduce dependence on river bed sand, with assured government procurement of M-sand.

questions.q: The Rising Rajasthan Global Investment Summit was held at Jaipur on:
questions.exp: The summit was held from 9 to 11 December 2024 at the Jaipur Exhibition and Convention Centre, Sitapura, and was inaugurated by the Prime Minister.

questions.q: The ranking/categorisation of States and Union Territories on Ease of Doing Business under the Business Reform Action Plan is carried out by:
opts: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade
questions.exp: DPIIT, under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry, conducts the Business Reform Action Plan assessment of States. The World Bank's global Doing Business report was discontinued in 2021.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about RIICO:
I. It was incorporated in 1969 as the Rajasthan State Industrial and Mineral Development Corporation.
II. Its mineral wing was separated in 1980 to form the Rajasthan State Mines and Minerals Limited.
III. It is the nodal agency for acquisition, development and allotment of industrial land in Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. RSIMDC of 1969 became RIICO on 1 January 1980 after the mineral activities were transferred to RSMML.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the specialised parks developed by RIICO:
I. The MedTech Medical Device Park is at Boranada in Jodhpur.
II. The Sports Goods and Toys Zone is at Khushkhera in the Bhiwadi region.
III. The Integrated Resource Recovery Park is at Tholai in Jamwa Ramgarh, Jaipur.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are RIICO parks. RAS Pre 2024 asked the same set with 'Agro Food Park, Udaipur' as the odd one out.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC) in Rajasthan:
I. The largest share of the length of the corridor's alignment passes through Rajasthan.
II. Khushkhera-Bhiwadi-Neemrana is one of the DMIC investment regions in the state.
III. Jodhpur-Pali-Marwar is the second DMIC node located in Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. About 39% of the DMIC alignment lies in Rajasthan, and the state has two notified nodes - KBNIR and JPMIA.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the textile industry of Rajasthan:
I. Bhilwara is the largest centre of synthetic suiting fabric in the state.
II. Pali is an important centre for dyeing and printing of cloth.
III. Kaithun in Kota district is famous for Kota Doria weaving.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. Sanganer and Bagru are the state's best known hand block printing centres.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the cement industry of Rajasthan:
I. The state's first cement plant was set up at Lakheri in Bundi district in 1915.
II. J.K. Cement's plant at Nimbahera is in Chittorgarh district.
III. Mangalam Cement's plant at Morak is in Sirohi district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. Mangalam Cement's Morak plant is in Kota district; Sirohi has the Pindwara/Jaykaypuram cement units.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Hindustan Zinc Limited:
I. Its registered office is at Udaipur.
II. Its zinc smelter at Debari is located in Udaipur district.
III. The Zawar mines, among the oldest zinc mines of India, are in Bhilwara district.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. The Zawar mines are in Udaipur district, not Bhilwara; Rampura-Agucha in Bhilwara is the state's largest zinc-lead mine.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the salt industry of Rajasthan:
I. Rajasthan is the third largest producer of salt in India after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu.
II. Sambhar Salts Limited is a joint venture of Hindustan Salts Limited and the Government of Rajasthan.
III. Didwana and Pachpadra are salt producing centres of the state.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. Sambhar is India's largest inland salt lake and Rajasthan's biggest source of salt.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajasthan Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (Facilitation of Establishment and Operation) Act, 2019:
I. A new enterprise may commence operations on filing a declaration of intent and obtaining an acknowledgement certificate.
II. The acknowledgement certificate was originally valid for three years and the period was raised to five years by an amendment in 2023.
III. The Act makes prior environmental clearance compulsory for every micro enterprise before it starts production.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. The Act's purpose is the opposite of III - it frees new MSMEs from most approvals and inspections during the exemption period.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajasthan Investment Promotion Scheme (RIPS) 2024:
I. It was notified in October 2024 and replaced RIPS-2019.
II. It offers benefits such as reimbursement of State GST, exemption from stamp duty and electricity duty and an employment generation subsidy.
III. It is administered by the Industries and Commerce Department, with the Bureau of Investment Promotion as the facilitation agency.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. RIPS-2024 is the state's principal fiscal incentive package for new and expanding enterprises. (As of September 2026.)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rising Rajasthan Global Investment Summit:
I. It was held at Jaipur in December 2024 and was inaugurated by the Prime Minister.
II. Memoranda of Understanding of the order of about Rs 35 lakh crore were reported around the summit.
III. A Pravasi Rajasthani Conclave and an MSME Conclave were organised as part of the summit.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. The summit was held from 9 to 11 December 2024 at JECC, Sitapura, Jaipur.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Ease of Doing Business assessment of Indian States:
I. The assessment under the Business Reform Action Plan is carried out by the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade.
II. DPIIT functions under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
III. In the BRAP 2020 assessment, States were placed in categories such as Top Achievers, Achievers, Aspirers and Emerging Business Ecosystems.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. Rajasthan was placed in the 'Aspirers' category in the BRAP 2020 assessment released in 2022.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the startup ecosystem of Rajasthan:
I. iStart Rajasthan is the state's startup platform run by the Department of Information Technology and Communication.
II. QRate is the evaluation and rating mechanism used for startups on the iStart platform.
III. The Rajasthan Startup Policy 2022 replaced the earlier Startup Policy of 2015.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. iStart also runs the iStart Nest incubation centres across the state.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Park/Zone of RIICO)   List-II (Location)
A. Japanese Zone   1. Balotra
B. MedTech Medical Device Park   2. Neemrana
C. Sports Goods and Toys Zone   3. Khushkhera
D. Rajasthan Petro Zone   4. Boranada
questions.exp: Japanese Zone - Neemrana; MedTech Park - Boranada (Jodhpur); Sports Goods and Toys Zone - Khushkhera (Bhiwadi); Rajasthan Petro Zone - Balotra.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Cement plant)   List-II (District)
A. J.K. Cement, Nimbahera   1. Chittorgarh
B. Binani Cement, Pindwara   2. Sirohi
C. Mangalam Cement, Morak   3. Kota
D. Shree Cement   4. Beawar
questions.exp: Nimbahera is in Chittorgarh, Pindwara in Sirohi, Morak in Kota and Shree Cement's original plant is at Beawar.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Industrial unit)   List-II (District)
A. Zinc smelter, Debari   1. Kota
B. Fertiliser plant, Gadepan   2. Chittorgarh
C. Zinc-lead smelter, Chanderiya   3. Udaipur
D. Sugar mill, Keshoraipatan   4. Bundi
questions.exp: Debari is in Udaipur, Gadepan in Kota, Chanderiya in Chittorgarh and the Keshoraipatan co-operative sugar mill is in Bundi.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Craft)   List-II (Centre/District)
A. Thewa   1. Rajsamand
B. Kota Doria   2. Pratapgarh
C. Terracotta of Molela   3. Jaipur
D. Blue pottery   4. Kota
questions.exp: Thewa work belongs to Pratapgarh, Kota Doria to Kaithun in Kota, Molela terracotta to Rajsamand and blue pottery to Jaipur.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Centre)   List-II (Known for)
A. Bhilwara   1. Hand block printing
B. Sanganer   2. Suiting and polyester fabric
C. Pali   3. Kota Doria weaving
D. Kaithun   4. Dyeing and printing of cloth
questions.exp: Bhilwara - suiting fabric; Sanganer - hand block printing; Pali - dyeing and printing; Kaithun (Kota) - Kota Doria weaving.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Organisation)   List-II (Principal function)
A. RIICO   1. Term loans to small and medium enterprises
B. RFC   2. Development and allotment of industrial areas
C. RSMML   3. Marketing of handicrafts and small industry products
D. RAJSICO   4. Mining and marketing of minerals
questions.exp: RIICO develops industrial areas, RFC provides term loans, RSMML handles minerals and RAJSICO markets handicrafts and small-industry products.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Policy/Act of Rajasthan)   List-II (Year)
A. MSME (Facilitation of Establishment and Operation) Act   1. 2022
B. Rajasthan Startup Policy   2. 2019
C. Rajasthan Investment Promotion Scheme   3. 2015
D. E-Governance, IT and ITeS Policy   4. 2024
questions.exp: The MSME Act is of 2019, the Startup Policy of 2022, RIPS of 2024 and the E-Governance, IT and ITeS Policy of 2015.

questions.q: Which one of the following parks/zones has NOT been developed by RIICO in Rajasthan?
opts: Integrated Resource Recovery Park, Jamwa Ramgarh (Jaipur)
Sports Goods and Toys Zone, Khushkhera (Bhiwadi)
questions.exp: The first three are RIICO parks; there is no RIICO Agro Food Park at Udaipur. This exact question was asked in RAS Pre 2024.

questions.q: Which one of the following industry-centre pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Sriganganagar is known for sugar, mustard oil and cotton ginning, not cement. Rajasthan's cement belt lies in Chittorgarh, Sirohi, Nagaur, Bundi and Kota.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of an industrial location and its district is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Bhainslana, famous for black marble, is in Jaipur district, not Nagaur. Nagaur's marble centre is Makrana, known for white marble.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the Rajasthan Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (Facilitation of Establishment and Operation) Act, 2019?
opts: A new enterprise can start operations after filing a declaration of intent
It grants permanent exemption from all State approvals to every MSME
An acknowledgement certificate is issued through the Raj Udyog Mitra portal
The exemption period was extended by an amendment made in 2023
questions.exp: The exemption is time-bound, not permanent - three years originally, raised to five years by the 2023 amendment, after which normal approvals apply.

questions.q: Which one of the following portals is NOT correctly matched with its purpose?
opts: RAJ NIVESH - single window clearance for investors
Raj Udyog Mitra - acknowledgement certificate for new MSMEs
iStart Rajasthan - registration and support for startups
Udyam Registration Portal - allotment of RIICO industrial plots
questions.exp: The Udyam Registration Portal of the Ministry of MSME is used for MSME registration; RIICO plots are allotted through RIICO's own online system.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of an organisation and its headquarters is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Rajasthan State Mines and Minerals Limited - Udaipur
questions.exp: Hindustan Zinc Limited has its registered office at Udaipur, not Jodhpur. RSMML is also headquartered at Udaipur.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in the correct chronological order of their enactment/announcement:
I. Rajasthan MSME (Facilitation of Establishment and Operation) Act
II. Rajasthan Startup Policy
III. Rajasthan Investment Promotion Scheme (RIPS)
IV. Rajasthan M-Sand Policy
questions.exp: MSME Act 2019, Startup Policy 2022, RIPS notified 8 October 2024 and the M-Sand Policy announced in December 2024.

questions.q:
Arrange the following events in the correct chronological order:
I. Incorporation of the Rajasthan State Industrial and Mineral Development Corporation
II. Establishment of the Rajasthan Financial Corporation
III. Renaming of the corporation as RIICO
IV. Rising Rajasthan Global Investment Summit
questions.exp: RFC was set up in 1955, RSIMDC was incorporated in 1969, it was renamed RIICO in 1980 and the Rising Rajasthan summit was held in December 2024.

chapters.title: Services, Tourism and IT in Rajasthan
factsheet: Services (tertiary) sector contributes about 47.7% of Rajasthan's Gross State Value Added (Rajasthan Economic Review 2025-26) - the largest of the three broad sectors; industry 26.5%, agriculture and allied 25.7%.
Bank of Baroda is the convenor bank of the State Level Bankers' Committee (SLBC) for Rajasthan; the Reserve Bank of India has a regional office at Jaipur.
Under the 'One State-One RRB' policy, Rajasthan's Regional Rural Banks were amalgamated with effect from 1 May 2025 into a single Rajasthan Gramin Bank (headquarters Jaipur).
Tourism was granted the status of an industry in Rajasthan in 1989; RTDC (Rajasthan Tourism Development Corporation) was set up on 1 April 1979 for accommodation, catering and transport services.

Tourist arrivals in Rajasthan, calendar year 2024: domestic about 2,300.84 lakh (roughly 23 crore) and foreign about 20.72 lakh, both showing double-digit growth over 2023; Rajasthan is among India's top five states in tourist visits.
Palace on Wheels - luxury tourist train started in 1982, run jointly by Indian Railways and RTDC; Royal Rajasthan on Wheels was introduced in 2009.
RITTMAN (Rajasthan Institute of Tourism and Travel Management), Jaipur - established 1996 for training in tourism and travel management.

Rajasthan Tourism Policy, 2020 - approved in September 2020 for five years; provides for special tourism zones, a Tourist Assistance Force, home-stay/guest-house promotion, a Policy Implementation Unit and diversification into desert, adventure, eco, tribal, rural and wellness tourism.
Paying Guest Scheme - registration of private householders to provide tourist accommodation; Heritage Hotel - a fort, palace, castle or haveli built before 1950 and converted into a hotel.
Rajasthan announced a Film Tourism Promotion Policy in 2022 to offer subsidy and single-window facilitation for films shot in the state, and a Rural Tourism Scheme to develop village tourism units.

Tourist circuits: Desert (Jaisalmer-Barmer-Bikaner-Jodhpur), Shekhawati (Sikar-Jhunjhunu-Churu), Mewar (Udaipur-Chittorgarh-Rajsamand), Hadoti (Kota-Bundi-Jhalawar-Baran), Dhundhar/Golden Triangle (Jaipur), Braj-Mewat (Bharatpur-Deeg-Alwar).

Swadesh Darshan (theme-based tourist circuits) and PRASHAD - Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Augmentation Drive - are Ministry of Tourism schemes launched in 2014-15; Ajmer-Pushkar is a PRASHAD site in Rajasthan.
UNESCO World Heritage properties in Rajasthan (four): Keoladeo National Park, Bharatpur (1985); Jantar Mantar, Jaipur (2010); Hill Forts of Rajasthan (2013); Jaipur City (2019).
Hill Forts of Rajasthan (2013) comprise six forts - Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore (Sawai Madhopur), Amber (Jaipur), Jaisalmer and Gagron (Jhalawar). Mehrangarh is NOT part of the inscription.
Jaipur, inscribed in 2019, is the second Indian city after Ahmedabad to be listed as a UNESCO World Heritage City.

Rajasthan's E-Governance, IT and ITeS Policy was announced in 2015; the nodal department is the Department of Information Technology and Communication (DoIT&C) and the implementing arm is RajCOMP Info Services Limited (RISL).
e-Mitra - single-point delivery of government and utility services to citizens through kiosks; e-Mitra Plus machines extend self-service access.

Jan Aadhaar Yojana - launched in December 2019, gives every family a ten-digit Jan Aadhaar number and card ('one number, one card, one identity'); it replaced the Bhamashah Yojana as the delivery backbone for state benefits.
Bhamashah Yojana - family-based, woman-headed direct benefit transfer scheme relaunched on 15 August 2014, later subsumed in Jan Aadhaar.
SSO Rajasthan (Single Sign On) - one login identity for citizens, government employees and businesses across state government portals.

Raj Kaj - e-file and human resource management platform for state government offices; Rajasthan Sampark - public grievance registration and redressal portal with a toll-free helpline; Raj eVault - secure digital storage and sharing of citizens' documents.
RAJ NIVESH is the single window clearance portal for investors; Raj Udyog Mitra serves new MSMEs; RajDhara is the state's geospatial/GIS platform.

iStart Rajasthan (DoIT&C) is the state's startup platform; QRate is its startup evaluation and rating mechanism; Bhamashah Techno Hub, Jaipur is one of the country's large startup incubation facilities.
Kerala was the first Indian state to be declared a 'Digital State' (2016) - a fact asked in RAS Pre 2016.
Rajasthan's IT/ITeS activity is concentrated in Jaipur (Sitapura, Mahindra World City SEZ, Jhalana), with expanding facilities at Jodhpur (Boranada) and Udaipur.
BharatNet, RajNET and the Rajasthan State Wide Area Network provide the state's e-governance connectivity backbone; Rajasthan Sampark helpline number is 181.
Tourism is a major employment generator in Rajasthan and a key element of the services sector, supporting handicrafts, hotels, transport and guiding services.
Tourism institutions and roles: Department of Tourism (policy and promotion), RTDC (hotels, transport, fairs and festivals), RITTMAN (training), Tourist Assistance Force (tourist safety).

questions.q: As per the Rajasthan Economic Review 2025-26, the share of the services (tertiary) sector in the Gross State Value Added of Rajasthan is approximately:
questions.exp: Services contribute about 47.7% of Rajasthan's GSVA, the largest share among the three broad sectors, ahead of industry (26.5%) and agriculture and allied (25.7%).

questions.q: Which bank is the convenor of the State Level Bankers' Committee (SLBC) for Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Bank of Baroda is the SLBC convenor bank for Rajasthan; the SLBC coordinates the annual credit plan and reviews the credit-deposit ratio of the state.

questions.q: Under the 'One State-One Regional Rural Bank' policy, the Regional Rural Banks of Rajasthan were amalgamated with effect from 1 May 2025 into a single bank named:
questions.exp: Baroda Rajasthan Kshetriya Gramin Bank and Rajasthan Marudhara Gramin Bank were merged into Rajasthan Gramin Bank from 1 May 2025 under the One State-One RRB consolidation.

questions.q: The number of domestic tourists who visited Rajasthan in the calendar year 2024 was of the order of:
questions.exp: Rajasthan received about 2,300.84 lakh (roughly 23 crore) domestic tourists in 2024, a growth of nearly 28.5% over the previous year.

questions.q: Foreign tourist arrivals in Rajasthan during the calendar year 2024 were of the order of:
questions.exp: Rajasthan received about 20.72 lakh foreign tourists in 2024, an increase of nearly 22% over 2023. Foreign arrivals are heavily concentrated in Jaipur, Udaipur and Jaisalmer.

questions.q: Tourism was accorded the status of an industry in Rajasthan in the year:
questions.exp: Rajasthan declared tourism an industry in 1989, which enabled tourism units to receive industrial incentives and concessional infrastructure tariffs.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Tourism Development Corporation (RTDC) was established on:
questions.exp: RTDC was set up on 1 April 1979 to provide accommodation, catering, transport and entertainment services to tourists and to run the state's fairs and festivals.

questions.q: The luxury tourist train 'Palace on Wheels' was started in the year:
questions.exp: Palace on Wheels was launched in 1982 as a joint venture of Indian Railways and RTDC. Royal Rajasthan on Wheels followed in 2009.

questions.q: RITTMAN, the institute set up at Jaipur in 1996, is concerned with:
opts: training in tourism and travel management
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Institute of Tourism and Travel Management (RITTMAN), Jaipur, trains manpower for the hospitality, travel and tourism trade.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Tourism Policy which provided for special tourism zones and a Tourist Assistance Force was approved in:
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Tourism Policy, 2020 was approved in September 2020 for a period of five years and covers special tourism zones, home stays, guest houses and a Tourist Assistance Force.

questions.q: Rajasthan announced a policy to promote the shooting of films in the state, offering subsidy and single-window facilitation to film producers, in the year:
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Film Tourism Promotion Policy was announced in 2022 to attract film shootings, which in turn promote destination tourism.

questions.q: The Paying Guest House Scheme of the Rajasthan Tourism Department is intended to:
opts: allow registered private householders to provide accommodation to tourists
convert forts and palaces into luxury hotels
questions.exp: Under the Paying Guest Scheme, private families register with the Tourism Department to host tourists, adding rooms in cities where hotel capacity is limited.

questions.q: In the classification followed for tourist accommodation, a 'Heritage Hotel' in Rajasthan is essentially:
opts: a palace, fort, castle or haveli built before 1950 and converted into a hotel
a hotel with more than one hundred rooms
a hotel located inside a national park
questions.exp: Heritage hotels are properties built before 1950 - palaces, forts, castles and havelis - converted into hotels; Rajasthan has the largest number of such hotels in India.

questions.q: The Swadesh Darshan scheme for the development of theme-based tourist circuits is implemented by:
opts: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
questions.exp: Swadesh Darshan, launched in 2014-15 by the Ministry of Tourism, funds theme-based circuits such as the Desert Circuit, Krishna Circuit and Heritage Circuit in Rajasthan.

questions.q: In the PRASHAD scheme of the Government of India, under which Ajmer-Pushkar has been taken up, the letter 'P' stands for:
questions.exp: PRASHAD stands for Pilgrimage Rejuvenation and Spiritual Augmentation Drive, a Ministry of Tourism scheme for the development of pilgrimage destinations.

questions.q: How many properties of Rajasthan are inscribed on the UNESCO World Heritage List?
questions.exp: Four: Keoladeo National Park (1985), Jantar Mantar Jaipur (2010), Hill Forts of Rajasthan (2013) and Jaipur City (2019).

questions.q: Jaipur was inscribed as a World Heritage City by UNESCO in 2019. It thus became the:
opts: first Indian city with this status
second Indian city with this status
third Indian city with this status
fourth Indian city with this status
questions.exp: Jaipur is the second Indian city to be inscribed as a World Heritage City, after Ahmedabad which was inscribed in 2017.

questions.q: The E-Governance, Information Technology and ITeS Policy of Rajasthan was announced in the year:
questions.exp: The Rajasthan E-Governance, IT and ITeS Policy was announced in 2015 to promote IT investment, IT parks, BPO units and e-governance in the state.

questions.q: RISL, the implementing agency for the information technology projects of the Government of Rajasthan, stands for:
questions.exp: RajCOMP Info Services Limited (RISL) works under the Department of Information Technology and Communication as the executing agency for state IT and e-governance projects.

questions.q: The e-Mitra kiosks of Rajasthan are meant primarily for:
opts: single-point delivery of government services and utility payments to citizens
questions.exp: e-Mitra provides citizens a single window at kiosk level for utility bill payment, certificates, applications and other government services.

questions.q: The Jan Aadhaar Yojana of Rajasthan, launched in December 2019, provides each family a unique identification number of:
questions.exp: The Jan Aadhaar number is a ten-digit family identification number issued with a Jan Aadhaar card - 'one number, one card, one identity' - and is the backbone for state benefit transfers.

questions.q: The Jan Aadhaar Yojana of Rajasthan replaced which earlier family identification and benefit transfer scheme?
questions.exp: Jan Aadhaar replaced the Bhamashah Yojana, the woman-headed family scheme relaunched on 15 August 2014, as the state's DBT platform.

questions.q: The Single Sign On (SSO) facility of the Government of Rajasthan enables a user to:
opts: access multiple state government applications with one identity
questions.exp: SSO Rajasthan gives citizens, government employees and businesses a single login identity for e-Mitra, Raj Kaj, iStart, scholarship portals and other state applications.

questions.q: iStart Rajasthan, the state's startup platform, is run by which department?
opts: Department of Information Technology and Communication
Department of Skill, Employment and Entrepreneurship
questions.exp: iStart Rajasthan is a DoIT&C initiative offering startup registration, incubation through iStart Nest and the QRate evaluation mechanism.

questions.q: Which was the first state of India to be declared a 'Digital State'?
questions.exp: Kerala was declared India's first digital state in 2016. This fact was asked in RAS Pre 2016 - in fact twice within the same paper.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the services sector of Rajasthan:
I. It has the largest share among the three broad sectors in the state's Gross State Value Added.
II. Trade, hotels and restaurants, transport, real estate and public administration are counted within it.
III. Tourism is an important component of the state's services economy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Services account for about 47.7% of Rajasthan's GSVA and the sector has grown faster than agriculture in recent years.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about banking in Rajasthan:
I. Bank of Baroda is the convenor bank of the State Level Bankers' Committee for Rajasthan.
II. The credit-deposit ratio measures the proportion of deposits deployed as credit in the state.
III. The Reserve Bank of India has no regional office anywhere in Rajasthan.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. The RBI has a regional office at Jaipur, so III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about tourism in Rajasthan:
I. In the calendar year 2024, both domestic and foreign tourist arrivals recorded growth over the previous year.
II. Foreign tourist arrivals in Rajasthan in 2024 exceeded domestic tourist arrivals.
III. Rajasthan is among the top five states of India in terms of tourist visits.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and III are correct. Domestic arrivals (about 23 crore) vastly outnumber foreign arrivals (about 20.7 lakh), so II is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajasthan Tourism Policy, 2020:
I. It provides for the declaration of special tourism zones.
II. It provides for a Tourist Assistance Force.
III. It was to remain in force for five years from the date of its notification.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. The policy also promotes home stays, guest houses and diversification into desert, eco, tribal, rural and wellness tourism.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'Hill Forts of Rajasthan' inscribed by UNESCO in 2013:
I. Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh and Ranthambore forts are part of the serial inscription.
II. Gagron fort in Jhalawar district is part of the inscription.
III. Mehrangarh fort of Jodhpur is part of the inscription.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The six forts inscribed are Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Amber, Jaisalmer and Gagron. Mehrangarh is not part of the inscription.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Department of Information Technology and Communication is the nodal department for e-governance in Rajasthan.
II. RajCOMP Info Services Limited is its implementing agency.
III. The e-Mitra programme is run by the Department of Tourism.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are correct. e-Mitra is a DoIT&C initiative implemented through RISL and district e-governance societies, not the Tourism Department.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the e-governance initiatives of Rajasthan:
I. Rajasthan Sampark is the state's public grievance redressal portal and helpline.
II. Raj Kaj is used for e-file work and human resource management of government offices.
III. Raj eVault allows citizens to store and share digital copies of their documents.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three statements are correct. Rajasthan's e-governance portals have been asked repeatedly in RAS Prelims.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. RTDC was set up in 1979 to provide accommodation, catering and transport services to tourists.
II. The Palace on Wheels is operated jointly by Indian Railways and RTDC.
III. Rajasthan granted industry status to tourism before it framed the Tourism Policy of 2020.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Industry status was granted in 1989, well before the 2020 policy, and the Palace on Wheels began in 1982.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Tourist circuit)   List-II (Districts covered)
A. Desert circuit   1. Sikar, Jhunjhunu, Churu
B. Shekhawati circuit   2. Kota, Bundi, Jhalawar
C. Mewar circuit   3. Jaisalmer, Barmer, Bikaner
D. Hadoti circuit   4. Udaipur, Chittorgarh, Rajsamand
questions.exp: Desert circuit - Jaisalmer, Barmer, Bikaner; Shekhawati - Sikar, Jhunjhunu, Churu; Mewar - Udaipur, Chittorgarh, Rajsamand; Hadoti - Kota, Bundi, Jhalawar.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (World Heritage property in Rajasthan)   List-II (Year of inscription)
A. Keoladeo National Park   1. 1985
B. Jantar Mantar, Jaipur   2. 2010
C. Hill Forts of Rajasthan   3. 2013
D. Jaipur City   4. 2019
questions.exp: Keoladeo 1985, Jantar Mantar 2010, Hill Forts 2013 and the walled city of Jaipur 2019.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Portal/Platform)   List-II (Purpose)
A. Jan Aadhaar   1. Single window clearance for investors
B. RAJ NIVESH   2. Family identification for delivery of benefits
C. Raj Kaj   3. Startup registration and support
D. iStart   4. Government office e-file and HR management
questions.exp: Jan Aadhaar - family identification; RAJ NIVESH - single window investment clearance; Raj Kaj - office e-file and HR; iStart - startups.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Heritage site)   List-II (District)
A. Keoladeo National Park   1. Jhalawar
B. Kumbhalgarh fort   2. Bharatpur
C. Gagron fort   3. Jaisalmer
D. Sonar fort   4. Rajsamand
questions.exp: Keoladeo - Bharatpur; Kumbhalgarh - Rajsamand; Gagron - Jhalawar; Sonar (Golden) fort - Jaisalmer. All except Keoladeo belong to the Hill Forts inscription.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (IT initiative)   List-II (Function)
A. RISL   1. Rating of startups on the state platform
B. e-Mitra   2. Single identity for state government applications
C. QRate   3. Implementation of state IT projects
D. Single Sign On   4. Citizen service delivery kiosks
questions.exp: RISL implements IT projects, e-Mitra delivers citizen services, QRate rates startups and SSO gives a single login identity.

questions.q: Which one of the following forts is NOT included in the UNESCO World Heritage 'Hill Forts of Rajasthan'?
questions.exp: The six inscribed forts are Chittorgarh, Kumbhalgarh, Ranthambore, Amber, Jaisalmer and Gagron. Mehrangarh of Jodhpur is not among them.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Palace on Wheels - luxury tourist train
RITTMAN - training in tourism and travel management
Paying Guest Scheme - registered accommodation in private homes
questions.exp: RTDC provides accommodation, catering, transport and entertainment services to tourists; industrial investment promotion is the work of the Bureau of Investment Promotion and RIICO.

questions.q: Which one of the following portals of the Government of Rajasthan is NOT correctly described?
opts: e-Mitra - single-point delivery of citizen services
Raj eVault - online payment of electricity bills
Rajasthan Sampark - registration and tracking of public grievances
SSO Rajasthan - single login for state government portals
questions.exp: Raj eVault is a digital locker for storing and sharing citizens' documents; utility bill payment is done through e-Mitra.

questions.q: Which one of the following circuit-district pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Bharatpur belongs to the Braj-Mewat region, not the Mewar circuit, which covers Udaipur, Chittorgarh, Rajsamand and neighbouring districts.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a UNESCO World Heritage property located in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The Sun Temple at Jhalrapatan is a protected monument but is not a World Heritage property. Rajasthan has four UNESCO inscriptions.

questions.q:
Arrange the following World Heritage inscriptions relating to Rajasthan in correct chronological order:
I. Jaipur City
II. Keoladeo National Park
III. Jantar Mantar, Jaipur
IV. Hill Forts of Rajasthan
questions.exp: Keoladeo 1985, Jantar Mantar 2010, Hill Forts 2013 and Jaipur City 2019.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Rajasthan attracts one of the largest numbers of foreign tourists among the states of India.
Reason (R): The state has four UNESCO World Heritage properties besides forts, palaces, desert landscapes and wildlife destinations.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: Both statements are true and the heritage and desert product mix is the principal reason for Rajasthan's high share of foreign tourist visits.

chapters.title: Infrastructure of Rajasthan: Energy, Transport, Communication
factsheet: Rajasthan State Electricity Board (RSEB) was constituted on 1 July 1957 and was unbundled in 2000 into five successor companies under the state's power sector reforms.
Post-unbundling: RVUNL (Rajasthan Rajya Vidyut Utpadan Nigam) = generation; RVPNL (Rajasthan Rajya Vidyut Prasaran Nigam) = transmission; three discoms = Jaipur VVNL, Ajmer VVNL and Jodhpur VVNL.
Rajasthan Electricity Regulatory Commission (RERC), Jaipur, was set up under the Rajasthan Electricity Reforms Act, 1999; it determines tariffs and regulates licensees.
Suratgarh Super Thermal Power Station (Sriganganagar district) - the 'Thermal Power House of Rajasthan'; 2,820 MW, including two 660 MW supercritical units - the state's largest thermal station.
Kota Super Thermal Power Station (Kota, on the Chambal) - Rajasthan's FIRST coal-based thermal power station, 1,240 MW, a repeated national productivity award winner.
Chhabra Thermal Power Project - Baran district (1,000 MW subcritical + 1,320 MW supercritical). Kalisindh Thermal Power Project - Jhalawar district, 2 x 600 MW supercritical.
Lignite stations: Giral (Barmer, 250 MW), Barsingsar (Bikaner, NLC India), and the Bhadresh/Barmer station fed by the Jalipa-Kapurdi lignite fields.
Gas-based stations: Ramgarh (Jaisalmer) and Dholpur Combined Cycle (Dholpur, 330 MW).

Rawatbhata Atomic Power Station (Chittorgarh district, on the Chambal near Rana Pratap Sagar) is Rajasthan's only nuclear station; Unit-1 was built with Canadian collaboration using pressurised heavy water reactor technology.
Hydel: Rana Pratap Sagar 172 MW (Chittorgarh), Jawahar Sagar 99 MW (Kota), Mahi Bajaj Sagar 140 MW (Banswara). Chambal projects are shared 50:50 by Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh.
Rajasthan Renewable Energy Corporation Ltd (RRECL), Jaipur - the state NODAL AGENCY for solar, wind, biomass and green hydrogen; successor to the Rajasthan Energy Development Agency (REDA).
Bhadla Solar Park - Bhadla village, Phalodi district (carved out of Jodhpur) - India's largest solar park, about 2,245 MW over roughly 5,700 hectares, completed in four phases by March 2020.
Rajasthan ranks FIRST among states in installed solar capacity and SECOND in total renewable capacity, behind Gujarat (as of March 2026).
Rajasthan's total installed generation capacity was 54.77 GW as on 31 October 2025, up from 22.02 GW in March 2020 (Rajasthan Energy Department).
Rajasthan Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024 - target 125 GW by 2029-30: 90 GW solar + 25 GW wind and hybrid + 10 GW hydro, pumped storage and battery storage.
Rajasthan Solar Energy Policy 2019 set a 30 GW solar target; the Rajasthan Wind and Hybrid Energy Policy was also issued in 2019. Both are now subsumed in the Integrated Clean Energy Policy 2024.
Rajasthan Green Hydrogen Policy, 2023 (approved September 2023) - target 2,000 KTPA of green hydrogen by 2030; exemption from wheeling and transmission charges; thrust-sector status under RIPS.

PM-KUSUM (2019, Ministry of New & Renewable Energy): Component-A = decentralised ground-mounted RE plants up to 2 MW on barren land; Component-B = standalone solar pumps; Component-C = solarisation of grid-connected pumps. Rajasthan leads in Component-A.
PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana - launched 13 February 2024, outlay about Rs 75,021 crore, rooftop solar for 1 crore households with up to 300 free units a month.
Mukhyamantri Kisan Mitra Urja Yojana (2021, Energy Department, Rajasthan) - grant of up to Rs 1,000 per month, maximum Rs 12,000 a year, on the bills of metered agricultural consumers.

UDAY (Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana), 20 November 2015 - states take over 75% of discom debt (50% in 2015-16, 25% in 2016-17); AT&C loss target 15%. Rajasthan was the THIRD state to sign a UDAY MoU (December 2015) and carried the largest discom debt.
Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), 2021 - about Rs 3.03 lakh crore for prepaid smart metering and loss reduction, targeting AT&C losses of 12-15%.
Rural electrification: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (2015, feeder separation) and Saubhagya - Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (September 2017, household connections).

Delhi-Mumbai Expressway (NE-4), about 1,350 km, 8 lanes expandable to 12; Rajasthan carries 373 km - the second longest state share after Gujarat's 426 km - through Khairthal-Tijara/Alwar, Dausa, Sawai Madhopur, Bundi and Kota.
The first stretch of the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway, the 246 km Sohna-Dausa-Lalsot section, was opened on 12 February 2023.
RSRTC was established on 1 October 1964 under the Road Transport Corporations Act, 1950 (HQ Jaipur); RSRDC (1979) builds state roads and bridges on a corporate model.
PMGSY (25 December 2000, Ministry of Rural Development) connects habitations of 500+ (250+ in desert, tribal and hill areas); Rajasthan also runs the Mukhyamantri Gram Sadak Yojana.

North Western Railway zone, HQ Jaipur, was created on 1 October 2002 with four divisions - Jaipur, Ajmer, Bikaner and Jodhpur. The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (JNPT-Dadri) runs through Rajasthan, including the Rewari-Madar section.

Jaipur Metro is Rajasthan's first metro - the Mansarovar-Chandpole section opened on 3 June 2015. Jaipur (Sanganer) is the state's only international airport; Kishangarh airport was commissioned in 2017 under UDAN.

Jal Jeevan Mission (15 August 2019) guarantees 55 lpcd of BIS-10500 quality tap water; Centre-State sharing is 50:50 for Rajasthan; JJM 2.0 was approved in March 2026 with a Rs 8.69 lakh crore outlay and a December 2028 target. RUIDP is the ADB-assisted urban infrastructure programme.

questions.q: The Rajasthan State Electricity Board was constituted in which year?
questions.exp: The RSEB was constituted on 1 July 1957 and functioned until the power sector reforms of 2000, when it was unbundled into five successor companies.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Electricity Regulatory Commission was established under which legislation?
questions.exp: RERC was set up under the Rajasthan Electricity Reforms Act, 1999 and continues under the Electricity Act, 2003. It fixes tariffs and regulates licensees in the state.

questions.q: Which thermal power station is known as the 'Thermal Power House of Rajasthan'?
questions.exp: Suratgarh STPS in Sriganganagar district, with 2,820 MW, is the state's largest thermal station and is called the Thermal Power House of Rajasthan.

questions.q: Rajasthan's first coal-based thermal power station, standing on the bank of the Chambal, is:
questions.exp: Kota Super Thermal Power Station (1,240 MW) was Rajasthan's first coal-fired thermal station and stands on the Chambal at Kota.

questions.q: The Giral thermal power station of Rajasthan is based on which fuel?
questions.exp: The 250 MW Giral station in Barmer district runs on locally mined lignite. Rajasthan's other lignite stations are at Barsingsar (Bikaner) and Bhadresh (Barmer).

questions.q: The Jalipa-Kapurdi lignite fields supply fuel to a power station located in which district?
questions.exp: The Jalipa and Kapurdi lignite mines feed the lignite-based power station at Bhadresh in Barmer district; Barmer also hosts the Giral lignite station.

questions.q: Rawatbhata Atomic Power Station is located in which district of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Rawatbhata, on the Chambal near the Rana Pratap Sagar dam, lies in Chittorgarh district and is Rajasthan's only nuclear power station.

questions.q: The Chambal valley hydro-electric projects are shared between Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh in which ratio?
questions.exp: Cost and power from the Chambal projects - Gandhi Sagar, Rana Pratap Sagar and Jawahar Sagar - are shared equally, 50:50, between Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh.

questions.q: Which organisation is the designated nodal agency for promotion of renewable energy in Rajasthan?
opts: Rajasthan Rajya Vidyut Utpadan Nigam Limited
questions.exp: RRECL, Jaipur - successor to the Rajasthan Energy Development Agency - is the state nodal agency for solar, wind, biomass and green hydrogen projects.

questions.q: Bhadla Solar Park, India's largest solar park, has an installed capacity of approximately:
questions.exp: Bhadla Solar Park has about 2,245 MW over roughly 5,700 hectares, developed in four phases and completed by March 2020.

questions.q: Bhadla Solar Park is located in which district of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Bhadla village lies in Phalodi district, carved out of the erstwhile Jodhpur district; older sources therefore place Bhadla in Jodhpur district.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024 sets a clean energy capacity target of:
questions.exp: The Integrated Clean Energy Policy 2024 targets 125 GW of clean energy capacity by 2029-30. As of the policy notified in December 2024.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Solar Energy Policy, 2019 set a solar capacity target of:
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Solar Energy Policy 2019 set a 30 GW solar target; it has since been superseded by the Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024.

questions.q: As of 2025-26, which state ranks first in India in installed solar power capacity?
questions.exp: Rajasthan ranks first in installed solar capacity and second in total renewable capacity after Gujarat (as of March 2026).

questions.q: Rajasthan's total installed electricity generation capacity as on 31 October 2025 was approximately:
questions.exp: Rajasthan's installed capacity stood at 54.77 GW on 31 October 2025, up from 22.02 GW in March 2020, almost all of the addition being solar and wind. Data as of October 2025.

questions.q: PM-KUSUM is implemented by which Union Ministry?
opts: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
questions.exp: Although it serves farmers, PM-KUSUM (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan, 2019) is administered by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.

questions.q: Under the PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, how many units of free electricity per month are envisaged for a beneficiary household?
questions.exp: PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, launched on 13 February 2024 with an outlay of about Rs 75,021 crore, targets rooftop solar in one crore households with up to 300 free units a month.

questions.q: Under the Mukhyamantri Kisan Mitra Urja Yojana of Rajasthan, the maximum electricity bill grant to an eligible farmer is:
opts: Rs 500 per month, up to Rs 6,000 a year
Rs 1,000 per month, up to Rs 12,000 a year
Rs 1,500 per month, up to Rs 18,000 a year
Rs 2,000 per month, up to Rs 24,000 a year
questions.exp: Launched in 2021 by the Energy Department, the scheme gives metered agricultural consumers a grant of up to Rs 1,000 per month subject to a ceiling of Rs 12,000 a year.

questions.q: UDAY, the scheme for the financial turnaround of power distribution companies, was launched in which year?
questions.exp: The Ujwal DISCOM Assurance Yojana was launched on 20 November 2015 by the Ministry of Power. Rajasthan was the third state to sign a UDAY memorandum of understanding.

questions.q: 'Saubhagya', the scheme for universal household electrification, is officially known as:
opts: Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana
Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana
questions.exp: Saubhagya is the Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana, launched in September 2017 to give electricity connections to all willing un-electrified households.

questions.q: The Delhi-Mumbai Expressway is officially designated as:
questions.exp: The Delhi-Mumbai Expressway, about 1,350 km long and eight lanes wide (expandable to twelve), carries the designation NE-4.

questions.q: The length of the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway passing through Rajasthan is approximately:
questions.exp: Rajasthan carries about 373 km of the expressway - the second longest state share after Gujarat's 426 km. Haryana has 129 km and Madhya Pradesh 244 km.

questions.q: The Amritsar-Jamnagar Economic Corridor passes through which group of Rajasthan districts?
questions.exp: The corridor enters Rajasthan in Hanumangarh and runs through Bikaner, Jodhpur, Barmer and Jalore towards Gujarat, giving western Rajasthan a freight link to the Kandla-Jamnagar ports.

questions.q: The Rajasthan State Road Transport Corporation was established in which year?
questions.exp: RSRTC was set up on 1 October 1964 under the Road Transport Corporations Act, 1950, with its headquarters at Jaipur.

questions.q: Under the Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana, the population norm for connectivity in desert, tribal and hill areas is habitations of:
questions.exp: The general PMGSY norm is 500 and above, relaxed to 250 and above in desert areas, Schedule V tribal areas and hill states. PMGSY was launched on 25 December 2000.

questions.q: The headquarters of the North Western Railway zone is at:
questions.exp: The North Western Railway zone, created on 1 October 2002, is headquartered at Jaipur and has four divisions - Jaipur, Ajmer, Bikaner and Jodhpur.

questions.q: The first section of the Jaipur Metro, opened in June 2015, ran between:
questions.exp: Phase-1A of the Jaipur Metro, Mansarovar to Chandpole, opened on 3 June 2015, making Jaipur the first city in Rajasthan with a metro rail system.

questions.q: The Western Dedicated Freight Corridor, a large part of which lies in Rajasthan, connects:
opts: Jawaharlal Nehru Port Trust to Dadri
questions.exp: The Western DFC runs from JNPT near Mumbai to Dadri near Delhi; the Rewari-Madar (Ajmer) section was among the first to be commissioned.

questions.q: BharatNet, the national broadband programme, is principally designed to provide optical fibre connectivity up to the level of:
questions.exp: BharatNet, originally the National Optical Fibre Network, aims to connect all gram panchayats with optical fibre; later phases extend connectivity to villages.

questions.q: The Jan Soochna Portal, India's first portal for proactive disclosure of government information, was launched by Rajasthan in:
questions.exp: The Jan Soochna Portal was launched on 13 September 2019 to place scheme and beneficiary information in the public domain under Section 4(2) of the RTI Act.

questions.q: RajSWAN and the Rajasthan State Data Centre together form the backbone of:
opts: State e-governance connectivity and data hosting
questions.exp: The Rajasthan State Wide Area Network and the State Data Centre provide connectivity and hosting for e-governance platforms such as e-Mitra, Jan Aadhaar and Raj SSO.

questions.q: The Jal Jeevan Mission provides for a service level of potable tap water of at least:
questions.exp: JJM, launched on 15 August 2019, guarantees 55 lpcd of drinking water of prescribed BIS 10500 quality through a functional household tap connection.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Urban Infrastructure Development Project (RUIDP) is chiefly assisted by:
questions.exp: RUIDP, operating since 2000, is an Asian Development Bank-assisted programme for urban water supply, sewerage, drainage and roads in Rajasthan's towns.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the restructuring of the Rajasthan power sector:
I. The Rajasthan State Electricity Board was constituted in 1957.
II. On unbundling in 2000, five successor companies were created.
III. The Rajasthan Electricity Regulatory Commission was created under the Electricity Act, 2003.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: RERC was created earlier, under the Rajasthan Electricity Reforms Act, 1999, and later continued under the Electricity Act, 2003. Statements I and II are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Suratgarh Super Thermal Power Station:
I. It is located in Sriganganagar district.
II. It includes supercritical units of 660 MW each.
III. It is Rajasthan's largest thermal power station by installed capacity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Suratgarh has 2,820 MW in all - six units of 250 MW and two supercritical units of 660 MW.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rawatbhata Atomic Power Station:
I. It is the only nuclear power station in Rajasthan.
II. Its first unit was built with Canadian collaboration.
III. It uses pressurised heavy water reactor technology.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. RAPS-1 was built under the Indo-Canadian agreement and introduced the PHWR line that India later indigenised.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajasthan Integrated Clean Energy Policy, 2024:
I. It was notified in 2024.
II. It subsumes the earlier separate solar and wind-hybrid energy policies of the state.
III. It includes a target for battery energy storage capacity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Of the 125 GW target for 2029-30, 10 GW is earmarked for hydro, pumped storage and battery energy storage.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajasthan Green Hydrogen Policy, 2023:
I. It was approved in 2023.
II. It sets a production target of 2,000 KTPA by 2030.
III. It provides exemption from transmission and wheeling charges for green hydrogen projects.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Green hydrogen is also a thrust sector under the Rajasthan Investment Promotion Scheme.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Bhadla Solar Park:
I. It is India's largest solar park.
II. It lies in an area carved out of the erstwhile Jodhpur district.
III. It was fully commissioned before the year 2010.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Bhadla was developed in four phases from 2015 and completed only in March 2020, so statement III is wrong. Bhadla lies in Phalodi district, carved out of Jodhpur.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about PM-KUSUM:
I. Component-A provides for decentralised ground-mounted renewable power plants of up to 2 MW.
II. Component-B provides for standalone solar agricultural pumps.
III. Component-C provides for solarisation of grid-connected agricultural pumps.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three components are correctly described. Rajasthan leads the country in implementation of Component-A.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Mukhyamantri Kisan Mitra Urja Yojana:
I. It is a scheme of the Government of Rajasthan.
II. The benefit is credited against the consumer's electricity bill.
III. It is available to metered agricultural electricity consumers.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The scheme is administered by Rajasthan's Energy Department through the three discoms.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about UDAY:
I. Participating states were to take over 75 per cent of the debt of their discoms.
II. Rajasthan was among the first three states to sign a UDAY memorandum of understanding.
III. The scheme aimed to bring AT&C losses down to about 15 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Rajasthan signed in December 2015 as the third state and carried the largest discom debt burden in the country at the time.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme:
I. It was launched in 2021.
II. It funds prepaid smart metering and loss-reduction works.
III. It aims to bring AT&C losses down to 12-15 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. RDSS has an outlay of about Rs 3.03 lakh crore and replaced the earlier distribution schemes.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Delhi-Mumbai Expressway:
I. The first stretch opened to traffic was the Sohna-Dausa-Lalsot section.
II. That section was opened in February 2023.
III. In Rajasthan the expressway passes through Dausa, Sawai Madhopur, Bundi and Kota districts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The 246 km Sohna-Dausa-Lalsot stretch was opened on 12 February 2023; the alignment in Rajasthan also touches the Khairthal-Tijara/Alwar area.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Jal Jeevan Mission in Rajasthan:
I. The Centre-State funding pattern applicable to Rajasthan is 50:50.
II. Village Water and Sanitation Committees are associated with implementation.
III. The mission was launched in 2019.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. For general-category states such as Rajasthan the sharing is 50:50; JJM 2.0 was approved in March 2026 with a target of December 2028.

questions.exp: Rajasthan has exactly three discoms - Jaipur, Ajmer and Jodhpur VVNL, all incorporated in 2000. There is no separate Kota discom.

questions.exp: Chhabra in Baran district is a COAL-based thermal project with both subcritical and supercritical units. The other three pairs are correct.

Rajasthan's wind capacity is concentrated in the Hadoti region
RRECL is the state nodal agency for renewable energy
Bhadla is India's largest solar park
questions.exp: Rajasthan's wind capacity is concentrated in the western desert districts - Jaisalmer, Jodhpur and Barmer - not in Hadoti. The other three statements are correct.

It is an eight-lane expressway expandable to twelve lanes
The Sohna-Dausa-Lalsot section was its first stretch to open

Kishangarh airport - Rajasthan's only international airport
North Western Railway - headquarters at Jaipur
questions.exp: Jaipur (Sanganer) is Rajasthan's only international airport; Kishangarh in Ajmer district is a domestic airport commissioned in 2017 under UDAN.

Arrange the following energy sector schemes in the correct chronological order of their launch:
