questions.exp: UDAY (2015), Saubhagya (2017), PM-KUSUM (2019) and PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana (2024) is the correct sequence.

chapters.title: Rural Development and Poverty Alleviation in Rajasthan
factsheet: NREGA was enacted in 2005 and came into force on 2 February 2006 from Anantapur (Andhra Pradesh); it was renamed MGNREGA on 2 October 2009.
MGNREGA guaranteed 100 days of unskilled manual wage employment per rural household per financial year as a legal right (Section 3), with 150 days in notified drought-affected areas.

MGNREGA safeguards: work within 15 days of demand or an unemployment allowance; work normally within 5 km of the village, else a 10% extra wage; at least one-third of beneficiaries to be women; social audit by the gram sabha; gram panchayat executes at least 50% of works.

Rajasthan has repeatedly topped the states in person-days generated under MGNREGA, and gives extra days of employment beyond the statutory guarantee to Sahariya (the state's only PVTG) and Kathodi families and in drought-notified and tribal sub-plan areas.

The Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025 (assent 21 December 2025) REPEALS MGNREGA 2005 and provides a statutory guarantee of 125 days of wage employment, with 60:40 Centre-State cost sharing.

Indira Gandhi Shahri Rozgar Guarantee Yojana - Rajasthan's URBAN employment guarantee, launched 9 September 2022 by the Department of Local Self Government; guarantee raised from 100 to 125 days per family per year in the 2023-24 budget; annual outlay about Rs 800 crore; job cards through Jan Aadhaar.

Rajasthan Minimum Guaranteed Income Act, 2023 - passed in July 2023; guarantees 125 days of employment a year (rural and urban) plus a guaranteed pension with an annual increment; Rajasthan was the first state to legislate a minimum guaranteed income.
NRLM was launched in June 2011 and renamed Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - NRLM (DAY-NRLM); Rajasthan's State Rural Livelihood Mission is RAJEEVIKA - the Rajasthan Grameen Aajeevika Vikas Parishad.

DAY-NRLM instruments: self-help groups, village organisations, cluster-level federations, revolving fund, community investment fund, interest subvention, SHG-bank linkage and the Lakhpati Didi initiative.
DDU-GKY (25 September 2014) is the placement-linked skill training arm of DAY-NRLM for rural youth aged 15-35; Aajeevika Grameen Express Yojana lets SHGs run rural transport services.
PMAY-Gramin was launched on 20 November 2016 from Agra, effective retrospectively from 1 April 2016, replacing the Indira Awaas Yojana.

PMAY-G unit assistance: Rs 1.20 lakh in plain areas and Rs 1.30 lakh in hilly, difficult and IAP districts; Centre-State sharing 60:40 for general states; beneficiaries identified from SECC 2011 and the Awaas+ list; 90/95 days of unskilled wage from MGNREGA is convergently available.

PMAY-Urban was launched on 25 June 2015 with four verticals - In-situ Slum Redevelopment, Credit Linked Subsidy Scheme, Affordable Housing in Partnership and Beneficiary-Led Construction. PMAY-U 2.0 was launched in 2024.

Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on 2 October 2014 with the target of an open-defecation-free India by 2 October 2019; SBM-G Phase II (2020-21 onwards) focuses on ODF Plus and solid and liquid waste management.

Jal Jeevan Mission (15 August 2019) - functional household tap connection with 55 lpcd of BIS 10500 quality water; Village Water and Sanitation Committees and Gram Panchayats operate the schemes; Centre-State share 50:50 for Rajasthan; JJM 2.0 approved March 2026, target December 2028.

Mukhyamantri Jal Swavlamban Abhiyan (MJSA) was launched on 27 January 2016 from Gardan Kheri village, Jhalawar district; it used the 'four waters' concept and community crowd-funding; Phase-I covered 3,529 villages in 295 panchayat samitis.

Watershed programmes: DPAP (1973-74), Desert Development Programme (1977-78, hot and cold arid areas), IWMP (2009-10) - all now merged into the Watershed Development Component of PMKSY. Rajasthan has the largest area under the Desert Development Programme.

National Food Security Act, 2013 covers up to 75% of the rural and 50% of the urban population; priority households get 5 kg of foodgrain per person per month and Antyodaya households 35 kg per family per month.
Antyodaya Anna Yojana was launched on 25 December 2000 for the poorest of the poor, initially covering one crore families with 25 kg (later 35 kg) of foodgrain per family per month.

Mukhyamantri Nishulk Annapurna Food Packet Yojana - launched 15 August 2023 for NFSA families; each free monthly packet has 1 kg chana dal, 1 kg sugar, 1 kg iodised salt, 1 litre soyabean refined oil, 100 g each of chilli and coriander powder and 50 g turmeric, distributed through PoS at ration shops.

Indira Rasoi Yojana was launched on 20 August 2020 with the slogan 'Koi Bhookha Na Soye' - a wholesome meal for Rs 8 with a state subsidy of Rs 17; it was renamed Shree Annapurna Rasoi Yojana in January 2024.
MPLADS (1993) gives each MP Rs 5 crore a year for local works; Rajasthan runs a parallel MLA Local Area Development scheme. Sansad Adarsh Gram Yojana was launched on 11 October 2014.
SVAMITVA (24 April 2020) uses drone survey to give record-of-rights property cards for inhabited rural abadi land.
NITI Aayog's National Multidimensional Poverty Index: Rajasthan's MPI headcount fell from 29.46% in 2015-16 (NFHS-4) to 15.31% in 2019-21 (NFHS-5).
Rajeevika works with SHGs, and the Rajasthan Rural Livelihoods Project (RRLP) is the World Bank-assisted livelihoods project focused on the tribal sub-plan and backward blocks.
Rajasthan was the FIRST state in India to introduce Panchayati Raj - inaugurated by Jawaharlal Nehru at Bagdari, Nagaur district, on 2 October 1959, following the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee report.

Rural drinking water and sanitation in Rajasthan is executed by the Public Health Engineering Department (PHED); rural development and panchayati raj schemes by the Rural Development and Panchayati Raj Department.
Rajasthan's rural relief architecture: the Rajasthan Relief Manual, girdawari-based crop loss assessment, notification of drought-affected villages, cattle camps and fodder depots.

questions.q: The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act came into force on:
questions.exp: NREGA was enacted in 2005 and came into force on 2 February 2006, launched from Anantapur district of Andhra Pradesh in 200 districts.

questions.q: The National Rural Employment Guarantee Act was renamed as MGNREGA on:
questions.exp: NREGA was renamed the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act on 2 October 2009, Gandhi Jayanti.

questions.q: Under MGNREGA, if employment was not provided within the prescribed period of the demand, the applicant became entitled to an unemployment allowance. That period was:
questions.exp: Work had to be provided within 15 days of the application, failing which the state government was liable to pay an unemployment allowance.

questions.q: Under MGNREGA, works were normally to be provided within what distance of the applicant's village, failing which an extra wage was payable?
questions.exp: Work was to be provided within a 5 km radius; if provided beyond that, an additional 10 per cent of the wage was payable to meet travel and living costs.

questions.q: Under MGNREGA, the minimum share of beneficiaries required to be women was:
questions.exp: At least one-third of the beneficiaries registered and demanding work under MGNREGA had to be women.

questions.q: The Act passed in 2025 that repeals the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005 is:
opts: Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025
questions.exp: The Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025 received presidential assent on 21 December 2025 and repeals MGNREGA, 2005.

questions.q: The statutory guarantee of wage employment under the Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025 is:
questions.exp: The 2025 Act raises the statutory guarantee from 100 days under MGNREGA to 125 days of unskilled wage employment per rural household per year, with 60:40 Centre-State cost sharing.

questions.q: Rajasthan's urban employment guarantee scheme, the Indira Gandhi Shahri Rozgar Guarantee Yojana, was launched in:
questions.exp: The scheme was launched on 9 September 2022 by the Department of Local Self Government as the urban counterpart of MGNREGA.

questions.q: The number of days of guaranteed employment per family per year under the Indira Gandhi Shahri Rozgar Guarantee Yojana was raised to:
questions.exp: The guarantee, initially 100 days, was raised to 125 days per urban family per year in the Rajasthan Budget 2023-24.

questions.q: The Indira Gandhi Shahri Rozgar Guarantee Yojana is implemented by which department of the Government of Rajasthan?
opts: Rural Development and Panchayati Raj Department
questions.exp: Being an urban scheme, it is run by the Department of Local Self Government through municipal bodies; job cards are issued on the basis of Jan Aadhaar.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Minimum Guaranteed Income Act was enacted in which year?
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Minimum Guaranteed Income Act was passed in July 2023, guaranteeing 125 days of employment a year and a guaranteed social security pension with an annual increment.

questions.q: Which particularly vulnerable tribal group of Rajasthan is given additional days of employment over and above the statutory guarantee?
questions.exp: Sahariya, the only PVTG of Rajasthan (mainly in Baran district), receives additional days of guaranteed employment; the state has also extended this concession to Kathodi families.

questions.q: The state rural livelihood mission of Rajasthan, implementing DAY-NRLM, is known as:
questions.exp: Rajeevika is the Rajasthan Grameen Aajeevika Vikas Parishad, the State Rural Livelihood Mission that mobilises rural women into self-help groups.

questions.q: The National Rural Livelihood Mission was launched in which year?
questions.exp: NRLM was launched in June 2011, restructuring the earlier Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana; it was later renamed Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - NRLM.

questions.q: The 'Lakhpati Didi' initiative is associated with which programme?
opts: Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihood Mission
questions.exp: Lakhpati Didi seeks to raise the annual household income of self-help group women to at least one lakh rupees; it works through DAY-NRLM and, in Rajasthan, through Rajeevika.

questions.q: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana is best described as:
opts: A placement-linked skill training scheme for rural youth
questions.exp: DDU-GKY, launched on 25 September 2014, is the placement-linked skill development arm of DAY-NRLM for rural youth aged 15-35 years.

questions.q: Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana - Gramin replaced which earlier housing scheme?
opts: Basic Services for the Urban Poor
questions.exp: PMAY-G, launched on 20 November 2016 from Agra and effective from 1 April 2016, replaced the Indira Awaas Yojana.

questions.q: Under PMAY-Gramin, the unit assistance for a house in plain areas is:
questions.exp: PMAY-G provides Rs 1.20 lakh in plain areas and Rs 1.30 lakh in hilly, difficult and IAP districts, shared 60:40 between Centre and general-category states.

questions.q: Beneficiaries of PMAY-Gramin are identified primarily on the basis of:
opts: Socio Economic and Caste Census 2011 with Awaas+ survey
questions.exp: PMAY-G beneficiaries are drawn from the SECC 2011 deprivation data, verified by the gram sabha, and supplemented by the Awaas+ list.

questions.q: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban) was launched in which year?
questions.exp: PMAY-Urban was launched on 25 June 2015 with four verticals - in-situ slum redevelopment, credit linked subsidy, affordable housing in partnership and beneficiary-led construction.

questions.q: The Swachh Bharat Mission was launched on:
questions.exp: SBM was launched on 2 October 2014 with the target of an open-defecation-free India by 2 October 2019, the 150th birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.q: The second phase of the Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) focuses primarily on:
opts: Construction of individual household latrines only
ODF Plus status with solid and liquid waste management
questions.exp: SBM-G Phase II, from 2020-21, aims at sustaining open-defecation-free status and adding solid and liquid waste management to make villages ODF Plus.

questions.q: The Mukhyamantri Jal Swavlamban Abhiyan was launched on 27 January 2016 from a village in which district?
questions.exp: MJSA was launched from Gardan Kheri village in Jhalawar district, using the 'four waters' concept of harvesting rainwater, surface water, groundwater and soil moisture.

questions.q: A distinctive feature of the funding of the Mukhyamantri Jal Swavlamban Abhiyan was:
questions.exp: MJSA relied heavily on community contributions and crowd-funding alongside state funds, in addition to convergence with existing watershed and MGNREGA works.

questions.q: The Desert Development Programme was launched in which year?
questions.exp: The Desert Development Programme was launched in 1977-78 for hot arid areas (Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana) and cold arid areas; Rajasthan has the largest area under it.

questions.q: Under the National Food Security Act, 2013, a priority household is entitled to foodgrain at the rate of:
questions.exp: Priority households receive 5 kg per person per month, while Antyodaya Anna Yojana households receive 35 kg per family per month.

questions.q: The Antyodaya Anna Yojana was launched on:
questions.exp: The Antyodaya Anna Yojana was launched on 25 December 2000 for the poorest of the poor, initially covering one crore families.

questions.q: The Mukhyamantri Nishulk Annapurna Food Packet Yojana of Rajasthan was launched in:
questions.exp: The scheme was launched on 15 August 2023 to give NFSA families a free monthly packet of essential commodities through fair price shops. Position as of 2026.

questions.q: The Indira Rasoi Yojana of Rajasthan, launched in 2020, was renamed as:
questions.exp: Indira Rasoi Yojana, launched on 20 August 2020 with the slogan 'Koi Bhookha Na Soye', was renamed Shree Annapurna Rasoi Yojana in January 2024.

questions.q: Under the Sansad Adarsh Gram Yojana, launched in October 2014, a Member of Parliament is required to:
opts: Contribute Rs 5 crore to each adopted village
Adopt and develop gram panchayats as model villages
Construct rural roads in the constituency
questions.exp: Under SAGY, launched on 11 October 2014 (Jayaprakash Narayan's birth anniversary), each MP adopts gram panchayats and develops them as Adarsh Grams through convergence of existing schemes; no separate funds are provided.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about MGNREGA:
I. It provided a legal guarantee of 100 days of unskilled manual wage employment to every rural household in a financial year.
II. In notified drought-affected areas the guarantee could be extended to 150 days.
III. Social audit of works was to be conducted by the gram sabha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. MGNREGA also required at least half of the works, by value, to be executed by gram panchayats.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Viksit Bharat - Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, 2025:
I. It repeals the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act, 2005.
II. It guarantees 125 days of wage employment.
III. It provides for 60:40 cost sharing between the Centre and general-category states.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Act received presidential assent on 21 December 2025 and requires states to notify implementing schemes within six months.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indira Gandhi Shahri Rozgar Guarantee Yojana:
I. It is a rural employment guarantee scheme of Rajasthan.
II. Job cards are issued on the basis of Jan Aadhaar.
III. The guarantee was raised from 100 to 125 days per family per year.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statement I is wrong - it is an URBAN employment guarantee scheme, the urban counterpart of MGNREGA, run through municipal bodies. Statements II and III are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about DAY-NRLM:
I. It was launched as the National Rural Livelihood Mission in 2011.
II. It works chiefly through women's self-help groups and their federations.
III. Its implementing agency in Rajasthan is Rajeevika.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. DAY-NRLM provides a revolving fund, community investment fund and interest subvention to SHGs federated into village organisations and cluster-level federations.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about PMAY-Gramin:
I. It was launched in 2016 and made effective from 1 April 2016.
II. Unit assistance is higher in hilly and difficult areas than in plain areas.
III. Beneficiaries may also draw unskilled wage support through convergence with the rural employment guarantee programme.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Assistance is Rs 1.20 lakh in plains and Rs 1.30 lakh in hilly, difficult and IAP areas, with 90-95 days of unskilled wage available by convergence.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Jal Jeevan Mission:
I. It was launched in 2019.
II. It provides for 55 litres per capita per day of potable water.
III. Village Water and Sanitation Committees are associated with operation and maintenance.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. JJM 2.0, approved in March 2026, extended the target for full coverage to December 2028.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Mukhyamantri Jal Swavlamban Abhiyan:
I. It was launched in 2016.
II. It was based on the 'four waters' concept.
III. Its first phase covered more than three thousand villages.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Phase-I of MJSA covered 3,529 villages across 295 panchayat samitis, beginning 27 January 2016 from Jhalawar.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Food Security Act, 2013:
I. It covers up to 75 per cent of the rural population.
II. It covers up to 50 per cent of the urban population.
III. It gives a legal entitlement to maternity benefit to pregnant and lactating women.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Act also provides a food security allowance if entitled foodgrain is not supplied, and designates the eldest woman of the household as the head for ration card purposes.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Mukhyamantri Nishulk Annapurna Food Packet Yojana:
I. The packet is provided free of cost to eligible families.
II. It is distributed through fair price shops using point-of-sale machines.
III. It is available only to families outside the National Food Security Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statement III is wrong - the packet is meant primarily for NFSA families. Statements I and II are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about poverty in Rajasthan:
I. NITI Aayog's National Multidimensional Poverty Index measures deprivation in health, education and standard of living.
II. Rajasthan's multidimensional poverty headcount declined between 2015-16 and 2019-21.
III. The National MPI uses National Family Health Survey data.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Rajasthan's MPI headcount fell from 29.46 per cent in 2015-16 to 15.31 per cent in 2019-21.

questions.q:

questions.exp: Antyodaya Anna Yojana 2000, Swachh Bharat Mission 2014, PMAY-Gramin 2016 and Jal Jeevan Mission 2019.

questions.q:

D. Annapurna Food Packet Yojana   4. 2020
questions.exp: MJSA 2016, Indira Rasoi 2020, Indira Gandhi Shahri Rozgar Guarantee Yojana 2022 and the Annapurna Food Packet Yojana 2023.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Programme)   List-II (Principal focus)
A. DDU-GKY   1. Rural housing
B. PMAY-G   2. Placement-linked skill training
C. SVAMITVA   3. Property cards for abadi land
D. Rajeevika   4. Self-help group based livelihoods
questions.exp: DDU-GKY trains and places rural youth, PMAY-G builds rural houses, SVAMITVA issues property cards after drone survey, and Rajeevika runs the SHG-based livelihoods mission.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Area development programme)   List-II (Year of launch)
A. Drought Prone Areas Programme   1. 2009-10
B. Desert Development Programme   2. 1973-74
C. Integrated Watershed Management Programme   3. 2000
D. Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana   4. 1977-78
questions.exp: DPAP 1973-74, DDP 1977-78, IWMP 2009-10 and PMGSY 2000. DPAP, DDP and IWMP are now merged into the Watershed Development Component of PMKSY.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Food security instrument)   List-II (Entitlement/feature)
A. Antyodaya Anna Yojana   1. 5 kg per person per month
B. NFSA priority household   2. Free monthly packet of essential commodities
C. Annapurna Food Packet Yojana   3. 35 kg per family per month
D. Shree Annapurna Rasoi Yojana   4. Cooked meal at a subsidised price
questions.exp: AAY gives 35 kg per family, NFSA priority households 5 kg per person, the Annapurna Food Packet is a free commodity packet and Shree Annapurna Rasoi serves a subsidised cooked meal.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Employment programme)   List-II (Feature)
A. MGNREGA   1. Urban employment guarantee of Rajasthan
B. Indira Gandhi Shahri Rozgar Guarantee Yojana   2. Statutory guarantee of 125 days from 2025
C. VB-G RAM G Act, 2025   3. 100 days rural wage employment guarantee
D. DDU-GKY   4. Placement-linked skill training
questions.exp: MGNREGA guaranteed 100 days, the Rajasthan urban scheme is IGSRGY, the 2025 central Act raises the guarantee to 125 days and DDU-GKY is a skilling programme.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Scheme)   List-II (Implementing department in Rajasthan)
A. Indira Gandhi Shahri Rozgar Guarantee Yojana   1. Food and Civil Supplies
B. Jal Jeevan Mission (rural)   2. Local Self Government
C. Annapurna Food Packet Yojana   3. Rural Development and Panchayati Raj
D. MGNREGA   4. Public Health Engineering
questions.exp: The urban employment scheme is with Local Self Government, rural piped water with PHED, the food packet with Food and Civil Supplies and MGNREGA with Rural Development and Panchayati Raj.

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT a feature of MGNREGA?
opts: Guarantee of 100 days of wage employment per rural household
Unemployment allowance if work is not provided in time
Reservation of at least one-third of works for women
Guarantee of skilled employment to one member of every household
questions.exp: MGNREGA guaranteed UNSKILLED manual wage employment, not skilled employment. The other three were genuine features; women were to be at least one-third of beneficiaries.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: MPLADS - Rs 25 crore per MP per year
Rajeevika - state rural livelihood mission of Rajasthan
SVAMITVA - property cards using drone survey
Sansad Adarsh Gram Yojana - adoption of gram panchayats by MPs
questions.exp: MPLADS provides Rs 5 crore per Member of Parliament per year, not Rs 25 crore. The other three pairs are correct.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a vertical of Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (Urban) as launched in 2015?
questions.exp: The four original verticals were ISSR, CLSS, AHP and Beneficiary-Led Construction. Affordable Rental Housing Complexes came later, in 2020, as a separate sub-scheme.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Indira Rasoi Yojana of Rajasthan is NOT correct?
opts: Its slogan was 'Koi Bhookha Na Soye'
It provided a subsidised cooked meal
It was launched by the Rural Development Department for villages only
questions.exp: Indira Rasoi was an URBAN scheme run through urban local bodies under the Local Self Government Department, not a village scheme of the Rural Development Department.

questions.q: Which one of the following items is NOT part of the packet distributed under the Mukhyamantri Nishulk Annapurna Food Packet Yojana?
questions.exp: The packet contains chana dal, sugar, iodised salt, edible oil, chilli powder, coriander powder and turmeric. Wheat and rice come separately under NFSA.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of programme and its objective is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Swachh Bharat Mission (Gramin) - rural housing for the poor
Desert Development Programme - mitigating adverse effects of desertification
Drought Prone Areas Programme - drought-proofing of fragile areas
Integrated Watershed Management Programme - watershed based land and water development
questions.exp: SBM (Gramin) is a sanitation programme aimed at eliminating open defecation, not a housing programme; rural housing is PMAY-G.

questions.q:
Arrange the following schemes in the correct chronological order of their launch:
I. Antyodaya Anna Yojana
II. MGNREGA (coming into force)
III. Swachh Bharat Mission
IV. Jal Jeevan Mission
questions.exp: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (2000), MGNREGA in force (2006), Swachh Bharat Mission (2014) and Jal Jeevan Mission (2019).

questions.q:
Arrange the following Rajasthan schemes in the correct chronological order of their launch:
I. Mukhyamantri Jal Swavlamban Abhiyan
II. Indira Rasoi Yojana
III. Indira Gandhi Shahri Rozgar Guarantee Yojana
IV. Mukhyamantri Nishulk Annapurna Food Packet Yojana
questions.exp: MJSA (2016), Indira Rasoi (2020), Indira Gandhi Shahri Rozgar Guarantee Yojana (2022) and the Annapurna Food Packet Yojana (2023).

chapters.title: Social Services in Rajasthan: Education, Health, Nutrition
factsheet: Rajasthan literacy (Census 2011): 66.11% — male 79.19%, female 52.12%; male-female gap 27.07 percentage points, the widest among major states.
Highest literacy district (Census 2011): Kota (76.56%); lowest: Jalore (54.86%), which also has the lowest female literacy.
Rajasthan sex ratio (Census 2011): 928 females per 1,000 males; child sex ratio (0-6 years): 888.
NFHS-5 (2019-21) Rajasthan: TFR 2.0 (below the replacement level of 2.1); sex ratio 1,020 females per 1,000 males; sex ratio at birth 929 (NFHS-4: 919).
SRS 2019-21: India's MMR is 93 per lakh live births; SRS 2021: India's IMR 27, U5MR 31, NMR 19 — Rajasthan's IMR remains above the national figure.
Right to Health Act, 2022 — Rajasthan is the FIRST Indian state to legislate a right to health; passed by the Assembly on 21 March 2023, Governor's assent 12 April 2023 (Act No. 7 of 2023).

Health insurance chain: Bhamashah Swasthya Bima Yojana (announced 13 Dec 2015, effective 30 Jan 2016) -> Ayushman Bharat Mahatma Gandhi Rajasthan Swasthya Bima Yojana (1 Sept 2019) -> Mukhyamantri Chiranjeevi Swasthya Bima Yojana (1 May 2021) -> Mukhyamantri Ayushman Arogya Yojana (renamed 2024).

Chiranjeevi cover: Rs 5 lakh (2021) -> Rs 10 lakh (1 May 2022) -> Rs 25 lakh (Feb 2023); annual premium Rs 850 for the paid category; free for NFSA, SECC-2011, small & marginal farmers and contractual state employees.
Mukhyamantri Chiranjeevi Durghatna Bima Yojana — accidental death/disability cover raised to Rs 10 lakh.
Mukhyamantri Nishulk Dawa Yojana — 2 October 2011; Mukhyamantri Nishulk Janch Yojana — 7 April 2013 (World Health Day); both supplied through the Rajasthan Medical Services Corporation (RMSC, 2011).
Mukhyamantri Bal Gopal Yojana (29 November 2022) — milk to Class 1-8 in government schools; 150 ml for Class 1-5 and 200 ml for Class 6-8 (reconstituted from milk powder).
Annapurna Doodh Yojana — launched 2 July 2018 at Dehmi Kalan (Jaipur); milk three days a week to government school children.
Mid Day Meal Scheme (started 1995 as the National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education) was renamed PM POSHAN in 2021.
Gargi Puraskar — Rs 3,000 to girls scoring 75%+ in Class 10, disbursed on Basant Panchami through the Balika Shiksha Foundation; Balika Protsahan Puraskar — Rs 5,000 for 75%+ in Class 12.
Kali Bai Bheel Medhavi Chhatra Scooty Yojana — scooters to meritorious girl students; named after Kalibai Bheel, the martyr of Rastapal (Dungarpur), 19 June 1947.
Devnarayan Chhatra Scooty Vitaran Yojana — for girls of the Most Backward Classes (Gurjar, Banjara, Gadia Lohar, Raika-Rebari, Gadaria).

Mukhyamantri Anuprati Coaching Yojana — free competitive-examination coaching for SC/ST/OBC/MBC/EWS/minority students; the original Anuprati scheme dates to 2005 and the revamped coaching scheme to 2021-22.

Swami Vivekananda Government Model Schools — one per panchayat samiti (block), English medium on the CBSE pattern; Adarsh Vidyalaya — one per gram panchayat; Mahatma Gandhi Government English Medium Schools from 2019.
Shala Darpan — MIS portal for government schools; Shala Darshan — for private schools; RTE Act 2009 reserves 25% of entry-class seats in private unaided schools for EWS/disadvantaged children.

University of Rajasthan, Jaipur (1947, originally the University of Rajputana) is the oldest university of the state; Vardhman Mahaveer Open University, Kota (1987, as Kota Open University) was the first open university.
SMS Medical College, Jaipur (1947) is the oldest medical college of Rajasthan; the Rajasthan University of Health Sciences (RUHS), Jaipur was set up in 2005.
Rajasthan Skill and Livelihoods Development Corporation (RSLDC) is the state's nodal skilling agency; Samagra Shiksha is implemented through the Rajasthan Council of School Education.
ICDS — launched 2 October 1975; anganwadi centres are run by the Women & Child Development Department; Poshan Abhiyaan was launched by the Prime Minister on 8 March 2018 from Jhunjhunu, Rajasthan.
Indira Gandhi Matritva Poshan Yojana — Rs 6,000 in five instalments to a woman on the birth of her second child; PMMVY (central) gives Rs 5,000 for the first living child.
Rajasthan's public health structure: Sub-Centre -> Primary Health Centre -> Community Health Centre -> Sub-district/District Hospital; the National Health Mission is the umbrella programme.

questions.q: As per Census 2011, the literacy rate of Rajasthan was:
questions.exp: Rajasthan's literacy rate in Census 2011 was 66.11% (male 79.19%, female 52.12%), below the all-India figure of 74.04%.

questions.q: According to Census 2011, the female literacy rate of Rajasthan was:
questions.exp: Female literacy in Rajasthan was 52.12% against male literacy of 79.19% — a gap of 27.07 percentage points, the widest among the major Indian states.

questions.q: Which district of Rajasthan recorded the highest literacy rate in Census 2011?
questions.exp: Kota recorded the highest literacy rate (76.56%) in Census 2011; Jhunjhunu and Sikar followed. Jalore had the lowest at 54.86%.

questions.q: As per Census 2011, the district of Rajasthan with the lowest literacy rate as well as the lowest female literacy rate was:
questions.exp: Jalore had the lowest overall literacy (54.86%) and the lowest female literacy in Rajasthan in Census 2011.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Mukhyamantri Bal Gopal Yojana of Rajasthan:
I. It provides milk to children of Classes 1 to 8 in government schools.
II. It was launched in the year 2022.
III. Children of Classes 1 to 5 receive 150 ml of milk.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Mukhyamantri Bal Gopal Yojana was launched on 29 November 2022 to supply milk (reconstituted from milk powder) to Class 1-8 children of government schools — 150 ml for Classes 1-5 and 200 ml for Classes 6-8.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Annapurna Doodh Yojana of Rajasthan:
I. It was launched in the year 2018.
II. Under it milk was provided to children of government schools three days a week.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: The Annapurna Doodh Yojana was launched on 2 July 2018 at Dehmi Kalan in Jaipur district and supplied milk to government school children three days a week; milk supply was later continued through the Mukhyamantri Bal Gopal Yojana (2022).

questions.q: The Gargi Puraskar of Rajasthan is awarded to girl students who secure at least 75 per cent marks in:
questions.exp: Gargi Puraskar is given to girls scoring 75% or more in the Class 10 board examination; it is disbursed on Basant Panchami through the Balika Shiksha Foundation. The Balika Protsahan Puraskar is for 75%+ in Class 12.

questions.q: The Kali Bai Bheel Medhavi Chhatra Scooty Yojana of Rajasthan is named after a martyr associated with which place?
questions.exp: Kalibai Bheel was killed on 19 June 1947 at Rastapal in Dungarpur district while trying to save her teacher Sengabhai during the tribal education movement. The scheme gives scooters to meritorious girl students.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Scheme)   List-II (Beneficiary group)
A. Devnarayan Chhatra Scooty Vitaran Yojana   1. Meritorious girl students in general
B. Kali Bai Bheel Medhavi Chhatra Scooty Yojana   2. Girls of Most Backward Classes
C. Balika Protsahan Puraskar   3. Children of Classes 1 to 8 in government schools
D. Mukhyamantri Bal Gopal Yojana   4. Girls scoring 75 per cent in Class 12
questions.exp: The Devnarayan scheme is reserved for girls of the Most Backward Classes (Gurjar, Banjara, Gadia Lohar, Raika-Rebari, Gadaria); the Kali Bai Bheel scheme is a general merit scooty scheme; Balika Protsahan Puraskar rewards Class 12 performance and Bal Gopal supplies milk in schools.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Mukhyamantri Anuprati Coaching Yojana of Rajasthan:
I. It provides free coaching for competitive examinations.
II. Students of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, OBC, MBC, EWS and minority communities are eligible.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: The Anuprati scheme, which dates back to 2005 and was recast as the Mukhyamantri Anuprati Coaching Yojana in 2021-22, gives free coaching for examinations such as RAS, UPSC, IIT-JEE and NEET to students of SC/ST/OBC/MBC/EWS and minority communities.

questions.q: The 'Shala Darpan' portal of the Government of Rajasthan is associated with:
questions.exp: Shala Darpan is the management information system portal for government schools of Rajasthan; the corresponding portal for private schools is Shala Darshan.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Scheme)   List-II (Benefit)
A. Gargi Puraskar   1. Free coaching for competitive examinations
B. Anuprati Yojana   2. Cash award for 75% marks in Class 10
C. Kali Bai Bheel Yojana   3. Milk in government schools
D. Bal Gopal Yojana   4. Scooters to meritorious girl students
questions.exp: Gargi Puraskar rewards Class 10 performance, Anuprati provides free coaching, the Kali Bai Bheel scheme gives scooters and Bal Gopal supplies milk in schools.

questions.q: The Swami Vivekananda Government Model Schools of Rajasthan are established at the level of:
questions.exp: Swami Vivekananda Government Model Schools are English-medium CBSE-pattern schools opened one per panchayat samiti (block); Adarsh Vidyalayas are opened at the gram panchayat level.

questions.q: Under the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009, private unaided schools must reserve seats in the entry class for children of weaker and disadvantaged sections to the extent of:
questions.exp: Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act, 2009 requires private unaided schools to admit at least 25% of the strength of the entry class from weaker and disadvantaged sections of the neighbourhood.

questions.q: Which one of the following is the oldest university of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The University of Rajasthan, Jaipur was established in 1947 as the University of Rajputana and renamed in 1956; it is the oldest university in the state.

questions.q: Vardhman Mahaveer Open University, Kota is significant because it is:
opts: The first agricultural university of Rajasthan
The first open university of Rajasthan
The first private university of Rajasthan
The first technical university of Rajasthan
questions.exp: Established in 1987 as the Kota Open University and later renamed Vardhman Mahaveer Open University, it was Rajasthan's first open university.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Balika Protsahan Puraskar — 75% marks in Class 12
Adarsh Vidyalaya — One school per gram panchayat
Devnarayan Scooty Yojana — Scheduled Tribe girls
questions.exp: The Devnarayan Chhatra Scooty Vitaran Yojana is meant for girls of the Most Backward Classes, not for Scheduled Tribe girls. The other three pairs are correct.

questions.q: The Mid Day Meal Scheme, started in 1995 as the National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education, has been renamed as:
questions.exp: The Mid Day Meal Scheme was renamed PM POSHAN (Pradhan Mantri Poshan Shakti Nirman) in 2021. Poshan Abhiyaan is a separate nutrition mission.

questions.q: The nodal corporation for skill development in Rajasthan is:
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Skill and Livelihoods Development Corporation (RSLDC) is the nodal agency for skill training in the state. RIICO handles industrial infrastructure, RUIDP urban infrastructure and RMSC medical procurement.

questions.q:
Arrange the following educational initiatives of Rajasthan in the correct chronological order of their commencement:
I. Annapurna Doodh Yojana
II. Mukhyamantri Bal Gopal Yojana
III. Mahatma Gandhi Government English Medium Schools
IV. Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act
questions.exp: The RTE Act came into force in 2010, Annapurna Doodh Yojana in 2018, Mahatma Gandhi Government English Medium Schools from 2019 and Mukhyamantri Bal Gopal Yojana in 2022.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Institution/Programme)   List-II (Function)
A. Mukhyamantri Uchch Shiksha Chhatravriti Yojana   1. Nodal skilling agency of the state
B. Rajasthan Skill and Livelihoods Development Corporation   2. Scholarship for higher education
C. Rajasthan Medical Services Corporation   3. MIS portal for government schools
D. Shala Darpan   4. Procurement of drugs and equipment
questions.exp: The Mukhyamantri Uchch Shiksha Chhatravriti Yojana funds higher education of meritorious students from weaker families; RSLDC is the skilling agency; RMSC procures drugs; Shala Darpan is the school MIS portal.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Mahatma Gandhi Government Schools of Rajasthan:
I. They impart education through the English medium.
II. The first such schools were opened in the year 2019.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Mahatma Gandhi Government Schools are English-medium government schools; the programme began in 2019 with schools opened in Jaipur and subsequently extended across the state.

questions.q: The oldest medical college of Rajasthan is:
questions.exp: Sawai Man Singh (SMS) Medical College, Jaipur, established in 1947, is the oldest medical college of Rajasthan. The Rajasthan University of Health Sciences was set up at Jaipur in 2005.

questions.q: The Bhamashah Swasthya Bima Yojana of Rajasthan came into effect in the year:
questions.exp: Announced on 13 December 2015, the Bhamashah Swasthya Bima Yojana became operational on 30 January 2016. It was linked to the Bhamashah card and was the forerunner of later state health insurance schemes.

questions.q: The 'Ayushman Bharat Mahatma Gandhi Rajasthan Swasthya Bima Yojana' was launched in Rajasthan on:
questions.exp: The scheme was launched on 1 September 2019, replacing the Bhamashah Swasthya Bima Yojana, and was itself superseded by the Mukhyamantri Chiranjeevi Swasthya Bima Yojana in 2021.

questions.q: The Mukhyamantri Chiranjeevi Swasthya Bima Yojana was implemented in Rajasthan with effect from:
questions.exp: Registration under the scheme opened on 1 April 2021 and the insurance benefit became operative from 1 May 2021. It has since been renamed the Mukhyamantri Ayushman Arogya Yojana.

questions.q:
Arrange the following health insurance schemes of Rajasthan in correct chronological order of their commencement:
I. Mukhyamantri Chiranjeevi Swasthya Bima Yojana
II. Bhamashah Swasthya Bima Yojana
III. Ayushman Bharat Mahatma Gandhi Rajasthan Swasthya Bima Yojana
IV. Mukhyamantri Ayushman Arogya Yojana
questions.exp: Bhamashah Swasthya Bima Yojana (2016) came first, then Ayushman Bharat Mahatma Gandhi Rajasthan Swasthya Bima Yojana (2019), then Chiranjeevi (2021), which was renamed Mukhyamantri Ayushman Arogya Yojana in 2024.

questions.q: The Mukhyamantri Chiranjeevi Swasthya Bima Yojana has been renamed by the Government of Rajasthan as:
questions.exp: The scheme was renamed the Mukhyamantri Ayushman Arogya Yojana (MAA Yojana) in 2024 by the state government; the earlier name was Mukhyamantri Chiranjeevi Swasthya Bima Yojana (as of 2026).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Mukhyamantri Ayushman Arogya Yojana of Rajasthan:
I. Its treatment cover was raised to Rs 25 lakh per family per year.
II. It was earlier known as the Mukhyamantri Chiranjeevi Swasthya Bima Yojana.
III. Families of the NFSA category are covered without paying any premium.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The cover moved from Rs 5 lakh (2021) to Rs 10 lakh (2022) and to Rs 25 lakh (February 2023); the scheme was renamed Mukhyamantri Ayushman Arogya Yojana in 2024; NFSA, SECC-2011, small and marginal farmer and contractual state employee families are covered free of premium.

questions.q: Under the Mukhyamantri Ayushman Arogya Yojana (earlier Chiranjeevi Yojana), the annual premium payable by a family of the paid category is:
questions.exp: Families not covered under the free categories pay an annual premium of Rs 850 to join the scheme; the balance of the premium is borne by the state government.

questions.q: Under the Mukhyamantri Chiranjeevi Durghatna Bima Yojana of Rajasthan, the accidental insurance cover available to a beneficiary family is:
questions.exp: The accident insurance cover under the Chiranjeevi Durghatna Bima Yojana was enhanced to Rs 10 lakh; it is separate from the hospitalisation cover of the main health insurance scheme.

questions.q: Which Indian state became the first to enact a law guaranteeing the right to health?
questions.exp: Rajasthan became the first state in India to enact a Right to Health law — the Rajasthan Right to Health Act, 2022 — passed by the Assembly on 21 March 2023 and assented to on 12 April 2023.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajasthan Right to Health Act, 2022:
I. It was passed by the Rajasthan Legislative Assembly in March 2023.
II. It guarantees emergency treatment without prior payment of fees.
III. Rajasthan was the second state in India to enact such a law.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Act was passed on 21 March 2023 and guarantees, among other rights, emergency treatment and care without prepayment. Rajasthan was the FIRST — not the second — state to enact such a law, so statement III is wrong.

questions.q: The Mukhyamantri Nishulk Dawa Yojana was launched in Rajasthan on:
questions.exp: The free medicine scheme was launched on 2 October 2011; the companion Mukhyamantri Nishulk Janch Yojana (free diagnostics) was launched on 7 April 2013, World Health Day.

questions.q: The procurement and distribution of medicines under Rajasthan's free medicine scheme is carried out by:
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Medical Services Corporation (RMSC), set up in 2011, procures, tests and distributes drugs and equipment for the state's free medicine and free diagnostics schemes.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The Mukhyamantri Chiranjeevi Swasthya Bima Yojana was implemented from 1 May 2021, not 2019. The Ayushman Bharat Mahatma Gandhi Rajasthan Swasthya Bima Yojana was the 2019 scheme.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Scheme)   List-II (Year of commencement)
A. Mukhyamantri Nishulk Dawa Yojana   1. 2013
B. Mukhyamantri Nishulk Janch Yojana   2. 2011
C. Bhamashah Swasthya Bima Yojana   3. 2021
D. Mukhyamantri Chiranjeevi Swasthya Bima Yojana   4. 2016
questions.exp: Free medicines 2011, free diagnostics 2013, Bhamashah Swasthya Bima 2016 and Chiranjeevi 2021 — the four milestones of Rajasthan's health entitlement architecture.

questions.q: According to NFHS-5 (2019-21), the Total Fertility Rate of Rajasthan was:
questions.exp: Rajasthan's TFR fell to 2.0 in NFHS-5 (2019-21), below the replacement level of 2.1, compared with a higher rate in NFHS-4 (2015-16).

questions.q: As per NFHS-5 (2019-21), the sex ratio at birth in Rajasthan (females per 1,000 males born in the last five years) was:
questions.exp: The sex ratio at birth in Rajasthan improved from 919 in NFHS-4 to 929 in NFHS-5. The overall sex ratio of the population in NFHS-5 was 1,020 females per 1,000 males.

questions.q: As per Census 2011, the sex ratio and the child sex ratio (0-6 years) of Rajasthan were respectively:
questions.exp: Rajasthan's sex ratio in Census 2011 was 928 females per 1,000 males and the child sex ratio (0-6 years) was 888, both below the national averages of 943 and 919.

questions.q: As per the Sample Registration System (SRS) special bulletin for 2019-21, India's Maternal Mortality Ratio was:
questions.exp: India's MMR for 2019-21 was 93 per lakh live births, down from 130 in 2014-16. Rajasthan's MMR remains above the national average.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the public health infrastructure of Rajasthan:
I. The sub-centre is the most peripheral unit of the rural health delivery system.
II. The Community Health Centre functions as a referral centre for Primary Health Centres.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: The rural health hierarchy runs Sub-Centre -> Primary Health Centre -> Community Health Centre -> Sub-district/District Hospital; the CHC is the first referral unit above the PHC.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Mukhyamantri Ayushman Arogya Yojana is NOT correct?
opts: It provides cashless treatment in empanelled government and private hospitals
Registration is linked to the Jan Aadhaar card
It is implemented by the Medical, Health and Family Welfare Department
It provides only out-patient consultation and no hospitalisation cover
questions.exp: The scheme is essentially a hospitalisation (in-patient) cover of up to Rs 25 lakh per family per year, delivered cashlessly through empanelled hospitals and linked to Jan Aadhaar; it is not an OPD-only scheme.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the health insurance schemes of Rajasthan:
I. The Bhamashah Swasthya Bima Yojana was linked to the Bhamashah card.
II. Under the Mukhyamantri Ayushman Arogya Yojana, the treatment cover is Rs 25 lakh per family per year.
III. The Ayushman Bharat Mahatma Gandhi Rajasthan Swasthya Bima Yojana preceded the Chiranjeevi Yojana.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct: Bhamashah Swasthya Bima (2016) worked through the Bhamashah card, AB-MGRSBY (2019) preceded Chiranjeevi (2021), and the present cover under the renamed Mukhyamantri Ayushman Arogya Yojana is Rs 25 lakh.

questions.q: The Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) scheme was launched in India on:
questions.exp: ICDS was launched on 2 October 1975 and is delivered through anganwadi centres; in Rajasthan it is implemented by the Women and Child Development Department.

questions.q: The Poshan Abhiyaan (National Nutrition Mission) was launched by the Prime Minister on 8 March 2018 from which place?
questions.exp: Poshan Abhiyaan was launched from Jhunjhunu in Rajasthan on 8 March 2018 (International Women's Day). Beti Bachao Beti Padhao had earlier been launched from Panipat, Haryana.

questions.q: Under the Indira Gandhi Matritva Poshan Yojana of Rajasthan, financial assistance is provided on the birth of the:
questions.exp: The Indira Gandhi Matritva Poshan Yojana gives Rs 6,000 in five instalments to a woman on the birth of her second child, complementing the central PMMVY which covers the first living child.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Programme)   List-II (Principal target group)
A. ICDS   1. Pregnant women for the second child in Rajasthan
B. PM POSHAN   2. Children below six years and mothers
C. Indira Gandhi Matritva Poshan Yojana   3. Adolescent girls
D. Scheme for Adolescent Girls   4. School children up to Class 8
questions.exp: ICDS serves children under six and mothers, PM POSHAN feeds school children up to Class 8, the Indira Gandhi Matritva Poshan Yojana covers the second child in Rajasthan, and the Scheme for Adolescent Girls targets girls aged 14-18.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: PM POSHAN — Mid Day Meal Scheme renamed
Indira Gandhi Matritva Poshan Yojana — Assistance for the first child
questions.exp: The Indira Gandhi Matritva Poshan Yojana of Rajasthan gives assistance on the birth of the SECOND child; assistance for the first living child is given under the central PMMVY.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about nutrition programmes in Rajasthan:
I. Poshan Abhiyaan aims to reduce stunting, undernutrition and anaemia.
II. Supplementary nutrition under ICDS is provided to children up to six years of age.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Poshan Abhiyaan targets stunting, undernutrition, anaemia and low birth weight through convergence; ICDS supplementary nutrition covers children in the 0-6 years age group along with pregnant and lactating women.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about education indicators of Rajasthan is NOT correct?
opts: Rajasthan's literacy rate in Census 2011 was below the all-India average
The male-female literacy gap in Rajasthan is among the widest in India
Kota recorded the highest district literacy rate in Census 2011
Rajasthan's female literacy rate in Census 2011 exceeded 60 per cent
questions.exp: Female literacy in Rajasthan in Census 2011 was 52.12 per cent, well below 60 per cent. The other three statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajasthan Right to Health Act:
I. It creates a State Health Authority and District Health Authorities for implementation.
II. It draws upon Article 47 of the Constitution relating to the duty of the State to raise the level of nutrition and public health.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: The Act sets up a State Health Authority and District Health Authorities to implement and monitor the guaranteed rights, and is anchored in Article 47 read with Article 21 of the Constitution.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Balika Shiksha Foundation of Rajasthan:
I. It disburses the Gargi Puraskar and the Balika Protsahan Puraskar.
II. The Gargi Puraskar is distributed on the occasion of Basant Panchami.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: The Balika Shiksha Foundation administers the Gargi Puraskar (75%+ in Class 10) and the Balika Protsahan Puraskar (75%+ in Class 12); Gargi Puraskar amounts are handed over on Basant Panchami.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of Rajasthan's health institutions is NOT correctly matched?
opts: RMSC — Procurement of drugs and equipment
RUHS — Affiliating university for health sciences
questions.exp: Sardar Patel Medical College is located at Bikaner; the medical college at Udaipur is RNT (Rabindra Nath Tagore) Medical College.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Indicator for Rajasthan)   List-II (Value and source)
A. Literacy rate   1. 928 (Census 2011)
B. Sex ratio   2. 2.0 (NFHS-5)
C. Total Fertility Rate   3. 66.11 per cent (Census 2011)
D. Child sex ratio (0-6)   4. 888 (Census 2011)
questions.exp: Census 2011 gives Rajasthan's literacy as 66.11 per cent, sex ratio 928 and child sex ratio 888; NFHS-5 (2019-21) records a TFR of 2.0.

chapters.title: Welfare Schemes of Rajasthan
factsheet: Jan Aadhaar Yojana — announced in the 2019-20 state budget, launched 18 December 2019 and implemented from 1 April 2020; a 10-digit family identity number with the motto 'One Number, One Card, One Identity'; it replaced the Bhamashah Yojana (2008; relaunched 15 August 2014) and is the delivery backbone for state DBT.
Jan Soochna Portal — launched 13 September 2019, India's first portal for proactive disclosure of scheme data under Section 4(2) of the RTI Act; e-Mitra kiosks are the citizen-service delivery arm.
Mukhyamantri Rajshri Yojana — 1 June 2016; Rs 50,000 to a girl child in six instalments from birth to passing Class 12; Women & Child Development Department.
Lado Protsahan Yojana — launched 1 August 2024; a savings bond of Rs 1,50,000 released in seven instalments up to graduation/age 21; the Mukhyamantri Rajshri Yojana was merged into it (as of 2026).

Indira Mahila Shakti Udaan Yojana (also called I Am Shakti Udaan Yojana) — free sanitary napkins to women and adolescent girls; the umbrella Indira Mahila Shakti Yojana covers training, skilling and enterprise credit for women.

Palanhar Yojana (2005) — Social Justice & Empowerment Department; monthly maintenance to a relative/guardian ('palanhar') who raises an orphaned or destitute child; it began with children of parents sentenced to death or life imprisonment.
Rajasthan Mahila Nidhi (2022) — a credit cooperative federation lending to women's self-help groups, run with Rajeevika.

Social security pensions of Rajasthan: Mukhyamantri Vridhjan Samman Pension (women 55+, men 58+), Mukhyamantri Ekal Nari Samman Pension (widow/divorced/abandoned women 18+), Mukhyamantri Vishesh Yogyajan Samman Pension (40%+ disability), Mukhyamantri Laghu evam Simant Krishak Vriddhavastha Samman Pension — all through the RajSSP portal (ssp.rajasthan.gov.in).

Rajasthan Minimum Guaranteed Income Act, 2023 — passed in July 2023; Rajasthan is the first state to legally guarantee minimum income; 125 days of guaranteed employment (MGNREGA 100 + 25 extra in rural areas; 125 days urban under the Indira Gandhi Shahri Rozgar Guarantee Yojana), a minimum pension of Rs 1,000 per month, and a 15% annual increase in pension from 2024-25.
Indira Gandhi Shahri Rozgar Guarantee Yojana — launched 9 September 2022, India's largest urban employment guarantee programme; days of work raised from 100 to 125.
Indira Rasoi Yojana — launched 20 August 2020 on the slogan 'Koi Bhookha Na Soye', meal at Rs 8 per plate; renamed Shree Annapurna Rasoi Yojana on 5 January 2024 (as of 2026).
Annapurna Food Packet Yojana — launched 2023 through Mahangai Rahat Camps, free monthly food packets to NFSA ration-card families.

Mukhyamantri Anuprati Coaching Yojana — free coaching for SC/ST/OBC/MBC/EWS/minority students; Dr. Ambedkar DBT Voucher Yojana — food and accommodation assistance to such students studying at district/divisional headquarters.
Devnarayan Yojana — schemes (scooty, hostels, incentives) for the Most Backward Classes; Tribal Area Development (TAD) Department has its headquarters at Udaipur.
Scheduled Areas of Rajasthan: Banswara, Dungarpur and Pratapgarh districts entirely, plus parts of Udaipur, Rajsamand, Chittorgarh, Pali and Sirohi.
Van Dhan Vikas Kendras are implemented by TRIFED under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs for value addition to minor forest produce.

Rajasthan Silicosis Policy — 2019; Rajasthan was the FIRST state in India with a dedicated silicosis policy; certified patients get one-time assistance of Rs 3 lakh and Rs 2 lakh is paid to dependants on death, along with pension and other social security benefits.

'Vishesh Yogyajan' is the term used in Rajasthan for persons with disabilities; the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 recognises 21 disabilities and provides 4% reservation in government jobs.
Varishth Nagrik Tirth Yatra Yojana (earlier Mukhyamantri Vridhjan Tirth Yatra Yojana) — free pilgrimage by rail and air for senior citizens, run by the Devasthan Department.

Rajasthan Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board — funded by a 1% cess on construction cost under the BOCW Cess Act, 1996; schemes include Shubhshakti (Rs 55,000 for daughters/women workers), Nirman Shramik Sulabhya Awas (Rs 1.5 lakh housing assistance), Prasuti Sahayata and Nirman Shramik Shiksha evam Kaushal Vikas Yojana.
e-Shram portal — launched 26 August 2021 by the Union Ministry of Labour & Employment; national database of unorganised workers with a 12-digit Universal Account Number.

Mukhyamantri Yuva Sambal Yojana — unemployment allowance to educated unemployed youth for a maximum of two years, conditional on a four-hour daily internship for five days a week; family income limit Rs 2 lakh.
Indira Gandhi Shahri Credit Card Yojana (2021) — interest-free loan of up to Rs 50,000 to street vendors and informal-sector workers; the central counterpart for street vendors is PM SVANidhi.
Mukhyamantri Kisan Mitra Urja Yojana — launched 17 July 2021; subsidy of up to Rs 1,000 per month (Rs 12,000 a year) on farm electricity bills.
Rajasthan Kisan Kalyan Kosh — a dedicated corpus for farmer welfare set up in 2020-21; Mukhyamantri Krishak Sathi Yojana compensates farmers and farm labourers for accidental death or injury.
PM-KISAN gives Rs 6,000 a year in three equal instalments; Rajasthan tops it up under the Mukhyamantri Kisan Samman Nidhi.

Beti Bachao Beti Padhao was launched on 22 January 2015 from Panipat (Haryana); Sakhi One Stop Centres serve women affected by violence; Mukhyamantri Kanyadan Yojana gives marriage assistance to daughters of poor families.

Rajasthan Scheduled Castes & Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Cooperative Corporation provides subsidised credit for self-employment to SC/ST families; the Rajasthan Madrasa Board (1995, Jaipur) oversees madrasa education.

questions.q: The Mukhyamantri Rajshri Yojana of Rajasthan was launched with effect from:
questions.exp: The Mukhyamantri Rajshri Yojana came into force on 1 June 2016 and provides Rs 50,000 to a girl child in six instalments from birth up to passing Class 12.

questions.q: Under the Mukhyamantri Rajshri Yojana, the total assistance given to a girl child is:
questions.exp: The scheme gives Rs 50,000 in six instalments — at birth, on completion of one year with immunisation, on admission to Class 1, Class 6, Class 10 and on passing Class 12.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Lado Protsahan Yojana of Rajasthan:
I. It was launched in the year 2024.
II. It provides a savings bond of Rs 1,50,000 released in instalments.
III. The Mukhyamantri Rajshri Yojana has been merged into it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Launched on 1 August 2024, the Lado Protsahan Yojana issues a savings bond of Rs 1.5 lakh for a girl born in a government or approved institution, released in seven instalments up to graduation; the Mukhyamantri Rajshri Yojana was merged into it (as of 2026).

questions.q: The 'Indira Mahila Shakti Udaan Yojana' of Rajasthan is related to:
opts: Free sanitary napkins to women and adolescent girls
questions.exp: The Udaan scheme distributes free sanitary napkins to women and adolescent girls to promote menstrual hygiene; it forms part of the wider Indira Mahila Shakti programme.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indira Mahila Shakti Yojana of Rajasthan:
I. It is an umbrella programme for women's empowerment.
II. It is implemented by the Women and Child Development Department.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: The Indira Mahila Shakti Yojana is an umbrella women's empowerment programme of the Women and Child Development Department covering skill training, enterprise credit and the Udaan sanitary napkin component.

questions.q: The Palanhar Yojana of Rajasthan provides assistance for:
opts: Marriage of daughters of poor families
Old age homes in rural areas
Upbringing of orphaned and destitute children by a relative or guardian
questions.exp: Under the Palanhar Yojana (2005) a relative or acquaintance who takes charge of an orphaned or destitute child receives monthly maintenance and an annual grant; it is run by the Social Justice and Empowerment Department.

questions.q: The Palanhar Yojana of Rajasthan was originally introduced for children of parents who were:
opts: Sentenced to death or life imprisonment
questions.exp: The scheme began in 2005 for children of parents sentenced to death or life imprisonment and was later extended to orphans, children of widows, of divorced or abandoned women, of parents with disabilities and of AIDS patients.

questions.q: The 'Sakhi' One Stop Centres set up in the districts of Rajasthan are meant for:
opts: Integrated support to women affected by violence
Distribution of ration to migrant workers
questions.exp: One Stop Centres, popularly called Sakhi Centres, provide medical aid, police assistance, legal aid, counselling and temporary shelter to women affected by violence.

questions.q: The Mukhyamantri Kanyadan Yojana of Rajasthan provides:
opts: Free health check-ups for adolescent girls
Financial assistance for the marriage of daughters of poor families
questions.exp: The Mukhyamantri Kanyadan (Sahyog) Yojana of the Social Justice and Empowerment Department gives marriage assistance for daughters of BPL, widow and other eligible families, with a higher amount for better-educated brides.

questions.q: The 'Rajasthan Mahila Nidhi' established in 2022 is:
opts: A pension fund for working women
A credit cooperative federation for women's self-help groups
A corpus for women's higher education
An insurance scheme for women farmers
questions.exp: Rajasthan Mahila Nidhi is a women's credit cooperative federation that lends to self-help groups linked with Rajeevika, on the model pioneered by Telangana's Stree Nidhi.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Scheme)   List-II (Benefit)
A. Mukhyamantri Rajshri Yojana   1. Free sanitary napkins
B. Indira Mahila Shakti Udaan Yojana   2. Rs 50,000 to a girl child in six instalments
C. Palanhar Yojana   3. Marriage assistance to daughters of poor families
D. Mukhyamantri Kanyadan Yojana   4. Maintenance for orphaned and destitute children
questions.exp: Rajshri gives Rs 50,000 to a girl child, Udaan distributes sanitary napkins, Palanhar maintains orphaned children and Kanyadan assists with marriage expenses.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Lado Protsahan Yojana — Savings bond for a girl child
Palanhar Yojana — Orphaned and destitute children
Sakhi One Stop Centre — Women affected by violence
Rajasthan Mahila Nidhi — Free coaching for women candidates
questions.exp: Rajasthan Mahila Nidhi is a credit cooperative federation lending to women's self-help groups, not a coaching scheme.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about welfare schemes for the girl child in Rajasthan:
I. The Mukhyamantri Rajshri Yojana applies to girls born on or after 1 June 2016.
II. Under the Lado Protsahan Yojana the final instalment is released on completion of graduation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Rajshri covers girls born on or after 1 June 2016 in institutional deliveries; under Lado Protsahan the largest and last instalment is released after graduation and attaining 21 years of age.

questions.q: Rajasthan became the first state in India to enact a law guaranteeing a minimum income through which legislation?
questions.exp: The Rajasthan Minimum Guaranteed Income Act, 2023, passed in July 2023, made Rajasthan the first state to legally guarantee minimum income through guaranteed employment and social security pensions.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajasthan Minimum Guaranteed Income Act, 2023:
I. It guarantees 125 days of employment in a year.
II. It provides for a minimum pension of Rs 1,000 per month for eligible categories.
III. It provides for a 15 per cent annual increase in the pension amount.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Act guarantees 125 days of employment a year (MGNREGA's 100 days plus 25 extra in rural areas, and 125 days in urban areas), a minimum monthly pension of Rs 1,000 and an annual increase of 15 per cent in the pension from 2024-25.

questions.q: The Mukhyamantri Ekal Nari Samman Pension Yojana of Rajasthan is meant for:
questions.exp: The Ekal Nari Samman Pension is paid to widowed, divorced and abandoned (deserted) women aged 18 years and above who meet the income criterion.

questions.q: Under the Mukhyamantri Vishesh Yogyajan Samman Pension Yojana of Rajasthan, the minimum extent of disability required is:
questions.exp: A person certified with at least 40 per cent disability is eligible; the term 'Vishesh Yogyajan' is used in Rajasthan for persons with disabilities.

questions.q: The social security pensions of Rajasthan are administered by which department?
opts: Rural Development and Panchayati Raj Department
questions.exp: The Social Justice and Empowerment Department runs the state's social security pensions through the RajSSP portal (ssp.rajasthan.gov.in), with applications filed via e-Mitra using the Jan Aadhaar number.

questions.q: Under the Mukhyamantri Vridhjan Samman Pension Yojana of Rajasthan, the minimum qualifying age is:
opts: 55 years for women and 58 years for men
58 years for women and 60 years for men
60 years for both women and men
65 years for both women and men
questions.exp: Women aged 55 years and above and men aged 58 years and above are eligible for the old-age pension, subject to the prescribed family income limit.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Pension scheme)   List-II (Beneficiary)
A. Mukhyamantri Ekal Nari Samman Pension   1. Persons with 40 per cent disability
B. Mukhyamantri Vishesh Yogyajan Samman Pension   2. Widowed, divorced and abandoned women
C. Mukhyamantri Vridhjan Samman Pension   3. Small and marginal farmers in old age
D. Mukhyamantri Laghu evam Simant Krishak Vriddhavastha Pension   4. Elderly women and men
questions.exp: These four pensions together make up Rajasthan's social security pension architecture, all delivered through the RajSSP portal.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: RajSSP — Social security pension portal of Rajasthan
Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme — Ministry of Rural Development
Mukhyamantri Ekal Nari Samman Pension — Single women
Mukhyamantri Vishesh Yogyajan Pension — Landless agricultural labourers
questions.exp: The Vishesh Yogyajan Samman Pension is for persons with disabilities (at least 40 per cent), not for landless agricultural labourers.

questions.q: The Dr. Ambedkar DBT Voucher Yojana of Rajasthan provides:
opts: Assistance for food and accommodation to students studying away from home
Free bus passes to college students
questions.exp: Under this scheme students of SC/ST/OBC/MBC/EWS and minority communities who study in government colleges at district or divisional headquarters receive direct benefit transfer for accommodation and food.

questions.q: The headquarters of the Tribal Area Development (TAD) Department of Rajasthan is located at:
questions.exp: The Tribal Area Development Department, which implements schemes in the Scheduled Areas of southern Rajasthan, has its headquarters at Udaipur.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Scheduled Areas of Rajasthan:
I. Banswara, Dungarpur and Pratapgarh districts fall entirely within the Scheduled Areas.
II. Parts of Udaipur, Rajsamand, Chittorgarh, Pali and Sirohi districts are included in the Scheduled Areas.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Rajasthan's Fifth Schedule areas cover the whole of Banswara, Dungarpur and Pratapgarh and parts of Udaipur, Rajsamand, Chittorgarh, Pali and Sirohi; PESA, 1996 applies to them.

questions.q: The Van Dhan Vikas Kendras, aimed at value addition to minor forest produce, are implemented by:
opts: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
TRIFED under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs
questions.exp: Van Dhan Vikas Kendras are set up by TRIFED under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs; several are operational in the tribal belt of southern Rajasthan.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes Finance and Development Cooperative Corporation primarily provides:
opts: Subsidised credit for self-employment to SC/ST families
questions.exp: The Corporation channels subsidised term loans and margin money for self-employment ventures of Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe families, working with national finance corporations.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Scheme/Body)   List-II (Principal target group)
A. Devnarayan Yojana   1. Scheduled Tribes
B. Van Dhan Vikas Kendra   2. Most Backward Classes
C. Rajasthan Madrasa Board   3. Orphaned and destitute children
D. Palanhar Yojana   4. Minority communities
questions.exp: Devnarayan schemes serve the Most Backward Classes, Van Dhan Kendras serve tribal gatherers of minor forest produce, the Madrasa Board serves minority education and Palanhar supports orphaned children.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Scheme/Body)   List-II (Function)
A. Mukhyamantri Anuprati Coaching Yojana   1. Headquarters at Udaipur
B. Dr. Ambedkar DBT Voucher Yojana   2. Free competitive examination coaching
C. Tribal Area Development Department   3. Subsidised credit for self-employment to SC/ST families
D. Rajasthan SC/ST Finance and Development Cooperative Corporation   4. Food and accommodation assistance to students
questions.exp: Anuprati gives free coaching, the Ambedkar DBT Voucher covers food and lodging for students studying away from home, the TAD Department is headquartered at Udaipur and the SC/ST Corporation extends subsidised self-employment credit.

questions.q: Which state was the first in India to announce a dedicated Silicosis Policy?
questions.exp: Rajasthan announced the country's first dedicated Silicosis Policy in 2019, covering prevention, detection, certification, compensation and rehabilitation of workers in mining and stone-crushing.

questions.q: Under the Rajasthan Silicosis Policy, the one-time financial assistance payable to a certified silicosis patient is:
questions.exp: A certified silicosis patient receives one-time assistance of Rs 3 lakh; on the death of a patient, Rs 2 lakh is paid to the dependants, along with pension and other social security benefits.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Rajasthan Silicosis Policy, 2019:
I. Rajasthan was the first Indian state to frame such a policy.
II. Persons affected by silicosis are given social security benefits on par with persons with disabilities.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: The 2019 policy made Rajasthan the first state with a silicosis policy and extended pension and other benefits available to persons with disabilities to certified silicosis patients and their families.

questions.q: In Rajasthan, persons with disabilities are officially referred to by which term?
questions.exp: Rajasthan uses the term 'Vishesh Yogyajan' for persons with disabilities, reflected in the names of schemes such as the Mukhyamantri Vishesh Yogyajan Samman Pension Yojana.

questions.q: The free pilgrimage scheme for senior citizens of Rajasthan, now known as the Varishth Nagrik Tirth Yatra Yojana, is implemented by which department?
questions.exp: The Devasthan Department runs the senior citizens' pilgrimage scheme (earlier called Mukhyamantri Vridhjan Tirth Yatra Yojana), taking eligible elderly citizens on pilgrimage by rail and air.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about welfare provisions for the elderly and the differently abled in Rajasthan is NOT correct?
opts: The Devasthan Department runs a free pilgrimage scheme for senior citizens
'Vishesh Yogyajan' is the term used for persons with disabilities
The Silicosis Policy of Rajasthan was the first such policy in the country
The Vishesh Yogyajan Samman Pension requires a minimum disability of 75 per cent
questions.exp: The minimum qualifying disability for the Vishesh Yogyajan Samman Pension is 40 per cent, not 75 per cent. The other three statements are correct.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Rajasthan framed a dedicated Silicosis Policy in 2019.
Reason (R): Silicosis is an occupational lung disease widespread among workers in the state's mining and stone-crushing industry.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: Both statements are true and the reason explains the assertion: the high incidence of silicosis among mine and stone-crusher workers in Rajasthan prompted the country's first state silicosis policy in 2019.

questions.q: The Rajasthan Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board is financed mainly by:
opts: A share of the state's GST collections
A cess of 1 per cent levied on the cost of construction
Grants from the Union Ministry of Labour
questions.exp: Under the Building and Other Construction Workers' Welfare Cess Act, 1996 a cess of 1 per cent of the construction cost funds the welfare board's schemes for registered construction workers.

questions.q: Under the Shubhshakti Yojana of the Rajasthan Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, the assistance provided is:
questions.exp: The Shubhshakti Yojana gives Rs 55,000 to an eligible adult daughter (or the woman worker herself) of a registered construction worker for skill training, self-employment or marriage.

questions.q: The Nirman Shramik Sulabhya Awas Yojana of Rajasthan provides:
opts: Free rental accommodation at work sites
Interest subsidy on home loans for all workers
Housing assistance to registered construction workers
questions.exp: The scheme gives housing assistance of up to Rs 1.5 lakh to registered building and other construction workers for the construction or purchase of a house.

questions.q: The e-Shram portal, a national database of unorganised workers, was launched in:
questions.exp: The e-Shram portal was launched on 26 August 2021 by the Union Ministry of Labour and Employment; each registered worker receives a 12-digit Universal Account Number.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about welfare schemes for construction workers in Rajasthan:
I. Only workers registered with the Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board are eligible.
II. Maternity assistance is available to registered women construction workers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Board benefits, including the Prasuti Sahayata (maternity assistance) Yojana, are restricted to workers registered with the Rajasthan Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Scheme)   List-II (Benefit)
A. Shubhshakti Yojana   1. Housing assistance of Rs 1.5 lakh
B. Nirman Shramik Sulabhya Awas Yojana   2. Rs 55,000 to a daughter or woman worker
C. Prasuti Sahayata Yojana   3. Educational scholarships to workers' children
D. Nirman Shramik Shiksha evam Kaushal Vikas Yojana   4. Maternity assistance
questions.exp: All four are schemes of the Rajasthan Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board for registered construction workers and their families.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: BOCW cess — 1 per cent of construction cost
Prasuti Sahayata Yojana — Housing for construction workers
questions.exp: The Prasuti Sahayata Yojana provides maternity assistance; housing assistance is given under the Nirman Shramik Sulabhya Awas Yojana.

questions.q: Under the Mukhyamantri Yuva Sambal Yojana of Rajasthan, the unemployment allowance is payable for a maximum period of:
questions.exp: The allowance is paid for a maximum of two years or until the beneficiary gets employment, whichever is earlier; the family income limit is Rs 2 lakh a year.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Mukhyamantri Yuva Sambal Yojana:
I. Beneficiaries must do a four-hour daily internship for five days a week.
II. The scheme is meant for educated unemployed youth registered with an employment exchange.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: The revised scheme makes a four-hour daily internship in a government office or enterprise compulsory for five days a week, and applies to educated unemployed youth registered with the employment exchange.

questions.q: The Indira Gandhi Shahri Rozgar Guarantee Yojana of Rajasthan was launched on:
questions.exp: Launched on 9 September 2022, it guarantees wage employment to urban households; the guarantee was later raised from 100 to 125 days under the Rajasthan Minimum Guaranteed Income Act, 2023.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Indira Gandhi Shahri Rozgar Guarantee Yojana:
I. It provides guaranteed wage employment to urban households.
II. The number of guaranteed days was raised from 100 to 125.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: The scheme is the urban counterpart of MGNREGA; the Rajasthan Minimum Guaranteed Income Act, 2023 raised the entitlement from 100 to 125 days a year.

questions.q: 'Mission 2030' launched by the Government of Rajasthan in 2023 was:
opts: A vision document exercise for the state's development by 2030
questions.exp: Rajasthan Mission 2030 was a state-wide consultation exercise to prepare a vision document setting development targets for the year 2030.

questions.q: The Indira Gandhi Shahri Credit Card Yojana of Rajasthan provides:
opts: A crop loan to peri-urban farmers
A housing loan to urban poor families
A subsidy on electricity for urban households
An interest-free loan of up to Rs 50,000 to street vendors and informal workers
