Cabinet approved 18 September 2024: Chandrayaan-4 lunar sample return (~Rs 2,104 crore), Venus Orbiter Mission (~Rs 1,236 crore, target 2028), and the Bharatiya Antariksh Station (first module by 2028, complete by 2035); Indian crewed Moon landing target 2040.
Indian Space Policy 2023 — IN-SPACe (Ahmedabad) is the single-window authorisation body; NSIL (2019) is the commercial PSU arm; Antrix (1992) the earlier marketing arm.

Private sector: Skyroot Aerospace's Vikram-S (Mission Prarambh, 18 Nov 2022) first privately built Indian rocket; Agnikul Cosmos' Agnibaan SOrTeD (May 2024) used the world's first single-piece 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine.

Project NETRA + IS4OM (Bengaluru) handle space-debris tracking and space situational awareness; ISRO's goal is debris-free space missions by 2030. A second launch port for SSLV is coming up at Kulasekarapattinam, Thoothukudi district, Tamil Nadu; SSLV technology has been transferred to HAL.

Orbits: LEO 160-2,000 km; MEO up to 35,786 km; GEO 35,786 km (period ~24 h, inclination ~0 deg); sun-synchronous polar orbits (~98 deg inclination) are used for remote sensing. Earth's escape velocity 11.2 km/s, orbital velocity ~7.9 km/s.

Udaipur Solar Observatory — on an island in Fateh Sagar Lake, founded 1976 by Arvind Bhatnagar, run by the Physical Research Laboratory, Ahmedabad since 1981; 50 cm Multi Application Solar Telescope (MAST) operational 2015.

questions.q: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) was established in the year:
questions.exp: ISRO was formed on 15 August 1969, superseding INCOSPAR (1962). The Department of Space and the Space Commission were created in 1972.

questions.q: Who is regarded as the father of the Indian space programme?
questions.exp: Vikram Sarabhai founded INCOSPAR in 1962 and led the space effort until his death in 1971. Satish Dhawan headed ISRO from 1972 to 1984.

questions.q: Aryabhata, India's first satellite, was launched in 1975 from:
questions.exp: The 360 kg satellite was launched on 19 April 1975 by a Soviet Kosmos-3M rocket from Kapustin Yar. It was named after the ancient Indian astronomer.

questions.q: The first Indian satellite placed in orbit by an Indian-built launch vehicle was:
questions.exp: Rohini RS-1 was orbited by SLV-3 on 18 July 1980; the SLV-3 project director was A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.

questions.q: The first sounding rocket launched from the Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station in November 1963 was:
questions.exp: An American-supplied Nike-Apache was launched from Thumba on 21 November 1963. Thumba was chosen because it lies close to the geomagnetic equator.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (ISRO centre)   List-II (Location)
A. Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre   1. Ahmedabad
B. Space Applications Centre      2. Thiruvananthapuram
C. National Remote Sensing Centre 3. Hyderabad
D. U R Rao Satellite Centre       4. Bengaluru
questions.exp: VSSC (launch vehicles) is at Thiruvananthapuram, SAC (payloads and applications) at Ahmedabad, NRSC (remote sensing data) at Hyderabad and URSC (satellite building) at Bengaluru.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (ISRO facility)   List-II (Principal function)
A. Liquid Propulsion Systems Centre   1. Reception and dissemination of remote sensing data
B. National Remote Sensing Centre     2. Design of liquid propulsion stages
C. Space Applications Centre          3. Development of payloads and space applications
D. ISRO Propulsion Complex, Mahendragiri  4. Testing of liquid and cryogenic engines
questions.exp: LPSC designs liquid stages, NRSC handles earth-observation data, SAC builds payloads, and the ISRO Propulsion Complex at Mahendragiri (Tamil Nadu) tests liquid and cryogenic engines.

questions.q: ISRO's Master Control Facility, which controls India's geostationary satellites, is located at:
questions.exp: The Master Control Facility is at Hassan in Karnataka, with a second facility at Bhopal. Byalalu hosts the Indian Deep Space Network antenna.

questions.q: Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SHAR), India's principal launch port, is located at Sriharikota in:
questions.exp: Sriharikota is a barrier island on Pulicat Lake in Andhra Pradesh. The centre was renamed after Satish Dhawan in 2002.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV):
I. It is a four-stage vehicle with alternating solid and liquid stages.
II. Its first fully successful flight was PSLV-D2 in 1994.
III. The PSLV-CA variant flies without strap-on motors.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. PSLV-D1 (1993) failed; 'CA' stands for core alone. PSLV is often called ISRO's workhorse launch vehicle.

questions.q: In February 2017 ISRO set a world record by launching how many satellites in a single mission by PSLV-C37?
questions.exp: PSLV-C37 placed 104 satellites in orbit on 15 February 2017, with Cartosat-2 series as the primary payload. The record was surpassed by SpaceX's Transporter-1 (143 satellites) in January 2021.

questions.q: The Singaporean earth observation satellite TeLEOS-2 was placed in orbit in April 2023 by which Indian launch vehicle?
questions.exp: PSLV-C55 flew a dedicated commercial mission arranged by NewSpace India Limited on 22 April 2023, carrying TeLEOS-2 and Lumelite-4.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Mission)   List-II (Launch vehicle)
A. Chandrayaan-1   1. PSLV-C11
B. Mangalyaan      2. PSLV-C25
C. Chandrayaan-3   3. LVM3-M4
D. Aditya-L1       4. PSLV-C57
questions.exp: Chandrayaan-1 flew on PSLV-C11 (2008), Mangalyaan on PSLV-C25 (2013), Chandrayaan-3 on LVM3-M4 (2023) and Aditya-L1 on PSLV-C57 (2023).

questions.q: Chandrayaan-1, launched in October 2008, is chiefly credited with the discovery of:
opts: Water molecules on the lunar surface
Liquid water at the lunar south pole
questions.exp: NASA's Moon Mineralogy Mapper carried on Chandrayaan-1 confirmed hydroxyl and water molecules in 2009. Its Moon Impact Probe struck the surface near the south pole on 14 November 2008.

questions.q: Chandrayaan-3's lander Vikram made a soft landing on the Moon on:
questions.exp: India became the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon and the first to land near the lunar south pole. 23 August is now observed as National Space Day.

questions.q: The landing site of Chandrayaan-3 on the Moon has been named:
questions.exp: The Chandrayaan-3 landing site was named Shiv Shakti Point; the Chandrayaan-2 crash site was named Tiranga Point and the Chandrayaan-1 impact site is Jawahar Sthal.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Chandrayaan-2:
I. It was launched by GSLV Mk III-M1 in July 2019.
II. Its lander Vikram achieved a successful soft landing.
III. Its orbiter continues to function and send back data.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Vikram lander of Chandrayaan-2 crashed on 7 September 2019, but the orbiter remains operational and later supported Chandrayaan-3.

questions.q: India's Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan) was inserted into orbit around Mars on:
questions.exp: Launched on 5 November 2013 by PSLV-C25, MOM reached Mars orbit on 24 September 2014, making India the first country to succeed on its maiden attempt and the fourth agency to reach Mars.

questions.q: India's solar mission Aditya-L1 has been placed in a halo orbit around which point?
questions.exp: Aditya-L1 was inserted into a halo orbit around the Sun-Earth L1 point, about 1.5 million km from Earth, on 6 January 2024. Its primary payload VELC was built by the Indian Institute of Astrophysics.

questions.q: XPoSat, launched by ISRO on 1 January 2024, is dedicated to the study of:
questions.exp: XPoSat is the world's second dedicated X-ray polarimetry mission after NASA's IXPE. Its payloads are POLIX and XSPECT and it was launched by PSLV-C58.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Mission)   List-II (Principal domain)
A. AstroSat    1. Solar corona and solar wind studies
B. Aditya-L1   2. X-ray polarimetry
C. XPoSat      3. Multi-wavelength astronomy
D. NISAR       4. Radar earth observation
questions.exp: AstroSat (2015) is India's first multi-wavelength observatory, Aditya-L1 studies the Sun, XPoSat measures X-ray polarisation and NISAR is a synthetic aperture radar mission.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of an Indian satellite series and its purpose is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Oceansat — Ocean colour and wind studies
questions.exp: Kalpana-1 (2002), originally METSAT, was India's first dedicated meteorological satellite, later renamed after Kalpana Chawla. Navigation is provided by the IRNSS/NavIC series.

questions.q: The Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (NavIC) was designed as a constellation of how many satellites?
questions.exp: NavIC uses seven satellites in geostationary and geosynchronous orbits and covers India plus about 1500 km beyond its boundaries. GAGAN, developed with the Airports Authority of India, augments GPS for aviation.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about NavIC:
I. It provides coverage over India and about 1500 km beyond its borders.
II. Its satellites are placed in geostationary and geosynchronous orbits.
III. It is a global navigation system comparable in coverage to GPS.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: NavIC is a regional, not a global, navigation system. NVS-01 and NVS-02 are second-generation NavIC satellites.

questions.q: In a cryogenic rocket engine of the type used by ISRO, the propellant combination is:
opts: Unsymmetrical dimethyl hydrazine and nitrogen tetroxide
questions.exp: Cryogenic stages burn liquid hydrogen with liquid oxygen at extremely low temperatures, giving the highest specific impulse. Kerosene-LOX is used in semi-cryogenic engines such as the SCE-200 under development.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's cryogenic propulsion:
I. GSLV Mk-II uses the indigenous CE-7.5 cryogenic upper-stage engine.
II. LVM3 uses the CE-20 engine in its cryogenic upper stage.
III. India's first flight with an indigenous cryogenic stage was GSLV-D3 in April 2010.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: GSLV-D3 (2010) failed; the first successful flight of an indigenous cryogenic stage was GSLV-D5 in January 2014.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV):
I. It is designed to place about 500 kg in a 500 km low Earth orbit.
II. Its first developmental flight, SSLV-D1, was fully successful.
III. Its third developmental flight placed EOS-08 in orbit in August 2024.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: SSLV-D1 (August 2022) failed to achieve a stable orbit; SSLV-D2 (February 2023) and SSLV-D3 (August 2024) succeeded. SSLV technology has since been transferred to HAL.

questions.q: ISRO's Reusable Launch Vehicle autonomous landing experiments (Pushpak) were conducted at the Aeronautical Test Range in:
questions.exp: The LEX series of landing experiments was carried out at the Aeronautical Test Range, Chitradurga, Karnataka. The earlier RLV-TD hypersonic experiment (HEX-01) flew in May 2016.

questions.q: The success of ISRO's SpaDeX mission in January 2025 made India the fourth country to demonstrate in-space docking, after the USA, Russia and:
questions.exp: SpaDeX was launched by PSLV-C60 on 30 December 2024 with two spacecraft, SDX01 (Chaser) and SDX02 (Target); docking was achieved on 16 January 2025.

questions.q: NISAR, launched in July 2025, is a joint earth observation mission of ISRO and:
questions.exp: NISAR carries a dual-frequency synthetic aperture radar — NASA's L-band and ISRO's S-band — and was launched by GSLV-F16 on 30 July 2025 into a sun-synchronous orbit. (Status as of 2026.)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Gaganyaan programme, as of 2026:
I. The test flight TV-D1, demonstrating the crew escape system, was conducted in October 2023.
II. The human-rated launch vehicle for the mission is designated HLVM3.
III. The first crewed flight of the programme has already been completed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: As of 2026 no Indian crewed flight has been made; uncrewed missions, the first of which carries the humanoid Vyommitra, precede a crewed flight targeted for 2027.

questions.q: Group Captain Shubhanshu Shukla, who travelled to the International Space Station in 2025, became the second Indian in space after:
questions.exp: Rakesh Sharma flew aboard Soyuz T-11 to the Salyut-7 station in 1984. Shukla flew on the Axiom-4 mission in June 2025 and was the first Indian aboard the ISS.

questions.q: According to the plan approved by the Union Cabinet in September 2024, the first module of the Bharatiya Antariksh Station is targeted for launch by:
questions.exp: The first module is targeted for 2028 and the completed station for 2035, with an Indian crewed landing on the Moon envisaged by 2040. (Status as of 2026.)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Chandrayaan-4 mission:
I. It has been approved as a lunar sample-return mission.
II. It is planned to use two LVM3 launches with multiple modules.
III. It will carry the first Indian astronaut to the surface of the Moon.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Chandrayaan-4 was approved on 18 September 2024 with an outlay of about Rs 2,104 crore as an uncrewed sample-return mission. A crewed Indian Moon landing is a separate goal targeted around 2040.

questions.q: India's Venus Orbiter Mission (Shukrayaan), approved by the Union Cabinet in September 2024, is targeted for launch in:
questions.exp: The mission, with an outlay of about Rs 1,236 crore, is planned around the favourable Earth-Venus alignment of March 2028 and will study the Venusian surface and atmosphere. (Status as of 2026.)

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of an ISRO facility and its location is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology — Bengaluru
questions.exp: IIST, India's first space university, is at Valiamala near Thiruvananthapuram, not Bengaluru.

questions.q: The Udaipur Solar Observatory is situated on an island in which lake?
questions.exp: Founded in 1976 by Dr Arvind Bhatnagar, it has been run by the Physical Research Laboratory, Ahmedabad, since 1981. The surrounding water reduces ground-heating turbulence and improves image quality.

questions.q: The Multi Application Solar Telescope (MAST) commissioned at the Udaipur Solar Observatory has an aperture of:
questions.exp: MAST, a 50 cm aperture solar telescope, became operational in 2015. The observatory functions under the Physical Research Laboratory of the Department of Space.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. A geostationary satellite has an orbital period of about 24 hours and an inclination of nearly zero degrees.
II. Sun-synchronous polar orbits are preferred for remote sensing because they give consistent illumination conditions.
III. A geostationary orbit lies at an altitude of about 36,000 km above the equator.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The exact geostationary altitude is 35,786 km; sun-synchronous orbits have an inclination of about 98 degrees.

questions.q: The escape velocity from the surface of the Earth is approximately:
questions.exp: Escape velocity from Earth is 11.2 km/s; 7.9 km/s is the orbital velocity for a low Earth orbit and 2.38 km/s is the Moon's escape velocity.

questions.q: Rockets are built in multiple stages mainly because:
opts: A single engine cannot burn for more than two minutes
Multi-stage rockets need no guidance system
Shedding spent stages reduces the mass that must be accelerated further
It removes the need for a cryogenic engine
questions.exp: Discarding empty tanks and engines lowers the vehicle's mass, so the remaining propellant produces a much greater velocity increment.

questions.q:
Arrange the following ISRO missions in the correct chronological order of their launch:
I. Chandrayaan-1
II. Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission)
III. AstroSat
IV. Aditya-L1
questions.exp: Chandrayaan-1 (2008), Mangalyaan (2013), AstroSat (2015) and Aditya-L1 (2023).

questions.q:
Arrange the following Indian launch vehicles in the chronological order of their first flight:
I. SLV-3
II. ASLV
III. PSLV
IV. GSLV
questions.exp: SLV-3 first flew in 1979, ASLV in 1987, PSLV in 1993 and GSLV in 2001.

questions.q: Under the Indian Space Policy 2023, the single-window autonomous agency that authorises and regulates space activities by non-government entities is:
questions.exp: IN-SPACe (Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre) is headquartered at Ahmedabad. NewSpace India Limited is the commercial PSU arm and ISRO is to concentrate on research and development.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Indian private space firm)   List-II (Associated product)
A. Skyroot Aerospace   1. Agnibaan SOrTeD
B. Agnikul Cosmos      2. Vikram-S sounding rocket
C. Pixxel              3. Hyperspectral imaging satellites
D. Dhruva Space        4. Satellite orbital deployers
questions.exp: Vikram-S (Mission Prarambh, November 2022) was India's first privately built rocket; Agnikul's Agnibaan used the world's first single-piece 3D-printed semi-cryogenic engine.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about space debris:
I. Project NETRA is ISRO's initiative for tracking space objects that could threaten Indian assets.
II. The IS4OM centre for space situational awareness is located at Bengaluru.
III. ISRO has announced a goal of debris-free space missions by 2030.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: NETRA stands for Network for Space Object Tracking and Analysis; IS4OM is the ISRO System for Safe and Sustainable Space Operations Management.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Satellite series)   List-II (Principal application)
A. Cartosat   1. All-weather radar imaging
B. RISAT      2. Ocean colour and wind studies
C. Oceansat   3. High-resolution cartographic mapping
D. INSAT      4. Communication and meteorology
questions.exp: Cartosat-3 provides a panchromatic resolution of about 0.25 m; RISAT carries synthetic aperture radar for cloud-independent imaging.

questions.q: CMS-03, launched by LVM3-M5 in November 2025, is notable as:
opts: The heaviest satellite launched from Indian soil at the time of its launch
The first Indian satellite in a polar orbit
India's first satellite built entirely by a private firm
questions.exp: The multi-band communication satellite for the Indian Navy weighed about 4,410 kg and was launched from Sriharikota on 2 November 2025. It was surpassed by BlueBird Block-2, carried by LVM3-M6 on 24 December 2025. (As of September 2026.)

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about India's launch vehicles is NOT correct?
opts: SLV-3 was India's first vehicle to use a cryogenic upper stage
PSLV is often described as ISRO's workhorse launch vehicle
LVM3 was the launch vehicle used for Chandrayaan-3
GSLV Mk-II uses the indigenous CE-7.5 cryogenic engine
questions.exp: SLV-3 was an all-solid four-stage vehicle. India's first flight with an indigenous cryogenic stage was GSLV-D5 in January 2014.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Aryabhata, India's first satellite, was launched in 1975.
II. Bhaskara-I was India's first experimental earth observation satellite.
III. APPLE was India's first experimental communication satellite.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Bhaskara-I flew in 1979 and APPLE was launched by an Ariane rocket from Kourou in 1981.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Satellite)   List-II (Distinction)
A. Aryabhata   1. First Indian satellite
B. Rohini RS-1 2. First Indian experimental communication satellite
C. APPLE       3. First satellite orbited by an Indian launch vehicle
D. Kalpana-1   4. First Indian dedicated meteorological satellite
questions.exp: Kalpana-1, launched in 2002 as METSAT, was renamed in memory of Kalpana Chawla. EDUSAT (2004) was the first satellite exclusively for education.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the institutional history of India's space programme is NOT correct?
opts: INCOSPAR was set up in 1962 under the Department of Atomic Energy
The Department of Space was created in 1972
Vikram Sarabhai is regarded as the father of the Indian space programme
Antrix Corporation was set up in 2019 as the commercial arm of ISRO
questions.exp: Antrix Corporation was incorporated in 1992. NewSpace India Limited (NSIL) is the arm created in 2019.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The James Webb Space Telescope operates from the Sun-Earth L2 point.
II. NASA's Artemis-I was an uncrewed mission around the Moon.
III. China's Chang'e-6 returned the first samples from the far side of the Moon.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: JWST was launched in December 2021 on an Ariane-5, Artemis-I flew uncrewed in November-December 2022 and Chang'e-6 brought back far-side samples in June 2024.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of a space agency and its country is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: CNES is the French national space agency; Canada's agency is the Canadian Space Agency (CSA).

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Most Indian remote sensing satellites are placed in sun-synchronous polar orbits.
Reason (R): A sun-synchronous orbit lets a satellite cross a given latitude at nearly the same local solar time on every pass.
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.exp: Constant local solar time gives comparable illumination and shadow conditions between passes, which is essential for change detection in remote sensing.

chapters.title: Defence Technology
factsheet: DRDO founded 1 January 1958 by merging the Technical Development Establishment, the Directorate of Technical Development & Production and the Defence Science Organisation; began with 10 laboratories, now about 52.
DRDO motto: 'Balasya Mulam Vigyanam' (बलस्य मूलं विज्ञानम्) — 'Strength's origin is in Science', drawn from Kautilya's Arthashastra. HQ: DRDO Bhawan, New Delhi.

DRDO works under the Department of Defence Research and Development; its head is Secretary DD R&D and Chairman DRDO. Five DRDO Young Scientist Laboratories opened in 2020 (AI, quantum, cognitive, asymmetric and smart-materials technologies). Aero India is held at Yelahanka, Bengaluru.

Key DRDO labs: DRDL & RCI & ASL Hyderabad (missiles), ADE Bengaluru (UAVs), GTRE Bengaluru (Kaveri engine), LRDE Bengaluru (radars), CABS Bengaluru (Netra AEW&C), ARDE & HEMRL Pune (armaments, explosives), TBRL Chandigarh, CVRDE Avadi (Arjun), VRDE Ahmednagar, NPOL Kochi (sonar), NSTL Visakhapatnam (torpedoes), DFRL Mysuru (food), INMAS & DIPAS & DIPR Delhi, DRDE Gwalior, DIHAR Leh, SASE Chandigarh, DIBER Haldwani.
Defence Laboratory Jodhpur (DLJ) is DRDO's Rajasthan laboratory — camouflage, desert environment sciences, isotopes and radiation-detection kits.
Lukoskin — polyherbal drug for leucoderma (vitiligo) developed by DIBER, Haldwani from Himalayan herbs; technology transferred to Aimil Pharmaceuticals.

Other DRDO life-science products: 2-DG anti-COVID drug (INMAS with Dr Reddy's, 2021), Oxycare oxygen system (DEBEL), retort-pouch and extreme-climate rations (DFRL), seabuckthorn beverages (DIHAR, Leh).
IGMDP launched 1983 under A.P.J. Abdul Kalam; five missiles — Prithvi, Agni, Trishul, Akash, Nag; formally concluded 2008.
Ranges: Prithvi-I 150 km, Prithvi-II 250-350 km; Agni-I ~700-900 km, Agni-II 2,000+ km, Agni-III 3,000+ km, Agni-IV ~4,000 km, Agni-V 5,000+ km, Agni-Prime 1,000-2,000 km.
Mission Divyastra, 11 March 2024 — first flight test of Agni-5 with MIRV (Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicles).
Trishul ~9 km, Akash 25-30 km (Akash-NG ~70 km), Nag ATGM ~4 km, QRSAM ~30 km, VSHORADS/MANPADS ~6 km, Astra Mk-1 BVRAAM 100+ km, Nirbhay subsonic cruise ~1,000 km.

BrahMos — India-Russia joint venture (1998), named after the Brahmaputra and Moskva rivers; Mach 2.8-3, world's fastest operational supersonic cruise missile; range extended beyond the original 290 km after India joined MTCR. The Philippines was the first export customer (2022 contract, delivery 2024).
K-series SLBMs: K-15 Sagarika ~750 km, K-4 ~3,500 km — the sea leg of the nuclear triad on Arihant-class boats.

Pinaka MBRL (ARDE): Mk-I ~38 km, enhanced ~45 km, guided Pinaka 75+ km; used in the 1999 Kargil conflict. Pralay is a quasi-ballistic missile of 150-500 km. HSTDV — scramjet hypersonic demonstrator, flight tested 7 September 2020 at about Mach 6; a long-range hypersonic missile (LRAShM) was tested from Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Island in November 2024.

Ballistic Missile Defence: Phase-I has the exo-atmospheric Prithvi Air Defence and the endo-atmospheric Advanced Air Defence. Mission Shakti (27 March 2019) destroyed a satellite at ~283 km, making India the 4th ASAT power.
Tejas LCA designed by ADA, built by HAL; IOC 2013, FOC 2019; Mk-1A powered by GE F404. AMCA is India's fifth-generation stealth fighter programme, approved by the CCS in March 2024.

HAL platforms: Dhruv ALH, Rudra, Light Combat Helicopter 'Prachand' (inducted October 2022, first unit raised at Jodhpur), HTT-40 trainer; Su-30MKI licence-built at Nashik. C-295 transports are assembled at Vadodara with Airbus-Tata.
UAVs: TAPAS-BH (earlier Rustom-II), Nishant and Lakshya from ADE Bengaluru; SWiFT/Ghatak stealth demonstrator. Netra AEW&C (CABS) flies on an Embraer ERJ-145; the larger Phalcon AWACS uses IL-76.

Rafale — 36 aircraft from Dassault, first squadron No. 17 'Golden Arrows' at Ambala (2020); 26 Rafale-M for the Navy contracted in 2025. The MiG-21 was retired from Indian Air Force service in September 2025.
Navy: INS Vikrant (commissioned 2 September 2022, Cochin Shipyard, ~45,000 t) is India's first indigenously designed and built aircraft carrier; INS Vikramaditya was acquired from Russia in 2013.
Submarines: INS Arihant (2016) and INS Arighaat (2024) are indigenous SSBNs; the six Kalvari-class (Scorpene) diesel-electric boats under Project 75 end with INS Vagsheer (January 2025).

Recent commissionings: INS Nilgiri (Project 17A, Jan 2025), INS Surat (Project 15B, Jan 2025), INS Arnala (ASW shallow water craft, June 2025), INS Tamal (Talwar class, July 2025 — the last warship imported from abroad), INS Nistar (first indigenous diving support vessel, July 2025), INS Himgiri and INS Udaygiri (Project 17A, 26 August 2025).

Army systems: Arjun MBT (CVRDE Avadi), Zorawar light tank (DRDO with L&T), ATAGS 155 mm/52 cal towed howitzer (ARDE, ~48 km), Dhanush 155 mm/45 cal 'Desi Bofors', K-9 Vajra-T tracked self-propelled gun (L&T-Hanwha), M777 ultra-light howitzer, AK-203 rifles made at Korwa (Amethi).

Nuclear: Pokhran-I 'Smiling Buddha' 18 May 1974 in Jaisalmer district; Pokhran-II 'Operation Shakti' 11 and 13 May 1998 — 11 May is National Technology Day. Doctrine (2003): No First Use, credible minimum deterrence, massive retaliation, no use against non-nuclear weapon states.

Export-control regimes: India joined MTCR (2016), the Wassenaar Arrangement (2017) and the Australia Group (2018); India is NOT in the NSG and has not signed the NPT or CTBT. The nuclear triad was completed in 2018 with INS Arihant's first deterrence patrol.

Ordnance Factory Board dissolved on 1 October 2021 into 7 new DPSUs — Munitions India, Armoured Vehicles Nigam (AVANI), Advanced Weapons and Equipment India, Troop Comforts, Yantra India, India Optel and Gliders India.
Defence industrial corridors announced in Budget 2018-19: Uttar Pradesh (Aligarh, Agra, Jhansi, Kanpur, Chitrakoot, Lucknow) and Tamil Nadu (Chennai, Coimbatore, Hosur, Salem, Tiruchirappalli).

iDEX (2018) engages start-ups and MSMEs through the Defence Innovation Organisation; SRIJAN portal and the Positive Indigenisation Lists support Atmanirbharta. Defence exports reached a record of about Rs 23,622 crore in 2024-25, with a target of Rs 50,000 crore by 2029.

Chief of Defence Staff created 2019; Gen. Bipin Rawat first CDS (1 Jan 2020), Gen. Anil Chauhan since Sept 2022; CDS heads the Department of Military Affairs and is Permanent Chairman COSC. Tri-service formations: Andaman and Nicobar Command (2001, Port Blair) — India's first tri-service command; Integrated Defence Staff (2001); Strategic Forces Command (2003). Agnipath launched June 2022 — four-year Agniveer tenure, up to 25 per cent retention.

Rajasthan and defence: Pokhran Field Firing Range (nuclear tests, Exercise Bharat Shakti 2024, IAF's Vayu Shakti firepower demonstration), Mahajan Field Firing Range near Bikaner, Chandan range near Jaisalmer, Defence Laboratory Jodhpur, and the Jodhpur air base which hosted a phase of the multinational Exercise Tarang Shakti in 2024.

questions.q: The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) was established in the year:
questions.exp: DRDO was formed in 1958 by amalgamating the Technical Development Establishment, the Directorate of Technical Development & Production and the Defence Science Organisation. Its headquarters is DRDO Bhawan, New Delhi.

questions.q: The motto of the Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) is:
questions.exp: 'Balasya Mulam Vigyanam' (बलस्य मूलं विज्ञानम्) means 'Strength's origin is in Science' and is drawn from Kautilya's Arthashastra.

questions.q: Lukoskin, a polyherbal drug developed by DRDO, is used in the treatment of:
questions.exp: Lukoskin was developed from Himalayan herbs by the Defence Institute of Bio-Energy Research (DIBER), Haldwani, and the technology was transferred to Aimil Pharmaceuticals for manufacture.

questions.q: The anti-COVID-19 drug 2-deoxy-D-glucose (2-DG) was developed by which DRDO laboratory?
questions.exp: The Institute of Nuclear Medicine and Allied Sciences developed 2-DG with Dr Reddy's Laboratories; it received emergency-use approval in May 2021.

questions.q: The DRDO laboratory located in Rajasthan, which works on camouflage, desert environment sciences and radiation detection, is:
opts: Defence Institute of High Altitude Research, Leh
questions.exp: The Defence Laboratory, Jodhpur (DLJ) specialises in desert warfare support, camouflage materials and nuclear-radiation detection systems.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (DRDO laboratory)   List-II (Area of work)
A. GTRE, Bengaluru   1. Combat vehicles
B. NPOL, Kochi       2. Aero gas turbine engines
C. CVRDE, Avadi      3. Sonar and underwater systems
D. DFRL, Mysuru      4. Food technology
questions.exp: GTRE developed the Kaveri engine, NPOL builds sonars, CVRDE developed the Arjun tank and DFRL produces combat rations and preserved foods.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about DRDO:
I. It functions under the Department of Defence Research and Development in the Ministry of Defence.
II. It began in 1958 with about ten laboratories.
III. Its headquarters is located at Bengaluru.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: DRDO's headquarters is DRDO Bhawan in New Delhi. The organisation has since grown to about 52 laboratories.

questions.q: The Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP) was launched in 1983 under the leadership of:
questions.exp: The programme covered five missiles — Prithvi, Agni, Trishul, Akash and Nag — and was formally concluded in 2008.

questions.q: Which one of the following missiles was NOT a part of the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme?
questions.exp: BrahMos is a later India-Russia joint venture set up in 1998. IGMDP comprised Prithvi, Agni, Trishul, Akash and Nag.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Missile)   List-II (Type)
A. Prithvi   1. Anti-tank guided missile
B. Akash     2. Surface-to-surface ballistic missile
C. Nag       3. Beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile
D. Astra     4. Surface-to-air missile
questions.exp: Prithvi is a short-range surface-to-surface ballistic missile, Akash a medium-range surface-to-air missile, Nag a fire-and-forget anti-tank missile and Astra a beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile.

questions.q: Astra, developed by DRDO, is India's first indigenous:
questions.exp: Astra Mk-1 has a range of over 100 km and is integrated on the Su-30MKI and Tejas; the Mk-2 variant extends the range further.

questions.q: In defence technology, the term MANPADS refers to:
questions.exp: DRDO's indigenous MANPADS project is VSHORADS (Very Short Range Air Defence System), a shoulder-fired missile effective against low-flying aircraft, helicopters and drones at ranges of about 6 km.

questions.q: The Agni-V ballistic missile has a range of more than:
questions.exp: Agni-V is a three-stage, solid-fuelled, canisterised missile with a range of over 5,000 km. Agni-IV has a range of about 4,000 km.

questions.q: 'Mission Divyastra', conducted in March 2024, was the first Indian flight test of a missile fitted with:
questions.exp: Agni-5 was tested with MIRV technology on 11 March 2024, allowing a single missile to deliver several warheads to different targets.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the BrahMos missile:
I. It is a joint venture between India and Russia.
II. It is a supersonic cruise missile.
III. Its name is derived from the rivers Brahmaputra and Moskva.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: BrahMos Aerospace was set up in 1998; the missile flies at about Mach 2.8-3 and can be launched from land, sea, submarine and air platforms.

questions.q: The first foreign country to sign a contract to buy the BrahMos missile from India was:
questions.exp: The contract with the Philippines was signed in January 2022 and the first battery was delivered in April 2024; it was India's largest defence export order at the time.

questions.q: DRDO's Hypersonic Technology Demonstrator Vehicle (HSTDV), successfully flight-tested in September 2020, uses which type of propulsion?
questions.exp: A scramjet is a supersonic-combustion ramjet in which airflow through the combustor remains supersonic. The HSTDV achieved about Mach 6.

questions.q: Under 'Mission Shakti', conducted in March 2019, India demonstrated the capability to:
opts: Intercept an incoming ballistic missile in space
Destroy a satellite in low Earth orbit
questions.exp: The DRDO anti-satellite test destroyed a live satellite at about 283 km altitude, making India the fourth country after the USA, Russia and China to demonstrate ASAT capability.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Pinaka system:
I. It is a multi-barrel rocket launcher developed by DRDO.
II. It was used during the Kargil conflict of 1999.
III. Its guided variant has a demonstrated range of over 70 km.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Pinaka was developed by the Armament Research and Development Establishment, Pune. The Mk-I has a range of about 38 km and the guided variant exceeds 70 km.

questions.q: 'Pralay', developed by DRDO, is a:
questions.exp: Pralay is a solid-fuelled, conventionally armed quasi-ballistic missile with a range of about 150-500 km, cleared for induction with the armed forces.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Missile)   List-II (Approximate range)
A. Prithvi-II      1. 750 km
B. Agni-III        2. 350 km
C. K-15 (Sagarika) 3. 3,000 km
D. Agni-V          4. 5,000 km
questions.exp: K-15 Sagarika and the longer-ranged K-4 (about 3,500 km) are submarine-launched missiles carried by Arihant-class boats and form the sea leg of India's nuclear triad.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's Ballistic Missile Defence programme:
I. Its Phase-I comprises the exo-atmospheric Prithvi Air Defence and the endo-atmospheric Advanced Air Defence interceptors.
II. It has been developed by DRDO.
III. It was developed jointly with the United States.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The BMD programme is indigenous to DRDO. Phase-II envisages the AD-1 and AD-2 interceptors for longer-range threats.

questions.q: The Light Combat Aircraft Tejas is designed by the Aeronautical Development Agency and manufactured by:
questions.exp: Tejas received Initial Operational Clearance in 2013 and Final Operational Clearance in 2019. The Mk-1A variant is powered by the GE F404 engine.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) programme:
I. It aims to develop a fifth-generation stealth fighter.
II. It is being led by the Aeronautical Development Agency.
III. The aircraft has already entered squadron service with the Indian Air Force.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Cabinet Committee on Security approved AMCA development in March 2024; as of 2026 the prototype has not yet flown.

questions.q: The Light Combat Helicopter inducted into the Indian armed forces in October 2022 is named:
questions.exp: Built by HAL, Prachand can operate at altitudes above 5,000 m, making it suitable for Siachen-level operations. Its first squadron was raised at Jodhpur.

questions.q: TAPAS-BH, a medium-altitude long-endurance unmanned aerial vehicle, has been developed by which DRDO laboratory?
questions.exp: The Aeronautical Development Establishment developed TAPAS (earlier called Rustom-II) as well as the Nishant and Lakshya systems.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of an aerial platform and its description is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Netra — Airborne early warning and control system
questions.exp: Prachand is HAL's Light Combat Helicopter. HAL's indigenous basic trainer aircraft is the HTT-40.

questions.q: INS Vikrant, commissioned in September 2022, is significant as:
opts: India's first indigenously designed and built aircraft carrier
questions.exp: Built at Cochin Shipyard, it displaces about 45,000 tonnes. INS Vikramaditya, acquired from Russia, was commissioned in 2013.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. INS Arihant is India's first indigenously built nuclear-powered ballistic missile submarine.
II. INS Arighaat was commissioned in 2024.
III. The Kalvari-class submarines are nuclear-powered.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Kalvari-class (Scorpene) boats are conventional diesel-electric submarines built at Mazagon Dock under Project 75 with France's Naval Group; INS Vagsheer, the sixth, was commissioned in January 2025.

questions.q: INS Nistar, commissioned in July 2025, is India's first indigenously designed and built:
questions.exp: Built by Hindustan Shipyard Limited, Visakhapatnam, it supports deep-sea diving and submarine rescue operations. (Status as of 2026.)

questions.q: INS Himgiri and INS Udaygiri, commissioned together in August 2025, belong to which class of stealth frigates?
questions.exp: Project 17A frigates are built at Mazagon Dock and Garden Reach Shipbuilders. INS Nilgiri, the lead ship of the class, was commissioned in January 2025. (Status as of 2026.)

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of an Indian land-warfare system and its category is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Dhanush is a 155 mm/45 calibre indigenous towed howitzer derived from the Bofors gun, often called the 'Desi Bofors'. Nag is India's anti-tank guided missile.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (System)   List-II (Developing DRDO laboratory)
A. Arjun main battle tank   1. ARDE, Pune
B. Pinaka rocket system     2. CVRDE, Avadi
C. Varunastra heavyweight torpedo   3. NPOL, Kochi
D. Sonar systems for warships       4. NSTL, Visakhapatnam
questions.exp: CVRDE Avadi developed the Arjun tank, ARDE Pune the Pinaka, NSTL Visakhapatnam the Varunastra torpedo and NPOL Kochi India's sonar systems.

questions.q: The Advanced Towed Artillery Gun System (ATAGS) developed by DRDO is of which calibre?
questions.exp: ATAGS is a 155 mm/52 calibre towed howitzer developed by ARDE, Pune, with Bharat Forge and Tata Advanced Systems as production partners; it has demonstrated ranges of about 48 km.

questions.q:
Arrange the following events in Indian defence history in the correct chronological order:
I. Establishment of DRDO
II. Launch of the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme
III. Pokhran-II nuclear tests
IV. Commissioning of the indigenous aircraft carrier INS Vikrant
questions.exp: DRDO was set up in 1958, IGMDP launched in 1983, Pokhran-II conducted in 1998 and INS Vikrant commissioned in 2022.

questions.q: The AK-203 assault rifles for the Indian Army are being manufactured in India at:
questions.exp: They are produced by Indo-Russian Rifles Private Limited, an India-Russia joint venture. The AK-203 replaces the indigenous INSAS rifle.

questions.q: India's first nuclear test, code-named 'Smiling Buddha', was conducted in 1974 at Pokhran, which lies in which district of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The test was conducted on 18 May 1974. The Pokhran range in Jaisalmer district was used again on 11 and 13 May 1998 for Operation Shakti.

questions.q: National Technology Day is observed on 11 May every year to commemorate:
questions.exp: On 11 May 1998 India conducted nuclear tests at Pokhran under Operation Shakti; the maiden flight of the indigenous Hansa-3 aircraft and a Trishul missile test on the same day are also commemorated.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's nuclear doctrine adopted in 2003:
I. It is based on a policy of No First Use.
II. It promises massive retaliation to a nuclear first strike.
III. It permits the first use of nuclear weapons against non-nuclear weapon states.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: India has pledged non-use of nuclear weapons against non-nuclear weapon states, maintains credible minimum deterrence and observes a unilateral moratorium on further testing.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. India joined the Missile Technology Control Regime in 2016.
II. India is a member of the Wassenaar Arrangement and the Australia Group.
III. India is a member of the Nuclear Suppliers Group.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: India joined MTCR (2016), the Wassenaar Arrangement (2017) and the Australia Group (2018), but is not a member of the NSG and has signed neither the NPT nor the CTBT.

questions.q: The Ordnance Factory Board was dissolved in 2021 and its units were reorganised into how many new defence public sector undertakings?
questions.exp: The seven are Munitions India, Armoured Vehicles Nigam (AVANI), Advanced Weapons and Equipment India, Troop Comforts, Yantra India, India Optel and Gliders India; the change took effect on 1 October 2021.

questions.q: The two defence industrial corridors announced by the Government of India are located in:
questions.exp: Announced in the 2018-19 Union Budget, the Uttar Pradesh corridor has nodes at Aligarh, Agra, Jhansi, Kanpur, Chitrakoot and Lucknow, and the Tamil Nadu corridor at Chennai, Coimbatore, Hosur, Salem and Tiruchirappalli.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs relating to defence indigenisation is NOT correctly matched?
opts: iDEX — Engaging start-ups and MSMEs in defence innovation
Positive Indigenisation Lists — Items barred from import beyond a notified date
Agnipath — Corporatisation of the ordnance factories
questions.exp: Agnipath is the short-service military recruitment scheme launched in 2022; the ordnance factories were corporatised into seven DPSUs in 2021.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Agnipath scheme:
I. It was announced in June 2022.
II. Agniveers are enrolled for a tenure of four years.
III. Up to 25 per cent of each batch may be retained in regular service.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The scheme applies to all three services and was introduced to lower the average age profile of the armed forces.

questions.q: The Chief of Defence Staff, a post created in 2019, also functions as the head of which body?
questions.exp: General Bipin Rawat became the first CDS on 1 January 2020. The CDS is also the Permanent Chairman of the Chiefs of Staff Committee.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about India's tri-service defence structures is NOT correct?
opts: The Andaman and Nicobar Command, created in 2001, is India's first tri-service command
The Strategic Forces Command was created in 2003
The Chief of Defence Staff heads the Department of Military Affairs
The Integrated Defence Staff was created in 2019
questions.exp: The Integrated Defence Staff was set up in 2001 on the recommendations of the Kargil Review Committee; the post of CDS and the Department of Military Affairs were created in 2019.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Military exercise)   List-II (Partner country)
A. Yudh Abhyas   1. France
B. Varuna        2. Russia
C. Indra         3. United States of America
D. Surya Kiran   4. Nepal
questions.exp: Yudh Abhyas is the India-US army exercise, Varuna the India-France naval exercise, Indra the India-Russia exercise and Surya Kiran the India-Nepal army exercise.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Military exercise)   List-II (Partner country)
A. Mitra Shakti   1. Bangladesh
B. Sampriti       2. Sri Lanka
C. Dustlik        3. Uzbekistan
D. Ekuverin       4. Maldives
questions.exp: Mitra Shakti is with Sri Lanka, Sampriti with Bangladesh, Dustlik with Uzbekistan and Ekuverin with the Maldives.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of a joint military exercise and its partner is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Malabar — a naval exercise of India, the USA, Japan and Australia
questions.exp: Al Nagah is an India-Oman army exercise. The India-Egypt army exercise is named 'Cyclone'.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of a central armed police force and its year of raising is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The National Security Guard was raised in 1984. The Assam Rifles, raised in 1835, is the oldest paramilitary force in India.

chapters.title: Environment, Ecology, EIA, Biodiversity and Sustainable Development
factsheet: Ecology hierarchy: individual - population - community - ecosystem - landscape - biome - biosphere; term 'ecosystem' coined by A.G. Tansley (1935).
10 per cent law of energy transfer between trophic levels - Raymond Lindeman (1942); pyramid of energy is always upright.
Gaseous cycles: carbon, nitrogen, oxygen (reservoir = atmosphere). Sedimentary cycles: phosphorus, sulphur (reservoir = rocks); phosphorus cycle has no gaseous phase.
N-fixers: Rhizobium (symbiotic, legumes), Frankia (Casuarina), Azotobacter (free-living aerobic), Clostridium (anaerobic), Anabaena/Nostoc (cyanobacteria, Azolla).
Ecotone = transition zone between two ecosystems; edge effect = higher species density at the ecotone. Lichens are pioneers of xerarch (bare rock) succession.

Biodiversity hotspot criteria (Norman Myers, 1988): at least 1,500 endemic vascular plants AND at least 70% of primary vegetation lost. Four hotspots reach India: Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats-Sri Lanka, Sundaland (Nicobar).
Alpha diversity = within a community/habitat; Beta = turnover between communities along a gradient; Gamma = total diversity of a landscape or region.
IUCN (founded 1948, HQ Gland, Switzerland) Red List has 9 categories; 'threatened' = Critically Endangered + Endangered + Vulnerable.
Biosphere reserve zones: core (legally protected) - buffer - transition. India's first biosphere reserve: Nilgiri (1986). Rajasthan has none.
Project Tiger 1973 (nine reserves incl. Ranthambore); NTCA statutory in 2006 under the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972. Project Elephant 1992; Project Snow Leopard 2009; Project Dolphin 2020.
Rajasthan tiger reserves: Ranthambore (Sawai Madhopur), Sariska (Alwar), Mukundra Hills (Kota, 2013), Ramgarh Vishdhari (Bundi, 2022 - India's 52nd), Dholpur-Karauli (2023 - India's 54th).
Ramsar sites of Rajasthan (five): Keoladeo Ghana NP (1981), Sambhar Lake (1990), Menar (2025), Khichan (2025) and Siliserh Lake, Alwar (2025).
Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 (Act 53 of 1972): 2022 amendment (in force 1 April 2023) cut schedules from six to four - Sch. I & II animals, Sch. III plants, Sch. IV CITES specimens.

Biological Diversity Act 2002: three-tier - National Biodiversity Authority (Chennai), State Biodiversity Boards, Biodiversity Management Committees (People's Biodiversity Registers). 2023 amendment exempts registered AYUSH practitioners and decriminalises offences.

Forest (Conservation) Act 1980 renamed Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam 1980 by the 2023 amendment; exempts land within 100 km of international borders for strategic linear projects and 10 ha for security infrastructure.
Forest Rights Act 2006 - nodal Ministry of Tribal Affairs; Gram Sabha is the authority; cut-off date 13 December 2005.

Water Act 1974 created CPCB/SPCBs; Air Act 1981; Environment (Protection) Act 1986 (umbrella Act, under Article 253, following Stockholm 1972, after the 1984 Bhopal disaster); Environment Audit Rules notified 29 August 2025.

National Green Tribunal Act 2010 - NGT set up 18 October 2010, principal bench New Delhi, zonal benches Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata, Chennai; disposal within 6 months; India was the third country with a dedicated green court.
National AQI (2014): 6 categories - Good 0-50, Satisfactory 51-100, Moderate 101-200, Poor 201-300, Very Poor 301-400, Severe 401-500; 8 pollutants (PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, O3, NH3, Pb).
Acid rain = SO2 + NOx converting to H2SO4 and HNO3; rain with pH below 5.6 is acidic. NCAP launched January 2019; revised target 40% cut in particulate concentration by 2025-26 over 2017.
Greenhouse contribution order: CO2 (~60%) > CH4 (~20%) > CFCs (~14%) > N2O (~6%). Highest 100-year GWP: SF6.
BOD measured over 5 days at 20 degrees C; COD always exceeds BOD. Mercury-Minamata, Cadmium-Itai-itai, Nitrate-blue baby syndrome, Fluoride-fluorosis.
Single-use plastic ban effective 1 July 2022; carry bag thickness 120 microns from 31 December 2022; E-Waste (Management) Rules 2022 in force 1 April 2023; EPR = Extended Producer Responsibility.
Ozone: Vienna Convention 1985, Montreal Protocol 1987 (World Ozone Day 16 September), Kigali Amendment 2016 phases down HFCs (in force 1 January 2019; India ratified 2021).

Climate diplomacy: IPCC 1988 (WMO+UNEP); UNFCCC Rio 1992; Kyoto 1997; Paris 2015 (well below 2 C, pursue 1.5 C); COP26 Glasgow - Panchamrit and net-zero 2070; COP28 Dubai - first Global Stocktake; COP29 Baku - NCQG USD 300 bn/yr by 2035; COP30 Belem 2025 - 'global mutirao'; COP31 Antalya (Turkiye) 2026.
India's NDC: 45% emissions-intensity cut and 50% non-fossil capacity by 2030; new NDC (2031-35) approved 25 March 2026 - 47% intensity cut and 60% non-fossil capacity by 2035, net-zero 2070.

NAPCC (2008) - eight missions: Solar, Enhanced Energy Efficiency, Sustainable Habitat, Water, Sustaining the Himalayan Ecosystem, Green India, Sustainable Agriculture, Strategic Knowledge for Climate Change.
ISA launched 2015 (India-France), HQ Gurugram - first treaty-based international organisation headquartered in India; CDRI launched 2019, HQ New Delhi; Mission LiFE launched October 2022 at Kevadia.

EIA Notification 2006 (under EP Act 1986): stages Screening - Scoping - Public Consultation - Appraisal; Category A cleared by MoEFCC/EAC, Category B by SEIAA/SEAC (B1 needs EIA, B2 does not); public hearing conducted by the SPCB.

Disaster Management Act 2005: NDMA chaired by PM, SDMA by CM, DDMA by District Collector; NEC headed by Union Home Secretary; NDRF and NIDM created under it; Sendai Framework 2015-2030 has 4 priorities and 7 global targets.

questions.q: The '10 per cent law' of energy transfer between successive trophic levels in an ecosystem was proposed by:
questions.exp: Lindeman (1942) showed that only about 10 per cent of the energy at one trophic level is transferred to the next. Charles Elton gave the concept of the ecological pyramid.

questions.q: Which one of the following ecological pyramids is always upright?
questions.exp: Because energy is lost as heat at every transfer, the pyramid of energy can never be inverted. Pyramids of number and biomass may be inverted, as in a single-tree ecosystem or in the sea.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about food chains:
I. The grazing food chain begins with green plants.
II. The detritus food chain begins with dead organic matter.
III. In terrestrial ecosystems, a much larger fraction of energy flows through the detritus food chain than through the grazing food chain.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. In terrestrial ecosystems most net primary production is not grazed but enters the detritus pathway, whereas in many aquatic systems the grazing food chain dominates.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of an ecological category and its example is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The Great Indian Bustard (Godawan) is a critically endangered native bird and Rajasthan's state bird, not an invasive species. Lichens are classic indicators of sulphur dioxide pollution.

questions.q: The zone of transition between two adjacent ecosystems, which usually supports greater species richness than either of them, is called:
questions.exp: The greater species density and richness at an ecotone is called the edge effect, and species largely confined to it are edge species.

questions.q: Which one of the following biogeochemical cycles is a purely sedimentary cycle with no significant gaseous phase?
questions.exp: The reservoir of phosphorus is rock, and it has no appreciable gaseous component. Nitrogen, carbon and oxygen cycles are gaseous cycles with the atmosphere as reservoir.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Organism)   List-II (Mode of nitrogen fixation)
A. Rhizobium   1. Symbiotic with roots of legumes
B. Frankia   2. Symbiotic with Casuarina
C. Azotobacter   3. Free-living aerobic bacterium
D. Anabaena   4. Cyanobacterium associated with Azolla
questions.exp: Rhizobium nodulates legume roots, Frankia nodulates Casuarina, Azotobacter is free-living and aerobic, and Anabaena azollae lives in the leaf cavities of the water fern Azolla.

questions.q: In primary ecological succession on a bare rock surface, the pioneer community is normally formed by:
questions.exp: Lichens secrete acids that weather rock and initiate soil formation; mosses follow. Both xerarch and hydrarch successions ultimately converge on a mesic climax community.

questions.q: The diversity of species found within a single community or habitat is termed:
questions.exp: Alpha diversity is diversity within a habitat; beta diversity is the change in composition between habitats along a gradient; gamma diversity is the total diversity of a landscape or region.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Beta diversity refers to the change in species composition between communities along an environmental gradient.
II. Gamma diversity refers to the total species diversity of a large geographical region or landscape.
III. Alpha diversity of a habitat is always greater than the gamma diversity of the region containing it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statements I and II are the standard Whittaker definitions. Statement III is wrong: gamma diversity, being the regional total, is equal to or greater than the alpha diversity of any one habitat within it.

questions.q: Which one of the following biodiversity hotspots does NOT extend into Indian territory?
questions.exp: The Cerrado is a South American hotspot. Four hotspots reach India: Himalaya, Indo-Burma, Western Ghats-Sri Lanka and Sundaland (through the Nicobar Islands).

questions.q: The concept of 'biodiversity hotspots' was first proposed in 1988 by:
questions.exp: Norman Myers proposed the hotspot concept in 1988; Conservation International later refined it. Thirty-six hotspots are recognised worldwide.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a criterion for designating an area as a biodiversity hotspot?
opts: It must contain at least 500 endemic vertebrate species
It must contain at least 1,500 species of endemic vascular plants
It must have lost at least 70 per cent of its original primary vegetation
It is identified on the basis of both endemism and degree of threat
questions.exp: The two quantitative criteria relate to endemic vascular plants and to habitat loss; there is no vertebrate-endemism threshold.

questions.q: In the IUCN Red List, the three categories that together constitute 'threatened' species are:
opts: Extinct, Extinct in the Wild and Critically Endangered
Vulnerable, Near Threatened and Least Concern
questions.exp: The IUCN Red List has nine categories in all; the threatened group comprises Critically Endangered, Endangered and Vulnerable. IUCN was founded in 1948 and is headquartered at Gland, Switzerland.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. National parks and biosphere reserves are examples of in-situ conservation.
II. Cryopreservation of gametes is a form of ex-situ conservation.
III. Botanical gardens and seed banks are examples of ex-situ conservation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. In-situ conservation protects species in their natural habitat; ex-situ conservation maintains them outside it, as in zoos, botanical gardens, gene banks and cryopreservation facilities.

questions.q: The three zones into which a biosphere reserve is conventionally divided are:
questions.exp: Only the core zone is legally protected and free of human interference; limited activity is allowed in the buffer, and settled human use in the transition zone. India's first biosphere reserve was the Nilgiri (1986).

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Biosphere reserve)   List-II (State)
A. Nokrek   1. Meghalaya
B. Simlipal   2. Odisha
C. Dihang-Dibang   3. Arunachal Pradesh
D. Agasthyamalai   4. Kerala and Tamil Nadu
questions.exp: Rajasthan has no biosphere reserve. India's first was the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, notified in 1986.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Project Tiger:
I. It was launched in 1973.
II. The National Tiger Conservation Authority was given statutory status in 2006.
III. Ranthambore was one of the nine tiger reserves created at the launch of the project.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. NTCA was constituted under the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 through the 2006 amendment; the 2022 all-India estimate placed the tiger population at about 3,682.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Tiger reserve of Rajasthan)   List-II (District)
A. Ranthambore   1. Sawai Madhopur
B. Sariska   2. Alwar
C. Mukundra Hills   3. Kota
D. Ramgarh Vishdhari   4. Bundi
questions.exp: Ramgarh Vishdhari (Bundi) was notified in 2022 as India's 52nd tiger reserve; Dholpur-Karauli, approved in 2023, is Rajasthan's fifth and India's 54th tiger reserve.

questions.q: Which of the following pairs of Rajasthan wetlands were the state's first two Ramsar sites?
questions.exp: Keoladeo Ghana National Park (Bharatpur) was designated in 1981 and Sambhar Lake in 1990. Khichan and Menar were added on 5 June 2025, taking Rajasthan's Ramsar tally to five. (Siliserh Lake, Alwar, was added in 2025.)

questions.q: The National Tiger Conservation Authority is a statutory body constituted under:
questions.exp: NTCA was created by the 2006 amendment to the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 and is chaired by the Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

questions.q: After the Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act, 2022, the number of schedules in the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 was reduced to:
questions.exp: The 2022 amendment, in force from 1 April 2023, reduced the schedules from six to four and rationalised the species lists.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the schedules of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 after the 2022 amendment:
I. Schedules I and II list animal species.
II. Schedule III lists plant species.
III. Schedule IV lists specimens included in the appendices of CITES.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Schedule I species get the highest protection; Schedule IV was introduced to implement India's CITES obligations, with registration of scheduled live specimens through the PARIVESH portal.

questions.q: The National Biodiversity Authority constituted under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002 has its headquarters at:
questions.exp: The Act creates a three-tier structure: the NBA at Chennai, State Biodiversity Boards, and Biodiversity Management Committees at the local body level.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Biological Diversity (Amendment) Act, 2023:
I. It exempts registered AYUSH practitioners from sharing benefits for the use of codified traditional knowledge.
II. It decriminalises offences under the Act and replaces imprisonment with monetary penalties.
III. It abolishes Biodiversity Management Committees at the local level.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statement III is wrong: Biodiversity Management Committees continue and remain responsible for People's Biodiversity Registers. The parent Act of 2002 gives effect to the Convention on Biological Diversity, 1992.

questions.q: Under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, the body constituted at the local body level is the:
questions.exp: Biodiversity Management Committees are constituted by every local body and prepare People's Biodiversity Registers documenting local biological resources and associated traditional knowledge.

questions.q: The Forest (Conservation) Amendment Act, 2023 renamed the parent Act of 1980 as:
questions.exp: The 2023 amendment renamed the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980 as the Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam, 1980 and narrowed the categories of land to which it applies.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Forest (Conservation) Amendment Act, 2023:
I. Forest land within 100 km of an international border proposed for a strategic linear project of national importance is exempted from prior central approval.
II. Up to 10 hectares of forest land proposed for security-related infrastructure is exempted.
III. The Act was passed to give statutory backing to the Compensatory Afforestation Fund.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statement III is wrong: the Compensatory Afforestation Fund has its own statute, the CAF Act, 2016. The 2023 amendment created the border-area and security-infrastructure exemptions and also exempted zoos, safaris and eco-tourism facilities.

questions.q: The nodal ministry for implementation of the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 is the:
opts: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
questions.exp: The Gram Sabha is the authority that initiates determination of forest rights; the cut-off date for claims is 13 December 2005.

questions.q: The Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 was enacted by Parliament under Article 253 of the Constitution to implement the decisions taken at the:
opts: United Nations Conference on the Human Environment, Stockholm, 1972
questions.exp: The Act is India's umbrella environmental legislation and was passed in the aftermath of the 1984 Bhopal gas disaster. Article 253 empowers Parliament to legislate to implement international agreements.

questions.q: The Central Pollution Control Board was constituted under which one of the following Acts?
opts: The Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
The Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
questions.exp: CPCB was set up in 1974 under the Water Act and was later entrusted with functions under the Air Act, 1981 as well. The Water Act was amended in 2024 to decriminalise several minor offences.

questions.q: The National Green Tribunal, established under the NGT Act, 2010, has its principal bench at:
questions.exp: The NGT was set up on 18 October 2010 with zonal benches at Bhopal, Pune, Kolkata and Chennai. India became the third country, after Australia and New Zealand, to set up a specialised environmental court.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Legislation)   List-II (Year of enactment)
A. Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act   1. 1974
B. Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act   2. 1981
C. Environment (Protection) Act   3. 1986
D. National Green Tribunal Act   4. 2010
questions.exp: These four Acts, along with the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972 and the Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980, form the core of India's environmental law.

questions.q: Acid rain is caused mainly by the atmospheric emission of which pair of pollutants?
opts: Sulphur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen
questions.exp: Sulphur dioxide and oxides of nitrogen are oxidised in the atmosphere to sulphuric and nitric acid. Rain is regarded as acid rain when its pH falls below 5.6.

questions.q: The National Air Quality Index of India, launched in 2014, classifies air quality into how many categories?
questions.exp: The six categories are Good, Satisfactory, Moderate, Poor, Very Poor and Severe. The index is computed for eight pollutants: PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, ozone, ammonia and lead.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (AQI value range)   List-II (Category)
A. 0-50   1. Good
B. 51-100   2. Satisfactory
C. 201-300   3. Poor
D. 401-500   4. Severe
questions.exp: The intervening bands are Moderate (101-200) and Very Poor (301-400). The AQI is computed by CPCB and reported as the worst sub-index among the eight pollutants.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Clean Air Programme:
I. It was launched in January 2019.
II. Its revised target is a 40 per cent reduction in particulate matter concentration by 2025-26 over the 2017 level.
III. It is implemented by the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statement III is wrong: NCAP is implemented by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change through CPCB in identified non-attainment cities.

questions.q: Which one of the following pollutants is NOT included in the computation of India's National Air Quality Index?
questions.exp: The eight AQI pollutants are PM10, PM2.5, NO2, SO2, CO, ozone, ammonia and lead. Methane, though a potent greenhouse gas, is not an AQI pollutant.

questions.q: A high biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) value of a water sample indicates:
opts: Low content of biodegradable organic matter
High content of biodegradable organic matter
questions.exp: BOD is measured over five days at 20 degrees C and reflects the oxygen consumed by microbes decomposing organic matter. Chemical oxygen demand is always higher than BOD for the same sample.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about eutrophication:
I. It is caused by enrichment of a water body with nutrients, chiefly nitrates and phosphates.
II. Algal blooms raise the dissolved oxygen level of the water body.
III. Eutrophication can cause large-scale fish kills.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statement II is wrong: decomposition of the algal bloom consumes oxygen and creates hypoxic conditions, which is precisely why fish die.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Pollutant)   List-II (Disease)
A. Mercury   1. Minamata disease
B. Cadmium   2. Itai-itai disease
C. Fluoride   3. Skeletal fluorosis
D. Nitrate   4. Blue baby syndrome
questions.exp: Blue baby syndrome (methaemoglobinaemia) results from high nitrate in drinking water. Fluorosis is a serious problem in several districts of western Rajasthan.

questions.q: The ban on manufacture, sale and use of identified single-use plastic items in India came into effect from:
questions.exp: The ban was imposed under the Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2021. The minimum thickness of plastic carry bags was raised to 120 microns from 31 December 2022.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of a programme and its year of launch is NOT correctly matched?
opts: National Action Plan on Climate Change — 2005
questions.exp: The National Action Plan on Climate Change was released in 2008, not 2005. Namami Gange is implemented by the National Mission for Clean Ganga, and the National Ganga Council is chaired by the Prime Minister.

questions.q: Which one of the following ambient noise standards for day time, prescribed under the Noise Pollution (Regulation and Control) Rules, 2000, is NOT correctly stated?
questions.exp: The day-time limit for a silence zone is 50 dB(A) Leq and the night-time limit 40 dB(A) Leq. Silence zones extend 100 metres around hospitals, educational institutions and courts.

questions.q: Which one of the following gases makes the largest contribution to the enhanced greenhouse effect?
questions.exp: Carbon dioxide accounts for roughly 60 per cent of the enhanced greenhouse effect, followed by methane (about 20 per cent), CFCs (about 14 per cent) and nitrous oxide (about 6 per cent).

questions.q:
Arrange the following greenhouse gases in descending order of their contribution to the enhanced greenhouse effect:
I. Methane
II. Carbon dioxide
III. Nitrous oxide
IV. Chlorofluorocarbons
questions.exp: The conventional order is carbon dioxide, methane, chlorofluorocarbons and nitrous oxide. By global warming potential per molecule, however, the order is reversed, with sulphur hexafluoride highest of all.

questions.q: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) was established in 1988 by:
opts: The World Meteorological Organization and UNEP
questions.exp: The IPCC assesses published science and does not conduct its own research. Its Sixth Assessment Report cycle concluded with the Synthesis Report in March 2023.

questions.q: The United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change was adopted at the Earth Summit held in 1992 at:
questions.exp: The Rio Earth Summit of 1992 also produced Agenda 21 and the Convention on Biological Diversity; the UNFCCC entered into force in 1994.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in correct chronological order:
I. Montreal Protocol
II. Stockholm Conference on the Human Environment
III. Paris Agreement
IV. Kyoto Protocol
questions.exp: Stockholm 1972, Montreal Protocol 1987, Kyoto Protocol 1997 and the Paris Agreement 2015. UNEP was created in the wake of the Stockholm Conference and is headquartered at Nairobi.

questions.q: The Paris Agreement, 2015 commits the parties to holding the increase in global average temperature to:
opts: Below 3 degrees C above pre-industrial levels
Below 2.5 degrees C above pre-industrial levels
Well below 2 degrees C, and to pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5 degrees C, above pre-industrial levels
questions.exp: The Paris Agreement was adopted at COP21 and entered into force on 4 November 2016. It works through nationally determined contributions and a Global Stocktake every five years.

questions.q: The 30th Conference of the Parties (COP30) to the UNFCCC was held in November 2025 at:
questions.exp: COP30 at Belem adopted the 'global mutirao' decision. COP29 was held at Baku in 2024 and COP31 is scheduled for Antalya, Turkiye, in November 2026 (position as of September 2026).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about recent climate conferences:
I. COP28 at Dubai in 2023 concluded the first Global Stocktake under the Paris Agreement.
II. COP29 at Baku in 2024 agreed a New Collective Quantified Goal on climate finance of at least USD 300 billion a year by 2035.
III. COP30 at Belem adopted a binding roadmap for transitioning away from fossil fuels.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statement III is wrong: no fossil-fuel roadmap was included in the COP30 decision text, though the presidency announced that voluntary roadmaps would be brought to COP31. Position as of September 2026.

questions.q: India announced its target of achieving net-zero emissions by 2070, as part of the 'Panchamrit', at:
questions.exp: The Panchamrit announced at Glasgow in 2021 also included 500 GW of non-fossil capacity by 2030, meeting half of energy requirements from renewables, and cutting projected emissions by one billion tonnes by 2030.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's Nationally Determined Contribution for 2031-2035:
I. India will reduce the emissions intensity of its GDP by 47 per cent by 2035 from the 2005 level.
II. India will achieve about 60 per cent of cumulative electric power installed capacity from non-fossil fuel sources by 2035.
III. India's declared net-zero target year remains 2070.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Union Cabinet approved this NDC on 25 March 2026; it also targets an additional carbon sink of 3.5 to 4.0 billion tonnes of CO2 equivalent by 2035. Position as of September 2026.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Mission under the NAPCC)   List-II (Nodal ministry)
A. National Solar Mission   1. Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
B. National Water Mission   2. Ministry of Jal Shakti
C. National Mission for a Green India   3. Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
D. National Mission for Enhanced Energy Efficiency   4. Ministry of Power
questions.exp: The National Action Plan on Climate Change, released in 2008, has eight missions; the other four are Sustainable Habitat, Sustaining the Himalayan Ecosystem, Sustainable Agriculture and Strategic Knowledge for Climate Change.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT one of the eight missions under the National Action Plan on Climate Change?
opts: National Mission for Sustaining the Himalayan Ecosystem
questions.exp: Clean air is addressed by the National Clean Air Programme of 2019, which is not a NAPCC mission. States prepare State Action Plans on Climate Change aligned with the NAPCC.

questions.q: The International Solar Alliance, jointly launched by India and France in 2015, has its headquarters at:
questions.exp: The ISA was launched at COP21 in Paris and its secretariat is at Gwal Pahari, Gurugram. It is the first treaty-based international organisation headquartered in India.

questions.q: The Environmental Impact Assessment Notification currently governing environmental clearance in India was issued in:
questions.exp: The EIA Notification of 14 September 2006, issued under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986, replaced the 1994 notification. A draft notification of 2020 was published but has not replaced it.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the EIA Notification, 2006:
I. Category 'A' projects are appraised at the central level by an Expert Appraisal Committee.
II. Category 'B1' projects require preparation of an EIA report, whereas 'B2' projects do not.
III. The public hearing is conducted by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statement III is wrong: the public hearing is conducted by the concerned State Pollution Control Board or Pollution Control Committee.

questions.q: Under the EIA Notification, 2006, the public hearing for a project is conducted by the:
opts: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
questions.exp: The public consultation stage comprises a public hearing at the site and written responses from other concerned persons. Certain categories, such as modernisation of irrigation projects, are exempted from public consultation.

questions.q: Environmental clearance for Category 'B' projects under the EIA Notification, 2006 is granted by the:
opts: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
questions.exp: SEIAA acts on the recommendation of the State Expert Appraisal Committee. Where no SEIAA has been constituted, the project is treated as Category A and appraised at the central level.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT one of the four stages of the environmental clearance process prescribed under the EIA Notification, 2006?
questions.exp: The four stages are screening, scoping, public consultation and appraisal. Screening decides whether a Category B project needs a full EIA; scoping fixes the terms of reference.

questions.q: The Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer was adopted to give effect to which one of the following framework conventions?
opts: The Basel Convention on the Control of Transboundary Movements of Hazardous Wastes
The Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants
The Vienna Convention for the Protection of the Ozone Layer
The Rotterdam Convention on Prior Informed Consent
questions.exp: The Vienna Convention (1985) is the framework treaty; the Montreal Protocol (1987) is the binding instrument adopted under it and is the only UN treaty ratified by every member state. The Kigali Amendment (2016) later added the phase-down of hydrofluorocarbons, which do not deplete ozone but have a very high global warming potential; India ratified it in 2021.

questions.q: The Montreal Protocol of 1987 deals with:
questions.exp: It operationalises the Vienna Convention of 1985. World Ozone Day is observed on 16 September, the date the Protocol was signed. Hazardous waste movement is governed by the Basel Convention.

questions.q: The classic definition of sustainable development as development that meets the needs of the present without compromising the ability of future generations to meet their own needs was given in:
questions.exp: The Brundtland Commission was formally the World Commission on Environment and Development. 'The Future We Want' was the outcome document of the Rio+20 Conference of 2012.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sustainable Development Goals:
I. There are 17 goals and 169 targets.
II. They were adopted in September 2015 as part of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development.
III. In India, the SDG India Index is published by NITI Aayog.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
