questions.exp: All three are correct. The SDGs succeeded the eight Millennium Development Goals; SDG 13 relates to climate action and SDG 15 to life on land.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Disaster Management Act, 2005:
I. It provides for the constitution of the National Institute of Disaster Management.
II. It provides for the constitution of the National Disaster Response Force.
III. The National Executive Committee under the Act is chaired by the Union Home Secretary.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Act also created the NDMA at the national level, SDMAs in the states and DDMAs in the districts.

questions.q: India's first National Disaster Management Plan, aligned with the Sendai Framework, was released in:
questions.exp: The plan was released in 2016 and revised in 2019. It covers all phases of disaster management: prevention, mitigation, response and recovery.

questions.q: The Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction, adopted in 2015, covers the period:
questions.exp: Adopted at the third World Conference on Disaster Risk Reduction at Sendai, Japan, it has four priorities for action and seven global targets, and succeeded the Hyogo Framework of 2005-2015.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Body under the Disaster Management Act, 2005)   List-II (Ex-officio head)
A. National Disaster Management Authority   1. Prime Minister
B. State Disaster Management Authority   2. Chief Minister
C. District Disaster Management Authority   3. District Collector
D. National Executive Committee   4. Union Home Secretary
questions.exp: In a district with an elected zila parishad, its chairperson is co-chairperson of the DDMA. The NDMA has up to nine members besides the Prime Minister.

chapters.title: Agriculture, Horticulture, Forestry, Animal Husbandry (Rajasthan focus); S&T Policy and Indian Scientists
factsheet: Soil Health Card Scheme launched by the Prime Minister on 19 February 2015 from Suratgarh, Sri Ganganagar (Rajasthan).

Nutrient deficiency symptoms: nitrogen - chlorosis of older leaves; phosphorus - purplish tinge; potassium - scorching of leaf margins; zinc - khaira disease in rice. Calcium, magnesium and sulphur are secondary macronutrients.
Seed multiplication chain: breeder seed (golden-yellow tag) - foundation seed (white tag) - certified seed (azure-blue tag); truthfully labelled seed carries an opal-green label.
Rajasthan leads India in bajra, rapeseed-mustard, guar, coriander, cumin, fenugreek, isabgol, henna and moth bean, and is the largest wool producer and holder of the largest camel population.
HHB-67 Improved is an early-maturing, downy-mildew-resistant bajra hybrid; RGC-936 and RGC-1003 are guar varieties; Pusa Bold and Bio-902 are mustard varieties.
ICAR-Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research is at Sewar, Bharatpur (Rajasthan).

Desert locust = Schistocerca gregaria. The Locust Warning Organisation is headquartered at Jodhpur under the Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine and Storage, Faridabad; the Scheduled Desert Area lies in Rajasthan and Gujarat.
PMKSY (2015): 'Har Khet Ko Pani' and 'Per Drop More Crop' (micro-irrigation). Namo Drone Didi provides agricultural drones to women's self-help groups.
Khadin (Jaisalmer) is a traditional runoff-harvesting cropping system; other traditional structures are tanka, nadi, johad, baori and toba.
Seed spices of Rajasthan: coriander, cumin, fennel, fenugreek, ajwain, dill, celery and nigella; Rajasthan and Gujarat together dominate India's seed-spice output.
ICAR-National Research Centre on Seed Spices, Tabiji, Ajmer - established 2000.
ICAR-National Research Centre on Camel, Bikaner - established 1984; ICAR-Central Institute for Arid Horticulture, Bikaner - established 1993.
ICAR-Central Arid Zone Research Institute (CAZRI), Jodhpur - 1959; ICAR-Central Sheep and Wool Research Institute (CSWRI), Avikanagar, Malpura tehsil, Tonk district - 1962.
Arid Forest Research Institute (AFRI), Jodhpur - under ICFRE; Rajasthan Remote Sensing Centre, Jodhpur; Ch. Charan Singh National Institute of Agricultural Marketing (NIAM), Jaipur.
CSIR-Central Electronics Engineering Research Institute (CEERI), Pilani is the only CSIR laboratory in Rajasthan; BITS Pilani is a leading private deemed university of the state.

Udaipur Solar Observatory, on an island in Fateh Sagar Lake, was founded in 1975 by Dr. Arvind Bhatnagar and is operated by the Physical Research Laboratory, Ahmedabad; it hosts the Multi-Application Solar Telescope (MAST).
Agricultural universities: MPUAT Udaipur, SKRAU Bikaner, SKN Agriculture University Jobner, Agriculture University Jodhpur, Agriculture University Kota, RAJUVAS Bikaner; RARI is at Durgapura, Jaipur.

Sojat (Pali) is the henna (Lawsonia inermis) capital and holds a GI tag; isabgol is Plantago ovata; ashwagandha is Withania somnifera; safed musli is Chlorophytum borivilianum; guggul is Commiphora wightii.

Khejri (Prosopis cineraria) is the state tree, 'kalpavriksha of the desert', yielding sangri pods; Rohida (Tecomella undulata) is the state flower, called Marwar teak; Prosopis juliflora is the invasive 'vilayati babool'.
Kinnow belt - Sri Ganganagar and Hanumangarh; olive plantations - Lunkaransar (Bikaner) and Bassi (Jaipur); orange - Jhalawar; date palm - Jaisalmer and Bikaner; pomegranate - Barmer and Jalore.
Cattle breeds: Rathi (Bikaner-Sri Ganganagar, best milch), Tharparkar (Jaisalmer-Barmer), Kankrej (Jalore-Sirohi), Nagauri (Nagaur, draught), Malvi (Jhalawar), Hariana (Bharatpur-Alwar).

Sheep breeds: Chokla (Shekhawati, finest wool), Magra (Bikaner-Jaisalmer, lustrous carpet wool), Marwari (Jodhpur-Pali), Nali (Sri Ganganagar-Churu), Sonadi (Udaipur-Dungarpur), Pugal, Jaisalmeri, Malpuri.

Goat breeds: Sirohi (meat), Jakhrana of Alwar (milk), Marwari, Barbari. Camel breeds: Bikaneri, Jaisalmeri (riding), Mewari (milk), Kachchhi; camel declared state animal (domestic) in 2014 and protected by a 2015 state Act.

Livestock disease control: NADCP (2019) targets foot-and-mouth disease and brucellosis; Rashtriya Gokul Mission (2014) develops indigenous bovine breeds; lumpy skin disease is caused by a capripoxvirus.

National Forest Policy 1988 targets 33 per cent of geographical area under forest and tree cover; Joint Forest Management circular issued in 1990; Van Dhan Vikas Kendras are run by TRIFED under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.

Science days: National Science Day 28 February (Raman Effect, 1928), National Technology Day 11 May (Pokhran-II, 1998), National Space Day 23 August (Chandrayaan-3, 2023), National Mathematics Day 22 December (Ramanujan).

S&T institutions: CSIR founded 1942, DST 1971, DSIR and DBT in the 1980s; STIP 2020 is India's fifth S&T policy; the Anusandhan National Research Foundation was created by an Act of 2023 with the Prime Minister as ex-officio President.
Indian Nobel laureates in science: C.V. Raman (Physics 1930), Har Gobind Khorana (Physiology or Medicine 1968), S. Chandrasekhar (Physics 1983), Venkatraman Ramakrishnan (Chemistry 2009).

Scientists and contributions: Meghnad Saha - thermal ionisation equation; S.N. Bose - Bose-Einstein statistics; J.C. Bose - crescograph; Homi Bhabha - Bhabha scattering and the three-stage nuclear programme; Vikram Sarabhai - PRL and ISRO; Birbal Sahni - palaeobotany; Salim Ali - ornithology.
Daulat Singh Kothari, born at Udaipur, chaired the Education Commission of 1964-66 and was the first Scientific Adviser to the Ministry of Defence.

questions.q: The Soil Health Card Scheme was launched by the Prime Minister in February 2015 from which place in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: The scheme was launched on 19 February 2015 from Suratgarh. A soil health card reports twelve parameters, including the primary nutrients N, P and K and the micronutrients.

questions.q: Yellowing of older leaves, known as chlorosis, is the classic symptom of the deficiency of which nutrient in crops?
questions.exp: Nitrogen is mobile in the plant and is withdrawn from older leaves first, so deficiency shows there. Potassium deficiency shows as scorching of leaf margins.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Nutrient)   List-II (Deficiency symptom)
A. Nitrogen   1. General chlorosis of older leaves
B. Phosphorus   2. Purplish tinge on leaves and stems
C. Potassium   3. Scorching of leaf margins
D. Zinc   4. Khaira disease of rice
questions.exp: Zinc deficiency is widespread in the calcareous and sandy soils of Rajasthan. Neem-coated urea was made mandatory in 2015 to improve nitrogen use efficiency.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a micronutrient for plants?
questions.exp: Calcium, along with magnesium and sulphur, is a secondary macronutrient. The plant micronutrients are iron, manganese, zinc, copper, boron, molybdenum, chlorine and nickel.

questions.q: In India's seed certification system, the colour of the tag used for certified seed is:
questions.exp: Breeder seed carries a golden-yellow tag, foundation seed a white tag and certified seed an azure-blue tag; truthfully labelled seed carries an opal-green label.

questions.q:
Arrange the following classes of seed in the correct order of the seed multiplication chain:
I. Certified seed
II. Breeder seed
III. Foundation seed
questions.exp: Breeder seed is produced under the direct supervision of the plant breeder, is multiplied into foundation seed, and that in turn into certified seed for distribution to farmers.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. Rajasthan is India's largest producer of bajra.
II. Rajasthan is India's largest producer of rapeseed-mustard.
III. Rajasthan is India's largest producer of sugarcane.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Uttar Pradesh leads in sugarcane. Rajasthan also leads in guar, coriander, cumin, fenugreek, isabgol and moth bean.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about guar (cluster bean) in Rajasthan:
I. Rajasthan accounts for the bulk of India's guar production.
II. Guar gum is an important export item used in the oil and gas industry.
III. Guar is grown in Rajasthan as a rabi crop.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statement III is wrong: guar is a kharif crop sown with the onset of the monsoon. Sri Ganganagar, Hanumangarh, Bikaner, Churu and Nagaur are the main guar districts.

questions.q: HHB-67 Improved, an early-maturing and downy-mildew-resistant variety widely grown in Rajasthan, belongs to which crop?
questions.exp: HHB-67 Improved matures in about 62-65 days, which allows it to escape late-season drought in the arid west of the state.

questions.q: The ICAR Directorate of Rapeseed-Mustard Research is located at:
questions.exp: It is located at Sewar, Bharatpur, and began in 1993 as the National Research Centre on Rapeseed-Mustard. Rajasthan is India's leading rapeseed-mustard producing state.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a kharif crop of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Barley is a rabi crop, as are wheat, gram and mustard. Bajra, moth bean, guar, jowar, maize and cotton are kharif crops in the state.

questions.q: Inclusion of a legume in a crop rotation chiefly improves soil fertility by:
opts: Fixing atmospheric nitrogen through root nodule bacteria
Increasing the clay content of the soil
questions.exp: Rhizobium in the root nodules of legumes fixes atmospheric nitrogen. Guar, moth bean, moong and gram are the important legumes of Rajasthan's rotations.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about dryland farming:
I. It is practised in areas receiving less than about 750 mm of annual rainfall.
II. Conservation of soil moisture is its central objective.
III. Mulching reduces evaporation losses from the soil surface.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Most of western Rajasthan falls in the dryland and desert category, where khadin cultivation, mulching and drought-escaping short-duration varieties are standard practice.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about locusts in Rajasthan:
I. The species responsible for swarming attacks in western Rajasthan is Schistocerca gregaria, the desert locust.
II. The Locust Warning Organisation is headquartered at Jodhpur.
III. The Scheduled Desert Area for locust control lies in Rajasthan and Gujarat.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Locust Warning Organisation works under the Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine and Storage at Faridabad; a major upsurge affected Rajasthan in 2019-20.

questions.q: The headquarters of India's Locust Warning Organisation is at:
questions.exp: Circle offices are spread across the desert districts of Rajasthan and Gujarat. The parent Directorate of Plant Protection, Quarantine and Storage is at Faridabad.

questions.q: 'Per Drop More Crop', the micro-irrigation component promoting drip and sprinkler systems, is part of which scheme?
questions.exp: PMKSY was launched in 2015 with the motto 'Har Khet Ko Pani'. Sprinkler irrigation is especially widespread in Rajasthan because it suits sandy, highly permeable soils.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Integrated Pest Management:
I. It gives priority to cultural, mechanical and biological methods over chemical pesticides.
II. Trichogramma is used in it as a biological control agent.
III. Its objective is the complete eradication of the pest species.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statement III is wrong: IPM seeks to keep pest populations below the economic threshold level, not to eradicate them. Trichogramma is an egg parasitoid used against lepidopteran pests.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a protected cultivation structure?
questions.exp: Khadin is a traditional runoff-harvesting cropping system of the Jaisalmer region, in which a bund across a slope impounds runoff for growing a rabi crop on stored moisture.

questions.q: The 'Namo Drone Didi' scheme provides agricultural drones to:
questions.exp: The scheme equips selected women's self-help groups with drones for spraying fertilisers and pesticides, creating a rental service and a livelihood.

questions.q: Sprinkler irrigation is particularly suited to the sandy soils of western Rajasthan mainly because it:
opts: Reduces conveyance and deep percolation losses
questions.exp: In highly permeable sandy soils, flood irrigation loses much water to deep percolation; sprinklers apply water at a controlled rate close to the infiltration capacity.

questions.q: The ICAR National Research Centre on Seed Spices is located at:
questions.exp: The centre was established at Tabiji, Ajmer in 2000. Rajasthan and Gujarat together account for the bulk of India's seed-spice production.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Institute)   List-II (Location)
A. National Research Centre on Seed Spices   1. Ajmer
B. Central Institute for Arid Horticulture   2. Bikaner
C. Central Arid Zone Research Institute   3. Jodhpur
D. Central Sheep and Wool Research Institute   4. Avikanagar (Tonk)
questions.exp: The National Research Centre on Camel is also at Bikaner. CAZRI, established at Jodhpur in 1959, is the country's premier arid-zone research institute.

questions.q: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of seed spices grown in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Seed spices are those whose dried seeds or fruits are used; ajwain, dill, celery and nigella also belong to this group and are worked on at the National Research Centre on Seed Spices, Ajmer.

questions.q: Sojat in Rajasthan, whose produce carries a Geographical Indication tag, is famous for:
questions.exp: Sojat lies in Pali district and is the country's main henna processing centre. Henna is obtained from Lawsonia inermis.

questions.q: Isabgol, of which Rajasthan is the leading producer in India, is obtained from the plant:
questions.exp: The husk of the seed of Plantago ovata is psyllium, used as a laxative and largely exported. Jalore, Barmer, Sirohi and Nagaur are the main producing districts.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of a horticultural crop and its main growing area in Rajasthan is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: Jhalawar is famous for oranges. Olive cultivation in Rajasthan is concentrated at Lunkaransar in Bikaner and Bassi in Jaipur, where the state set up its olive plantation and refinery project.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Central Institute for Arid Horticulture, Bikaner:
I. It works on arid fruits such as ber, date palm, aonla and pomegranate.
II. It was established in 1993 as the National Research Centre for Arid Horticulture.
III. It functions under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statement III is wrong: like all ICAR institutes it functions under the Department of Agricultural Research and Education in the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare.

questions.q: Date palm cultivation in Rajasthan, promoted through tissue-culture plantations, is concentrated mainly in the districts of:
questions.exp: The hot, dry climate of the extreme west suits the date palm. The Central Institute for Arid Horticulture at Bikaner has been the lead institute for this programme.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Plant)   List-II (Botanical name)
A. Henna   1. Lawsonia inermis
B. Ashwagandha   2. Withania somnifera
C. Safed musli   3. Chlorophytum borivilianum
D. Guggul   4. Commiphora wightii
questions.exp: Ashwagandha grown around Nagaur is known locally as asgandh. Guggul is a threatened resin-yielding shrub of the Aravalli and desert tracts.

questions.q: The state tree of Rajasthan, the mainstay of desert agroforestry and the source of pods called 'sangri', is:
questions.exp: Khejri is called the kalpavriksha of the desert. The Bishnoi sacrifice at Khejarli in 1730, led by Amrita Devi, is commemorated by the Amrita Devi Bishnoi Wildlife Protection Award.

questions.q: Rohida (Tecomella undulata), the state flower of Rajasthan, is also popularly known as:
opts: Marwar teak or the teak of the desert
questions.exp: Rohida yields a hard, durable timber. The kalpavriksha of the desert is the khejri, which is the state tree.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The National Forest Policy, 1988 set the goal of bringing one-third of the country's geographical area under forest and tree cover.
II. Joint Forest Management was formally introduced through a Government of India circular in 1990.
III. The National Forest Policy, 1988 gave first priority to maximising revenue from forests.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statement III is wrong: the 1988 policy shifted the emphasis from revenue to ecological stability and the needs of forest-dependent communities. The policy target is 60 per cent cover in hills and 20 per cent in the plains.

questions.q: The Van Dhan Vikas Kendra scheme for value addition to minor forest produce is implemented by:
opts: Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education
TRIFED under the Ministry of Tribal Affairs
questions.exp: The scheme, launched in 2018, organises tribal gatherers into self-help groups for primary processing of minor forest produce, complementing the minimum support price scheme for MFP.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Cattle breed)   List-II (Home tract in Rajasthan)
A. Rathi   1. Bikaner and Sri Ganganagar
B. Tharparkar   2. Jaisalmer and Barmer
C. Kankrej   3. Jalore and Sirohi
D. Nagauri   4. Nagaur
questions.exp: Rathi is the best milch breed of the state, Tharparkar is dual-purpose and Kankrej and Nagauri are prized draught breeds. Malvi is found in Jhalawar and Hariana in the Bharatpur-Alwar tract.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Sheep breed)   List-II (Home tract)
A. Chokla   1. Sikar and Jhunjhunu
B. Magra   2. Bikaner and Jaisalmer
C. Sonadi   3. Udaipur and Dungarpur
D. Marwari   4. Jodhpur and Pali
questions.exp: Chokla, of the Shekhawati tract, yields the finest wool among Indian sheep breeds; Magra wool is lustrous and prized for carpets. Rajasthan is India's largest wool producer.

questions.q: The Jakhrana breed of goat, noted for its milk yield, belongs to which district of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Jakhrana is a village in Alwar district. The Sirohi breed is valued mainly for meat, and Marwari and Barbari are the other important goat breeds of the state.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the camel in Rajasthan:
I. The camel was declared the state animal (domestic) of Rajasthan in 2014.
II. The chinkara is the state animal (wild) of Rajasthan.
III. Rajasthan has the largest camel population among Indian states.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Rajasthan Camel (Prohibition of Slaughter and Regulation of Temporary Migration or Export) Act was passed in 2015; Bikaneri, Jaisalmeri, Mewari and Kachchhi are the recognised breeds.

questions.q: The National Research Centre on Camel is located at:
questions.exp: Established at Bikaner in 1984, it works on camel breeding, camel milk and camel-derived products. A camel milk dairy also operates at Bikaner.

questions.q: Which one of the following livestock diseases is NOT caused by a virus?
questions.exp: Brucellosis is a bacterial and zoonotic disease caused by Brucella species. Foot-and-mouth disease, PPR and lumpy skin disease are all viral.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about lumpy skin disease:
I. It is caused by a capripoxvirus.
II. It affects cattle and buffalo and is spread mainly by biting insects.
III. It is a zoonotic disease that spreads to humans through milk.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statement III is wrong: lumpy skin disease does not infect humans. The 2022 outbreak caused heavy cattle mortality in Rajasthan and neighbouring states, and the indigenous Lumpi-ProVacInd vaccine was developed in response.

questions.q: The National Animal Disease Control Programme launched in 2019 targets the control and eradication of:
opts: Bird flu and classical swine fever
questions.exp: The programme provides for 100 per cent central funding of vaccination of cattle, buffalo, sheep, goats and pigs against foot-and-mouth disease and of female calves against brucellosis.

questions.q: Rashtriya Gokul Mission, launched in 2014, is concerned with:
opts: Development and conservation of indigenous bovine breeds
questions.exp: The mission supports Gokul Grams, breed improvement through artificial insemination and embryo transfer, and conservation of registered indigenous breeds such as Rathi, Tharparkar, Gir and Kankrej.

questions.q:
Arrange the following research institutes in the correct chronological order of their establishment:
I. National Research Centre on Camel, Bikaner
II. Central Arid Zone Research Institute, Jodhpur
III. National Research Centre on Seed Spices, Ajmer
IV. Central Sheep and Wool Research Institute, Avikanagar
questions.exp: CAZRI Jodhpur 1959, CSWRI Avikanagar 1962, NRC on Camel Bikaner 1984 and NRC on Seed Spices Ajmer 2000.

questions.q: The Udaipur Solar Observatory, situated on an island in Fateh Sagar Lake, is at present operated by the:
opts: Aryabhatta Research Institute of Observational Sciences
questions.exp: The observatory was founded in 1975 by Dr. Arvind Bhatnagar; the island location gives steady daytime seeing. It hosts the Multi-Application Solar Telescope (MAST).

questions.q: The Central Sheep and Wool Research Institute at Avikanagar is situated in which district of Rajasthan?
questions.exp: Avikanagar lies in Malpura tehsil of Tonk district; the institute was established in 1962 and has developed sheep strains such as Avikalin and Bharat Merino.

questions.q: The Arid Forest Research Institute (AFRI), functioning under the Indian Council of Forestry Research and Education, is located at:
questions.exp: AFRI at Jodhpur was established in 1988 and works on afforestation of arid and semi-arid tracts of Rajasthan, Gujarat and Dadra and Nagar Haveli.

questions.q: The only laboratory of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research located in Rajasthan is the:
opts: Central Salt and Marine Chemicals Research Institute
Central Electronics Engineering Research Institute, Pilani
Central Institute of Mining and Fuel Research
questions.exp: CSIR-CEERI at Pilani was set up in 1953 and works on electronics, semiconductor devices and microwave tubes. CSIR itself was founded in 1942.

questions.q: The Ch. Charan Singh National Institute of Agricultural Marketing (NIAM) is located at:
questions.exp: NIAM at Jaipur, set up in 1988, is an autonomous institute of the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare for training and research in agricultural marketing.

questions.q: Which one of the following research institutes is NOT located in Rajasthan?
opts: Central Institute for Research on Goats
National Research Centre on Seed Spices
questions.exp: The Central Institute for Research on Goats is at Makhdoom in Mathura district, Uttar Pradesh. The other three are at Jodhpur, Ajmer and Jodhpur respectively.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (University)   List-II (Headquarters)
A. Maharana Pratap University of Agriculture and Technology   1. Udaipur
B. Swami Keshwanand Rajasthan Agricultural University   2. Bikaner
C. Sri Karan Narendra Agriculture University   3. Jobner
D. Agriculture University   4. Kota
questions.exp: Rajasthan also has an Agriculture University at Jodhpur and the Rajasthan University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences at Bikaner. The Rajasthan Agricultural Research Institute is at Durgapura, Jaipur.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. The Department of Science and Technology was established in 1971.
II. The Council of Scientific and Industrial Research was founded in 1942.
III. The Science, Technology and Innovation Policy of 2020 is India's fifth national science and technology policy document.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The earlier documents were the Scientific Policy Resolution 1958, the Technology Policy Statement 1983, the Science and Technology Policy 2003 and the Science, Technology and Innovation Policy 2013.

questions.q: National Science Day is observed in India on 28 February to commemorate:
opts: The discovery of the Raman Effect
questions.exp: C.V. Raman announced the discovery of the effect on 28 February 1928; the day has been observed since 1986.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Day)   List-II (Date)
A. National Science Day   1. 28 February
B. National Technology Day   2. 11 May
C. National Space Day   3. 23 August
D. National Mathematics Day   4. 22 December
questions.exp: National Technology Day marks the Pokhran-II tests of 1998, National Space Day the Chandrayaan-3 landing of 23 August 2023, and National Mathematics Day the birth anniversary of Srinivasa Ramanujan.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Anusandhan National Research Foundation:
I. It was established by an Act of Parliament in 2023.
II. The Prime Minister is the ex-officio President of its Governing Board.
III. It replaced the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statement III is wrong: the ANRF subsumed the Science and Engineering Research Board, while CSIR continues to function as before.

questions.q: The Shanti Swarup Bhatnagar Prize for Science and Technology is awarded annually by the:
opts: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
questions.exp: Instituted in 1958 and named after the first Director-General of CSIR, it is given in seven disciplines to scientists below the age of 45.

questions.q: The INSPIRE scheme of the Department of Science and Technology stands for:
opts: Indian Scheme for Promotion of Innovation and Research
Integrated Science Programme for Indian Research
Innovation in Science Pursuit for Inspired Research
questions.exp: Launched in 2008, INSPIRE attracts young talent to science through awards, scholarships and fellowships. Vigyan Jyoti, launched in 2019-20, encourages girls to take up STEM careers.

questions.q: C.V. Raman was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930 for his work on:
questions.exp: He was the first Asian to win a Nobel Prize in the sciences and was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1954.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Scientist)   List-II (Contribution)
A. Meghnad Saha   1. Thermal ionisation equation
B. Satyendra Nath Bose   2. Bose-Einstein statistics
C. Jagadish Chandra Bose   3. Crescograph
D. Homi J. Bhabha   4. Bhabha scattering
questions.exp: Homi Bhabha founded the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research in 1945 and framed India's three-stage nuclear programme.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. C.V. Raman received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1930.
II. Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1983.
III. Har Gobind Khorana received the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1968.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Statement III is wrong: Khorana's Nobel Prize of 1968 was in Physiology or Medicine, for interpreting the genetic code and its role in protein synthesis.

questions.q: The Physical Research Laboratory at Ahmedabad, founded in 1947, was established by:
questions.exp: Vikram Sarabhai, the father of the Indian space programme, also chaired INCOSPAR, set up in 1962, which evolved into ISRO in 1969. The Udaipur Solar Observatory is today a unit of PRL.

questions.q: Venkatraman Ramakrishnan was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 2009 for studies on the structure and function of the:
questions.exp: He shared the prize with Thomas Steitz and Ada Yonath. He was later President of the Royal Society.

questions.q: Operation Flood, which made India the world's largest producer of milk, was led by:
questions.exp: Verghese Kurien, the 'Milkman of India', built the Amul cooperative model at Anand and headed the National Dairy Development Board. Operation Flood began in 1970.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of a colour revolution and its associated product is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: The Blue Revolution relates to fisheries and aquaculture; oilseeds are associated with the Yellow Revolution. M.S. Swaminathan is regarded as the father of the Green Revolution in India.

questions.q: Salim Ali, known as the 'Birdman of India', is closely associated with the ornithological survey of which site in Rajasthan?
questions.exp: His long study of the Bharatpur wetland was central to its protection; he wrote 'The Book of Indian Birds'. The Salim Ali Centre for Ornithology and Natural History is at Coimbatore.

questions.q: Daulat Singh Kothari, born at Udaipur, chaired the Education Commission of 1964-66 and was the first Scientific Adviser to the:
questions.exp: A physicist trained under Rutherford, Kothari later headed the University Grants Commission; the Kothari Commission's report shaped the National Policy on Education of 1968.

chapters.title: Statement & Assumptions / Arguments / Conclusions / Courses of Action
factsheet: ASSUMPTION = something the speaker/writer has TAKEN FOR GRANTED while making the statement. It is unstated but necessary for the statement to make sense.
An assumption is never something merely desirable, merely possible, or a future effect of the statement - those are conclusions or hopes, not assumptions.
Reject any assumption containing an extreme word - only, all, never, always, none, every, cannot - unless the statement itself is that extreme.
An assumption restating the statement itself is NOT implicit (no new taken-for-granted idea is added).
In advertisements, the implicit assumptions are: (i) the product has the advertised quality, (ii) people want that quality, (iii) the ad will influence buyers.
In notices/instructions/appeals, it is implicit that (i) the reader can read and understand it and (ii) people are likely to comply.
In 'In spite of X, Y happened', it is implicit that X normally prevents Y.
ARGUMENT test = RELEVANCE + SIGNIFICANCE. A strong argument must be directly related to the question AND deal with a major, not a trivial, aspect of it.

Weak-argument markers: appeal to tradition, mere imitation of other countries, personal ridicule, ambiguity, sweeping generalisation, circular restatement of the proposal, and 'it will not solve the problem completely'.
An argument saying 'a measure is useless because it does not remove the whole problem' is WEAK - a partial remedy can still be justified.
'Yes/No' does not decide strength: a No-argument that gives a real, weighty objection is strong; a Yes-argument that gives a trivial gain is weak.
An argument based on an established fact or on a serious, foreseeable consequence is strong; one based on an unverifiable prediction or on emotion is weak.
CONCLUSION = what MUST be true given the statement. Test: could the statement be true and the conclusion false? If yes, it does not follow.
Percentages never give absolute numbers. A higher percentage in A than in B does NOT prove A has more persons than B (populations may differ).
'All P are Q' is NOT convertible to 'All Q are P', and does not mean 'only P are Q' - so nothing follows about a non-P.
'Some A are B' always yields 'Some B are A'. 'No A is B' always yields 'No B is A'. 'All A are B' yields only 'Some B are A'.
EITHER I OR II follows when neither follows singly, but the two conclusions are contradictory/complementary and together exhaust all possibilities.
NEITHER follows when both conclusions add outside information (causes, motives, comparisons, future behaviour) that the statement does not supply.
COURSE OF ACTION test: it must (i) address the problem stated, (ii) be practicable and within the authority of the agency, and (iii) be proportionate.
Reject a course of action that is extreme (ban everything, close it down, dismiss everybody), that punishes the victim, or that is a mere platitude ('people should be careful').
Both courses follow when one is an immediate remedy and the other is a preventive/long-term measure aimed at the same problem.
In a course-of-action item, the statement's problem must actually exist - do not choose an action that assumes a different problem.
'Should be investigated / responsibility should be fixed / relief should be given / awareness should be created through media' are the usual strong actions.
Do not import real-world knowledge into assumption and conclusion items - work only from the words given.
Standard option order used by RPSC/SSC: I only, II only, Either or Neither, Both - read the option list before keying, since papers reshuffle it.
Statement-Assumption, Statement-Argument, Statement-Conclusion and Statement-Course of Action have each appeared in every RAS Prelims paper - about 4-6 marks together.
Time discipline: these items need no calculation; 30-40 seconds each is enough. Read the statement twice, the options once.

questions.q:
Statement: The government has decided to increase the price of urea with effect from next month.
Assumptions:
I. The government has the authority to fix the price of urea.
II. Farmers will stop using urea from next month.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.exp: I is implicit: a body can announce a price rise only if it takes for granted that it may fix that price. II is a possible future effect, and an extreme one ('will stop'); an effect of the decision is never an assumption behind it. Hence only I.

questions.q:
Statement: 'Use Ujala detergent for whiter clothes.' - an advertisement.
Assumptions:
I. People want their clothes to look whiter.
II. Ujala is the only detergent available in the market.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.exp: Every advertisement takes for granted that the advertised quality is wanted by buyers, so I is implicit. II contains the extreme word 'only' and is not needed for the advertisement to make sense. Only I.

questions.q:
Statement: 'In case of any difficulty regarding this scheme, please contact our toll-free helpline.' - instruction printed on a scheme pamphlet.
Assumptions:
I. Some beneficiaries may face difficulty in understanding the scheme.
II. The helpline is able to resolve the difficulties of beneficiaries.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.exp: 'In case of any difficulty' presupposes that difficulty is possible - I is implicit. Directing people to a helpline is pointless unless it can help, so II is also taken for granted. Both are implicit.

questions.q:
Statement: 'All employees must reach the office by 9.30 a.m., failing which their casual leave will be deducted.' - office notice.
Assumptions:
I. Some employees are likely to come late unless a penalty is prescribed.
II. Deduction of casual leave is likely to deter late-coming.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.exp: A penalty clause is framed only because late-coming is expected (I) and because the penalty is believed to work as a deterrent (II). Both assumptions are necessary for the notice to make sense.

questions.q:
Statement: Ravi says to Sunil, 'You should read the editorial page of the newspaper daily.'
Assumptions:
I. Sunil does not read any newspaper.
II. The editorial page carries material worth reading every day.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.exp: Advising Sunil to read the editorial page does not presuppose that he reads no newspaper - he may read it but skip the editorials, so I is not implicit. The advice is meaningless unless the editorial page is worth daily reading, so II is implicit.

questions.q:
Statement: To improve its board results, the school has decided to hold extra classes for weak students on Sundays.
Assumptions:
I. Weak students are likely to attend the classes held on Sundays.
II. Additional teaching can improve the performance of weak students.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.exp: The decision is worth taking only if the students will turn up (I) and only if extra teaching can raise performance (II). Both are taken for granted by the school.

questions.q:
Statement: 'Buy from our winter collection now - 40% discount till 31 December.' - a shop's notice.
Assumptions:
I. A discount is likely to attract customers.
II. Customers normally postpone their purchases to the last day.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.exp: Offering a discount presupposes that discounts attract buyers - I is implicit. Nothing in the notice takes last-day buying for granted; a deadline is set precisely to prevent delay. Only I.

questions.q:
Statement: The municipal corporation has advised citizens to boil drinking water during the monsoon months.
Assumptions:
I. Drinking water is liable to get contaminated during the monsoon.
II. Boiling destroys the harmful germs present in water.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.exp: The advisory is issued because contamination is expected in the monsoon (I) and because boiling is believed to make the water safe (II). Both are unstated but necessary.

questions.q:
Statement: The Chief Minister will inaugurate the new expressway on Sunday.
Assumptions:
I. The construction of the expressway has been completed.
II. The Chief Minister is fond of travelling by road.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.exp: An inauguration presupposes that the work is finished and the road is fit to be opened, so I is implicit. The Chief Minister's personal preference is irrelevant to the announcement. Only I.

questions.q:
Statement: Anil scored 92 per cent marks in the Class XII board examination.
Assumptions:
I. Anil is the topper of his school.
II. No other student of his school scored above 92 per cent.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.exp: The statement reports one student's marks and takes nothing for granted about other students. I and II are comparisons that the statement neither states nor presupposes, so neither is implicit.

questions.q:
Statement: The company has announced a bonus equal to one month's salary for all its employees this year.
Assumptions:
I. The employees had gone on strike demanding a bonus.
II. The company will not be able to pay a bonus next year.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.exp: Neither the cause of the announcement (a strike) nor its future consequence is taken for granted by the announcement. A past reason that is not required for the statement to make sense, and a future prediction, are both outside the statement.

questions.q:
Statement: In spite of the heavy rainfall yesterday, the cricket match was completed on schedule.
Assumptions:
I. Heavy rainfall never affects the completion of a cricket match.
II. Heavy rainfall usually disrupts the play in a cricket match.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.exp: The construction 'in spite of X, Y happened' takes for granted that X normally prevents Y - so II is implicit. I says 'never', which is contradicted by the very use of 'in spite of'. Only II.

questions.q:
Statement: The invigilator instructed the candidates to reach the examination hall at least thirty minutes before the paper begins.
Assumptions:
I. Candidates always reach the examination hall late.
II. The candidates are likely to follow the instruction.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.exp: 'Always' makes I an extreme claim that the instruction does not presuppose. Any instruction is issued in the expectation of compliance, so II is implicit. Only II.

questions.q:
Statement: Meena told her colleague, 'I could not attend yesterday's meeting as I was unwell.'
Assumptions:
I. Meena remains unwell very often.
II. Meena was expected to attend yesterday's meeting.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.exp: Explaining one absence does not presuppose that one is unwell frequently, so I is not implicit. Offering an explanation for absence takes for granted that one's presence was expected - II is implicit. Only II.

questions.q:
Statement: The state government has decided to make the wearing of helmets compulsory for pillion riders on two-wheelers.
Assumptions:
I. Helmets reduce the risk of head injury to pillion riders.
II. The rule can be enforced by the traffic police.
Which of the assumptions is/are implicit in the statement?
opts: Neither I nor II is implicit
Both I and II are implicit
questions.exp: A safety rule is made only if the device is believed to protect (I) and only if the rule is believed to be enforceable (II). Both are taken for granted by the decision.

questions.q:
Statement: Should private cars be barred from the central business district of big cities during peak hours?
Arguments:
I. Yes, it would substantially reduce traffic congestion and air pollution in the most crowded part of the city.
II. No, car owners have spent a lot of money on buying their vehicles.
Which of the arguments is/are strong?
opts: Neither I nor II is strong
Both I and II are strong
questions.exp: I is relevant to the purpose of the proposal and deals with a major public gain - it is strong. II appeals to the private expenditure of owners, which does not weigh against a serious public problem - a weak argument. Only I.

questions.q:
Statement: Should education up to Class XII be made completely free in all government schools?
Arguments:
I. Yes, it would enable children of poor families to complete their schooling.
II. No, things that are given free are never valued by people.
Which of the arguments is/are strong?
opts: Neither I nor II is strong
Both I and II are strong
questions.exp: I addresses the central aim of the proposal with a significant benefit - strong. II is a sweeping generalisation ('never valued'), unsupported and irrelevant to school education - weak. Only I.

questions.q:
Statement: Should the minimum age for obtaining a driving licence for a motor car be raised to 20 years?
Arguments:
I. Yes, young people are always careless.
II. No, many people need to drive for work or study soon after school; road safety is better secured by strict testing and enforcement than by raising the age.
Which of the arguments is/are strong?
opts: Neither I nor II is strong
Both I and II are strong
questions.exp: I is a sweeping generalisation about all young people - weak. II gives a real cost of the proposal and points to a better-targeted remedy, which is both relevant and significant - strong. Only II.

questions.q:
Statement: Should coaching institutes preparing students for competitive examinations be banned in the country?
Arguments:
I. Yes, all successful candidates are products of coaching institutes.
II. No, a ban would only push coaching underground and deprive small-town students of guidance; the real need is to regulate fees, hours and advertising.
Which of the arguments is/are strong?
opts: Neither I nor II is strong
Both I and II are strong
questions.exp: I states an unverified generalisation and, even if true, does not support a ban - weak. II identifies a foreseeable perverse effect and offers a proportionate alternative - strong. Only II.

questions.q:
Statement: Should there be a complete ban on the manufacture and sale of firecrackers in India?
Arguments:
I. Yes, firecrackers cause severe air and noise pollution and a large number of burn injuries every year.
II. No, lakhs of workers depend on the firecracker industry for their livelihood, and regulated green crackers can cut pollution substantially.
Which of the arguments is/are strong?
opts: Neither I nor II is strong
Both I and II are strong
questions.exp: I cites major, documented harms; II cites a major livelihood cost and a workable middle path. Both are relevant to the question and deal with weighty aspects, so both are strong.

questions.q:
Statement: Should the age of superannuation of government employees be raised from 60 to 62 years?
Arguments:
I. Yes, experienced employees would remain available for two more years and pension liability would be deferred.
II. No, it would postpone fresh recruitment and reduce job opportunities for unemployed youth.
Which of the arguments is/are strong?
opts: Neither I nor II is strong
Both I and II are strong
questions.exp: Both arguments address the substantive consequences of the proposal - retention of experience and deferred pension outgo on one side, blocked recruitment on the other. Both are strong.

questions.q:
Statement: Should the study of Sanskrit be made compulsory in all schools of the country?
Arguments:
I. Yes, Sanskrit is the oldest language of the world.
II. No, students of today are not interested in old languages.
Which of the arguments is/are strong?
opts: Neither I nor II is strong
Both I and II are strong
questions.exp: I rests on a contested claim and, in any case, antiquity by itself is no ground for compulsion - weak. II is a sweeping assertion about students' interest, not a reasoned objection - weak. Neither is strong.

questions.q:
Statement: Should the examination system in schools be abolished altogether?
Arguments:
I. Yes, several other countries follow a different system.
II. No, examinations have been a part of our education system since ancient times.
Which of the arguments is/are strong?
opts: Neither I nor II is strong
Both I and II are strong
questions.exp: I is mere imitation - it does not say why the other system is better for us. II is an appeal to tradition. Both fail the relevance-and-significance test, so neither is strong.

questions.q:
Statement: Should all beggars found in big cities be sent back to their native villages?
Arguments:
I. Yes, this will reduce the population of big cities.
II. No, they will come back to the cities again.
Which of the arguments is/are strong?
opts: Neither I nor II is strong
Both I and II are strong
questions.exp: I offers a negligible effect on city population - trivial, hence weak. II is a defeatist remark that neither examines the causes of begging nor the merits of rehabilitation - weak. Neither is strong.

questions.q:
Statement: Should the subsidy on domestic LPG cylinders be withdrawn for high-income households?
Arguments:
I. Yes, targeting the subsidy at poor households releases scarce public resources for essential welfare expenditure.
II. No, the government should never interfere with the market.
Which of the arguments is/are strong?
opts: Neither I nor II is strong
Both I and II are strong
questions.exp: I gives a concrete fiscal and equity gain that goes to the heart of the proposal - strong. II is a slogan; besides, a subsidy is itself an intervention, so the argument is self-defeating - weak. Only I.

questions.q:
Statement: Should mobile phones be prohibited inside examination halls?
Arguments:
I. Yes, a mobile phone can be used to receive answers and thus destroys the fairness of the examination.
II. No, prohibiting mobile phones will not put an end to every form of cheating.
Which of the arguments is/are strong?
opts: Neither I nor II is strong
Both I and II are strong
questions.exp: I identifies a direct threat to the integrity of the examination - strong. II is the classic weak form: a measure is not useless merely because it does not remove the whole problem. Only I.

questions.q:
Statement: Should all the major rivers of India be interlinked through canals?
Arguments:
I. Yes, it will solve the water problem of the country forever.
II. No, large-scale interlinking would submerge forests and displace people, and its ecological consequences have not been fully assessed.
Which of the arguments is/are strong?
opts: Neither I nor II is strong
Both I and II are strong
questions.exp: I overstates the case with 'forever' and gives no evidence - weak. II points to serious, foreseeable ecological and human costs of the very proposal under discussion - strong. Only II.

questions.q:
Statement: Should all public recruitment examinations in the country be conducted only in the online mode?
Arguments:
I. Yes, online examinations are the fashion of the day.
II. No, a large number of rural candidates lack reliable internet connectivity and devices, and would effectively be excluded.
Which of the arguments is/are strong?
opts: Neither I nor II is strong
Both I and II are strong
questions.exp: I appeals to fashion, not to any advantage of the mode - weak. II shows that the proposal would exclude a large class of eligible candidates, a decisive objection - strong. Only II.

questions.q:
Statement: Should agricultural income above a high threshold be brought within the ambit of income tax?
Arguments:
I. Yes, it would check the routing of non-farm income through the agricultural exemption and would widen the tax base.
II. No, the income of the vast majority of farmers is low and uncertain, and the cost of assessing farm income may exceed the revenue collected.
Which of the arguments is/are strong?
opts: Neither I nor II is strong
Both I and II are strong
questions.exp: I addresses a real avenue of tax evasion; II addresses feasibility and the administrative cost-benefit of the measure. Both are relevant and weighty, hence both strong.

questions.q:
Statement: Should the use of plastic carry bags be completely banned in the state?
Arguments:
I. Yes, plastic bags choke drains, are swallowed by stray cattle and take centuries to decompose.
II. No, unless affordable alternatives are made widely available, the ban will mainly burden small shopkeepers and poor consumers.
Which of the arguments is/are strong?
opts: Neither I nor II is strong
Both I and II are strong
questions.exp: I states established environmental harm; II states a serious implementation difficulty that decides whether the ban will work. Both are strong.

questions.q:
Statement: The literacy rate of District A is 78 per cent, while that of District B is 62 per cent.
Conclusions:
I. District A has a larger number of literate persons than District B.
II. Some persons in District B are illiterate.
Which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statement?
questions.exp: A rate is not a number: if District B has a far larger population, 62 per cent of it can exceed 78 per cent of District A, so I does not follow. Since B's literacy is 62 per cent, the remaining 38 per cent are illiterate, so II must be true. Only II follows.

questions.q:
Statement: All trains running between Jaipur and Delhi were cancelled today because of dense fog.
Conclusions:
I. No train left Jaipur for Delhi today.
II. Dense fog can disrupt railway operations.
Which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statement?
questions.exp: 'All trains were cancelled' entails that none ran, so I follows. The statement itself gives fog as the cause of the cancellation, which establishes that fog can disrupt operations, so II follows. Both follow.

questions.q:
Statement: Every student who scored above 90 marks was awarded a scholarship. Ramesh scored 85 marks.
Conclusions:
I. Ramesh scored less than 90 marks.
II. Ramesh was not awarded a scholarship.
Which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statement?
questions.exp: 85 < 90, so I follows. The statement makes scoring above 90 SUFFICIENT for a scholarship, not necessary - scholarships may also have been given on other grounds, so II does not follow. Only I.

questions.q:
Statement: The price of petrol has been raised for the fourth time in this calendar year.
Conclusions:
I. The price of petrol has been raised more than once this year.
II. People will shift from private vehicles to public transport.
Which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statement?
questions.exp: 'Fourth time' entails 'more than once', so I follows. II is a prediction about people's behaviour for which the statement supplies no evidence. Only I.

questions.q:
Statement: Of the 500 employees of a company, 300 are graduates, and 150 of these graduates are women.
Conclusions:
I. Most of the women employees of the company are graduates.
II. At least 150 employees of the company are women.
Which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statement?
questions.exp: The total number of women in the company is not given, so we cannot say what proportion of women are graduates - I does not follow. But 150 women graduates are themselves employees, so the company has at least 150 women. Only II.

questions.q:
Statement: The Food Safety Commissioner has warned that anyone found selling adulterated milk will be prosecuted.
Conclusions:
I. Nobody will now sell adulterated milk.
II. Selling adulterated milk is punishable under the law.
Which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statement?
questions.exp: A warning does not guarantee universal compliance, so I does not follow. A threat of prosecution presupposes and therefore establishes that the act is an offence, so II follows. Only II.

questions.q:
Statement: A large number of tourists visited Rajasthan during the winter months this year.
Conclusions:
I. Tourists do not visit Rajasthan during the summer.
II. Rajasthan is the most visited state in India.
Which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statement?
questions.exp: The statement reports winter arrivals only; it says nothing about summer (I) and makes no comparison with other states (II). Both conclusions add information not contained in the statement, so neither follows.

questions.q:
Statement: The sale of electric two-wheelers in the state doubled last year.
Conclusions:
I. Electric two-wheelers are cheaper than petrol two-wheelers.
II. The sale of petrol two-wheelers fell last year.
Which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statement?
questions.exp: A rise in sales tells us nothing about relative prices (I), and the market may have expanded so that petrol vehicle sales also rose (II). Neither conclusion follows.

questions.q:
Statement: In a class test the highest marks were obtained by exactly one student, and it is known that this student is either Anil or Bharat.
Conclusions:
I. Anil obtained the highest marks.
II. Bharat obtained the highest marks.
Which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statement?
questions.exp: Neither conclusion can be established on its own, but the statement guarantees that exactly one of the two is true and that no third possibility exists. When two conclusions are complementary and jointly exhaustive, the answer is 'Either I or II follows'.

questions.q:
Statement: The school will remain closed on Monday and Tuesday on account of the festival.
Conclusions:
I. The school will not function on Monday.
II. The school observes holidays on the occasion of festivals.
Which of the conclusions logically follows/follow from the statement?
questions.exp: Closure on Monday is stated, so I follows. The statement gives the festival as the reason for the closure, which shows the school does close for festivals, so II follows. Both follow.

questions.q: In a survey of 200 households it was found that 120 own a two-wheeler, 60 own a car and 20 own both. Which one of the following conclusions is definitely correct?
opts: 40 households own neither a two-wheeler nor a car
30 households own both a two-wheeler and a car
questions.exp: Households owning at least one vehicle = 120 + 60 - 20 = 160. Hence 200 - 160 = 40 own neither. (Only-two-wheeler = 120 - 20 = 100, only-car = 60 - 20 = 40, both = 20, so the other three options are wrong.)

questions.q:
Statement: Every member of the drama club is also a member of the music club. Some members of the music club are members of the debating club.
Which one of the following conclusions definitely follows?
opts: Some members of the drama club are members of the debating club
All members of the music club are members of the drama club
Some members of the music club are members of the drama club
No member of the drama club is a member of the debating club
questions.exp: Drama club is contained in the music club and is non-empty, so some music-club members are drama-club members - that is certain. The debating-club overlap may lie entirely outside the drama club, so neither an overlap nor its absence can be asserted.

questions.q:
Statement: The morning bus reaches Jaipur on time only if it leaves Jodhpur before 6 a.m. Today the morning bus reached Jaipur on time.
Which one of the following conclusions definitely follows?
opts: The bus left Jodhpur before 6 a.m. today
The bus left Jodhpur after 6 a.m. today
The bus leaves Jodhpur before 6 a.m. every day
Every bus that leaves Jodhpur before 6 a.m. reaches Jaipur on time
questions.exp: 'P only if Q' means P implies Q. Here P = reaches on time, Q = left before 6 a.m. Since P is true today, Q must be true today. The converse (option 4) and the generalisation (option 3) do not follow.

questions.q:
Statement: If it rains, the match will be cancelled. The match was not cancelled.
Which one of the following conclusions definitely follows?
opts: The match was played in the rain
Nothing can be said about the rain
questions.exp: This is modus tollens: from 'Rain implies cancellation' and 'not cancelled', we get 'not rain'. If it had rained, the match would necessarily have been cancelled.

questions.q:
Statement: Only those candidates who have passed the written test are called for the interview. Mohit has been called for the interview.
Which one of the following conclusions definitely follows?
opts: Mohit will be selected for the post
Mohit obtained the highest marks in the written test
Every candidate who passed the written test has been called for the interview
Mohit has passed the written test
questions.exp: 'Only those who passed are called' makes passing a necessary condition for being called. Mohit was called, so he must have passed. It does not follow that all who passed were called, nor anything about his rank or final selection.

questions.q:
Statement: Several passengers were injured when an overcrowded bus overturned on a state highway.
Courses of action:
I. The transport authority should immediately check overloading of buses on this route.
II. All bus services on this route should be stopped permanently.
Which of the courses of action logically follows/follow?
questions.exp: I attacks the stated cause (overcrowding) and is within the authority's power - it follows. II is disproportionate and would deprive commuters of transport instead of correcting the fault. Only I.

questions.q:
Statement: A large number of students of a school failed in mathematics in the annual examination.
Courses of action:
I. The school should hold remedial classes in mathematics and review its method of teaching the subject.
II. The school should expel all the students who failed.
Which of the courses of action logically follows/follow?
questions.exp: I addresses the problem at its source and is practicable. II punishes the victims of poor results and does not remedy the teaching problem. Only I.

questions.q:
Statement: The number of dengue cases reported in the city has risen sharply in the last two weeks.
Courses of action:
I. The municipal body should carry out fogging and remove stagnant water in the affected localities.
II. The health department should advise residents through the media to use mosquito nets and to report fever early.
Which of the courses of action logically follows/follow?
questions.exp: I is the direct vector-control measure and II is the accompanying awareness measure; both are practicable and both attack the same problem. Both follow.

questions.q:
Statement: In several villages of a district the drinking water has been found to contain fluoride above the permissible limit.
Courses of action:
I. Defluoridation units should be installed and alternative safe sources of drinking water arranged in the affected villages.
II. The health department should screen the residents for fluorosis and treat those affected.
Which of the courses of action logically follows/follow?
questions.exp: I removes the cause and II deals with the damage already done; both are within the competence of the state agencies. Both follow.

questions.q:
Statement: A newly constructed flyover developed wide cracks within six months of being opened to traffic.
Courses of action:
I. The flyover should be demolished immediately.
II. A technical inspection should be ordered and responsibility for the substandard work fixed.
Which of the courses of action logically follows/follow?
questions.exp: Demolition before any technical assessment is premature and extreme. An inspection followed by fixing of responsibility is the standard, proportionate response. Only II.

questions.q:
Statement: Some candidates were found using unfair means during a state recruitment examination.
Courses of action:
I. The system of holding recruitment examinations should be abolished.
II. The candidates found guilty should be debarred and proceeded against under the law relating to unfair means in recruitment examinations.
Which of the courses of action logically follows/follow?
questions.exp: Abolishing recruitment examinations because a few candidates cheated is an extreme reaction that destroys the system instead of protecting it. Debarring the guilty and prosecuting them under the applicable law is the proper action. Only II.

questions.q:
Statement: The air quality index of the city has remained in the 'very poor' category for the whole of last week.
Courses of action:
I. All the residents of the city should be advised to leave the city till the air improves.
II. The state pollution control board should enforce restrictions on construction dust and on the open burning of waste in the city.
Which of the courses of action logically follows/follow?
questions.exp: Asking a whole city to move out is impracticable. Enforcing dust and waste-burning restrictions attacks identified sources of the pollution and lies within the board's powers. Only II.

questions.q:
Statement: A private school has been charging fees far in excess of the limit prescribed under the state fee-regulation law.
Courses of action:
I. Parents should stop sending their children to that school.
II. The education department should hold an inquiry and take action against the school under the Act.
Which of the courses of action logically follows/follow?
questions.exp: Withdrawing children penalises the students, not the school, and is not a remedy for an illegality. Enforcement of the law by the competent department is the appropriate action. Only II.

questions.q:
Statement: Farmers of the district have suffered heavy crop losses because of unseasonal hailstorms.
Courses of action:
I. The administration should order a special crop-loss survey (girdawari) and disburse relief to the affected farmers.
II. The cultivation of the affected crops should be banned in the district.
Which of the courses of action logically follows/follow?
questions.exp: A survey followed by relief is the established and practicable response to a natural calamity. Banning the crop punishes farmers for a weather event they did not cause. Only I.

questions.q:
Statement: Very long queues are seen every morning at the registration counter of the district hospital.
Courses of action:
I. The hospital should introduce token or online appointments and open additional counters during peak hours.
II. The hospital should reduce the number of patients it registers each day.
Which of the courses of action logically follows/follow?
questions.exp: I increases the capacity to serve and removes the bottleneck. II denies treatment to patients, which defeats the purpose of the hospital. Only I.

questions.q:
Statement: The number of road accidents caused by drunken driving has increased sharply in the state.
Courses of action:
I. The sale of motor vehicles in the state should be banned.
II. All persons who consume liquor should be arrested.
Which of the courses of action logically follows/follow?
questions.exp: Neither action is aimed at the stated problem. Banning vehicle sales does not stop drunken driving by existing drivers, and arresting everyone who drinks is neither lawful nor practicable. Neither follows. (Breath-analyser checking and licence suspension would.)

questions.q:
Statement: The board examination results of a government school have been poor for three consecutive years.
Courses of action:
I. The school should be closed down.
II. The students of the school should be asked to appear as private candidates.
Which of the courses of action logically follows/follow?
questions.exp: Closing the school deprives the locality of education instead of improving it; making the children private candidates removes teaching altogether. Neither addresses the cause of poor results, so neither follows.

questions.q:
Statement: A number of complaints have been received about the poor quality of mid-day meals served in some schools of the district.
Courses of action:
I. The mid-day meal scheme should be discontinued in the district.
II. The parents who complained should be warned against spreading rumours.
Which of the courses of action logically follows/follow?
questions.exp: Discontinuing the scheme punishes the children it is meant to feed, and silencing complainants suppresses the information needed to fix the problem. Neither follows; inspection of kitchens and action against defaulting suppliers would.

questions.q:
Statement: Several old buildings in the walled city have been found to be in a dangerously dilapidated condition.
Courses of action:
I. The municipal corporation should get the buildings surveyed and issue notices to vacate those declared unsafe.
II. Arrangements should be made for the temporary rehabilitation of the families required to vacate.
Which of the courses of action logically follows/follow?
questions.exp: I removes the danger to life through the competent authority; II takes care of the consequence of I for the displaced families. Both are practicable and both follow.

questions.q:
Statement: A large number of young people in the state remain unemployed even after completing graduation.
Courses of action:
I. Skill-development and employability training should be integrated with degree courses.
II. Industry-institute linkages and campus placement arrangements should be strengthened.
Which of the courses of action logically follows/follow?
questions.exp: Both actions address the stated mismatch between degrees and employability - one on the supply side of skills, the other on the demand-linkage side. Both follow.

chapters.title: Analytical and Critical Reasoning; Syllogism
factsheet: Four standard propositions: A = All A are B (universal affirmative), E = No A is B (universal negative), I = Some A are B (particular affirmative), O = Some A are not B (particular negative).
Valid conversions: 'Some A are B' gives 'Some B are A'; 'No A is B' gives 'No B is A'; 'All A are B' gives only 'Some B are A' (never 'All B are A').
'Some A are not B' has NO valid conversion - 'Some B are not A' does not follow from it.
Two particular premises (Some + Some) give no definite conclusion. Two negative premises give no definite conclusion.
If one premise is particular, the conclusion must be particular; if one premise is negative, the conclusion must be negative.
The middle term (the term common to both statements) must be distributed at least once, and must not appear in the conclusion.
All + All = All (A + A = A); All + No = No (A + E = E); Some + All = Some (I + A = I); Some + No = Some-not (I + E = O).
No + All in that order (E + A) gives 'Some ... are not ...' after conversion; check the direction of the terms carefully before keying.

EITHER-OR case: when neither conclusion follows separately but the two are contradictory (All-Some not; Some-No; A pair covering every possibility) and share the same subject and predicate, the answer is 'Either I or II follows'.
POSSIBILITY conclusions ('All A being B is a possibility') follow whenever at least one consistent Venn diagram allows it; they fail only when the statements definitely forbid it.
A definite conclusion and its possibility-negation cannot both hold: if 'No A is B' definitely follows, 'Some A being B is a possibility' is false.
Existential convention followed in Indian competitive exams: every class named in a statement is taken to be non-empty, so 'All A are B' yields 'Some B are A'.
In cause-and-effect items, the earlier and independently occurring event is the cause; if both events are consequences of a third, unmentioned event, the answer is 'effects of a common cause'.
Two events that are merely simultaneous, or belong to unrelated spheres (world gold price and local vegetable price), are effects of independent causes, not cause and effect.

FACT = something already known/observed or verifiable from published data. INFERENCE = a conclusion drawn from given facts. JUDGEMENT = an opinion, approval, disapproval or recommendation ('should', 'better', 'ought').
Words like 'must have', 'therefore', 'is likely to' signal an inference; 'should', 'must be made', 'better than' signal a judgement.

In critical reasoning, an argument = premises + conclusion. To WEAKEN, supply an alternative explanation for the evidence; to STRENGTHEN, rule out alternative explanations (a controlled or randomised comparison is the strongest support).
Correlation is not causation: if a third factor accompanies both the supposed cause and the effect, the causal claim collapses.
Common flaws: affirming the consequent, confusing a necessary condition with a sufficient one, hasty generalisation from a small or self-selected sample, and appeal to authority or tradition.
In 'A only if B', B is necessary for A - so A implies B, never B implies A.
Modus ponens: If P then Q; P is true, therefore Q. Modus tollens: If P then Q; Q is false, therefore P is false. 'Q is true therefore P' and 'P is false therefore not Q' are both fallacies.
Two-set formula: n(A or B) = n(A) + n(B) - n(both); neither = Total - n(A or B); exactly one = n(A) + n(B) - 2 x n(both).

Logical Venn representation: fully included classes (Rajasthan-India-Asia) = concentric circles; mutually exclusive classes inside a wider class (Aunt-Uncle-Relative) = two separate circles inside a bigger one; partly overlapping classes = intersecting circles.
In ordering puzzles, convert every clue into a single chain with '>' before answering; count positions only after the whole chain is fixed.
In truth-teller puzzles, test each possibility one by one against every statement and keep the case that satisfies the given count of true statements.
In input-output items, identify what moves at each step (largest/smallest number, alphabetically first/last word) and to which end it moves; the untouched elements keep their relative order.
Syllogism and logical Venn diagram items have appeared in RAS Prelims 2021, 2023 and 2024 - always draw the diagram, never rely on the 'sound' of the sentence.

questions.q:
Statements:
All pens are books.
All books are papers.
Conclusions:
I. All pens are papers.
II. Some papers are pens.
Which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements? (Take the statements to be true even if they seem at variance with commonly known facts.)
questions.exp: Pens lie inside books, and books lie inside papers, so pens lie inside papers - I follows. Since the pen circle is non-empty and lies within the paper circle, some papers are pens - II follows (A + A = A, and 'All A are B' converts to 'Some B are A'). Both follow.

questions.q:
Statements:
Some cats are dogs.
All dogs are animals.
Conclusions:
I. Some cats are animals.
II. All animals are cats.
Which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements? (Take the statements to be true even if they seem at variance with commonly known facts.)
questions.exp: The cats that are dogs must be animals, since all dogs are animals - so I follows (I + A = I). II reverses a universal without warrant; the animal class may contain many non-cats. Only I.

questions.q:
Statements:
All flowers are roses.
No rose is a leaf.
Conclusions:
I. No flower is a leaf.
II. Some leaves are flowers.
Which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements? (Take the statements to be true even if they seem at variance with commonly known facts.)
questions.exp: Flowers lie inside roses and the rose circle is wholly separate from the leaf circle, so no flower can be a leaf - I follows (A + E = E). II directly contradicts I and therefore cannot follow. Only I.

questions.q:
Statements:
Some books are pens.
No pen is a pencil.
Conclusions:
I. No book is a pencil.
II. Some books are not pencils.
Which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements? (Take the statements to be true even if they seem at variance with commonly known facts.)
questions.exp: The books that are pens cannot be pencils, so at least some books are not pencils - II follows (I + E = O). But books that are not pens may well be pencils, so the universal negative in I does not follow. Only II.

questions.q:
Statements:
All singers are dancers.
Some dancers are poets.
Conclusions:
I. Some singers are poets.
II. Some poets are dancers.
Which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements? (Take the statements to be true even if they seem at variance with commonly known facts.)
questions.exp: The dancers who are poets need not be singers, so I does not follow (the middle term 'dancers' is undistributed). II is only the conversion of 'Some dancers are poets', which is always valid. Only II.

questions.q:
Statements:
Some pens are books.
All books are copies.
Conclusions:
I. All pens are copies.
II. Some pens are not copies.
Which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements? (Take the statements to be true even if they seem at variance with commonly known facts.)
questions.exp: From the statements only 'Some pens are copies' is certain; the remaining pens may or may not be copies. So neither I nor II follows separately. But I and II are contradictories that between them cover every possibility, so 'Either I or II follows'.

questions.q:
Statements:
All cups are plates.
Some plates are spoons.
Conclusions:
I. Some cups are spoons.
II. No cup is a spoon.
Which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements? (Take the statements to be true even if they seem at variance with commonly known facts.)
questions.exp: The spoons among the plates may lie inside the cup circle or entirely outside it, so neither conclusion is certain. As the two conclusions are contradictory and exhaust all possibilities, either I or II must be true - the 'Either or' case.

questions.q:
Statements:
Some mangoes are apples.
Some apples are grapes.
Conclusions:
I. Some mangoes are grapes.
II. All apples are mangoes.
Which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements? (Take the statements to be true even if they seem at variance with commonly known facts.)
questions.exp: Two particular (Some + Some) statements never yield a definite conclusion: the mango-apple overlap and the apple-grape overlap may be different parts of the apple circle, so I is not certain. II is a universal that goes far beyond 'some'. Neither follows.

questions.q:
Statements:
All doctors are engineers.
No engineer is a teacher.
Conclusions:
I. Some doctors are teachers.
II. Some teachers are engineers.
Which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements? (Take the statements to be true even if they seem at variance with commonly known facts.)
questions.exp: Doctors lie inside engineers, and engineers are wholly outside teachers; hence no doctor can be a teacher, which refutes I. 'No engineer is a teacher' converts to 'No teacher is an engineer', which refutes II. Neither follows.

questions.q:
Statements:
No student is lazy.
All lazy persons are sleepy.
Conclusions:
I. Some sleepy persons are not students.
II. Some sleepy persons are lazy.
Which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements? (Take the statements to be true even if they seem at variance with commonly known facts.)
