chapters.title: National Affairs: Polity, Governance and Schemes
factsheet: NOTE: This chapter was compiled in September 2026 and should be refreshed in November 2026 for the final weeks before the exam.

Key office-holders (as of Sept 2026): President — Droupadi Murmu; Vice-President — C.P. Radhakrishnan; Chief Justice of India — Justice SURYA KANT (53rd CJI); Chief Election Commissioner — Gyanesh Kumar.

More office-holders: CAG — K. Sanjay Murthy; Attorney General — R. Venkataramani; Solicitor General — Tushar Mehta; RBI Governor — Sanjay Malhotra; Cabinet Secretary — T.V. Somanathan; NSA — Ajit Doval; Chief Economic Adviser — V. Anantha Nageswaran.

Also: Lok Sabha Speaker — Om Birla; UPSC Chairman — Ajay Kumar; SEBI Chairman — Tuhin Kanta Pandey; ISRO Chairman — Dr V. Narayanan; NHRC Chairperson — Justice V. Ramasubramanian; RBI Deputy Governors include Poonam Gupta and Shirish Chandra Murmu (appointed Sept 2025, succeeding M. Rajeshwar Rao).
WINTER SESSION 2025 (1-19 Dec 2025; 15 sittings): 9 Bills introduced, 7 passed, 2 referred to committees.
Nuclear Energy Bill, 2025 — replaced the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and permits private-sector participation in nuclear power generation and fuel handling.
The law replacing MGNREGA (VB-G RAM G) raised guaranteed rural employment from 100 to 125 days and changed centre-state funding to 60:40.

Insurance Laws (Amendment), 2025 — FDI in insurance raised to 100%; net-owned-fund requirement for foreign re-insurers cut from Rs 5,000 crore to Rs 1,000 crore. Repealing and Amending Act, 2025 repealed 71 obsolete laws.

Referred to committees in Dec 2025: Securities Markets Code, 2025 (consolidates SEBI Act, Depositories Act and Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act) and Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025 (single regulator replacing UGC, AICTE and NCTE).

BUDGET SESSION 2026 (28 Jan - 18 Apr 2026): six Bills passed — Industrial Relations Code (Amendment); Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment; Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (Amendment); Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation (Amendment); Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions); Central Armed Police Forces (General Administration).

Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026 decriminalises/rationalises offences across 80 central Acts. CAPF (General Administration) Bill, 2026 mandates 50% of IG and 67% of ADG posts by IPS deputation.

The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 — on DELIMITATION — was VOTED DOWN on 16 April 2026. It proposed raising Lok Sabha strength from 550 to 850, delimitation on the basis of Census 2011, and commencement of women's reservation.
MONSOON SESSION 2026 (20 Jul - 13 Aug 2026): 12 Bills introduced, 11 passed. Lok Sabha functioned about 15% and Rajya Sabha about 33% of scheduled time.

Monsoon 2026 laws: Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment; Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment); Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment; MSME Development (Amendment) — mediation within 90 days; Registration of Births and Deaths (Amendment).

More Monsoon 2026 laws: Bankers' Books Evidence Bill (digital records as legal evidence); Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment); TRIBUNALS REFORMS BILL — sets up a National Tribunals Commission; MMDR (Amendment); NCDC (Amendment); KERALA (ALTERATION OF NAME) BILL — renames the state 'Keralam'. The Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026 was referred to a standing committee.
Supreme Court, 17 Mar 2026: adoptive mothers are entitled to 12 weeks' paid maternity leave irrespective of the child's age.
Supreme Court, 24 Mar 2026: Scheduled Caste status is confined to Hinduism, Sikhism and Buddhism; conversion out of these results in loss of SC status.
Supreme Court, 30 Dec 2025: suspended the 100-metre height criterion for classifying the Aravallis; ordered a high-level expert committee (Rajasthan, Haryana, Delhi-NCR).

New/expanded schemes: BHAVYA Rasayan (Aug 2026) — three chemical parks, Rs 3,030 crore, 2026-27 to 2030-31; GOBARdhan (Aug 2026) — compressed biogas, Rs 23,731 crore, 2026-27 to 2035-36; PNG Incentive Scheme (Aug 2026).

Extensions: PMGSY-III continued to March 2028 with revised outlay Rs 83,977 crore; Jal Jeevan Mission extended to December 2028 with Rs 8.7 lakh crore outlay; UDAN revamped with Rs 28,840 crore for 2026-36; RoSCTL extended to September 2026.

Rules and frameworks: Online Gaming Rules, 2026 (22 Apr 2026) set up an Online Gaming Authority and require registration of e-sports; Telecom User Identification Rules, 2026 (21 Aug 2026) mandate Aadhaar-based biometric verification of subscribers; Petroleum and Natural Gas Rules, 2025 replaced the 1959 Rules.
India's updated NDC approved 25 Mar 2026 — 47% reduction in emissions intensity of GDP by 2035 and 60% non-fossil installed capacity by 2035.

Defence and law: 6th Positive Indigenisation List (18 Aug 2026) — 405 items, Rs 3,070 crore business potential; a Ladakh sitting of the Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh High Court was regularised in August 2026.

2026 ASSEMBLY ELECTIONS (counting 4 May 2026): West Bengal — BJP 206 of 294, TMC 81; Assam — BJP 82 of 126, Himanta Biswa Sarma continued as CM; Tamil Nadu — TVK single largest with 107 of 234; Kerala — Congress-led UDF; Puducherry — NDA, AINRC 18 of 30, N. Rangaswamy.

Global indices (latest editions as of Sept 2026): World Happiness Report 2026 — India 116th of 147; Global Hunger Index 2025 — 102nd of 123; HDI (UNDP) — 130th of 193; Global Innovation Index 2025 (WIPO) — 38th of 139.

More indices: Henley Passport Index 2026 — India 81st; Corruption Perceptions Index 2025 (Transparency International) — 91st of 180; World Press Freedom Index 2026 (RSF) — 157th of 180; Global Gender Gap Index 2025 (WEF) — 131st of 148; Global Peace Index 2026 — 127th.
Money and macro: RBI cut the repo rate to 5.25% on 5 December 2025 (from 5.5%) and held it at 5.25% through the April and August 2026 reviews. GDP growth in Q1 of 2026-27 was 7.8%.
Trade: India-Oman CEPA (Dec 2025); India-New Zealand FTA signed 28 April 2026 (duty-free access for essentially all Indian exports); India-Canada CEPA terms of reference signed 2 March 2026.
Health and social: the nationwide HPV vaccination campaign was launched by the Prime Minister from AJMER (Rajasthan) on 28 February 2026.

Committee/report themes of 2026: standing committee reports on cyber crimes and women's safety, oilseeds and pulses, water-efficient seeds, artificial intelligence (recommending comprehensive AI legislation), and a Joint Parliamentary Committee on the Corporate Laws (Amendment) Bill.

questions.q: Justice Surya Kant took office as which Chief Justice of India?
questions.exp: Justice Surya Kant became the 53rd Chief Justice of India. He was in office as of September 2026; verify before the exam as the office changes with retirements.

questions.q: Who is the Chief Election Commissioner of India as of September 2026?
questions.exp: Gyanesh Kumar was serving as Chief Election Commissioner as of September 2026. The CEC and Election Commissioners are appointed under the 2023 Act by a committee of the PM, a Union Minister and the Leader of the Opposition.

questions.q: Who is the Comptroller and Auditor General of India as of September 2026?
questions.exp: K. Sanjay Murthy is the CAG of India as of September 2026. The CAG is appointed under Article 148 and removed in the manner of a Supreme Court judge.

questions.q: Who is the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India as of September 2026?
questions.exp: Sanjay Malhotra is the RBI Governor as of September 2026. Under him the repo rate was reduced to 5.25 per cent in December 2025 and held there through August 2026.

questions.q: Who is the Chairperson of the National Human Rights Commission as of September 2026?
questions.exp: Justice V. Ramasubramanian is the NHRC Chairperson as of September 2026. The NHRC was set up under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.

questions.q: Who is the Chairman of the Securities and Exchange Board of India as of September 2026?
questions.exp: Tuhin Kanta Pandey heads SEBI as of September 2026. The Securities Markets Code, 2025, introduced in December 2025, proposes consolidating the SEBI Act with the Depositories Act and the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act.

questions.q: Who is the Vice-President of India as of September 2026?
questions.exp: C.P. Radhakrishnan is the Vice-President of India as of September 2026 and is ex officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha under Article 64.

questions.q: Who is the Chairman of the Union Public Service Commission as of September 2026?
questions.exp: Ajay Kumar is the UPSC Chairman as of September 2026. The UPSC is a constitutional body under Article 315.

questions.q: Who was appointed a Deputy Governor of the Reserve Bank of India in September 2025, succeeding M. Rajeshwar Rao?
questions.exp: Shirish Chandra Murmu was appointed RBI Deputy Governor for a three-year term in September 2025, succeeding M. Rajeshwar Rao. Poonam Gupta is another serving Deputy Governor.

questions.q: Who is the Chairman of ISRO as of September 2026?
questions.exp: Dr V. Narayanan is the Chairman of ISRO and Secretary, Department of Space, as of September 2026.

questions.q: The Nuclear Energy Bill passed in December 2025 replaced which existing law?
opts: The Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010
questions.exp: The Nuclear Energy Bill, 2025 replaced the Atomic Energy Act, 1962 and allows private-sector participation in nuclear power generation and fuel handling.

questions.q: The law passed in December 2025 replacing MGNREGA raised the guarantee of rural employment from 100 days to:
questions.exp: The new rural employment law raised the guarantee from 100 to 125 days per household per year and changed the centre-state funding pattern to 60:40.

questions.q: Under the law that replaced MGNREGA, the centre-state funding ratio was fixed at:
questions.exp: The Act altered the funding pattern to 60:40 between the Centre and the states, from the earlier arrangement under MGNREGA (December 2025).

questions.q: The Insurance Laws (Amendment) Bill passed in December 2025 raised the foreign direct investment limit in the insurance sector to:
questions.exp: The Bill raised the FDI ceiling in insurance to 100 per cent and cut the net-owned-fund requirement for foreign re-insurers from Rs 5,000 crore to Rs 1,000 crore.

questions.q: The Repealing and Amending Bill, 2025 repealed how many obsolete laws?
questions.exp: The Repealing and Amending Bill, 2025, passed in the Winter Session of December 2025, repealed 71 obsolete laws.

questions.q: Which Bill introduced in December 2025 proposes to consolidate the SEBI Act, the Depositories Act and the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act?
questions.exp: The Securities Markets Code, 2025 was introduced in December 2025 and referred to a Standing Committee; it consolidates the three principal securities laws.

questions.q: Which Bill proposes a single higher-education regulator to replace the UGC, AICTE and NCTE?
opts: Higher Education Commission of India Bill, 2025
questions.exp: The Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025 was introduced in December 2025 and referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee; it seeks a single regulator in place of the UGC, AICTE and NCTE.

questions.q: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, which was voted down in April 2026, dealt primarily with:
opts: Creation of an All India Judicial Service
Delimitation of parliamentary and assembly constituencies
Reservation in promotions for Scheduled Castes
questions.exp: The Bill proposed raising the Lok Sabha's maximum strength from 550 to 850, delimitation on the basis of Census 2011 and the commencement of women's reservation. It was defeated on 16 April 2026.

questions.q: Which Bill passed in 2026 decriminalises or rationalises offences across 80 central Acts?
opts: The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026
The Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, 2026
questions.exp: The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026, passed in the Budget Session, decriminalises or rationalises offences across 80 central Acts.

questions.q: The Central Armed Police Forces (General Administration) Bill, 2026 mandates that what proportion of Inspector General posts be filled by IPS deputation?
questions.exp: The Bill mandates 50 per cent of Inspector General posts and 67 per cent of Additional Director General posts in the CAPFs to be filled through IPS deputation.

questions.q: Under a Bill passed in the Monsoon Session 2026, the name of the state of Kerala was altered to:
questions.exp: The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, 2026 renames the state 'Keralam'. Alteration of a state's name is done under Article 3 by a simple-majority parliamentary law.

questions.q: Which legislation of 2026 provides for the establishment of a National Tribunals Commission?
opts: The Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, 2026
questions.exp: The Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026, passed in the Monsoon Session, provides for a National Tribunals Commission.

questions.q: The Bankers' Books Evidence Bill, 2026 principally provides for:
opts: Recognition of digital records as legal evidence
questions.exp: The Bankers' Books Evidence Bill, 2026, passed in the Monsoon Session, permits digital banking records to be used as legal evidence.

questions.q: The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026 requires mediation in delayed-payment disputes to be completed within:
questions.exp: The Bill centralises enterprise classification and requires mediation to be completed within 90 days (passed August 2026).

questions.q: In a judgment of March 2026, the Supreme Court held that adoptive mothers are entitled to paid maternity leave of:
questions.exp: On 17 March 2026 the Supreme Court held that adoptive mothers are entitled to 12 weeks of paid maternity leave irrespective of the age of the adopted child.

questions.q: In a judgment of March 2026 the Supreme Court held that Scheduled Caste status is confined to persons professing which religions?
questions.exp: On 24 March 2026 the Court held that SC status is limited to Hinduism, Sikhism and Buddhism, and that conversion out of these results in loss of the status. This mirrors the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950.

questions.q: The BHAVYA Rasayan scheme approved in August 2026 provides for the setting up of:
questions.exp: The BHAVYA Rasayan scheme, approved on 10 August 2026, provides for three chemical parks with an outlay of Rs 3,030 crore for 2026-27 to 2030-31.

questions.q: The GOBARdhan scheme approved in August 2026, with an outlay of Rs 23,731 crore, promotes:
questions.exp: The revamped GOBARdhan scheme approved on 6 August 2026 promotes compressed biogas production, with an outlay of Rs 23,731 crore for 2026-27 to 2035-36.

questions.q: The Jal Jeevan Mission was extended in March 2026 up to:
questions.exp: In March 2026 the Jal Jeevan Mission was extended to December 2028 with an outlay of about Rs 8.7 lakh crore.

questions.q: The Online Gaming Rules notified in April 2026 provide for the establishment of:
questions.exp: The Online Gaming Rules, 2026, notified on 22 April 2026, establish an Online Gaming Authority, define online money games and require registration for e-sports.

questions.q: The Telecom User Identification Rules, 2026 notified in August 2026 make which of the following mandatory for all subscribers?
opts: Physical presence at a telecom exchange
questions.exp: The Telecom User Identification Rules, 2026, notified on 21 August 2026, mandate Aadhaar-based biometric verification of all telecom subscribers.

questions.q: India's updated Nationally Determined Contribution approved in March 2026 targets a reduction in the emissions intensity of GDP by 2035 of:
questions.exp: The NDC approved on 25 March 2026 targets a 47 per cent reduction in emissions intensity of GDP by 2035 and 60 per cent non-fossil installed capacity by 2035.

questions.q: The counting of votes for the 2026 assembly elections in West Bengal, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Assam and Puducherry took place on:
questions.exp: Counting for the five 2026 assembly elections took place on 4 May 2026; Tamil Nadu polled in a single phase on 23 April and West Bengal in two phases on 23 and 29 April 2026.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Nuclear Energy Bill, 2025:
I. It replaces the Atomic Energy Act, 1962.
II. It permits private-sector participation in nuclear energy generation.
III. It was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee instead of being passed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Bill was among the seven passed in the Winter Session of December 2025, so III is wrong. The two Bills referred to committees in that session were the Securities Markets Code and the Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Winter Session of Parliament, 2025:
I. It was held from 1 to 19 December 2025.
II. It had 15 sittings.
III. Seven Bills were passed during the session.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Nine Bills were introduced, seven were passed and two were referred to committees.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026:
I. It proposed raising the maximum strength of the Lok Sabha from 550 to 850.
II. It proposed delimitation on the basis of the Census of 2011.
III. It was passed by Parliament in April 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Bill was voted down on 16 April 2026, so III is wrong. It also linked the commencement of women's reservation to the delimitation exercise.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Monsoon Session of Parliament, 2026:
I. It ran from 20 July to 13 August 2026.
II. Twelve Bills were introduced and eleven were passed.
III. The Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026 was referred to a standing committee.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. During the session the Lok Sabha functioned for about 15 per cent and the Rajya Sabha for about 33 per cent of scheduled time.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Supreme Court judgments delivered in March 2026:
I. Adoptive mothers were held entitled to 12 weeks of paid maternity leave irrespective of the child's age.
II. Scheduled Caste status was held to be confined to Hinduism, Sikhism and Buddhism.
III. The Court struck down the Jan Vishwas Bill, 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026 was passed by Parliament and was not struck down, so III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's updated Nationally Determined Contribution approved in March 2026:
I. It targets a 47 per cent reduction in the emissions intensity of GDP by 2035.
II. It targets 60 per cent non-fossil installed electricity capacity by 2035.
III. It was approved by the Union Cabinet in March 2026.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct as of September 2026. NDCs are submitted under the Paris Agreement framework.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 2026 assembly elections:
I. The BJP won 206 of the 294 seats in West Bengal.
II. Himanta Biswa Sarma continued as Chief Minister of Assam.
III. The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam emerged as the single largest party in Tamil Nadu.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct according to the results declared on 4 May 2026. The Congress-led UDF won Kerala and the NDA retained Puducherry.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the law replacing MGNREGA passed in December 2025:
I. It raised the guarantee of employment from 100 to 125 days.
II. It changed the centre-state funding pattern to 60:40.
III. It abolished the statutory right to work.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Act retained a statutory employment guarantee, in an enlarged form of 125 days, so III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Bills referred to committees in the Winter Session of 2025:
I. The Securities Markets Code, 2025 was referred to a Standing Committee.
II. The Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill, 2025 was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
III. The Viksit Bharat Shiksha Adhishthan Bill proposes a single regulator to replace the UGC, AICTE and NCTE.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. These were the two Bills of the December 2025 session that were referred to committees rather than passed.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Budget Session of Parliament, 2026:
I. It ran from 28 January to 18 April 2026.
II. Six Bills were passed during the session.
III. The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill was among the Bills passed.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill was defeated on 16 April 2026, so III is wrong. The six Bills passed included the Jan Vishwas and CAPF Bills.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the monetary policy of the Reserve Bank of India:
I. The repo rate was reduced to 5.25 per cent in December 2025.
II. The repo rate was retained at 5.25 per cent in the reviews of April and August 2026.
III. GDP growth in the first quarter of 2026-27 was reported at 7.8 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct as of September 2026. The December 2025 cut took the repo rate from 5.5 per cent to 5.25 per cent.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Office)   List-II (Incumbent as of September 2026)
A. Attorney General for India   1. T.V. Somanathan
B. Solicitor General of India   2. V. Anantha Nageswaran
C. Cabinet Secretary            3. R. Venkataramani
D. Chief Economic Adviser       4. Tushar Mehta
questions.exp: As of September 2026: Attorney General R. Venkataramani; Solicitor General Tushar Mehta; Cabinet Secretary T.V. Somanathan; Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Bill of the Monsoon Session 2026)   List-II (Principal subject)
A. Tribunals Reforms Bill   1. Renaming of a state
B. Bankers' Books Evidence Bill   2. National Tribunals Commission
C. Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill   3. Regulation of mineral-bearing lands
D. Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill   4. Digital records as legal evidence
questions.exp: The Tribunals Reforms Bill sets up a National Tribunals Commission; the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill recognises digital records; the Kerala Bill renames the state 'Keralam'; the MMDR Amendment empowers the Centre to regulate mineral-bearing lands.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Scheme/mission)   List-II (Outlay or extended period announced in 2026)
A. GOBARdhan   1. Rs 83,977 crore, up to March 2028
B. BHAVYA Rasayan   2. Rs 8.7 lakh crore, up to December 2028
C. PMGSY-III   3. Rs 3,030 crore, 2026-27 to 2030-31
D. Jal Jeevan Mission   4. Rs 23,731 crore, 2026-27 to 2035-36
questions.exp: GOBARdhan got Rs 23,731 crore to 2035-36; BHAVYA Rasayan Rs 3,030 crore to 2030-31; PMGSY-III was continued to March 2028 with Rs 83,977 crore; the Jal Jeevan Mission was extended to December 2028 with about Rs 8.7 lakh crore.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Global index)   List-II (Publishing organisation)
A. World Happiness Report   1. World Intellectual Property Organization
B. Global Innovation Index   2. Transparency International
C. Corruption Perceptions Index   3. Henley and Partners

questions.exp: The World Happiness Report is published by the UN SDSN; the Global Innovation Index by WIPO; the Corruption Perceptions Index by Transparency International; the passport ranking referred to here is the Henley Passport Index.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Index, latest edition as of September 2026)   List-II (India's rank)
A. World Happiness Report 2026   1. 38
B. Global Hunger Index 2025      2. 130
C. Human Development Index       3. 116
D. Global Innovation Index 2025  4. 102
questions.exp: As of September 2026: World Happiness Report 2026 — 116th of 147; Global Hunger Index 2025 — 102nd of 123; HDI — 130th of 193; Global Innovation Index 2025 — 38th of 139.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Session of Parliament)   List-II (Number of Bills passed)
A. Winter Session 2025   1. Eleven
B. Budget Session 2026   2. Seven
C. Monsoon Session 2026  3. Six
D. Bills referred to committees in Winter Session 2025   4. Two
questions.exp: Winter 2025: seven Bills passed, two referred to committees. Budget 2026: six passed. Monsoon 2026: eleven of twelve passed.

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the codes given below:
List-I (Rules/framework notified)   List-II (Subject)
A. Online Gaming Rules, 2026   1. Aadhaar-based biometric verification of subscribers
B. Telecom User Identification Rules, 2026   2. Replaced the 1959 Rules on oilfield leases
C. Petroleum and Natural Gas Rules, 2025   3. Composite licences for nuclear plants
D. Draft SHANTI Rules, 2026   4. Establishment of an Online Gaming Authority
questions.exp: The Online Gaming Rules 2026 create an Online Gaming Authority; the Telecom User Identification Rules 2026 mandate Aadhaar biometric verification; the Petroleum and Natural Gas Rules 2025 replaced the 1959 Rules; the draft SHANTI Rules of August 2026 propose single composite nuclear plant licences.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of office and incumbent, as of September 2026, is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Chief Justice of India — Justice Surya Kant
Comptroller and Auditor General — K. Sanjay Murthy
Governor, Reserve Bank of India — Sanjay Malhotra
questions.exp: Gyanesh Kumar is the Chief Election Commissioner as of September 2026. The other three pairs are correct.

questions.q: Which one of the following Bills was NOT passed during the Monsoon Session of Parliament, 2026?
questions.exp: The Indian Statistical Institute Bill, 2026 was introduced in August 2026 and referred to a standing committee; the other three were passed by both Houses.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of index and India's rank in its latest edition, as of September 2026, is NOT correctly matched?
questions.exp: India ranked 38th of 139 in the Global Innovation Index 2025 published by WIPO. The rank of 91st out of 180 belongs to the Corruption Perceptions Index 2025.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs relating to schemes announced or revised in 2026 is NOT correctly matched?
opts: PMGSY-III — Rural road connectivity extended to March 2028
UDAN — Regional air connectivity with Rs 28,840 crore for 2026-36
questions.exp: BHAVYA Rasayan provides for three chemical parks with an outlay of Rs 3,030 crore; it is GOBARdhan that supports compressed biogas.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the 2026 assembly elections is NOT correct?
opts: Counting of votes took place on 4 May 2026
The Congress-led United Democratic Front won Kerala
N. Rangaswamy of the AINRC led the winning side in Puducherry
The Trinamool Congress retained power in West Bengal
questions.exp: The BJP won 206 of 294 seats in West Bengal, with the Trinamool Congress reduced to 81. The other three statements are correct.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a correct statement about legislation passed in December 2025?
opts: The Nuclear Energy Bill replaced the Electricity Act, 2003
The Insurance Laws (Amendment) Bill raised the FDI limit to 100 per cent
The Repealing and Amending Bill repealed 71 obsolete laws
The law replacing MGNREGA raised the employment guarantee to 125 days
questions.exp: The Nuclear Energy Bill, 2025 replaced the Atomic Energy Act, 1962, not the Electricity Act, 2003.

questions.q: With reference to central legislation of 2026, which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
opts: Central Armed Police Forces (General Administration) Bill, 2026 — 50 per cent of IG posts by IPS deputation
Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026 — Establishment of a National Tribunals Commission
MSME Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026 — Mediation to be completed within 90 days
Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 — Delimitation of constituencies
questions.exp: The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026 decriminalises offences across 80 central Acts; the National Tribunals Commission is provided for by the Tribunals Reforms Bill, 2026.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in correct chronological order:
I. Winter Session of Parliament 2025
II. Presentation of the Union Budget and start of the Budget Session 2026
III. Counting of votes in the 2026 assembly elections
IV. Monsoon Session of Parliament 2026
questions.exp: The Winter Session ran 1-19 December 2025; the Budget Session began 28 January 2026; counting for the assembly elections was on 4 May 2026; the Monsoon Session ran 20 July to 13 August 2026.

questions.q:
Arrange the following developments in correct chronological order:
I. Supreme Court ruling on maternity leave for adoptive mothers
II. Defeat of the Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill
III. Signing of the India-New Zealand Free Trade Agreement
IV. Approval of the GOBARdhan scheme with a Rs 23,731 crore outlay
questions.exp: The maternity-leave ruling was on 17 March 2026, the 131st Amendment Bill was defeated on 16 April 2026, the India-New Zealand FTA was signed on 28 April 2026 and GOBARdhan was approved on 6 August 2026.

chapters.title: National Economy and Union Budget
factsheet: NOTE: This chapter was compiled in September 2026 and should be refreshed in November 2026 for the final weeks before the exam.
Union Budget 2026-27 (presented 1 Feb 2026, theme Viksit Bharat 2047, three 'Kartavyas'): total expenditure Rs 53,47,315 crore (+7.7% over RE 2025-26).
Budget 2026-27 receipts (excl. borrowings) Rs 36,51,547 crore; borrowings Rs 16,95,768 crore; nominal GDP growth assumed at 10%.
Budget 2026-27 deficits: fiscal 4.3% of GDP, revenue 1.5%, primary 0.7%; outstanding liabilities 55.6% of GDP, target ~50% by 2030-31.
Budget 2026-27: revenue expenditure Rs 41,25,494 crore; capital expenditure Rs 12,21,821 crore (+11.5%); interest payments Rs 14,03,972 crore = 26% of total spending, 40% of revenue receipts.

Largest ministry allocations 2026-27: Defence Rs 7,84,678 cr (15% of budget) > Road Transport & Highways Rs 3,09,875 cr > Railways Rs 2,81,377 cr > Home Affairs Rs 2,55,234 cr > Education Rs 1,39,289 cr.
Biggest schemes 2026-27: VB-G RAM G (replaced MGNREGA) Rs 95,692 cr; Jal Jeevan Mission Rs 67,670 cr; PM-KISAN Rs 63,500 cr; PMAY-Gramin Rs 54,917 cr; Samagra Shiksha Rs 42,100 cr.

New in Budget 2026-27: Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana Rs 20,083 cr; Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme Rs 40,000 cr; Biopharma SHAKTI Rs 10,000 cr; CCUS mission Rs 20,000 cr; SME Growth Fund Rs 10,000 cr; City Economic Regions Rs 5,000 cr each.

Budget 2026-27 tax measures: income-tax slabs unchanged; MAT cut 15%->14%; IFSC tax holiday 10->20 years; STT raised (options 0.15%, futures 0.05%); TCS on education/medical remittances and tour packages cut to 2%.
Budget 2026-27: disinvestment/miscellaneous capital receipts target Rs 80,000 crore (+136%); transfers to states Rs 26,20,769 cr; tax devolution Rs 15,26,255 cr; capex loans to states Rs 1,85,000 cr.
Budget 2026-27 subsidies: food Rs 2,27,629 cr, fertiliser Rs 1,70,799 cr, total Rs 4,54,773 cr (down 3.1%).

Union Budget 2025-26: total expenditure Rs 50,65,345 cr; fiscal deficit 4.4% of GDP; nil income tax up to Rs 12 lakh in the new regime; Nuclear Energy Mission Rs 20,000 cr; Urban Challenge Fund Rs 1 lakh crore; Maritime Development Fund Rs 25,000 cr.
Economic Survey 2025-26 tabled 29 January 2026: 2025-26 growth estimated 7.4%; 2026-27 projected 6.8-7.2%; medium-term potential 7%.
Economic Survey 2025-26: retail inflation 1.7% (Apr-Dec 2025-26) vs 4.6% a year earlier; current account deficit 0.8% of GDP in H1; FDI USD 81 billion in 2025; unemployment 3.2% (2023-24).
National Accounts base year shifted 2011-12 -> 2022-23; revised series released February 2026; back-series to 1950-51 due December 2026; new sources include ASUSE, PLFS, GSTN, e-Vahan, PFMS.
GDP: FY2025-26 real growth 7.7% (Provisional Estimates), Q4 8.6%; Q1 of 2026-27 grew 7.8%; manufacturing 10.7% in FY26; agriculture 3%.
56th GST Council (September 2025, chaired by FM Nirmala Sitharaman): two principal slabs 5% and 18% plus a 40% demerit rate; new rates effective 22 September 2025.

GST 2.0: individual life and health insurance premiums exempted; cement, ACs, TVs, small cars and <=350cc two-wheelers moved 28% -> 18%; pan masala, gutkha, cigarettes, yachts and >350cc motorcycles at 40%.
RBI Monetary Policy (August 2026 review): repo 5.25%, SDF 5.00%, MSF and Bank Rate 5.50%, stance neutral, decision unanimous; Governor Sanjay Malhotra.
RBI August 2026 projections: FY2026-27 real GDP 6.7%; CPI inflation 5.0% for the year, core 4.3%; polymer (plastic) banknotes proposed from the next financial year subject to field trials.
16th Finance Commission (Chairman Arvind Panagariya), award period 2026-27 to 2030-31, report tabled 1 February 2026: vertical devolution retained at 41% of the divisible pool.

16th FC horizontal criteria: income distance 42.5%, population (2011) 17.5%, demographic performance 10%, area 10%, forest & ecology 10%, and a NEW criterion - contribution to GDP 10%; tax-and-fiscal-effort dropped.

16th FC: grants of Rs 9.47 lakh crore over five years (rural local bodies Rs 4.4 lakh cr, urban Rs 3.6 lakh cr, disaster management Rs 1.56 lakh cr); revenue deficit grants discontinued; Centre's fiscal deficit to 3.5% of GDP by 2030-31.

Trade deals: India-UK CETA signed 24 July 2025, in force 15 July 2026 (90.2% of India's exports duty-free); India-Oman CEPA signed 18 December 2025; India-New Zealand FTA signed 27 April 2026; India-EU FTA concluded January 2026 (97% of tariff lines, 99.5% of trade value).

Monsoon Session 2026 (20 July-13 August) passed the Bankers' Books Evidence Bill 2026 (replacing the 1891 Act), MSME Development Amendment Bill, Taxation and Other Laws Amendment Bill and Tribunals Reforms Bill (National Tribunals Commission).
Cabinet decisions: Atal Pension Yojana continued till 2030-31 (Jan 2026); BHAVYA-Rasayan chemical parks scheme Rs 3,030 crore; GOBARdhan National Circular Bioenergy Scheme Rs 23,731 crore.

Indices: Global Innovation Index 2025 (WIPO) India 38th of 139; RBI Financial Inclusion Index 67 (March 2025); GIFT City 43rd in Global Financial Centres Index (38th edition); NITI Aayog Fiscal Health Index topped by Odisha.
Foreign Assets Disclosure Scheme Rules 2026: undisclosed foreign assets up to Rs 1 crore (property up to Rs 5 crore) may be declared by 31 December 2026 on payment of 60% of value.

questions.q: The total expenditure budgeted in the Union Budget 2026-27 is approximately
questions.exp: The Union Budget 2026-27, presented on 1 February 2026, budgeted total expenditure at Rs 53,47,315 crore, 7.7% above the revised estimates of 2025-26.

questions.q: The fiscal deficit target set in the Union Budget 2026-27 is
questions.exp: The 2026-27 Budget targets a fiscal deficit of 4.3% of GDP, down from 4.4% in 2025-26. The revenue deficit is 1.5% and the primary deficit 0.7% of GDP.

questions.q: The nominal GDP growth rate assumed while framing the Union Budget 2026-27 is
questions.exp: Budget 2026-27 assumes nominal GDP growth of 10%. The 2025-26 Budget had assumed 10.1%.

questions.q: In the Union Budget 2026-27, interest payments account for what share of total expenditure?
questions.exp: Interest payments of Rs 14,03,972 crore make up about 26% of total budgeted expenditure and about 40% of revenue receipts in 2026-27.

questions.q: Which ministry received the largest allocation in the Union Budget 2026-27?
opts: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
questions.exp: Defence received Rs 7,84,678 crore, about 15% of the total Budget, followed by Road Transport & Highways (Rs 3,09,875 crore) and Railways (Rs 2,81,377 crore).

questions.q: The rural employment guarantee programme that replaced MGNREGA and received the largest scheme allocation in the Union Budget 2026-27 is
questions.exp: VB-G RAM G, which replaced MGNREGA, was allotted Rs 95,692 crore in 2026-27, the largest single scheme allocation. Audit rules for it were placed in the public domain in August 2026.

questions.q: The target for disinvestment and other miscellaneous capital receipts in the Union Budget 2026-27 is
questions.exp: The 2026-27 Budget set a disinvestment/miscellaneous capital receipts target of Rs 80,000 crore, an increase of over 136% on the previous year's revised estimate.

questions.q: In the Union Budget 2026-27, the Minimum Alternate Tax (MAT) rate was reduced to
questions.exp: MAT was cut from 15% to 14% and made a final tax. Personal income tax slabs were left unchanged in 2026-27.

questions.q: Under the Union Budget 2025-26, income up to what level was made free of income tax under the new tax regime?
questions.exp: The 2025-26 Budget raised the effective nil-tax income under the new regime from Rs 7 lakh to Rs 12 lakh; income above Rs 24 lakh is taxed at 30%.

questions.q: The Urban Challenge Fund announced in the Union Budget 2025-26 has a corpus of
questions.exp: The Union Budget 2025-26 announced a Rs 1 lakh crore Urban Challenge Fund, alongside a Rs 25,000 crore Maritime Development Fund and a Rs 20,000 crore Nuclear Energy Mission.

questions.q: The Nuclear Energy Mission announced in the Union Budget 2025-26 carries an outlay of
questions.exp: The Nuclear Energy Mission for research and development of Small Modular Reactors was given Rs 20,000 crore in the 2025-26 Budget.

questions.q: The Economic Survey 2025-26 was tabled in Parliament on
questions.exp: The Economic Survey 2025-26 was tabled by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on 29 January 2026, ahead of the Union Budget presented on 1 February 2026.

questions.q: The Economic Survey 2025-26 projected India's real GDP growth for 2026-27 in the range of
questions.exp: The Survey projected 6.8-7.2% growth for 2026-27 and estimated 7.4% for 2025-26, with medium-term potential growth of about 7%.

questions.q: According to the Economic Survey 2025-26, retail inflation during April-December of 2025-26 averaged about
questions.exp: Retail inflation fell to about 1.7% in April-December 2025-26 from 4.6% in 2024-25. As of September 2026 the RBI's tolerance band remains 4% (+/-2%).

questions.q: In the bi-monthly monetary policy review announced in August 2026, the RBI kept the policy repo rate at
questions.exp: The MPC held the repo rate at 5.25% with a neutral stance in its August 2026 review. As of September 2026 the SDF stands at 5.00% and the MSF and Bank Rate at 5.50%.

questions.q: Who announced the Reserve Bank of India's monetary policy decisions during 2026?
questions.exp: Sanjay Malhotra is the Governor of the Reserve Bank of India and chaired the Monetary Policy Committee through 2026, including the August 2026 review.

questions.q: In its August 2026 statement, the Reserve Bank of India projected India's real GDP growth for 2026-27 at
questions.exp: The RBI revised its 2026-27 growth projection upward to 6.7% in August 2026, with CPI inflation projected at 5.0% for the year.

questions.q: The revised GST rates approved by the 56th GST Council came into effect from
questions.exp: The 56th GST Council met in September 2025 and its restructured rates took effect on 22 September 2025.

questions.q: The highest 'demerit' rate of GST introduced by the 56th GST Council is
questions.exp: Besides the two principal slabs of 5% and 18%, a 40% demerit rate was created for goods such as pan masala, gutkha, cigarettes, yachts, helicopters and motorcycles above 350 cc.

questions.q: After the September 2025 GST restructuring, the rate of GST on premiums of individual life and health insurance policies is
questions.exp: Individual life and health insurance premiums were fully exempted from GST with effect from 22 September 2025 - among the most publicised changes of GST 2.0.

questions.q: The new base year adopted for India's National Accounts series is
questions.exp: The National Statistical Office shifted the base year from 2011-12 to 2022-23, releasing the revised series in February 2026. Back-series data to 1950-51 is due in December 2026.

questions.q: Who chaired the Sixteenth Finance Commission?
questions.exp: Dr. Arvind Panagariya chaired the 16th Finance Commission, whose report for 2026-27 to 2030-31 was tabled in Parliament on 1 February 2026.

questions.q: The share of states in the divisible pool of central taxes recommended by the Sixteenth Finance Commission is
questions.exp: The 16th Finance Commission retained the vertical devolution at 41%, the same as recommended by the 15th Finance Commission.

questions.q: The India-United Kingdom Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) entered into force on
questions.exp: CETA was signed on 24 July 2025 and entered into force on 15 July 2026, together with the Agreement on Social Security Contributions. It makes 90.2% of India's exports to the UK duty-free.

questions.q: As per the Provisional Estimates released by the National Statistical Office, India's real GDP growth in 2025-26 was
questions.exp: Provisional Estimates put 2025-26 real GDP growth at 7.7%, with fourth-quarter growth of 8.6%. Figures are on the new 2022-23 base; as of September 2026 these remain provisional.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Union Budget 2026-27:
I. Capital expenditure is budgeted at about Rs 12.22 lakh crore.
II. The revenue deficit is estimated at 1.5% of GDP.
III. Total expenditure is budgeted lower than the revised estimates of 2025-26.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Capital expenditure of Rs 12,21,821 crore is 11.5% higher and total expenditure 7.7% higher than the 2025-26 revised estimates, so statement III is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the decisions of the 56th GST Council:
I. The number of principal GST slabs was raised to three, namely 5%, 12% and 18%.
II. Cement was moved from the 28% slab to the 18% slab.
III. Premiums of individual life and health insurance policies were exempted from GST.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Council reduced the structure to two principal slabs, 5% and 18%, plus a 40% demerit rate; the 12% and 28% slabs were done away with. Hence statement I is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Economic Survey 2025-26:
I. It estimated real GDP growth of 7.4% for 2025-26.
II. It reported a current account surplus of 0.8% of GDP in the first half of 2025-26.
III. It placed FDI inflows in 2025 at about USD 81 billion.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The Survey reported a current account DEFICIT of 0.8% of GDP in H1 2025-26, down from 1.3% a year earlier, so statement II is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sixteenth Finance Commission:
I. Its award period is 2026-27 to 2030-31.
II. It introduced 'contribution to GDP' as a criterion with a weight of 10%.
III. It discontinued revenue deficit grants to states.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Commission also dropped the 2.5% weight earlier given to tax and fiscal effort and recommended grants of Rs 9.47 lakh crore over five years.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the RBI monetary policy review of August 2026:
I. The Monetary Policy Committee cut the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.25%.
II. The standing deposit facility rate was 5.00% and the marginal standing facility rate 5.50%.
III. The Committee retained the neutral policy stance.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The MPC left the repo rate UNCHANGED at 5.25% in August 2026; it did not cut it. The decision was unanimous. Rates are as of the August 2026 review.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the revision of India's National Accounts series:
I. The base year was shifted from 2011-12 to 2022-23.
II. The revised series was first released in February 2025.
III. GST network data and e-Vahan vehicle registrations are among the new data sources used.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

chapters.title: International Affairs and Organisations
factsheet: NOTE: This chapter was compiled in September 2026 and should be refreshed in November 2026 for the final weeks before the exam.
COP30 of the UNFCCC: Belem, Brazil, 10-22 November 2025; President Andre Correa do Lago; about 56,000 registered delegates.

COP30 outcome package named the 'global mutirao' (Portuguese for collective effort); it called for tripling adaptation finance by 2035 and created a Just Transition Mechanism, but contained NO fossil-fuel phase-out roadmap.
COP30 also launched a voluntary 'Global Implementation Accelerator'; the presidency promised separate fossil-fuel and deforestation roadmaps at COP31.
COP31 (2026): hosted at Antalya, Turkiye, while AUSTRALIA holds the presidency and leads the negotiations - a compromise announced on 20 November 2025.

20th G20 Summit: Johannesburg, South Africa, November 2025 - the FIRST G20 Leaders' Summit on African soil; theme 'Solidarity, Equality, Sustainability'; the 122-paragraph Leaders' Declaration invoked the African philosophy of Ubuntu.

G20 Johannesburg launches: Mission 300 (electricity for 300 million people in sub-Saharan Africa by 2030, World Bank + AfDB), the Nelson Mandela Bay Target on youth NEET rates, a Cost of Capital Commission and a Critical Minerals Framework. The United States holds the next G20 presidency.

India's proposals at G20 Johannesburg: G20 Initiative on Countering the Drug-Terror Nexus, a G20 Global Healthcare Response Team, a Global Traditional Knowledge Repository, an Open Satellite Data Partnership and a Critical Minerals Circularity Initiative.
25th SCO Summit: Tianjin, China, 31 August-1 September 2025; PM Modi attended; Kyrgyzstan takes the next chair.
17th BRICS Summit: Rio de Janeiro, July 2025. INDIA holds the BRICS chairship for 2026 and hosts the 18th Summit; BRICS works strictly by consensus.
22nd ASEAN-India Summit: Kuala Lumpur, 26 October 2025 (PM Modi joined virtually). APEC 2025: Gyeongju, Republic of Korea, 31 October-1 November 2025.
Gaza: US 20-point peace plan announced 29 September 2025; Gaza Peace Summit at Sharm el-Sheikh, Egypt, 13 October 2025.

UN Security Council Resolution 2803, adopted 17 November 2025 by 13-0 (China and Russia abstaining), endorsed the plan and authorised a Board of Peace and an International Stabilization Force for Gaza.
Nobel Prizes 2025 - Medicine: Mary E. Brunkow, Fred Ramsdell, Shimon Sakaguchi (peripheral immune tolerance, regulatory T cells).
Nobel Physics 2025: John Clarke, Michel Devoret, John Martinis (macroscopic quantum mechanical tunnelling and energy quantisation in an electric circuit).
Nobel Chemistry 2025: Susumu Kitagawa, Richard Robson, Omar Yaghi (metal-organic frameworks, MOFs). Nobel Literature 2025: Laszlo Krasznahorkai (Hungary).

Nobel Peace 2025: Maria Corina Machado of Venezuela. Nobel Economic Sciences 2025: Joel Mokyr, Philippe Aghion and Peter Howitt (innovation-driven growth; creative destruction). Prize value about 11 million Swedish kronor.
Sanae Takaichi became JAPAN'S FIRST WOMAN PRIME MINISTER, elected on 21 October 2025.

President Putin visited India on 4-5 December 2025 for the 23rd India-Russia Annual Summit: 16 inter-governmental agreements and 15 MoUs; trade target USD 100 billion by 2030 (trade then about USD 68.7 billion).
16th India-EU Summit, New Delhi, January 2026; the India-EU FTA was concluded in January 2026 covering about 97% of tariff lines and 99.5% of bilateral trade value.

UAE state visit to India, 19 January 2026: bilateral trade target doubled to USD 200 billion by 2032; a 10-year HPCL-ADNOC LNG agreement from 2028; UAE investment in the Dholera Special Investment Region.
Germany visit, 12-13 January 2026: 12 Joint Declarations of Intent, 5 MoUs and 2 other agreements; visa-free transit through Germany for Indian passport holders.
India AI Impact Summit, New Delhi, 16-20 February 2026, theme 'People, Planet, Progress'; it set a Guinness World Record with 250,946 AI-responsibility pledges.
11th Raisina Dialogue: New Delhi, 5-7 March 2026. 9th Indian Ocean Conference: Port Louis, Mauritius, 10-12 April 2026.
PM Modi's five-nation tour, 15-20 May 2026: UAE, the Netherlands, Sweden, Norway and Italy - including the 3rd India-Nordic Summit; his first visit to Norway in over four decades.
India-Uzbekistan relations were elevated to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership in August 2026, with a bilateral trade target of USD 5 billion by 2030.

India in global indices: Global Innovation Index 2025 (WIPO) 38th; Global Terrorism Index 2026 13th; Climate Change Performance Index 2026 23rd; Climate Risk Index 2026 9th most affected; Human Development Report 2025 130th; Global Hunger Index 2025 102nd; Corruption Perceptions Index 2025 91st.

Other index facts: World Happiness Report 2025 - Finland first for the 9th year, India 116th; Global Gender Gap 2025 - Iceland first for the 16th year, India 131st; SIPRI - Russia supplied about 40% of India's arms imports.
WMO Greenhouse Gas Bulletin 2025: atmospheric CO2 reached 423.9 ppm in 2024. WHO Global TB Report 2025: TB cases fell 21% between 2015 and 2024.

chapters.title: Science, Technology, Environment and Defence in the News
factsheet: NOTE: This chapter was compiled in September 2026 and should be refreshed in November 2026 for the final weeks before the exam.

LVM3-M6 (24 Dec 2025, 08:55 IST, SDSC-SHAR Sriharikota) placed AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird Block-2 in LEO — described by ISRO Chairman V. Narayanan as the heaviest satellite ever lifted from Indian soil by an Indian launcher; commercial mission of NewSpace India Ltd (NSIL).

PSLV-C62 (12 Jan 2026) — ISRO's first mission of 2026 — FAILED after an anomaly in the third stage (PS3); payload EOS-N1 plus 14 co-passenger satellites. Second PSLV failure within a year (after PSLV-C61).
GSLV-F17 (4 Sept 2026, 02:55 IST, Second Launch Pad, SDSC-SHAR) launched EOS-05 into sub-GTO — India's FIRST imaging satellite in geosynchronous orbit; 19th flight of the GSLV.
Gaganyaan: uncrewed G1 on LVM3 carrying the humanoid robot Vyommitra; first crewed flight (H1) targeted 2027 (as of September 2026). ISRO Chairman: V. Narayanan.
Agni-5 with MIRV (Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicle) advanced flight test, 8 May 2026, Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island, Odisha.

DRDO Ballistic Missile Defence: three flight tests, 10-11 June 2026; the AD-2 endo/exo interceptor reached 'intercontinental class'. Naval Anti-Ship Missile-Medium Range (about 350 km) completed its maiden trial.
Rudram-II (about 300 km) and Rudram-III (about 550-600 km) anti-radiation missiles; Project Kusha long-range air-defence system (350+ km, induction target 2028-29).
AMCA (Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft), India's fifth-generation fighter — RFP issued 27 May 2026 to three shortlisted development partners; first flight targeted 2032, deliveries from 2035.
First India-assembled C-295 transport aircraft made its maiden flight on 10 June 2026 from the Tata-Airbus facility at Vadodara.

21 June 2026 commissionings: INS Dunagiri (Project 17A stealth frigate), INS Sanshodhak (Survey Vessel Large) and INS Agray (Arnala-class anti-submarine warfare craft) — all with over 75% indigenous content.

Record defence numbers FY 2025-26: production about Rs 1.78 lakh crore; exports about Rs 38,424 crore (roughly $4.1 billion), a 63% jump. DFPDS-2026 unveiled 4 June 2026 delegating procurement powers of Rs 1.25+ lakh crore a year. Lt Gen Dhiraj Seth appointed Chief of the Army Staff, 13 June 2026.

Exercises 2026: MILAN (Visakhapatnam, Feb — theme 'Camaraderie, Cooperation, Collaboration'), Vayushakti-26 (Pokhran Range, Jaisalmer), Khanjar-XIII (India-Kyrgyzstan, Assam), Dharma Guardian (India-Japan, Uttarakhand), Vajra Prahar (India-USA, Himachal Pradesh), Dosti-17 (India-Sri Lanka-Maldives, Male), Lamitiye (India-Seychelles), Kakadu, Sea Dragon.

Exercises 2025: Malabar-2025 (Quad, near Guam), Ajeya Warrior-25 (India-UK, in RAJASTHAN), Bold Kurukshetra (India-Singapore, in RAJASTHAN), Yudh Abhyas 2025 (Alaska, USA), Trishul (tri-service, Pakistan border), Konkan (UK), JAIMEX (Japan), SLINEX (Sri Lanka), Garuda (France), TROPEX (Navy's largest).

India AI Impact Summit 2026 — 16-21 Feb 2026, Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi; 100+ countries and 20 international organisations; concluded with the NEW DELHI DECLARATION endorsed by 92 countries/organisations.

AI Summit outputs: Global AI Impact Commons, Equitable AI Transition Playbook (with ILO), Charter for Democratic Diffusion of AI, Trusted AI Commons, Alliance for Advancing Inclusion Through AI (with UNICEF), Network of AI for Science Institutions.

AI Summit investments: over $200 billion pledged — Reliance $110 bn over 7 years, Google $15 bn AI hub at VISAKHAPATNAM, Lightspeed $10 bn, General Catalyst $5 bn. IndiaAI Mission GPU capacity to rise from 38,000+ to 58,000+.
COP30 (UNFCCC) — Belem, BRAZIL, 10-22 November 2025; President Andre Correa do Lago; final package named the 'GLOBAL MUTIRAO'.

COP30 outcomes: call to TRIPLE adaptation finance by 2035; new JUST TRANSITION MECHANISM; voluntary 'Global Implementation Accelerator'. NO fossil-fuel phase-out roadmap in the decision text — the presidency promised separate roadmaps.

Ramsar: India has 101 sites (August 2026) across 28 States/UTs. 101st = GLAW LAKE, Arunachal Pradesh (3 Aug 2026); 2026 additions also included Chhari-Dhand (Gujarat), Shekha Jheel, Patna Bird Sanctuary and Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary (all UP).

Rajasthan's Ramsar sites (5): Keoladeo Ghana (1981), Sambhar Lake (1990), Khichan, Menar and Siliserh (all 2025). Largest Indian site: Sundarban Wetland, West Bengal (4,230 sq km); smallest: Renuka (HP) and Vembannur (TN), 0.2 sq km each.
Montreux Record (India, 2 sites): Keoladeo Ghana NP, Rajasthan (1990) and Loktak Lake, Manipur (1993).

Wildlife numbers: tigers 3,682 (All-India Tiger Estimation 2022, a Guinness record exercise); leopards 13,874 (2022, 5th cycle, NTCA-WII); snow leopards 718 (SPAI, 2019-23); Asiatic lions 891 (2025, up from 674 in 2020). 58 tiger reserves as of March 2025.
Project Cheetah: 53 cheetahs in India as of March 2026 including 33 India-born cubs, at Kuno National Park and Gandhi Sagar Sanctuary (Madhya Pradesh).
International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA) — formally established 12 March 2024, headquartered in India, covers SEVEN big cats, Rs 150 crore support for 2023-28.

Health: WHO declared EBOLA a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in May 2026 (DRC/Uganda); a Sudan-strain vaccine trial began in Uganda. India certified TRACHOMA-free by WHO in April 2025.

India carries about 25% of the global TB burden (Global TB Report 2025). Nationwide HPV vaccination campaign for 14-year-old girls launched March 2026. First 'AI clinic' opened at GIMS, Greater Noida, January 2026.

Vaccines/therapies in the news: R21/Matrix-M malaria vaccine (Oxford + Serum Institute of India), DengiAll (ICMR-Panacea Biotec, dengue), HILLCHOL (Bharat Biotech, oral cholera), BIRSA 101 (CSIR-IGIB, sickle-cell gene therapy).

Global elimination milestones: Niger — first African country validated for eliminating onchocerciasis/river blindness (Dec 2025); Nepal declared malaria-free (2025); Maldives achieved triple elimination of mother-to-child HIV, Hepatitis B and syphilis (Oct 2025).

Nobel science 2025 — Physics: Clarke, Devoret and Martinis (macroscopic quantum tunnelling and energy quantisation in an electric circuit); Chemistry: Kitagawa, Robson and Yaghi (metal-organic frameworks); Medicine: Brunkow, Ramsdell and Sakaguchi (peripheral immune tolerance).

questions.q: Which satellite was placed in orbit by ISRO's LVM3-M6 mission launched on 24 December 2025?
questions.exp: LVM3-M6 lifted off from Sriharikota on 24 December 2025 with the BlueBird Block-2 direct-to-mobile communication satellite. ISRO described it as the heaviest satellite ever lifted from Indian soil by an Indian launcher (as of September 2026).

questions.q: The BlueBird Block-2 satellite launched by LVM3-M6 was built for which company?
questions.exp: AST SpaceMobile (USA) is building a direct-to-mobile satellite constellation. The launch was a commercial mission executed under an agreement with NewSpace India Limited (NSIL), ISRO's commercial arm.

questions.q: ISRO's PSLV-C62 mission of January 2026 failed following an anomaly in which stage of the vehicle?
questions.exp: PSLV-C62, launched on 12 January 2026, was lost after an anomaly in the solid-fuelled third stage (PS3). It was the second PSLV failure within a year, following PSLV-C61 (as of September 2026).

questions.q: Which Earth observation satellite was the primary payload of the unsuccessful PSLV-C62 mission?
questions.exp: PSLV-C62 carried EOS-N1 along with 14 co-passenger satellites. The mission was ISRO's first launch attempt of 2026.

questions.q: EOS-05, launched in September 2026, is significant as India's first
opts: imaging satellite in a geosynchronous orbit
satellite powered by a nuclear battery
satellite launched from a sea-based platform
questions.exp: EOS-05 was injected into a sub-geosynchronous transfer orbit and later raised to geosynchronous orbit, enabling repeated imaging of large areas for agriculture, disaster management and land monitoring (as of September 2026).

questions.q: EOS-05 was launched on 4 September 2026 by which launch vehicle?
questions.exp: GSLV-F17, the 19th flight of the Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle, lifted off from the Second Launch Pad of the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota.

questions.q: Who is the Chairman of the Indian Space Research Organisation, as of September 2026?
questions.exp: V. Narayanan heads ISRO and is Secretary, Department of Space (as of September 2026).

questions.q: The advanced version of the Agni-5 missile fitted with MIRV technology was flight-tested in May 2026 from
opts: Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island, Odisha
questions.exp: DRDO carried out the test on 8 May 2026 from Dr APJ Abdul Kalam Island (Wheeler Island) off the Odisha coast.

questions.q: In the context of India's Agni-5 missile, MIRV stands for
questions.exp: A MIRV payload allows a single missile to deliver several warheads to different targets. India first demonstrated it under 'Mission Divyastra'.

questions.q: Which DRDO interceptor, tested in June 2026, was described as having reached the 'intercontinental class' in the Ballistic Missile Defence programme?
questions.exp: Three flight tests on 10-11 June 2026 validated the multi-layered BMD system; the AD-2 interceptor destroyed Agni-series target missiles (as of September 2026).

questions.q: The first C-295 transport aircraft fully assembled in India made its maiden flight in June 2026 from a Tata-Airbus facility at
questions.exp: The Vadodara Final Assembly Line is the first private-sector military aircraft assembly plant in India; the flight took place ahead of schedule on 10 June 2026.

questions.q: India's nationwide HPV vaccination campaign launched in March 2026 targets girls of which age?
questions.exp: The campaign vaccinates 14-year-old girls against human papillomavirus to prevent cervical cancer (as of September 2026).

questions.q: Who took over as the Chief of the Army Staff of the Indian Army in June 2026?
questions.exp: Lt Gen Dhiraj Seth was named Chief of the Army Staff on 13 June 2026 (as of September 2026).

questions.q: The Request for Proposal for India's fifth-generation Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA) was issued in May 2026 with the first flight targeted for
questions.exp: Three development partners were shortlisted; deliveries are expected from 2035. AMCA is being developed by the Aeronautical Development Agency with HAL and private industry (as of September 2026).

questions.q: Exercise 'Vayushakti-26', the Indian Air Force's integrated firepower demonstration held in 2026, took place at
questions.exp: Vayushakti is periodically staged at the Pokhran Range in Jaisalmer district of Rajasthan, where the IAF demonstrates day-and-night integrated air operations.

questions.q: Exercise MILAN 2026, the multilateral naval exercise hosted by the Indian Navy, was held at
questions.exp: MILAN 2026 was conducted at Visakhapatnam under the Eastern Naval Command with the theme 'Camaraderie, Cooperation, Collaboration'.

questions.q: The India AI Impact Summit 2026 was held in February 2026 at which venue in New Delhi?
questions.exp: The summit ran from 16 to 21 February 2026 at Bharat Mandapam and drew participants from over 100 countries and 20 international organisations.

questions.q: At the India AI Impact Summit 2026, India's GPU capacity under the IndiaAI Mission was announced as expanding to more than
questions.exp: Capacity was stated as rising from over 38,000 GPUs to over 58,000 GPUs under the IndiaAI Mission (as of February 2026).

questions.q: At the India AI Impact Summit 2026, Google announced a $15 billion artificial intelligence hub in India at
questions.exp: The Visakhapatnam AI hub was among investment pledges exceeding $200 billion made around the summit; Reliance Industries pledged $110 billion over seven years.

questions.q: The 30th Conference of the Parties (COP30) to the UNFCCC was held in November 2025 at
questions.exp: COP30 was held at Belem in the Brazilian Amazon from 10 to 22 November 2025, with about 200 parties participating.

questions.q: The final decision package adopted at COP30 was named
questions.exp: 'Mutirao' is a Portuguese-Brazilian term for collective community effort; the 'Global Mutirao' decision called for tripling adaptation finance by 2035.

questions.q: Who presided over COP30 as its President?
questions.exp: Brazilian diplomat Andre Correa do Lago was the COP30 President. Simon Stiell is the Executive Secretary of the UNFCCC.

questions.q: As of August 2026, the total number of Ramsar sites in India is
questions.exp: India crossed the century mark in 2026; the 101st site, Glaw Lake in Arunachal Pradesh, was designated on 3 August 2026. The sites are spread over 28 States and Union Territories (as of September 2026).

questions.q: Glaw Lake, designated in August 2026 as India's 101st Ramsar site, is located in which State?
questions.exp: Glaw Lake became India's 101st Ramsar site on 3 August 2026 (as of September 2026).

questions.q: As of March 2026, the total number of cheetahs in India under Project Cheetah was reported to be
questions.exp: The figure of 53 included 33 India-born cubs. The cheetahs are held at Kuno National Park and Gandhi Sagar Sanctuary in Madhya Pradesh (as of September 2026).

II. G1 will carry the humanoid robot Vyommitra.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: Gaganyaan's uncrewed G1 mission on LVM3 will carry Vyommitra; the crewed mission follows the uncrewed test flights and is targeted for 2027 (as of September 2026).

questions.exp: All three are correct. Defence exports rose about 63% to roughly $4.1 billion, and the three warships commissioned on 21 June 2026 each had over 75% indigenous content (as of September 2026).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the India AI Impact Summit 2026:

questions.exp: The summit (16-21 February 2026) was attended by over 100 countries and 20 international organisations, and its declaration was endorsed by 92 countries and organisations.

questions.q:

II. It established a new just transition mechanism.
III. It adopted a binding roadmap for phasing out fossil fuels.

questions.exp: Statement III is wrong — no fossil-fuel roadmap was included in the 'Global Mutirao' text; the presidency instead promised separate voluntary roadmaps. A 'Global Implementation Accelerator' was also launched.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's Ramsar sites:

questions.exp: Sundarban Wetland covers about 4,230 sq km. Keoladeo Ghana (Rajasthan) was placed on the Montreux Record in 1990 and Loktak (Manipur) in 1993.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
I. India was certified by the World Health Organization as having eliminated trachoma in April 2025.
II. As per the Global TB Report 2025, India accounts for about one-fourth of the global tuberculosis burden.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Both are correct. Trachoma is a bacterial eye infection and a leading infectious cause of blindness; India remains the world's largest contributor to the TB caseload (as of September 2026).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about global health developments:
I. The World Health Organization declared Ebola a Public Health Emergency of International Concern in May 2026.
II. In December 2025 Niger became the first African country validated for eliminating onchocerciasis (river blindness).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Both are correct. The Ebola PHEIC related to outbreaks in the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, where a Sudan-strain vaccine trial was launched.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA):
I. It is headquartered in India.
II. It covers seven big cat species.
III. India had 58 tiger reserves as of March 2025.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: The IBCA was formally established on 12 March 2024 with Rs 150 crore of Indian support for 2023-28, and covers the tiger, lion, leopard, snow leopard, cheetah, jaguar and puma.

questions.q: The selection committee for the National Sports Awards 2025 was headed by
questions.exp: Retired Supreme Court judge Justice Arun Kumar Mishra chaired the committee that announced the National Sports Awards 2025.

questions.exp: The Rashtriya Khel Protsahan Puraskar recognises corporate and institutional promotion of sport; the Army Paralympic Node, Pune received it for 2025.

questions.q: The Arjuna Award (Lifetime Achievement) 2025 was given to I. Arumainayagam, a former player of which sport?
questions.exp: I. Arumainayagam is a former Indian footballer. Seventeen sportspersons received the regular Arjuna Award for 2025.

questions.q: The final of the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2026 was played at
questions.exp: India beat New Zealand by 96 runs in the final at Ahmedabad on 8 March 2026.

questions.q: India won the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2026 by defeating which team in the final?
questions.exp: India beat New Zealand by 96 runs on 8 March 2026 to lift a record third T20 World Cup and become the first side to win back-to-back titles.

questions.q: India won its first-ever ICC Women's Cricket World Cup in November 2025 by defeating which team in the final?
questions.exp: India beat South Africa in the final of the 2025 Women's Cricket World Cup to win their maiden ODI world title.

questions.q: The 2026 Asian Games are being held in which city/country?
questions.exp: The 20th Asian Games are scheduled at Aichi-Nagoya, Japan from 19 September to 4 October 2026, followed by the Asian Para Games in October (as of September 2026).

questions.q: The 2026 Winter Olympic Games were held in which country?
questions.exp: The Winter Olympics were held at Milan (Milano-Cortina) in Italy from 6 to 22 February 2026, followed by the Winter Paralympics in March 2026.

questions.q: The BWF World Badminton Championships 2026 were hosted by India in which city?
questions.exp: New Delhi hosted the BWF World Championships from 17 to 23 August 2026. Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty went out in the quarter-finals.

questions.q: The 2026 Chess Olympiad is being held in which city?
questions.exp: Samarkand in Uzbekistan hosts the 2026 Chess Olympiad in September 2026; the FIDE Candidates Tournament earlier in the year was held at Paphos, Cyprus.

questions.q: The Nobel Peace Prize 2025 was awarded to
questions.exp: Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado received the 2025 Nobel Peace Prize for promoting democratic rights and a peaceful transition in Venezuela.

questions.q: The Nobel Prize in Literature 2025 was awarded to Laszlo Krasznahorkai, a writer from
questions.exp: The Hungarian novelist was honoured 'for his compelling and visionary oeuvre that, in the midst of apocalyptic terror, reaffirms the power of art'.

questions.q: Which film won the Academy Award for Best Picture at the 98th Academy Awards held in 2026?
questions.exp: 'One Battle After Another' won Best Picture, and Paul Thomas Anderson won Best Director, at the 2026 Oscars.

questions.q: The Pulitzer Prize for Fiction 2026 was awarded to Daniel Kraus for which work?
questions.exp: 'Angel Down' won the 2026 Pulitzer Prize for Fiction; Bess Wohl's 'Liberation' won the Pulitzer for Drama.

questions.q: Which Indian film actor was named in the TIME 100 Most Influential People list of 2026?
questions.exp: Ranbir Kapoor featured in the TIME 100 list released on 15 April 2026, with his profile written by Ayushmann Khurrana. Chef Vikas Khanna and Google CEO Sundar Pichai also featured.

questions.exp: All three are correct. India won 39 medals overall and led boxing with 7 golds and 3 silvers (as of September 2026).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2026:

II. India won a record third T20 World Cup title.
III. India became the first team to win back-to-back T20 World Cups.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct; India also became the first side to win the T20 World Cup on home soil, beating New Zealand by 96 runs at Ahmedabad on 8 March 2026.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. Vidit Gujarathi was the other chess player among the 2025 Arjuna awardees (as of September 2026).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Nobel Prizes 2025:
I. The Prize in Physiology or Medicine was awarded for discoveries concerning peripheral immune tolerance.
II. The Prize in Economic Sciences was shared by Joel Mokyr, Philippe Aghion and Peter Howitt.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Both are correct. Mary Brunkow, Fred Ramsdell and Shimon Sakaguchi shared the Medicine prize for work on regulatory T cells; the Economics prize recognised innovation-driven growth and creative destruction.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Padma Awards 2026:
I. A total of 131 awards were announced.
II. They included 5 Padma Vibhushan awards.
III. They included 13 Padma Bhushan awards.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct; the remaining 113 were Padma Shri awards (as of September 2026).

questions.q:

I. The President approved 70 gallantry awards, including six posthumous ones.
II. Three Kirti Chakras were announced.
III. Thirteen Shaurya Chakras were announced.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.exp: All three are correct. The Kirti Chakra went to Group Captain Prasanth Balakrishnan Nair, Major Arshdeep Singh and Naib Subedar Doleshwar Subba.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sahitya Akademi Awards 2025:

II. Mamta Kalia received the Hindi award for 'Jeete Jee Allahabad'.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Both are correct. 'Crimson Spring' is a novel set around the Jallianwala Bagh massacre; 'Jeete Jee Allahabad' is a memoir.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 2026 FIFA World Cup:
I. It was held in June-July 2026.
II. It was jointly hosted by the United States, Mexico and Canada.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.exp: Both are correct. The tournament ran from 11 June to 19 July 2026 across North America and was the first World Cup with 48 teams.

questions.q:

questions.exp: Both are correct. Ram Sutar died on 18 December 2025 at the age of 100; Swaraj Kaushal, a senior advocate and former Governor of Mizoram, died on 5 December 2025.
